Warframe certainly sets the standard when it comes to
games available on steam.
Personally it's been a long time since I've found such a friendly and helpful community, where the developers are as dedicated and just as friendly. Like most games the sheer amount of content available can be daunting, something which in the past has literally forced me away from a game. The community in Warframe however was friendly enough to provide me with links, advice on youtubers and directions to other online resources too - From here my journey as a Tenno begun.
The gameplay from start captivated me. Primarily being that there's so many variables in how any given player can choose to play. Players have access to numerous different "waframes" which in turn all have unique and varying abilities/powers. Players can then decide to carry numerous different weapons, again having their own 'abilities' which effect game entities differently. Warframe also provides options of equipping a companion, a companion in the form of Sentinels, Kurbrows or Kavats
again each of which have varying abilities.
As sufficient time passes however, it does become obvious that Warframe is a truly an RNG based game, with the RNG becoming more & more predominant in recent times. The rise of the 'Hema' and the required resources to research this being a prime example. All of this RNG that Tenno must suffer only to be built upto, well... Nothing.
Which brings me to the biggest issue in Warframe! - End-Game content, or lack of.

I'm writing this review for the latest update for ARK: Survival Evolved, v254. The update added the sheep, Baryonyx, Purlovia, and the giant sausage shark as well as hair growing and the new set of equipment players can use.
I've noticed the biggest boo from this update is the TEK Tier equipment which is basically the endgame armor for your character. People claim that this will ruin ARK because alpha tribes will take advantage of it and basically screw over any tribe that is weaker to them. Personally to me, I think this aspect is great. It gives a new meaning to go hunt for bosses to get more than just a flag and a head to put on a trophy and gives you to do more than just tame the best dinos and guarding your base with them or other of your best dinos. Not to mention the elements needed to run the TEK Tier runs out much faster than you expected and this goes to the next point.
Even the biggest and baddest of tribes can go down to flames because they'll have to choose whenever to constantly farm all three bosses to learn the TEK Engrams or defending their base from other tribes that plan to take them down. Not to also mention they would have to be online constantly and essentially locking themselves in their house in order to maintain control of the server. (That is if you are playing on a server where admins don't abuse their power).
People also complain that TEK Tier too far from the primitive region of the game. What part of the game is primitive? We don't have specimen implants into our arms and not to mention there are three god damn floating obelisks which take you away to a completely different place to fight them. I mean the game is called "ARK: Survival Evolved" where evolution is of the matter here. If you want to play a primitive game, play RUST.
I'm lightly bashing on the players who will quit an early access game because of one big update. The game could be better, but you're not giving them time to make it probably one of the best survival games I've played in a while. I think the update is amazing, but don't take my word for it if you disagree.

A game with rather Great Potential, Great Atmosphere Graphics, that is quite addictive, Yes you might enjoy your many first hours, building & taming, till you start realizing How awefully Grindy/time consuming this game is, along with how unrewarding is every feature in it, and the many under-developed aspects of the game (ex: basic & silly character fighting mechanics - useless tools - crappy looking weapons/armors - painful Building System - ..etc), that far in development, Moreover they have released a Paid DLC even when the game is still in Alpha, and according to what they say, this wont be the last time they do such a thing, so if you like to buy Alpha games that make you pay more than once for it, go ahead and buy the game!
This Game is focused mainly on wild life, Dinos and what not, taming and breeding, while little to nothing of the focus is given to the human character each player operates (ex: no bags to increase the carry-able weight, or carts to drag heavy weights around, or any kind of vehicle/transportation to travel/transport; without the use of tamed creatures. a very small variety of Armors, early to med game armors look like crap, no matter how good the tools you have are; the gathering ratio of them is horribly unreliable, and outfits only affect weather tolerance and armor, except the Ghillie set which increases the player stealthiness, but they don’t affect other important aspects like Health, Speed, Weight or Damage), so expect to count heavily on tamed creatures to pretty much do anything you need.
other issues:

{Optimization & Functionality}
the game requires a big space on your Drive, and half that space as free space, in order to reduce the errors that might occur during installing updates, though that wont eliminate the errors that will happen every now and then while updating the game in anycase, Moreover, the game runs Poorly on Medium to Low-end gaming PCs, making it almost impossible to enjoy the game or its graphics, which is pretty much the highest & Most developed aspect of the game -though that doesn't mean that the structures or early/mid armors and weapons look any good, they actually look quite.... classic and boring-, to run the game on max settings, you need to have not just any high end PC, but the Highest of the highest.
Personally, my work is graphic design so it requires a Decent Laptop to handle it, my laptop runs every game you could think of on high settings easily, but on Ark it barely runs a mixture of medium/Low settings, to work as smoothly as possible, and as high on settings as possible, yet Still Ark is the ONLY game that drives my laptop to blue-screen-of-death often enough, and I followed the best of guides on how to run Ark smoothly.

{Tutorial & Story}
there is no Tutorial in the game, or scenes, or a story to the game, even though the developers promised it almost right after the release of the Alpha game, but till now, its just bits and pieces of nothingness.

{Spawn Points}
if you start on an official Server, you are highly likely to spawn "inside" or "under" the base of someone, cause the developers did not see the need to put any restrictions on spawn points, due to the randomness of spawn points, nor any kind of spawn point protection for newbies, But if you spawned in an area abandoned by other players and structures, you are highly likely to die way more than you should, Cause every wild creature on the island would be so eager to introduce itself to you, to get to know how your insides taste like, since almost everything will kill you just by looking at you, and you cant do jack♥♥♥♥♥♥♥about it, thanks to how weak and fragile humans are in the game, losing everything on you on each death, till you actually get to build a hut and add a bed to it.

{Item Details & Appearance}
the character and every Tool, Weapon, and Armor that gets crafted early to mid game, looks quite usual, there is nothing fancy or stunning about them, and sadly the quality/rarity of an item does not have any effect on its appearance, so the highest rarity of an item sadly looks exactly as the lowest rarity of it, Moreover there are no Meshes till now of all the items, except poop & eggs, if you drop any item out of the inventory, it appears in the shape of a box, or a bag, depending on the quantity of the dropped items, which is kinda tolerable for an Early Access game, though one would think that this would have been resolved when the game is that far in development, anywho, checking the details on weapons and seeing (100%? 200%? 230%? - how is that remotely helpful? why not use solid numbers instead of just giving a percentage? Or even mixing Solid numbers with added percentage according to the rarity of the item??), where are the important and critical details in-game on weapons and tools?

{Building System & Structures}
can’t say its bad, but can’t say its good either, For small builders, its gonna be good enough, but for big builders, its not, its hard to build something that looks good out of it, but not impossible, given the right amount of tolerance, patience, brains, time and effort.

This Game has Passed its given out-of-Alpha-phase date by A LONG SHOT, its all about unpolished and/or useless features, and often lacks the sense of achievement, while nothing is rewarding enough aswell, and usually Cosmetics are the only reward for most of the events.
BE WARNED, this is Not a Survival Game, This is a Dino Farm Simulation Game, and a very bad one at it, Taming and Breeding Dinos might sound Fun, but when you See how Heavily Time Consuming they are, you will change your mind, its not about skill to hunt and tame a dino, its all just about time, so 1h in real time at least to find a proper Dino to Tame, another 1h at least to actually tame it, and 24hours at least to breed any dino.
A game with rather Great Potential, Great Atmosphere Graphics, that is quite addictive, Yes you might enjoy your many first hours, building & taming, till you start realizing How awefully Grindy/time consuming this game is, along with how unrewarding is every feature in it, and the many under-developed aspects of the game (ex: basic & silly character fighting mechanics - useless tools - crappy looking weapons/armors - painful Building System - ..etc), that far in development, Moreover they have released a Paid DLC even when the game is still in Alpha, and according to what they say, this wont be the last time they do such a thing, so if you like to buy Alpha games that make you pay more than once for it, go ahead and buy the game!
This Game is focused mainly on wild life, Dinos and what not, taming and breeding, while little to nothing of the focus is given to the human character each player operates (ex: no bags to increase the carry-able weight, or carts to drag heavy weights around, or any kind of vehicle/transportation to travel/transport; without the use of tamed creatures. a very small variety of Armors, early to med game armors look like crap, no matter how good the tools you have are; the gathering ratio of them is horribly unreliable, and outfits only affect weather tolerance and armor, except the Ghillie set which increases the player stealthiness, but they don’t affect other important aspects like Health, Speed, Weight or Damage), so expect to count heavily on tamed creatures to pretty much do anything you need.
other issues:

{Optimization & Functionality}
the game requires a big space on your Drive, and half that space as free space, in order to reduce the errors that might occur during installing updates, though that wont eliminate the errors that will happen every now and then while updating the game in anycase, Moreover, the game runs Poorly on Medium to Low-end gaming PCs, making it almost impossible to enjoy the game or its graphics, which is pretty much the highest & Most developed aspect of the game -though that doesn't mean that the structures or early/mid armors and weapons look any good, they actually look quite.... classic and boring-, to run the game on max settings, you need to have not just any high end PC, but the Highest of the highest.
Personally, my work is graphic design so it requires a Decent Laptop to handle it, my laptop runs every game you could think of on high settings easily, but on Ark it barely runs a mixture of medium/Low settings, to work as smoothly as possible, and as high on settings as possible, yet Still Ark is the ONLY game that drives my laptop to blue-screen-of-death often enough, and I followed the best of guides on how to run Ark smoothly.

{Tutorial & Story}
there is no Tutorial in the game, or scenes, or a story to the game, even though the developers promised it almost right after the release of the Alpha game, but till now, its just bits and pieces of nothingness.

{Spawn Points}
if you start on an official Server, you are highly likely to spawn "inside" or "under" the base of someone, cause the developers did not see the need to put any restrictions on spawn points, due to the randomness of spawn points, nor any kind of spawn point protection for newbies, But if you spawned in an area abandoned by other players and structures, you are highly likely to die way more than you should, Cause every wild creature on the island would be so eager to introduce itself to you, to get to know how your insides taste like, since almost everything will kill you just by looking at you, and you cant do jack♥♥♥♥♥♥♥about it, thanks to how weak and fragile humans are in the game, losing everything on you on each death, till you actually get to build a hut and add a bed to it.

{Item Details & Appearance}
the character and every Tool, Weapon, and Armor that gets crafted early to mid game, looks quite usual, there is nothing fancy or stunning about them, and sadly the quality/rarity of an item does not have any effect on its appearance, so the highest rarity of an item sadly looks exactly as the lowest rarity of it, Moreover there are no Meshes till now of all the items, except poop & eggs, if you drop any item out of the inventory, it appears in the shape of a box, or a bag, depending on the quantity of the dropped items, which is kinda tolerable for an Early Access game, though one would think that this would have been resolved when the game is that far in development, anywho, checking the details on weapons and seeing (100%? 200%? 230%? - how is that remotely helpful? why not use solid numbers instead of just giving a percentage? Or even mixing Solid numbers with added percentage according to the rarity of the item??), where are the important and critical details in-game on weapons and tools?

{Building System & Structures}
can’t say its bad, but can’t say its good either, For small builders, its gonna be good enough, but for big builders, its not, its hard to build something that looks good out of it, but not impossible, given the right amount of tolerance, patience, brains, time and effort.

While the game play for this has been intense and challenging, the biggest problem on the servers are the tribes.  Once a tribe has established itself on a server, they probably in most cases were early adopters of the game.  The problem is not PVP, but that the established tribes that have worked up their skill levels and bases to the point that new players, just trying to learn the game, are within days of building a structure, killed off by the tribes that dominate these public servers.  There really is no level playing field at this point because there never is a clean server wipe to put everyone back to square one.  If you like this concept, fine but I suspect the sales for this are falling off and it is being heavily discounted because they cannot attract new players to these dominated servers with tribes with attitudes of "this is OUR server".  Hours of work destroyed overnight by these tribes that control key points of the maps. Unless unlimited new public servers are set up, the number of existing servers are controlled for the most part by a small number of players in tribes that paid for the game and new revenue for this game will dwindle off. Best chances are to play the PVE servers, but then there are still issues within those as well.

Early Access game with more content than most complete titles, but poorly optimised, though a mid-high end PC can easily run it with stunning Crysis-tier graphics. As of right now, you'd need at least a 1080 to max it out. Though lower end PCs can use launch settings to run it in directx 10 mode, which, whilst it doesn't look quite as good, it's still quite the eye candy, and the performance increase is huge. Haven't got the chance to see how low it can go, but it should run fine on pretty much anything, just follow the guides in which it's better explained how to do that.
To sum up all my experiences with this game so far:
Single player: With a few settings tweaked to gather more resources and be able to fend off without the need for an entire tribe, a few mods to spice things up and fix some problematic vanilla game mechanics, I see it as the second best way to play Ark, as there is no rush, no need to play daily as the game doesn't run while you are logged out, you can experience months or years of Ark in just a few weeks. It gets exponentially better if you host a small server and bring in a few friends.
Official PvE Servers: One of the friendliest online environments I've ever seen, pretty much everyone helps everyone, it's very peaceful and relaxing.
Official PvP Servers: Impossible for new players as everyone is killing everyone, you won't get a single chance start a base, and even if you would, you'd be raided instantly.
Dedicated/smaller unofficial servers: See SP, just that the owner makes the rules, and usually PvP servers have rules to protect noobs, probably the best way to go if you can't convince your friends to play with you.
Also ended up buying the expansion just to support the devs, but, after having tried it out, Scorched Earth is also really good and challenging, a very welcome change in scenery from The Island and The Center, even though cross-ark transfers are impossible in single player or on small servers and horrifyingly bugged on the servers which support it.
Props to the devs for the frequent updates, though it really sucks that The Center gets everything much slower than The Island or even SE. Price-quality ratio is amazing, ~$30 for 200+ hours is completely worth it, not to mention ~$10 when it's on sale. The expansion is not an urgent buy, think about it after a full game on The Island. Haven't tried SotF and I doubt I ever will, much too competitive for me, but I understand it's for Ark what King of the Hill is for H1Z1. Primitive+ is also a good change if you're not into the modern riot/guns tier or sci-fi tek tier things.
Overall, I'd say it's the best survival game out there at this moment, far beyond Rust and anything else, and very much past Early Access. 10/10 would recommend.

One of the most enjoyable action/RPGs I've played.  Not pay-to-win, either.  The premium currency can be used either as a shortcut or for cosmetic items.  I've probably spent more than I should have on this game for cosmetics or items that I didn't feel like grinding for, but at no point did it feel like a rip-off or that I 'had' to spend cash.
Each frame (think of a character class) feels unique and dynamically alters the way you play, and each are viable and uniquely suited for a given situation.  After you get past the clunky tutorial, the missions flow easily - you can solo most missions if you feel like exploring and opening every single loot cache. . . or you can find other players fairly quickly to tackle the harder missions.  Mastery ranks encourage players to try new things and keep their experience fresh, but the forma mechanic also allows you to keep any item you enjoy viable at all levels of play.
I'm a little ashamed of the time I spent playing this, but let that be testament to its replay value.  I normally burn out on games much faster.

The game itself is fun, and the monetization practices are probably some of the best I've seen. But due to some developer decisions, I can't really recommend it.
Do you like playing games with your friends? Do you want to have fun with your friends in Warframe? Too bad! The matchmaking in this game is Garbage. I say that with a capital G because Warframe's matchmaking is it's own special kind of garbage. Peer-to-peer hosting has never worked for any MMO. It never worked for S4 League, it never worked for Vindictus, it never worked for a lot of games I won't spend my time listing. So why the hell did Digital Extremes think it would somehow magically work for them? I can't even play with a single friend without getting the dreaded "host migration" screen before it kicks one or both of us to our orbiters or our own instances. The netcode for this game is a damned trainwreck.
Warframe also tries way too damn hard to shove PvP down their players throats. Most people don't participate in PvP because said Garbage-with-a-capital-G matchmaking is somehow worse in Conclave, even once you look past all the people getting buttmad and disconnecting thus ruining the match for everyone else. Digital Extremes seems to have this raging hard-on for putting PvP modes in story missions for the sake of drawing more players to Conclave. The Index in the mission "The Glast Gambit" is probably the worst example of this, because not only does it force you to play PvP against a bunch of buggy AI, it sucks up all your credits, too.
Combine these two glaring flaws with a bug-riddled PC version (many bugs are progression breakers and force you to abandon missions, which not only effect your mission success rate, but are months if not years old yet DE is oddly adamant about not fixing them), the existence of riven mods, sorties, and a god-awful community, and you have yourself a game I really do want to like, but I really can't recommend to anyone.

If not, the game will be so much boring as it keeps grinding and grinding and grinding again and again, though within a procedural map that was created everytime you enter the map. A lot of terms seem to be associated with warframe, the main ones I hear are Addictive, Pay2win and Grindy as all seven circles of hell.
Only the first statement is entirely true.
The game is actually well made and plays great. The weapons are all varied and fun to use, the mod system is great and adds multiple, meaningful, and radically different ways to customize every piece of equipment. The level design is pretty good, and feels varied even if you're playing on the same tileset for an hour. Though it can get dull at times, that's not something unforgivable, coming from a free to play game.
The monetization system is fair and pretty great(Though weapon slots are a bit limited without cash and it has had a few instances of scummy behavior once or twice), anything non-cosmetic is available in game. Which brings us to the ultimate question: Is it a boring piece of hell grindfest to obtain?
The answer is, to most people's pleasure, no! It's not actually that bad! Sure, you'll be farming for whatever you want, but there are things easy to build for the early game, and farming materials becomes trivial once you hit level 30 gear, which is going to take you days at most.
If anyone were to come up to me and ask me "Is warframe worth a try?" I would say most definitely.

Probably the best free-to-play game I've played so far.
Gunplay feels smooth and fast paced, Graphics are nice and not too demanding. Can play on 720p on medium on a 5 year of laptop with dedicated graphics.
Warframes feel quite unique and their abilities make each frame useful in certain types of missions. It doesn't look like there is one "super frame" that will do everything better than the others. (Probably there is some deeper meta gameplay that I haven't discovered yet)
The monetarisation aspect of the developer is not obstrusive at all.
I've played over 100 hours of it now and do not feel pushed to buy anything so far.
You only need to be willing to read the game wiki and most frames will drop after a couple mission runs. Also you don't progress on a strict linear path like in WarThunder (that gets slower and slower the further in you are) after your first frame, you'll start collecting mods in missions and make up your mind which frame to get next. Some drop from bosses on early planets, other on more difficult bosses (but you'll always find players willing to run you through a boss if you are nice) a few frames are difficult to aquire via Sortie missions, I'm not that far, so I can't tell how frustrating it is.
All in all after 5 frames and a dozen of weapons leveled to 30, it seems all very well balanced and designed.

Ok, so what I've been hearing about PVP sounds absolutely horrendous and bad, but I only play with a couple of friends so I've never ran into that, so keep that into account if you want to play the game that way.
I love building and taming in this game. There's a clear progressions system, and since I play alone/with 2 or 3 people at a time and I'm the admin, you can tweak the game settings to be more catered to this type of playstyle. There isn't really any set goals, but I find myself just saying I want a certain thing, may it be something I have to craft or a dino, and it leads to this adventure of scavenging, running and fighting. There's something insanely satisfying when you achieve that goal you set for yourself and you know you planned ahead, set everything in place, maybe tamed a big dino, etc.
The maps are also full of interesting things to explore, and most of the time it isn't just repeated garbage like some other exploration games *cough no man's sky cough*. Since exploration is so harsh, it makes it way more satisfying to actually clear out a new cave or something, because it normally takes mutiple trips back to make sure you have the right gear and are ready to dive in.
If you can get a couple of friends together, I would 100% recommend this game, if you want to play solo, I probably would as well, but if you're in it for playing on public servers and doing the whole social raid/defend thing, I'd probably just tell you to play Rust or something.

I usually don't buy games like this in early access as they tend to be broken and incomplete, however, this game has been in early access for a long time and looked cool. I thought that maybe it was in a polished enough state for me to play and enjoy so I picked it up when it was on sale. Fact is, this game is still a buggy, glitchy, un-optimized mess. It has HUGE memory leaks. If you want to play this game get  at least 32 GB of RAM. Even with 16 GB of 1866 DDR3 and a GTX 970, this game crushes my computer on medium settings. But it's only because of a memory leak. I know this because the game plays fine for about 45 mins from when I start it.Then, performance starts to drop off and it gets stuttery every once in a while. About an hour and a half into a play session it becomes unplayable and you have to shut down the client entirely and restart it. This wouldn't be so bad if the game didnt take 15-20 minutes to actually load into a server. My advice is stay away from games like this in general. The Devs have had well over a year to optimize their game and make it playable and they have shown that they would rather spend time and money making a paid expansion pack for a game that hasn't even come out of early access yet.
The WORST part is, this game seems so fun! The concepts are great and the mechanics work well enough. There are plenty of things to craft and build, taming dinosaurs is cool and the weapons are cool. I want this game to be playable so badly! The reality is though, it just isn't and since the devs seem more focussed on content updates (as opposed to optimization updates) I doubt it will be anytime soon.

There are games you play that have incredible moments, memories that are indelibly linked with that game. And then there are other times when I see a game's title and I think "Have I played that?". Sometimes, there are games like Dragon Age where I even get to the end, and a few weeks later I can remember nothing about the game.
ARK is one of those games that has incredible moments; wandering into a valley full of Brontosaurus' being hunted by a pack of T Rex, and trying to manouevre through the semi-darkness to raid the bodies, or discovering a T Rex has wandered into my encampment, and managing to down it only after it had killed all my dino pets and was chomping on my house. These moments have proper tension, fear, even panic.
But then they are tempered with the awful dread that they bring, the sinking feeling of "oh my god, it took 5 hours to build that". This game has a huge amount of grind, a really huge amount.
The truth is it is balanced for multiplayer, the idea that you will be working together with others in order to survive and build up over time, and as a multiplayer experience that is fine (to a point) - yet multiplayer carries it's own risk from the curious choice to let other tribes port themselves, levelled to the eyeballs, onto your server and wipe you out.
So stick to single player then? There are a few sliders to speed things up, but even maxed out, you will spend way too much of your time gathering stuff and carting it backwards and forwards, so that even after many hours of play, you really wonder if it is all really worth it for those peaks.
ARK is also labelled as Early Access, yet this is a very curious model going on here, especially considering the up front price. But then you'd think it was great to get free dinosaur additions from time to time right? Right. What about a paid for DLC when it's still in Early Access? Pretty odd. Especially when you consider the game has some pretty fundamental issues still. Manouevring a dinosaur around anything larger than a breadcrumb is so frustrating that my neighbours came to see what I was shouting about, and the clipping is something special to behold.
But what about those moments? Are they enough? On balance, probably not, unless you are patient. The multiplayer experience carries serious risks, and the single player has so much time wasting it's really hard to come out with a thumb's up. Do I like it? Yes. Would I recommend it? Not yet - not till those issues are fixed.

This game is one of few F2P games on Steam that are really nice, but it comes with its good and bad.
PROS:
1) Very fun.
2) Solid storyline.
3) Not money hungry.
4) Fantastic diversity (Class choice, weapon choice, appearance choice).
5) No need to pay a single penny if you want everything.
6) Great variety of maps.
7) Beautiful graphics and immersion.
CONS:
1) ♥♥♥♥♥♥ AI.
2) A lot of bugs. (I MEAN ALOT!)
3) If you truly want to get everything without to pay, you'll need to farm alot.
4) Extremely harsh rules (AKA. You can get perma-banned for swearing at people kinda harshness).
5) Great imbalance between some classes and weapons.
6) The community is horrible. (Atleast most of it are).
7) Overpriced market items (AKA. if you want to buy something from market, you'll need to pay much more than if you would pay for the same items from trade chat).
8) Horrible match-making.
9) A lot of metas, certainly alot of maps, weapons, and classes, but only few stand out as the ultimate.
In conclusion, this game is extremely good if you can cope up with the disadvantages and the lost time (You can get like 1K-2K hours and still haven't obtained anything, well, until you pay that is.)

The game itself is fun, and the monetization practices are probably some of the best I've seen. But due to some developer decisions, I can't really recommend it.
Do you like playing games with your friends? Do you want to have fun with your friends in Warframe? Too bad! The matchmaking in this game is Garbage. I say that with a capital G because Warframe's matchmaking is it's own special kind of garbage. Peer-to-peer hosting has never worked for any MMO. It never worked for S4 League, it never worked for Vindictus, it never worked for a lot of games I won't spend my time listing. So why the hell did Digital Extremes think it would somehow magically work for them? I can't even play with a single friend without getting the dreaded "host migration" screen before it kicks one or both of us to our orbiters or our own instances. The netcode for this game is a damned trainwreck.
Warframe also tries way too damn hard to shove PvP down their players throats. Most people don't participate in PvP because said Garbage-with-a-capital-G matchmaking is somehow worse in Conclave, even once you look past all the people getting buttmad and disconnecting thus ruining the match for everyone else. Digital Extremes seems to have this raging hard-on for putting PvP modes in story missions for the sake of drawing more players to Conclave. I like Warframe, I like it a lot.
There are reasons of course, the improved parkour system makes the game both easier and faster to play, giving you the ability to dodge enemies and quickly move through the terrain.  All the weapons, besides a few pistols that look the same, feel completely unique and the types range from the normal types, like your assault riffles and your snipers.  Along with the normal however is the laser riffles, guns that shoot sawblades, and living pistols that shoot toxic needles.
The gameplay is varied, not just a mixture of platforming and shooting, but the entire game has been expanded since it's release, the stand out being the Spy Missions, where you have to sneak around at a certain point, or else the enemy faction will destroy the data.  The standards are there as well, defending a point, exterminating X number of enemies, and king of the hill with capturing towers are all in play.  It Has all sorts of ways to vary the gameplay, but the biggest is the way they use modular level tilesets to form levels, however this is both brilliant and a bit of a mess, because some rooms can have misleading entrances and exits that can cause you to become lost when something looks like it's the way and ends up leading to a dead end.
There is plenty of end game stuff as well, Viod missions award powerful prime parts and other rewards, however there is quite a bit of grinding involved, the current big bad of 'never have enough' is the resource Neurode.
The game has it's faults, but is also a vastly superior product to what some AAA publishers will charge you sixty bucks for, and everything that can be bought in the store that has functionality can also be made.

It sucks to give this game a bad review because there is some good potential here. I got this game knowing that it would be very demanding and to no surprise it was. I dont claim to have the best pc out there but most games I can handle on high settings apart from open world games like this, which is understandable because its hard for computers to render lots of polygons and map textures. The problem with this game is not that it has bad game design far from it. Its not that the game is extreamly demanding which is fine. No the problem with this game is that is very poorly optimised. even when i have this game at all low settings, ground textures off, all sky effects off, and lots of other graphical settings off this game still runs at 5 fps. This could be because of high pings from servers but my graphics cards twin nvidia geforce gtx 770's with msi enabled should be able to run this game fine at low or even medium settings. And its not the gpu's I swear, I did a thorough check of my gpu's running this and they both work at their highest performance. I know this is an early access game and I know it will get better it is pretty good allready I just hope that the game devs improve the optimisation settings for people with less capable pc's. That said if you want to buy this game I recomend 2 things. 1: wait untill this game is not in early access anymore, and 2: make sure you have at least a nvida geforce gtx 1070 or higher in case they dont fix these issues. All things considered this is a very decent game but please add better optimisation settings for the less capable pc's.

I feel like Ark is a very quickly developing game, with very active developers. You dont see devs like this in many other games, and I can appreciate the dev team for that. I do recommend this game because even though it is very hard to run on some PCs, the game is so much fun, even for how much of a time sink it is. If there is one tip I have to give, it would be to NEVER BUILD ON BEACHES, you will be noticed easily and trolled all the time.

Although I rage-quitted ark a couple of times, it is one of the best games I ever played. In this game a lot of freedom is given to the players, rendering the survival experience more than amazing, where you have not only to fear the dinosaurs but mostly the other players. This is not an easy game, it requires a lot of effort and the risk of loosing everything if one is not careful. I myself, lost everything once or twice, but this is part of PvP, and there is still a fun side in restarting from zero. This is a game where you have responsabilities, you have your own tribe where you to "survive the ark" together, this can lead to a lot of internal arguing or to a development of deep friendship. The complicated mechanics and unlimited options make this game much more interesting and innovative than what it seems on surface. Although I have 600+ hours, there is still a lot I discover week by week. Although it is indeed true that this game is a bit laggy, the developers are very proactive and update the game so frequently that I believe this problem will be soon fixed. I would reccommend anyone to give this game a try because it is worth it.

The problem though is that a decent number of official servers have severe lag and rubberbanding.  If they are not suffering from poor performance, they are suffereing from DDoS attacks to the point where the servers are simply taken offline for 24 hours.  It would be nice if all servers were on equal hosting providers, but some providers hosting official servers are just terrible, and Wild Card doesn't seem to care.
I was on a server that ran pretty good, but it was under constant DDoD attack for a month straight leaving it down a majority of the time.  When it was up, it ran pretty damn good.  The past week, they changed providers, and while the server is always up now, the lag is so bad, it might as well be down.  This is with just 3 peope online in early mornings.  Have no idea how the server is suppose to handle 70 people.
While a majority of the servers are probably 'fine,' I just can't support a company that doesn't get some kind of Service Level Agreement with the companies hosting it's servers.  I have a 35-45ms ping to the IP address of the server, but in-game it feels like I'm playing with a 900ms ping as the same time as downloading a large while (which is not happening). This is going to be a long review so for the tl;dr version check the bottom of this wall of text.
I was initially not impressed with the idea of a free to play game about aliens fighting other aliens or zombie-like aliens in space but this is not what this game is about.
From the first few hours this game won me over. The graphics were beyond anything I'd ever seen in a free to play game, the controls and abilities were really easy to pick up and get used to them and the missions are pretty straightforward.
When you start, you have the option to choose between 3 Warframes as they are called, which is somewhat like choosing a class with different abilities and passives etc. but not exactly. Since my friends started playing this game a couple of days before I picked it up, I chose the 3rd option for the sake of diversity but it proved to be the best choice I could make for my liking.
So we play some missions and I get the hang of it, this game really is beautiful. The combat animations are different and may vary from weapon type (one handed, two handed heavy weapons, pistols, shotguns, bows etc.). The graphics as I said, were beyond anything I had ever seen. I kept wondering how can a free to play game be so beautiful. The display/graphics options had a lot to offer, with many switches to toggle on and off to customize your performance, I was impressed to see how good the game was optimized as I was running Medium settings 1080p @ 120fps (R9 280).
After the first 20-30 hours you may find that the missions are repetitive but frankly I was okay with it.
As for the in-game market. It's a trap. Do not-and I can't stretch this enough- spend your starting platinum-which is the game's second currency bought with money from the store- on cosmetic stuff. The best use of your starting platinum, in my opinion, would be Warframe slots. Warframe slots are needed so that you can own more Warframes, they cost 20 platinum each and you will most definitely need them. Also, most of the stuff from the market are ridiculously expensive, for example Fusion Cores. A three-Fusion Core bundle in the market costs 80p the rought equivalent of 5$. BUT, if you trade with other players, you can get 80 Fusion Cores with the same amount of money, because they cost nearly nothing (credit to STAR_).
Also, the Warframe wiki may come in very handy for any questions that may arise through your gameplay. Lots of info about drop rates, mods, warframes and anything you can imagine, so keep that in mind.
To sum this up aka
: Warframe is a unique and distinguishable free to play game with surprising aspects on its gameplay and beautiful graphics. It is definitely worth trying it out if you enjoy third person games, shooters, rpgs and mmos. The in-game market has a lot of cosmetic stuff and weapons/equipment but nearly everything can be acquired by playing the game so beware with your purchases. The Warframe wiki is an incredibly useful tool throughout your gameplay experience.

(Sorta tl;dr last 2 paragraphs) Ok so Warframe is honestly good on its surface. Its fun and action packed, tons of things to collect. Im not gonna ride the wagon of 'theres no true end-game' like everyone does. Although said fact is true, lets be real, its a F2P.
What I AM gonna rant about however is how much of a mess the game currently is. Looking beyond the surface gets you thinking, God knows why, but the devs seem to be TRYING to slowly run this ship aground.
1) Actual new content takes way too long to pop out, with literally every new anticipated release (be it weapon or skin or quest) being delayed multiple times, before finally getting released. Even after all that, the end product is guranteed to be buggy and/or completely lackluster OR completely gamebreaking, rendering hours of hardwork done previously completely pointless as something else stupidly more powerful replaces your craft, OR completely pointless as the new release is utter crap.
2) There are so many gameplay flaws that have been discussed by the community for literal years, so many of said problems already have potential excellent (simple) solutions requested by the community that could make a HUGE impact on the game. INSTEAD of merely listening, poorly thought out 'new' mechanics are introduced, most of these being obvious blatant ways of forcing us players to spend more time on the game. Stretching out every task players must make for progress instead of making said content better and worthwhile.
3) It. Is. Repititive. Only one way to achieve your goal, didnt get it? Do it again until you do. Why are you getting it? So you can use it to get other goals. Thats literally all it is, plus each goal achieved can branch out numerous other kinds of repitive grind of its own. The repititive system itself repeats itself.
And these are just the MAIN problems. What  makes this worse is that the devs present themselves as people who care for their playerbase but do nothing to solve issues, instead, they constantly abuse and decieve the community for personal gain. It needs profits, yeah, but it can do that without making a fool out of themselves and dishonouring long time supporters.
With that being said, it is clear that Warframe is slowly shaping into the typical F2P problem that exists too much these days. I wouldnt say this game isnt fun, at times its superb, I wouldnt ask people to not play it, its a dopamine inducing addiction spree that satisfies temporary egoistical desires, and to some people thats the best part. Even I played it because of this. But Warframe opened my eyes to the reality of many games, a mere cycle for cheap joys that WILL get you hooked and WILL eventually leave you feeling empty later on, making you stare at the hours spent, realising how wasted all that time was.
I for one am surely done with that for good.

Warframe is the pet project of Digital Extreme, the canadian development team that has been behind the Unreal series, Bioshock and The Darkness 2 (along with Homefront which was still a good game overall despite its many flaws). A cooperative third person shooter with impressive visuals and art style, refined parkour and mobility options as well as an interesting take on sci-fi, it is one of the most active, successful and evolving game on the F2P market.
Set in the far future of the darkSector universe, the solar system is now in a constant war between the conquering Grineer and the merchant guilds of the Corpus while also brushing off the Infested, remnants of a bio-weapon from the past. In this age of conflict, An order of warriors who were thought to have disappeared come back at the request of an entity known only as the Lotus. The Tenno are awakened from their slumber anew, their powers only matched by their mastery of the Warframes
Being a free to play title, this question will always come at the forefront of people's mind. Put simply, let's take in consideration what "Pay to Win" entails : the term signifies that a game allows paying customers to
than non-paying customers with no option for the non-paying customers to match this power equitably.
Warframe does not, in fact, allow paying customers to gain such power. In fact, most of the exclusively paying content of Warframe lies in cosmetics alternatives like skins, color sets, accessories and such. While you 'can' purchase some weapons, Warframe and such with platinum (the paid currency in the game), these are also obtainable through seeking out the equipment's blueprints and parts then crafting them into the desired items.
Even more so, many of the Prime equipment (more embellished version of the regular gear) cannot be bought outright except outside of a Prime Access offer which allows paying customers to gain a set of gear corresponding to the most recent Prime Warframe released. Even so, the difference lies that those who purchase a Prime Access do get a few cosmetics atop of the already obtainable Warframe and weapons through regular play.
Moreover, the Platinum currency is often used in ingame trading between players as the mean to buy Prime equipment part blueprints and other such tradeable ressources. Thus, the Warframe economy works on a supply and demand system where gaining rare parts and mods (more about this later) can be then be exchanged to other players in order to gain Platinum without personally spending money.
Firstly, Warframe is a constantly evolving game that has been nearly three years running. The game that it was in closed beta (where I got the first chance to play) has changed so very much that many that returns to the game today find it an almost completely different experience. From the game being now more approachable to having added many features that the community suggested to even revamping entire systems already in place for others that expand the gameplay greatly :
As a free to play game, there is the required incentive for players to pay for things they could get for free by playing, aka a "time wall". For one, crafting of most weapons and Warframes isn't instantaneous and usually can be counted in hours and, in case of an entire Warframe build, days (aka 12 hours per part, which can be done simultaneously, then a 3 day build for the final combination of the parts into a Warframe). Along these are some of the few points that might vary depending on the player's opinion on them :
Warframe will appeal to those who wish to play a shooter with satisfying firearm and melee combat mechanics, flashy powers that are varied and unique to every Warframe. While the loot drops and slight grindiness can be a turn off, it is often offset by just how the gameplay feels fluid and intuitive to get into.

Ark Survival Evolved has a lot of potential, whether or not Wild Card ( WC from here on out ) has the ability to truly capitalize on it is yet to be determined. So far my experience has been mixed to the extremes, at times it can be very fun and at other times so frustating that it forces me quit playing the game for months.  It's in early developement, a bold face lie if you ask me, but it's such at such a slow pace that it makes me question if part of the problem is that they have too many artist and not enough actual coders. As a result content is slow to come out and bugs tend to stick around, however they have slightly gotten better about this, not much better but still better than they once had been. I play solely on an official Primitive plus server, because despite how much slower the modded server is to the normal version of the game the balance just feels so much better. I bring that up because one of my biggest gripes with Ark is how WC seems to have a habbit of fixing aspects of the game by adding more end game stuff, which in turn makes it more difficult for those joining a server with pre-established tribes. Another gripe of mine is how it feels like most creatures just have way too much HP and that there's a huge desparity between the usefullness of a level 5 dino and a level 100, sure there should be some but not as much as there is. Then there's the servers themselves, I do not know if it's the servers or the netcode but lag, desync, hitching, freezing, and client time outs are a huge issue. I cannot begin to count the number of times I have been killed due my client freezing just long enough for the creature I'm fighting/taming to get close enough to attack and kill me without being able to do anything about it.
That being said, Ark is possibly the most polished and playable of the First / Third Person persistent survival experiences, which says a lot about the genre on a whole.
The reasons I cannot reccommend this game is simple, it's no where near balanced, it lacks stability, and WC has yet to show any inclination on changing any of that any time soon. So unless you're a person who enjoys a survival expereince that is very front loaded in terms of difficulty, both natural and artificial, and have the ability to enjoy springing back from constant and overwhelming defeat, then you're not likely going to find this game fun for very long.

This review is focused on comparing Warframe to a somewhat similar game, Destiny.
Warframe shares a lot of ideas with Destiny, but in my honest opinion has been executed far better than Destiny. I am saying this out of experience, having played just over 650 hours of Destiny on PS4.
The big differences and comparisons I have picked up on between these two games are that:
-Warframe is f2p, while Destiny will cost you over $150 if not $250 due to all of the 'DLCs and             Expansions' to play.
-The PvP in Warframe is roughly tacked on and isn't that popular, as it is not supposed to be a big part of the game. Destiny has come to revolve around PvP which I think sucks as they are both supposedly co-op RPGs but Destiny really does not play much like one.
-They are both loot and grind focused but in Destiny once you get the 'best' three or four weapons you don't really grind for loot anymore. In Warframe grinding and obtaining new gear actually remains relevant as you get mastery points from leveling up gear which in turn levels your account up, unlocking more gear to obtain and level, as well as new missions for you to play.
-In Warframe clans actually do important stuff, like provide access to otherwise restricted gear, unlike in Destiny when they are just displayed under your name so people think you look cool.
I have so much more I could say, but I really wanted to keep this review short and concise. In my experience I have found Warframe to be better than Destiny in many ways, but both can be boring so if you excessively play WF I would recommend playing with friends, makes it a lot more enjoyable.

Jail/handcuffs. While I think this is a neat feature, it needs to be temporary. There needs to be a cool down feature or something. Imagine having your 1000+ hours into the game on one character, get that character captured and have no way to get out of jail. This also leads me back to the toxic community as most alpha tribe believe in torture in the form of leaving a secondary character logged in and having music or profanity blasted through local chat standing outside the cage. This is just one example.
Tame time is to long- Why does it only take an hour to tame a level 10 T-rex but 4 hours to tame a level 10 anklyo. I spent 12 hours taming a level 150 parcer one time. The new tame times have been reduced but not much. expect 6-8 hours on most high level tames if you don't have kibble.
Egg drop times are too long.
Day 1 bugs still around--- Belongings falling through the earth. Dinosaurs disappearing from your taming pen. Dinosaurs spawing into your base. servers rubberbanding. Building placement glitch. These are some of the worse but there are many more.
Cross server transfers--While interesting at first, it quickly became evident that this is a problem. 1000 hours that I played were on only one official server. The rest were boucing around trying to help other people after my server was taken over. It was much more enjoyable to build a nemisis on one server that you could constantly battle. Sometimes it was three against one. I feel like they could have added environmental distruction instead of cross server transfers that would have made server more balanced. Imagine a tornado knocking out your turrets or breaking down a wall. Our server was overrun by a tribe of 50+ members. Most servers are 70 players capped. This means that only a handfull of members were able to log in and defend their homes during the super raids.
Cheating--Battle eye does nothing but take up memory. I don't have a video capture so I couldn't record it, but our entire server would send wildcard a message when this happened. Cheat engines are widely available for this game and used all the time. The cheating I've seen has been shooting through walls killing tames, going under the map and destorying the base from underneath. walking through walls, duplicating tames and items. I'm not sure if the PS4 or xbox has these problems. Wildcard states that it needs to be captured in order for there to be any action. This could be avoided if they had dedicated admins (I'm expecting this to change after official release)
Overall for me because I like a challenge and play on official PvP servers. I don't recommend this game in it's current state. Definitely wait and come back. If you enjoy single Player or PvE then by all means try this game out. PvP is the bread and butter of Ark. Fingers crossed that these problems will get fixed.

After clocking almost 1300 hours into ARK, i think its finally time i made a review of it, so here goes nothin'
I should preface this by saying that it is a borderline necessity to play this with a group either through LFG or better yet, a group of friends. Some of my best moments in this game were in the company of my friends, and ARK really provides a platform for some brilliant and genuinely funny moments. So outside of humour, what does ARK bring to the table as a survival game?
PROS:
- VERY addictive gameplay. You get out what you put in, and while i see this as a pro, its a double edged blade, and i understand why a few will see this as a negative
- Healthy unofficial community. Contrary to what Reddit may have you think, the unofficials are the place to be. Official is dominated by griefer tribes and tyrannical alphas so avoid like the plague. A server with good admins, and a good community is something truly special (even if your being raided)
- Pokemon esque gameplay. Though this is billed as a survival game, id argue it as being a pseudo MMO. The grind is very much palpable in this game, and you reaaaaaly get out what you put in. Getting up at 6 in the morning may mean the stat difference needed for your T Rex to be able to come out on top in a skirmish, and much like things like  Pokemon, you’ll be vying to catch em' all ( don’t sue me plz )
CONS:
- Don’t expect to play official now unless you have a platoon ready to invade a server, griefers, hackers, and tyrants run amok in these servers and while there a few decent ones, your always at risk of an incursion from some less than friendly folk.
- As a survival game the balance is awful to put it plainly. The early game is PUNISHING, with virtual minibosses such as the Therizinosaurus, and the Raptor on steroids known as the Troodon menacing the beaches of ARK. Saying early game is tough is not doing it justice, and take it from me, unless you expand quickly, be prepared to die, like, a lot.
To further enforce this, the late game is also trivial too. None spoiling mushrooms that stack to over 99 will solve all food issues, high tier armour wards of attacks from all but the deadliest of creatures, and the animals you tame and breed become boss fights in their own regard. The mid game for me is where ARK shines as a survival game, but this changes very fast once you start to tame Rex's and Argents.
CONCLUSION:
From my prior points, you may be under the impression im somewhat salty with ARK, im not. In terms of game time it’s only thwarted by DayZ Mod, the titan of survival games, and im a sucker for anything dinosaur. But the experience I have playing this game is none I’ve had before. Maybe im just sad, but the reward of perfecting a bloodline of Rex's fit for our servers PVE arena, is something few games come close to hitting, and when the time to fight comes, boy are the stakes high.
I treat ARK as a pseudo MMO because that’s what i believe ARK is, at least late game. Treat it that way and a lot of ARK's issues can be overlooked, especially if you play unofficial. I truly believe that out of the cess pit of early access, ARK will be the one to rise to the top and release properly, and i VERY much so look forward to seeing what the finished product in a few months’ time.
As for arbitrary score, im gonna give ARK a 7/10. The game has flaws and issues aplenty, but for me PERSONALLY rather than professionally, i can overlook these issues and enjoy the game at heart, so if you’re accustomed to survival games, I’d recommend ARK. To quote John Hammond, "it’s right up your alley ;)"
Cheers for Reading!

i would say that it could go either way, it's both a good game and in some ways a bad one. i was MR 13 when i gave up. (a bit better now in my opinion)
Pros:
lots of content to hunt for, (even more now, it even have CATS!)
from what i encountered it has a good community, quite friendly. (likely haven't changed)
everything except the starting gear is viable for use at any point in the game so a favorite weapon or frame can be used but there are some that make it easier. (depending on your build even the starting weapons can be used somewhat later on)
you "can" play it for free if you have the time to put into it. it was how i played it, mostly because i waited for the 75% disscount. (by using another site for trading free to play is a bit more manageble)
it has responsive movement controls, it rarely did something i had not intended it to do.
Cons:
the most obvius one, the grind, if you want something very specific it can be impossible to get it simply from RNG, one of the last things i went for before it felt it wasen't worth the time anymore was the Archwing weapons, a low droprate and missions that weren't fun to do alone, interception or defense mainly, even sabotage was boring. (some of the grind is changed with the new drop system, archwing might still be bad though)
the way the monetization is done is in most ways good, but because you need to buy slots to have more than i think 3 warframes and 7?weapons at the start you have to spend quite sometime in tradechat and that is not fun, mostly people spam their offers at the earliest time possible swamping the rest of it, making finding the offer you wanted or trying to contact them a hassle, (can use another site to make bids/offer and leave it alone, don't know if they changed it since i left)
the way the missions are done everything except spy and sabotage take significantly longer to do and in some cases are impossible without very specific tricks, (naramon school is currently a bit broken and is the only reliable way to do some things solo) and every event i participated in was close to impossible for me to do at the time without teamates, and with a less than dessired internet i often got dissconected from host and booted back to my ship, everything done in the mission to that point is lost. and the last event, with a boss that had homing attacks and required you to hack enemies to damage him (meaning you stand still and is completely defensless) made it impossible to get anywhere. (probably a major pain still but now that endless missions aren't much use Naramon isn't an issue really.)
to get higher Mastery Rank you have to level up weapons and warframes by taking them into missions but most missions are so bad for it that you have to do a few specific missions to get anywhere in decent time, i know MR is pointless past a certain point but with my personality i couldn't just waste experience or skip things that had a completed state, (MR have a point now)
The Codex both one of my biggest joys and worst dissapointments, there are a few things in it that are ridiculuss rare to find and any time i did find them they were stuck behind something blocking them of,i found 3 in my total playtime and i looked for them and none of them i could scan. really annoying. (still likely a problem with scanning, but with the vaccom update loot can be reached now even without carrier)
to make it short, it is fun for a time but after a point you will only farm for Focus/MR experience and no longer take any enjoyment in the game itself, you can't even "finish" the achivements as there is no way to get to MR 30 or whatever the final rank is as there isn't enough equipment in the game yet. (with the changes more missions are viable and feel like less of a grind)
for me id rather have left earlier, as there was to much time needed to be put aside for it. limited timed loot drops kept me from doing anytine that required time and such i wasen't really doing anything most of the time. quite pointless now. (not as much an issue now)
Edit: as they have made some updates now that changes some of the things i found annoying, MR now have a point (higher mod limit from rank 0), you get rewards even if you disconect from host (a big thing that annoyed me), with the exception of some rare encounters scanning have been made easier with a scan weapon so the small enemies aren't a problem, universal vacoom so even if rare containers are behind walls can still be reached (the few times it happened they were within a few meters 1-3? maybe), more missions are viable for exp/focus. so with these changes i give it a possitive and may even get back in when i have the time. (might have been overly harsh earlier, but doing that boss solo was a nightmare)

Ark...Where to start
TL:DR
Lots of fun
Beautiful
Constantly updated
Devs seem to give a crap
Server lag issues need resolving but at Alpha this wont be top of their priorities!
The Premise of the game (in a nut shell) is this.
You wake up on a deserted Island with nothing but a loin cloth and have to try and survive as best you can.
Cons
You wait through the "waking on a beach" intro, "WOW this is a beautiful place" you think to yourself. only to turn around and get your♥♥♥♥♥chewed of by a massive crocodile with worse teeth than Shane MacGowen.
The lag, sometimes you will be hitting a tree and about 10 seconds later hit a bloody trike which will instantly kill you without any problem!
Server issues - as follows
1) You choose a server and log in - Someone has already claimed the area and walled the whole area off - no choice but to kill yourself or find a new server
2) You choose a different location - first thing you need to do is find somewhere safe away from the above Pogue and take down a couple of trees and build a camp fire...but wait...some nublet has placed pillars the entire length of the beach and your only option is to head inland...which is never a good idea at level 1!
3) PvP - Alpha tribes will kill you...even if they seem friendly at first.
4) Bit naughty about the paid DLC at Alpha stage - but once one person has the DLC they can transfer pretty much all the important stuff to Vanilla and share it with their tribe
The good
1) Its a s*** ton of fun once you find a decent area to set up base away from Shane macCrocChops
2) The graphics on the dinos/landscapes/everything are stunning
3) The devs are constantly updating and adding to the game
4) Outside of PvP the community is (in my opinion) the nicest I've seen in any multiplayer game (I dont think i have joined a PvE server yet where someone on a massive lizard hasnt dropped of a crap ton of food for me...even though I have nowhere to store it and it will all rot real quick
5) Its regularly at a price where those on a budget can get it without much risk
6) so much crafting...and the way it is done makes you think about which equipment you need more than others because you cant learn everything (may seem like a bad thing, but trust me, its a beautiful addition)
7) Even with the server lag you can see the ping replies of realms so can make an informed decission as to which one will run smoothest for a bit

(Sorta tl;dr last 2 paragraphs) Ok so Warframe is honestly good on its surface. Its fun and action packed, tons of things to collect. Im not gonna ride the wagon of 'theres no true end-game' like everyone does. Although said fact is true, lets be real, its a F2P.
What I AM gonna rant about however is how much of a mess the game currently is. Looking beyond the surface gets you thinking, God knows why, but the devs seem to be TRYING to slowly run this ship aground.
1) Actual new content takes way too long to pop out, with literally every new anticipated release (be it weapon or skin or quest) being delayed multiple times, before finally getting released. Even after all that, the end product is guranteed to be buggy and/or completely lackluster OR completely gamebreaking, rendering hours of hardwork done previously completely pointless as something else stupidly more powerful replaces your craft, OR completely pointless as the new release is utter crap.
2) There are so many gameplay flaws that have been discussed by the community for literal years, so many of said problems already have potential excellent (simple) solutions requested by the community that could make a HUGE impact on the game. INSTEAD of merely listening, poorly thought out 'new' mechanics are introduced, most of these being obvious blatant ways of forcing us players to spend more time on the game. Stretching out every task players must make for progress instead of making said content better and worthwhile.
3) It. Is. Repititive. Only one way to achieve your goal, didnt get it? Do it again until you do. Why are you getting it? So you can use it to get other goals. Thats literally all it is, plus each goal achieved can branch out numerous other kinds of repitive grind of its own. The repititive system itself repeats itself.
And these are just the MAIN problems. What  makes this worse is that the devs present themselves as people who care for their playerbase but do nothing to solve issues, instead, they constantly abuse and decieve the community for personal gain. It needs profits, yeah, but it can do that without making a fool out of themselves and dishonouring long time supporters.
With that being said, it is clear that Warframe is slowly shaping into the typical F2P problem that exists too much these days. I wouldnt say this game isnt fun, at times its superb, I wouldnt ask people to not play it, its a dopamine inducing addiction spree that satisfies temporary egoistical desires, and to some people thats the best part. Even I played it because of this. But Warframe opened my eyes to the reality of many games, a mere cycle for cheap joys that WILL get you hooked and WILL eventually leave you feeling empty later on, making you stare at the hours spent, realising how wasted all that time was.
I for one am surely done with that for good.

This is an update review for february 2, 2017 my last up was  september 8th 2016.
So my last review was a negative review to ark. The hole controversy with the scorched earth dlc has died down and now its time for an update. My last review I talked about how I loved ark and how it's awesome but it still needs work. But with the scorched earth dlc being you had to pay for it when ark is a EA title did not sit well with me.
Now for the updated review (I play on a private server. I played on official but it was not my cup of tea)
As it says above there I play on a private server pve and never really played pvp much because its not my cup of tea. As for ark I find it more fun when you play with friends on a private server that way you play when you want and it does not feel like a chore to play, so in my opinion private server is the best to go.
Now on to the pro's about ark
You can tame dino's: Each dino brings something to the table. There are one's that can help you build by getting resources, attack dino's to attack/defend and some are just for pack mules. But the main pro to ark is you can mate dino's and ride them. I think we can all agree that's a big pro.
You can build: Yes you can build a house of your very own and not just a house. You can make a farm to keep your dodo birds in, make a green house for your plants or just make a base for your tribe. Building is fun and customizable.
Tribe's: Tribe's are like clans in mmorpgs like world of warcraft or guild wars 2 but really tribe's to me is more of a community. You have to work together and get along or it just does not work. Some time's things go well and others it does not. It can make ark more fun to join a tribe but its not a must.
Character customization: You can make your character male or female, hair color, skin color and body look how ever you want.
New hair mechanic: It's cool you can cut your hair/facial to what style they have available and use that hair to make it into something.
Breedings dino's: Ever wanted to have a baby t-rex and raise it to a big t-rex? Now you can with the breeding system. It's kind of like...pokemon for say. You can breed two dino's to get a really good dino in return. Or you can just breed dino's for a friend.
Level system: As you gather things, make things, kill dino's and some time's...just sit there you will gains levels both you and your dino's. As you level up you up your stats of you and your dino's. As you level up you get points to learn something new to make and points to up your stats. Each stats does something to help you survive, like more stamina means you can run longer and movement speed determines how fast your run/walk.
Now for the cons
It's not a easy game: To me this a good thing and makes me work hard for what I want but for other's not so much. Things are not given to you and you really need to work hard to get what you want.
Not much of a tutorial: Well....there is none really. It just throws you out there and you have to survive. I would look up a guide before playing
Optimization: It's not to bad for me but others it can be a pain. Keep in mine there working on it but they can do a lot better in my opinion.
Bug's and crashes: Yeah this game is a EA game so there will be bugs and the game can crash. It's ok for me but others it can very.
Officical server: This is not really a bad thing but at the same time I hate when on a offcical server some guy puts pillars all around the land so you cant build.
Transfer system: Now for me this is good because I play on a pve private server but for other's on pvp offcical server's its hell. I have not seen it with my own eye's but from what I have herd and seen in video's people do not like this. What this means is you can take all your op dinos and gear to another server and just take over and make everyone's day a living hell. It's good for some but it seems most people don't like this feature.
You lose everything on death: I can live with this and at time's it makes me think twice about doing something but this can be a turn off for some. You donlt lose your XP or stats on death so your good there.
Diseases: There is a sickness on ark called swamp fever. It makes all your stats go down by 20% and even on death it does not go away as far as I know. You need a cure or leveling up your health attribute removes the sickness so it says on the WIKI
Payed DLC for an EA game: It's not a good idea to have payed dlc for a game that is still not out of EA but some time's it can work.
My thoughts on Ark
Well I really enjoy ark and all of my time is spent on a private server and some might say that will obscure my view on the game but hey if thats what makes ark fun then so be it. I did say on my last review that I gave ark a negative review because  of the payed DLC scorched earth and how it's unacceptable to have DLC for a EA game. But I did get scorched earth on sale and after a few trys and a sale its not bad. I would wait for a sale to get the DLC though.
But I think the best thing about ark is that I made some good friends that are very close to me and that is the best part about ark to me, that I found people that even though we are in different countries it feels more like were best friends then anything.

A game with a lot of potential, ruined by extremely poor balancing and the faux-MMO system of interserver transfer. The game has an extremely sharp curve off from the early to late game, with large quantities of resources necessary to break through. All tiers of buildings below Metal can be destroyed en masse by the Mid-Game and above equipment, creating a heavy incentive for players on servers to relentlessly hunt and destroy all other players on the server.
The game's servers also have a Transfer System, where players may transfer characters and equipment from one server to another en masse, allowing sudden and massed invasions. Combined with little to no support for the Offline Raid Protection mode, even the most stable and amicable of servers can be wiped clean and replaced with hyper-agressive tribes while people are in bed or at work.
Quite simply, there is no early game here - Players in the mid to late game are in absolute control, and typically use this position to intentionally drive other players away from the game. The developers' response to this issue is to add more higher-tier equipent that renders the balance even more lopsided - The previews of the upcoming Tek Tier release showed players in the new, higher-tier power armour destroying early game player's structures by walking through them. Unless you know someone who already owns the game and plays in a powerful tribe, don't bother with this game.

PROS:
- Great graphics
- More polish than a lot of early access games
- Enjoyable gameplay with a pretty decent GUI
- Many, many mods
- Full of features
NEUTRAL??:
- Has DLC? Yes, this EARLY ACCESS, UNFINISHED game has FULL PRICE DLC!! This does not mean the developers have abandonded this game without the DLC, nor do they think the game is finished in its current state. It is just an opportunity to make more money (hopefully to fund more development for the base game) and they took it.
CONS:
- Loading times (especially with mods installed)
- MMO servers have very toxic people who go around destroying your hard work
- Performance may be an issue for most people. I, however, have a high-ish-end PC (i7 6700k 4.4GHz, GTX 1070 OV, 16GB RAM, 2560x1080p monitor) and if I manage the settings well, I can run mostly on high and get a solid 45+ FPS. It is not just do to the fact it's not 100% optimised yet, it IS A VERY DEMANDING GAME. However, I have heard that on lower end systems on the low settings that it still doesn't run well. You should probably expect less from early access games in general.
- Bugs; this includes having to regedit my default GPU settings so the graphics driver doesn't think it's crashed trying to load Ark, sometimes it'll just crash either to the desktop or my whole PC, but again it is to be expected.
TLDR:
It is a good game for someone with a > mid-tier PC who doesn't intent playing with 40-odd people on a public server. If you're fine playing by yourself or with a few friends (or however many you like on a private server) then give it a go, especially when the game goes on sale.

The latest patch seemed to address my main issue with the game, which is optimization. I have a relatively powerful computer (its not a super rig, but it was built to play games) and it seemed that I had to adjust the video settings to the lowest settings possible to get anything other than a slideshow framerate. Since the latest update, I can run the game with everything but view distance maxed out (the view distance slider doesnt really affect the view distance, but rather the distance smaller objects pop in to view) at a pretty solid 30FPS as opposed to the 10-14 I was getting before.
I don't have a huge amount of play time, and I cant review the online aspects of the game as I havent dared touch them outside of playing on a non-dedicated server with 3 other friends (yes, the limit for players on a non-dedicated server is 4). The game does have a number of horrifically frustrating bugs, the AI is pretty garbage, and joining friends can be difficult a lot of the time. If you can learn to live with this (yes this is an EARLY ACCESS game, and if you feel like throwing a negative review at the game for technical issues, the only thing I can say is you payed for it, knowing what Early Access means, and if you didn't, thats on you), the crafting system is extremely addictive and fun, the leveling system is compelling, and taming your first dino feels incredibly satisfying. Be prepared to smash your keyboard; you will die a lot, lose your items a lot, and your dinos you have grown to love will get killed on a whim the second you're not looking, but hey, this is a survival game and that's what it's all about right?
I think the community's main problem with the game is that they love it, and they want to see it finished. Too many projects have never left early access and been cancelled, so naturally everyone is wary of early access. This is a very ambitions game, and people seem to expect triple A quality from it, but this is an indie game. I really feel that people are holding expectations that are too high, and are going to end up disappointed. Do I agree with releasing DLC before the game is finished? No, but the devs really do seem passionate about the game, and as kids who loved dinos I know we all as a community are too, but we need to keep our expectations in check.
