This review isn't so much an issue with the game itself but more with the problems of Steam.
If you are wondering if this game is any good, it is. Even after 100+ hours, I feel like I have barely scratched the surface of this game. The melee combat is visceral and the gunplay is satisfying. More than that, the game is being actively updated with hotfixes every week. You can really tell that this game was made with care and passion. Also, this game is by no means play to win. Every gameplay aspect of this game can be unlocked through the game.
However, I would recommend this game if you download it directly from the Warframe website. I have recently faced numerous problems with my warframe files being completely wiped from my computer for no reason. For example, I played the game for 2 hours in the afternoon. I turned off my computer and went for another few hours only to come back to my Warframe game being removed from the library. I have checked the file directory and it seems it has completely been deleted for no reason at all. There are other numerous reports about this issue and it seems to stem from the fact that Steam stores and older version of this game so when the files are updated, Steam doesn't recognize them and wipes them.
Once again, I really do enjoy this game. I haven't this much fun with a game in a long time. But I must stress the fact that Steam has a major problem with Warframe right now.

TLDR: PVE = The best shooter(with melee). Collectionist? Great game!  PVP? Dont Bother! Grinding? Yes!
Parkour? Much! Content: All free, updates often! Cash shop? Expensive! Some gear can be bought outright but its pricey and doesnt effect other players at all!
I've been playing this since Beta days, given I haven't always been playing, there have been multi-month breaks at times. IMHO this is what Destiny should be at the fraction of the production cost. Its a shooter with lots of different weapons that vary greatly, powered by Mods which can enchance your weapon and make it completely different from the next guy's. The melee weapons (my favorite) are viable and effective, you can use a melee weapon exclusively and get by for a good 90% of the game, some bosses and archwing content excluded.
Which speaking of archwings, they have space combat via jetpacks which offer their own unique weapons, its still in its infancy so there isnt a terrible amount of content...but it is still well made.
Being completely forward the game can be grindy, if you want specific gear (like prime parts) you will have to farm for it, and RNG is well, RNG. The beauty of it is you honestly dont need it to play the game competently and have fun, its more for the collectionists or lovers of all that is shiny.

Throughout gameplay, I have a soft spot for Dinos. This is one of those games you either love or completely hate. I personally do not like it. The developers are very arrogant and the community hates them. This game started off as a fun survival Rust & Minecraft like game but with beautiful graphics and tameable beasts/dinos. I personally liked it to begin with but I later noticed the developers had no idea what they were doing. First it started with DLC --- Scorched Earth was a let down, not because it wasn't fun but because it was DLC in early access. This blew some people's minds, imagine a brand new game with paid-for DLC. Then the devs added the ability to transfer dinos from one place to another. This is just horrid gameplay mechanics. You can start off and already destroy people and npc dinos without even the basic pickaxe. Now, they made the STILL early access game 60$.
This is an abomination for players that still do not own it, for it was 30$ just a few months ago. The Devs have still yet to omptimize the gameplay. It is laggy like hell if you do not own a 600$ graphics card or 64gig ram. This grinds my gears; they should focus on actual ability to play rather than gameplay alone. Instead of increasing gameplay and having an influx in money focus more on the gameplay addives and remarkable graphics do not make up for lack of actual community. I reccomend this game to only close friends to play with. I'd rather keep the money in my own pockets and buy a game like Grand Theft Auto 5 or Rust.

ARK, the one game I can literally say I've had a love-hate relationship with.
I've got some history with this game, back before Lystrosaurus was a thing. Even from the very beginning, I wanted to tear my hair out. Couldn't stay alive, couldn't get used to the inventory, couldn't understand the fact that this game was unforgiving, and unceremonious. It took forever to build anything, and I always felt weak in the world so willing to see me dead.
Advice to new players: You will die, a lot. Your tamed, bred, and beloved dinosaurs will die. You'll make mistakes, you'll lose your gear, and you'll want to stop playing altogether. All of these ideas and situations have crossed me at some point, and yet I've got right around 300 hours logged in the game. Sometimes it's due to ridiculous game mechanics, and other times it's your fault. A nice analog to real-life, no?
This is by far the most punishing game I've ever played. For some people it's Dark Souls, but Dark Souls has a formula, and once you find that formula, the game becomes quite a bit easier. ARK doesn't give you that, and instead chucks you into the wilderness with your fists and says "screw you".
If you can believe it, these game elements are those that I love, and are a far cry from those I hate. I love a game that doesn't hold your hand. I love a game that is punishingly difficult. What I don't love, is an unoptimized mess, which ARK undoubtedly is. I think AMD card owners have it worse off, but from what I've read about, and seen, more than a few people have been having system memory issues, graphical glitches, crashes, slow-downs, low FPS, etc.
Personally, on a brand new AMD card, I've had to turn down most of the settings and halve my resolution in windowed mode to get it to run above 40 FPS. I don't think this is okay, and I urge the developers to at least address and recognize these issues, which I wholly think they have.
Which brings me to the point: The developers are 100% aware of your issues, and they won't fix them right away. Why? Getting to a state that is content complete is mind-bogglingly easier that trying to optimize a game that isn't even finished yet, or trying to optimize a game after every content patch. Remember that whole "early access" label on the game before you bought it? All of these people demanding the developers fix their performance problems apparently don't understand this concept. I complain too, I'm guilty of that, sure. It's natural for us to lash out when frustrated, but we should have known what we were getting into.
I know now that I'm just going to have to deal with the performance degradation and issues. The developers have made an outstanding game. The mechanics are easily some of the most fun I've had the pleasure of experiencing in an open world RPG. In fact they're down right innovative.
I see so many thumbs down reviews from players with /thousands/ of hours played. That's just nonsense -- no game you play for even 100 hours could be labeled as "bad" or "not worth it". I think it would behoove these people to take the game for what it is, an early access open world rpg with dinosaurs, and get on knowing you had the chance to play a game like this in your lifetime.

Friends I know spend more time keeping everything they've established up and protected than enjoying the game.
That being said, there is honestly not much to enjoy in this game. With a group of friends you can easily hit endgame without triggering the Alpha (assuming the Alpha tribe is not a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥). However, the optimization is poor, the servers have issues, the community is toxic and, yes... a paid expansion which shifts the balance even more during Early Access is not ethical. I did not enjoy the expansion, but felt it was a necessity to keep up with competition. In that regard, well done, Wild Card.
Eventually, our efforts proved to be futile however as level caps were raised rendering your hours of breeding and taming of exquisite animals (such as Wyverns) naught. Cross Ark transfers were opened, despite that function having a notorious and horrible history. You see, people who don't know history are doomed to repeat it... And yet Wild Card repeats that history willingly and fully aware of the consequences.
Yes, the game does have a steady release of patches and content, but all of that is merely throwing glitter and shine over manure. The core game is broken, the experience is terrible and all that new content is simply adding more Arkemon to add to your virtually messed up Jurassic Ark. It's a distraction, and nothing more.
My sincere advice: buy this game AND its expansion when it's in a huge sale (<10€) if you have friends to play and explore with and if you can forgive performance issues.
If you're intending on building something huge in harsh environments to leave a legacy, forget about it, you'll never make it unless you have a gaming community of over 140 people blindly following you. No exaggeration.
Finally, if you wonder how I've got > 1.000 hours in this game despite not fully enjoying it; I was more busy helping my friends than doing anything useful myself (such as taming, for example). They needed help to farm, I'd provide it while being semi-AFK. I've lost interest in this game since a long time, but only that kept me going.

Its a shooter with lots of different weapons that vary greatly, powered by Mods which can enchance your weapon and make it completely different from the next guy's. The melee weapons (my favorite) are viable and effective, you can use a melee weapon exclusively and get by for a good 90% of the game, some bosses and archwing content excluded.

Being completely forward the game can be grindy, if you want specific gear (like prime parts) you will have to farm for it, and RNG is well, RNG. The beauty of it is you honestly dont need it to play the game competently and have fun, its more for the collectionists or lovers of all that is shiny.

This game is f***ing amazing and heres why:
It is not pay to win. At. ALL. You can get everything in the game just by playing. No exclusives for people that pay a bunch of money. If you like a certain weapon and think it looks cool then you can just play the game to get it. Even if someone on your team has payed 1 million dollars it wouldnt be affecting you in a bad way. They would be helping you since they are on your team. The only downside to this is that it is very grind heavy... And I mean VERY grind heavy to the point where you will spend days trying to get a certain item... BUT this doesnt matter if:
1. You like grinding
2. You can find other things to do while grinding (leveling up warframes, weapons, sentinels, etc.)
3. You can put on some music that you like (because trust me, if you are grinding and you put on some music you are going to have a blast, you wont even notice the fact that you are grinding)
To add on to the fact that this game is heavily free to play, I sold on item on the game for a total of approximately 50 dollars. And I got that item by JUST playing the game. As easy as that. Its amazing. Also, this game is essentialy never ending! Meaning you can play however long you want and there will STILL be more stuff to unlock.
Pros:
-Not pay to win at all

-Creators are always hard at work creating new content and fixing bugs

Friends I know spend more time keeping everything they've established up and protected than enjoying the game.
That being said, there is honestly not much to enjoy in this game. With a group of friends you can easily hit endgame without triggering the Alpha (assuming the Alpha tribe is not a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥). However, the optimization is poor, the servers have issues, the community is toxic and, yes... a paid expansion which shifts the balance even more during Early Access is not ethical. I did not enjoy the expansion, but felt it was a necessity to keep up with competition. In that regard, well done, Wild Card.
Eventually, our efforts proved to be futile however as level caps were raised rendering your hours of breeding and taming of exquisite animals (such as Wyverns) naught. Cross Ark transfers were opened, despite that function having a notorious and horrible history. You see, people who don't know history are doomed to repeat it... And yet Wild Card repeats that history willingly and fully aware of the consequences.
Yes, the game does have a steady release of patches and content, but all of that is merely throwing glitter and shine over manure. The core game is broken, the experience is terrible and all that new content is simply adding more Arkemon to add to your virtually messed up Jurassic Ark. It's a distraction, and nothing more.
My sincere advice: buy this game AND its expansion when it's in a huge sale (<10€) if you have friends to play and explore with and if you can forgive performance issues.
If you're intending on building something huge in harsh environments to leave a legacy, forget about it, you'll never make it unless you have a gaming community of over 140 people blindly following you. No exaggeration.
Finally, if you wonder how I've got > 1.000 hours in this game despite not fully enjoying it; I was more busy helping my friends than doing anything useful myself (such as taming, for example). They needed help to farm, I'd provide it while being semi-AFK. I've lost interest in this game since a long time, but only that kept me going.

My fiancée has been playing this game for weeks, and gave me a copy.
I watched him playing this game, so I already have some opinions even before I started playing it myself.
Ark Survival has an interesting premise, kinda "Land of the Lost" (the 70's kid tv series, not the film), the "Lost" series and "Jurassic Park" movies had a kid. To make it short, you're thrown in a place filled with dinosaurs and megafauna with only your wits to survive.
There are four official maps to choose: "The Island" (recommended for beginners imo), the Center and Scorched Earth (you get this one with the DLC, it's HARD to start there) and finally Ragnarok (an amazing BIG map). There´s a new incoming map, "Aberration".
The dino taming and breeding is one of the most interesting features of this game - a pity that some are very time-consuming.
The servers can be PvE or PvP, and you can transfer your character to change maps (and get some dinos you won't find in some maps) - PvP to PvP servers, and PvE to PvE servers. No way to transfer from singleplayer to multiplayer or vice/versa - also, Legacy servers (the ones from Early Access) to Legacy only.
I started to play this game on EA, and it just hit final release - there are lots of updates and yeah, there´s still a ton of bugs, exploits and many many players complaining about all of then. Not going to list then here, everyone who plays Ark knows how it is.

The remaining EA servers are now called Legacy and have zero support from WC - yea you read it right... Everyone is leaving those servers and eventually WC wipe then too - thats what they intended to do since the beginning.

I very much recommend this game. The only issue is that eventually you get to a point where you need platinum (in-game paid currency) to increase slots for weapons/warframes. For weapons you only get 9 across melee, secondary and primary. For warframes themselves, you get 2. Now this may seem very low, but realisticly you should be sticking with a weapon/warframe until they are level 30 (Max).
I hit the 'pay-wall' 40 hours in, however, you can still play completely 100% free to play, and have all slots unlocked if you are smart. What you can do is sell in-game items on the  trade market (not steam market), and slots don't cost that much, it's about 20 platinum per 1 warframe slot/12 per 2 weapon slot.
All in all, a very good game, however if you don't want to trade to get platinum, you can always buy 10$ worth (170) and there are pretty much sales on a lot of the time. 170 platinum can keep you going for a long time.

Don't get me wrong I have had a lot of fun playing Warframe and there are many features that make this such an enjoyable game but I feel as though it is best to let me spare you the time of reading this review by only pointing out the flaws before you start delving into the Warframe universe. The reason I am giving this one a negative review is that is that it has been sucked into that microtransaction, paywall, p2w crisis that many F2P games face today.
The Grind: The whole point of the game is to obtain as many items such as warframes, weapons, companions etc. to kill your enemies. This process requires hours and even days of farming at a time for resources, blueprints etc and waiting for your desired item to finish building which is extremely excruciating. However, all of this can be sped up by buying in-game currency known as platinum with real life money which goes on to the next problem.
The Paywall: The motto 'Ninjas Play Free' only applies to playing the game. Progressing and getting more items is difficult to impossible without spending real life money. Most items can be obtained by playing the game however the number these items is severely limited unless you buy more weapon, warframe and companion slots with platinum. These limitations are what I hate about most F2P games and it is shame to see Warframe, an extremely fun and addicting game full of potential fall down this path. P.S. as of March 17, 2015 the devs introduced the Prime Vault. It is when items get periodically get removed from the game drop tables and placed into a metaphorical vault, which renders it unavailable to anyone who has not collected the items before it was vaulted or to players who started playing late. This was a detestable move by Digital Extremes the developer which basically forces completionists like me to spend real life money to obtain these items. I would appreciate it if they limited platinum spending to cosmetics, buying items outright to save time etc. If they had done this I would most definitely support the developers, helping them the fixes the bugs that plague the game.
The Bugs: I have never experienced as many bugs in a video game as I have in playing Warframe. From getting stuck in the map, graphical errors, gameplay issues, game breaking exploits, clan problems, statistics, internet issues such as logging out, disconnects, DNS and UDP errors and plenty more. I experience at least one more problems every time I play such as those that I have mentioned before which is unacceptable. I have lost count of the number of support tickets I have sent the developers.

Read the reviews. Look at all those red thumbs down. This game will
, and you will never want to
an early-access or open-world/survival/crafting/adventure game again.
You either dedicate ALL your time to this game, from the minute you wake up to the second you go to sleep, or what other time you spend on this game goes to waste as you get raided when you're inactive or a glitch ruins your entire base.
Oh, something people are failing to mention? Taming times. It's not a matter of "go pet that dinosaur and it'll be your friend", unless you're thinking of taming flipping dodo birds. It's more like taking shifts with friends to feed goddamn vegetables to animals for eight hours, and if you just so happen to either a) not feed the thing or b) forget to give it narcotics (keeping it unconscious), IT WAKES UP AND YOU LOSE ALL THAT PROGRESS. SO YOU'D BETTER HAVE SOME DAMN FRIENDS TO FEED VEGETABLES TO YOUR VIRTUAL PET DINOSAUR.
"What about PvE? Can't I just have friends and take on the dino world? :-)" Sure, but if other player's aren't gonna be your enemy, the game has to. Or that "friendly" clan who's built a base literally around the entire map and say you're welcome to tour the server but they already own every damn thing on the island.
"Okay... what about singleplayer?! :-D". Righto. Play SP. Build a cool base. Tame or kill dinosaurs. Get bored. Cheat. Get bored. Play online. *Soul defiled again*.
I'm just glad I only spent 116 hours on the game and then realised the game felt more like a chore than a game, like "oh darn I have to go feed my virtual dino's and ensure no one has destroyed my entire civilisation". I feel a great deal of pity for those who have spent up to thousands of hours on this game before they've realised what it was doing to them.
Stay away from this game like it were the plague.

Let me start off by saying that this is a very fun game. It's a third person skill-shot shooter with lots of different styles to choose from, and it includes things like pets and PVP and end-game bosses.
That being said, it is a game that has a LOT of repetitive grinding. It is also MUCH easier to get started if you have a friend help you, otherwise you have to grind through several missions on each planet to get to the assassination mission to unlock the other planets. There are resources on some of the higher level planets that you must acquire to create new weapons and frames, and if you're just starting out, you could be stuck at a lower rank just because you don't have enough resources to create more frames/weapons/etc.
There is always the option of buying Platinum, and I don't believe this makes the game "pay to win" since everything that isn't aesthetic is able to be acquired through in-game progress. It does make things infinitely easier though, since without platinum you have a limited number of warframe slots and weapon slots (meaning you can only have so many things in your 'inventory' at a time). If you want to create a new weapon, you may have to sell another one before you can claim it, or pay the 10 platinum to unlock another "slot." You CAN, however, earn platinum through trading with other players as well, once you are finding items that other people want.
All-in-all, this is a very interesting game and it is definitely something that I will be playing on and off. I don't see myself getting too sucked in though, just because of the repetitiveness and my lack of time.

Anyone who tries this game will either love it a lot, or hate it a lot. The extremes. Me? I LOVE this game.
Struggled a bit at the start, but fell in love with the freedom of movement... wall walking, jumping, sliding, shoot, stab, cleave, assassinate, rocket launchers, laser beams, flying space battles... you name it....
PROS:
-Freedom of Movement (as I said above...), yes, a lot of game have it now, but back then, it's revolutionary.
-Space ninjas setting, which is unique
-Excellent combination, a lot of games tried to combine 2 or more conflicting theme / style / culture, and failed. Warframe did it with stealth ninjas, 3rd person shooting and .... space battles. And they did it almost perfectly.
-Online Multiplayer Co-op up to 4 (8 for trials). Can be played solo too.... but you'll miss a lot of things.
-Thriving community, 2 years + with ever increasing active players both old and new
-Online player trading. You can buy almost everything in game with platinums (in-game currency) which can be obtain via trading items you got from quests and missions.
-Free to play. So you can spend no real money in this game but can still enjoy it to the fullest. Just takes a bit more effort via trading.
-Extensive Customizations. By modding.
-Constant updates and new contents
-Doesn't need that high end of a spec to play it. (playing on PC)
-Skill, not specs. This game relies heavily on your skill to play it. Everything maxed at lvl 30, and you can reach that in 30  minutes top if you know how. Yes, good equipments is a necessity, but if you didn't know how to use it, you'll crash and burn in this game.
CONS:
-Constant farming.... unless you're willing to spend quite a bit of real money into it.

Fun if you can handle the grind.
Also don't waste your plat.

Crashing issues that are not dealt with fixes even though the game receives "constant updates." Rather than fix the elder game and polish it up like a real studio, Wildcard chose to milk thier players for even more money and release an expansion for a game that was broken in some areas, unplayable for some players and with mechanics that were poorly implemented at best.
The idea of ARK is wonderful. Taming animals, building bases, exploring, hunting - it's a fun concept. However, Studio Wildcard makes shockingly bad decisions and when called out for it, plays word games and sweeps questions under the rug. Players with problems are asked, by their volunteer community team, to "provide solutions" to the problems with the game. Isn't that the studio's job?
Go play a different and better game than ARK. Now that Conan is out and newer survival games are getting some traction, ARK's days are numbered and the player base will dwindle to those who just can't let go of the hope that Studio Wildcard will figure out how to be a real game studio and produce a game that works well with ideas that are tested and challenged internally before pushed out to the players.

I don't have as many hours as a large amount of this community, but I can easily say that the time I've spent on Ark has been some of the best time I've spent gaming. If you're anything like me, Ark isn't a game you'll have fun with by yourself. Personally, I don't enjoy Official servers. I'm not that hardcore of a player. Frankly, if you are that kind of player, this review won't really be helpful to you.
First things first, the game is, in my opinion, absolutely gorgeous. Unfortunately, in order to get 60 fps on the settings required to make the game breathtaking, you'll need a pretty top notch computer. Even on lower settings, I think the game has a charm about it.
When you start the game, you'll have one or two reactions. Either you'll be completely overwhelmed by everything going on, and everything you'll feel like you need to do, or you'll be so ♥♥♥♥ing pumped because there's dinosaurs running around and the game is basically a realization of your Jurassic Park fantasies. I happen to fall in the latter camp. I bought the game the second day it was out on steam because someone described it to me as Rust with dinosaurs, and that sentence was enough to get me to pay full price. But I just happen to ♥♥♥♥ing love dinosaurs.
As you learn more and more about the game, and start to figure out surviving and rudimentary PvP, the game really opens up. You start taming more dinos, bigger ones, you start getting fancy gear. If you're on an official server, you die. But if you're not, this is when I think the game is the most fun. You can practice what styles you like to play, and there are so many viable builds. For instance, I love pouring all of my stat points into speed and running around like some sort of coked up Kenyan with a shotgun. Some people prefer becoming a tank. It's all about playstyle preference. There's just absolutely so much you can do.
Once you start to know everything, start min-maxing breeding, start hitting what I consider to be end-game, the game, to me, becomes less enjoyable. You might not be like me. This might be your favorite part of games like this, where you're better than most players. You know what to do because you've done it before. You can get on a new server, and with friends and dedication, have a formidable base and dino force in just a matter of days. You can raid bases reliably, you can become the alpha on unofficial, maybe even official servers. If you're anything like me, this is still a ton of fun, but it's not quite the same.
For me, Ark is a game that is honestly magical at first. When you first wake up on the beach, and you see a Brontosaur walking next to you, and you know eventually, you're going to ride that? For me, it's magic.

ARK's a much better game than it was around a year ago. The performance is basically gone now in my eyes. But it looks like if you're using - say a GTX 950 to 970. You don't really get the best.
Gameplay is great and it looks to have followed it's original concept. There are plenty of dinos, ranging from Dodo to Giganotosaurus. There are hundreds of items to unlock and craft. ARK also has a simple but effective levels which usually levels out the playing-field when you're playing multiplayer. Lastly there are plently of small things in ARK that add some fun and mystery to the game. These are things like the Artifacts from deep within the caves, Dossiers dotted around the map and Ruins which show signs of human life.
Multiplayer is good in most cases. We have mostly played on good, straightforward servers with nice and friendly players. Our experiences on the good servers are essentially what makes the game great. But be warned: some servers have Alpha Tribe's who ruin the fun for you and give you a real hard time. And I wouldn't suggest the Official servers because things like breeding and taming take not hours but days usually for good dinos and dinos to breed.

Since most of the negative changes WildCard made to the game have been noted, I'll keep my tale short and sweet. Played since game was released on steam, was buggy but very gorgeous, and enjoyable to play. Surviving wasn't too bad, made a lot of new friends. Gradually over time, the game slowed down a bit, but the updates were frequent enough with new dinos/content that it was still very playable. Mods also helped keep the gave from going stagnent.
Enter battle-eye era. Secure, triple map choice servers. The Center and Valhalla became big. They were enormous, revitalized a lot of players to come back from dormant states.
Titanosaur update happens, and this is where things went fred flintston, yabba dabba dooo. Patched in all the spawn badness and killed a LARGE amount of their player base due to tribes being able to server hop, raid, and leave with resources. No one wanted Barney Rubble over for dinner while they are off at work in the gravel pit, or hell, sleeping. No one was able to 24/7 guard their fruity pebbles or Dino's. Que the Pteradactl caw-caw, and enter waking up to everything being gone/stolen/dead and if it wasn't all down the rocky road, it was damaged enough to lose half the players/tribe members.
Overall, it was a fun ride at the start, the vanilla so to speak. I didn't play scorched earth, and don't intend to. I really loved this game, as it felt like "jurassic park meets open world" , and it was going down a great path. I just really wish they didn't kill their own product with server hopping shananigans.

October 2016- RIP Uninstalled 0/10

Great game, even with steam client issues it has, however, this is not a Free to Play game... about 70+ hours in, you'll get hit with what is essentially a paywal, and you will only realise it at that point, the game will never inform you about it before...
There are about 30 warframes in the game, and 50-60+ weapons...
However, you have 2  (free) warframe slots and about 8 or so weapon slots... and you have to unlock/buy new slots with the in game "premium" currency... ie for real cash... You can theoretically unlock new slots by trading with other people for the "premium" currency... but at that point you're just better of paying a few dollars or whatever...
This kind of an unethical bait and switch i will not support. Yes, you can still play the game (if you delete your weapons and warframes before building new ones etc). This, however, is, simply a pure greed manouver that has no basis in anything other then the developers wish to suck you into the game before saying "whoops, sorry, but now it's time for you to pay". Had they said it upfront, i'd have no problem with it. But for this bait and switch, the developers can take a hike.
Otherwise, it's a fine, grindy as hell, but fine game. Just be prepared to caugh up, if you don't like paying for mods, like i do not, no worries, be prepared to play for enjoying. Because this is a clear trap, they will not get money.

Ingredients
2 (12-ounce) lean, grass-fed New York strip steaks
1 teaspoon kosher salt
3/4 teaspoon black pepper
1 tablespoon olive oil
2 tablespoons butter
2 thyme sprigs
2 garlic cloves, crushed
Preparation
1. Let steaks stand 30 minutes at room temperature.
2. Sprinkle salt and pepper evenly over steaks. Heat a large cast-iron skillet over high heat. Add oil to pan; swirl to coat. Add steaks to pan; cook 3 minutes on each side or until browned. Reduce heat to medium-low; add butter, thyme, and garlic to pan. Carefully grasp pan handle using an oven mitt or folded dish towel. Tilt pan toward you so butter pools; cook 1 1/2 minutes, basting steaks with butter constantly. Remove steaks from pan; cover loosely with foil. Let stand 10 minutes. Reserve butter mixture.
3. Cut steak diagonally across grain into thin slices. Discard thyme and garlic; spoon reserved butter mixture over steak.

I was very hesitant in whether I should or shouldn't recommend this game. Here's why:
Ark is a VERY enjoyable game, but it is also very buggy. Bugs are expected in an "Early Access" game. However, if a game is released DLC's for an early access game, then that leads me to believe that it's not really "Early Access". This is an unrefined game that should not be releasing additional content for a game that should be focusing on the already existing bugs than another way of making profit.
Having been spoiled with developers like Blizzard's teams, Ark's development team looks like Valve's team. Not much communication with the community, except for a mod that somebody made, incredible btw, and took it and implemented it into the game. Kudos to that.
As long as they don't start offering crates or whatever, I'm happy.

Anyone who tries this game will either love it a lot, or hate it a lot. The extremes. Me? I LOVE this game.
Struggled a bit at the start, but fell in love with the freedom of movement... wall walking, jumping, sliding, shoot, stab, cleave, assassinate, rocket launchers, laser beams, flying space battles... you name it....
PROS:
-Freedom of Movement (as I said above...), yes, a lot of game have it now, but back then, it's revolutionary.
-Space ninjas setting, which is unique
-Excellent combination, a lot of games tried to combine 2 or more conflicting theme / style / culture, and failed. Warframe did it with stealth ninjas, 3rd person shooting and .... space battles. And they did it almost perfectly.
-Online Multiplayer Co-op up to 4 (8 for trials). Can be played solo too.... but you'll miss a lot of things.
-Thriving community, 2 years + with ever increasing active players both old and new
-Online player trading. You can buy almost everything in game with platinums (in-game currency) which can be obtain via trading items you got from quests and missions.
-Free to play. So you can spend no real money in this game but can still enjoy it to the fullest. Just takes a bit more effort via trading.
-Extensive Customizations. By modding.
-Constant updates and new contents
-Doesn't need that high end of a spec to play it. (playing on PC)
-Skill, not specs. This game relies heavily on your skill to play it. Everything maxed at lvl 30, and you can reach that in 30  minutes top if you know how. Yes, good equipments is a necessity, but if you didn't know how to use it, you'll crash and burn in this game.
CONS:
-Constant farming.... unless you're willing to spend quite a bit of real money into it.

Fun if you can handle the grind.
Also don't waste your plat.

At least I can say it is being improved consistently, while the dev/mod team has been known to be a little corrupt & selfish with making certain aspects pay to play or grind a metric ♥♥♥♥♥on to get, it overall is a solid game. Graphics are top notch, runs extremely well on low end systems too, the gamemodes are interesting and fun, although after a long grind they can get a bit repetetive, although they are adding new content continuously.
With the recently added content, End game is slowing shaping up to be pretty enjoyable, but getting there is the main problem.
The first 50 hours or so is a very slow grind, and the tutorials are just plain AWFUL at explaining what's important in the game, and you may waste your starting plat on things other than slots, I've helped literally HUNDREDS of players who simply were not explained how important mods were, and how to get other warframes and weapons to even unlocking other planets, so yeah, if you are having a tough time learning what to do, that's probably normal and expected.
However, once you get passed that, the game becomes a lot more fun, in terms of F2Pness, it is pretty easy to be free to play, although it will be a little slow at start. Personally I was able to get 12  warframe slots, some weapon slots, extra color pallets, and other cosmetics all free to play, but it does take time, I never felt after the start that the game was pay to win, although I did drop $10 on stuff when I got a coupon after that, as I felt the game had earned my money's worth.
Platinum is easy to earn in bursts, but it's hard to get a small amount fast, as you will generally need to find items worth selling, and of course a buyer, but say if you work to farm up a rare-ish prime set or weapon, those can easily net you enough plat to take care of all your needs for a while, but it requires patience.
Overall, I'd say
Actual Gameplay : 8/10
Graphics : 9/10
F2P : 7/10
Starting Difficulty : Grindy and annoying
Ending difficulty: A little on the easy, side, but grindy and fun for the most part.
Definitely give it a try, space ninjas with magical powers, fun stuff.

I love the concept but it kinda falls flat. The game plays nothing like its trailers.
Lets start with what i like:
- Exploration
- Maps are great. All but The Island.
- Lots of creatures that all have something unique about them.
- Trapping/Taming said creatures (also a dislike)
- Building (with mods)
- PVE dangers are real (also a dislike)
Things i dislike:
- AI is VERY simplistic. It feels like a few lines of If/than/else statements. basically run straight at player, run into object, attempt to walk around object, fail, repeat. Its not very immersive at all.
- Taming even low level creatures will take HOURS unless ur on an unofficial server. I honestly dont get how ppl play on official servers.
- The game relies on stats WAY too much. Nothing wrong with levels but this game doesnt implement it very well. Pretty much every unofficial server plays with per point stat values which doesnt help.
- PVP is nothing like the trailers. 90% of the time PVP will consist of someone destroying ur place while ur offline for no reason besides because they can and its easy. 1 man raids are common place even later down the road.
- Crafting is pretty boring. It just seems like ur not getting anything cool or fun to craft.
- Farmville style breeding. No joke. You have to return every so many hours to take care of babies to up its stats through imprinting. Its not required to breed but its useful.
People id recommend this game to:
- sadists and/or masochist
- people that enjoy simple pve.
- people that want "pvp" where theres no real threat.

Don't get me wrong I have had a lot of fun playing Warframe and there are many features that make this such an enjoyable game but I feel as though it is best to let me spare you the time of reading this review by only pointing out the flaws before you start delving into the Warframe universe. The reason I am giving this one a negative review is that is that it has been sucked into that microtransaction, paywall, p2w crisis that many F2P games face today.
The Grind: The whole point of the game is to obtain as many items such as warframes, weapons, companions etc. to kill your enemies. This process requires hours and even days of farming at a time for resources, blueprints etc and waiting for your desired item to finish building which is extremely excruciating. However, all of this can be sped up by buying in-game currency known as platinum with real life money which goes on to the next problem.
The Paywall: The motto 'Ninjas Play Free' only applies to playing the game. Progressing and getting more items is difficult to impossible without spending real life money. Most items can be obtained by playing the game however the number these items is severely limited unless you buy more weapon, warframe and companion slots with platinum. These limitations are what I hate about most F2P games and it is shame to see Warframe, an extremely fun and addicting game full of potential fall down this path. P.S. as of March 17, 2015 the devs introduced the Prime Vault. It is when items get periodically get removed from the game drop tables and placed into a metaphorical vault, which renders it unavailable to anyone who has not collected the items before it was vaulted or to players who started playing late. This was a detestable move by Digital Extremes the developer which basically forces completionists like me to spend real life money to obtain these items. I would appreciate it if they limited platinum spending to cosmetics, buying items outright to save time etc. If they had done this I would most definitely support the developers, helping them the fixes the bugs that plague the game.
The Bugs: I have never experienced as many bugs in a video game as I have in playing Warframe. From getting stuck in the map, graphical errors, gameplay issues, game breaking exploits, clan problems, statistics, internet issues such as logging out, disconnects, DNS and UDP errors and plenty more. I experience at least one more problems every time I play such as those that I have mentioned before which is unacceptable. I have lost count of the number of support tickets I have sent the developers.

The amount of time I've spent on ARK is quite a lot. I haven't reached 1,000 hours yet, but I know I will. Though when I first bought the game back during the release I could not run it on my computer at the time, I longed to play it every day. Finally after getting enough money for a good pc I was able to play the game. I remember starting out not knowing how to play very well. I think pve is a good way to start unless you already have experience with games such as Rust. I spent hours upon hours discovering The Island and learning how to tame and where to find certain resources. After about 100-200 hours of playing on the island I was becoming somewhat tired of ARK. Then came along The Center, in my opinion, the best looking map of all ARK maps. It was another brand new experience of exploring and having an awesome time with friends. After playing pve for a while you may become bored, such as I did. Have no fear there is pvp. Pvp in ARK is honestly the most fun I've had of all games I've ever owned. Though there is the initial hesitation, and a new play style to learn, you won't regret it. I still remember having 3 turrets on the inside of my base thinking I was practically unraidable. Then I came on after taking a 30 minute break to shower and eat to find out I'd been raided. Being raided teaches you things, and how to get better at pvp. You learn how to improve your base, and how to raid others, After spending my past 500 hours of ARK on pvp I could never go back to pve. In the end there are a few glitches with ark you have to deal with, but we all come back to the game anyways, atleast I do. I hope that if you took the time to read this you purchase the game. I know I haven't regretted my almost 800 hours of game time.

The Janky:
The need to fix their default graphics settings, because they are awful and it took me forever to realize that it was the reason I couldn't get the game to work at first.

The good:
Besides the fact I've spent 300hrs on this game with a full time job schedule shows how addicting it can be.
The devs just added so much content and features.
It's a real time action game, which is something I didn't realize going in. I thought it was more MMO rule like.
The game is Skyrim meets minecraft in an island filled with tameable dinosaurs that you can ride on.
The game has as much depth as you give it.
I do recommend buying right now since it's on sale, I consider it my game of the year.
The survival mechanics are pretty good, I'm not a fan of the official server xp/leveling system nor the settings for certain animal tames. It can be a bit much and just completely overwhelming, I feel like well tuned unofficial servers can give a much better game experience.
This is definitely a multiplayer game, just jump in, make friends, survive and thrive.

Update 09/01/2017:
So the game has reached "Full Release" status and it's rocking a full arsenal of content and looking good while doing it.  There are plans for future DLC and the game is continually being optimized and updated.  Cool Beans.  However now that the end of the Early Access trail has finally come and we have graduated from being an alpha and beta release to a full release I must say I was expecting more in the way of gameplay and optimization.
Since the last major update the game now crashes just under a minute after entering the game world.  No message or anything explaining why, it just crashes my whole system.  None of my other games do this and there are many titles in my library that are graphically superior and applications that are more cpu intensive.
The game, though thought out as far as content is concerned, still struggles in areas of gamplay that would make it a much more immersive experience and in some ways it still feels incomplete.  In short, this game is not worth $60.  Maybe at some point it will be, but when you consider that triple A titles all sell at that price point unless bundled with a season pass or dlc content after which they go for $79-$89, Ark Survival is way over priced for the amount of quality control that you get out of your money.  This is not a triple A title in my opinion, although I do believe it could be with more time.  The Season Pass, is severly overpriced, especially for those folks who haven't already purchased the Scorched Earth DLC.  I've read and understand that the remaining two DLCs bring at least 300 hours of content each, which is nice to hear, but at this point in the process I think it would have been better to suggest all three DLCs (if that amount of additional gameplay is accurate) at the $29 price as oppose to what it is now.
I still think that Ark Survival is a great game and I do believe it is worthy of a fair price.  $39 maybe, and if it were better optimized.  I don't know of any Early Access title yet that is worthy of the $60 price point.  It doesn't matter how long the game has been in development for various reasons.
Update 06/09/2017:
Okay so it's been a little while and several changes have been made to the game resulting in more content and far better optimization in the game code resulting in better performance and smoother gameplay.  I wish the optimization had taken priority over the additional content but they did eventually take action and the results are present in the game.  The extra content is a bonus.  I still think with some more tweaking and adjustments we could squeeze a bit more performance out of the game without tampering with the graphic fidelity.
Speaking of that, the "Dynamic Tesselation" option still doesn't do anything to the game.  What's the deal with that?  So far, as mentioned in my original review below, my Titan X Pascal on water was running at 56c while playing this game and now it hovers around 41c which is a drastic improvment, so thumbs up there!
I would personally like to see a more in depth character creation experience.  Sure, some people like to argue you hardly ever see your own character but then it's the character customization that makes the foundation of who your avatar is within the game world.  Scars, Tattoos, facial expressions, more hairstyles, eye and nose shapes and the ability to adjust the elements, and body morphs all the way down to the fingernails would be awesome for a game like this.
Over all, this is a good game with lots of content.  Not much of a story per say, but then it is a survival game, so you pretty much make your own.  It's a cool experience.

Ark: Survival Evolved is a very nice game. It runs in the same veins as other survival games where you're dumped into a hostile world and must make the most of what is available to you, but with a prehistoric twist, dinosaurs. The beautiful, expansive environment is littered with them, and best of all, you can tame the majority of the mighty creatures. Ever want to ride around on a T-Rex?  No problem. Eat other giant great white sharks with your very own. Sure. Soar through the air on a Pteranodon?  You can do it in Ark.
I've only played the single player, but even so, the sheer volume of things you can do, places to explore, and challenges to overcome, make the game well worth the sale price for sure.

Ark: Survival Evolved is a very nice game. It runs in the same veins as other survival games where you're dumped into a hostile world and must make the most of what is available to you, but with a prehistoric twist, dinosaurs. The beautiful, expansive environment is littered with them, and best of all, you can tame the majority of the mighty creatures. Ever want to ride around on a T-Rex?  No problem. Eat other giant great white sharks with your very own. Sure. Soar through the air on a Pteranodon?  You can do it in Ark.
I've only played the single player, but even so, the sheer volume of things you can do, places to explore, and challenges to overcome, make the game well worth the sale price for sure.
I believe the majority of negative reviews are coming from angry Multiplayers. Single player can be unforgiving enough, I can only imagine how it must be when someone smashed through your new base with a high level (Yes, you and your dinos can level up) T-Rex.
This game has it's flaws, such as dinos getting stuck in the environment, and a weird one where nothing spawns in caves, as well as a blinding glare issue, but the developers seem to be very active in adding content and improving their already amazing game.

Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥it is just a grind fest. To get 21/21 you need to level more than 39 characters, 248 weapons, 25 pets, 4 jet packs and 15 jetpack weapons from level 1 - 30. To get all of those need to grind more than 27 different in-game currencies and one real money currency. To effectively fight the monsters required to grind these currencies you need to get and level up (more grinding) some subset of the 718 mods. To spend the currencies you worked for you need to repeatedly grind missions to get "blueprints", which you put all of your required currencies into, then wait 12-144 hours to get an item out so you can grind to level then dispose of or use to more effectively grind. At some point select weapons need to be re-leveled (up to eight or more times) to become strong enough so you can fight for a few more minutes in missions that only end when you give up.
At some point you realize that this is all pointless and you try to find fun and excitement in the flashy lights of the combat system. That works until you realize this is just a numbers game, you need to use one certain combination of items to get the highest numbers. So you work towards the one best way while waiting for the next "event" apointment that you don't want to miss out on.
I guess I'm just tired of it all and don't want to spend a couple thousand dollars to skip most of that.

I love this game very much, i'd hate to compare it to minecraft, but its  500 times better minecraft. You start of as a naked caveman, and progress to future tek stuff. I recomend this game to anyone who loves trying to survive with or from players, but also over 100 different kinds of wildlife/dinos, some are passive, others extremly aggresive and dangerous. Graphics are extremly good as well as amazing differences and behavior in the dinosaurs. Ark defenently has its moments too, just hidding behind a giant rock with a camp fire going in the middle of the night in a jungle, not knowing whats making the noises around you. Until resently there were no ambeint noises, so if you hear somthing, that means there is somthing near. Another cool thing about Ark, is every single dino has its own sounds, so over time you learn to recognize every dino sound and you feel safer, i remember the first time a heard a little puny dodo bird and could not see it, i freaked out because i did not know what it was lol. And the best part is you can ride most dinos and use them for what they were desinged to do, there are even dinos that collect valuable resources. There is alos a whole ocean to explore, like sea caves, oil, pearls, even giants whale and squid like creatures (just to name a few). To finish this review even though i could go on and on, Ark is worth the $30 by a long shot, i would even pay double for this game, its one of the best i've ever played!

Games vary on what you are into. Some people mindlessly shoot people like in COD or Battlefield. Others enjoy platforming like the Homie Crash, Ratchet and Clank and Jak and Daxter. Some enjoying grinding for what they want so they can earn it. Others simply want rewards whenever they feel like or want it as soon as they find out about it. This game is a combination of most of these things. I personally consider this as a 3rd person Platformer shooter with Grind fest^34th. Its more than just ninjas in space. Your tools truly do shape you. You go in there with a halfmodded class, youre gonna have to work your♥♥♥♥♥off in order to not die and keep up with your friends. Go in there with actual modding setup, you'll be able to hold your own and even half play while you text your girl about spring break plans (Sorry, didnt mean to sound objective) Unless you put in the time to properly prepare and some research to crunch numbers on what build is most effective agasint what with what team composition. The gameplay itself is fun, sure some frames can use similar abilities or nowhere near similar abilities to reach the same result,♥♥♥♥♥♥dying or getting from point a to ledge b for example. There are dozens of weapons and while theres a significant bit that are garbage or have unrealistic standards for making the weapon, theres still a crapton of weapons that are effective and plainly just FUN.  I've been playing this since Update 9 during Ember prime access on console all the way to Update 13 or 14, took a break, came over to pc RIGHT before the chroma update. So I'm not some dude who came through during the tailend of stuff, I've been around for AWHILE so I can honestly take appreciation for all the changes and advances in the mechanics, bullet jump is awesome. Outside of Gameplay, the story you have to string together yourself. READ EVERYTHING. The codex entries, the dialogue the bosses havem, pay attention during the quests and whatever else Lotus (Space Mom) says to you. From a writers standpoint, the story was ok and has vass amount of potential until Update 18.0. The big Reveal in the quest "The Second Dream" For Update 18.0 was lame, made many plot holes, and disappoints many. Alot of people don't have the patience to piece together the story and so many don't see the problem with the plot twist but imagine that you put in the time and effort and the research to actually know whats going on and why every alien species/factions are afraid of you and hate you. Imagine putting forth the initiative only for the biggest sack of disappointment to where you literally say "Ooook this is getting stupid". Imagine getting that middle finger to the face about the claim of everything being canon even though the lore is stabbed in multiple parts and has stab wounds known as plot holes. Imagine the fact the director of this warframe project , Steve Sinclair, replies to criticism about this plot hole like a snobby 5 year old. He doesnt take criticism well so when he is told that his creation wasnt thought out very well and doesnt make sense, he's gonna be a prick about it. He doesnt go as far as to ban you or block you but he will make you reconsider coming to him for help. As a whole, we've witnessed Steve Sinclair And Rebecca Ford go at it because as the community manager Rebecca gets paid to know how we are and our thoughts towards things that need to be changed or improved upon. Steve can't accept that the things he does arent 100% full proof so its an uphill battle for Ford. Sorry for the ranting, just wanted to make this as honest as possible. Gameplay is good, Grinding is insanely high and sometimes broken, Story was good until the garbage "Plot twist" known as the 2nd dream. If you don't care about story and can deal with not getting that thing you want anywhere from 8 hours to 2 months later, by all means, play this game my friends.

Time to replace my early access review.
First thing I want to say is that your enjoyment of the game heavily depends on the server you join. Avoid official servers like the plague and just search the forums or just the server browser for an unofficial server that suits you. Playing offline single-player or non-dedicated with your friends can be fun as well.
However, the most important thing I can say is DO NOT I repeat DO NOT use steam reviews, Positive or Negative to dictate whether or not you buy this game. Due to how fun tis game can be and how anger-inducing it can be there are plenty of heavily biased reviews on both sides that don't look at the bigger picture.
Go on YouTube, read guides, play it on a friend's shared library if possible. I personally don't believe the game is worth $60, not and outright waste of money but it is a stretch, grab it on a sale if you do.
My personal opinion is that this game is worth consideration, but be wary how you play it and with whom you play it.

First off, ARK: Survival Evolved is an in-depth game with many mechanics and tricks to learn. Lossage is expensive. If a powerful dino you took 3 hours to tame, dies, it's dead. That being said, the learning curve is intense as the game will not forgive you for not knowing or making mistakes. This is absolutely frustrating for new players starting to learn the game.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If you are looking for a survival game where you can build a nice house and tame some of your favourite dinos with your friends and have a blast, then you've come to the wrong game.
ARK  is 24/7 PVP, unless you are on PVE then you aren't actually playing ARK. What that means is that even when you log out, you can get attacked and lose everything in an hour. And when I say everything, I mean everything but your character level. And if that isn't bad enough, if the aggressor is committed enough, he can imprison you and you'd not even have your character anymore. Basically what that means is that the smaller tribes are at the whims of the bigger, more established tribes and people aren't as docile in real life as in video games. Majority of the people will destroy your hours of work just for the funsies.
Because of this intense PVP environment, it is a constant race between tribes to build up weapons and defences. And if there is an active war, a constant race of recovering and attacking. What that basically boils down to is that the player that plays the most wins. And although that sounds fair, which it is, it also means that if you want to enjoy ARK, you will need to be the most active tribe on the server to outproduce anybody else to sercure your safety. And with the ability for one server to attack another server, you'd have to be the most active tribe in the world if you want to feel safe in ARK. Or your base and hours of gameplay is doomed to eventually be destroyed.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Of course the game is in development and there are plenty of bugs. But the cost of the bugs can be massive due to high tier dinos being so hard to acquire whether by it being acquired by breeding or taming from the wild, dinos can glitch out  of your base and be swarmed and killed by wild dinos while you are offline or somewhere else or simply just vanish from existence.
This can even be more frustrating than being attacked because you are being griefed by the game, not by another person. How do you fight back against the game?
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Pros:
1. In-depth with many mechanics to play with
2. Sandbox game with creative ways to tackle various problems.
3. Intense PVP
Cons:
1. Too intense PVP
2. Sell your soul to ARK or be destroyed by more active players.
3. You can lose EVERYTHING if you get wiped one night while you are sleeping.
4. Bugs can cost you hours of work.
5. You can't put the game down and continue a few days later because of the intense PVP
6. I'd continue about how intense the PVP is but you get the point. PVP makes the game fun but it is also ruining the game entirely.
Overall, it is a great game for the select few who have made their lives ARK but the rest normal gamers do not have a place in the game.
And yes, I have sold my soul to the game and I want it back. From being in straw houses to stone and being wiped by raiders several times, my tribe being newcomers to the server, became the most active players on the server by playtime and now that we out produced the raiders, we are now established. But tribes from other servers are still a threat and will forever be a threat. Take my word for it, don't buy this game.

Trading: I like trading and getting that plat, don't get me wrong, I hate the trading chat, that's why I use a site called warframe.market.
Grind: Now some people see grind as a bad thing. But in Warframe's case grind is good because if you like the game then it's enjoyable to grind.
Different mission types.
Customization AKA Fashionframe.
Uranus (If you know what I mean).
Warframe (class) variety: at the moment there's 28 different warframes.
Melee combat: from slashing and dashing with swords to ragdolling enemies all over the map with a hammer
Parkour: after all it's a ninja game :D
Modding: collect mods, upgrade them, make your own build (or multiple builds) for each warframe!
Having my own spaceship: hanging out in my own ship or being stuck in menus? I'll take the ship please.

Carrier: this guy picks up (or vacuum's) things for you!
Rebecca... I mean Lotus.

Getting loot: I like my loot.
Crafting: now put that loot to use.
Community: wow I've met so many friendly people in warframe (except from that one russian guy that yels at you via voice chat).

Chat system: seriously, you have to look for group in the LFG chat or if you want to sell something you have to spam in the cancerous trade chat. Thank god for the 3rd party sites.
Waiting for things to finish crafting: it's like you're an 8 year old and your mom buys you a toy you always wanted. And then what does she do with that toy? She puts it right in front of your face and says that you will only be able to play with it in 3 days.

As of the time of this review, this game has been on its most aggressive update cycle since I got it. It's hard to keep up with the pacing of it, but every update I get to see a new level of beauty come from this game. The optimizations have been done by a thousand cuts, so no one update shows massive fixes, but everytime I show this game to a friend, be it a modern hardcore gamer or someone out of touch with 3D gaming at all, they're all blown away. Yes, you have to fork over some money to get a rig that runs it with all settings maxed, but it's not as bad as so many reviews hark it as. I recently built my rig for streaming, and ended up buying a bit more than I needed and still spent under $2k, and with that, not only can I play heavily modded ARK with all settings maxed (minus motion blur. That stuff is nothing but instant migraine) and an average of 70 FPS (if that doesn't satisfy you, your eyes must be 10 times better than mine, which is possible), but I also STREAM it with absolutely no perceptible performance issues. I hate to say, but the minimum requirements listed have, to my knowledge, always been wrong, and by a rediculous ammount. The game gets a solid green thumbs up even with the new pricetag, because let's face it. The team has put as much work into this game as any 4 generations of CoD combined, and you know the pricetags that those easily sell by.

There are two sides to this game.
The unofficial servers and modding community are amazing, so that's a thumbs up for that.
The official servers are awfull, there are many glitches and bugs that can be abused and make the pvp worthless on those servers.
- You can slide under the map to build unatainable bases (unless you know those glitches yourself)
- shoot rockets through terrain to destroy bases that would require much effort to be taken down otherwise.
- You can also block all spawn points with spikes and prevent anyone from joining the server (which could be easily fixed by setting up random spawn points anywhere)
- Huge tribes can blitz a server to full capacity (70 max pop) and thus prevent you or friends from logging in to defend.
- people can aimbot (and apparently do it through terrain too)
So go PvP if you wish but be aware that's it's not a fair playing field, regardless of whatever the balance is, game breaking glitches and the possibility to use third party programs is unacceptable.
The devs can't really handle that by banning faulty players because there will always be too much for them to keep up with. Howver it is their fault that those issues exist in the first place and they should be their highest priority.
If you think that's fine because you prefer PvE, abuses are even worse on PvE:
- people spam the map with structures that prevents you from building, harvesting resources, or entering caves that contain most of the game's attractions (and since it's PvE you can't destroy those blocking structures).
- there is an agressive wild dino that can destroy all tiers of buildings and people will aggro it to your bases, which will force you to build with griefers in mind, on PvE servers where you shouldn't need to think about it.
For those things I can only put a negative review
However the solo experience on dedicated servers is excellent and unofficial servers also have great admins and great mods (or some no mods if you like) and will deal with abusers much more efficiently than the WildCard team possibly can on officials. So very positive for solo + unofficial play.

I have played this game for two years, and have ambivalently enjoyed it.  There are many things it does really well -- the action and feel is great, when it's great.  And it's got personality, complete with your missiongiver (the Lotus) being creepily manipulative and codependent, and your ship's AI being hilariously Tourettesy and sullen.  The good parts have been good enough to overlook a lot of really irritating things.
But, after years of playing this, I have to turn my thumbs down given the path it's been on for quite a long time.  The good has been shrinking rapidly in proportion to the bad, and, given that a game like this is one you play for the long haul, I can't recommend it to anyone starting out.  As time goes on, at least in the two years I've been playing, it has only become *more* buggy, *more* tedious and *less* rewarding, to the point where I wonder if the devs respect their playerbase.
Problems (short version):
1) The game has longstanding, serious game-ruining bugs that do not get addressed, while new content introduces new embarrassingly-bad bugs that should not have survived beta testing.  They just don't seem interested in fixing them.
2) The game is a grindfest, and that's part of the game and has been for a long time, and that's fine within reasonable bounds.  But the reward curve has been getting worse while the game has been getting more tedious and requiring more mind-numbing repetition of missions not interesting enough to sustain that repetition.
3) In their quest to extend game life and make more challenge, the devs have been creating artificial difficulty by, for example, creating missions that are long and tedious, and, rather than requiring skill, require patience as the players repeatedly engage in Skinner-box behaviors until the mission is finally complete.
Putting 2) and 3) together, the game is becoming a less- and less-rewarding Skinner box, and it's known as Trollframe to many players now because of its irritating non-rewards after extended, much-repeated tedious missions.
Problems (long version):
1) The devs seem to have become sloppier and sloppier.  Pretty much all new content is patched in with insufficient testing, and serious game-degrading/session-ruining bugs and frustrating glitches go uncorrected.  Most recent case has been the change of how enemies spawn in Extermination-type missions, in which you have to kill all enemies on the map to complete it.  Apparently, the devs found that some players had figured out how to complete these missions more quickly by stealthing them, making them able to grind faster.  Horrors!  So the devs immediately implemented a change that staggers them differently and makes some spawn well-behind the players -- sometimes at the mission start! -- making for a lot of time-consuming backtracking.  It also makes it so not all enemies are spawned by the time the players reach the final room of the mission, so the players just sit there from 3-10 minutes waiting for them to spawn in onesies and twosies.  It's disproportionately frustrating, like an extended, interactive loading screen that just sits there for a long time but requires your continued attention to progress.  This change has not been retracted 3 months after the fact, and it's not fixed.  Why not test it before putting it into production, or withdraw it until fixed, if it contains a serious bug?
There are lots of things like this.  There are a lot of bugs that just don't get addressed, and some of them (like falling out of the map, which happens more frequently than it should) have no in-game remedy and are mission-ruiners.
On the other hand, if there is a grinding shortcut, the devs are ON that, lickety-split.  So, instead of fixing the backspawning problem (making the player run all the way back to early parts of the mission to kill a newly-spawned mob, making the mission take a couple minutes longer with what amounts to a fetch quest) that has annoyed players for at *least* two years, they instead introduced *more* spawn delay and backspawn to thwart players that might be able to cleverly shave a minute or two off a mission (and, interestingly, completely avoid the backspawning bug).  From this, I can only infer that backspawning is intentional, and what bothers them is when players can *avoid* experiencing it.  Your priorities are showing, DE.  That one right there gets them a big middle finger from me.
2) The game has been increasingly oriented toward endless, frustrating grinding with worse and worse chances of getting desired item drops -- it's been getting worse, such that these days people commonly refer to it as Trollframe.  The game is grinding-oriented -- we all know this.  But the devs have increasingly been orienting the content such that it involves this sort of grinding: so-and-so mission will be available for 7 days, and you can only get X item from it.  You need to collect all its pieces from repeating a long, tedious mission, which has a random chance to drop them as its end-mission reward.  They've set up the drop tables (percentage chances of getting each item at the end) so you can get a couple of the items reasonably, but one of the items has a very low percentage chance to drop, so you pile up extras of the first parts while you get silly junk items the other half of the time.  So you repeat this mission twenty, thirty, forty times, til you're numb with it and despise it, but you're pressing that twenty-minute Skinner box button sequence hoping for the thing.  Grinding can be fun and engaging, but they've pushed the envelope too far.
3) In terms of actual gameplay, there's been an irritating trend toward more tedious and irritating missions and enemies.  The latest one at the time of this writing, the giant robot-dog Razorback, is a mission filled with bugs and made artificially long and tedious.  It's not difficult once you know how to do it, but it takes forever because of the way it is strucured (press this button, wait for bursa robot to jump down, knock him down and hack him, wait for him to disable Razorback's defenses, now shoot Razorback in a 2-second time window that isn't really very clear when it starts so you might miss it, and repeat 6 to 30 times depending on player DPS and other factors).
Eh, I'm tired of the game looking more and more like a literal Skinner box -- that Razorback mission is almost humorously literal in being one.  Except we only have a small chance of getting our birdseed at the end, and I'm tired of doing it.
Nope, can't recommend it.  Devs are reaching into more and more questionable game mechanics and feedback mechanisms to extend its life, and it's become a burnout-inducing tedium-fest.

Warframe is a very interesting game for me, for a variety of reasons. The biggest being that I have sunk 120 hours of gameplay into it (as of the writing of this) and it is actually outside the genres that I normally find fun.
Warframe is like a lot of genres mixed into one game, and it does all of them rather well. You can stealth a lot of missions, a lot, not all. There are FPS/gunplay elements, you can be melee. There's the occasional rescue (escort) mission... but they actually did the almost impossible and made them not horrible. There are a lot of "classes", each warframe is different and has different stats and abilities. There are a TON of weapons, and you can equip one melee, one main gun, and one sidearm at any given time.
The game is incredibly customizable. You want a sniper rifle that is completely silent? You can put a mod on the gun to do that! You want to be able to send out shockwaves anytime you land heavily? You can put a mod on your warframe to do that! How about a pet that can open extra loot containers? One to put a cloaking field over you for added stealth capabilities? Make the giant heavy blade have a reach of more than double its normal one? Turn the magazine size of a certain rocket launcher from its standard 3 to an amazing 21? YOU CAN DO ALL THAT!
Warframe is amazingly fun. There are quests to help you advance, but a lot of the game is you find something that you want to make, and you work towards making it. The game is very grindy, but it doesn't really feel like it because you are almost always working towards something.
Very nice voice acting, although the Grineer bosses talk too much. Music is nicely atmospheric and actually not playing most of the time so you can hear things going on around you. Sound effects are appropriate and well done. One of the warframes is a berserker, when you put her into berserker mode the sound of gunfire is greatly reduced for you since your character would be lost in bloodlust. Very nice little touches that make the overall game better.
There is a very, VERY large downside though. The game SUCKS, and I mean SUCKS, at teaching you how to play the game! It never tells you how important it is to fuse mods to make them stronger which makes your equipment stronger... and it only mentions the fusing of mods as an aside, it never tells you how to rank up your account level to unlock new things, it never tells you how to get the xp to level up your account. It does not tell you what drops what. Let's pick something that is annoying to get... the Ivara warframe blueprints. You get one at the end of a mission and you decide you want to get her. The game never tells you where you can hunt down the rest of the pieces to make her. Her parts are only gotten at the end of spy missions, and certain parts can be gotten from certain difficulties. And you are not going to figure that out on your own in game. (See my comment below this review for how to do the things I mentioned.)
You are going to need the wiki, or youtube videos to figure this stuff out. The game is incredibly unfriendly towards new players simply in the fact that it never tells you how to do things. Some of them are required to actually advance any in game, such as fusing mods.
Another issue is that the secondary objectives (they give 1k-5k extra xp) you randomly get at the beginning of each mission needs an overhaul as well. Some are impossible to do for the mission you are doing. You can get 20 pistol kills, 5 kills while sliding, and 30 rifle (primary weapon) kill objectives in archwing missions. You do not have a pistol, can not slide, and evidently your gun does not count as a rifle. You can get hack a console objective in missions that have 0 consoles (such as defense missions). You also can get kill 10 unalerted enemies in missions where all enemies are already alerted (defense and survival) although various warframes can force them into an "unalerted" state, so that is semi-acceptable.
There are pay to win elements to the game, but anything you can buy (with the exception of some unique purely cosmetic items) can all be gotten through playing the game. The pay to win elements don't hinder the game though. You can buy a later game warframe, but you still have to level it and get the mods to make it better. The game has some pvp, but I haven't heard anybody mention it in game, and as far as I can gather it is not done much, so the pay to win aspects don't really matter.
Aside from the new player experience, which needs a complete and total overhaul to actually teach you how to play, I absolutely love the game. There's random missions that show up every day, with rewards that can't be gotten any other way (aside from paying real money), high end raids... which I can't access yet, and all kinds of other things to keep you entertained and always going after something new.
Fantastic game, I am looking forward to playing more of it and getting more toys to play with.
