As of the time of this review, this game has been on its most aggressive update cycle since I got it. It's hard to keep up with the pacing of it, but every update I get to see a new level of beauty come from this game. The optimizations have been done by a thousand cuts, so no one update shows massive fixes, but everytime I show this game to a friend, be it a modern hardcore gamer or someone out of touch with 3D gaming at all, they're all blown away. Yes, you have to fork over some money to get a rig that runs it with all settings maxed, but it's not as bad as so many reviews hark it as. I recently built my rig for streaming, and ended up buying a bit more than I needed and still spent under $2k, and with that, not only can I play heavily modded ARK with all settings maxed (minus motion blur. That stuff is nothing but instant migraine) and an average of 70 FPS (if that doesn't satisfy you, your eyes must be 10 times better than mine, which is possible), but I also STREAM it with absolutely no perceptible performance issues. I hate to say, but the minimum requirements listed have, to my knowledge, always been wrong, and by a rediculous ammount. The game gets a solid green thumbs up even with the new pricetag, because let's face it. The team has put as much work into this game as any 4 generations of CoD combined, and you know the pricetags that those easily sell by.

There are two sides to this game.
The unofficial servers and modding community are amazing, so that's a thumbs up for that.
The official servers are awfull, there are many glitches and bugs that can be abused and make the pvp worthless on those servers.
- You can slide under the map to build unatainable bases (unless you know those glitches yourself)
- shoot rockets through terrain to destroy bases that would require much effort to be taken down otherwise.
- You can also block all spawn points with spikes and prevent anyone from joining the server (which could be easily fixed by setting up random spawn points anywhere)
- Huge tribes can blitz a server to full capacity (70 max pop) and thus prevent you or friends from logging in to defend.
- people can aimbot (and apparently do it through terrain too)
So go PvP if you wish but be aware that's it's not a fair playing field, regardless of whatever the balance is, game breaking glitches and the possibility to use third party programs is unacceptable.
The devs can't really handle that by banning faulty players because there will always be too much for them to keep up with. Howver it is their fault that those issues exist in the first place and they should be their highest priority.
If you think that's fine because you prefer PvE, abuses are even worse on PvE:
- people spam the map with structures that prevents you from building, harvesting resources, or entering caves that contain most of the game's attractions (and since it's PvE you can't destroy those blocking structures).
- there is an agressive wild dino that can destroy all tiers of buildings and people will aggro it to your bases, which will force you to build with griefers in mind, on PvE servers where you shouldn't need to think about it.
For those things I can only put a negative review
However the solo experience on dedicated servers is excellent and unofficial servers also have great admins and great mods (or some no mods if you like) and will deal with abusers much more efficiently than the WildCard team possibly can on officials. So very positive for solo + unofficial play.

Way too much DLC for an "early access" game.  Can't support that kind of behavior.
Other than that, I experienced some mild enjoyment in the few hours I've spent playing the game.  But that enjoyment quickly waned when I saw the way tribes would lock down all of the territory on a server by placing small pillars every few feet, making it impossible to build anywhere.  It would probably be best played either solo, or in a small group on a private, custom server.  But even then, the grindiness takes away from the fun when you realize that in order to tame creatures, you have to sit there and keep feeding them toxic berries for 9 hours after knocking them out.  Eventually you gain more skills and can do it faster, but none of that stuff is fun or interesting to me.  When you make your own server, you can tweak a lot of things and possibly alleviate everything I'm complaining about, but I'm not sure, and not particularly inclined to find out.
Granted, a lot of the reason I don't like this game is probably because I'm beginning to realize that I just don't like open-world survival crafting games.  Especially early access ones (which all of them are).  Conceptually, they seem cool, but I get sick of having to farm and gather and craft every single thing I use in the game.  It just seems like a shallow mechanic to stretch out the gameplay and dangle a carrot in front of the player.  "It's not fun now, but we promise it will be after you farm the stuff and build the thing!"  The worst example I can think of in that regard is This War of Mine.  I kind of liked that game, but the player's progress is bottlenecked so severely through the scarcity of supplies that it all becomes overwhelmingly tedious.  When done effectively, scarcity of ammo and supplies can add to the tension, but that's not what happens with TWoM, and it's not what happens with ARK.
Overall it's a decent concept with the humans and the dinosaurs and the strange futuristic/prehistoric setting.  And it looks cool, but I can't recommend it unless you really really really love early access open world survival crafting games.

To overcome the ridiculous amount of bad reviews I shall post mine. I have done a bit of research into this game and played a LOT of this game.
The BAD: DLC in early access was an incredibly unpopular decision and I think the chief cause of these negative reviews for an otherwise VERY popular game. Partly because nobody wanted to pay for something before the initial purchase was redeemed. And also because they are fearful that it will set a precedent for future Early Access games dividing their product unfairly. The other very problematic thing is that in the patchnotes for the base game it was stated we would get a desert biome. That has now been removed from the vanilla patchnotes shortly before the release of the DLC Expansion pack. Now this could either be an indication of downright shenanigans, or merely another example of the sometimes hilariously bad communication Wildcard has with the public. (Id est: the last two sales for this year [2017] were stated to have lasted from 2016-2016.) it's not like they don't communicate, it's tat they are bad communicators and that they seem to not know themselves when an update will need pushing back. Also the game (espescially on console) has bad UI at the moment. Clipping is a huge issue at times, and the inclusion of free trans-server travel on PVP servers was another somewhat unpopular and unusual (but not unprecedented) choice. Also tameing and breeding dinos especially can take forever. HOWEVER.
The GOOD: There is NO other videogame exactly like ARK. There are similar videogames in the works like "The Isle". There are older games that I think clearly inspired ARK: Rust, Minecraft, and Toruk. But nothing is really that big crazy dinos on the loose hardcore survival/sandboxgame. Words can't describe this game. It's the game you didn't know you wanted. As for the Early Access DLC, it is a genuine expansionpack in the spirit of what expansionpacks should be, also development of Scorced Earth started sometime in Dec of 2015  (I know this from an old interview from before that month) by a separate design team from the main team.(I know this because I asked them and that's also how videogames are made: modularly) This was 6 months before the original release date of the game. The fact is Ark has been so successful that the Devs redefined their objective and made the game far more ambitious than before. And the simple fact is that contend adding comes before bugfixes since adding more content adds more bugs. This is how games are made. Anyone complains about this logical aspect of Ark's design process should be fed to the troodons. (lolz just kidding.)
Another potential reason for the weirdly early release was the fact that Wildcard was settled a lawsuit for about 40 million dollars to Trendy Entertainment and Insight Venture Management. Clearly they may have wanted more money to keep up with their new ambitions. And as long as the initial patchnotes stating the inclusion of a desert biome in the vanilla game are either ultimately fulfilled, (technically can't you play a desert mod in vanilla?) or if the patchnotes were not meant to be taken as solid promises but more like tentative goals (or just bad communication) then there is technically nothing all that wrong with the Early Access DLC. It is receiving regular updates along with the base game after all!

What I like about Warframe:
Free to play: everything is obtainable for free, even platinum (the currency you can buy with real money). You can sell your rare items and mods to get platinum. I myself obtained hundreds of platinum by selling unwanted items.
Free DLC: Devs constantly update the game.
Trading: I like trading and getting that plat, don't get me wrong, I hate the trading chat, that's why I use a site called warframe.market.
Grind: Now some people see grind as a bad thing. But in Warframe's case grind is good because if you like the game then it's enjoyable to grind.
Different mission types.
Customization AKA Fashionframe.
Uranus (If you know what I mean).
Warframe (class) variety: at the moment there's 28 different warframes.
Melee combat: from slashing and dashing with swords to ragdolling enemies all over the map with a hammer
Parkour: after all it's a ninja game :D
Modding: collect mods, upgrade them, make your own build (or multiple builds) for each warframe!
Having my own spaceship: hanging out in my own ship or being stuck in menus? I'll take the ship please.
Kubrows: who doesn't like weird... dog... pet... things?
Carrier: this guy picks up (or vacuum's) things for you!
Rebecca... I mean Lotus.
Ragdoll: enemies flying all over the place. What else should I say?
The Second Dream: dat story tho!
Getting loot: I like my loot.
Crafting: now put that loot to use.
Community: wow I've met so many friendly people in warframe (except from that one russian guy that yels at you via voice chat).
Ordis.
What I don't like:
Chat system: seriously, you have to look for group in the LFG chat or if you want to sell something you have to spam in the cancerous trade chat. Thank god for the 3rd party sites.
Waiting for things to finish crafting: it's like you're an 8 year old and your mom buys you a toy you always wanted. And then what does she do with that toy? She puts it right in front of your face and says that you will only be able to play with it in 3 days.
Weird bugs (or whatever) that makes you disconnect in the middle of a mission: that doesn't happen that often but it does happen.
Ordis.

I was obsessed with this game for 2 weeks, it was great. But the bugs started to show up one by one and it became increasingly frustrating to accomplish anything. When the biggest adversary is the physics, you have a problem.
-The walls are basically cosmetic. Dinos can clip through them and attack objects and characters inside. They can even walk right through them or over them verticaly.
-The collisions are terrible. You fall through the world for multiple reasons. Everytime my Pteradon would buck me I'd be permanently stuck falling through the world. If you fall to your death, expect your corpse and backpack to also fall through the ground. A major exploit griefers use is to clip[ through the ground and attack your base from below. Your Wandering Dinos can fall through foundations and I would fall through my foundations into the water every time I logged in (I have a house boat)
-The PvP is fairly one sided, in that most of it occurs while the defenders are offline. Add that to the fact that unless you devote your life to farming materials, your defenses arent going to be up to par. Now add to that the tek tier weapons that are comming out and youre going to have a very hard time starting out. If youre going to PvP, you're better off finding an unofficial server.
-The devs have said they would prefer to push out as much content as possible before working on any bug fixes, so it's going to be a while if at all before these issues will be fixed.
-Paid DlC for an early access game. The entire idea is just offensive.
I would gladly play this again if they fixed a lot of the bugs, but from what the devs have been saying, I'm not going to hold my breath.

After 2 years of playing this game (I spent more time playing the non-steam version because of personal hardware restrictions back then), this is what I think is a F2P 3rd person co-op shooter done right.
Believe me, it is not exactly Pay-2-Win, but more of a Pay-2-Skip-The-Waiting-Process. Even then it's usually worth the wait for most parts.
At first, new players might be overwhelmed by the content of this game. And that is true, since the tutorial didn't really offer detailed explanations on how each of the features work. However, with the help of the wiki and its community, it should be easier for them to sink in to the gameplay.
Also, the leveling system here is a bit different than the usual MMORPG style. First of, there are two types of 'level' in Warframe:
1. Gear Rank: Each and every "Warframe" and weapons will have these that can be leveled up to rank 30. every rank gained will provide more 'mod points' for inserting mods, which in turn will improve their overall performance.
2. Mastery Rank: This pretty much depicts your overall ranking in the game. Higher ranks will unlock more weapons to use. Mastery ranks are increased by maxing out the Gear Rank of each and every new Warframe and weapon you've obtained.
While it's heavily based on grinding, just remember these three things:
1. Every Warframe has its own unique set of skills and playstyle, and every weapon has their own strength and weaknesses. You'll eventually find the combination that suits you the most, so go and experiment with all of those gears!
2. Everything can be obtained without spending actual money (Warframes, weapons, resources, consumables can be crafted), aside from the majority of cosmetics and quick access to specific resources (the latter can still be obtained through grinding). And trust me, whenever you've actually decided to spend money on this, it'll be worth every damn cent.
3. May RNGesus be with you. Because like I said before, Warframe revolves around grinding (Aside from modding your gear). So if repetitive gameplay isn't your cup of tea, this might not be for you (although that's pretty much how most loot-based games go). You can choose pay to skip certain parts of the grind, but remember that even then, most of the better gears will not be available until you've reached a higher Mastery rank in the game.
All in all, if you're up for some fast-paced third person shooter with good graphics and content, I'd heavily recommend this. You get to be a gunslinging-bladeswinging space ninja, spreading death and terror throughout the solar system, what else do you need?

Graphics optimization is garbage. I have to set things on low/medium using a 1070. Hopefully this gets improved.
And yet, I love it. It's amazing. Once the kinks are worked out, and I'm sure they will be, this is going to be an amazing game.

After 2 years of playing this game (I spent more time playing the non-steam version because of personal hardware restrictions back then), this is what I think is a F2P 3rd person co-op shooter done right.
Believe me, it is not exactly Pay-2-Win, but more of a Pay-2-Skip-The-Waiting-Process. Even then it's usually worth the wait for most parts.
At first, new players might be overwhelmed by the content of this game. And that is true, since the tutorial didn't really offer detailed explanations on how each of the features work. However, with the help of the wiki and its community, it should be easier for them to sink in to the gameplay.
Also, the leveling system here is a bit different than the usual MMORPG style. First of, there are two types of 'level' in Warframe:
1. Gear Rank: Each and every "Warframe" and weapons will have these that can be leveled up to rank 30. every rank gained will provide more 'mod points' for inserting mods, which in turn will improve their overall performance.
2. Mastery Rank: This pretty much depicts your overall ranking in the game. Higher ranks will unlock more weapons to use. Mastery ranks are increased by maxing out the Gear Rank of each and every new Warframe and weapon you've obtained.
While it's heavily based on grinding, just remember these three things:
1. Every Warframe has its own unique set of skills and playstyle, and every weapon has their own strength and weaknesses. You'll eventually find the combination that suits you the most, so go and experiment with all of those gears!
2. Everything can be obtained without spending actual money (Warframes, weapons, resources, consumables can be crafted), aside from the majority of cosmetics and quick access to specific resources (the latter can still be obtained through grinding). And trust me, whenever you've actually decided to spend money on this, it'll be worth every damn cent.
3. May RNGesus be with you. Because like I said before, Warframe revolves around grinding (Aside from modding your gear). So if repetitive gameplay isn't your cup of tea, this might not be for you (although that's pretty much how most loot-based games go). You can choose pay to skip certain parts of the grind, but remember that even then, most of the better gears will not be available until you've reached a higher Mastery rank in the game.
All in all, if you're up for some fast-paced third person shooter with good graphics and content, I'd heavily recommend this. You get to be a gunslinging-bladeswinging space ninja, spreading death and terror throughout the solar system, what else do you need?

I wanted to like Warframe, but it's too complicated for itself. I liked it for the first few levels, but I soon noticed that the weapons I chose in the first mission. I chose a bow, a pistol and a staff. Not a good idea. I bought a blueprint, but it turns out that doesn't mean I get the weapon. There's more flaws than that. The game requires a third party account which takes a while to set up. Also, Warframe has too many microtransactions to be a good F2P. I think the devs tried to impliment a plot, but its so useless that it doesn't belong in the game. Also, Warframe's weapon modding system is terrible. In Warframe you can pick up mods for weapons, but not supplies needed to make weapons? Warframe's levels are open-ended, but that doesn't help, in fact, I think it just makes the game less enjoyable. I don't understand what the devs were thinking when they put the ship mechanic in. I would've enjoyed Warframe a lot more if you could explore planets. Also, there's almost no enemy diversity. Every one looks the same, and they all use the same weapons, look the same, etc, etc. Before I continue into telling you about the few good things about Warframe, I have to talk about microtransactions and how this game tries to be what it isn't. The one thing Warframe does what it wants to do correctly is being a third person shooter, but I'll talk about that later. Warframe is like Payday 2 in terms of microtransactions. You must buy in-game currency if you actually want to get a weapon. 5 bucks gets you like 500 coins, which is like half what you need for a decent weapon. Also, Warframe tries to be an MMO, which it really isn't. It's just a co-op game with a chat where you can talk to hundreds of other players. Ok, time to a be a little positive. What Warframe does best is be a co op third person shooter. The open ended levels aren't as bad when you mix it in with the good traversal system. The gunplay isn't bad, either. Warframe also has runs very well, and the graphics are pretty good. By default Warframe runs in a window, which is a little strange if you ask me. As you can see, I wouldn't recommend Waframe, that is unless you have a wallet that makes its own money. It performs well, and is good as a co-op third person shooter. It's free and there's not much to lose (except for a few hours of downloading and making the third party account) but it's all personal preference. If you're computer can run it, and you're willing to cash out a lot of time and money, then go ahead, play it. I'll keep enjoying other games with friends. I'll give it another try another time, but I don't plan on it being any time soon.
If you do decide to try it, and enjoy it, maybe you can explain to me as to why some people like it.

I have to give this game a cautious recomendation, its fun, but it is extremely repetitive and arguably "p2w" because of the grinding.
Pros:
1. The graphics are pretty good for a corridor shooter, nice lighting, effects (physx if you have it), and decent textures. Also its very well optimized. Never once dropped below 60fps on max settings with a mid ranged pc, even while streaming.
2. The gameplay is pretty fun, its a 3rd person shooter with a fun movement system and a large variety of warframes and weapons each with differant abilities, stats, and looks.
3. You can aquire everything in the game without paying for the ingame currency, there are a lot of paid for items in the market, including items you need to be viable for the endgame (orikin reactors, orikin catalysts, warframe and weapon slots) however you can trade with other players and get platinum from them by selling them valuable mods or parts to prime warframes or weapons

4. One of the nicest communities ive played with. So many veteran players offered to show me the ropes and actually gifted me items to get me started. I had many players taxi me through higher level content to help me get some decent weapons and warframes, all for free, just them wanting to help newer players.
Cons:
1. The grinding is absolutely ridiculous. I stated above that you need the orikin reactors and catalysts to be viable for the endgame and currently the only way to obtain them is to either pay platinum or wait for the biweekly alerts after dev streams to get a blueprint that will give you one, but you have to build it using resources and wait for it to finish building. If you want a weapon or warframe to be viable at all mid to late game you need to use these items on them to increase the mod capacity and if you add up the cost of making the warframes and weapons (especially the prime variants) and having to put a reactor or catalyst on each one of them, the playtime and grinding required is astronomical.

2. The game has a PvP component but its an absolute joke. You dont get anything decent from it and its poorly balanced.

3. Warframe and weapon slots. This system is incredibly frustrating paywall BS that forces you to build inventory slots for each warframe or weapon you build, otherwise you cannot use it. They start you off with 3 warframe slots, 2 open and the rest you have to pay platinum for. As i stated above you can aquire platinum ingame but this is adds to the insane amount of grind required to be viable mid to late game as you not only have to pay platinum for the reactors and catalysts, but also the slots for the warframes and weapons. Also the only way to progress into higher leveled weapons and content is through the Mastery Rank system, which you earn points for leveling each warframe and weapon up to level 30, which you cannot do unless you either pay the platinum for the slots, or delete weapons and warframes that you have put a shiitload of work into, and you dont get the reactors and catalysts back after deletion.

This game has an amazing idea behind the gameplay. Ark however is void of a plethora of simple and complex optimizations to make the game more enjoyable and fun. The good things about the game is that the sandbox feel, and impact on the world is successful. The survivor feels like he/she is making a lasting impact in the world around them. But Just some of the things I have noticed are irksome to say the least. As one person of the vox populi I feel that many will agree. The community I hope would also add onto any ideas they have in a constructive fashion regarding small tweaks/optimizations to improve gameplay and quality of life.
The escape menu should not have "Exit to main menu" as a second option where the default mouse courser position generally is over tribe manager. I feel that is an unspoken rule in gameplay development that the first Option is Resume, the second - options, then the third a core gameplay feature manager e.g tribe manager or something. Exit to main menu should always be at the bottom and options should always be second from the top.
The game has an outstanding and unparalleled environment and scenery, but this is taxing on a vast majority of computers. The fact that View distance does not change the render distance of the environment but rather boulders and dinosaurs is dumbfounding. A person that wants a lower view distance wants to see less of everything because it is so resource intensive to run.
Have floating names Person and dino independent. So you can see your tribe member without having to see your dinosaurs names.
Following Nameplates, Have floating nameplates for other survivors (maybe not on PvP) and health bars. On official servers we want to be able to associate to the environment around us not have to kiss a dinosaur or struggle with aiming a Spyglass. The aforementioned things are incredulously unforgiving to new players.
The Tribe Manager Rank settings is not intuitive in the sense of "maximum withdraw" associating with the rank you are editing. To me at least It seems like an over complication of a simple feature. To me it should be simple in the sense of who do you want to use what, how far above or below other ranks will they be.
Something to touch on also I the fact the game is early access despite you releasing other maps and expansion packs. I feel that it is not only myself that feels rather cheated of a wholesome and quality gameplay experience. People feel let down when you have a product that is still no way near as great as it potentially could be,yet you are happy to sell extensions and expansions without solving the existing problems. I can say personally I feel that the developers are just after financial gain instead of pleasing their community with a well rounded gaming experience.
Various graphical settings that are not intuitive or don't do what you think need to be worked on. render distance, camera views, Water detail, light blooms and sunshafts, anti-aliasing etc.
There is no tutorial which throws  individuals into the deep end. The idea is good, this is ARK, there is no help. However with an unintuitive gameplay and core design features this can rapidly become overwhelming and void of fun.
Many would agree and consequently many may not agree with what I have said. This game is incredible and has immense potential it just needs to focus on optimization instead of gameplay additions. If the creators were more involved with the community and actively sought feedback and responded to constructive criticism; the game would flourish. A stronger interaction between Developer - community/player, will keep me playing and please those that already play.
ARK: Survival Evolved has a lot to offer; consequently a lot to improve. It's majority unintuitive design is  contrasted by the conceptual idea behind the game itself. To those considering this game as a gift or maybe for themselves I would recommend the game. Ark however, is far from its final form and has a long way to go before it is fully evolved.

Sooo... Warframe. Heard of this game quite some time ago, but got my hands on it just now. And boy, it surely delivers.

Basically, it's freemium title that could be a full 40-60$ game, with its RPG elements, massive amount of content and such. Sooo... Yeah. Good game, nice mechanics, and despite some RPG elements, it's a shootery enough game so that it FEELS like a good, solid shooter. Worth trying out.

This game has an amazing idea behind the gameplay. Ark however is void of a plethora of simple and complex optimizations to make the game more enjoyable and fun. The good things about the game is that the sandbox feel, and impact on the world is successful. The survivor feels like he/she is making a lasting impact in the world around them. But Just some of the things I have noticed are irksome to say the least. As one person of the vox populi I feel that many will agree. The community I hope would also add onto any ideas they have in a constructive fashion regarding small tweaks/optimizations to improve gameplay and quality of life.
The escape menu should not have "Exit to main menu" as a second option where the default mouse courser position generally is over tribe manager. I feel that is an unspoken rule in gameplay development that the first Option is Resume, the second - options, then the third a core gameplay feature manager e.g tribe manager or something. Exit to main menu should always be at the bottom and options should always be second from the top.
The game has an outstanding and unparalleled environment and scenery, but this is taxing on a vast majority of computers. The fact that View distance does not change the render distance of the environment but rather boulders and dinosaurs is dumbfounding. A person that wants a lower view distance wants to see less of everything because it is so resource intensive to run.
Have floating names Person and dino independent. So you can see your tribe member without having to see your dinosaurs names.
Following Nameplates, Have floating nameplates for other survivors (maybe not on PvP) and health bars. On official servers we want to be able to associate to the environment around us not have to kiss a dinosaur or struggle with aiming a Spyglass. The aforementioned things are incredulously unforgiving to new players.
The Tribe Manager Rank settings is not intuitive in the sense of "maximum withdraw" associating with the rank you are editing. To me at least It seems like an over complication of a simple feature. To me it should be simple in the sense of who do you want to use what, how far above or below other ranks will they be.
Something to touch on also I the fact the game is early access despite you releasing other maps and expansion packs. I feel that it is not only myself that feels rather cheated of a wholesome and quality gameplay experience. People feel let down when you have a product that is still no way near as great as it potentially could be,yet you are happy to sell extensions and expansions without solving the existing problems. I can say personally I feel that the developers are just after financial gain instead of pleasing their community with a well rounded gaming experience.
Various graphical settings that are not intuitive or don't do what you think need to be worked on. render distance, camera views, Water detail, light blooms and sunshafts, anti-aliasing etc.
There is no tutorial which throws  individuals into the deep end. The idea is good, this is ARK, there is no help. However with an unintuitive gameplay and core design features this can rapidly become overwhelming and void of fun.
Many would agree and consequently many may not agree with what I have said. This game is incredible and has immense potential it just needs to focus on optimization instead of gameplay additions. If the creators were more involved with the community and actively sought feedback and responded to constructive criticism; the game would flourish. A stronger interaction between Developer - community/player, will keep me playing and please those that already play.
ARK: Survival Evolved has a lot to offer; consequently a lot to improve. It's majority unintuitive design is  contrasted by the conceptual idea behind the game itself. To those considering this game as a gift or maybe for themselves I would recommend the game. Ark however, is far from its final form and has a long way to go before it is fully evolved.

This game is SO much fun.  When you first start, you will die, repeatedly.  Once you become very experienced, you will die only when you take chances you knew were risky...
Now, I see a lot of people complaining about PVP.  It's your choice to play PVP, and play on servers who don't have good rules for that.  It's your choice to play on PVE servers that allow pillaring and other tactics that detract from game play.  This game is incredibly customizeable.  If there's something you don't like going on, then choose a server where it's not going on.  The game continues while you're offline, which is unique - but this is only true of the multiplayer servers.
Some servers have a 20 minute lock in place, so your things cannot be damaged or altered while you're offline.  (After 20 minutes, your base can't be touched).
The option to play solo on your own computer means you don't have to put up with other people at all, if you don't want to - and the game is still tremendous fun and a great challenge.  Or, set up a private multiplayer game, and invite only your spouse or closest friends - the game is active when you're on, and not when you aren't, when you play solo or private multiplayer.  This means you don't have to worry about things decaying or being destroyed while you're having a normal life.
The game is basically Minecraft Pokemon Jurassic Park.  You don't need other human players to make it challenging - really.  It's huge, and there's a tremendous area to explore and a lot to learn.  That's what makes it so addictive and so much fun.
But it IS an early access game.  It has bugs.  Sometimes updates will break things - even to the point where you can't load your saved game.  And sometimes the next update fixes them, so you can load it again.  (This happened).  Dinosaurs are frequently stuck in the scenery, everything clips through walls and objects quite a bit, and occasionally the physics engine will send something you have killed 2000 feet into the air, to land who knows where.  But none of those things prevent the game from being huge fun.
Note something about a lot of the negative reviews.  Note the amount of time those people spent playing this game.  If they really hated it, why did they put in 200+ hours playing it? :)  Obviously, they love the game, and are just disgruntled over some aspect that is currently annoying them.
Give it a try.  If you don't like the lag or social issues on official and open servers, then try a solo game.  You won't be disappointed.

8/10
Pros:
- Great animations, movement feels fluid and fast
- A Fun and flashy co-op experience (up to 4 players and 8 for raids)
- Tons of weapons (yes, by now it's just getting gratuitous)
- Unique system of modding weapons and warframe abilities, lots of combinations
- Passable PVP, fun yet unfortunately still not as popular as it could be
- Enjoyable PVE, lots of missions that are rewarding and enjoyable to blast through
- Rewarding end-game with enhanced prime warframes and weapons that keep you playing for a long period of time
- Fun and unique community events with exciting rewards such as cosmetics or weapons that ae entirely new and exclusive to the event
- Forma system which allows you to reset your weapon/warframe's level when at max rank (level 30) to grant the user a polarity slot so that you can fit more mods on your gear, keeps the game fresh and extends shelf-life
- Deep and well-written lore keeps the hope of new and exciting experiences alive as the game's story continues to unfold with new content
Cons:
- Super grindy! If you don't enjoy games that can get repetitive and dull after a time this game may only be worth a couple hundred hours to you
- End game equipment can be extremely frustrating to obtain, new items have dramtically decreased drop chances to keep you shackled to running the same level over and over again
- Questing is less than immersive, great voice actors, terrible lines. Only now are quest driven cutscenes being implemented into the game, even though it shows potential the questing is still sometimes dry and boring
- Irritating characters, namely Ordis, your ship's AI who's dry wit and poorly timed repetitive dialogue merritted the developers patching in a volume slider just for him.  Boss dialogue is more goofy than threatening, again also repetitive.
- Game is heavily loot based which requires a hefty time commitment in order to obtain and progress smoothly, even though it's not required some players (such as myself) well develop an obsession for collecting all the weapons or warframes in the game where as if you're just starting now you will have missed some content that may have been phased out or only set to appear during the occassional event.
Ultimately Warframe is a fantastic example of a highly innovated MMO third-person shooter.  It's essentially Destiny for the PC with more or less bells and whistles.  You can't beat FREE and it's very easy to get hooked on the combat and visuals which are all very attractive to behold.  Unfortunately after dumping over a thousand hours into this time-sync of a game, you'll probably start to feel really burned out.  The repetitive events which are (at my level) not challenging and more of a chore, the cheesy voice-acting and quest objectives, again a chore, running the same level over and over again for a chance at getting a piece of an item that you want to build, literally a chore; at the end of the day it really leaves you wanting more or at least more depth to keep things fresh and exciting.  The developers have put a wealth of time and effort into making this game continually exciting for their players but sometimes you'll find yourself coming back to the game just to pick up that one weapon or to blow through that two-week long event in about 2 hours and then go back to doing whatever it is you were playing before.  Again if you're new, or if you enjoy games that require repetition and grinding for long periods of time, this is definitely a game that won't disappoint you or your inner hoarder.

If you've got a powerful rig this can be a very entertaining and time consuming game. Out of all the survival games I've played this has to has the most features and content. Although it has quite a lot of content ranging from crafting, building, taming, different maps and even caves to explore... It seems the devs are contiuously adding content without much thought of the people who are currently playing their game and their experience.
Dinosaur features: You can tame, ride, build bases on, use in battle, use as mules, use for creature specific buffs.
Base building: You can build bases ranging from simple thatch to steel fortresses. You can build Dinosaur pens, green houses, base defenses such as ballistae, cannons and even plants to defend your base.
Item crafting: You can craft a wide variety of armor and weapons, along with other items such as boats. This game probably has the most diverse crafting system I've seen.
WORKSHOP! +
Things to consider if you're looking to purchase this game...
Most importantly, this game is very unpredictable whether it'll run decently on your system or horribly. If you've got a powerful rig chances are it'll run fine, HOWEVER, there's many people who experience otherwise... Personally I'm on a 970, i7 4790k with 16gb of ram and this game runs perfectly fine.
This game is in ALPHA and has a plethora of pros as well as cons.
You can see the direction Ark is going in and, if you're not unlucky, get to enjoy playing the game with stable fps.
If you're planning on playing on unofficial servers (which is likely) you'll have a lot of steam mods to download which conveniently it does automatically... allbeit buggy as hell sometimes... so make sure you've got alot of data!
Lastly, I definitely recommend this game but only for genuine fans of survival games who happen to also have a beefy rig. I DO NOT recommend this game for people w/o beefy rigs.
TLDR:
- Recommended for survival genre fans with good gaming rigs.
- Not recommended for people who can't handle FPS spikes.

Ark...where to begin?
Graphics are a solid 10/10 if your system can handle it. I highly recommend that one does NOT play this game on a mobile gaming rig...Ark blew out the motherboard of my Eon 17-X gaming laptop (this is after I lowered the settings to minimum, applied some proper thermal compound, used a cooling pad, etc). Had to mail it back to the US from China which then raised a hellstorm upon trying to get it back here to Beijing (Import taxes and fees).
tl;dr play it on a desktop with proper cooling or not at all.
Music and ambient sound effects are decent enough - no bugs encountered as far as static/ hiccups, and none of the creatures have any particularly off-putting sounds.
Gameplay, while difficult and facing a STEEP learning curve, is not impossible. There are a few bugs such as all of your flying mounts hopping off of whatever you placed them on onto the ground, thus rendering them vulnerable. Note that gameplay varies greatly between Singleplayer and Multiplayer. Playing on Multiplayer in China SUCKS as a laowai (foreigner) - you get raided constantly the moment you announce yourself by typing anything and the Chinese I've encountered in separate attempts on various servers know little English other than "F YOU F YOU I F YOUR MOTHER HAHAHA." One can attempt to play on a server far away but good golly does it suck when you're flying on the back of some beast and the server drops the connection due to high ping.
You essentially lose your flying mount and all of your belongings forever...this prompted several of my friends that I talked into buying this game to quit playing as the game became a struggle either against all of the dinos AND the server, or a stable server that was run by the rapacious Chinese.
So the move to Singleplayer was made. It was fun enough but without buds to play with...became boring. The joy of any Open World Survival game is doing it with your friends or other people. Solo gameplay is not only tedious but also downright impossible should one want to attempt to retrieve any of the /spoiler artifacts in-game. I managed to finally pull off one of the more difficult caves on The Center only by hitting the console commands and giving myself an inventory full of ammunition.
So altogether if you can get a solid group of people together to play this game on a decent server where you understand the native language (Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic, etc appears as solid boxes so you can't even screenshot and attempt to google translate with a scanning device) and are playing this on a non-exploding device such as a desktop PC, then you can expect to have a pretty damn good time.
4/5
It would be great if they would optimize the game. and improve graphics instead of adding content. more manpower to fixing the game instead of blindly adding more content to a half broken game.

I was going to write a super long sentimental post about this game, detailing my intimate experience with the game, however most of  the people reading these want something fast, so before I lose your attention, here is my shortened review.
Download if: you enjoy loot based games, RNG, space ninjas, melee combat, third person shooters, parkour, fastpaced gameplay, PvE
Don't download if: You prefer tactical realistic gameplay, you think that PvP is the most important mode in any game and should come first, you hate grinding, you find procedurally generated levels lazy. You hate random drops.
PROS:
Godtier parkour
Good balancing of melee and ranged combat
Each 'frame feels unique
Missions are fun
Large variety of weapons
Great community
Lots of customization
Great fun with others
Regular updates so that when you do get to a high level, you rarely go long without a new event to do or a new item to obtain.
Premium Currency can be acquired through trading items with other players.
CONS:
Lackluster description as to how modding works
Later planets in the solar system are near impossible to clear solo
Crafting timers on weapons/warframes that you create
RNG plays a large part in this game. While I enjoy RNG, it does get very frustrating to have the last component never drop for you (Oberon Systems blueprint I'm looking at you)
While I don't mind it, it takes a while to collect required resources/parts to craft new stuff. Although this does make new gear feel more valuable
Favorite parts of the game:
The core gameplay feels great, the endgame content is far more substantial, that along with semiregular content   drops means that you rarely go more than a month or two without new missions/quests/items. The general artstyle of the game is very unique.

It almost feels like, when you step into the game and start from scratch, the island slowly builds to your playstyle so you can adapt too, including how to catch food to sustain yourself, how to start making tools to help on your adventures, how to avoid larger predators that stalk the island in the search for blood, how to find, tame and befriend the many creatures of the island and how to keep yourelf safe when darkness cloaks the island, you will always have a thrill on the isle of ARK.
As for the creatures themselves, they are so diverse and incredible to look at, it almost feels like your not in a game, but more of a documentary with David Attenborough (love that guy!). the diversity is astonishing from start to finish, you have for example, the pegomastax, which a nice addition for i felt bored just carrying around items and not being able to feed the animals of the wild, well now, "chiyo-chan" here is a cute, new addition with a rather amusing gimmick, going near it will cause "chiyo" to leap around and attack you, then grab an item from your invatory, and run away like an embarrassed anime school girl,  it's hilarious!
Then further into the game you encounter more creatures, like the snoozy Megalosaurus, the Therizinosaurus, who not only just wants some privecy, but think of it as the (manly voice) "edgy" rethinking of Golden Darkness from to love-ru, pelting enemies with wolverine-style claws, the Castoroides, which is so good at lumberjacking it's almost broken, the Titanosaurus, the "edgy" Bronto-godzilla hybrid (still waiting on someone to do that sort of thing guys) and the giganotosaurus, or as i like to call it, DANTE'S 7 CIRCLE OF HELL! MWUHAHAHA! But still, he's one tough sid to pop, i wouldn't recommend waking him up in the morning.
Alas, it doesn't stop there, for there is also, flying and aquatic reptiles, mammals and insects, some examples are the recent Tusotheuthis (PRAISE KRAKEN), the Manta ray who can kick up a deadly storm if not handled right, the Tapejara, who is basically like having a helicopter that strafes, the Quetzalcoatlus who can make entire AIRCRAFTS cry in terms of transportation, the Arthropleura (Good luck sleeping tonight, kiddies!) and the Beelzebufo, who loves his insect legs somethin' real good!
As for the bosses, while there are three of them, make up for with amazing stratagy, the first boss, the Broodmother is a giant arachnid that spews poisonous acid and summons spiderlings to do her bidding, the Megapithicus (PRAISE KING KONG) and the dragon (admittingly that's a boring name) that loves to burn his foes to doritos!
And that's not the end of it all! A new land was discovered in september of 2016, new and rare beasts were discovered and mysterious relics leading to the greatest discovery of all time are out there, are you worthy enough to find the treasure of scorched earth?
Ultimately, i can't wait for this game to leave early access, it's potential as an amazing game is so good, that it's officaly my favourite game of all time, end this review by saying long live the wildcard team and good luck to all on the ARK! :)

Fish Sauce Fried Chicken
Ingredients:
about 2-3 pounds chicken drumsticks or thighs, skin-on and bone-in
For the marinade:
1/4 cup (60ml) vegetable oil
1/4 cup (60ml) fish sauce
1 Tablespoon (15g) Brown Sugar
1 Tablespoon (15ml) rice vinegar
4-5 large cloves garlic, finely minced or crushed
1/2 teaspoon fresh ground black pepper
For frying:
1 cup (125g) all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon (5) baking powder
about 2 cups (480ml) cold water
Oil for frying
Directions:
Make the marinade: In large bowl, combine the vegetable oil, fish sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar, garlic and black pepper. Set aside.
Rinse the chicken and pat it dry. Add the chicken to the marinade and gently toss the chicken in to get it coated evenly. Marinate the chicken for at least 1 hour (2-3 hours preferred) so the chicken can soak up all the flavor. Gently stir up the chicken in the marinade at least twice during the 1-3 hours so that all the pieces of chicken get an even soak in the marinade.
Make the flour coating: In a large bowl, combine the flour and baking powder. Slowly add the cold water and mix well with a fork. Start with about 1.5 cups and add more if needed. Break up any clumps of flour so that the mixture is smooth. What you want to get is a thick and moist flour mixture that will cling to the chicken.Please see reference photo on the post
Heat a large frying pan or Dutch oven. Fill the pan or Dutch oven with oil about 1-in deep. Heat the oil to 350-375 degrees F.
Gently remove the chicken from the marinade and let the excess drip off. Dip the chicken in to the wet flour mixture. Allow excess to drip off and place the chicken in the hot oil.
Cooking in small batches, fry the chicken on both sides till crispy and cooked through, about 10-15 minutes. Don't crowd the chicken.

¿Que es WarFrame?
Es un juego de Disparo en tercera Persona donde eres un Robot/Extraterrestre/Ninja...
OK OK OK Ya es Descripcion Suficiente. Fuera de eso, desde un punto de vista menos Subjetivo, la posivilidades de Parkour, Gran variedad de Armas, personajes, modo Sigiloso, Multijugador al igual que SoloPlay le añade una gama de maneras para terminar una mision. A veces menos es mas y para ser un jugador del primer año del Alpha, las actualizaciones no se han desviado mucho del concepto original.
Podria Considerarse un PayToWin pero la posibilidad de Vender tus Objetos por Cash a otros usuarios lo mejoran mucho.

The Community:
It isn't cancer. Everyone is friendly, even the veterans who are maxed ranks always are helpful. You will occasionally get a guy who just acts like he's better than everyone else and noone can climb his ego, but you get that anywhere. 9/10 for the community rating.
The Gameplay:
Excellent mix of gunplay, melee combat, ability combat, and companion mechanics! Being able to slide around and jump 50 meters in the air, while shooting an enemy, slamming a giant axe down on another, then unleashing your ultimate on a group in front of you is just always satisfying. There is a variety of missions, weapons, Frames (basically characters), and items to keep you entertained for a long time, and although it does either take a TON of work and time to get these (this can also be bypassed completely by purchasing Platinum, one of the two in-game currencies), it still will keep you feeling acomplished and wanting more. There is also so many combinations/varieties of ways you can mod your weapons, frames, and even companions, to get some awesome buffs and an overall edge in combat. The combat mechanics gets a 10/10 because they literally give you so many combat options, and it is sooo much more polished than what it used to be a few years back.
Free to Play? So it's Pay to Win right?:
The game is mainly a co-op game, and there really isn't a competitive aspect to it, so I wouldn't necessarily call it Pay to Win, I'd call it Pay to Skip weeks of hard work and frustration. It is 100% possible to obtain every single item in the game (minus exclusive frames/Items that aren't obtainable anymore, but may be at some point) without shelling out a pennie, but you would be talking months, maybe even a year to complete and catch up with the updates, which they are always adding new stuff to keep it fresh. You are able to obtain Platinum by completing missions and objectives to obtain Prime items (an upgraded version of a weapon/frame) and then sell them to other players in the trading channel for platinum. You could even merch off items if you had the time and bought the right items cheap and sell them for more. All in all, it's not a pay to win game and if you wanted to buy platinum, all you would be doing is supporting the development of the game and thanking them, in a way.
Negatives/Complaints:
-The modding system, crafting system, navigation, and sydicate system is criminally underexplained. They need to make it more friendly to new players and make a quest of some sort that has them upgrade a mod to complete a mission in some way and write a lot of dialogue for Ortis to explain how this system works, because I found myself reading the wiki, watching videos, and asking others how these things worked.
-If you are someone who doesn't have a whole lot of time on their hands, you won't really be able to progress much in this game, because it takes a buttload of hard work and time to progress, without spending money on platinum. This game is all about the GRIND. If you don't have time, it will take you even longer to progress in this game.
-At times, the missions become more and more repetitive and it starts to kill your motivation. They are at work at trying to improve these problems and I have faith that it can be done, with time.
In conclusion, I would rate the game 8/10. It has those 10/10 moments all the time though, so its a very full cup sitting at 8/10. Thanks for spending the time to read this review
EDIT: Even more amazing with the Plains of Eidolon Update

The core of politics is the struggle to get or keep power. Much as the media like to portray it as strictly a partisan thing, politics has a personal side as well. That’s what I write about. And sometimes, a story becomes a series, like these…
Maira Bundis
What if the reason it’s so difficult to take action against global climate change is that the wealthy few who control the world’s great corporations have realized that it can be even more profitable than war? In 2095, the sea wall that kept the Pacific Ocean from submerging the California lowlands all the way to Sacramento has collapsed, and the official story is that it was terrorists. Infrastructure analyst Alphon Quince knew it was a lie. What he didn’t know was what they were willing to do to protect that lie.
1. “Bait” (Sep 2013) — Alphon knew the Golden State Barrage wasn’t destroyed by explosives. The government was lying again. But why?
2. “Hollow Threat” (Nov 2013) — Ferd couldn’t wait to see what the mystery package they’d ordered contained. Meg would never know.
3. “Under an Icy Sky” (Dec 2013) — They’d gathered to honor Meg’s memory, but ended up with others too dreadful to shake.
4. “In the Company of Vipers” (Jan 2014) — Phoebe’s trip home didn’t exactly go as planned, but it wasn’t because of the terrorist in the next seat.
5. “Standing to Resist” (Feb 2014) — The last thing you want when you’ve just hijacked a military drone is company, especially if they’re armed.
6. “Lightning Strikes” (Mar 2014) — Victor thought the nightmare he had after a confrontation with his parents was bad, until he got the call from work.
7. “Maira Bundis” (Jun 2014) — Exposing a ‘terror mastermind’ might have been the highlight of Cinquetta’s career. Now she’ll never know.
Confidence
Have you ever held your tongue when someone made an offensive remark, or yielded to an unreasonable demand just to ‘keep the peace’? Each time you do it, you lose some self-confidence, and the perpetrator is emboldened. (I blogged the process of turning that thought into the first story in this series.) Councilwoman Sue Winston hadn’t lost a political fight yet because she hadn’t been in one. But when her brother called with a hot tip, she knew she had to put her own neck on the line and try to prevent a calamity.
1. “Crossing the Line” (Sept 2012) — Newly elected councilwoman Sue Winston had never even been to the Occupy in her district. Now she has to protect it from her brother.
2. “Making it Count” (Sept 2012) — Kendrik just watched a livestream of his grandmother being arrested for using the People’s Mike, and his mom expects him to go to school? Get real.
3. “Scaling K2” (Dec 2012) — When what remained of the capitol’s OWS saw Kendrik’s interview, they knew they had to act. But how?
4. “Representation” (Apr 2013) — The developer who had the mayor evict OWS wants the site rezoned, but the council room has been occupied as well.
5. “Kendrik House” (May 2013) — Councilman Flange went off-script stumping to create a virtual district… way off script, but that’s not the problem.
6. “Authenticity” (Jun 2013) — The city’s homeless could also benefit from Flange’s scheme, except for the six that were just killed.
7. “Engaging Constituency” (Jul 2013) — A lash-up of OWS and the homeless community may have won the special election, but can they agree on a representative to city council?
Riffing the Life Fantastic
What if you knew your future? That was Ben’s curse. (Mine was that I didn’t know his name until the third installment.) He’d been born with memories of the important turnings of his life, memories that had netted him several fortunes. The trick to landing his next one was to trash his motorcycle on the highway, a crash he was guaranteed to walk away from. Try explaining that to the officer.
1. “Riffing the Life Fantastic” (Dec 2010) — Living out my memories of the future was profitable before, but this was the first time it meant risking my life.
2. “Divine Intervention” (Dec 2010) — With my memories of the future having run out, who or what was directing my life?
3. “Fairy Dust” (Jan 2011) — To Ben, life without a safety net could be scary, so how does anyone else do it?
4. “Outlier” (Jan 2011) — Ben’s comforting memories of the future may have run their course, but they’d led to a different kind of nightmare.
5. “Toasted Roles” (Feb 2011) — Steeling himself to talk with the cops should have ended it, but all it did was expose him to Franklin’s nightmare.
6. “Particle Wave” (Feb 2011) — The side-trip to Ben’s salvation should have been a breeze, but now there’s a fly in Kaylee’s ointment.
7. “Prices to Pay” (Feb 2011) — Ben returns to Kansas to face his past, but instead finds his future.
Corporate Punishment
Several years before Mitt Romney assured us that “corporations are people, my friend,” I wrote this series in which a fictional Supreme Court granted them that Pinocchio wish. But being people cuts both ways, for they were also subject to the legal consequences of committing crimes.
1. “Logical Conclusion” (Aug 2007) — The Supreme Court finally gave corporations complete personhood, and I was determined to make it stick.
2. “Full Circle” (Sep 2007) — FW’s CEO Edward Reese lay in wait for Randolph Starling. Swatting down the upstart should have been child’s play.
3. “Prison Break” (Sep 2007) — Reese saw the company’s sentence as a game, and he was determined to win.
4. “Turnabout” (Sep 2007) — Now that FW’s parole officer Claire Fuller had given union rep Alizondo Klee a seat at the table, he wasn’t about to let Reese have his way.
5. “Serving Time” (Nov 2007) — The prison-garbed FW Diner employees may have been the pawns in Reese’s game, but they weren’t about to let him run their lives.
6. “Going Down” (Nov 2007) — When Blogger John Frachetti ducked into a re-fitted FW Diner to hide, nobody there knew the true power unleashed by Reese’s scheme.
7. “Unplanned Outing” (Nov 2007) — Claire Fuller visited the FW Diner for a quiet meeting behind bars with Alizondo Klee. Too bad it didn’t turn out that way.
8. “Unvarnished Siding” (Nov 2007) — Claire Fuller didn’t find her voice until Judge Clary confronted her.
9. “The Tallysheet Bankers” (Dec 2007) — Blogger John Frachetti hesitated before entering the FW boardroom. He needn’t have.
10. “Bank Shot” (Dec 2007) — Being guest speaker at the FW union hall was a daunting prospect for blogger John Frachetti, so he decided to listen instead.
11. “Signing Statement” (Mar 2008) — Unemployed artist Leetha Berismont decided to splurge on a dinner at the FW. Now her future isn’t looking so bleak.
12. “Frachetti’s Challenge” (Apr 2008) — Leo Agrolkin spent his off-hours from his job at the FW blowing jazz around the chain. Maybe there was something better he could use that time for.
Synthetic Rights Now
Why is it so easy for people to feel superior to whatever segment of humanity is unlucky enough to be ‘The Other’ this week? Maybe someday, everyone will finally get past that and treat one another as equals. Who will we pick on then? (Soon after I posted “The A Word”, a reader asked for a follow-up. I succumbed a few days later.)
1. “The A Word” (Jun 2006) — When I explained my civil rights case to Lamar, I detected some reluctance to take it on.
2. “Edifice of Lies” (Feb 2008) — Joanna Bjornsen held the key to our freedom. It was a good thing I held the gun.

tl;dr It's not a "skill game", it's a collect and level game. Great for time wasting, great fun in the beginning but terribly buggy when you push the mechanics. You pay to eliminate the crafting wait, otherwise you will wait for everything.
-( GOOD STUFF )-
- Warframe is fun and very polished.
- A variety of unique frames and weapons to destroy interesting and varied enemies with.
- Gameplay is smooth and extremely fluid. There's a lot of depth to the parkour and general movement in the game.
- Incredibly interesting universe with great backstory and very memorable encounters and characters.
- ITS FUN!!!
- Bugs are fixed.
- Not a bad public game community.
-( BAD STUFF )-
Have you ever played an F2P game online?
Warframe has the exact same pros and cons you get in most other F2P modeled games: content creation is prioritized over improving what's already there. You can't monitize bugfixing. However you can monetize content.
- You get stuff. You level stuff. More stuff. Level stuff. More stuff. Level stuff. More stuff. Level stuff. etc.
- The bugs are fixed,
- except those buggy areas of the game that have never been fixed and the developers refuse to acknowledge exist.
--- When you google bugs, you find those sycophantic "I LOVE THIS GAME" people who keep insisting that "The bugs are fixed." Yeah, except those that have NEVER been fixed and dont seem likely to be fixed soon.
- In late game Survival mode I'm more likely to die to: a stuck door, a lagging console, a wrong/broken timer/counter, a broken weapon animation, a broken weapon switching animation, my warframe animation bugging out or broken reload animations, than I am likely to die to any intentional game mechanic. Bugs should NOT be a gamer's biggest fear in your game. Some say it's a minor inconvenience, I say it's disrespectful to your milk-cow... uhh, customers? Consumers, is the word I was looking for. Consumers.
- Some maps are bug-rotten concerning their doors, their modes, enemy spawns etc. Modes like Exterminate (kill X amount of enemy) have recently been broken by the devs and kind of fixed again (couldn't finish the missions due to bugs).
I want to love it but it keeps breaking before I can really delve into the mechanics. When players have to develop in-game habits to deal with the constant buggery then you know you have a problem. When your community views your game as bloated while ignoring large chunks of said bloated game, then you know you have a problem.
-( Crafting and/or Real Money )-
Oh yeah, you can buy anything with real money. Crafting  weapons and frames takes anywhere from 12 to 72 hours to craft. Many items have components that take 12 hours each. The late game is levelling items while you wait for other items to finish crafting so you can level them too. So 12 hours at a time, there's no crafting queue, you have to log in regularly to grind your items for rank so you can access more items to grind so you can rank more so you can grind more items... inevitably this is where you end up.  You pay per component to eliminate the wait. Otherwise you wait.
F2P standards applied to another good idea. F2P has an unmistakable character.

Warframe is a third person shooter with small elements of nijitsu spread around. it is also an rpg but doesnt really do well on the rpg part and heres why;
1. Poor story
well almost every free to play rpg has a bad story but this isnt even an accurate plot. i was in the first chapter and all of the sudden i play a planet ahead and i jump to the final chapters (so far). the quest system doesnt really tell you what to do and when it does it wants you to grind for materials so you can build an item. people say its easy but when you're a beginner with no idea of what to do, you're basiclly doomed. plus noone plays on the first 3 planets so expect to go in solo unless you get a friend to help you.
2. Crafting system/ Build system
this shouldnt even be in the game but its there to force you to spend money to get through quicker. in order to get new weapons you have to buy blueprints of them, and collect materials for them, some of which are only avilable in one planet. its basiclly a game of russian roulette where you have to play levels over and over just to get that one piece for that new sword your getting. and when you do get the materials, you have to wait a day or two for it to build. dont forget there are level requirements (duh i know) on the weapons, but you get blueprints of high level weapons even if you're bearly master rank 1 or 2. its a paywall basiclly.
3. Levels/ Planets
Remember that rock from mars? well your gonna find that exact rock and spot in venus. what about that cave with the crashed ship in pluto? oh wait its at neptune. if you feel like your getting deja-vu, well dont be surprised because the levels in one region are the same exact layout in another region. so dont expect a new hallway because there wont be one.
4. Tennos
so the "ninja robots/aliens" aka tenno are all unique. they all play diffrently and they all have diffrent abilities and purposes. the basic all round tenno most people choose is excalibur, which is a pretty cool tenno when i first played, but soon he will become useless and you will need a new ninja to join the fight, all you got to do is fight the same boss 6 to 8 times to get blueprints of the body parts of these tennos and wait 3 days to build. dont want to go through that process? pay ten bucks and you get it instantly.
yay pay2win.
5 Gamemodes
eerrr yeah there are gamemodes into these planets, and some require more than one player to be successful so good luck going solo in the first 3 planets! most are defence missions and theyre quiet boring honestly. have fun protecting a computer from a wave enemies who decide to melee you instead of shooting you.
6. NPCs
you know how this is a ninja game? the idea of sneaking around in vents and doing kickass assasinations? well throw that idea out of the window! these guys have no idea how to aim and most will try to stab you rather than to shoot. some will even stare at you in plain sight for 5 seconds before reacting.
overall, its not that i hate the game, the game CAN be cool if you play the right levels, but most of the time you will be smashing e and spacebar to get somewhere. so unless they remove the paywall (which theyre not) the game isnt fun unless you play with a buddy.

For example, a mod that added ammo max was useless, then update came that increased ammo consumption of a weapon (I am not joking), so all of sudden the same weapon is eating ammo like crazy, thus making a useless mod, more useful, for a price of losing a spot of 8 possible mods, to a ammo increase mod or ammo mutation mod. The same happened with other weapons, where some weapons are simply stronger than others, and the rarer mods you have the stronger you are ingame. As I said, if it involved some skill then great, but even the normal exploits, the gameplay that is not cheating, you follow the rules and all, became banned, so if you stand in same spot and just shoot at things, you can become afk (away from keyboard) like a bot is playing in your stead, and lose the mission rewards, as well as not receiving bonuses from mission. Voting system, where if someone is indeed afk and not playing, to just vote him out, or if all other players are and you want out, that you can leave (now you can't leave). Tenno out of ten m8's.

The Good:
- Unique artstyle. Each faction is visually distinctive: The Tenno are biomechanical, sleek, and graceful in a powerful way. The Grineer are round and brute, as if they're made in a production line. The Corpus are square and streamlined, with function over form. The Infested are... disgusting. And the Orokin are like the Tenno but golden.
- Gameplay is fun, if repetitive, and makes you feel powerful. You're a space cyborg mutant ninja annihilating hordes of lowly mooks while running and jumping around like a hyperactive gazelle high on coke.
- Each frame feels,looks and plays unique. Throw fireballs around, cut your enemies in half while invisible, turn enemies against each other, become a blade master with an energy sword, release the kraken on hordes of unsuspecting Lancers, and much more. No two frames are the same.
- The devs, despite making some (BIIIIG) mistakes, listen to community feedback, and often try to fix their mistakes.
- While some bosses are still generic goons with a different paint, some of the reworked bosses are unique and memorable. Tyl Regor's smooth jazz voice, Alad V's slightly flamboyant mannerisms, and Kela de Thaym's over the top boasts, all are very difficult to forget.
The Bad:
- Grinding. Lots and lots of grinding and farming. And I mean LOTS. Be prepared to run the same missions over and over and over and over and over again, hoping to get that item with 0.1% drop chance.
- Enemy scaling is 50 shades of fu***d. At high levels, if you're not properly equipped, get ready to tickle away at basic troopers while they kill you with 2 shots (3 if you're a tanky frame).
- Enemy AI is stupid. They run straight at you with little to no strategy. Different units have almost no synergy at all.
- No variety in modding weapons. Damage mods are mandatory, Multishot mods are mandatory, if your weapon has high critical chance and damage, you'd be stupid to not put Crit mods. Elemental mods are also mandatory, though you have a but of variety based on what faction you'll fight (Radiation + Viral for Grineer, Magnetic + Toxin for Corpus, Corrosive + Blast for Infested, and Corrosive + Cold for Corrupted).
- Terrible new player experience. Though recent updates have tried to address that, most new players get lost too easily, and have no idea what to do.
- The devs sometimes make some very stupid decisions, like nerfing weapons that did not need nerfs, buffing enemies that are already too strong (looking at you, Nullifiers), and removing/nerfing popular grinding spots.
The Awesome:
- Waifus. Cyborg Ninja Mutant Waifus.
- Husbandos too.
Overall, despite all these glaring flaws, Warframe is still a great game, and you should definitely give it a try.

8/10
Pros:
- Great animations, movement feels fluid and fast
- A Fun and flashy co-op experience (up to 4 players and 8 for raids)
- Tons of weapons (yes, by now it's just getting gratuitous)
- Unique system of modding weapons and warframe abilities, lots of combinations
- Passable PVP, fun yet unfortunately still not as popular as it could be
- Enjoyable PVE, lots of missions that are rewarding and enjoyable to blast through
- Rewarding end-game with enhanced prime warframes and weapons that keep you playing for a long period of time
- Fun and unique community events with exciting rewards such as cosmetics or weapons that ae entirely new and exclusive to the event
- Forma system which allows you to reset your weapon/warframe's level when at max rank (level 30) to grant the user a polarity slot so that you can fit more mods on your gear, keeps the game fresh and extends shelf-life
- Deep and well-written lore keeps the hope of new and exciting experiences alive as the game's story continues to unfold with new content
Cons:
- Super grindy! If you don't enjoy games that can get repetitive and dull after a time this game may only be worth a couple hundred hours to you
- End game equipment can be extremely frustrating to obtain, new items have dramtically decreased drop chances to keep you shackled to running the same level over and over again
- Questing is less than immersive, great voice actors, terrible lines. Only now are quest driven cutscenes being implemented into the game, even though it shows potential the questing is still sometimes dry and boring
- Irritating characters, namely Ordis, your ship's AI who's dry wit and poorly timed repetitive dialogue merritted the developers patching in a volume slider just for him.  Boss dialogue is more goofy than threatening, again also repetitive.
- Game is heavily loot based which requires a hefty time commitment in order to obtain and progress smoothly, even though it's not required some players (such as myself) well develop an obsession for collecting all the weapons or warframes in the game where as if you're just starting now you will have missed some content that may have been phased out or only set to appear during the occassional event.
Ultimately Warframe is a fantastic example of a highly innovated MMO third-person shooter.  It's essentially Destiny for the PC with more or less bells and whistles.  You can't beat FREE and it's very easy to get hooked on the combat and visuals which are all very attractive to behold.  Unfortunately after dumping over a thousand hours into this time-sync of a game, you'll probably start to feel really burned out.  The repetitive events which are (at my level) not challenging and more of a chore, the cheesy voice-acting and quest objectives, again a chore, running the same level over and over again for a chance at getting a piece of an item that you want to build, literally a chore; at the end of the day it really leaves you wanting more or at least more depth to keep things fresh and exciting.  The developers have put a wealth of time and effort into making this game continually exciting for their players but sometimes you'll find yourself coming back to the game just to pick up that one weapon or to blow through that two-week long event in about 2 hours and then go back to doing whatever it is you were playing before.  Again if you're new, or if you enjoy games that require repetition and grinding for long periods of time, this is definitely a game that won't disappoint you or your inner hoarder.

¿Que es WarFrame?
Es un juego de Disparo en tercera Persona donde eres un Robot/Extraterrestre/Ninja...
OK OK OK Ya es Descripcion Suficiente. Fuera de eso, desde un punto de vista menos Subjetivo, la posivilidades de Parkour, Gran variedad de Armas, personajes, modo Sigiloso, Multijugador al igual que SoloPlay le añade una gama de maneras para terminar una mision. A veces menos es mas y para ser un jugador del primer año del Alpha, las actualizaciones no se han desviado mucho del concepto original.
Podria Considerarse un PayToWin pero la posibilidad de Vender tus Objetos por Cash a otros usuarios lo mejoran mucho.

The Community:
It isn't cancer. Everyone is friendly, even the veterans who are maxed ranks always are helpful. You will occasionally get a guy who just acts like he's better than everyone else and noone can climb his ego, but you get that anywhere. 9/10 for the community rating.
The Gameplay:
Excellent mix of gunplay, melee combat, ability combat, and companion mechanics! Being able to slide around and jump 50 meters in the air, while shooting an enemy, slamming a giant axe down on another, then unleashing your ultimate on a group in front of you is just always satisfying. There is a variety of missions, weapons, Frames (basically characters), and items to keep you entertained for a long time, and although it does either take a TON of work and time to get these (this can also be bypassed completely by purchasing Platinum, one of the two in-game currencies), it still will keep you feeling acomplished and wanting more. There is also so many combinations/varieties of ways you can mod your weapons, frames, and even companions, to get some awesome buffs and an overall edge in combat. The combat mechanics gets a 10/10 because they literally give you so many combat options, and it is sooo much more polished than what it used to be a few years back.
Free to Play? So it's Pay to Win right?:
The game is mainly a co-op game, and there really isn't a competitive aspect to it, so I wouldn't necessarily call it Pay to Win, I'd call it Pay to Skip weeks of hard work and frustration. It is 100% possible to obtain every single item in the game (minus exclusive frames/Items that aren't obtainable anymore, but may be at some point) without shelling out a pennie, but you would be talking months, maybe even a year to complete and catch up with the updates, which they are always adding new stuff to keep it fresh. You are able to obtain Platinum by completing missions and objectives to obtain Prime items (an upgraded version of a weapon/frame) and then sell them to other players in the trading channel for platinum. You could even merch off items if you had the time and bought the right items cheap and sell them for more. All in all, it's not a pay to win game and if you wanted to buy platinum, all you would be doing is supporting the development of the game and thanking them, in a way.
Negatives/Complaints:
-The modding system, crafting system, navigation, and sydicate system is criminally underexplained. They need to make it more friendly to new players and make a quest of some sort that has them upgrade a mod to complete a mission in some way and write a lot of dialogue for Ortis to explain how this system works, because I found myself reading the wiki, watching videos, and asking others how these things worked.
-If you are someone who doesn't have a whole lot of time on their hands, you won't really be able to progress much in this game, because it takes a buttload of hard work and time to progress, without spending money on platinum. This game is all about the GRIND. If you don't have time, it will take you even longer to progress in this game.
-At times, the missions become more and more repetitive and it starts to kill your motivation. They are at work at trying to improve these problems and I have faith that it can be done, with time.
In conclusion, I would rate the game 8/10. It has those 10/10 moments all the time though, so its a very full cup sitting at 8/10. Thanks for spending the time to read this review
