After reading a lot of recent reviews, I've come to realize that everything is situational. All of the recent negative reviews I've read leave out the fact that the devs have opened the door for unofficial servers to correct some of the issues players have with the official server content.
I started out with hundreds of hours on a PvE Official server and came to realize that I just don't have the kind of time it takes to solo even on PvE. I tried PvP Official but encountered a desolate wasteland of immature adolescents roaming the hills griefing everything they could while the major tribes had no use for me until I could manage to level up.
My next foray was into Unofficial servers. As a father of four who works 70+ hours a week, increased rates servers were more sensible for me. A lot of recent reviews point to unbalanced gameplay and admin abuse, which I'll grant happen a lot and are huge turn-offs. What they fail to mention is that after some time browsing around, you can and will find a server that meets your needs and have one of the best gaming experiences available. New mods are constantly being developed by an awesome workshop community that extend and enhance current features as well.
Ark doesnt have to be a second job, a relentless grind, futile struggle against megatribes or badmins. It can be all of those things for sure, but take the time to look around and see what fits your style. You'll be surprised what a little research can yield.

Let me give you a comparison to a game that had a five-hundred million dollar budget compared to this game that literally took funding from its fans in the beginning.
Destiny
--------
-Declines previous content
-Useless endgame progression with no reward
-Terrible developers lacking in communication and experimenting on its fanbase
-Decent story not present in game
-DLC/Microtransaction Scheme worse than Payday 2's
-Unbalanced combat system
-Near meaningless events
-Ungodly RNG system
-Lack of Customization
-MANY, MANY, features cut from the game
-Hard to even enter some content
Now lets talk about Warframe.
--------------------------------
+Tries to reinvigorate its mechanics by creating overhauls (Combat 2.0, Movement 2.0)
+Free To Play
+Procedurally Generated Levels
+Frequent updates and hotfixes
+Large amounts of gun customization
+Good/Decent Character customization
+Awesome and helpful community
+Steam Workshop Support
+/- Story seems somewhat unclear (That could just be me, though the Second Dream clears up a few of my questions)
+/-Microtransaction system is very present in this game (Though with some help from friends, randoms, guides, or even the Recruiting chat tab you can get just about anything without paying for a dime.)
+/- Beginners may have a tough time trying to be good at endgame
Overall, Warframe is a very good game and can get very addicting with friends.

I've been playing the game on and off in early access for the past ~14 months, and while it was understandabe that it had some rough edges when it was an early access product, I'm convinced that the developers have no intention of fixing some of the game breaking bugs that have existed the entire time. Not least of which because the exact same bugs that drove my friends away from our private server half a year ago are still in the game today!
One of the central features of the game is taming and breeding of dinosaurs and other wild animals.  This is a time and resource intensive thing to do making your tamed dinos prized posessions.  Unfortunately the game has fundamental glitches that cause tamed dinosaurs to die or disappear for no reason.  I know this because I ran a tribe on a password protected PvE server with friends only, and we were constantly having our tamed dinosaurs de-spawn.
I had been giving the devs the benefit of the doubt but after checking recently to see what their status was on this game breaking bug, I've learned that Wildcard barely acknowledges the problem and usually dismisses it as 'it's in beta'.  That's not going to fly now that the game is released and this bug can eat dozens or hundreds of hours of taming/breeding progress at a whim.
While some of their community mods have at least acknowledged the problems, their last attempt to fix it was half a year ago...
As a post release sanity check I decided to hop in and see if they had fixed the new player experience either (another rough spot) - even being a veteran player who has hundreds of hours in the game it was a horrible ordeal to put myself in the shoes of a new player.  I spawned in an 'easy' zone and got shreded by compys within two minutes.  After resapwning I was immediately set upon by raptors and murdered.  After respawning a 3rd time I harvested long enough to reach level 2 but then got torn about by a dilophosaur.  This is the problem with completely randomized spawns in that it makes the NPE potentially hellish, and will likely turn off a lot of people before they even give the game a chance.
I can't recommend buying this game until the developer gets their priorities straight and decides to start fixing this and other game breaking bugs rather than trying to sell DLC while still in early access, then season passes for future DLC.

I personally only play on official servers as I have had too many bad experiences with the unofficial ones, so this review is mostly about the official servers. Also, I only play on PvP servers.
When the game was first released it was such an awesome game. Everyone had fun and everyone made a lot of friends on the server. We fought with some tribes, traded with others and even made alliances or merged with other friendly tribes.
As time went on, more and more dinos were introduced to the game and the fighting became more and more boring and the alpha tribes got bigger and bigger leads on the other tribes on their server.
I was a member of the alpha tribe on my server and we tried to keep our server friendly and peaceful. When trolls/griefers joined our server, we would protect the other tribes. When anyone needed help, they only had to ask and one or more of us would come over and help out any way we could.
Then, however, WildCard introduced the cross-server mechanism, where you can take dinos and items from one server to another. This destroyed the community on pretty much all of the official servers, as the alpha now had to worry about other alphas invading their server(s). After a while, this lead to a very toxic environment on most of the official servers, as alpha tribes wiped out everyone who wasn't them, as the other tribes were just a liability, or worse, spies.
This is when I quit the game, as I do not enjoy being alone on a server without any other tribes, constantly farming for more bullets and rockets to defend against possible mega tribes invading our server some day in the future.
Our server went from pretty much always being full (which brought its own set of problems) to being populated by max 5 players (our tribe was spread out over a bunch of servers) in a very short amount of time. Gone were the days of just hanging around in my public tavern and having friendly conversations in the chat with other people.
Another thing I am unhappy about is the number of different species of dinos. There is so much overlap between dinos now and so many obsolete dinos. And if you combine the awful performance of the game/servers with a number of different species of dinos, you get very few dinos per species compared to the way it was before, making it so much harder to find good dinos. You might say it's a good thing to have more choice in what kind of dino you want, but you don't really have a choice, as you will always go for the one with the highest efficiency for a specific task.

This is easily the most fun game I ever played and it never get's old. There's always new things to try, build or explore. I seriously highly recommend this game.

If i could give this game a "meh" recommendation, I would; because there are so many good things about Warframe surrounded but several large issues.
Let's start with the good:
+story is relatively good
+parkour is really fun in the middle of a pitched battle
+guns are cool looking, interesting, and (more or less) balanced
+warframes themselves are generally unique with very different styles of gameplay (Frost tank ftw)
The story is pretty good when you consider that this is F2P, but mediocre if I was forced to pay for it; it also takes a ridiculous amount of time to get to each story quest (more on that later).
Now, the negatives:
-story takes FOREVER to get into
-the only parkour anybody actually uses is the bullet jump, because all the other mechanics are buggy and hard to control at best
-the entire RNG system is reliant on players' ability to farm rather than players using farming to get around RNG (explained below)
-rooms for each map are recycled multiple times in the same map; In other words, you can travel through the exact same room model multiple times in one level before finishing it. Every single level in warframe does this.
-game has a bad case of "devs don't play their own game": devs are far more interested in shoving more content in your face than fixing the bugs that have defined this game since the beginning
Let's start with the story. In a similar game, the story would be there for you to experience at your leisure while the majority of the actual game content had to be earned by playing the game; in warframe, it's the exact opposite. You need to FARM to unlock the story quests. you want to guess how you unlock basically anything else in the game? You gessed it: FARMING. The whoel RNG system AND story progression is only unlocked by hours upon hours of farming the same god damn enemies and areas.
OR you can pay for whatever you want. Now I know fans are immediately thinking "but the in-game market doesn't allow you to purchase prime items with real money so it's not pay-to-win" and they're right in the fact that you can't purchase primed items from the game. Instead you can purchase anything you need from other players for almost twice their actual value using in-game currency you can pay for with real money. I'm not trashing the devs here (i know they need some kind of revenue to keep going), but please do not praise warframe for being completely F2P with absolutely no P2W involved, because that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
I know I spent more time on the negative than the positives, and there is a whole lot more I would like to say on the fact that probably 150 fo the 200 hours I have played have been spent farming or sitting in my ship arguing over market prices in chat. But even with all that, I still think it's a decent F2P game in a world of P2W monstrosities.
6/10 at least try it out
P.S. plz stop comparing this to destiny 2; the only thing they have in common is loot-based RNG mechanics. It's like comparing a pumpkin to a watermelon (because they're both big and round) and saying the watermelon is better because it's jiucier. I get why people are♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥about Destiny, but at least compare it to another game with dimilar gameplay

+guns are cool looking, interesting, and (more or less) balanced
+warframes themselves are generally unique with very different styles of gameplay (Frost tank ftw)
The story is pretty good when you consider that this is F2P, but mediocre if I was forced to pay for it; it also takes a ridiculous amount of time to get to each story quest (more on that later).
Now, the negatives:
-story takes FOREVER to get into
-the only parkour anybody actually uses is the bullet jump, because all the other mechanics are buggy and hard to control at best
-the entire RNG system is reliant on players' ability to farm rather than players using farming to get around RNG (explained below)
-rooms for each map are recycled multiple times in the same map; In other words, you can travel through the exact same room model multiple times in one level before finishing it. Every single level in warframe does this.
-game has a bad case of "devs don't play their own game": devs are far more interested in shoving more content in your face than fixing the bugs that have defined this game since the beginning
Let's start with the story. In a similar game, the story would be there for you to experience at your leisure while the majority of the actual game content had to be earned by playing the game; in warframe, it's the exact opposite. You need to FARM to unlock the story quests. you want to guess how you unlock basically anything else in the game? You gessed it: FARMING. The whoel RNG system AND story progression is only unlocked by hours upon hours of farming the same god damn enemies and areas.
OR you can pay for whatever you want. Now I know fans are immediately thinking "but the in-game market doesn't allow you to purchase prime items with real money so it's not pay-to-win" and they're right in the fact that you can't purchase primed items from the game. Instead you can purchase anything you need from other players for almost twice their actual value using in-game currency you can pay for with real money. I'm not trashing the devs here (i know they need some kind of revenue to keep going), but please do not praise warframe for being completely F2P with absolutely no P2W involved, because that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
I know I spent more time on the negative than the positives, and there is a whole lot more I would like to say on the fact that probably 150 fo the 200 hours I have played have been spent farming or sitting in my ship arguing over market prices in chat. But even with all that, I still think it's a decent F2P game in a world of P2W monstrosities.
6/10 at least try it out
P.S. plz stop comparing this to destiny 2; the only thing they have in common is loot-based RNG mechanics. It's like comparing a pumpkin to a watermelon (because they're both big and round) and saying the watermelon is better because it's jiucier. I get why people are♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥about Destiny, but at least compare it to another game with dimilar gameplay

I personally only play on official servers as I have had too many bad experiences with the unofficial ones, so this review is mostly about the official servers. Also, I only play on PvP servers.
When the game was first released it was such an awesome game. Everyone had fun and everyone made a lot of friends on the server. We fought with some tribes, traded with others and even made alliances or merged with other friendly tribes.
As time went on, more and more dinos were introduced to the game and the fighting became more and more boring and the alpha tribes got bigger and bigger leads on the other tribes on their server.
I was a member of the alpha tribe on my server and we tried to keep our server friendly and peaceful. When trolls/griefers joined our server, we would protect the other tribes. When anyone needed help, they only had to ask and one or more of us would come over and help out any way we could.
Then, however, WildCard introduced the cross-server mechanism, where you can take dinos and items from one server to another. This destroyed the community on pretty much all of the official servers, as the alpha now had to worry about other alphas invading their server(s). After a while, this lead to a very toxic environment on most of the official servers, as alpha tribes wiped out everyone who wasn't them, as the other tribes were just a liability, or worse, spies.
This is when I quit the game, as I do not enjoy being alone on a server without any other tribes, constantly farming for more bullets and rockets to defend against possible mega tribes invading our server some day in the future.
Our server went from pretty much always being full (which brought its own set of problems) to being populated by max 5 players (our tribe was spread out over a bunch of servers) in a very short amount of time. Gone were the days of just hanging around in my public tavern and having friendly conversations in the chat with other people.
Another thing I am unhappy about is the number of different species of dinos. There is so much overlap between dinos now and so many obsolete dinos. And if you combine the awful performance of the game/servers with a number of different species of dinos, you get very few dinos per species compared to the way it was before, making it so much harder to find good dinos. You might say it's a good thing to have more choice in what kind of dino you want, but you don't really have a choice, as you will always go for the one with the highest efficiency for a specific task.

Warframe brings the best parts of Destiny and Metal Gear Rising with gorgeous graphics, satisfying gameplay, and hardcore sci-fi action in one free-to-play package.
Pros:
This game fulfils every childhood dream of being a ninja and an astronaught at the same time; I personally spent five minutes running back and forth across the map with Warframe's parkour system which allows the player to traverse areas smoothly and quickly without hampering gameplay.
Cons:
The only downside I found while playing Warframe was the Archwing missions.  It's a really cool idea to be able to fly around in space and fight enemies, but this mechanic is executed poorly with mostly repetitive defense or exterminate missions; thankfully there is only one archwing mission per planet, and even then they are optional.
In conclusion, Warframe is the perfect free-to-play MMO for any sci-fi junkies who want a game literally about space ninjas or just to hang with friends within Warframe's many hub areas.

I've enjoyed my time with Ark, especially early on, but at the stage of EA that I played it has some pretty glaring issues. Probably the 2 biggest problems are...
A: How the game handles disconnects.
- When you disconnect, you do not leave the game. Your body ragdolls onto the ground where you are and you're available to be attacked, drowned, robbed, etc... This actually isn't all that terrible, though I'd like to see some tweaks. The problems come from some more specific circumstances. A large part of the game is spent mounted on various creatures, and the big issue comes that when you disconnect you're also dismounted. 300 feet up in the air over dangerous territory...? Now you're on the ground, and likely dead before you'll be able to reconnect. The ragdolls almost always fall off of or through platforms, meaning that you can't log out while on a structure built over water or log out standing on top of large creatures that can support platforms.
B: The game has an ridiculous fascination with watching paint dry.
- Lots of games have a minor issue with putting annoying time sinks in. Some of Ark's most pivitol mechanics are simple a question of how long you're willing to watch paint dry. Taming creatures is just a matter of dealing with the occasional hostile creature (and I mean very occasional, over the course of an hour I'd typically kill one thing. And even then, not typically because it actually became hostile, just it got a little closer than I'd like) and occasionally pumping it full of more narcotics. Many tames don't even require that... so it's literally just a matter of standing nearby on the off-chance it gets attacked for sometimes in excess of 3 hours. Breeding creatures has the exact same problem. Babies are just a matter of keeping them full of food and on extremely rare occasion (about every 3-4 hours) doing some menial and ridiculously simple task like giving them a short walk or feeding them a particular piece of food.
Riddled with other minor issues like completely ineffective base defenses, a power creep that renders anything but end-game PvP pointless, and a server-architecture that causes consistent teleporting and rubberbanding and the game's just not in a good state at the moment. Some of these I've got a great deal of confidence will be fixed... other's I'm much more worried about and could destroy the game's playability.
I thoroughly enjoy the concept and look forward to amending this review in the future, but for the vast majority of people I just can't see Ark being an enjoyable game in it's current state.

Used to be a great idea, great concept, but somewhere along the way it became a beautiful repetitive game, that is all about grinding and randomly generated loot, where all loot stands in the way of you and having all of the great weapons and mods in the game. It can be fun, it should be fun, but now it is mostly just play something over 50+ times to get a part, then do the same for other 3-4 parts, and that is just one weapon, then repeat for the rest of it.
Take it from someone who was playing this since beta version, I do love the game and the concept, but last year was so bad with updates, that all this game is now, can be summed up in grind, grind, grind. RNG (Random Number Generetion) is killing this game more and more, where real skill is less important, and just having a rarer mod is. For example, a mod that added ammo max was useless, then update came that increased ammo consumption of a weapon (I am not joking), so all of sudden the same weapon is eating ammo like crazy, thus making a useless mod, more useful, for a price of losing a spot of 8 possible mods, to a ammo increase mod or ammo mutation mod. The same happened with other weapons, where some weapons are simply stronger than others, and the rarer mods you have the stronger you are ingame. As I said, if it involved some skill then great, but even the normal exploits, the gameplay that is not cheating, you follow the rules and all, became banned, so if you stand in same spot and just shoot at things, you can become afk (away from keyboard) like a bot is playing in your stead, and lose the mission rewards, as well as not receiving bonuses from mission. So they want me to play the same mission over 50+ times and enjoy it, even if I just came to play it so that I might receive some new rare mod/weapon part/whatever. It is not fun, it is just boring and repetitive and you want to make it last less and less, thus the exploits - for instance, you take some Warframe that is great at killing, I take one that is great support, gives energy and HP, we take a good spot and stay there for 60minutes to receive great rewards, and we repeat. Since when you defend a single spot, it is easier to defend it and you can survive for longer, they edited that so that you must move at least once per minute, and you have to move a lot, which is just annoying. Now if you use the same pattern when you move, game thinks that you might be a bot again, so forget it, I don't like it. I did give the good solution to this problem, they refuse to listen, since it is beta and still in development, and also whatever reason. Voting system, where if someone is indeed afk and not playing, to just vote him out, or if all other players are and you want out, that you can leave (now you can't leave). So you can be stuck in game with people who refuse to leave, or the host can exit the game and you lose all rewards, etc. The game has a lot of these issues, and more.
There are so many things this game can offer, and it is a great game, hours to prove it, it just became more and more something I don't like, a repetitive grind, for new weapons, for new this and that, where with every update that comes a new weapon comes a nerf (decrease of parameters) of other weapons, which makes the new weapons a must have in a way. And yes the best part is, it is still in beta, for 3 years now, maybe more, so they don't have to make excuses to you about anything, and anything that can change, will change for worse.

Since most of the reviews seem to be people who play on public servers and not on private games with several friends, and as someone who is of the latter group, I thought I'd throw my hat into the ring.
The first thing to note is that I started playing ARK in the early months of 2016 on XBOne and recently got it on PC once I did some upgrades to my rig. A more accurate representation of my playtime would be what it is now, plus around 120-140 hours from console. (PS, the host-tether on Xbox is downright cancerous, but that won't reflect in my review)
My review for ARK is a tenative recommended. I find the game very enjoyable and truly a fun time, and despite its flaws, my friends and I plan to be playing this game for a good, long while. First few playthroughs will be on the Island, one maybe two on the Center, and then we'll look to modding.
At the moment, there are a few game-breaking bugs and the optimization is garbage. I have a GTX 960, 16gbs of RAM, and an i7 CPU and I still had to give up some higher graphical settings for a playable, stable fps. Wildcard does seem to be one of those devs that hides behind early access as an excuse to not take full responsibility for bugs and glitches that render the game uplayable. However, I do have to commend them on a very active involvment with development, and have not left the game to rot on the shelf of Steam Early-Access like a lot of other games that have potential.
If you're starting out, and have a few friends that can run the game, I STRONGLY recommend you feel the game out on a private game before attempting public servers. The host-tether can be annoying at times, but it can be made to be utterly massive (if your PC can handle it), and is something I willingly give up to avoid having to play on a public server. The learning curve is so steep, it's almost a 90 degree angle, and starting out is incredibly difficult. That is a minor annoyance to this game, is that starting out is downright painful, especially with the most recent Dec 23 F-U update, which added some choice butt-monkey dinos, such as the Therizno, the Pegomastax, and the Tranq-and-Spank Troodons.
TL;DR, have some friends, have mid-to-high tier specs on your PC or don't even bother buying, don't try to pub-stomp right away, and stick to the southeastern shore until you're at least level 30.

Warframe is definitely the most amazing game I have ever played. It's combat, movement and parkour, and cooperative nature are all of quality that is rarely, if not never, found in free to play games. That being said, this game is in no way pay-to-win, literally everything can be acquired without spending money on the game except some cosmetic items. The community is also something that should be praised. On the whole, the community of this game is very friendly, helpful, and cooperative. This is matched by an equally responsive developer team. Even when I don't agree with a decision, I can at least understand that it was the general community who wanted the change. Lastly, with the introduction of the Second Dream Quest, Warframe now also has one of the most fantastic lore storylines that I have ever seen.
The only bad thing about Warframe is the grind. Sometimes it can be a bit much, but if you take breaks from the game once in a while, it will always retain its enjoyment.
As you can see with my absolutely ridiculous hour count, I love this game, and have yet to find someone who didn't, so as I always say to new players: Welcome to Warframe!
Also, find out who Clem is. His existence alone makes this game worth playing :D

Since most of the reviews seem to be people who play on public servers and not on private games with several friends, and as someone who is of the latter group, I thought I'd throw my hat into the ring.
The first thing to note is that I started playing ARK in the early months of 2016 on XBOne and recently got it on PC once I did some upgrades to my rig. A more accurate representation of my playtime would be what it is now, plus around 120-140 hours from console. (PS, the host-tether on Xbox is downright cancerous, but that won't reflect in my review)
My review for ARK is a tenative recommended. I find the game very enjoyable and truly a fun time, and despite its flaws, my friends and I plan to be playing this game for a good, long while. First few playthroughs will be on the Island, one maybe two on the Center, and then we'll look to modding.
At the moment, there are a few game-breaking bugs and the optimization is garbage. I have a GTX 960, 16gbs of RAM, and an i7 CPU and I still had to give up some higher graphical settings for a playable, stable fps. Wildcard does seem to be one of those devs that hides behind early access as an excuse to not take full responsibility for bugs and glitches that render the game uplayable. However, I do have to commend them on a very active involvment with development, and have not left the game to rot on the shelf of Steam Early-Access like a lot of other games that have potential.
If you're starting out, and have a few friends that can run the game, I STRONGLY recommend you feel the game out on a private game before attempting public servers. The host-tether can be annoying at times, but it can be made to be utterly massive (if your PC can handle it), and is something I willingly give up to avoid having to play on a public server. The learning curve is so steep, it's almost a 90 degree angle, and starting out is incredibly difficult. That is a minor annoyance to this game, is that starting out is downright painful, especially with the most recent Dec 23 F-U update, which added some choice butt-monkey dinos, such as the Therizno, the Pegomastax, and the Tranq-and-Spank Troodons.
TL;DR, have some friends, have mid-to-high tier specs on your PC or don't even bother buying, don't try to pub-stomp right away, and stick to the southeastern shore until you're at least level 30.

I played this game wayyy back when during Closed Beta, it was kinda fun but there was a lot of stupid things that they did. Fast forward to after closed beta, immediately they got rid of the horrendous weapon upgrade tree and added mods to make it more customizable.

They also fixed the glitchy movement system where everyone did spin attacks to move faster and implemented a better more responsive bullet jump/wall jump system (wall jump still needs some work in my opinion).
Pretty much every time there is something boring in the game they always fixed it to make it more fun or added new functions to the combat as well as include a ton more weapons, frames, and things to do.
It used to be boring, but now with quests, events, and now recently added 8-man raids. There are a ton of things to do.
Game is very solid and although there will be times you will feel compelled to pay for plat at times, its not a game where you NEED to pay to win. If you do, get plat if you get a discount for logging in, its not bad to support the developers, they use the money/resources to pay the developers to constantly update the game. They definitely deserve it.

Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Warframe is fun, and very pretty. There are some really nice ideas. The game is almost entirely co-op, and unlike traditional MMO's, it doesn't distract you with a 'game world' that you have to travel around in. Plays like a shooter - moreso even than Borderlands - with parkour elements. You can jump in and jump out of maps at will, which is a really great idea, reminding me much more of Left 4 Dead than World of Warcraft. You can change classes, or "warframes", at will, provided you've acquired the class. Very few classes feel the same, even when if you look at them 'on paper' or in theory, they seem to be similar.
Warframe requires significant time investment, though. There is a premium currency system which allows you to buy items - classes and weapons - but the real power in the game comes from "mods", which are random loot drops. You can buy mod packs for the premium currency, but those too, are random. You can trade premium currency for these mods with other players, but frequently you have to level them up on your own, which still costs a lot of time as you have to acquire in-game currency and items to do THAT.
Some of these mods are very basic and considered 'required' for playing certain classes or using certain typees of gear, yet you can go 100 hours without getting one. The basic gun damage mod, "Serration", is one of these, although the melee damage mod, "Pressure Point" is commonplace, guiding new players to melee combat builds, for example.
All of the character classes have basic ability to use guns and melee weapons, meaning that even if you can't get the mods to really use your class as intended, you can always sword and rifle your way through the maps.
Compared to other MMO's, the time investment required to get to certain game levels is actually pretty comparable. The problem is that there's no 'xp bar' or the like that will tell you when your next important mod or powerup will drop, only that RNG will ensure that it drops for you - sooner or later, which exaggerates the player's frustration - and the random nature of them means that it's very hard to plan your character, unless you take a fistful of premium currency to the trading channel.
I wouldn't recommend this game, but if you want to put the time into it and can deal with the random nature of your character's power curve, you could find a lot of fun playing it. The community in game is fantastic (as of this writing) and not elitist in the way you may be accustomed to seeing in other MMO's, which is really great.

Do not take my recommendation to strongly, as I have many a problem with this game. It's just overall worth a go.
The playable characters are highly customizable, and each feels unique in it's own right.
But in order to customize them well, you must obtain items from some of the harder difficulties of the game (Orokin Derelicts). And their Unique abilities are limited by essentially an ammo system, except enemies can drain, disable, or nullify this kind of ammo.
The world is vast, and, to a first time player, very rich and exciting. Your first experience with the Infested could be very memorable. But it's also very inhostpitable to new players, as the tutorial explains little to nothing on what you are supposed to do next. furthermore, the excitement quickly fades, like in all MMO's, as you spend hours playing the same portion to grind for EXP, Loot, or Credits(Currency).
The "Modding" system as a whole is a nice concept, allowing for players to alter their weapons without Developers needing to dedicate resources to create actual changes to weapon parts. (for example, "modding" in Scoping range does not change the look of the scope, so Developers can focus on making the weapon work, rather than have a fancy scope)
Warframe also has no gameplay balance to speak of. Enemies endlessly gain damage and durability, while players have a set cap on how durable / damage-dealing they can be. Thus, the only characters that are practical in late-game use are ones that can stop enemies in their tracks, such as time-freezing them. Many unique abilities are rendered useless, and thus many characters are deemed worhtless. same goes for weapons: If it does not do max DPS, it is unusable once things get tough.
And, as either a cause or and effect of this lack of balance, there is no offical game point. you start grinding levels right out the gate, and never have anywhere to go with it, except to grind more, but in levels with more damage-spewing-bullet-sponges. The game is litterally all grinding.
I, personally, have found myself playing this less and less, for once you get to a certain point, the above-mentioned flaws becoming glaringly obvious.
I still recommend this, however. It still provides a nice experience, near the beginning. Just don't expect much after you've gotten pretty far into it.

Warframe is definitely the most amazing game I have ever played. It's combat, movement and parkour, and cooperative nature are all of quality that is rarely, if not never, found in free to play games. That being said, this game is in no way pay-to-win, literally everything can be acquired without spending money on the game except some cosmetic items. The community is also something that should be praised. On the whole, the community of this game is very friendly, helpful, and cooperative. This is matched by an equally responsive developer team. Even when I don't agree with a decision, I can at least understand that it was the general community who wanted the change. Lastly, with the introduction of the Second Dream Quest, Warframe now also has one of the most fantastic lore storylines that I have ever seen.
The only bad thing about Warframe is the grind. Sometimes it can be a bit much, but if you take breaks from the game once in a while, it will always retain its enjoyment.
As you can see with my absolutely ridiculous hour count, I love this game, and have yet to find someone who didn't, so as I always say to new players: Welcome to Warframe!
Also, find out who Clem is. His existence alone makes this game worth playing :D

At first this is what I said,
"A BIG FAT YES!!!! And here is why.
After almost 200 hours I still have not been bored with the game. I have not even tamed a Rex yet because there is just so many other things to do. Whether I play alone of with my wife time seems to fly when in ARK. My wife and I actually had some get to bed at 2am "mistakes" thanks to ARK. Yes there are a couple of issues such as the optimization and the seemingly fragile design that does crash quite often, but the time spend in game does make up for it and IMO does so in a BIG way.
The crafting and the depth in which the crafting goes. The dino breeding, looking for that "super" dino offspring, taming nightmares seen only in movies and then riding them into battle. Settling down in you purpose built base looking over the plethora of beasts tamed by your hand makes for a very rewarding experience.
I know there are a lot of people that will complain about the lag and the rendering optimization and all the other little things but to me being able to escape the real world, go back in time and walk amongst creatures long extinct has a certain romance to it. Visually some of the sunsets in the game are more beautiful than some posts cards I have seen and makes ARK even more immersive.
I would not recommend this to anyone that wants an arcade game experience as this is NOT that but if you have some time on you hands and feel like taking a step back in time, come and visit the ARK, but be warned time might catch up with you......."
Now however its definitely not the case anymore. If you have any semblance of a real life you will never be able to enjoy the end game content unless you play either on a crazy boosted server or have made a conscious decision to neglect/abandon any or all other things/priorities in life. I have heard people say WoW/Dota/LoL to be family destroyers and the like but this is on a whole different level. The time it takes to breed proper dinos to compete in end game content, the imprinting, the feeding all set to real life alarms is just plain ridiculous. Sleeping for 4 hours in a 48 hour period just to make sure your dinos have a 100% imprint does not sound healthy to me. Not to mention the time needed to obtain all the resources for the above mentioned.
Don't get me wrong I still play ARK and love every minute of it but on my terms on my local dedicated server, which when time is up or real life comes knocking I can stop. switch of and come back to when I have the opportunity. My local server affords me the freedom to do all the fun stuff but with the option of "quitting the game" and coming back to exactly where I was before I left with out worrying about dying dinos or breeding being influenced negatively or anything thing like that which is not the case when you join public servers.
So my negative review is not about the game being in a bad state or useless Devs or any of that, it about the time sink it will become if this great game really gets hold of you.

Ok so, let me ask you guys one thing. Would you like to,
1. Be a ninja.
2. Be a ninja in the future.
3. Be able to do all those ninja jumps and flips without having to press thousands of keys.
Well i can safely say Warframe delivers this and a lot more, being able to complete many missions with a variety of weapons including many different melee weapons starting with a standard sword.
Now of course maybe you're thinking, i've heard from others it's pay to win, not true, paying to win should only apply to games that are mainly PVP. Warframe does have a PVP mode but it's priority is on a COOP scale. You may use money to buy many new things such as warframes (your class) or different weapons, attachments, colours, skins, pets, sentinels, components, parts for your warframe, etc.
But don't be put off by this, the games unique because almost anything you can buy with Platinum (the ingame money you used your well earned cash on), you can buy with Credits which as you guessed is the standard money set for the game. Lets say you want a new melee weapon but you don't want to spend any real money on this because you're unsure how the game may turn out, well you can purchase "blueprints" for nearly anything in the game. So you purchase a new sword blueprint with your credits, now! You can't just jump in with creating it, because you need components, and to retrieve these components you need to do missions! However different planets have different components so you need to play missions to unlock more missions that will unlock more planets thus getting more components. Now if you're still with me you can now use new said components to create your sword you've worked so hard for, but now you have to wait maybe 12 hours for this sword to create, so now it's up to you whether you relax or carry on playing to get more components for even more items! Then we'll fast foward and VOILA! Your new sword is ready for combat.
Now, the leveling up system, your weapons all have a max rank of 30, or at least thats where mine say max rank, your warframe however can get much higher but there's somewhat of a twist to this. Like on most shooters today, you get to a max rank and then can "prestige" as most of us know it to be, but with this say you get to level 10, you then take a test to prove to "The Lotus" that you are capable of using your weapons so you'll use your primary weapon to fight numerous waves of enemies. When you have completed this you'll be level 10 still but next to your name will be "1", then again with level 20 you'll take another test and then instead of "1" it will now be "2"...complicated enough? nah you guys are smart.
Mods, use these to make your weapons stronger and your warframe more powerful, mods are slotted in when available, hence needing to level up your gear. These mods can cause more damage, elemental attributes, quicker speed, longed range etc...etc.
If this wasn't enough you can also obtain "Sentinels" and "Kubrows" to fight alongside you and of course these guys can be upgraded as well. But to obtain them you must complete missions further on in the game to accomplish this task!
Bottom line this game might need a lot of grinding but at least you get the feeling of achievement, you've put your time and hard work into gathering the components to create a new weapon because you liked the look of it, now you can use that weapon to succeed in more missions to then create even more weapons or warframes.
So if my review has peaked your interest in wanting to try out for yourself then feel free to, if you don't fancy having a go then no problem, my review is not meant to be persuasive but informative.
Enjoy Warframe :)

When I first bought this game, it was a laggy mess with a spattering of well known, boring dinosaurs, and I didn't really play it. Then I noticed it had been getting updates upon updates upon updates, and I revisited it. It was optimised - it seems to be optimised for some people and not for others, so I'd try it out and if it isn't, refund it - it had hoards of new creatures with interesting skills, like wall climbing and huge leaps, and a ton of new items and mechanics.
I now play this a little like I play skyrim. Skyrim, I play infrequently, however I play for long bursts of just Skyrim and then a long gap. ARK, I play frequently, with medium bursts of just ARK and then long periods of ARK and other games, followed by short periods of no ARK. Sometimes I play with cheats because the game has a long-game style of crafting, unlocking and experience points, as well as requirements to unlock the higher tear, and I often find that I like messing around with this stuff. I also play without cheats, which is even more fun, although I do recommend increasing the taming speed on any singleplayer worlds you have.
I also often play with mods from the workshop, which, if they have enough potential and work put into them, become offical mods, like The Centre and Ragnarok. Other mods add new and useful stuff - what I'm saying is, the game has an active and productive modding community if that's your style.
I'm not too much of a fan of PvP, so I tend to stick to singleplayer or non dedicated multiplayer (just friends), however, I can tell that the game is meant for multiplayer - there's always something missing in the singleplayer: the threat of an enemy tribe, although that's to be expected.
In my experience, the game is brilliantly optimised, updated infrequently enough for me to be sure it should be out of Alpha, but frequently enough for me to know the devs are still working on it, and full of boundless things to do. The DLC - Scorched Earth has, at least - add entire new ways to play the game, so they're worth it too.
TL; DR
Buy it now. It's worth it. Trust me.

If you enjoy the same repetitive gameplay over and over again, you'll probably like warframe more than I do. But I seriosly can't play too much more of it.
The maps aren't randomly generated, but the order in which you access different parts of the maps are. Just imagine a map with rooms being shuffled around every time you play. It ends up being a dull and repetitive experience, at least for gamers who cannot deal with repetitiveness. The combat feels so buggy and yucky, but considering you're most likely going to be spraying at everything anyway, it won't matter much. There's no story, just forget about it. They try to shoehorn some story ark, but it's pretty insignificant and you've gotta do some of those missions in order to progress in where you can go, what you could buy, etc. And it's a shame that those missions are literally nothing different than the typical grinding missions, maybe with a boss at the end. Big whoop.
There isn't too much variety in the missions and how they affect gameplay. Missions are a lot of "go here and protect
from waves of enemies," "kill all enemies in the map," "capture
zones against waves of enemies," "find
and then escape," etc. It always just ends in the same gameplay, but different objective. Just mowing down waves of enemies until you complete your job and get out of there.
But hey, maybe I'm being too harsh, it is a f2p game after all, and a good one at that. But that's still not saying too much. If you're the type of person that loves endlessly shooting things and doing the same kind of stuff over and over again to afford better armor, then this game may be for you. But personally, it's not for me.

Generally it's a fun game with excellent mechanics, but it's over the top on several points and messes up in ways that make it very hard to have any fun on it for more than a couple hours.
On any public server the food and water requirements are set so insane you basically have to drink gallons and gallons of water an hour and eat insane amounts of food that rots in seconds/minutes. You basically are forced to focus a huge amount of time on just maintaining the diet and thirst requirements of several dozen people for yourself.
And the multiplayer mechanics suck, if you have any life whatsoever you CAN NOT enjoy this game on a public server, period. If you ever sleep more than a couple hours, you can't enjoy it. Regardless of clan, group, etc., if you don't invest enough time you can never get anywhere or establish anything, and it's always too easy to destroy, even at very high levels.
I'm not complaining about difficulty, I don't mind the difficulty level. What bothers me is the way the game forces you to spend most of your time on tedius, dull activities, and punishes you so strongly for doing anything else with your life. It's far more extreme of a time suck and demand to maintain a presense on a server than any MMO I've played.
On the upside, it has beautiful graphics, an amazing huge world and environments full of content, secrets, variety that you can almost never run out of. The single player mode struggles to be fun as once you get further you spend most of your time moving resources around to build things and very little time actually doing anything interesting, and without people to compete against it's just flat out dull. It has an excellent level of "get good or get dead" which is expected on an island covered in horrific dinosaurs. The taming mechanics are great, the custom meals, mounts, buildings, it is all so well done. I think they just made some fundamental mistakes when it comes to balance that make it unplayable unless you pay for your own private server.

Doubled the price, then made a 50 dollar (CAD) season pass. FFS. As a warning, and a message that most likely won't reach the devs, DO NOT BUY THIS GAME AT FULL PRICE. Wait til a sale. I got the main game a year or so ago on humble monthly, and I do not regret the purchase for even a second, but having to pay full price for a game that is literally no closer to being finished after it's fully released is a bit scummy. Along with that, the new Free dlc gives acess to all the enjoyable parts of the paid dlc Scorched Earch, only lacking the map and some map specific elements, but the free map Ragnarok, despite being release less than half done (that's not a blow at the game, it was literally half done) was probably the definitive way to play. That is very sad.
There are also many reasons why the game itself is subpar, and many elements that go above and beyond, but many and I mean MANY elements just fall flat. I'm going to sum it up as to not make the review last ages.
The leveling system is garbage. Flat. Out. Garbage. Stat increases are made for PVE, and ONLY PVE. They upgrade a stat of your choice in increments, making it feel tangable, but not too extreme. but if someone that is a higher level than you put a ton of points into melee damage and some into extra health, you CAN'T beat them. Ever.
Worthwhile ranged weapons are locked until later than they should be, and someone with even just a club and a high melee stat, they can knock you out almost instantly, making you literally impossible to defend yourself.
Also, on the note of unlocking stuff, the engram system, despite recieving a slight rework recently, is still entirely garbage.
Now I'm just gonna list a lightning round of garbage: Item stacks are beyond awful. Food is annoying to deal with. Heat levels are nothing but a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ and always have been, they are not fun or challenging, they're tedious and annoying. The game is unplayable on official servers without a zerg clan or devoting literal hundreds of hours that would otherwise only take dozens. Building is unintuitive and repetitive. loot crates are still annoying. There is basically no reason to use any gun other than the basic pistol with the exception of certain specific circumstances, until you unlock the late game stuff with attatchments. melee combat is a garbagefest of flailing stuff at eachother until someone gets knocked out, or actually dying from it first, if that can actually happen. Spawn mechanics are terrible and still easily abusable for people with large bases, or just simple spikes. Once you get a wyvern or other strong creature, you can beat literally anyone under you, but no one above you, making tames only available to bully the weak, as they can't fight back, and the leveling system just cements it. smelting ores is just bad, like, worse than rust or minecraft, in those games it's quick and easy. F*** Troodons. No one uses the compound bow, it's too late into the game with too high of a price for an unnapealing weapon. F*** the fabricator. F*** the fabricated sniper especially, it breaks so quickly but costs so much. I have literally never seen someone use the assault rifle in this game once. As with most similar games, the rocket launcher sucks, but ARK manages to make it worse than most to use. F*** the flyer update. Much like rust, the game relies HEAVILY on the modding community to stay alive, the only difference: the devs on rust are adding content to bring players back on a regular basis. Most of the *new* dinos were just one upping previous dinos.
I could go on for ages, but I'm assuming people are just skimming this, All in all, NONE of the fundamental flaws have been fixed since i first got this game, and since the game is fully released now, I'm guessing they never will.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

On the upside, it has beautiful graphics, an amazing huge world and environments full of content, secrets, variety that you can almost never run out of. I think they just made some fundamental mistakes when it comes to balance that make it unplayable unless you pay for your own private server.

Doubled the price, then made a 50 dollar (CAD) season pass. FFS. As a warning, and a message that most likely won't reach the devs, DO NOT BUY THIS GAME AT FULL PRICE. Wait til a sale. I got the main game a year or so ago on humble monthly, and I do not regret the purchase for even a second, but having to pay full price for a game that is literally no closer to being finished after it's fully released is a bit scummy. Along with that, the new Free dlc gives acess to all the enjoyable parts of the paid dlc Scorched Earch, only lacking the map and some map specific elements, but the free map Ragnarok, despite being release less than half done (that's not a blow at the game, it was literally half done) was probably the definitive way to play. That is very sad.
There are also many reasons why the game itself is subpar, and many elements that go above and beyond, but many and I mean MANY elements just fall flat. I'm going to sum it up as to not make the review last ages.
The leveling system is garbage. Flat. Out. Garbage. Stat increases are made for PVE, and ONLY PVE. They upgrade a stat of your choice in increments, making it feel tangable, but not too extreme. but if someone that is a higher level than you put a ton of points into melee damage and some into extra health, you CAN'T beat them. Ever.
Worthwhile ranged weapons are locked until later than they should be, and someone with even just a club and a high melee stat, they can knock you out almost instantly, making you literally impossible to defend yourself.
Also, on the note of unlocking stuff, the engram system, despite recieving a slight rework recently, is still entirely garbage.
Now I'm just gonna list a lightning round of garbage: Item stacks are beyond awful. Food is annoying to deal with. Heat levels are nothing but a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ and always have been, they are not fun or challenging, they're tedious and annoying. The game is unplayable on official servers without a zerg clan or devoting literal hundreds of hours that would otherwise only take dozens. Building is unintuitive and repetitive. loot crates are still annoying. There is basically no reason to use any gun other than the basic pistol with the exception of certain specific circumstances, until you unlock the late game stuff with attatchments. melee combat is a garbagefest of flailing stuff at eachother until someone gets knocked out, or actually dying from it first, if that can actually happen. Spawn mechanics are terrible and still easily abusable for people with large bases, or just simple spikes. Once you get a wyvern or other strong creature, you can beat literally anyone under you, but no one above you, making tames only available to bully the weak, as they can't fight back, and the leveling system just cements it. smelting ores is just bad, like, worse than rust or minecraft, in those games it's quick and easy. F*** Troodons. No one uses the compound bow, it's too late into the game with too high of a price for an unnapealing weapon. F*** the fabricator. F*** the fabricated sniper especially, it breaks so quickly but costs so much. I have literally never seen someone use the assault rifle in this game once. As with most similar games, the rocket launcher sucks, but ARK manages to make it worse than most to use. F*** the flyer update. Much like rust, the game relies HEAVILY on the modding community to stay alive, the only difference: the devs on rust are adding content to bring players back on a regular basis. Most of the *new* dinos were just one upping previous dinos.
I could go on for ages, but I'm assuming people are just skimming this, All in all, NONE of the fundamental flaws have been fixed since i first got this game, and since the game is fully released now, I'm guessing they never will.

Ok so, let me ask you guys one thing. Would you like to,
1. Be a ninja.
2. Be a ninja in the future.
3. Be able to do all those ninja jumps and flips without having to press thousands of keys.
Well i can safely say Warframe delivers this and a lot more, being able to complete many missions with a variety of weapons including many different melee weapons starting with a standard sword.
Now of course maybe you're thinking, i've heard from others it's pay to win, not true, paying to win should only apply to games that are mainly PVP. Warframe does have a PVP mode but it's priority is on a COOP scale. You may use money to buy many new things such as warframes (your class) or different weapons, attachments, colours, skins, pets, sentinels, components, parts for your warframe, etc.
But don't be put off by this, the games unique because almost anything you can buy with Platinum (the ingame money you used your well earned cash on), you can buy with Credits which as you guessed is the standard money set for the game. Lets say you want a new melee weapon but you don't want to spend any real money on this because you're unsure how the game may turn out, well you can purchase "blueprints" for nearly anything in the game. So you purchase a new sword blueprint with your credits, now! You can't just jump in with creating it, because you need components, and to retrieve these components you need to do missions! However different planets have different components so you need to play missions to unlock more missions that will unlock more planets thus getting more components. Now if you're still with me you can now use new said components to create your sword you've worked so hard for, but now you have to wait maybe 12 hours for this sword to create, so now it's up to you whether you relax or carry on playing to get more components for even more items! Then we'll fast foward and VOILA! Your new sword is ready for combat.
Now, the leveling up system, your weapons all have a max rank of 30, or at least thats where mine say max rank, your warframe however can get much higher but there's somewhat of a twist to this. Like on most shooters today, you get to a max rank and then can "prestige" as most of us know it to be, but with this say you get to level 10, you then take a test to prove to "The Lotus" that you are capable of using your weapons so you'll use your primary weapon to fight numerous waves of enemies. When you have completed this you'll be level 10 still but next to your name will be "1", then again with level 20 you'll take another test and then instead of "1" it will now be "2"...complicated enough? nah you guys are smart.
Mods, use these to make your weapons stronger and your warframe more powerful, mods are slotted in when available, hence needing to level up your gear. These mods can cause more damage, elemental attributes, quicker speed, longed range etc...etc.
If this wasn't enough you can also obtain "Sentinels" and "Kubrows" to fight alongside you and of course these guys can be upgraded as well. But to obtain them you must complete missions further on in the game to accomplish this task!
Bottom line this game might need a lot of grinding but at least you get the feeling of achievement, you've put your time and hard work into gathering the components to create a new weapon because you liked the look of it, now you can use that weapon to succeed in more missions to then create even more weapons or warframes.
So if my review has peaked your interest in wanting to try out for yourself then feel free to, if you don't fancy having a go then no problem, my review is not meant to be persuasive but informative.
Enjoy Warframe :)

REVIEW BASED IN PART ON 100+ XBOX HOURS (Owned since December 2015)
I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS GAME IF YOU HAVE FRIENDS TO PLAY WITH
This game is beautiful!  The intristic designs of the landscape and the dinosaurs is amazing.  If your computer can handle the high graphics settings, you'll see what I mean.  If not, the low graphics still provide an elegant display.
The concept of this game is awesome. Taming and riding real dinosaurs, building and designing your own settlements, building and designing settlements ON your tamed dinosaurs.  This game is amazing!  You can spend thousands of hours in this game and still find new things to do.  Then, they'll probably come out with even more for you to do!  If you want a game with replay value that you'll find yourself playing over and over, welcome to Ark!
With Friends:
This game is SO much better when you're playing with friends.  Solo play is a lot of tedious grinding to be able to ride dinosaurs.  If you get friends involved, it makes it a lot more fun.  When you're not killing eachother and dropping each other in the ocean with pteranodon's for megalodon bait, you can laugh, build, and chase dinosaurs around while joking with each other.  It also makes the time go by a lot faster to have a friend by your side through everything.  Makes it a lot easier to take down the bigger dinosaurs too.  If you want this game I HIGHLY recommend you get a friend who will be able to play it with you.  You can play with friends on a private server, but you have to be within 250 meters of each other.  If not, the hosting player will drag the friend who joined the server.  You can play on a free public dedicated server without this problem, but you're facing other opponents by doing this.  You can even rent dedicated servers for a group of friends to play on w/o having to deal with other PvP players and allowing anyone to log on at anytime, and getting rid of the hosting player dragging people.
Before you buy:
If you want something you can quickly get into and play, this is not the game for you.  You will have to spend countless hours getting everything the way you want.  If you want to tame the biggest and baddest dinosaurs, you're going to have to spend hours leveling, even longer farming the items you need to take down the dinosaurs (early dinosaurs can be taken down with slingshots and rocks, big dinosaurs will boulders and homing missles,) and then even more time trying to tame the dinosaurs.  For example, a Gigantosaurus level 60+ is going to take you AT LEAST an hour to tame w/ the BEST food source to tame it.
HOWEVER, if you play this game solo, you can customize all the settings to super boost everything.  You will level insanely fast, you will harvest materials at exponential rate, and you can make it where you don't die.  This is only if you desire to.  All settings are customizable on your own world, and you can play with a group of friends this way as well.
I have seen the game go for about $12.99 when the Steam sales hit, so wait until you see that price or lower to buy!

Overall I'd rate ARK: Survival Evolved a 7/10.
This game is highly enjoyable! While rather frustrating to start, one can come to appreciate their dedication and watch their own knowledge and skill blossom as they progress. However, the game has many, many flaws when it comes to running your own server and the basic singleplayer option.
There is nothing wrong with the game itself, in fact, there's so much to do you'll find yourself entrapped for hours just wandering and evolving in your skills and building bases and taming dinosaurs. However, in my opinion, this is where the downfall begins. While I appreciate the developers constantly adding content and trying to create the most accomplished full game possible, I feel like they have been lacking when it comes to optomizing the game.
I run my own server for my Steam group. Sometimes is runs fairly well but I'll say about 90% of the time the game will crash or nothing will load or I will get a video card error. Keep in mind I have a fairly pricy gaming PC that can run The Witcher 3 on the "ultra" graphics settings and I can run my own server on other games with an even bigger file size than ARK with little to no problems. While you may see this as ranting about somthing that doesn't concern you, this is
frustrating to my teammates and others that join the server to have it crash and have to wait 30 minutes to an hour just to play for ten minutes and have the server crash again. I have a very good internet connection and I have called my ISP and they claim I should be able to run the server without issue (I called to see if there was a firewall in their system that was cancelling the server connection, causing the errors).
The singleplayer game to me also seems obsolite. If you don't have people to play with, this is your only option other than joining a random dedicated server. It is almost impossible to do anything alone in ARK, especially when it comes to taming and gathering building materials. I have tried playing singleplayer and have found myself frustrated rather than making any sort of reasonable progress. However, if this is how you play and you have made substational process through this, kudos to you but I personally do not find any charm in this way of playing the game.
There are also some bugs that need to be addressed. We have had flying dinosaurs stuck in the air for all eternity, dinosaurs glitch through our base walls and we have also had dinosaurs disappear on us with no trace. I know no game is going to be bug-free but some of these problems have been going on for quite a while and I would love to see them fixed. I have seen a lot of players stop playing ARK because of their frustration over the bugs that have gone so long without even a slight attempt of being fixed.
I do suggest this game to people; however, if you decide to buy, be warry. I do enjoy this game very much, but sometimes the cons outweigh the pros.

Honest opinion of the game:
The idea is great, and at first play through its amazing, who doesn't love dinosaurs and survival?? However, there are a lot of issues with the game, enough issues that i would not recommend buying it at this time. I was really excited, and at first loved playing it, but its been in early access forever and it isn't getting any better. Dino spawns are messed up, dinos will glitch in the map constantly, pvp is extremely hard since you are constantly battling latency and memory leaks that make you crash. Unfortunatly, Wildcard doesn't seem to put these kinds of issues high on their plate. So far its been non-stop dino releases (which don't get me wrong, more dinos is great) but so many of the major game-breaking issues are not addressed.
You will get mad at this game for losing your dino's, you will be mad you crash because of memory leaks, you will be mad when you walk into a broken spawn and 50 predators run at and kill you.
Then there is the fact instead of finishing the base game, they released paid DLC. I personally don't think it would have been a huge issue if they would have addressed the more pressing game breaking issues in the game sooner, but its been months and still no end in sight. I honestly WANT to recommend this game because I really want it to succeed, but I simply cannot recommend paying money for this game at this time. There are too many issues and Wildcard keeps claiming things are fixed, or such problem doesnt exists when the player base clearly is seeing the same problems over and over. This game is stuck in being "early access" forever and the problems just keep piling up.
TLDR: want to recommend game but simply cant, please do not buy this game it will only lead to frustrations.

Overall I'd rate ARK: Survival Evolved a 7/10.
This game is highly enjoyable! While rather frustrating to start, one can come to appreciate their dedication and watch their own knowledge and skill blossom as they progress. However, the game has many, many flaws when it comes to running your own server and the basic singleplayer option.
There is nothing wrong with the game itself, in fact, there's so much to do you'll find yourself entrapped for hours just wandering and evolving in your skills and building bases and taming dinosaurs. However, in my opinion, this is where the downfall begins. While I appreciate the developers constantly adding content and trying to create the most accomplished full game possible, I feel like they have been lacking when it comes to optomizing the game.
I run my own server for my Steam group. Sometimes is runs fairly well but I'll say about 90% of the time the game will crash or nothing will load or I will get a video card error. Keep in mind I have a fairly pricy gaming PC that can run The Witcher 3 on the "ultra" graphics settings and I can run my own server on other games with an even bigger file size than ARK with little to no problems. While you may see this as ranting about somthing that doesn't concern you, this is
frustrating to my teammates and others that join the server to have it crash and have to wait 30 minutes to an hour just to play for ten minutes and have the server crash again. I have a very good internet connection and I have called my ISP and they claim I should be able to run the server without issue (I called to see if there was a firewall in their system that was cancelling the server connection, causing the errors).
The singleplayer game to me also seems obsolite. If you don't have people to play with, this is your only option other than joining a random dedicated server. It is almost impossible to do anything alone in ARK, especially when it comes to taming and gathering building materials. I have tried playing singleplayer and have found myself frustrated rather than making any sort of reasonable progress. However, if this is how you play and you have made substational process through this, kudos to you but I personally do not find any charm in this way of playing the game.
There are also some bugs that need to be addressed. We have had flying dinosaurs stuck in the air for all eternity, dinosaurs glitch through our base walls and we have also had dinosaurs disappear on us with no trace. I know no game is going to be bug-free but some of these problems have been going on for quite a while and I would love to see them fixed. I have seen a lot of players stop playing ARK because of their frustration over the bugs that have gone so long without even a slight attempt of being fixed.
I do suggest this game to people; however, if you decide to buy, be warry. I do enjoy this game very much, but sometimes the cons outweigh the pros.

Warframe is one of those games that you can binge and maybe get bored after a couple weeks, but is always just as enjoyable to come back to.  The devs for this game are dedicated and are quite consistent in updates and more free content.  I know a few people are put off by the phrase "Free-to-play" nowadays and for a lot of games that repulsion is justified.  However Warframe has a pretty decent business model, you can buy weapons straight out with the premium currency - platinum, but you can also buy the blueprints for the same weapons for a reasonable amount of credits.  The mechanics for this game are also fluid and consistent, I have not had too many problems in the way of bugs or glitches, and as someone who generally does not enjoy third person shooters, this one manages to keep me coming back for more.  Partly resoponsible for that is the whole aesthetic of the game, the maps are a bit same-y but the whole space ninja thing is pretty awesome just as a concept and the look and feel of the abilities and weapons really fit it well.
Overall I would recommend this game, simple as pie.

Not talking around it for long-
Warframe is one of the best, if not the best F2P game I ever got to play.
-This game has absolutely no P2W. You do have a little advantage if you pay Platinum (the in game currency) to rush weapons and other equipment in your foundry to get done more quickly, or if you simply buy them as complete items in the shop. Pretty spendy though so that's that.
-The content this game offers without demanding a single dime out of your pocket is astonishing. I am playing this game for over 300 hours and it never seizes to surprise me yet again.
-There ARE bugs, but they are sort out so quickly, that you can't even complain about them before a hotfix is coming.
Downside on that is,that there might be days where several hotfixes are deployed. But on the other-other hand, the hotfixes are deployed while you play and it notifies you when they are ready to download. You'll just simply have to restart the game and give those 5 MB a little to settle in your game.
-The God.Damn.Variety. The bandwidth of playing styles is incredible.
There are several warframes (characters,if you want to call it like that), that play completely differently from one another, and they even have own setups that specialize them on several occassions, which often are needed for the more special forces-like gaming tier. The weapons are...just wow. Lots of them,and they're all badass.
Putting it short, no matter what you want to play like, this game can offer you exactly what you need for your style.
-You can achieve EVERYTHING in this game without paying any RL-money. As a matter of fact, you can get Platinum through trading! So if you ever have any desires like cosmetics etc. you go and farm for stuff that people want, and you get to trade it in for Platinum. Thriving market, guys. Better than what the real world has to offer.
-The game updates continuously. The developers keep adding more content to the game, thus keep expanding it. And they never ask you to pay money to access that content.
-It looks amazing. The graphics are great and the optimization is top-notch. I have a mid tier computer that can't run ARK on mid settings without experiencing FPS drops.
On Warframe,I've got the graphics settings way up high on maximum.
60+ FPS constantly. No joking.
-The community is incredibly nice. There's always people that are happy to help newcomers to the game and explain things, because at the start, it can all be quite confusing. I myself have fun helping others where I can, just for the heck of helping. And I'm by far not the only one to do that. Not saying there's no jackasses around in that game, there are.
But you're less likely to see them there than in most other online games.
All in all, Warframe is a top notch title that delivers everything you'd expect from a good F2P game. And much more.
If you're looking for a free game with a nice community, interesting lore, style, cool devs and more upsides than I could list in this sentence, then Warframe is your game.
