It's a great game, no questions, I love it and I hate it.
Singleplayer, local, or unofficial servers might work without problems, even though there are still many bugs around. but you'll miss out on trading across servers and teaming up with people to beat caves and bosses.
If you want to play on official servers though, expect lags, rubberbading, and sometimes rollbacks that will make you lose your tamed dinos more than once - it can take hours-days (real life time) to even get your hands on some of them.
this game takes time, a lot of it. it will cost your sleep and your neves, especially when you start breeding animals.
If you really want to play, make sure to read a lot about the game before you buy - taming timers, breeding timers, game modes, maps - learn about the community and make sure you choose a friendly server (if you can get on any, since there are not enough to accomodate all players at release).
I would totally not recommend buying dlcs yet. Scorched earth had exclusive animals and items which were later released on the free to play Ragnarok map. so unless you love desert maps or whatever other maps are planned, don't buy a dlc just for for the creatures or items on it.
The main reason of my negative review is the unprofessional company, especially the community manager. Yes, they are a small company. Yes I can understand technical difficulties not to be solved immediately, like full servers (again) on launch day, or animals that were to be released being postponed because they still need rework.
Most of the updates are delayed, some by hours, some by days. this has not happened early in the EA phase, but up until the release.
Update is planned for a certain day/time, postponed to an unknown day and time; You were planning on playing this Saturday? Surprise Patch with 15 min ingame warning prior. Most likely the update will fix something but break another thing. good chance there will be another patch or hotfix soon.
finding you baby dinos starved or falling to your death from a flier after a patch is not fun.
But promising something to the community, then changing plans and leave the EA players hanging, that's just sad.
(We won't wipe on release -> we will only wipe low populated servers with like zero people online all the time -> we will wipe 10% of the lowest populated servers with 30 day warning so everyone can move to another server in time-> in the end wiping 33% of the servers with 5 days warning, breaking the item transfer system on the last day instead of making the transfer changes on release, also last-minute scrapping support for the legacy servers).
There is a official forum, but if you want information quick you'll need to use twitter. if you want a reply you'll also get that on twitter if you are lucky, hardly ever on their own website. You can send a ticket ofc and GM will reply.
Get ready to endure a love-hate relationship with this game. it will be frustrating. and it will be the best you have ever played.

After 1500 hours in ark, I'm willing to give a review and it's really a word of warning. Read all the other negative reviews, they aren't exaggerating. Either give up any life you had in real life Ark to play this ark, because you can't have both. When you spend hundreds of hours farming a base and taming dinos, be prepared to spend hundreds of hours maintaining that, because if you aren't constantly growing your defenses and and watching all your assets, a zerg tribe from some far off country and server will come and wipe everything you had, and not even feel a little bad about it.  And when you go to take your favorite battle Quetz loaded with Ascendant weapons and armor to seek revenge on those block lettered tribes that killed all your passive tames you spent hundreds of hours on.... It'll despawn. With the last of your precious things. And the Developers won't help get any of it back.
Ark is a game that you can spend 18 hours on a day, and the moment you go to sleep, someone in an opposite timezone will come and take all your things. Don't sleep long, because they will spend the entire 6-8 hours you sleep tanking all your defenses, slowly sliding their way into the most intimate parts of your base, and there's nothing you can do about it.
It's a cold blooded game that will destroy everything around you. If you want a life, turn around and run. Play some FPS that you can turn off and walk away from and not start over again.
Please read the reviews. It's a game you will hate to love.  It's a bad kind of addicting. It's like meth or coke, you'll want to leave, but you just can't quit.

Pros
Multiplayer does not lag or feel terrible to be playing, very stable.
Developers listen to feedback from their fans and will make changes if necessary.
Vast amount of dinos to hunt or tame.
The game is available on most consoles.

The world is so immense and has alot to explore.
The sound engineering is superb!
Visuals are absolutely amazing!
Cons
The Devs add more items and dinos than they fix bugs and make sure the game is good for when its fully released!
The Devs made paid DLC for an early access game, I mean come on, I love Ark but this is just shady!
The game is VERY recourse demanding, I would suggest seeing the minumum requirements tab before purchasing!
Non deticated servers require a tether limit, of course they need this as the servers are not paid for, but seeing as they made DLC for an early access game, Im pretty sure they can handle that.
Game does require constant farming in some cases, other than that its fine.
The DLC costs as much as the game (As you can tell I am not a fan of this DLC craze Ark is favoring to their hearts content)
So all in all I think Ark is a pretty good game and I would rate it an 8/10. I hope you found this review helpful and I hope it pushed you towards buying the game to help support the Devs!

ARK: Survival Evolved was a promising game but is fast going down the same failed path of so many "Alpha, Early Access" titles, and a series of recent confusing changes, that I can only imagine are aimed to boost sales in anticipation of its mid 2017 launch.
First it is in my opinion one of the better, if not best, survival games on the market based on the game alone. Its exciting, fast paced, and a unique blend of minecraft, DayZ, with Dinosaur and other animal taming. I truely enjoyed it for its first months of launch.
First, not counting private servers, there are 3 modes of play PVE, PVP and a new Offline Protection PVP there are pros and cons to each.
First PVE is geared to more relaxing play, no worries about raids by hostile players and trolls, most people I know play this mode, except, you are missing out on a good portion of the game by playing this mode, raiding other players bases and defending your own base is a core part of this survival game and shouldn`t be missed. also unchecked, bases of established players grow to ridiculous lag inducing sizes.
PVP is the true ARK experience, but don`t believe the flashy exciting trailers. PVP is not riding your raptor into battle, armed with an assault rifle, flanked by your bronto carrying an armored fortress on his back. you will be knocked off your dinosaur by a couple of jerks with a pteradon, and dropped into the swamp, as they hack your dinosaurs apart with hatchets. retaliate, and they may just call in their old buddies from another mega tribe to wipe the server, which brings me to the new confusing changes to ARK
Once, you were stuck on a server for good, there was a way to upload your dinosaurs and player character for download on another server, but this was for private unofficial servers only. It was a cool way to save the magnificent perfect tame, if you were transfering to unofficial, and keep your levels,  All good but following the addition of Server transfers, now players can move across servers at will taking any dinos with them AND resources. now there is a plague of Mega tribes once stuck on servers they wiped clean of players, transfering to launch server wide attacks. In response players locked the obelisk and drop spawn points to prevent transfers, but the devs have made this harder with every patch. Yes, there are defenses one can build, but good luck defending your tribe of 5 friends against a 40+ man mega tribe funneling in resources and dinos from 2+ servers.
This enviroment has led to some of the most toxic players I have ever seen, and the updates seem to only feed these trolls, heres a cage to lock players up with, you can feed them these drugs to knock them out so you can force feed them to keep them alive, feed them their own feces while you`re at it, thats always fun. heres a plague that you can infect players with, heres a dino that can pluck enemy players off their mounts. and so on.
The expansion Scorched Earth was GREAT in my opinion, I love the new map and the new dinos, but IT IS pay to win. the Fire, poison or lightning Wyverns are OP and will dominate a server, along with the rock elementals, and  flame throwers it introduced.
Also on the horizon is the Tek Tier gear, which includes, laser helmets for rexes, jetpacks, the ability to power punch through wood bases flattening them. laser guns, INVR style HUDs and pressurised undersea bases, all sounds awesome but I fear like the Wyverns, Giganotosaurus, Miniguns and Rock Elementals these will be out of reach of the average player, and will be owned by the few Alpha tribes to dominate their servers.
At the current state of the game, it is harder than ever for a new player to get started, with a lot of the new dinos possesing knock out effects and poisons. and the hostile mega tribes are only making it worse. a server I was on was recently wiped by hackers, and while WildCard does make an excellent effort to stop these players, you are still left with 40+ hours work gone. At 250 hours Im an ARK noob compared to some, my girlfriend having over 2000 hours logged, but its still a devastating loss. players are paranoid of server wipes, and while perhaps overreacting. there is a definite backlash to the addition of Chinese servers, their players being listed  kill on site by some Alpha Tribes I`ve met.
The game is still buggy and full of glitches and frequent crashes, and not optimized for any but the most high end PCs
I cannot recomend the game in its current state. wait for the REAL release. watch the reviews then decide, don`t waste $30.00 ($50 including DLC) and a week of your life for a bug, hacker, or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to chew it up, poop it out and stuff down your throat.
If you must, I recomend either Offline raid protected PVP maps, or even unofficial.
I have uninstalled, will see if its better at launch.
The moral of the story, DON`T PAY TO TEST A DEVELOPERS GAME, THAT IS THEIR JOB.

TLDR - It's a grind wall and cash vacuum. The game also fails to explain how pretty much anything works.
Is it free to play? Yes. But - you can see right underneath that the DLC will set you back $220. Buying the single transaction maximum of the top-tier in game currency costs $160. Prime access costs $140 and the additional prime addon pack costs another $50.
Obviously nobody would ever buy all of these things together. But things add up quickly in this game. At the current conversion ratio of 18.75 'Platinum' to 1 dollar - purchasing one character costs roughly $16 (with top-tier characters priced at 20). A single weapon costs somewhere between $10 and $13. Naturally, all weapons and characters are about useless without 'mods' - powerups. Mods come in random packs of 5 which cost on average $3.2. One individual random mod will cost, on average, $.60. Mods will have to then be fused with each other or with 'fusion cores'. Fusion cores come in 3 packs which are priced at $3.73. An individual core will therefore cost $1.24, and it is up to chance on whether or not the cores will be rare or powerful. Creating a powerful mod will require numerous mods and fusion cores. One character equips 3 weapons - and both the character and all the weapons will require multiple mods. The total costs here are immense.
Now, in fairness, my conversion ratio is basd on the lowest purchase level of platinum. In my defense, I believe that most players would start out by testing the waters by purchasing at this level first. While someone wouldn't attempt to buy everything all at once from scratch - I think it's useful to know the full cost of creating a character from a pay route. Look through the negative reviews - see the people who have spent hundreds or thousands of dollars on this game. It is part of the game mechanics.
The gameplay is fun, and almost all of these things are attainable through inputting hours of your life into the system. But the hours:unlock ratio is simply unfair  and the pay scheme is in my opinion abusive. I would be willing to pay for this game - but the model works so that there is no way to be able to pay a 'normal' $60 price equivalent.
There is a human emotion that compels us to discount what we already have and desire that which we do not. Games like warframe exploit that emotion in a ruthless and shameless fashion.

The game was good and fun.  But they announced a server upgrade.  When the upgrade happened, they relocated the servers to Germany.  Latency skyrocketed as a result.  And the game is currently experiencing constant lag spikes and rubberbanding.  It is common to have big lag spikes lasting 15 to 60 seconds at least once every 5 minutes.  In game timers are slipping two to three hours every 24 hours.  That's a lot of lag.  I have watched torpor on a creature bouncing back and forth three to five times before advancing one increment during a tame.  And this is the everyday norm.
Another negative of the game is that the server limit is set to 70 people logged on.  But over the past 16 months, the game has never been worth playing once we have over 20 people logged on.  By the time there are 25 players online, the creature spawns have been shut down to nothing.  This is great if you are a starting player.  There's nothing to kill you as you gather and build.  But once you have tamed dinos, you better be able to log in while the player count is low. Otherwise, you'll be struggling to find enough meat to feed your carnivores.
The only reason that  I have not quit the game permanently is that I am tribed with a small group of good players.  But I have cut back to minimal gathering of resources.  No more taming.  Rarely getting out and about on the island.  And I honestly don't care for it at this point.  I barely know anything about the last two rounds of new dinos that they have introduced for that matter.  I'll wait and hope that they relocate the North American servers to North America so we can play it again.

I have redone this review 3-4 times now, as my experience and time spent in game have furthered and progressed, and I feel that I can now conclude that, UNLESS the ark devs at Studio Wildcard make some major changes, this game will be in a downward spiral for the rest of its existence. I say this for multiple reasons, though three of them stand out far ahead of the rest.
The first of these reasons is that the playerbase of this game makes all those 8 year old mic spammers playing COD on their Xboxes seem like holy saints by comparison. Truly the people who play this game are toxic. More toxic than any other playerbase or group I have come across in my lifetime. Their are always those few kind and enjoyable players who we meet from time to time, but it is exponentially more likely you will encounter some griefing warlord who only wishes to prove how big of a man he is by picking on those who have less than him. The amount of times I have had my base raided by someone with gear that was hundreds of hours more advanced than my own, simply so the other guy could get a kick out of it, far outnumber the amount of times somebody has offered to help. These players run rampant and no amount of work by any single group can stop them.
The second of these three reasons is the "recently" implemented cross-ark transfer system. Essentially this system allows any player to "upload" their character with all of their stats and inventory, as well as their tamed dinosaurs, then "download" this character onto a different server that is part of the same cluster. This can be nice as you can change maps freely in search of a server with a certain building location that is open, or join some newly made friends on their home server. These upsides are, however, rarely the reason the transfer system is used. The primary use of the transfer system is for 50-100 man mega tribe who take over entire servers to join other servers, then wipe out the local population, and take all valuable present, or sometimes even take the server hostage, but the catch is, no ransom can buy this server back, only anotehr mega tribe raiding.
The third and final nail in the coffin of the once great and perhaps even genre changing game Ark: Survival Evolved, is the devs. Ever since november of 2016 the devs have seemed to make continuously worse and worse decisions, from implemeting a dino that can take up to 12 REAL LIFE HOURS OF CONTINUOUS BABYSITTING to tame, to putting insanely annoying dinos which can knock you out in 1-2 hits, then eat you alive while you lay there unconscious, with no way to defend yourself near places where new players spawn. The most obvious of these poor decisions was perhaps the only one that was issued with good intent, and EXTREMELY poor execution was the recent nerf to flying dinosaurs. This nerf made it so that you can no longer increase the flight speed of said dinos, as well as cutting down stamina, which is required for flight, and increasing stamina regen times. These are only a few of the mistakes I have seen Ark's devs make over and over.
Perhaps the saddest part of all this is that if the devs would jsut face their playerbase and say "Look, we've screwed up several times recently, but we want to make things right. We will reverse parts of the flier nerf, and will hold out on adding additional content for a few months to iron out some of the longstanding issues with the game." I feel that many players would come back to Ark. All it would take it one simple display understanding to convince at the very least me and my friends to come back to Ark.
TL;DR - This game was great, but in recent months has been driven into the ground by a toxic playerbase, systems which favor the powerful getting more powerful, and the weak being kicked while they are down, and poor decisions by the developers. This game had so much potential, and all it would take is one simple show of understanding to make at the very least me and my friends come back.
Final Ratings

Now - 2/10

TLDR - It's a grind wall and cash vacuum. The game also fails to explain how pretty much anything works.
Is it free to play? Yes. But - you can see right underneath that the DLC will set you back $220. Buying the single transaction maximum of the top-tier in game currency costs $160. Prime access costs $140 and the additional prime addon pack costs another $50.
Obviously nobody would ever buy all of these things together. But things add up quickly in this game. At the current conversion ratio of 18.75 'Platinum' to 1 dollar - purchasing one character costs roughly $16 (with top-tier characters priced at 20). A single weapon costs somewhere between $10 and $13. Naturally, all weapons and characters are about useless without 'mods' - powerups. Mods come in random packs of 5 which cost on average $3.2. One individual random mod will cost, on average, $.60. Mods will have to then be fused with each other or with 'fusion cores'. Fusion cores come in 3 packs which are priced at $3.73. An individual core will therefore cost $1.24, and it is up to chance on whether or not the cores will be rare or powerful. Creating a powerful mod will require numerous mods and fusion cores. One character equips 3 weapons - and both the character and all the weapons will require multiple mods. The total costs here are immense.
Now, in fairness, my conversion ratio is basd on the lowest purchase level of platinum. In my defense, I believe that most players would start out by testing the waters by purchasing at this level first. While someone wouldn't attempt to buy everything all at once from scratch - I think it's useful to know the full cost of creating a character from a pay route. Look through the negative reviews - see the people who have spent hundreds or thousands of dollars on this game. It is part of the game mechanics.
The gameplay is fun, and almost all of these things are attainable through inputting hours of your life into the system. But the hours:unlock ratio is simply unfair  and the pay scheme is in my opinion abusive. I would be willing to pay for this game - but the model works so that there is no way to be able to pay a 'normal' $60 price equivalent.
There is a human emotion that compels us to discount what we already have and desire that which we do not. Games like warframe exploit that emotion in a ruthless and shameless fashion.

Crack the warm eggs into a bowl, add salt and blend with a fork. Heat a 10-inch nonstick aluminum pan over medium-high heat. Once the pan is hot, add the butter and brush around the surface of the pan. Pour the eggs into the center of the pan and stir vigorously with a rubber spatula for 5 seconds. As soon as a semi-solid mass begins to form, lift the pan and move it around until the excess liquid pours off into the pan. Using your spatula, move it around the edge of the egg mixture to help shape into a round and loosen the edge. Let the omelet sit in the pan for 10 seconds without touching. Shake the pan to loosen from the pan. Lift up the far edge of the pan and snap it back toward you. Using your spatula, fold over one-third of the omelet. Slide the omelet onto a plate and fold over so that the omelet is a tri-fold. Coat with the remaining butter and sprinkle with the chives. Serve immediately.
Nothing says “good morning” like a fresh omelet.

While I enjoy this game, you shoud realize that this game isn't really a survival game.  A survival game implies that you stay alive as long as possible and "survive."  But ARK is all about mercilessly slaughtering you, over and over.  You'll likely die at least ten times before you get four walls and a roof up, because an integral component of this game is death.  You will spawn in the first time, and go through a long, drawn-out "waking up" animation that 2 out of 3 times gets you killed just because it takes so long.  Moreover, the spawns don't bother to check for nearby hostile dinos, so you often spawn right onto dinos that kill you while you're watching the slightly shorter "not the first time waking up" animation.    It can be very frustrating just trying to build a simple shelter.  IMO, this game would be majorly improved by cutting out some of the early-game nonsense (give the characters more starter recipes, better stats).
Edit:  I remember why I never rate this game as recommended now - the ♥♥♥♥ing BUGS.  They NEVER get fixed and so you lose tons of hours of work on dinos simply because they vanish without a trace for no reason, collision glitches occur, or other glitches.  For example, I spent hours taming a high level tapejara last night, only to have it vanish the instant it was tamed.  It didn't die - it's recorded in the log as tamed, but no death.  But it's just gone.  I've searched a ton of the map for it - gone.
And then I was riding a ptero, got low to the ground to grab a drop and was fighting some snakes.   This is my good ptero, level 225, that I spent hours taming as well.  Suddenly for no explainable reason I'm knocked out of the saddle and die, and of course the ptero dies in the time it takes me to get back.
And now that I think about it, this has always been a problem in this game.  Dino glitches have existed forever and are never addressed - the devs are too focused on trying to add new content.  The staff just says "Sorry" when your dinos go missing and won't do anything about it, and it often takes 10-20+ real hours to tame these things.  Hugely insulting from the company that they don't address this after years of development and tons of money.

The game doesn't have many problems considering it's an early access game. Warframe.. hmm where should i truly begin?
Pro's
-The game isnt P2W
-Large variaty of things to do so you cant get bored
-Clans(Guild) can fight for domination over certain planets
-PVP is balanced
-Large variaty of Warframes to play as so you can find one that just fits your playstyle
-Storyline is wonderful, though a few people say its not.. but those are the ones who claim the game is P2W
-Storyline choices, depending on the route you pick determines your characters Evil/Good
-Many planets to do missions in which doesnt force you to just one.
-Pretty Challenging if you dont have the right weapons or warframe for the job
-Customization of your warframe
-Cosmetics
-Pets
-Pets Cosmetics
-Ship Cosmetics
-Wonderful Graphics, So good this game could go P2P
-Devs work to fix bugs activily with Hotfixes
-Good community
Cons
-Can get boring without friends after a long time of playing
-Play 2 Grind(Which many confuse for P2W but its not)
-Need to be in a Clan if you ever wish to get far in the game(Not needed but only so for clan research material)
-Without a good frame or weapon might mean the end for you in a mission
-May be too difficult for people who assume they will come in and conquer easily.
-Trading Chat(Alot of people selling things makes your items u post in chat not catch anyones eye unless its for a good price or its a good piece of merchandise)

This game is great despite the collection of bugs, and the current bugs should be expected considering this game is still in Early-Access. For someone who has not played as much as some of the other players with 1,000+ hours on record, I honestly enjoy the heck out of this game. In its current state, Ark is loads of fun because it combines the survival aspect with an intense desire to explore the vast open maps it has to offer.
Many complain that the Scorched Earth is WildCard's way of getting a good cash grab from its players while it is still in early access, I don't feel this way. Yes, it is quite odd that the developers would release a paid DLC for a game that is still in Early-Access, but I feel like it's worth the extra cash to buy this map. The Scorched Earth DLC introduces so much more content to get your hands on while pressing harsh enviromental conditions making your experience quite interesting and difficult. It is definitely harder compared to the other maps, but you can't turn down all the more stuff you have access to in this new map.
Putting the DLC aside, the first two maps are also great and help you create a better understanding of the game. In my opinion, this game is MUCH better with friends. Ark is fun to play by yourself, but playing with friends really makes the experience a lot more enjoyable. I have not played on any of the official servers yet and prefer to play on a dedicated server I host myself. My friends and I started off playing on a Non-Dedicated server which is great except for the fact that host tethering exists. Getting out of a certain range of the host will slingshot you back towards the host, making exploration very difficult and inconvenient. We never thought much of it until I would go too far in a certain direction and my friends would be teleported to the bottom of the ocean where they would either drown or get mauled by the many creatures that reside there. The only way to get rid of host tethering (that I know of) is hosting a dedicated server and playing on there, making it so you and other players can roam freely without the horrid slingshot effect.
I haven't gotten to experience all the aspects of Ark: Survival Evolved, but will continue to play to gain some of the knowledge that the players with much more playing time on their record than me have. I highly reccomend this game to anyone who likes a good surival game with a grind and a fun experience for both you and your friends. I know that most of this review is biased, but I thought I'd bring a little light to the game in the variety of negative reviews that swarm around the game. If you are considering buying this game, feel free to look at other people's reviews to get more insight on if this is the game you really want, but I think that if you have the temptation to add this title to your library, I give it a thumbs up for everyone to try.

Although my current hours dont show much, i have plenty hours of experience to review. This game has me on the fence. Half of me think "wow this game is so fun imma get back into it again." The other half of me thinks "do i really need another chore?" This game is great by all means, but if you decide to play a PvP server you are in for a commitment if you decide to got through with it till the reset. Even a PvE server needs attention, althought not that much  ( like 20-45 minutes every other day). This is game you cannot simply "take a break" from for more than  about a week without everything you have either dying or being destroyed. This is different if you decide to get in a tribe where they will look after your stuff for the time, but most "dedicated" tribes will often kick members if they decide to take some time off.
Over all the game is a 7/10 imo because while you play it, it's a blast (ecspecially with a group of friends). But once you get burned out its basically a reset of what you've come to do.

I have well over 1k hours into this game and have been playing it since shortly after it came out. While not perfect, it has improved GREATLY in stability since release. ARK is personally my favorite (maybe ever) I have played and certainly in a sand box survival game. I can't reccomend it enough.

Ark is one of those games you start off with having little idea of what you're doing.
You play around with the mechanics, just figuring out how to build a fire, when suddenly you meet your first raptor.
The raptor, being of a carnivorous persuasion, requests that you share with it some of your juicy quadriceps. You weren't using them anyway, unless you set the sliders all the way to max.
Naturally, this seems like a bit of a raw deal, but attempting to back out of the negotiations quickly sees diplomacy becoming a more and more unlikely method of resolving your predicament.
If you've played this game, you know the sheer sense of achievement following your first raptor tame.
It's that kind of experience that makes this game shine, and why I will recommend it, because that experience only grows grander and grander in scale as you tame larger dinosaurs and make a little slice of the island your own.
I played with a friend on a stable and friendly unofficial server, so thankfully I was able to avoid the recent uproar following the official cross-server transfers. In my experience, the best way to enjoy ARK is on a small, unofficial server, where you don't have to compete with aggressive and well-settled tribes.

At the time I write this, I have put about 3500 hours into this game. I have been playing it for over a year now and have had a lot of ups and downs. I play on a PvP server and I have had everything I had taken from me and all my tames killed many times. I have worked my way back up over and over and have managed to secure my tribe as a beta tribe on a server and am in an alliance with the alpha tribe.
Then Wild Card dropped Scortched Earth and the ability to transfer players and items into the server I play on. My server did everything we could to protect ourselves and it paid off. Then Wild Card made all the supply drops not effected by structures so they would still drop. So, we blocked them all off with vaults. Now Wild Card made it so the drops land on top of anything under them. We don't have any defense against that.
Why are we worried? Because for the better part of the last year, many servers have been taken over completely my mega tribes. Tribes that regularly hit server cap with who plays on the server. Who farm servers of all their resources and have been unchecked because no one could farm enough resources to fight them on their own servers. Now that they can travel from server to server, they are slowly working their way through all official servers and wiping the servers of everything.
For people like myself who have dumped litterally thousands of hours into this game, we are doing all we can to defend, but we can only do so much as we can't be online all day everyday. With the servers not being region locked, we have Chinese, Russian, and Australian tribes coming to our server during peak times for them, but the early morning hours for us. Meaning, we have no one on to defend what we worked hard to make. We now have to work in shifts, like it is a job, to defend what we have, all because Wild Card decided to open the arks up and have the players wipe the servers for them.
When a large server falls, most of the players quit playing the game. They move onto something else. That is good for Wild Card, because then the servers become low population, so they can repurpose them or remove them and that saves them a lot of money. They already made all they will make off of the players currently playing. So, if they remove us, they can save on server costs and use that for more advertising to get more unsuspecting players into the game.
Overall, Wild Card doesn't listen to their players unless those players are praising how great the game is. The players that riducule the game, are ignored or banned due to rule violations. Wild Card doesn't know what they are doing in terms of making a game that isn't completely broken nor do they know how to have a conversation with their player base that isn't just the positive things about the game. They refuse to hear or even acknowledge there is anything wrong with their game and that is a huge problem.
Bottom line, only get this game if you're going to play on unofficial servers or you like logging in and finding that everything you have is gone, yet again, and you get to punch a tree and start over.
ADDED February 02, 2017:
I mainly talked about the PvP on Official servers in the review above, so I am adding the other ways to play the game here to hopefully give a more well rounded review.
Single Player is nice as well, but nothing is persistant. So you need to increase a lot of rates in single player to make it fun. Like, at stock, if taming something takes 6 hours, you need to be logged into the game for 6 hours to tame it. If you exit, that timer pauses. Breeding anything becomes too cumbersome without increasing rates because 4 real life days that pauses when you exit the day is just not possible. Unless you want it taking 2 weeks to raise one thing. I just use single player as a "creative mode" to spawn everything in and build to see what I would need for the server I actually play on.
PvE is enjoyable but frustrating in a different way. You can't build near others and as long as you close your doors, no one can take your things. People can annoy you and get in your way and just be asshats to you, and you can't do anything to them because you can't fight them. They can build walls around your base at the build limit so you can't get out or in. It's like the 12 year olds at malls that will be annoying little ♥♥♥♥♥ and and when you tell them to quit being ♥♥♥♥♥, they try to egg you on by telling you that you can't do anything because they are a minor and you can't hit them. Just really disrespectful. In some cases it's worse than PvP.
The unofficial servers are nice as it's less ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s and more good players. Though, then you run the risk of the admins of the servers spawning in whatever they want and wiping the server anytime without notice. So, you could log in and the whole server is wiped and you lost everything. They could change up the mods on the server without notice and just shut the server down because they didn't want to pay for it anymore. If you're playing PvP on their server and you wipe them and become alpha, they can just delete everything you have, rollback the server to before you wiped them, spawn in a level 1million titanosaur and smash everything you have, or any combination of those.
My biggest gripe with the game is that it's not fun anymore. It was fun for the last year and with the last few months of updates, it's just not fun anymore. You can have a lot of fun on unofficial servers, but they are also very volatile as well. Maybe more so than PvP official servers. The way I see it, is that if you never played this game before and you join a server, you should have fun right away. You shouldn't have to join unofficial servers and add mods to the game to make it fun. To me, that says the developers failed at their job for making a fun game. Sure, int he future, you might get bored of the offical servers and mod the game to get some NEW excitement out of it, but you shouldn't have to mod a game after you bought it in order to get fun from it.
If Wild Card wants to keep all transfers open the way they have it now when you can transfer creatures, players, and items from server to server, then I suggest they do a full wipe of every server so everyone has a fair start to build up. Otherwise the mega tribes that basically own official servers have so much unchecked power to just wipe servers and take all their resources and get even bigger. There isn't any hope to fight them off.
But, if Wild Card just limits you transferring your character, that would be better as then you need to build up on a server. I have seen a few smaller tribes band together and wipe alphas that are just mean and ruin your day for fun. It happened on my server last year. The alpha we have now is friendly and helps the server anytime they can and uses their power to defend the server against attacks.

Best free to play game I've ever found.
- You're tenno, a super cool space ninja protecting the balance. At first, there were only fractions of the story. But later, thanks to updates, you can experience the story by doing quests, and the last one (The Second Dream) had a really big impact on the game. You shouldn't search for spoilers and try to avoid them, it's much better to experience the story.
- The game itself is a 3rd person shooter, with a parkour system, and a lots of weapons. The game focuses on 4 player COOP with a lots of classes that you can modify by mods for your liking( There's also PVP but it isn't very popular). The main menu, is you wandering around your orbiter (ship), interacting with objects. You can jump into action by selecting missions in navigation. There are a lots of them. Capture, Survival, Spy, Exterminate, Defense, Hijack, Interception, Excavation and the list goes on and on on different maps. It never feels you're doing the same thing over and over again, because the maps are made together with the rooms in random sequence.
- Mods are basicly the way to upgrade your equipment, weapons, warframes. You can collect them by killing certain types of enemies, completing certain missions. You usually get common / uncommon ones every mission. By gathering affinity (xp) your weapons and warframes will level until rank 30. BUT, warframes only gain health, energy, shield and better abilities, and weapons gain nothing by leveling up. The rank shows how many modslots you have, so basicly your equipment won't get stronger by simply leveling them up, you need to mod them. There are thousends of different mods, so you can mod your equipment how you want. Ofc there are certain builds, but your own works as well, and you can go do crazy stuff sometimes.
- Lot's of them. There aren't much recolors of weapons, and when there are there is reasoning behind them. There are  3 types of weapons. Primary, secondary, and melee.
Primaries are your main weapons, shotguns, rifles, sniperrifles, bows, grenade launchers, rocket launcher etc.
Secondaries are pistols, akimbo pistols, shurikens, small rocket launchers, etc.
Melees are scythes, swords, dual swords, polearms, staves, daggers, dual daggers, whips, heavy weapons etc.
You get stuff by buying blueprints and building them with parts and resources.
Get dogs or sentinels helping you, yey!
Sometimes I'm wondering why is this a free2play game...
- You can join (or create) a clan, have fun together, do raids (8player hard missions) and help eachother. A clan is goodway to have some people help you when you're a newbie, because IT IS HARD to get into the game, and understand stuff.
- After time you'll be visiting more places, building more weapons, building more warframes(classes(you're not limited to one)), gathering more more resources, gathering more mods. Then with well modded weapons, warframes and teammates, you can complete higher level / more difficult missions.
I often try out free to play games. Then I realise it's pay to win or there are features that can't be obtained without spending money. That sucks doesn't it? An enemy really shouldn't have an advantage by just spending money. Well, you can get stuff here for real money, but it doesn't pulls you back. It's PVE. Also, cosmetics, weapons and warframe slots are for platinum only. It's also disturbing when you play the game for the first time and you see the market full with stuff only obtainable by platinum. So there's premium currency, bad game right?
1st - You can obtain weapons by buying blueprints(not for platinum) and build them with reasources, same with warframes, and some warframes are obtainably by doing it's quest.
2nd - You actually can get platinum (lots of them) without spending a penny. You CAN buy cosmetics, and you CAN have more weapon and warframe slots... this brings us to:
- You can trade with other players if you reached mastery rank 2 ( account rank, you rank up by leveling weapons). The easiest way is to have a clan. You can trade, in the clan's dojo or in Maroo's Bazaar. You can trade, prime weapon parts(obtainably in the void ( maptype)), mods, special weapons, and... PLATINUM. You get stuff, sell them for plat, and buy a cape to look cool yey! ( or actually use them in the right way :D) The accepted trading currency is platinum, so for example:
You want a mod that you want to get but you're unlucky getting it / it's rare. It's easier to sell stuff for platinum, and buy the mod you want for platinum, than trying to trade your stuff with the other players stuff, so it's hard to not get any platinum out of something you want to sell.
- The game is evolving nonstop. Hotfixes and updates, coming and coming. The best is, the devs are regularly playing with the community together, and they care about what we think. There are devstreams, giving us information about incoming updates and hotfixes.
It's a hard game to get into, but when you do it feels good. There are ofc features I forgot about, there's too many of them. Sorry for any grammar mistakes, my English isn't perfect.

I would say that survival games sort of break into three components: suviving in a hostile world, exploration, and building stuff.  This one does the first two great. Warframe is a fantastic game. The gameplay style and mechanics are some of the more unique ones I've seen in a game in quite a while. Rather than just being your typical shooter game where you just jump and sprint around the place, you can select a variety of weapons for gunplay and melee combat, and various accessories that make your player unique. But enough descriptions, let's dig into the game.
As I mentioned in the introduction, this game has some unique mechanics. Rather than simple movement, (jumping, walking, and sprinting), you can perform parkour moves like wall running, double jumping, sliding, and many more. But that's not just everything. You can also combine certain movements to perform even more moves. For example, Jump+Crouch will shoot you forward, destroying any destructible objects in your path. There are many more you can perform, which I won't list here.
The gunplay is like your typical shooter game where you point and shoot. There's not much that's unique about it. The same applies for your secondary weapon and your melee weapon. The one feature that sets these weapons apart from other games is weapon and armor mods. While you play the game, you randomly acquire mods which you can apply to your weapons and warframes. These mods add new behaviors to your weapon and/or warframe. For example, a weapon mod could add fire damage to your weapon, or a warframe mod might add more health to your player.
I haven't gotten very far into the main storyline, but so far it's pretty basic. While it's not bad per se, it's not exactly intriguing or intricate. If you want to play this game solely for the story, don't. The missions are almost more interesting than the story itself, but not quite.
Warframe has decent multiplayer in the forms of PvE and PvP. PvE is essentially multiple people playing the same mission at the same time and working together to complete the goal of said mission. I personally enjoy it more than PvP. PvP, on the other hand is multiple players fighting against each other with their own unique warframes, weapons, and mods. The thing that irks me a little is that PvP multiplayer doesn't have a matching system based on player skill level. This means that you, a less experienced player, might be fighting against someone with more than a year of experience, and some of the best gear possible, which can lead to many frustrating matches where you simply just keep losing over and over again.
This is the worst part of Warframe. Rather than working towards the materials needed to craft yourself weapons or a warframe, one can simply spend cash to buy whatever they want. In addition, crafting items can be quite annoying, and will often take hours of grinding the same missions over and over again. I'd be much happier if DE just put one simple price tag on this game and removed all in-game purchases.

The game suffers from a design flaw rather than a technical one, though there is the issue with the FPS. Mechanically the game is beautiful. The models are great, the build systems needs a cleanup on the snapping but works well considering the versatility of the landscape, and the dinosaur's stats and purposes were fairly balanced till the development of Scorched Earth. It's easy to have a goal and feel the pressure of survival in the early game.
Past the introduction is where we run into a problem. The design philosophy focuses on the confrontation of multiplayer but not with the mentality of a game. Because of the way that resource acquisition ramps up and the overall brittleness of your accumulated wealth, it's very easy to get hit with total ruin and then the game actually fights you on the climb back to the top by granting even greater benefits to everyone ahead of you in their wealth accumulation. It just keeps accelerating the rich to be richer because that's the designed reason to continue playing the game. You just can't however. Unless you have an overwhelming amount of force in the form of man power, you live in a constant fear of your sandcastle getting kicked over as soon as another player spots you aren't there to man the brittle walls and protect you vulnerable and easy-to-exploit-and-kill dinosaur companions. A new character with a boomerang can, will, and probably already killed your entire posse. The hands off policy of the server admins does NOT help. Seriously, anything you can do to exploit your fellow man is fair game. I personally had a tribe member use their permissions to demolish our gates and steal every valuable dino before transferring to a rival and using the same dino's they stole to flatten our base to the ground. It's not a fair system; it's not supposed to be. It's multiplayer in its most primal form which means you shouldn't expect to give anyone a run for your money. You will be cheated and you will lose eventually and they WILL keep you down.
The problem with single player in this sand box is again, the unfortunate design that's used to keep players playing the multiplayer. Ramped up resource generation makes the game easier but, unlike some other sand boxes like Minecraft, it doesn't allow you to create content. The simplistic building system doesn't allow for sprawling bases or pillared mountain passes, or even a basic bridge across a river without a considerable exploitation of the building system's off-by-one error in dealing with the base snapping. You can't build that dream place you want without dedicating hours and hours of time and resources into researching and exploiting bugs till they accidently patch the one bug you need, accidently wrecking their own building system. But I digress. The design features a lack of content creation or even objective creation after you reach the top. There is no opposition. There is no resource loss. There's no danger. After you reach the top, challenge is gone, only grinding remains so you can afford the resources necessary to pay for the constant demolishing you need to do to take advantage of the building system.
As a whole, wait and watch the game. Wait for them to redesign it. It's a beautiful beta with interesting procedural generation, lovely dinosaurs, and a wonderful world to explore. But Jesus Christ, the ugliest human elements are reflected in the design, execution, player base and it won't be fixed any time soon. It can't be. The design is flawed on the highest level and they need to sit down and rethink everything. Seriously, watch this developer closely. If they release games (or even this game) with this design in the future, you can and will be cheated.

Just to be clear, this is just my opinion. I rarely make game comments, but at 2000+ hours, I’ve a strong opinion and appreciate reading others insights when they REALLY spend some time in a game.
All in all ARK is a good game. Like all games, if the IP doesn’t attract you there’s nothing about this environment that will change your opinion. On the presentation of an immersive prehistoric world, they’ve done a fantastic job. Feels like survival even if there isn’t a human ganking you for your thatch. You will spend hours learning the pain of lost gear and joy of riding a T-Rex like a living tank. Lots of moment to moment issues that popup and make the play demanding and rewarding at the same time. Many of the issues with the game are technically incomplete, un-optimized or bug problems; and not missing mechanics. In fact the studio supports modders who do a great job filling in glaring holes on the PvE side of the equation.
However, ARK is a game with dual personality disorder. It’s trying to be a PvP pro-game even though it shines as a PvE sandbox builder. This is a fight in which the product and player don’t win. Because the studio is putting a lot of effort into improving the PvP instead of polishing what they already have. I couldn’t say why they’re doing this definitively, but it’s only the modding community that is floating the game… and Kudos to them and the studio for making it possible.  The end result is that they’ve postponed optimization and completed features and are still in early access.
PvP is sadly missing serious balance and Meta game design. The competition for your PvP gaming dollars would be better spent on one of the many other more thoroughly developed shooters on the market. PvP in ARK fosters destructive, community crushing behavior that pushes out the players that invest in creating things that the griefer needs to destroy. This eventually causes the griefing players to lose interest when no one tries any longer to make something for them to destroy, but by that time the builders have abandoned the server or perhaps ARK all together. Bad plan.
Fortunately Wildcard allows unofficial servers. Here you have a chance on finding a tweaked and fan managed environment, with or without modding. You can also find better PvP experience since it may be managed; moreover in my option it is perhaps the best PvE experience. My advice would be to avoid public servers with PvP and seek out some learning time on a PvE server. Playing alone is fine but doesn’t really fulfill the games potential nor your enjoyment when surviving is hard and lonely work. If the game still intrigues you, Mods will expand the fun and extend the value of your purchase.
In summary, at $20 dollars this is a good value. You don’t need Scorched Earth expansion to start, so don’t feel you’ll miss out too much without it as this is not a MMO like WoW etc. It’s mostly just a change of environment and some different dinos. So, go play with dinosaurs the way you always dreamed of, just don’t expect PvP to as fun.

You can't build that dream place you want without dedicating hours and hours of time and resources into researching and exploiting bugs till they accidently patch the one bug you need, accidently wrecking their own building system. But I digress. The design features a lack of content creation or even objective creation after you reach the top. There is no opposition. There is no resource loss. There's no danger. After you reach the top, challenge is gone, only grinding remains so you can afford the resources necessary to pay for the constant demolishing you need to do to take advantage of the building system.
As a whole, wait and watch the game. Wait for them to redesign it. It's a beautiful beta with interesting procedural generation, lovely dinosaurs, and a wonderful world to explore. But Jesus Christ, the ugliest human elements are reflected in the design, execution, player base and it won't be fixed any time soon. It can't be. The design is flawed on the highest level and they need to sit down and rethink everything. Seriously, watch this developer closely. If they release games (or even this game) with this design in the future, you can and will be cheated.

Warframe is a game of seeming contradictions that works out surprisingly well. It heavily aims at online co-op play, yet for the most part it works equally fine as a single-player experience. And it is a game in which space ninjas may run around wielding shotguns and other noisy weaponry.
It's free to play, yet of remarkable quality in its visuals and design - and in addition its paid content policy is comparatively fair - you can access almost everything without the need to pay any real money, the only real limitation in this case would be a rather limited inventory (i.e. not more than two or three warframes and five weapons, iirc). Other than that, paid content is mainly cosmetics and indirect time-savers (ressource/XP boosts and the like), but to some degree even these can be obtained without the need to pay money. And even if you really don't want to spend money, the premium currency is still tradable in-game and with a moderate amount of extra work you can relatively easily get quite a sum of it to pay for those extra inventory spaces or whatnot. I do know of some players for who this approach works perfectly fine.
Content-wise this game has come a long way, so that by now there's plenty of stuff to check out - it also continues to be changed and expanded on and will probably for quite a while longer, and noticeably! Basically to the degree that by now even I (as someone who only started when the game was already out for two years) have witnessed some players who have taken a break for a year or more coming back and remarking that a lot of things have changed, but usually for the better.
The most amazing feat about Warframe to me is the level design. Sure, all levels are basically pieced together from a rather limited set of predefined tiles (putting aside the recently released Plains of Eidolon, which are actually a fixed open-world area), so that you'd think you've seen them all after a couple hours of play. However, these tiles are built in such a way that they may be traversed in a grand multitude of ways, and by going through them differently you'll encounter all sorts of nooks and crannies that contain additional loot or other secrets, which at least to me provided a lot of replay value. Last but not least, even these tiles continue to see improvements, be that subtle lighting changes or slight reorganisation, and sometimes even some new tiles get thrown into existing tilesets to keep them from becoming too repetitive.
Nevertheless, I will certainly admit that Warframe is not for everyone. It is a fast-paced cooperative game (there is technically PVP, but almost nobody plays that), and it's all about that grind. While I personally don't mind the grind as much, since even if the missions themselves tend to be rather repetitive after a while, there is almost always some more new stuff to unlock and play around with. But, as I can very well understand, for some people this is not exactly motivating. Another point is the lore and story of Warframe: it's there, and it's also surprisingly deep, but it doesn't exactly jump at you. You have to go looking for it, and potentially dig a while to get to the more subtle implications of it - awesome for me, but probably not for people who prefer to be entertained rather than finding entertainment in trying to unearth another story hint.
All in all, it's hard for me not to recommend Warframe. It's free, so even if you don't like it it's usually not a waste of money. And if you like co-op shooters, you should definitely give it a try. Or if you always dreamed of being a magical robot space ninja fighting laser-armed robot chicken from space. Or if you always wanted to go spear-fishing on earth a couple hundred milennia in the future. Or...
The story is still better than Twilight!

In Warframe, everything is about grinding. You start with one frame and a few weapons, and you grind to upgrade your weapons and get materials in order to craft more weapons so you can grind to upgrade them.
All in all, Warframe is easily one of the best games I've played in a while, though I recommend bringing a few friends along for the ride. Its not quite as much fun killing a few hundred enemies when you have to do it alone.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

I've been playing this game for over a year now, and I have to say that it is my favorite game that I have ever played, however that doesn't mean that it runs well, or isn't a buggy mess, because it is. However it is still in early access.
I do not by any means have a good computer. It is several years old and has a core i3 processor, and the rest of its specs are about as impressive as that one. The requirements for ark, just to run the game on the worst possible settings (essentially looking like roblox with dinosaurs) are average. If you have a high end PC, I'm sure you could run it no problem on the highest settings and enjoy the graphics.
While I love this game, I would not recommend it to people without a beast of a computer if stunning graphics and consistantly smooth gameplay are what makes or breaks a game for you. Even if your computer has no issues running the game, there will most likely be a TON of server lag.
(The following experiences I have had were all on multiplayer servers, I have not played the game in single player.) On all the servers I have played on there have been extreme lag spikes, leading to me and my dinos being killed many times. The other players I have played with on the servers have complained about the amount of lag as well. I have noticed that official servers seem to have the most lag, and until the game is worked on a bit more I would recommend that people play on unofficial servers if they have extremely bad lag on official servers. (just be sure the server has been established for a while and that there are no plans to shut it down in the near future, because that's a sure fire way to lose dinos and character data unless you upload them into an obelisk *if you plan to use the upload/download feature to transfer data I would recommend looking it up first).
If you are someone that focuses mainly on game content, the open world experience and constantly changing gameplay, I would highly recommend this game, as long as you have the patience to spend the sometimes hours it takes to run the game at a playable level, and the willingness to start over if the game glitches and you find yourself or your dinos dead. If you don't want to put alot of time and effort into this game, I would suggest waiting for it to leave early access.

(I've updated my review to be more objective.)
TL;DR: The game was designed to suck as much of your time as possible using several Skinner boxes. However, if you host your server and use mods, you can make that a much better experience.
The game is really fun in terms of exploration and survival.
There are very beautiful vista and places to explore, especially on the Ragnarok map.
Being able to ride dinos, or just build fortresses is pretty nice too.
There are, however, strongly negative points:
- unless you host your own server and tweak the settings, this game is just a massive boring grind. For example, it takes hours to tame one dinos! This is insane!
- you will never make it to end game unless you have a very big tribe, or host your own server with tweaked settings. This game is very unfriendly to small tribes, or lone players.
- the contruction system is clunky, will almost never be able to make things look the way you want due to bugged snap points or overlaps.
- The paid DLC should have been free content, seriously.
So, why do I still recommend the game?
Simply put, because of the possibility to host your own server, in which you can adjust the settings to fix almost all the negative points. Mods are also a great source of fixes to enhance the experience.
Conclusion: The developers have done a great job overall, but the balance of these systems is underwhelming.

Warframe is a good game.
for a few hundred hours.
I've realized after playing so much of the game, most of the game is just a repetitive grind farming materials, warframes, weapons, and then improving your equipment with formas, catalysts, and reactors. All for what? It makes a lot of missions incredibly easy unless you are doing some of the end game content like raids. Now for a few hundred hours it's a ton of fun doing this with your friends but then after a while you realize that this is the whole game. Yeah there's quests you can do like the second dream and the new strange but after you do them, you can't even replay most of them and even if you could replay all of them you probably won't even want to. The upgrading process is terrible due to nerfs to guns and warframes. You'll spend a ton of time on a weapon or warframe that you really like then it has the possibility of getting nerfed so all of your resources go to waste. That might be the worst part of this game for everyone. Also if you spend your time upgrading a weapon or warframe that isn't special like a prime, wraith, or vandal, they could make that item have a special counterpart and you waste your resources. While i'm not a game developer, I know something like this can be easily fixed. I feel that there should be a refund or at least a partial refund system so that you are able to refund any upgrades you put on your equipment. That would definitely improve the game for everyone. Now you're probably wondering why I'm giving this a postive recommendation. This is for a two reasons. One, the game is free to try out so if you are curious about playing the game, I'd recommend it since you won't have to worry about spending money to play it. Two, the game is a lot of fun for a few hundred hours like I said in the beginning especially with friends. In the end, I think it's worth checking out because it's free and you could have fun with it more than I did after a while. If you love grinding then this will be your favorite game of all time. It's best if you play this game in short bursts and not for hours and hours and hours so you don't get burnt out of it.
tl;dr: The game is fun for a while but has a lot of flaws that can cause burnout.

This is probably the best free to play game I have played. It's addictive in nature to people who like fast paced action games and I haven't gotten bored of it yet.
The bad. The game requires you to grind your characters quite a bit to be able to play effectively, this could be a detriment if you don't like the idea of level grinding. The game takes a long time to get into and has a decently steep learning curve for a free to play multiplayer game, but on the other hand it isn't as steep as games like League of Legends or Smite, or nearly as steep as the plateaued cliff that is DOTA 2. And the music in the game is decently unoriginal with the voice acting being passable.
The good. The game is visually astounding, which is something that you don't often, if ever see in a free to play game. The gameplay is pretty smooth once you get into it and there is nothing more satisfying than quickly breezing through a level while getting fast melee kills. The game is also very fun and easy to pick up for around a half hour to an hour. The other bit I like about it is that it isn't pay to win, each of the characters is just as good as the next and if a character is more support then the game actually tells you that the character is in the characters description. If you like playing solo most support characters can also be played very effectively as damage classes. Having a real world time period were a blueprint needs to be made makes you take a break from the game was well, it makes me come back the next day to get my new weapon, or in a few days to get the new Warframe. Really the only thing you have to pay for is aesthetics for your Warframes and weapons.

On the verge of buying ARK but looking at reviews first? Good thing I'll give MY honest breakdown of the game for you. This review is biased as all hell, so don't look any further into this if you're easily triggered or dislike a lot of words.
ARK is one of those games you develop a love-hate relationship with.
If you're looking for a fun game to sink a LOT of time into, ARK might just be for you.
If you like taming sh*t, killing sh*t, building sh*t, crafting sh*t, eating the developers sh*t, ARK might just be for you.
This comes at a cost, though. Bugs and exploits? Look no further because ARK will satisfy all your needs! Dinos disappearing into thin air, dying to nothing, losing your entire inventory to the void, and much, much more!
If you don't play at least a somewhat modded server or at least a server with higher rates, look forward to the constant grind and eternal suffering. Nothing is fun about sitting around a dinosaur for 12 hours babysitting basically nothing. You press a button to make sure it doesn't wake up while it eats the food in its inventory. Vanilla ARK has its quirks and some people enjoy it, don't get me wrong - but this just never suited my needs; so I turned to modded servers.
As of this review I have 1.3k+ hours, and <400 were spent on vanilla ARK. Finding an unofficial server to fit your needs won't take much time as long as you check the "server advertisement" area. There's a big issue with mods and ARK though, and that is that they're not quite... compatible yet. Is that the right word to use here? The reason I mention this is because ARK will make you sit your ♥♥♥ through a 10-20 minute loading screen on heavily modded servers. Heavily modded meaning ~20+ mods, assuming they have at least a few of the larger ones in there (such as the dino overhauls, i.e Annunaki, ARK Comes Alive, Extinction). I always considered this as a sacrifice for a much more enjoyable and fun playthrough.
The game itself is rather unoptimized even for beefier PCs. I've had the exact same PC specs since I started this game, and my FPS throughout the patches have been spotty, some days I'm at a constant 60, other days jumping between 40-60. As of right now, even on my mid-grade PC I can run mostly highs and a few mediums WITH SM5 disabled. If you buy this game, Google "ARK launch options" and profit with the extra 20-30 FPS.
This game can be fun on your own, but if you're not playing with friends the experience is a lot less amazing. So pack a friend or two and bring them along for the hunt.
Now, here's a my quick overview of the pros and cons to ARK.
Pros:
Huge variety of dinosaurs. Gotta catch 'em all :^)
Flying dinos, water dinos, land dinos, take your pick
Thousands of servers to pick from, all with different rules, players, and mods
PvE, PvP, PvPvE, you name it, theres a spot for everyone
Lots and lots of items to craft - weapons, armors, tools, structures, workstations (smithy, chem bench, etc)
Breeding dinosaurs. That feeling when you get a beautiful, high-statted dino... hnnng
One of those games where you just turn on some good music and grind/tame/build away
Resources aren't impossible to get but the grinding itself is rather tedious
Cons:
Grinding - if you dislike it, you will most likely not enjoy ARK
Harsh on beginners. The game is difficult and has a learning curve, prepare to die a lot
Lots and lots of bugs/exploits
Vanilla ARK sucks
Optimization
Characters customization. A set male and a set female with a few sliders and hair/eye colors
Devs are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s - sorry - but they do not usually listen to their community and will do as they please
Balance - dinosaurs really aren't a fearsome presence once you get something scary yourself
You can build some crazy sh*t, but snapping and collision are a HUGE issue. I put this in cons, however I personally enjoy the building (besides the side of salt usually served with it)
Not a voxel-based game - this means no digging into the ground
AND BEFORE ANYONE SAYS ♥♥♥♥: YES, I DO KNOW THIS GAME IS EARLY ACCESS, but this is for the people looking to buy this game NOW. I am personally satisfied with ARK hence the thumbs-up. My review will remain like this until these issues have been ironed out.

I really wish I could recommend games like this, but I suffer from a very philosophical problem when I talk about this game with others, and it's not even a problem specific to ARK: Survival Evolved; it's a problem with taking advantage of being in Early Access.
The game is fun, and it was enjoyable, and it looks good. I don't mind paying money for an Early Access game; however there has to be a line in the sand somewhere and for me it's defined by this game. If you can't even officially release a game, you shouldn't be doing development on an expansion, especially not one you feel like you should charge people for. Finish your base game, and while I personally think it's in poor taste you could even do your expansion pack as day 1 DLC, but I cannot back a game whos developers hide behind the Early Access curtain.
It really feels like the only reason this happens is so that if you do something underhanded like charge for an expansion pack to an unfinished game, and people end up hating a feature or something the developers can just say "Well it's early access so we're still toying with this idea." And then the bandwagon of "You should have known x, y, and z; it's early access afterall" gets going, but it shouldn't be a justification of having a questionable development cycle.

The game is fun, and it was enjoyable, and it looks good. I don't mind paying money for an Early Access game; however there has to be a line in the sand somewhere and for me it's defined by this game. If you can't even officially release a game, you shouldn't be doing development on an expansion, especially not one you feel like you should charge people for. Finish your base game, and while I personally think it's in poor taste you could even do your expansion pack as day 1 DLC, but I cannot back a game whos developers hide behind the Early Access curtain.
It really feels like the only reason this happens is so that if you do something underhanded like charge for an expansion pack to an unfinished game, and people end up hating a feature or something the developers can just say "Well it's early access so we're still toying with this idea." And then the bandwagon of "You should have known x, y, and z; it's early access afterall" gets going, but it shouldn't be a justification of having a questionable development cycle.

This one's just not for me. While I'll definitely say I love the art direction, some of the concepts, and that the combat is fast paced and a ton of fun. However...
It only took me a few hours before I realized "Oh balls, this game is a massive grindfest, isn't it?"
I don't recommend this game if you're the kind of peson who isn't up for grinding the same missions over and over again to try and earn something rather than buy it outright. Unless you REALLY like the gameplay or are willing to spend real money to entirely bypass the grind, this will probably get stale quickly.
To get anything in this game you need to either spend a disproportionately large amount of time grinding the same missions over and over for the resources you need to craft something, or break out that wallet and get anything immediately. Once I got enough credits, I went to the marketplace, and after I'd managed to get through all the pages of stuff that wants me to spend the premium currency on, I found where I could get stuff I earned with in game cash. I decided at this point I wanted a new secondary weapon. While I could afford any of the weapons available at my level, I couldn't craft any of them because they all required either resources I couldn't get anywhere, or required me to have other weapons already that weren't even for sale.
So screw it, I thought. I'll try one of the other warframes. I wanna try out Volt. Oh, they don't even sell it? Well, how about Ember? So I bought the blueprint for Ember, and then I needed all the parts of Ember which after looking up how to get them online, saw none of them were available to me either. But if I crack out my wallet I could have any gun available for my rank, and any warframe immediately. I would be fine with this if buying something wasn't so disproportionate to the amount of time needed to spend on it if you don't pay for it.
I might play this game some more if I have a little time and just want to kill a lot of things as a super cool space ninja. But I'm not going to be putting in the effort to actually work towards anything. In my own personal opinion, it's too grindy and repetitive for it to be worth the payoff.

Overall, I love what Ark has done during its developement. It has its flaws, and yes its Early Access, but I whole heartedly reccomend this game. Look at the progress, the updates, the work done over its year and a half. Is it still in early access, yes, but its one of the most frequently updated titles amongst that sea of vaporware.
I will address the elephant in the room, paid DLC. Yes, its asking for more money before its even been released. You dont have to buy it, it goes on sale regularly as does the game itself. I purchased both at full price because I want to see the game go further. The Scorched Earth dlc is practically a seperate game, its a true expansion pack and when are those ever free? It's more than a simple map, and quite frankly its hard.
Optimization is still a mess but it has improved dramatically. As someone who has played since early on when running medium spec was a challenge its vastly improved. My friend runs it on a dated gaming laptop. Initially it stuttered around at about 20fps tops on min settings, but now even his laptop is running mostly medium spec in a playable range.
The biggest drawback is the community. Official servers end up a joke since there are no admins. Reviews and posts you read about invading Chinese and Russian players aren't actually joking, it is a thing. Obviously griefers come from all over but specific groups have made names for themselves using their distant ping spike and aimbots to their advantage. I hear Rust has the same problem. Play with friends, find a good unofficial server or run your own, and you'll have a good time.
This game has a bright future and I look forward to its completion. Edit: I wanted to update this for all the idiots commenting on the sheep being only available if it won the vote. They stated very clearly that it was being implemented whether it won OR NOT, but many recent reviews still call them out on it incorrectly. It wasn't some fine print, or hidden message, and certainly not a threat. If people would actually read they would have seen the glaringly obvious print stating it was coming win or lose.
