Overall, I love what Ark has done during its developement. It has its flaws, and yes its Early Access, but I whole heartedly reccomend this game. Look at the progress, the updates, the work done over its year and a half. Is it still in early access, yes, but its one of the most frequently updated titles amongst that sea of vaporware.
I will address the elephant in the room, paid DLC. Yes, its asking for more money before its even been released. You dont have to buy it, it goes on sale regularly as does the game itself. I purchased both at full price because I want to see the game go further. The Scorched Earth dlc is practically a seperate game, its a true expansion pack and when are those ever free? It's more than a simple map, and quite frankly its hard.
Optimization is still a mess but it has improved dramatically. As someone who has played since early on when running medium spec was a challenge its vastly improved. My friend runs it on a dated gaming laptop. Initially it stuttered around at about 20fps tops on min settings, but now even his laptop is running mostly medium spec in a playable range.
The biggest drawback is the community. Official servers end up a joke since there are no admins. Reviews and posts you read about invading Chinese and Russian players aren't actually joking, it is a thing. Obviously griefers come from all over but specific groups have made names for themselves using their distant ping spike and aimbots to their advantage. I hear Rust has the same problem. Play with friends, find a good unofficial server or run your own, and you'll have a good time.
This game has a bright future and I look forward to its completion. Edit: I wanted to update this for all the idiots commenting on the sheep being only available if it won the vote. They stated very clearly that it was being implemented whether it won OR NOT, but many recent reviews still call them out on it incorrectly. It wasn't some fine print, or hidden message, and certainly not a threat. If people would actually read they would have seen the glaringly obvious print stating it was coming win or lose.

Is Warframe grindy? Yes, it is.
Does that make it a bad game? Nope.
Okay, so. I'm usually not one for grindy games, I feel it's boring and a waste of time. Surprisingly Warframe doesn't feel that way. You have to farm materials and blueprints so you can build tons of stuff (weapons, frames, forma, etc) but the fact that you have to grind a bit for some stuff (because RNG is RNG) doesn't take away the fun. The game is fast-paced, has parkour (space-ninja style parkour, but parkour nontheless) and while there are limited types of missions it's still fun because every run is different.
The game is F2P, which is always nice, and you can buy almost everything with in-game currency (credits). Cosmetic stuff is usually purchased with Platinum (plat is like Riot Points, you pay some real money and get platinum to spend ingame) but you can get blueprints for some of it (different helmets for frames, etc). You can also spend plat to speed up anything you're building from a blueprint, like weapons, helmets and you can even accelerate the incubation of a kubrow egg!
So, instead of saying that it's "pay to win" I'd say is "pay-to-not-wait-days-for-stuff", because let me tell you building frames is a long process of buying the blueprint with credits, farming the boss that drops the three components you need to build it (helmet, chassis and systems) plus the materials you need to build each plus the Orokin cell you need for certain frames and THEN you have to wait a ♥♥♥♥♥on of hours for it to get built. You can speed up the process with plat but it's completely unnecesary if you're a patient person.
Anyway, would I recommend this game? Yeah, sure. If you don't mind grindy stuff and you like weird♥♥♥♥♥space ninjas this is your game. They also update the game and deploy hotfixes regularly and the community is usually helpful.

It only took me a few hours before I realized "Oh balls, this game is a massive grindfest, isn't it?"
I don't recommend this game if you're the kind of peson who isn't up for grinding the same missions over and over again to try and earn something rather than buy it outright. Unless you REALLY like the gameplay or are willing to spend real money to entirely bypass the grind, this will probably get stale quickly.
To get anything in this game you need to either spend a disproportionately large amount of time grinding the same missions over and over for the resources you need to craft something, or break out that wallet and get anything immediately. Once I got enough credits, I went to the marketplace, and after I'd managed to get through all the pages of stuff that wants me to spend the premium currency on, I found where I could get stuff I earned with in game cash. I decided at this point I wanted a new secondary weapon. While I could afford any of the weapons available at my level, I couldn't craft any of them because they all required either resources I couldn't get anywhere, or required me to have other weapons already that weren't even for sale.
So screw it, I thought. I'll try one of the other warframes. I wanna try out Volt. Oh, they don't even sell it? Well, how about Ember? So I bought the blueprint for Ember, and then I needed all the parts of Ember which after looking up how to get them online, saw none of them were available to me either. But if I crack out my wallet I could have any gun available for my rank, and any warframe immediately. I would be fine with this if buying something wasn't so disproportionate to the amount of time needed to spend on it if you don't pay for it.
I might play this game some more if I have a little time and just want to kill a lot of things as a super cool space ninja. But I'm not going to be putting in the effort to actually work towards anything. In my own personal opinion, it's too grindy and repetitive for it to be worth the payoff.

This game is captivating. As your first survivor loads into the Ark you stare in wonder at your surroundings. Some are lucky and start on a beach, or among herbivores. Other spawn in and are immediately mauled by a carnivore. Make no mistake, you will die a few times before you get yourself situated and start making progress. Once you make a home, and start exploring, the game really opens up.
The world is well detailed and full of beautifully crafted creatures. There is almost always a sense of danger when exploring new areas because you never know what you will see, or see you.
I really suggest playing this game with friends. With multiple players taking different crafting engrams you can really take advantage of resources and make it easier to survive. The game becomes more enjoyable as you level, tame new dinosaurs, and reach more complex technologies.
Regarding the paid DLC Scorched Earth and the large amount of negative feedback I am seeing on this board. I thoroughly enjoyed the DLC and feel very satisfied with my purchase. It is important to note that the DLC is intended to be a significantly more challenging experience than the original map and you will die very frequently until situated. With knowledge of the game mechanics you can overcome these challenges and easily enjoy the content.
Regarding a pre-launch game putting out DLC with a price tag, I don't see the issue. It's a quality product and I've gotten more than my money's worth from it.
I've played this pre-launch game more than any full retail release game I've gotten in the past few years. If you like gathering resources, building, exploration, and dinosaurs...this game is for you.

This is honestly a pretty cool game I love the dino textures they look great, there are of course "random death events" like running into a Alpha Raptor early on, but if you like survival challenges like me then stuff like that, as long as it doesn't happen to to often, keeps the game interesting. ok sense the revews section is around 85% people complaining about optimisation and releasing paid DLC in early acsess, allow me to give you a better idea of actual Gameplay/ and before i start, yes, this game is morbidly optimised, if your not sure about your grafics card. make sure you have atleast 16 gigs of ram, i have a decent graphics card (or so i'm told) and can get 20 or so FPS with normal game play, with evreything on low, and no sky effects, so yeah,
ARK: survival evolved is a survival game about taming dinosaurs and other prehistoric creatures to make your life eaiser. while wildcard has sticked relitivly close to there source material, some exeptios have been made because Gameplay>realism. the progression system is decent, and prevents players from getting to OP to quickly, while this game can be grindy, whenever you load up a world, you can change nearly evrey mechanic's stats, tame rate, level rate, player resistance, you name it, you can tweak it (quick tip, you can change the numbers manually beyond the slider limit), and the modding community is also very good, while they're mostly just small quality of life things, such as any mas stack mod, there are a small few massive content packs. such as Annuaki genesis that ad tons of content,
this game ofcourse is not without it's flaws, as said above, optimisation, but if you can run this at full power, this game looks downright butiful, just don't complain when you can't make a steak out of a potato, ok? and this game has it's fair share of bugs, (but what do you expect from a game? no game is ever compleatly bug free) and refer to other reveiws for server things, i only play single player, or with a friend in a private server), there's also the fact that A. you can only have 1 save per map, so you can't have 2 diffrent playthroughs oon the island or center, and the music can be WAY to intense at times, sometimes you'le be crafting somthing then all of the sudden some really intense battle-esq music will start playing and you'll start feeling really tense, which wouldn't be a bad thing, had this been a horror game, but it's not sooo.
and as for the whole "paid DLC while in early acsess" thing, i have no major issues with it, sure, locking somthing as useful as Vultures and Epic as Wyverns was a bit of a jerk move on wildcard's part, Ark (apart from the horrible optimisation) feels like a compleated game to me, heck, if they went through and optimised it a bit(lot) they could release it as a compleated game with updates, like minecraft for say, noone would complain.
all'n'all i give this a 7.8/10- poor optimisation, and to much water (c-mon i'm a mudkip(as of writing this) i had to make that joke)

to any aspiring survivors, i unrelentingly recomend taming a herd of Ovis (sheep) as the mutton they drop is more effective than kibble for taming (most) carvivores. for example in order to tame a lvl 150 giga with a 1x tame rate it takes 37 quetzal kibble, and 2:13 hours to tame, while it take 39 raw mutton and only 1:27 hours to tame a 150 giga, however, it spoils Very quickly, taking 9m 20s to do so, and only having a stack sive of one, probably your best bet would be to get a quetzal with fridges on its back and only havesting the mutton when you plan to tame somthing (it last 16 hours in a fridge). or, if you don't have and acsess to a fridge or such, you can cook it and, while certainly loosing effectiveness, it lasts around 7x longer and stacks intoo thirty, all while still being more effective than raw priime meat, taking 73 cooked mutton and 2h 44m for the before mentioned giga, or 97 raw prime meat and 3h 38m, all while constintally having to gather said prime meat inorder to avoid the spoil time worse than the mutton's. now how do can i get my hands on the holy sheep you may ask? well it's possibly the eisest tame in ark, all you have to do is feed it a single sweet vegitable cake and watch the magic happen... what? i said the tame is easy, i said nothing about getting the food for said tame. wall to y'all who are unaware of how tho get the cake, first you must plant rockarrot, savorroot, and longrass, the eisest way to do this is to collect seeds and place them in a medium crop plot with some poop and FULL waterskins for fertiliser and water, but you will need to keep an eye on the waterskins as they will need refilling in order to keep the crops irrigated, the more efficent way would be to build a green house using crystal, metal and cementing paste and irrigating the crop plots with stone or metal pipes, along with putting the poo in a fertiliser bin with some thatch and waiting, and waiting, and waiting some more, but if you want to cut the (metiforicle) crap and use (literal) crap instead, the most efficent way is to tame a phiomia (pig) and force feeding is stimberries, gaining one medium animal feces per 6(ish) berries, yoou also need sap, which requires a tree tap and by extention a tree platform in the redwood, but due to the tree snap mechanics you may aswell go all out and place 4 taps for quadruple the fun (and stickyness) keep in mind that each tree tap can only hold 2 sap, so check in often, you also need some stimulant (5 stimberries and 2 spark powder(1 stone and 2 flint)) and some fiber, now combine 7 sap, 2 rockarrots, 2 savoroot, 2 longrass, 4 stimulant, 25 fiber and a water canister with atleast 25% water remaing in a cooking pot or industrial cooker and vwalla (man that looks better in italics) you now have the sweet vegitable cake required to tame the ovis, but what other uses does it have you may ask? well, it can be given to a herbivor to automatically heal it when it health begins to drop, or it can be used to feed achitnas for an automatic cementing paste and polymer farm. oh, and you can collect woll from the sheep, did i mention that?

I've thousands of hours in this game, and I still enjoy going back to it every now and then. While I've exhausted most of the gameplay that I want to explore in the game, there's still a lot of depth to it and it's pretty hard to have 'completed everything there is to do'.
If you find yourself tiring of the game, take a hiatus. Come back in some time and you'll have a refreshed view on the game. A reason to play.
When playing the game, don't cheat yourself by taking shortcuts, and don't burn yourself out by trying to farm for a single part. Do alternative things.
The Good
-The flow of the game, the speed and fluidity of movement is still unparalleled
-Still one of the best free to play games out there
-It's still really pretty and gets prettier pretty frequently (alliteration all the way)
-There's a LOT of content to play through
-Each mission is generated differently
-Best with friends
-Pay wall can be bypassed through trading
-Game steadily gets better
The Bad
-Content trickles in
-Some of the recipes are ludicrous and require a lot of playtime to craft
-Some things are really grindy and/or locked behind RNG walls
-Some design decisions are convoluted and take months to correct
-Balancing is infrequent for the PvE element of the game, making the game either too easy or too hard for long periods of time and sometimes devs don't seem to pay attention to it
-Story content is kinda lightweight and dialogue can be a bit cheesy
-Can't replay quests yet
The Ugly
-I put over 1800 hours into this game total, got about 200 hours in before open beta.
-Power creep is prevalent and a major problem

Perhaps the best Free-to-Play game I've ever played.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Pros-
Mastery Rank over 20(I have pretty much everything, including all cosmetics) and I've only spent $10 on this game, and that was years ago.
Platinum(Premium Currency) is pretty easily obtainable as long as you know how to play the market, supply and demand is a real thing here.
Everything that effects your in combat efficiency is obtainable without Platinum.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cons-
Although every in-combat advantage is obtainable without Platinum, farming some Warframes can take literally a week if you're lucky(statistically possible, HIGHLY improbable) and have the time to put in.
Also, there are some Warframes that are unfarmable and locked behind random occurances in game; Unlike low drop rates, some actual bosses, weapons, and Warframes are not obtainable in the game unless the completely random "Alert" system allows them to be.
Trade chat is very fast paced and can be difficult to keep up with. On top of that, the in game chat leaves much to be desired.
(Pro&Con)As this game is in a seemingly permanent BETA, major systems are frequently changed/overhauled

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Other thoughts
The developers are very transparent and open to criticism; They're not above admitting when they've made mistakes and will openly discuss where they went wrong and how they plan to improve/fix problems.
They regularly host dev streams on their Warframe Twitch.tv channel and have been doing this for years now. They seem very committed to always improving their game.
If you're looking to not spend a dime, but still want to get everything and look cool while doing it, that is very possible with this game.
I would highly recommend that anyone not wanting to spend real money, just consider Platinum to be another farmable resource. Learn where to farm it in the Trade chat, you'll be looking for the items following "WTB".
Save yourself the time and trouble, be sure to buy Equinox with Platinum.

Remember watching the Jurassic Park movies and seeing vulnerable people trying to make their way through dense forests hoping they can get out alive without encountering a dinosaur? Well imagine you being in that situation.
Survival Evolved indeed. After hundreds of hours in Minecraft and roughly 150 hrs into 7 Days to Die (unfortunately once you have a protected base and gear, the game goes from survival mode to routine sadly).
I now turn to Ark.
I wasn't sure exactly when I was going to review this game, but I knew I was going to. Well the events of last night were reason enough to post my review sooner rather than later. Let me set the scenario for you all...
Myself and 2 coworkers are playing on a private server together working as a group. Set out with our newly crafted mobile water base with trapping container on the back, we made our second expedition to the North West to kill penguins and gather polymer so we can finally move into crafting mechanical/electronic components and weapons.
We pull up along side a massive cliff and one of my friends gets out to mine a rich metal node. I stayed on the boat with my rifle out to cover him in case a dire wolf or Argentavis showed up to ruin his day. When suddenly a Rex was standing behind him. The Rex apparently slide down the mountain and fell right behind my buddy. Damn near sh!t myself as this was my first experience with a Rex less than 50ft from me and I wasn't on the back of a bird and out of reach.
So I yell "Holy Sh!t theres a Rex attacking Shawn!". Squeeze off a round from my rifle, clearly not enough to bring down a Rex and Shawn dies. Myself and my other coworker jump on the boat but its too late, the Rex is upon us in seconds. My buddy takes the helm and pulls away from the shore line, the Rex is now standing on our boat trying to kill us as we sail out to open water. Out of sheer luck, the Rex glitches through the wall of our trapping container and is now in the trapping container. Suddenly we are safe to tranq and tame our first Rex. We stop the boat, bring her down and tame her. All 1 level of her ROFL. A level 1 Rex dropping out of the sky turned what might have been a dull expedition to the North into a scary moment that I now look back on and laugh my butt off at.
It's moments like these that turn an already fun game, into an amazing experience. And I look forward to many more with the guys I play this game with.
Hunting, Taming, Breeding and Riding dinosaurs all while trying to forage and craft to survive harsh weather and terrains. Pitch black darkness at night. Scary ambient sounds. The game is also very pretty graphically. Advance your way through the tech ladder, moving from simple weapons/tools like a stone axe, to manned and unmanned turrets. Turn a simple raft into a mobile fortress, taming cage or expedition boat. Build a sky base at the top of a mountain. There is so much to do in this game and after reading the rumored patch notes for the upcoming changes, I feel like this game will stand on it's own for quite a while.
Devs release updates multiple times a week. The game may not be a perfect experience, but it's a damn fun one!

This game is fantastic. Honestly, I cannot think of anything to fault it by.
Warframe is one of these games that seems to get more immersive with every hour spent on it. You develop your understanding of the game, your arsenal, your weapons, your chosen Warframe, (i.e. your "character", so to speak), and unlock new things as well. It never gets dull, never gets repetitive. There's just something about it that makes you thirst for more adventure, and hunger for action.
Whether its the feeling of Godly empowerment this game gives, the lore behind it and the superb writing of the game, the awesome parkour you can pull off, how visually stunning it is, (and how great the game sounds, too), the sense of Community and socialisation, (such as the trading feature), and how much you can get involved in, is all uncertain. I find it to be a mixture of all of the above, and more - to list all the reasons that make this game so fun to play and so enthralling would be impossible.
Warframe offers this perfect balance between challenge and a feeling of empowerment; missions vary in difficulty, where some can be completed within the blink of an eye, and others require a full squad of hardcore pros who've each got at least 1,500 or so hours of game time racked up. It offers a unique PVE experience that most of the game is structured around, however, there is an element of PVP that is strongly integrated with the game's lore. Furthermore, each game type offers something unique and different; PVE offering resources, credits, schematics for new items, mods boss fights, syndicate progress, and so much more, while PVP offers unique items, new characters right out the box, and a different style of play altogether.
What's more, this game is not Pay to Win at all. Certainly, you can unlock new weapons and characters with Premium currency, but all of this is obtainable through a unique trading experience, where you don't have to spend anything. Players get the option to trade items with one another, which can often earn you quite a lot of Premium currency; there is a bustling trading chat window, where each day, thousands of transactions are made and friendships are formed. You do not have to put a single penny, dime, or dollar into Warframe for anything - trading can earn you all that you need. Moreover, through this, Warframe also offers a unique and rare Community aspect, and there's something about this that just makes the game that more lovely to play.
In one short review, I cannot summarise even a hundredth of what this game has to offer. Just try it for yourself. Play for a few hours, visit different worlds, try the PVE and the PVP, and experience it for yourself. I was hooked instantly, as many others have been, but I cannot describe to you what this game can offer. You have to experience it for yourself, and I strongly advise that you drop whatever it is you're doing right now, and do so.
All I can say is "Brace Yourself", because you're in for one Hell of a ride, and one that you won't soon forget...

Nonetheless, I had to spend most of that time on a PvP server, simply due to the fact that PvE servers are horribly broken by the way the building system is implemented. Players are allowed to build anywhere except in an area where someone else has built. This allows a single person (or tribe) to claim any amount of land, or to block off any important resource it wishes, including item drops. Since you cannot harm other players' structures in PvE, this means whoever blocades the resources can keep them closed off indefinitely.
Also: The building system seems to be deliberately designed to be as frustrating as humanly possible, with snap points that vibrate all over when trying to build simple structures. I have no idea why there isn't simply a button to switch between snap points, instead of the 'auto' snap.

Warframe to me has the perfect balance of grind, enjoyable content, decent balance, solid developers, and intrigue. You are a Tenno, an independent band of space ninja's who fight the good fight against the Grineer(Mechanized clones), Corpus(Tech savvy traders) and the infested(mutated monsters). Operating in the shadows your actions will impact the solar system in positive and negative ways. Using specialized suits called Warframes you are given a set of abilities in addition to a Primary, Secondary and Melee weapon. You must use all of them to be successful.
Warfame caters to many crowds, those who like PvE, those who wish to kill each other(PvP), they just added raids(8 man very difficult missions) and now Sorties, which offer end game specific bonuses to your characters. The game itself provides many ways to dispatch enemies, with around 100-125 weapons and warframes, all customizable using a trading card esque system, where mobs drop weapon and warframe augments that do anything from extra damage, to increased health.
I have been playing since Update 7 or 8, mainly in bursts of extended play. At 246 hours played I have only scratched the surface of Warframe, in which I still have plenty of frames and weapons to collect and level up.
Large updates come at around 1 per two months or so, sometimes less, sometimes more, with smaller patches getting released bi weekly or so, which introduce new weapons, limited offer Tactical Alerts, or new warframes. The developers are quite fair, and the game is by no means pay to win. All items aside from some cosmetics can be had through ingame currency and crafting, with some grinding involved. Speaking of in game currency, Platinum is used to buy new weapons, frames, cosmetics, convenience items, and to speed the crafting wait times. The best part? you can trade almost anything you find for platinum if someone is willing to pay. This allows the totally free players to still enjoy the perks of platinum.
TL;DR
Pros:
-Varied gameplay: PvE, PvP, Raids, Sorties
-Varied mission styles: Exterminate, Defense, Survival, Mobile Defense, Capture, Rescue, Spy, Interception and a few more
-Frequent updates
-Tons of items and builds to be made, tweaked, and refined
-Crafting System
-Great graphics that are very well optimized. The game is going through a PBR(Physically based rendering) upgrade, as well as getting ambient occlusion added, along with PhysX particle support.
-Pretty solid community, most people will help you out and offer guidance if you ask the right questions and are willing to learn.
-Fair premium currency: Login rewards can net you discount coupons to buying the plat itself, or you can trade ingame items for premium currency at a pretty reasonable return rate.
Cons:
-Very grindy: I usually hate this, but warframe offers so many different weapons to choose from its really not that bad. Farming for a specific piece of gear can get VERY time consuming though.
-Still a little buggy: personally have not experienced anything game breaking, but there are a few annoying things that happen from time to time. Some clipping issues with weapon models and cosmetics.
-Tough to start out: as a new player they really don't give you much. The experience has been improved but you are left with sub par weapons to use for quite a while. Pro Tip - Find a nice clan to join that will give you a hand, there are plenty.
Overall the game has improved so so much since I first started playing, with the recent update it just keeps getting better and better. Would absolute recommend this game to anybody who wants to spend a little time killing some bad guys.

This game is fantastic. Honestly, I cannot think of anything to fault it by.
Warframe is one of these games that seems to get more immersive with every hour spent on it. You develop your understanding of the game, your arsenal, your weapons, your chosen Warframe, (i.e. your "character", so to speak), and unlock new things as well. It never gets dull, never gets repetitive. There's just something about it that makes you thirst for more adventure, and hunger for action.
Whether its the feeling of Godly empowerment this game gives, the lore behind it and the superb writing of the game, the awesome parkour you can pull off, how visually stunning it is, (and how great the game sounds, too), the sense of Community and socialisation, (such as the trading feature), and how much you can get involved in, is all uncertain. I find it to be a mixture of all of the above, and more - to list all the reasons that make this game so fun to play and so enthralling would be impossible.
Warframe offers this perfect balance between challenge and a feeling of empowerment; missions vary in difficulty, where some can be completed within the blink of an eye, and others require a full squad of hardcore pros who've each got at least 1,500 or so hours of game time racked up. It offers a unique PVE experience that most of the game is structured around, however, there is an element of PVP that is strongly integrated with the game's lore. Furthermore, each game type offers something unique and different; PVE offering resources, credits, schematics for new items, mods boss fights, syndicate progress, and so much more, while PVP offers unique items, new characters right out the box, and a different style of play altogether.
What's more, this game is not Pay to Win at all. Certainly, you can unlock new weapons and characters with Premium currency, but all of this is obtainable through a unique trading experience, where you don't have to spend anything. Players get the option to trade items with one another, which can often earn you quite a lot of Premium currency; there is a bustling trading chat window, where each day, thousands of transactions are made and friendships are formed. You do not have to put a single penny, dime, or dollar into Warframe for anything - trading can earn you all that you need. Moreover, through this, Warframe also offers a unique and rare Community aspect, and there's something about this that just makes the game that more lovely to play.
In one short review, I cannot summarise even a hundredth of what this game has to offer. Just try it for yourself. Play for a few hours, visit different worlds, try the PVE and the PVP, and experience it for yourself. I was hooked instantly, as many others have been, but I cannot describe to you what this game can offer. You have to experience it for yourself, and I strongly advise that you drop whatever it is you're doing right now, and do so.
All I can say is "Brace Yourself", because you're in for one Hell of a ride, and one that you won't soon forget...

I've thousands of hours in this game, and I still enjoy going back to it every now and then. While I've exhausted most of the gameplay that I want to explore in the game, there's still a lot of depth to it and it's pretty hard to have 'completed everything there is to do'.
If you find yourself tiring of the game, take a hiatus. Come back in some time and you'll have a refreshed view on the game. A reason to play.
When playing the game, don't cheat yourself by taking shortcuts, and don't burn yourself out by trying to farm for a single part. Do alternative things.
The Good
-The flow of the game, the speed and fluidity of movement is still unparalleled
-Still one of the best free to play games out there
-It's still really pretty and gets prettier pretty frequently (alliteration all the way)
-There's a LOT of content to play through
-Each mission is generated differently
-Best with friends
-Pay wall can be bypassed through trading
-Game steadily gets better
The Bad
-Content trickles in
-Some of the recipes are ludicrous and require a lot of playtime to craft
-Some things are really grindy and/or locked behind RNG walls
-Some design decisions are convoluted and take months to correct
-Balancing is infrequent for the PvE element of the game, making the game either too easy or too hard for long periods of time and sometimes devs don't seem to pay attention to it
-Story content is kinda lightweight and dialogue can be a bit cheesy
-Can't replay quests yet
The Ugly
-I put over 1800 hours into this game total, got about 200 hours in before open beta.
-Power creep is prevalent and a major problem

Host migration
DE are very hands on with their game and community, e.g. dev streams every other Friday, and active participation in their forums
Cons:
Starting game can be sluggish and inconsistant in its learning curve
Repetitive/grindy/RNG will not bless you this day
Peer-to-peer system
Can't kick AFK players
Many weapons are MR (mastery) fodder, and become useless once rank 30
Archwing hasn't been fleshed out yet and is irrelevant at this point
Conclusion:
While starting game can feel sluggish, once you've completed the tutorial and played a few games, it can be addictive and moreish. The huge variety of weapons, mods, and warframes allows for multiple play styles, so if one style doesn't work for you, try another! Has PvE missions, the AI bots are rather good, they respawn often, and coordinate, with a long sight range.  You need to be good at shooting and melee games to play this game.  Game also has several special movement like Running along walls, ziplines, Sliding, and going to need be good at using those too.
You start with 1 warframe from choice of 3 ( Excalibur, Volt, Mag). Each warframe has a level cap of 30.
There is a choice of weapons in the tutorial.
If you start playing, you need to do more research on how to play and what to buy and craft.
Give this game a try, it is free to play.

I think at this point, with 48 days of non-stop playtime in Ark, I have to openly admit that it is "my jam." The game that keeps on giving, the game that sucks away the hours and leaves me bleary eyed, husky voiced, and begging for more as I pour my 17th cup of coffee. I might have work in an hour or two, but half the time I won’t realize until my morning alarm rings; no regrets. I’m an adult, damnit. I refuse to acknowledge the months of less than stellar optimization, and see only the glory which is a giant stone box filled with baby war machines all begging for a kibble I ran out of days ago. I find it very peaceful, relaxing, even, managing to build a fortress, escape the onslaught of death machines and ding bats, and build a sanctuary as the grenades of the peons fall at my gates. Ark has brought me hours of enjoyment; I’ve met some really cool people, a few not so cool people, but mostly really awesome people. They have made Ark the experience it has been, and for me, the community has been stellar. It’s been one heck of a great ride, watching The Island transform from forest, mountains, and prairie, to a diverse ecosystem with various biozones to riding a wyvern across a desolate wasteland, wow, just wow.
So yea, I think Ark is pretty sweet. Something about 1150 hours tells me I’ve gotten my monies worth, 10/10 would no life, for life, again.

Ark: Survival Evolved... TL;DR version, The digital equivalant of an abusive spouse.
The longer version... Well stuff your face in a bucket of chum and inhale the salted blood deep, then get kicked in the daddy bag or throat punched by a complete stranger and savor that you paid cash money for this moment of glee.
I have had a love / hate relation with this game since day 1. Many have eloquently summed up the veritable storm of dino turds. So I'll just toss in my standard Pro / Con argument and walk away...
Pros!
+Frequent updates: Keeps the game new and fresh.
+No Motherf***ing zombies. Zombies are like vegan food... both had their time and should now just go away!
+Dino POWER, start out as a dweeb, tame an army, Rule the world!
+Not EA games. I shouldn't need to elaborate on that... Die in a fire EA.
+Robust crafing / building system. Everything is a multistep system that feels rewarding.
+It's pretty. Not much of a positive I know, but at least it doesn't look pieced together by farsighted T-rexes.
Cons!
-Playing alone is lonely... 200 hours of building a base to show it to dummies who interupt gaming with social visits.
-Playing on a a private server is lonely, A sea of 1-man tribes yay!
-Playing on a server... aka keeping the host on speed dial in case of an update locks out everyone.
-Dino GLITCH! Random despawns, random deaths, ARGH-tarded AI pathing.
-ULTRA-MEGA-CO-COMBO GRIND! Everything beyond making a campfire and straw hut takes hours if not days, or weeks.
-Base building glitch mess, aka the OCD inflammation device. Building is a steaming mess of raptor poo... end of story.
I may go back to playing it in the future, but at the moment I'm having a moment of lucidity. And if the devs got super awesome about bug squashing that may make me forget some things in the past. But as far as survival games go the power curve is laughable. Once you start amassing an army of disposable minions things go from scary to cakewalk real fast, and loading a Quetz with a battery of turrets to turn it into a flaying death fortress... You win... K... you just win.
I do reccomend this game to some however, despite being a glitchy time sink. The first 30-40 levels are rough, and playing with friends who are proactive boosts the fun factor, especially in a game where the actual fun is in getting set up to rule the world and be the big chief Pain-in-the-butt.
Endgame however is a massive void of why bother... you get to a point where the only thing you have is time and a big playground that becomes a grind of, Tame because I feel like it, kill things because - boredom, and hunt to feed the disposable army.
In closing, early game: big win, mega fun battery vibrating massage device of happy! It's thrilling, challenging, and suspenseful to explore the landscape, every moment alive is an achievement.
Late game: Is like taking a bath with grandpa... You just want something to happen to rip you away to a magical land... but the magic is gone and your hoping thats soap-on-a-rope in your hands. Or at least late game feels less like a game and more like a second job.

If you plan to play on official PVP... then don't play this game. Many who play on the official servers are constantly complaining about tribes who claim to use DDOS attacks and aimbots. Many of these who claim to use these tactics, claim get away with such because either they know the developers, or Battleeye does not stop it and that the devs won't do anything to fix this issue. (The reason that I believe this is do to videos and screenshots showing these players baragging, and these hacks in action.)
Also be prepared to be constantly moving from sever to sever, and never being able to accomplice all that much due to many of "mega tribes" chasing smaller tribes and single players from server to server. Many have been cuaght bragging on forums and in game about how they have bullied players into playing on PVE, unofficial servers, and or forcing them into giving up on playing the game all together. The least that can the devs could do is give smaller tribes and single players the ability to hide from the bigger tribes. Another good idea is to make where only tribes of the same size can attack one another, and i mean "one on one" and not several "small tribes" ganging up on one tribe
Another issue is that there is no real balance to this game on the PVP side. This is due to everything that the devs do that favor tribes that either have vast amount of players or those who don't have a life, and the gap continues to widen with each patch and update added to the game. PVP is all about balance with the deciding factor being the skills of the player, and not who has certain tames and outnumber the other group ten to one. Many of these tames are far too hard for the average player to get, due to be limtied amount of time an average person can invest into the game. To further rub salt into the wound many players are constantly busy with the upkeep and protection of what they alreaady have, and thus further limiting their time. Also many of the tames that you have aquired earlier in the game have all become pratically useless. With the only reason why you have gotten them in the first place is because you needed it for five minutes to reach the next stage in the game.
If you wish to still play PVP then i highly recommend to either play unofficial with a admin who actually cares about balance. Another optiion whould be to try the new offline raid protection servers, there you can base your play time to either when the alpha tribe isn't on, or at least a majority of their players.

Ark: Survival Evolved... TL;DR version, The digital equivalant of an abusive spouse.
The longer version... Well stuff your face in a bucket of chum and inhale the salted blood deep, then get kicked in the daddy bag or throat punched by a complete stranger and savor that you paid cash money for this moment of glee.
I have had a love / hate relation with this game since day 1. Many have eloquently summed up the veritable storm of dino turds. So I'll just toss in my standard Pro / Con argument and walk away...
Pros!
+Frequent updates: Keeps the game new and fresh.
+No Motherf***ing zombies. Zombies are like vegan food... both had their time and should now just go away!
+Dino POWER, start out as a dweeb, tame an army, Rule the world!
+Not EA games. I shouldn't need to elaborate on that... Die in a fire EA.
+Robust crafing / building system. Everything is a multistep system that feels rewarding.
+It's pretty. Not much of a positive I know, but at least it doesn't look pieced together by farsighted T-rexes.
Cons!
-Playing alone is lonely... 200 hours of building a base to show it to dummies who interupt gaming with social visits.
-Playing on a a private server is lonely, A sea of 1-man tribes yay!
-Playing on a server... aka keeping the host on speed dial in case of an update locks out everyone.
-Dino GLITCH! Random despawns, random deaths, ARGH-tarded AI pathing.
-ULTRA-MEGA-CO-COMBO GRIND! Everything beyond making a campfire and straw hut takes hours if not days, or weeks.
-Base building glitch mess, aka the OCD inflammation device. Building is a steaming mess of raptor poo... end of story.
I may go back to playing it in the future, but at the moment I'm having a moment of lucidity. And if the devs got super awesome about bug squashing that may make me forget some things in the past. But as far as survival games go the power curve is laughable. Once you start amassing an army of disposable minions things go from scary to cakewalk real fast, and loading a Quetz with a battery of turrets to turn it into a flaying death fortress... You win... K... you just win.
I do reccomend this game to some however, despite being a glitchy time sink. The first 30-40 levels are rough, and playing with friends who are proactive boosts the fun factor, especially in a game where the actual fun is in getting set up to rule the world and be the big chief Pain-in-the-butt.
Endgame however is a massive void of why bother... you get to a point where the only thing you have is time and a big playground that becomes a grind of, Tame because I feel like it, kill things because - boredom, and hunt to feed the disposable army.
In closing, early game: big win, mega fun battery vibrating massage device of happy! It's thrilling, challenging, and suspenseful to explore the landscape, every moment alive is an achievement.
Late game: Is like taking a bath with grandpa... You just want something to happen to rip you away to a magical land... but the magic is gone and your hoping thats soap-on-a-rope in your hands. Or at least late game feels less like a game and more like a second job.

I got ARK: Survival Evolved because, on one hand, I like survival games and, on the other, I really like dinosaurs. I can't say I've been disappointed on either count. However, it's not perfect and neither is this review - At the time of writing almost all of my play time has been single-player.
The game features a bit of a learning curve which is aided and abetted by the lack of a tutorial - I found reading a new player guide in PC Gamer to be helpful. However, it also seems that once you get the hang of the game the difficulty seems to come from events you bring on and random dinosaur spawns.
Crafting-wise, I don't mind ARK's model: instead of having to figure out how to arrange components you simply learn "engrams" and with the required materials you can create anything you have the engram for. I also like the progression of materials, especially early on the ability to slowly upgrade from simple, stone tools and thatch building to more advanced tools and weapons and wooden buildings feels like something is being accomplished.
As for those random dinosaur spawns are an important part in creating suspense in the game. Once food, shelter and clothing are taken care of it seems that the only real risks come from encountering dinosaurs. The possibility of in-game work being lost due to a dinosaur attack does create some tension as does trying to gather up the equipment needed to recapture what was lost and avenge yourself. Beyond this and trying to fasion more interesting and involved buildings, I haven't found a whole lot more to do, especially that's feasible on your own.
Overall, I have enjoyed my time playing ARK and I would recommend it to anyone who likes Minecraft and dinosaurs and has a decently rated system, especially if it's on sale. For people with lower-end systems, I would recommend holding off on it.

Ark: Survival Evolved is an almost famous, almost fully developed game that promises to make it big by using a simple recipe: survival, crafting and dinosaurs.
If you are curious about how you would fare on a remote island peppered with hostile conditions, head to the Early Access section of Steam and get the title.
The concept of the game is simple: you wake up naked and weaponless on a far away island and you must use your ingenuity, survival and dinosaurs' taming skills to stay alive.
Developer Studio Wildcard has already registered surging download numbers on Steam, and the coders focus to release variants for PS4 and Xbox One.
In an interview with Gadgets 360, Jesse Rapczak, the co-founder and co-creative director at Studio Wildcard, explained how Ark: Survival Evolved scored such a radiant success in the notoriously crowded Steam library.
Rapczak describes Early Access as both a "blessing and a curse." He notes that 100 percent transparency is paramount when dealing with fans, and developers must consistently listen to their feedback and implement the pertinent suggestions.
"Finally, even though the game is in an incomplete state, all steps should be taken to treat it as a live game to keep the quality of life high for users," Rapczak adds.
Visibility is another issue when trying to showcase a new concept to the public, and the hordes of titles that come out every year put additional pressure on developers, big and small.
So, how did Studio Wildcard's dinosaur-taming game manage to outplay the likes of Grand Theft Auto V and Metal Gear Solid V?
"Partnering with streamers, the media, getting the word out to players through lots of updates" is one part of the recipe of success, according to Rapczak.
He points out that players appreciate the way in which the game evolves, and the fact that they witness changes that they contributed to is very compelling.
YouTube traffic numbers show that Ark: Survival Evolved was one of the four most popular games on the video streaming platform for 2015.
Studio Wildcard's co-founder affirms that gamers can enjoy the title on the Xbox One, but his company has plans to bring it to the PS4 as well, in 2016. What is more, Xbox One owners can play Ark: Survival Evolved in couch co-op mode, which should make the exploration of the wild perilous world more fun with family or friends.
Seeing how console players expect a greatly polished product to arrive on their gaming systems, Ark: Survival Evolved takes a great leap of faith by launching early versions for Xbox and PS4.
"[C]onsoles still should have a higher level of polish and quality than a PC game because there is only one hardware target," Rapczak states. He explains that players should expect fewer updates for consoles, and at longer intervals than those for PC.
"We must go through the console owner [Microsoft or Sony] and they validate and test our updates before passing them on to users," he says.
Rapczak expressed his appreciation for how Microsoft's ID@Xbox team helped Studio Wildcard transform their dreams into a game. In spite of gaming studios' preference to launch their games on PS4 first, Rapczak discovered that Microsoft made it clear who is "developer-friendly."
Rapczak, who worked on Microsoft's Hololens as technical art director, further mentions that the game has virtual reality compatibility and all it needs is for the goggles to hit the stores.
PC gamers agree that Ark: Survival Evolved is a neat example of nicely wrapped early access. Whether console players will find it to their liking or not, only time can tell. Until then, Studio Wildcard promises to deliver a backstory, an end game and multiple expansions.
"It's really amazing, and I'm so humbled by the positive impact Ark: Survival Evolved has had on people.

It's somewhat hard to recommend this game. First, let's go over the good things about it, before I say what I don't like about it and why.
+Free to play done well. I can't say it's done completely right, but it is done very well. Part of this is what makes it hard for me to go back to the game, though. I'll explain later.
+Smooth as silk. The game runs really well and looks good (unless you're a graphics fanatic) on even low settings. The gunplay is good, melee is fun, and running around is a joy, particularly a they continue to update and refine the whole mechanics.
+A lore that keeps you digging. You'll get tidbits of the backstory and such through playing, and that certainly helps bring you back.
I could go on, but I'll spare the long essay. Really, you have no reason not to at least try it.
But, the biggest problems this game faces is actually one big problem that's a combination of a lot of things. Symptoms of a root disease, if you will.
It's free to play. In order for teh developers to make money, they have to have a cash shop of sorts. I'm not complaining about the shop itself. Almost everything is cosmetic. Or a quick qay to earn other things. Which is the biggest problem here.
Warframe is a grind. That's it. That's all this game has to offer. I've been gaming since I was a child. 20 years of gaming. And Warframe is the biggest grind of my life, thus far. A combination of limited game modes (Mostly PvE, haven't bothered a lot with PvP. The basic go kill the things, go get the thing, protect the thing(s), take the thing to the thing). To the developer's credit, they are adding new modes, and Archwing was a massive update that did a lot of good, but also piled more onto the big problem stack. It's still a grind. They don't seem to want to alleviate this. The PvE game modes all consist of doing basically the same thing with minor differentiations to the location and enemies. Taking a page from games like GTAV would be a perfect solution to this. Give the players more things to do than just shoot at everything, and don't make them wait for those extras from a Dojo.
And then, the dreaded RNG. Running the same, potentially challenging, level seven times for four seperate parts, and only managing to get two of them is discouraging. This is a major problem as you'll eventually either struggle through the enemies that get steadily tougher, or wipe the field every ten seconds with a push of a button. I'm not afraid of a challenge, but it gets stressful doing the same challenge for hours on end, or sitting in one spot mashing a button for hours on end, just hoping that maybe I'll get that thing I want.
But, once you do have those lovely parts, what do you do? You have to wait. Sometimes for a literal week for the item to craft. A real time week. It's a pain. Sure, you can spend that time grinding for other things, but if you're the type of player that doesn't like all the things, you're going to be frustrated.
Tl;dr: The game is a grind. It's very much a test of patience. But, it's also very fun at its core, and, at the very least, worth a try. Give it a go. It's free.

Warframe is shooter that envokes Sci-Fi and Elaberate Weapon and Frame Customization. No game can do better, when this beatiful-looking game is Free To Play.
Generally, one might think this is a Pay-To-Win game. More like Pay-To-Pimp. Warframe has a complexity of level designs and enemies. Ranging from Melee dependent Infested, to the wicked Corpus (Seriously, I hate those guys...) However, with their being so much content being locked away and put under "Pay to get" catagory, you can everything in the game (Other than some cosmetic items) by just putting your time, and [ingame] money into it. Don't get me wrong, I like Grindy, but when it's this Grindy? Oh god, does it ever feel good to compelete or craft that one thing you ever wanted since day 1.
Warframe does many things well; Beautiful Environments, unique weapons, unique missions and modifications, make this game a one-of-a-kind. For a free to play game? Nothing I can think of is better in the "Sci-Fi Shooter" Catagory.
With its amazing design, Warframe also comes with a very helpful guide, aswell as many, many players willing to help solve your biggest concerns, issues or lack of resources to craft that one weapon. The community is just fantastic.
Loot. Lots of it. Tons of it. THOUSANDS of Mod Cards, 100's of weapons, and many warframes. There is even those super-rare Prime Versions of certain frames and weapons, making you want to grind even more for that one thing to destory everything in your path.
There is tons of Co-Op, including 4 player missions, 6 man missions, and 8 player raids. Trading, customizing, modding, everything you want in an MMORPG, right here, in this free to play masterpiece.
However, WarFrame's story is lackluster, and left me wondering. Many things left uncovered. I had to go on the wiki to find some of the main story and lore behind WarFrames and eneimes. There are so bugs, like some guns reload bad, or don't shoot at the time you want them too... However, this does not hinder the game's overal beauty!
If you are looking for a very well designed, supportive, and grindy RPG, you've got one... SO what are you waiting for?

Warframe... more like Warfarm.
Not a good way to start off a review, but it gets like that after about mastery rank 6 or so. Warframe is freemium by nature, but pretty much anything except gifting someone can be collected through farming. Even though it's a glorious game, it can get a little grind heavy for those last few plastids.
When I say it's a glorious game, I mean GLORIOUS, not glorious. Killer graphics, smooth as butter gameplay, constant AND consistent updates, wide range of in-game customization both for gameplay and display, lots of fast-paced cut-em-up shoot-em-up action, and your very own spaceship. Your very own spaceship didn't used to be a thing, and since then the developers have given us dog-thing pets and a new "Upgrade-past-the-Max-Level" system that fits in well with the lore. Kinda feels tacked on while playing, but it's still kinda cool.
Freemium? Yes. Totally free to download, play, and get into? Yes. Pay-to-win? No, if you don't mind the grind. Addicting? Absolutely. Boring? Only after binging for a few hours. The missions can get redundant. New missions, modes of gameplay, and quests are being added about every month, though. Good Devs? Oh yes. All Hail The Red Text. These guys clearly care about the community and to be honest spoil us rotten with goodies, bugfixes, hotfixes, and updates. Digital Extremes is their name and Warframe is their flagship. It did NOT used to be this pretty, but now you get an essentially AAA title that's fun, replayable, and free(mium) that's only getting better.
There are still some bugs here and there, some optimization flaws for older computers. Most of the bugs I see nowadays lie in the Clan Dojo. I guess that not enough people are complaining about them to garner attention. Most of the updates for Dojos are limited to new researchable items and some new rooms these days. I can only hope that some bugfixes are on the way, particularly for the Arena.
Given the sucky nature of the starting gear, anyone coming into this should be ready to get their butts kicked for a while until they can build some better gear. If you're hurting for credits, head over to the recruiting channel and hope to get in on some Void runs.

This game is designed to lure you into its world and make you want to survive inside it. BUT... it requires a LOT of time to spend inside the game's world. If you dont plan on spending at least 6h per day for the next few months then don't even bother to start playing because you will fail. Additionaly it seems the developers are going to do anything to make more people play their game so the game is loosing its original style. In my opinion the game lacks the following things and has these weak sides:
- no ability to set up special shields for the time you are going to be offline (i know there are no offline raid servers but that is not it)
- no ability to build under the ground (building under the water is not the same as building under the ground)
- physics of buildings is very simple, almost non-existent (other than lift/elevator you can not make structures which move, ie. no chain bridges and the huge gates close themselves by pressing a button and not by using the force of your muscles or dinos etc.)
- there are automatic machine gun turrets, tek shields and teleporters but there are no simple electric fences or simple dynamic bridges
- it usually takes hours to tame a dino, it often takes a second to loose it, plenty of times because of some bug
- some items require lots of resources, a lot more than in real life
- some items break very fast because of usage, a lot faster than in real life
- you can not burn a wooden house, not even thatch
- the building blocks are huge, you place whole walls, whole pillars, you can not place single bricks and so the buildings are all the same and no surprises there
- the dinos look nice but they interact artificially with the surroundings
- the night is made by decreasing brightness of the screen and people overcome this by using gamma changing software, why dont they (developers) use dithered masking to at least partially fix (mitigate) this hack?

I'm glad I didn't review this in the earlier days of Warframe, because I wouldn't have reccomended it. But now, no doubt. I quit warframe sometime after I got a prime weapon and a couple prime frames due to it being so repetitive with no end game content available. Now they are adding endgame content, including end game dailies known as "sorties" that offer great rewards, raids, and augments in certain missions to add difficulty. It's what the game was missing. Not to mention they furthered the story with the Second Dream, which I will not spoil for anyone interested.
Here's the fault in Warframe as of now: The start.
Good lord starting out is awful, and it's the very reason most are driven away. Thankfully I had some friends ease me into the game, but without them I would have been lost and not knowing where to go. Your starter weapons are awful, so right when you level it to 30, toss it and invest either into a prime weapon or something in the dojo labs/store. Look up guides on how to start. Once you get past that, the game is infinitely better. Nothing is better than getting a new frame and messing around with it. There is a frame that will cater to EVERYONE'S playstyle, whether you want to go invisible, control the earth around you and summon golems, summon tentacles to aid in defense, place snowglobes to keep safe, freeze your enemies, magnetize them, or suck them into a vortex, it's there for you to choose. Some frames are easy to obtain, some are not, but it's always rewarding.
As for weapons, well... there is more than enough to choose from. Some don't scale well into late game (essentially 100+) but that doesn't necessarily mean you shouldn't use them. There's too much cool stuff in this game to not use, so try it out, but be sure to have something that works well in late game. Grinding them up isn't really exciting, but there is a good method to get it done it about an hour. Plenty of guides are available to aid you in building a formidable arsenal, just check youtube.
What's unique about this game is the mod system, where your weapon really means nothing, the mods do. Mods totally define how your weapon will perform, but they don't come easy. Ranking mods is expensive, finding them can be difficult, certain ones that is. Once you get them, you don't have to worry. If it becomes too difficult, you can always trade. There are weapon mods, companion mods, warframe mods, pvp mods, and ability mods (change how certain frames abilities function). I do know there are nearly 700 unique mods in the game, so if you want customization and options, there you go.
Modes: Survival, Escort, Spy, Defense, Mobile Defense, Interception (CTF), Sabatoge, Exterminate, Hive (Infested Unique), Rescue, Raid, Assasination (Boss Fights), Archwing (Space Flight/Combat)
Game is centered around cooperative play, each frame playing their part. Certain frames excel where others do not, so they all have their uses. Plenty of unique enemies with unique traits. Endgame area is the void where you can find the prime weapons/warframes. Plenty to do in this game, just have to deal with the grinding parts, as all RPGs tend to have nowadays.
Lastly, the building system in this game is probably either going to a be + or - for you. I like it, it extends the lifespan of the game. Frames take 3 days to build, weapons take 12-24 hours, end game materials (forma, reactor, catalysts) all take 24hrs, and so on. You have the option to rush it, but you have to pay the bought currency to do so.
This game is entirely free-to-play. You can earn platinum rather than buy it, something a lot of games lack at times. It's not too hard either.
Recap: Horrible start, but once you get past it, it's great. Grindy, but to be expected, normally quite rewarding. Has good endgame content, plenty of weapons and frames, customization is enormous. Really cool bossfights, some not so much. Great story, has a lot of lore you can read if you want. Every frame truly is unique, none are necessarily bad. Plenty to do in the game, lots of playtime and hours. Great coop play. Plenty of modes, cool puzzles at times, action packed gameplay. A lot of unique enemies. Entirely free to play, you never have to pay, everything can be earned. Cool parkour system since the revamp. Clans and dojos that are customizable. Events (Alerts, Sorties, Invasions, and Unique Limited Events).
Overall: 8/10 The new warframe is good, if it were the old warframe, not so good. Definitely worth a shot, just be prepared for an awful start.

Don't listen to all of the negative reviews... Does this game have paid DLC in early access? Yes. Is this game the best optimized game out there? No. So be it. The game is a lot of fun, and rather addicting.  My kids and I will play it most of the day on the weekends.  Don't let the low price tag fool you, though.  This is a very expensive game to play at the highest settings.  You'll need an SSD, but I recommend a RAID or M.2 NVME.  You'll need 16gb ram, but I recommend 32.  I'm usually pushing 10 GB or more on the server, and I've seen some people push 20.  You'll need 8gb vram, but I recommend 16 (yes, I know it doesn't exist in a graphics card, yet.)  It uses the entire gtx 1080 vram.  You'll need a quad-core i5 or i7, but I recommend overclocking them.  Oh, and with MODS, and I recommend MODS, you'll need a 250 GB drive - just for the game, the mods, and ARK SOTF.  I think I'm using about 170 GB right now.  You'll need another computer to host a server with similar specs, but not a graphics card, if you want to have something private.  And, that's for 1080p.  We could probably run higher resolution, but we only have 1080p monitors.  Keep in mind, that's four computers for our family.  We use 200 Mbps internet, but I recommend 1 Gbps with 50 Mbps upload.   It's worth it, though.  I'd buy it, again.  It's the best game I've ever played and my kids love playing it, but it's not cheap by any means.
With that said, if you turn the graphics down to medium, it looks OK and the play is still fun, so you can get by with a less powerful build.

Update: I'm changing this review from negative to positive. I managed to get this game to be stable using the following launch options: -useallavailablecores -d3d10 -nomansky
I'm running an AMD RX480 8G GPU.
Previous (negative) Review:
I will admit, the content is amazing and playstyle is amazing and they've updated the AI, but the core engine is still extremely buggy. There are a number of user workarounds, but none have worked for me. This is the only game in my library that hardlocks my PC.
The devs seem to be focused on more content and pushing DLC over fixing core bugs and issues.
Original Review (Early Access/Sorched Earth DLC):
I honestly wanted to like this game, as it was given to me by a friend. But I simply found it gave me a headache with the constant hardcore survival, player and dino levels that made no logical sense, limited progression without a tribe, and above all else, the poor attempts at minecraft-like creative aspects in an FPS engine. Granted, several mods make the creative side bearable, but the game and graphics core are so demanding, it taxes my 8-core, 32GB system -- all that for a game that looks like a polished, naked version of Unreal.
On top of the fact this has been in "Early Access" since June 2, 2015, and they released a cash DLC over a year later (September 1, 2016), without word when the game will be coming out of development stages, or when core stability would be fixed.
I will not recommend, nor support, any developer who conducts such marketing practices --- Finish your game FIRST!

I started on Sargon's Mesopotamia server with one goal, a noble goal, of getting sempai to notice me! Actually I just bought ARK on the summer sale, found out official servers are cancer, then noticed Sargon had a server and asked myself, "Just how much more cancerous could it be?"
I built a little thatch hut on south tropical island, and it was promptly annihilated by a charming young lady called Alicia on a dragon. Apparently she had claimed the entire island, one of the only 2 starting islands.
So I made a new hut on North Tropical Island, which was controlled by a tribe called ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore. They came down to play weaboo music at me and paint swastikas on my dinos but mostly left me alone.
A couple of days of harsh grinding later I was lvl 60 and had a pteranadon flying mount. I asked to join Babylon - Sargon's tribe, and he said no :(
Not just that but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore told me to get off their island now or they'll annihilate me. I flew off into the sunset and bumped into a lovely fellow called Sunderbraze who invited me to join Babylon
Sunderbraze had an awesome high tech ship made of metal with turrets, power generators and facilities for crafting explosives and guns. He also had a fridge. Sunderbraze became my new sempai!
I made a new ship out of stone right outside his ship. It looked absolutely amazing! It had a ram made of spikes!
While this was happening a little drama was going on. Dear Alicia had expelled all the people in her tribe because they stole one of her birds. All their dinos had switched allegiance to her and were attacking their former owners. They cried out for help and Sunderbraze answered, blowing a hole in the wall of her base, luring her dragon away and letting the poor former members escape. They formed a new tribe - Carthage, and came under attack by Alicia until Sunderbraze took her down.
♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore claimed she was their ally and demanded to know what happened. Alicia wouldn't stop whinging about that bird and promised doom and destruction. Rumour has it, some Babylon members had been offline raiding prior to this.
And then at 1:30am ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore attacked with dragons!
Sunderbraze's ship went down, the base was getting levelled and only 1 other person was online, who was a fresh recruit like me. I sailed away into the swamps as one gave chase, dropping grenades down upon me. Explosions tore through the hull of the Mary Celeste, crates exploding and my few worldly possessions lost to the bottom of the swamp. Even in the darkness I could not lose him, and after getting ensnared on some vines I was knocked unconscious by Yngling and carried away
My captor set me down briefly and started searching his dragon's inventory, but because I had put points into fortitude I woke up quite quickly. I immediately rushed forward into a pen full of raptors and started punching them. Before he knew what was happening I was dead, and quickly respawned in a hut near the swamps, crafted a raft, sailed to my half-wrecked ship and made my escape
The next day the dust settled and Babylon had been levelled. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore claimed they had only been searching for prisoners and never meant to cause total annihilation or to offline raid; even as they continued to destroy more of our bases and hunt us mercilessly. Our leader Sargon was captured and, according to rumours, forced to eat Yngling's poo. I flew further west into the deepest reaches of the map where I upgraded my ship, stockpiled supplies and waited...
The rest of the server was miffed with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s for their cowardly tactics and support of Alicia. A coalition was formed of the remaining tribes - Babylon, Carthage, DiGRA and Zulu. We gathered on the beach across from ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore. Massive armoured brontos with turrets on their backs, dragons, swarms of dimorphs and me with a stockpile of explosives and a bone to pick.
We swam across that lake and stormed the beach. In the confusion the war brontos moved ahead, one of which I was driving and were isolated from the rest of the group. Yngling laid into us on his wardragon, spewing fire and tearing into us. The turrets were malfunctioning so I began firing rockets down on him. I was caught in a blast of fire, my armour broke and my HP was reduced to 10%. Down on the beach the battle had turned against us, the enemy dragons had slain our own, no help was coming. My bronto fell and Yngling turned his dragon to attack the other injured bronto. I stood, blood covering my face, yelled into my mic "ALLAHU AHKBAR!" and fired my trusty rocket launcher.
Yngling was blown off his saddle and killed, his dragon flew away and I made my escape, parachuting down the cliff into the north tropical island's ravine, and swimming for safety. We lost 5 dragons and 2 war brontos, and countless dimorphs that day. Not everyone came back from ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore, and no one was the same.
The next 7 days were a long war between the Alliance and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s lost many dragons in failed assaults and their satellite bases were raided. In the end we mounted another assault. The only new addition was a stone wall lines with spikes and sign depicting masturbating anime cat girls and so, meeting no resistance, we implemented the Carthaginian solution and wiped them out for good.
10/10 would storm ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore again.
Also check out Vae Victis's youtube channel for the footage of the first and second battles of ♥♥♥♥ lord Shore!

Great game in the hands of a horible company. The 'Great Migration' was a perfect example of this. In a move to satisfy both the wipe and don't wipe crowds Wild Card decided to wipe 'some' servers upon launch. And a move I agree with. Now this is reasonable. However, they gave everyone only 5 days to do it. And oh wait, it gets better. In some game servers running special modes (primitive plus) they never turned on the ability to transfer! So two days into the 5 day transfer period to escape deletion they finally turn it on and we enter a mad rush to get our many tames and items and characters to the new server. On the 5th day Wild Card puts out a patch (never a smooth roll out) and breaks transfers. More than 24 hours BEFORE transfers close, the transfers close! And, in a true scumbag move Wildcard doesn't postpone deletion. Many characters who were going back and forth between servers to move items were now trapped along with many tames that were about to be uploaded on these doomed servers. Minutes turned into hours and finally the deadline came and many of our tribemates stood on obi transport pads with their tames and items hoping Wild Card would allow them to not be deleted. But it never happened. Thousands of hours of work gone. And the final insult. Never a word on this issue from the dev team despite hundreds of posts on the forums.
Don't get me wrong. The game is great. I will continue to play it. But I will probably never buy another product from WC. If you are thinking of buying this game, do so with one warning from me. Only proceed if you are okay with without warning having everything you worked for taken from you due to Wild Card for no good reason.

Super fun game with an incredibly involved team of developers that only gets better with time. 10/10.
EDIT 1/30/16: I'll expand on this. Graphically and aesthetically speaking, this game gets an A++. Awesome visuals, really hard to believe this is a f2p game. Gameplay and controls are smooth as butter, and warframes have incredible mobility. Everyone says this is basically a game about space ninjas, and they're right - you will feel like a total badass. Weapon selection is awesome, skins are awesome, warframes are awesome. Almost everything in the game can be acquired without spending real money (the only exception being Prime Access exclusives), since you can earn platinum (real life cash currency) by farming things and selling them to other players. Admittedly, it can be a bit of a grind to get certain parts and resources some time, but this game manages to steer well clear of the p2w trap that a lot of f2p games fall into. Anyway, A+ game, hard to go wrong with this one - just pick out a favorite warframe and have a blast.
