Asking for a Review....? *le sigh* if you insist... *tries not to quit and go back to playing the game...*
By that, I begin my Review of this:
This game has been out for YEARS now, and it is now 2016! This makes DESTINY look like the red-headed stepchild, beaten with an ugly stick, beaten with the no-story stick, beaten with the Lack-of-Content Stick, and overall, Destiny is just a black and blue mess with so much lost potential compared to this game! I wouldn't be surprised if they stole the Sword Melee Stance from this game to make their Sword playing, and their drop ship design!
that previous run-on paragraphic sentence shows how much I feel about Destiny and the difference this game makes me feel in how different they are! You've got DOZENS of ninjas to pick and choose from to vary your play-style, you've got a community that is both caustic and friendly. You'd got graphics and shiny flashes and beautiful effects that make the difference all the more between the two game "giants". Despite all the glitches, all the mishaps, WARFRAME just... FEELS like a constant Endgame, where Destiny... Where IS the storyline beyond killing THE TAKEN KING? In this you start off with VOR, and then you escalate to HUNHOW, and I just KNOW they're not going to let it drop with THAT.
Oh, and I think I just forgot the PLETHORA OF WEAPONS AND MODS. Sure, Destiny has a LOT of weapons, but... like Borderlands, which they stole the idea from, there're crap guns ALLLLLLLL over, and you want the best one you can find? Like the INFINITY PISTOL from Borderlands 2, Destiny has EXOTIC and LEGENDARY weapons, most of which are either crap, or beat out their Exotic counterparts even... In WARFRAME? You've got your regular guns, and then you have your PRIME variants, which are better, and take a lot more of a concentrated effort working with others to gather and build the weapons, and frames. The PRIME variants are few and not all-encompassing, much as many of them ARE endgame tools... Like Trinity Prime and Frost Prime. This doesn't completely make every other weapon "worthless", but adds to the content. The basic weaponry are the items you can buy the blueprints for, and build, and although several of them, like the Braton and the Strun, are SIMPLY exp fodder, they do make EXCELLENT starting weapons, which you CAN take into PVP and use to great effect. Now to talk about the MODS. Mods are cards you collect in missions, buy from the market, buy from other players, even get as rewards for doing great feats of agility, strenth, etc., which you can add to your WARFRAMES and weapons, and even your "companions" the Sentinals and Kubrow, THIS is what gives WARFRAME it's weapon customizations and upgrades. Compared to Borderlands or Destiny, you DON"T just toss away weapons when you're DONE with them, NO! You keep them, if you have bought the Inventory Weapon slots, Same for Warframes!
Now... for the PROS AND CONS of WARFRAME over BORDERLANDS and DESTINY....
Pros:
-FREE-TO-PLAY
-Data saved directly to Steam Cloud or DE's private server.
-Class and Gun changes, modifications
-Shinier than both Borderlands and Destiny
-CHOICES.
-Content will take you MONTHS to "finish" the game.
-Storyline makes you feel good about yourself.
-Gore Control(for when those pesky cousins annoy you to try playing out the game, or watch you play it...
-CLAN DOJOs are expansive and BEAUTIFUL, and decoratable.
-Weapons are NEVER made completely Obsolete(I am looking at you, Destiny! I want my fraggin Gjallerhorn Year 2!)
-PC population is astronomical
Cons:
-Micro-transactions out the wazzoo!
-Micro-transactions for opening up Frames and Weapons slots.
-Glitches can sometimes be lethal to your in-game character, throw you out of the level.
-RNG grind-fest, for when you desperately need that ONE FINAL BLUEPRINT to make your next Frame.
-RNG may cause player to constantly go back through a level OVER AND OVER AND OVER AGAIN.
-RNG is a jerk, usually...
-PVP is broken.
-Micro-transactions are expensive.
-Some items are ONLY available during certan parts of the day or only for some random events that ONLY last maybe 12 hours. RIP Orokin Catalysts and Reactors that we have all missed out on...
-RNG is sometimes almost as bad as Destiny's, sometimes just as good.
-HUGE download, make take as long as 8 hours to download depending on your Service provider.
-Controls can sometimes be wonky.
-Lotus/Ordis/Operator can sometimes be ANNOYING, or say the wrong thing.
-Console populations are very much nil. Separate from PC/steam Population
Now... is this game WORTH the HUNDREDS OF DAYS many people have put into the game? YES. I give it a 9/10 Ninja-shooter-EPIC. Can't really give an UNFINISHED game a 10/10!,and pvp is broken...
Hint hint: Destiny got a 3/10 when it came out, still gets only a 4/10 with Taken King

Overall, this is a great game to play with friends and family. As in any online multiplayer game there are pitfalls, but if you start well and on a good server you can have a great time!
In my opinion, the single most important choice you can make to affect the enjoyability of the game is to find the right server for you. Our first server was literally "ruled" by a tribe that was so scared of griefers coming in and ruining their world that they themselves became ruiners of other people's experience.
One thing they did was to place high level (metal) structures where "drops" would occur, so that people couldn't get the random boosts provided by the server. This greatly hampered low-level new players from growing without simply grinding their way upwards. They also blocked the obelisks which allow a character to travel from one sever to another. If you find these items blocked, stop playing that server and create a new character on another server.
Our current server is a "cluster" which allows us to travel among a group of servers so that we can experience each map/world with the same character.
If you find yourself having a bad experience, especially on a PVP server, stop playing that server and find another one.
On any server, it's going to be a challenge to survive. You'll find being in a tribe can be helpful, and there are nice people around who will help you, but it's still pretty hard - especially on the Scorched Earth servers. ...but that's the cool thing about this game. It's a real challenge with a hard environment and there are real people to deal with.
Very cool game.

Update: I'm changing this review from negative to positive. I managed to get this game to be stable using the following launch options: -useallavailablecores -d3d10 -nomansky

Previous (negative) Review:
I will admit, the content is amazing and playstyle is amazing and they've updated the AI, but the core engine is still extremely buggy. There are a number of user workarounds, but none have worked for me. This is the only game in my library that hardlocks my PC.
The devs seem to be focused on more content and pushing DLC over fixing core bugs and issues.
Original Review (Early Access/Sorched Earth DLC):
I honestly wanted to like this game, as it was given to me by a friend. But I simply found it gave me a headache with the constant hardcore survival, player and dino levels that made no logical sense, limited progression without a tribe, and above all else, the poor attempts at minecraft-like creative aspects in an FPS engine. Granted, several mods make the creative side bearable, but the game and graphics core are so demanding, it taxes my 8-core, 32GB system -- all that for a game that looks like a polished, naked version of Unreal.
On top of the fact this has been in "Early Access" since June 2, 2015, and they released a cash DLC over a year later (September 1, 2016), without word when the game will be coming out of development stages, or when core stability would be fixed.
I will not recommend, nor support, any developer who conducts such marketing practices --- Finish your game FIRST!

The Bird that Launched a Thousand Dragons.
I started on Sargon's Mesopotamia server with one goal, a noble goal, of getting sempai to notice me! Actually I just bought ARK on the summer sale, found out official servers are cancer, then noticed Sargon had a server and asked myself, "Just how much more cancerous could it be?"
I built a little thatch hut on south tropical island, and it was promptly annihilated by a charming young lady called Alicia on a dragon. Apparently she had claimed the entire island, one of the only 2 starting islands.
So I made a new hut on North Tropical Island, which was controlled by a tribe called ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore. They came down to play weaboo music at me and paint swastikas on my dinos but mostly left me alone.
A couple of days of harsh grinding later I was lvl 60 and had a pteranadon flying mount. I asked to join Babylon - Sargon's tribe, and he said no :(
Not just that but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore told me to get off their island now or they'll annihilate me. I flew off into the sunset and bumped into a lovely fellow called Sunderbraze who invited me to join Babylon
Sunderbraze had an awesome high tech ship made of metal with turrets, power generators and facilities for crafting explosives and guns. He also had a fridge. Sunderbraze became my new sempai!
I made a new ship out of stone right outside his ship. It looked absolutely amazing! It had a ram made of spikes!
While this was happening a little drama was going on. Dear Alicia had expelled all the people in her tribe because they stole one of her birds. All their dinos had switched allegiance to her and were attacking their former owners. They cried out for help and Sunderbraze answered, blowing a hole in the wall of her base, luring her dragon away and letting the poor former members escape. They formed a new tribe - Carthage, and came under attack by Alicia until Sunderbraze took her down.
♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore claimed she was their ally and demanded to know what happened. Alicia wouldn't stop whinging about that bird and promised doom and destruction. Rumour has it, some Babylon members had been offline raiding prior to this.
And then at 1:30am ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore attacked with dragons!
Sunderbraze's ship went down, the base was getting levelled and only 1 other person was online, who was a fresh recruit like me. I sailed away into the swamps as one gave chase, dropping grenades down upon me. Explosions tore through the hull of the Mary Celeste, crates exploding and my few worldly possessions lost to the bottom of the swamp. Even in the darkness I could not lose him, and after getting ensnared on some vines I was knocked unconscious by Yngling and carried away
My captor set me down briefly and started searching his dragon's inventory, but because I had put points into fortitude I woke up quite quickly. I immediately rushed forward into a pen full of raptors and started punching them. Before he knew what was happening I was dead, and quickly respawned in a hut near the swamps, crafted a raft, sailed to my half-wrecked ship and made my escape
The next day the dust settled and Babylon had been levelled. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore claimed they had only been searching for prisoners and never meant to cause total annihilation or to offline raid; even as they continued to destroy more of our bases and hunt us mercilessly. Our leader Sargon was captured and, according to rumours, forced to eat Yngling's poo. I flew further west into the deepest reaches of the map where I upgraded my ship, stockpiled supplies and waited...
The rest of the server was miffed with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s for their cowardly tactics and support of Alicia. A coalition was formed of the remaining tribes - Babylon, Carthage, DiGRA and Zulu. We gathered on the beach across from ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore. Massive armoured brontos with turrets on their backs, dragons, swarms of dimorphs and me with a stockpile of explosives and a bone to pick.
We swam across that lake and stormed the beach. In the confusion the war brontos moved ahead, one of which I was driving and were isolated from the rest of the group. Yngling laid into us on his wardragon, spewing fire and tearing into us. The turrets were malfunctioning so I began firing rockets down on him. I was caught in a blast of fire, my armour broke and my HP was reduced to 10%. Down on the beach the battle had turned against us, the enemy dragons had slain our own, no help was coming. My bronto fell and Yngling turned his dragon to attack the other injured bronto. I stood, blood covering my face, yelled into my mic "ALLAHU AHKBAR!" and fired my trusty rocket launcher.
Yngling was blown off his saddle and killed, his dragon flew away and I made my escape, parachuting down the cliff into the north tropical island's ravine, and swimming for safety. We lost 5 dragons and 2 war brontos, and countless dimorphs that day. Not everyone came back from ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore, and no one was the same.
The next 7 days were a long war between the Alliance and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s lost many dragons in failed assaults and their satellite bases were raided. In the end we mounted another assault. The only new addition was a stone wall lines with spikes and sign depicting masturbating anime cat girls and so, meeting no resistance, we implemented the Carthaginian solution and wiped them out for good.
10/10 would storm ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shore again.
Also check out Vae Victis's youtube channel for the footage of the first and second battles of ♥♥♥♥ lord Shore!

In a move to satisfy both the wipe and don't wipe crowds Wild Card decided to wipe 'some' servers upon launch. And a move I agree with. Now this is reasonable. However, they gave everyone only 5 days to do it. And oh wait, it gets better. In some game servers running special modes (primitive plus) they never turned on the ability to transfer! So two days into the 5 day transfer period to escape deletion they finally turn it on and we enter a mad rush to get our many tames and items and characters to the new server. On the 5th day Wild Card puts out a patch (never a smooth roll out) and breaks transfers. More than 24 hours BEFORE transfers close, the transfers close! And, in a true scumbag move Wildcard doesn't postpone deletion. Many characters who were going back and forth between servers to move items were now trapped along with many tames that were about to be uploaded on these doomed servers. Minutes turned into hours and finally the deadline came and many of our tribemates stood on obi transport pads with their tames and items hoping Wild Card would allow them to not be deleted. But it never happened. Thousands of hours of work gone. And the final insult. Never a word on this issue from the dev team despite hundreds of posts on the forums.
Don't get me wrong. The game is great. I will continue to play it. But I will probably never buy another product from WC. If you are thinking of buying this game, do so with one warning from me. Only proceed if you are okay with without warning having everything you worked for taken from you due to Wild Card for no good reason.

Ive played this game for quite a bit and i wanted to make an almost full review for it on my opinions.
So lets Start :)
Pros:
-This game has nice graphics and runs with ease on almost any computer
-All the warframes give out an almost completely different style of gameplay and freedom to choose what to play
-Levels are big and spacious most of the time allowing for more use of environment using the acrobatics
-Many different weapons to choose from that allow for more customizability in the game
-You can customize your Warframe and guns with almost any colors you want (more in cons) Also there are accesories that you can pick for your warframe and even battle regalias
-Mod cards allow the player to customize their gun's and warframe's playstyle in the folowing ways , you can choose to build your warframe with more overal hp or lower hp and more shield ,and maybe and an energy increase, how about making him more stealthy with some silencing mods for your guns , or even go crazy with increase  in fire rate and ammo capacity
-Thats all i can think of at the moment for the pros
Cons:
-Warframes take a ridiculous amount of time to build, its around 12 hours to build the parts and 72 (i think) to make the overall warframe and even guns and melee weapons need around 12 hours to construct , thank god you can construct many things at once or i would still be building my first warframe :(
-Maybe its just me but sometimes when i alt-tab the game needs around a minute to load when i try to go back
-Sometimes you see the same rooms over and over again in some missions and you can see the same room copied twice or even three times in a single mission wich kinda makes the level quality lack in variance
-The game forces you to get a clan that has inside its clan dojo a Tenno Lab i think its called which is needed to construct certain warframes and weapons which in my oppinion sucks for players that dont really socialize in games and just want to play the game alone
-Also the game doesnt give you all the colors to be able to customize your warframe , you need to play to unlock most of them
Overall:
The game has some bad features (like bad construction time for the warframes) and many good features (like good customizability overall) and in my oppinion its deffinently worth a shot by anyone that likes mmos with a bit of futuristic style into them , I play this game with my friends and we have alot of fun doing the alerts and farming bosses.
That is all for this review , Hopefully it was helpfull :)

Warframe. I spent 1000 hours on that game. Never played a game so much in my life. And guess what. I had fun in it. Plenty. The actual gameplay isn't even bad.
But the game is flawed.
1) Welcome to grindland.
It's basicaly a huuuuge grind. Everything can be either bought with money or grinded, but buying in-game items with real cash is out of the question because of the ridiculously high "platinum" prices.
But hey, who wants to pay to get stuff anyway right? Go out there and farm that orokin golden bling bling gear, mighty space ninja!
As much as  I like the fact this is a TRUE free to play, I just can't stand game where the sole sense of achievement you get from playing it is about your possessions. In fact, the entire rank of your account is based on how many different weapons you own. Doesn't that give you a slight hint on how much of a grinding simulator this is?
2) "Balance? what is that lawlzors"
I started playing at update 8. That was almost 3 years ago.
At times, some weapons were already better than others, but not by that much (eg. Boltor). You could run any set of gear and still enjoy all the different playstyles they provide. but as the game progressed over the years, it was crippled by some MAJOR powercreeping. To this day, those weapons I played with at update 8 are completely useless. Some of them had slight buffs, but are still absolute trash (see Lanka for instance). Basicaly all the "top gear" that all those high level players use are either  a new weapon that's blatantly overpowered (Just think of the Soma when it came out) or a prime variant of it, which is basicaly a better, shinier version of a gun, that sometimes is already too strong, because the devs have zero knowledge in how to balance the game (Soma prime?! What a good idea!).
What this means is that to run harder missions, the best choice of gear will always be that one new weapon that's just stronger than the rest, not that cool polearm you loved so much, simply because it's being outclassed by that one new melee weapon that just came out, or whatever else is considered the best weapon at times. This restricts a ton of different playstyles from being anything near viable. Want to play a Sniper zephyr with glaive with the Vectis's unique playstyle? Well sorry, but the glaive is old, thus underpowered, and a new sniper just came out which is better than the vectis by a long shot. Yeah, I had that happen to me.
It's just a race to aquire the strongest weapons, which are then replaced when a new patch brings out something better. Meanwhile older but sometimes more fun gear are left in the closet accumulating dust due to their innefectiveness. Playstyle diversity is a joke is this game. Even the many different classes have only one, 2 rarely, viable build for the late game.
-=Conclusion=-
The reason why I can't recommend this game is probably because I grew up, and started to dislike games centered about grinding and possessions. Yeah, Warframe's gameplay is good, but you'll never jump into a mission telling yourself "I'm here to have a nice game" , but instead thinking "I'm here to get X item". Some of my friends enjoy these types of game, so if that's your thing, go ahead and jump in. But to anyone reading this who doesn't feel like grinding the life out of yourself while using the same broken gear in every mission, feel free to pass.

Came back to WF after U18 hit after dropping it for nearly a year. The lore they dropped in this update was amazing. Definitely explained a lot of what's been going on. Plus the sorties have been a lot of fun, finally got some more content for high level players to have fun with.
For those that haven't played Warframe... You're a magic space ninja. Four player coop. You get your own space ship. There's a super confusing (at first) mod system. Really good traversal system. Hundreds of weapons to build and buy. Pretty decent variety of mission types. They'll say that stealth and sniping is better... it's still not good. This game is all about brutal in your face wrecking enemies. They've reworked a few bosses to be truly entertaining.
And it's grindy. Really grindy. When I started I had a few friends I played with, and it made the whole experience vastly more enjoyable. They quit playing, I kept going. Highly recommend playing with friends.
Also, the free to play model is good. You can earn everything by playing the game, including Platinum (the paid currency) by trading mod cards and parts you get from running missions.

A very ambitious game with promising survival-themed character development that has apparently no good community, no questlines, and a VERY DIFFICULT TO RENDER environment.
This last detail —how difficult it is to run the graphics properly —is what forced me to refund... I've seen many other different games with way better graphics that can run smoothly on my PC (WoW, Bioshock: Infinite, Civilization 5, Civilization 6, AION). I suspect there's a (heavy) problem with coding graphics at ARK: my framerate was choppy and sometimes froze alltogether, despite the 24GB RAM.
Another thing that bothered me is that unless you don't find a tribe that doesn't backstab you and/or unless you cannot play like 4 hours of the game in a single sitting, all of your progress might get lost. It takes about 2-3h per sitting to start actually accessing the most of the game's true content; i.e. getting a single dinosaur, which I couldn't. All I got to do was talking to a guy that didn't really want to show me the ropes, and opening his storage out of curiosity, at which moment I was mercilessly murdered, lol.
I'd love to advise the developers to take this as feedback to improve the game. I really love dinos, I love their initiative,  and I love where the game is going EXCEPT for these details; namely, inexplicably horrible framerates, bad community and/or difficult socialization, no quests, and no way to progress unless you can sit to play many hours straight.
Don't see why people are complaining so much, I haven't experienced any hackers and enjoyed the game.

For those of you who do not want to read much: This is one of the most fantastic free to play games I have ever experienced. But beware of the grind. That is all.
If you want to get a more thorough review, then read on.
As you should know by now, this game is free to play, yet unlike a lot of free to play games, there is no premium content locked to all but the wealthy. Every item in game can be farmed for, except for cosmetics, which are bought with premium currency, but even those cosmetics can be obtained without paying a cent. The trading system allows players to sell certain upper-tier weapons/weapon parts to other players for that premium currency, and these items can be obtained just by playing.
The gameplay is also incredibly well done. Combat is fast-paced and dynamic, and the variety of enemies and locations make for an incredibly rewarding experience. There is solid gunplay, one of the best parkour and movement systems that I have ever seen in any game, underwater combat, space combat, and fleshed out melee combat system that flows smoothly with other aspects of gameplay.
The variety in this game is ridiculous. For starters, there are 28 classes, with more added every couple of months, and almost 200 different weapons, all divided into different categories, such as rifles, bows, longswords, shotguns, whips, claws, hammers etc. There is always some new weapon you haven't tried yet.
The community is fantastic. There is very little toxicity among the players and people treat each other like human beings for the most part. The one thing you should watch out for is the official forums. That's where the salty loud minority of players are. If you are looking for people to talk to in-game, just find a good clan to be with. Avoid the forums altogether.
Most of the story in the game is told in a dark-souls manner, through pieces of writing throughout the game. A lot of the things we "know" about the game are merely speculations or theories that we have concocted based on what we actually know. This has led to a lot of people saying that Warframe has no story at all. Rest assured, this is not true, as several recent story Quests have provided us with a convoluted plot-twist ridden story that makes our heads hurt. I'm not going to give any details, because spoilers. Find out for yourself.
I think that's all I have to say about this game, other than go play it for yourself. It's free. What do you have to lose?

Ive played this game for quite a bit and i wanted to make an almost full review for it on my opinions.
So lets Start :)
Pros:
-This game has nice graphics and runs with ease on almost any computer
-All the warframes give out an almost completely different style of gameplay and freedom to choose what to play
-Levels are big and spacious most of the time allowing for more use of environment using the acrobatics
-Many different weapons to choose from that allow for more customizability in the game
-You can customize your Warframe and guns with almost any colors you want (more in cons) Also there are accesories that you can pick for your warframe and even battle regalias
-Mod cards allow the player to customize their gun's and warframe's playstyle in the folowing ways , you can choose to build your warframe with more overal hp or lower hp and more shield ,and maybe and an energy increase, how about making him more stealthy with some silencing mods for your guns , or even go crazy with increase  in fire rate and ammo capacity
-Thats all i can think of at the moment for the pros
Cons:
-Warframes take a ridiculous amount of time to build, its around 12 hours to build the parts and 72 (i think) to make the overall warframe and even guns and melee weapons need around 12 hours to construct , thank god you can construct many things at once or i would still be building my first warframe :(
-Maybe its just me but sometimes when i alt-tab the game needs around a minute to load when i try to go back
-Sometimes you see the same rooms over and over again in some missions and you can see the same room copied twice or even three times in a single mission wich kinda makes the level quality lack in variance
-The game forces you to get a clan that has inside its clan dojo a Tenno Lab i think its called which is needed to construct certain warframes and weapons which in my oppinion sucks for players that dont really socialize in games and just want to play the game alone
-Also the game doesnt give you all the colors to be able to customize your warframe , you need to play to unlock most of them
Overall:
The game has some bad features (like bad construction time for the warframes) and many good features (like good customizability overall) and in my oppinion its deffinently worth a shot by anyone that likes mmos with a bit of futuristic style into them , I play this game with my friends and we have alot of fun doing the alerts and farming bosses.
That is all for this review , Hopefully it was helpfull :)

So I've been wanting to write a review for this game for a while now. I've been playing this game since the start of Open Beta and I myself am a founder (sadly I don't have Excalibur Prime). This game has come a long way and instead of getting worse it's getting better as times goes on as games should, but sadly a lot of games don't I.E. League of Legends but that's besides the point I still have hope for League.
Warframe itself has had many ups and downs and still has some balancing issues (BLUE OSPREYS NEED NERF!!!!! & Forma BP Drops in a 60 min T4 survival tyvm......) but that is beside the point. The Story for this game was lacking in the beginning and they ended up reworking a lot of the story they did have on multiple occassions, but that was to be expected (It was Beta after all). But now they have finally started to develop the story more with the Second Dream questline and all. This questline fits in so many different peices of the puzzle that is Warframe. And if you're not the type of person to care about the story it's ok cause the combat is still pretty good.
The Combat for this game is amazing in the sense that you have freedom to do anything you want (Parkour Heaven). You can play this game in any style that suits you. If you want to be stealthy you can and it's not just limited to a single frame (that's what you call the different suits that you wear to battle) though certain frames are better for certain situations I.E. Frost with his snowglobe (which is like a force feild that slows enemies that are in it and blocks projectiles from getting into it) which is great for defence missions and a pretty much must if you want to get into higher level defence missions. There are a huge number of frames and they are still adding more! With such a wide range of frames and weapons to choose from you can do whatever you want. You can be a tank and still be able to deal the most damage based on your weapons. There are no weapons that are "class" specific, because there are no classes each frame is different and sure they some are ment for a certain play style, but if you have good Parkour skills and good weapons you can solo any mission granted it is easier to play with others.
EVERY frame (Excalibur Prime is an Exception this frame was limited to Founders of the game I think they were Third Teir and Higher? I forget) is farmable. Though you can get most frames from the cash shop, but wait you can earn Plat (the Cash shop currency) IN GAME!!!! Through Trading!!! This is one of the best features of the game. But this requires heavy farming, if your not up to farming then I recommend you try out this game until your at least MR 4. Because by then you will have a pretty good idea about the game and how everything works.
MR is your own level think of it like prestiging. You can only use certain weapons at certain MR ranks and certain questlines are locked until you hit the minimum MR requirement. You can gain exp for your MR by leveling up your frames and weapons, but once you max your weapons and frames you won't be able to gain more MR experience from those weapons or frames even if you delete them and rebuild them or Forma them (you won't have to worry about formaing your stuff until mid/late game).
Remember how I was saying you could earn plat? how you ask? well it's relatively simple all you have to do is do void missions and farm for Prime Parts and then trade them with real people for plat and then use that plat to buy yourself a cool color scheme and some new slots for your warframes and weapons. (I'm a horder I like to horde everything I build though my plat can rarely keep up T_T). Void keys are a really easy farm to just do defence missions and you can get some nice drops of void keys.
The support for this game is phenominal. The DE's actually listen to the players and they take to consideration everything that the players say. If we want more story they give us more story (Second Dream). If we want more frames they give us more frames!! If we want better Combat they give us better combat (Melle 2.0 and Parkour 2,0). They are a prime example of how game develepors should act. They even do frequent live streams where they give plat to lucky players that get picked by RNGesus.
This is seeming more like a beginners guide to warframe then a review, but I feel that this should be known. So to wrap it all up I HIGHLY recommend Warframe. Though farming does get annoying at times... (RNGesus please take pity on me T_T)

Warframe. I spent 1000 hours on that game. Never played a game so much in my life. And guess what. I had fun in it. Plenty. The actual gameplay isn't even bad.
But the game is flawed.
1) Welcome to grindland.
It's basicaly a huuuuge grind. Everything can be either bought with money or grinded, but buying in-game items with real cash is out of the question because of the ridiculously high "platinum" prices.
But hey, who wants to pay to get stuff anyway right? Go out there and farm that orokin golden bling bling gear, mighty space ninja!
As much as  I like the fact this is a TRUE free to play, I just can't stand game where the sole sense of achievement you get from playing it is about your possessions. In fact, the entire rank of your account is based on how many different weapons you own. Doesn't that give you a slight hint on how much of a grinding simulator this is?
2) "Balance? what is that lawlzors"
I started playing at update 8. That was almost 3 years ago.
At times, some weapons were already better than others, but not by that much (eg. Boltor). You could run any set of gear and still enjoy all the different playstyles they provide. but as the game progressed over the years, it was crippled by some MAJOR powercreeping. To this day, those weapons I played with at update 8 are completely useless. Some of them had slight buffs, but are still absolute trash (see Lanka for instance). Basicaly all the "top gear" that all those high level players use are either  a new weapon that's blatantly overpowered (Just think of the Soma when it came out) or a prime variant of it, which is basicaly a better, shinier version of a gun, that sometimes is already too strong, because the devs have zero knowledge in how to balance the game (Soma prime?! What a good idea!).
What this means is that to run harder missions, the best choice of gear will always be that one new weapon that's just stronger than the rest, not that cool polearm you loved so much, simply because it's being outclassed by that one new melee weapon that just came out, or whatever else is considered the best weapon at times. This restricts a ton of different playstyles from being anything near viable. Want to play a Sniper zephyr with glaive with the Vectis's unique playstyle? Well sorry, but the glaive is old, thus underpowered, and a new sniper just came out which is better than the vectis by a long shot. Yeah, I had that happen to me.
It's just a race to aquire the strongest weapons, which are then replaced when a new patch brings out something better. Meanwhile older but sometimes more fun gear are left in the closet accumulating dust due to their innefectiveness. Playstyle diversity is a joke is this game. Even the many different classes have only one, 2 rarely, viable build for the late game.
-=Conclusion=-
The reason why I can't recommend this game is probably because I grew up, and started to dislike games centered about grinding and possessions. Yeah, Warframe's gameplay is good, but you'll never jump into a mission telling yourself "I'm here to have a nice game" , but instead thinking "I'm here to get X item". Some of my friends enjoy these types of game, so if that's your thing, go ahead and jump in. But to anyone reading this who doesn't feel like grinding the life out of yourself while using the same broken gear in every mission, feel free to pass.

I've been playing this game as of about April 2013, a Founder I am.  There are a few things that I didn't like about the game, back then there were a few things that felt a little out of place with the movement, as well as just a few general gameplay problems, and occasional bugs.  However, coming on nearly 3 years, still playing the game, and many hours, weeks, months, and the past couple years poured into the game, it's come a long way, and still more to come.
The developer, Digital Extremes (DE), is very kind, and a group of quite entertaining (funny and otherwise), people, to anyone that watches their streams every other week, of course, depending on the stream, every week.
Things that I don't like about the game:
-Many of the tile sets feel a little predictable.
-It can be fairly easy to get burnt out, if played too much.
Things that I like about the game:
-A variety of classes, or Warframes
-Variety of weapons to choose from.
-Variety of companions.
-More colors, and minor customizasions than nessecary (but totally worth all of them).
-Diverse mission types, and rewards.
-Each Frame behaves differently than another, close in role, but different.
-Navigational "Star Map" is well designed (to be changed at some point).
-Cinamatic story piece (only one, but word is that there's more to come).
...And quite a lot more.
By no means is it a game for everyone, and the movement style can be difficult to grasp (kind of), but once you have it down, it's really easy to get around, and I find myself often wondering what the map limitations are, and for the most part, I've found that, if you can see it, it's possible to get to it, but a bit of thought is required to get to that point (sometimes, and dependant on what Frame you're on).

I want to like this game.  I really do.  But it has a ton of issues that I'm not sure will ever be addressed.  The devs seem to be focusing on constantly adding new dinos or various craftables.  Normally you'd think great!, but honestly the Island is already overcrowded as it is and I'd say it's beyond time to focus on polishing the hell out of what you have.
+ Tons of prehistoric creatures, a lot of them adjusted slightly to make them more unique and fun, most of them trying to eat you!
+A pretty solid set of features.  There's painting, raising from eggs, taming, lots of crafting, and son on.
+Again, taming a freaking dinosaur and than crafting a saddle to ride on it.  This is cool as hell the first few times.
+Looks great.  Although you I'd suggest using the "-USEALLAVAILABLECORES -sm4 -d3d10 -nomansky -lowmemory -novsync" launch option.  For a minor dip in graphics the game becomes playable.
+Multiplayer.  You can even invite friends into your local game, you are just tethered X distance from each other.  I played with a 1.2km and it was pretty fun.  Just whatever you do don't play on official servers.  I mean unless you like joining a server with huge alpha tribes that control everything and typically destroy everything they see that isn't theirs.
-The game is grindy.  I mean really grindy.  Every crafting recipe has inflated requirements, taming is a huge bore where you sit and stare at the creature for ages while waiting for a bar to fill, and so on.  I typcially play on my own local server and have crazy inflated values and I STILL say this.  For example, most of the time you harvest 5-10 wood from a tree if I remember right.  A single wooden wall that is barely taller than the player requires 40 of these in addition to some thatch and fiber.  Usually most people end up making their walls 2 high at least otherwise it's pretty tiny feeling inside, so 80.  That needs a foundation to be placed on, which is another 80 pieces of wood.  And finally a ceiling is 60 wood.  Now multiply that by how big you want your house to be, and realize you should ideally have a large fence around it as well otherwise dinos can break through your houses walls easily.  And this is only the second crafting tier of materials.
-No real creature AI yet.  Been promised almost a year now, but I expect it will never get added.  Creatures don't sleep.  They don't actually travel in a pack/herd, they just kind of wander next to each other after spawning that way.  They don't have routines where they get water or hunt for food.  Carnivores attack anything they consider a valid target until they themselves die of cumulative damage recieved.  Several species are designed to ONLY target players on sight, they ignore other creatures unless it hits them first.  Basically don't be expecting a game where you can stalk your prey and have grand hunting trips while being imersed in the world.
-The game is pretty horribly optimized.  It's far better than it was, and they are making improvements all the time, but damn does it run bad unless you tweak the heck out of your settings or use some launch options.  Do not play this with a low-medium rig.
-You can only build structures at right angles.  No curved walls, no diagonal walls.  Makes everything look boxy.  This is just a minor complaint.
-The engram system.  While this was a great idea initially, I think it needs scrapped or streamlined pretty bad.  Having 1 friend pick up most of the builder engrams means they will level one hell of a lot faster than you.  And since everything has prerequisites, you have to get all of them as well if you want to build something yourself later on.  And a lot of engrams are split into their own pointless ones.  I mean a chair is it's own engram?  Slopping roof left and slopping roof right are separate extra engrams?

The game completely lacks basic tutorials, too: I had to learn the ins and outs of fusing mods, mods being a means just as important to customization as Warframes and weapons, from a YouTube video. It's also unclear how different elemental type simpact different enemy types without looking it up outside of the game, etc.
People who invest in the game often really love it, but I wanted to put my experience down here: if you want to just try it for a bit and see how you like it before dedicating, you might not get a very good experience.

ARK is a great game about building bases, taming creatures, and making friends(or enemies). It has a large variety of creatures not limited only to dinosaurs, and has prehistoric/extinct animals such as the Argentavis, Titanboa, Mammoths, and lots more. Each of the creatures have uniqueness in them, from creatures that can aid in farming materials, hunting/taming more creatures, and razing villages of other people. The environment is also great, the landscapes are breathtaking, and the maps are huge. If content is what you seek, this game definitely has it.
The gameplay is fun. Early in the game is where it's hardest. You die a lot, you rage a lot, but after you have built a proper base, everything will be fine. It would be great if you find friends in the server and build together with them to make the game easier, in-terms of survival.
Official servers are really slow, like harvesting materials are quite a hassle, but can give tons of entertainment. If a slow game is not what you want, then you can play the game in Unofficial servers, which have multipliers in them to make things go faster. This game requires a lot of your time.
The bad things about ARK mostly stated from previous reviews are true, however. If you play in old servers, chances are there are 1 or 2 "Alpha" tribes playing there. If those tribes are small-minded people, it's better to move to another server. There are Alpha tribes who block important resource points, such as metal quarries or pearl areas, making progress impossible unless you make them your allies. These tribes can also destroy bases that took hundreds of hours to build in a matter of minutes. But that does not mean all of them are bad. There are also Alpha tribes in some servers that actually help newbies.
All-in-all, this is a great game which makes you want to play this game again and again. Definitely worth for its price.

So I've been wanting to write a review for this game for a while now. I've been playing this game since the start of Open Beta and I myself am a founder (sadly I don't have Excalibur Prime). This game has come a long way and instead of getting worse it's getting better as times goes on as games should, but sadly a lot of games don't I.E. League of Legends but that's besides the point I still have hope for League.
Warframe itself has had many ups and downs and still has some balancing issues (BLUE OSPREYS NEED NERF!!!!! & Forma BP Drops in a 60 min T4 survival tyvm......) but that is beside the point. The Story for this game was lacking in the beginning and they ended up reworking a lot of the story they did have on multiple occassions, but that was to be expected (It was Beta after all). But now they have finally started to develop the story more with the Second Dream questline and all. This questline fits in so many different peices of the puzzle that is Warframe. And if you're not the type of person to care about the story it's ok cause the combat is still pretty good.
The Combat for this game is amazing in the sense that you have freedom to do anything you want (Parkour Heaven). You can play this game in any style that suits you. If you want to be stealthy you can and it's not just limited to a single frame (that's what you call the different suits that you wear to battle) though certain frames are better for certain situations I.E. Frost with his snowglobe (which is like a force feild that slows enemies that are in it and blocks projectiles from getting into it) which is great for defence missions and a pretty much must if you want to get into higher level defence missions. There are a huge number of frames and they are still adding more! With such a wide range of frames and weapons to choose from you can do whatever you want. You can be a tank and still be able to deal the most damage based on your weapons. There are no weapons that are "class" specific, because there are no classes each frame is different and sure they some are ment for a certain play style, but if you have good Parkour skills and good weapons you can solo any mission granted it is easier to play with others.
EVERY frame (Excalibur Prime is an Exception this frame was limited to Founders of the game I think they were Third Teir and Higher? I forget) is farmable. Though you can get most frames from the cash shop, but wait you can earn Plat (the Cash shop currency) IN GAME!!!! Through Trading!!! This is one of the best features of the game. But this requires heavy farming, if your not up to farming then I recommend you try out this game until your at least MR 4. Because by then you will have a pretty good idea about the game and how everything works.
MR is your own level think of it like prestiging. You can only use certain weapons at certain MR ranks and certain questlines are locked until you hit the minimum MR requirement. You can gain exp for your MR by leveling up your frames and weapons, but once you max your weapons and frames you won't be able to gain more MR experience from those weapons or frames even if you delete them and rebuild them or Forma them (you won't have to worry about formaing your stuff until mid/late game).
Remember how I was saying you could earn plat? how you ask? well it's relatively simple all you have to do is do void missions and farm for Prime Parts and then trade them with real people for plat and then use that plat to buy yourself a cool color scheme and some new slots for your warframes and weapons. (I'm a horder I like to horde everything I build though my plat can rarely keep up T_T). Void keys are a really easy farm to just do defence missions and you can get some nice drops of void keys.
The support for this game is phenominal. The DE's actually listen to the players and they take to consideration everything that the players say. If we want more story they give us more story (Second Dream). If we want more frames they give us more frames!! If we want better Combat they give us better combat (Melle 2.0 and Parkour 2,0). They are a prime example of how game develepors should act. They even do frequent live streams where they give plat to lucky players that get picked by RNGesus.
This is seeming more like a beginners guide to warframe then a review, but I feel that this should be known. So to wrap it all up I HIGHLY recommend Warframe. Though farming does get annoying at times... (RNGesus please take pity on me T_T)

- the warframes (the characters you control) have all their own unique abilities which make every one fun to play with
- players there are nice and no 13-year-old flamer kiddies
The disadvantages are just disadvantages if you intend to play it more often than as a casual game.

Basically a Third Person Shooter co-op RPG with a very original and fun to use level-up system. It used to be Pay-to-Win, but it gained A LOT of balancing updates and the dev team completely remade the movement parkour system in order to be even more easy and fast.
Do not listen to people who say it's still pay to win. You can craft ANYTHING in this game if you dedicate yourself enough. The farming proccess itself is very fun if you have friends, it's actually relaxing in lower levels and it can really get your adrenaline on in those difficult missions. And you will usually end with resources and parts for lots of different weapons along the way, which is great because the level up system depends on you experimenting with multiple weapons and warframes.
Also if you want to spend money on it, there are lots of opportunities to get huge discounts, like almost every week I can get 25-50% discounts, and it's not hard to get 75%
The only cons I have is having to buy extra weapon slots in the inventory, the space is limited. And you don't get a lot of exposition on the game's lore in the beginning, but the devs are really working on this particular problem.
Literally the only online RPG that really got my attention. Movement mechanics are a lot of fun by itself, and combat is easy to learn, hard to master and has LOTS of variety, as well as the missions themselves

I usually play several months before I review a Game but I can't wait to do  this one.
It's just that awesome.
For me this has been the best free game I have ever found  and it is of the level of the best AAA games out there.
It is truly free and not pay-to-win. It is so well made that if you decide to spend real money for platinum (the in-game currency) to gain items faster you will not feel ripped off. In fact you will probably be proud to fund the brilliant developpers that made this game because it's just sooo great!
You can stop reading my review now and just download  the game right away, or continue reading for more details.
Visually the graphics and environnements are among the best and the game is amazingly stable. The level of details in the artwork for mods indicates that talented graphic artists were involved in the creative process.
In the past few weeks I have been a space ninja who has escaped from a menacing faction with the help of a cybernetic female called Lotus who gave me lots of good advice, done a variety of missions such as assasination, capture, exterminate, infiltrate with stealth and hack secret data avoiding traps and sentinels, defending excavation sites, uncovered blueprints for equipment that require collecting a variety of ressources. Sometimes you go in with guns blazing with teammates in huge furball battles and sometimes you solo missions involving stealth and exploration. I have learned it is possible to acquire your own hovering robotic sentinel to help you fight enemies and eventually a ferocious dog-like pet called a kubrow but first you will need a quest that will unlock after a certain level, an egg, an incubator and a whole bunch of stuff I currently have no clue where to get yet. One You Tube reviewer just said to enjoy the game , play it like you want and eventually you will discover plenty of tricks and resources to be an even more powerful and efficient killing machine.
There is just so much to do here, items and mods to collect, levelling warframes, weapons, mods, mastery levels, finding the best builds for your playstyle, exploring a cool Science-Fiction environment, collecting and trading rare stuff, you can customize your own ship, join clans or factions that will provide benefits.
This game is so addictive and fun that you should probably be followed by a psychiatrist if you already suffer from obsessive compulsive disorder.
It might ruin your social life but after playing WF for a while  you may start thinking  social life is overrated .
One last word of advice: when you create your account you get 50 platinum for free. Do not waste it on something frivolous. Best advice I found so far is to use it to buy an extra warframe slot and its weapons slots. You will then have a total of 3 slots for  warframes with different  skill sets and the required weapon slots. After that it will probably take the average player many months to get more... You will have to find rare mods, items, blueprints to trade other players for $P.
Good luck Tenno, may the force be with you.

Ok to start things off, this is one of the best free-to-play games out there IF YOU DON'T MIND THE GRIND. This game has a heavy emphasis on grinding, crafting, and waiting. If you aren't into that kind of thing, this game might not be for you. Buuuut...
Pros:
- Great combat, very very fun melee system + solid gunplay + silly synergy combos = amazing
- Great graphics
- Great customization (if you don't mind grinding to get the plethora of weapons, mods, and cosmetics)
- Very in-depth progression system (if you're into that kind of thing)
- Every frame feels unique
- Every playstyle can be satisfied: stealth, melee, run-and-gun, nuke everything, support, sniping etc.etc.
- PARKOUR!
- Lots of content to enjoy that you can access for FREE, no payment is necessary unless you want specific cosmetics or to speed up the gear obtaining process either by shortening the crafting or avoiding the grind
- The game can be played solo, with friends, with clan mates, or with random pick-up players
- Decent PvP system, can be annoying at times but it's a fun addition
Cons:
- The game has a very stubborn meta-game. Pretty much 4-5 frames are wanted for high-level missions in the recruiting tab. I've been rejected a few times for trying to play a less well-known frame =(
- Very, very, VERY buggy. You WILL get stuck on random things in the level especially while parkouring. Downright frustrating if you get out of the map and can't get back in, which has happened to me quite a bit. Mission bugs occur once in a while, sometimes when you want to extract from a mission the game will randomly throw you back in and instant-fail it and lose all loot/bonus exp from the mission (super annoying, thankfully not a common problem, has happened to me 5 out of 600+ missions).
- LAG and lots of matchmaking issues. I've had many instances where open parties constantly ping back as full, and also many instances where people report that my party is full despite me being the only member. Host migration is a pain, as the game often experiences severe lag issues after the migration
- A bit overwhelming. To new players this game is sort of thrown at you with rather vague instructions on how to do things or progress forward in the game, prepare to do a lot of external research (wiki helps but it isn't enough) or spend a lot of time fumbling around trying to find what you need.
I wrote a lot on the cons section because these problems are very specific and are what I encountered in my Warframe journey. However, I admit that I just blitzed through much of the early content and got very confused along the way so definitely take it slow and give it time. Overall, super fun game, and it's free! Give it a shot at least.

I can't in good conscience recommend this game anymore. The game is pretty good overall, and definitely worth the price point, but the devs have gotten full of themselves after it exploded in popularity. After settling a lawsuit for a non-compete and possible asset theft, they went on to release a paid DLC - while the game is still in Early Access - even after promising the game would go into release in summer 2016. Most recently, they tried to bribe players into voting for them for the Steam Awards, which is an event that's supposed to just be for fun.
Devs aside, recent updates have allowed cross-server transferring of tribes which has completely destroyed anyone's chance of building and maintaining a base. BattleEye doesn't work for keeping hackers and cheaters out, either. The PvP in this game boils down to who can cheat the fastest. There's no real "survival" feel to PvP anymore.
A lot of great modders have backed out of the scene after the DLC fiasco as well, so many of the best mods to come out for the game are in maintenance mode and not adding content. Their reasons are understandable, but that combined with the devs' attitudes leaves the future of this game pretty uncertain.
Buy if you want many hours of solo/private server fun. Don't buy if you want a game to invest in for the long term.

I'm not normally a fan of free-to-play games, but Warframe seems to do it right. Fun and interesting combat, though it could do with more of a variety of enemies rather than just sending 10,000 of the same five or six guys at you at once.
Making your own weapons is kind of stupid and grindy, but as long as you've got good people in a group, it can be lots of fun, even if you don't get what you were trying to.
(Don't listen to people who tell you that this game has a stealth system, though. As of U18, the game is NOT designed with this in mind, and despite most people's descriptions of this game as "SPACE NINJAS IN SPACE", trying to do a majority of the missions stealthily does not work.)
The story is actually very interesting and in-depth, even if some of the bosses are cookie-cutter stereotypes. The update I mentioned before (U18) brought a very large piece of the story to the game that took most people's breath away.
In a word:  Buggy.  In another word:  addicting.  Still playing despite issues that pop up.  Most issues are promptly removed, but hey, apparently the game never left beta.

I've been playing this game as of about April 2013, a Founder I am.  There are a few things that I didn't like about the game, back then there were a few things that felt a little out of place with the movement, as well as just a few general gameplay problems, and occasional bugs.  However, coming on nearly 3 years, still playing the game, and many hours, weeks, months, and the past couple years poured into the game, it's come a long way, and still more to come.
The developer, Digital Extremes (DE), is very kind, and a group of quite entertaining (funny and otherwise), people, to anyone that watches their streams every other week, of course, depending on the stream, every week.
Things that I don't like about the game:
-Many of the tile sets feel a little predictable.
-It can be fairly easy to get burnt out, if played too much.
Things that I like about the game:
-A variety of classes, or Warframes
-Variety of weapons to choose from.
-Variety of companions.
-More colors, and minor customizasions than nessecary (but totally worth all of them).
-Diverse mission types, and rewards.
-Each Frame behaves differently than another, close in role, but different.
-Navigational "Star Map" is well designed (to be changed at some point).
-Cinamatic story piece (only one, but word is that there's more to come).
...And quite a lot more.
By no means is it a game for everyone, and the movement style can be difficult to grasp (kind of), but once you have it down, it's really easy to get around, and I find myself often wondering what the map limitations are, and for the most part, I've found that, if you can see it, it's possible to get to it, but a bit of thought is required to get to that point (sometimes, and dependant on what Frame you're on).

Well skeptic gamer, let me tell you this: it's the best F2P game out there. Originally when I got a steam a year ago I was not into PC gaming, my how much has changed. Over that course of the year I played Warframe.
The game has evolved into a beautiful world I couldn't believe how far they've come from launch day. You play as the Tenno, basically Space Samuari with Ninja moves whose are the only people in the galaxy with these advanced suits called Warframes. Each one is different than the other giving you incredible abilities like vanilla powers of speed and fire, to unique ones such as creating illusions and controlling magnetic polarity.
The game works as a PvE where in every mission you can play solo or with 3 other players/friends in a typical dunegon crawl fashions as different planets and high tech buildings.
Weapons, Warframes, Companions like alien dogs and flying robots and your angel jetpack wings (yeah you heard me. You can get wings ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥rrrr), all can be attained without paying a cent. Sure it will take you forver, but that's okay. Your weapons and warframe levels up over time, and can even prestiege to make it stronger over time. So you could basically have one warframe for hundreds of hours and it can be ready for high level bosses.
The game helps you out a lot with cool story quests and guides you through the various game modes, and how much you can customize things! You have your very own ship which you can color code, or even get a brand new one. Since one of the updates it can now help you in Air support.
Whether you want to be stealthy, all meelee or guns blazing it doesn't matter because you can play any way you want! The game offers you so much freedom in these levels.
The downside? Some Warframes are exclusive to preminum players and/or have to purchase them to acquire it. It can also be very repetitive since you're grinding for money and resoruces to make your own weapons and warframes. So play this game evenly to avoid getting bored.
The reason why it's a fair F2P game is their business model is really decent. Didn't feel like I need to buy anything, but it does tell you if you want a bigger inventory you gotta upgrade using Plantinum, usually acquired by buying it for real (unless you go on high level raids).
Fans of Borderlands, Titanfall, Mass Effect and Call of Duty Advanced Warframe should definitely give this a try. You won't be disappointed by it.

I usually play several months before I review a Game but I can't wait to do  this one.
It's just that awesome.
For me this has been the best free game I have ever found  and it is of the level of the best AAA games out there.
It is truly free and not pay-to-win. It is so well made that if you decide to spend real money for platinum (the in-game currency) to gain items faster you will not feel ripped off. In fact you will probably be proud to fund the brilliant developpers that made this game because it's just sooo great!
You can stop reading my review now and just download  the game right away, or continue reading for more details.
Visually the graphics and environnements are among the best and the game is amazingly stable. The level of details in the artwork for mods indicates that talented graphic artists were involved in the creative process.
In the past few weeks I have been a space ninja who has escaped from a menacing faction with the help of a cybernetic female called Lotus who gave me lots of good advice, done a variety of missions such as assasination, capture, exterminate, infiltrate with stealth and hack secret data avoiding traps and sentinels, defending excavation sites, uncovered blueprints for equipment that require collecting a variety of ressources. Sometimes you go in with guns blazing with teammates in huge furball battles and sometimes you solo missions involving stealth and exploration. I have learned it is possible to acquire your own hovering robotic sentinel to help you fight enemies and eventually a ferocious dog-like pet called a kubrow but first you will need a quest that will unlock after a certain level, an egg, an incubator and a whole bunch of stuff I currently have no clue where to get yet. One You Tube reviewer just said to enjoy the game , play it like you want and eventually you will discover plenty of tricks and resources to be an even more powerful and efficient killing machine.
There is just so much to do here, items and mods to collect, levelling warframes, weapons, mods, mastery levels, finding the best builds for your playstyle, exploring a cool Science-Fiction environment, collecting and trading rare stuff, you can customize your own ship, join clans or factions that will provide benefits.
This game is so addictive and fun that you should probably be followed by a psychiatrist if you already suffer from obsessive compulsive disorder.
It might ruin your social life but after playing WF for a while  you may start thinking  social life is overrated .
One last word of advice: when you create your account you get 50 platinum for free. Do not waste it on something frivolous. Best advice I found so far is to use it to buy an extra warframe slot and its weapons slots. You will then have a total of 3 slots for  warframes with different  skill sets and the required weapon slots. After that it will probably take the average player many months to get more... You will have to find rare mods, items, blueprints to trade other players for $P.
Good luck Tenno, may the force be with you.

I feel by this point (after having spent far too many hours playing this game) I can offer a balanced opinion on Warframe. First of all I would like to say that I like the game and will no doubt play it for a while longer, however my tastes will not be the same as yours so take what I say with a grain of salt.
It is a very grind heavy game, if you do not have time to invest in gaming then it is unlikely that you'll get very far in warframe - I do not mean to discourage anyone but it is a simple fact that you'll struggle to reach TRUE end game (#FashionFrame). By this I mean to say that there will always be someone better than you in terms of equipment/mod setup.
It is a very unique game, I've heard warframe compared to Destiny but I think that is not a very favourable comparison for Destiny. Warframe is free and it has a huge amount of features, it is stunningly diverse in terms of abilities and finding the synergies between these is utterly rewarding. I don't think I could name more than a handlful of other games that are nearly as diverse and rewarding as Warframe when it comes to finding synergies.
It is NOT pay to win, lots of people complain that they feel pressured into buying platinum in order to progress but that simply is not true (from my experience at least). While platinum can certainly speed up your progression through the game, you are in no way forced to buy it. I have friends who have never spent any money on Warframe but still manage to have a relatively competitive and high end account, you just need to know how to negotiate and trade your in game items for platinum.
It is fun, that's probably the essence of why I love the game, it's a game where you can alternate between try-harding and chilling out in a heartbeat and I just love that freedom. The community is probably one of the best communities on Steam in terms of players helping players and simply put it is a great atmosphere to be in. Whether you get the game or not is your choice but I would ask you to think on this, is there any other game that you WANT to log on to EVERYDAY, that's Warframe for me.

Warframe is a free-to-play cooperative third-person shooter video game developed by Digital Extremes for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One. Equipment can be earned through gameplay or bought with premium currency called Platinum. Most cosmetics and boosts can only be purchased with platinum, though some items are available from other sources.
Gameplay
In Warframe, players control members of the Tenno, a race of ancient warriors who have awoken from centuries of cryosleep to find themselves at war with Grineer, a race of militarized human clones; The Corpus, a mega-corporation with advanced robotics and laser technology; and the Infested, disfigured victims of the Technocyte infection. To fight back, the Tenno use advanced exo-armor with unique abillities - the eponymous Warframes. Available missions are scattered across the planets of the solar system, the moons Phobos and Europa and dwarf planets Pluto, Ceres, Eris and Sedna. Additionally, players can also access missions set in a pocket dimension known as "The Orokin Void" or "The Orokin Derelict" through the use of keys.
Up to four (Trial missions allow eight) players work together to complete missions, such as eliminating enemies, retrieving data from terminals, assassinating high ranking/dangerous targets, defending an artifact, or surviving as long as possible. Players wear a battlesuit called a Warframe, each with its own set of abillities and statics; and are equipped with three weapons - a primary weapon (such as a rifle, bow, or shotgun), a secondary weapon (typically a pistol, but sometimes ranged bladed weapons like kunai), and a melee weapon (such as swords, axes, and hammer). There are also Companions that can accompany Tenno on mission, each with their powers. These can either float near the Tenno's head, or following a quest, players can earn their own Kubrow, a hound-like animal with a horned nose. Players earn Affinity (experience points) for killing enemies and completing missions, and the higher the Affinity rank of any piece of equipment, the more mods it can accomodate.
Undoubtedly it's one of the best sci-fi games.

Although I only have <200 hours on Warframe as of this review, I actually started playing the game way back in open beta (I didn't add it on Steam until recently). Back then, the game was still pretty good, but not ground-breaking or anything. I considered it a novelty, and played it for a few (around 12 or so) hours and then left it to play other games like Destiny.
I came back to the game just under a year ago, and I can say without a doubt that I consider this free-to-play game way better than games like Destiny. Over the years Digital Extremes has added so much stuff to the game, the most recent of which was the amazing cinematic quest, "The Second Dream".
Unlike most other multiplayer games where the player is given a choice of a few classes, Warframe (as of this review) gives the player a choice between a whopping 28 different Warframes (effectively classes), which they can switch between at will once they are obtained.
The game also includes a smorgasbord of weapons with extremely varying mechanics (grenade launchers, bows, laser rifles, explosive throwing stars, nunchaku, etc.), rather than a bunch of rifles which differ only in their stats.
The community is also very helpful and easy to play with thanks to Warframe's simple matchmaking system.
In addition, the developers actually listen to the community and have very close interactions with us through the forums and even DevStreams. They are also almost always adding new content with new weapons, warframes, and/or quests coming out almost every month or so.
All that being said, the game can seem a little bit grindy at times, but I don't really feel that way since I consider what some people think of as "grinding" as just putting in the work to achieve a certain goal.
Also, while this is a free-to-play game, the only time when I felt required to spend premium currency was in order to buy warframe slots and weapon slots. Personally, I have never spent a dime on this game and got all my platinum either through in-game trading (selling rare mods or parts to other players for premium currency) or giveaways (I got pretty lucky :P).
Overall, I absolutely love this game and would definitely recommend it to a friend.

Well skeptic gamer, let me tell you this: it's the best F2P game out there. Originally when I got a steam a year ago I was not into PC gaming, my how much has changed. Over that course of the year I played Warframe.
The game has evolved into a beautiful world I couldn't believe how far they've come from launch day. You play as the Tenno, basically Space Samuari with Ninja moves whose are the only people in the galaxy with these advanced suits called Warframes. Each one is different than the other giving you incredible abilities like vanilla powers of speed and fire, to unique ones such as creating illusions and controlling magnetic polarity.
The game works as a PvE where in every mission you can play solo or with 3 other players/friends in a typical dunegon crawl fashions as different planets and high tech buildings.
Weapons, Warframes, Companions like alien dogs and flying robots and your angel jetpack wings (yeah you heard me. You can get wings ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥rrrr), all can be attained without paying a cent. Sure it will take you forver, but that's okay. Your weapons and warframe levels up over time, and can even prestiege to make it stronger over time. So you could basically have one warframe for hundreds of hours and it can be ready for high level bosses.
The game helps you out a lot with cool story quests and guides you through the various game modes, and how much you can customize things! You have your very own ship which you can color code, or even get a brand new one. Since one of the updates it can now help you in Air support.
Whether you want to be stealthy, all meelee or guns blazing it doesn't matter because you can play any way you want! The game offers you so much freedom in these levels.
The downside? Some Warframes are exclusive to preminum players and/or have to purchase them to acquire it. It can also be very repetitive since you're grinding for money and resoruces to make your own weapons and warframes. So play this game evenly to avoid getting bored.
The reason why it's a fair F2P game is their business model is really decent. Didn't feel like I need to buy anything, but it does tell you if you want a bigger inventory you gotta upgrade using Plantinum, usually acquired by buying it for real (unless you go on high level raids).
Fans of Borderlands, Titanfall, Mass Effect and Call of Duty Advanced Warframe should definitely give this a try. You won't be disappointed by it.

I first picked this game up at the beginning of 2014. I played through a bit of it and thought that it was repetative, the UI was clunky, and there was a lack of story. Fast forward almost 2 years and things have changed drastically. The UI looks sharp, the game is more optimized, different story lines were added, and I gained a deeper understanding to the lore as the lore itself expanded.
DE has made a fantastic game for the amazing price of $0. I've had more fun playing this than some AAA titles. They add content for free and constantly update the items.
The thing I love about Warframe is that you can aquire almost ANY item without having to pay a single cent of real world currency.

The gameplay itself can be challenging at times, but you can just go to a different world that is easier. There is a variety of difficulty in the game which covers a very large player skill base.
The people who play are usually kind enough to help you out if you need help defeating a certain boss or if they need to find some potato blueprints.
Speaking of blueprints, you'll use a lot of them if you don't want to spend money. The way they work is that you have to have the required components and money to start the blueprint. Then the blueprint will go through a construction period   which varies for each item. One item can be made in 1 minute while another takes 36 hours. Usually, the longer you wait, the sweeter the reward.
With a wide diversity of weapons, skills, and playstyles, you play how YOU want to play. If you want to sit back with a sniper in the shadows while invisible, go for it. If you want a machine gun and extra armour to blast through the front line of the enemy, go for it. There are tons of different combinations avaliable to each player.
Overall, I'd give it a
. It's a very solid game, and you'll get tons of hours of enjoyment from it.

It's awesome. You get to be a space ninja. Nuff said.
If you want more on why it's good then here it is.
A) They have a good free to play model. Much better than most free to play games.
The reason I say this is simple. There is nothing paying gets you that you can't get by playing. The only things that can only be bought by platinum (the currency that you pay for) are appearance items. The best part is that you don't have to pay for them. If you get deeper into the game you can get platinum by trading with other players. So you do a bit of farming, or you get an item that needs a certain faction rank, and you trade it for platinum. It makes it so you can play for free, and still get the things that would need you to pay.
B) It's just awesome.
Not to long ago they added a new movement system to the game. It is now more about timing it to be quick, and knowing your limits than it is getting a certain item to move fast. You can run around duel-wielding swords, and blocking lasers with them! You aren't a real space ninja until you've charged 20 soldiers all shooting laser-rifles, and you block every blast. It's awesome. You also get tense moments. There are certain bosses that show up after certain events (going against a certain faction, or killing bosses) that can make you heart nearly pound it's way out of your chest. Leveling up a low level frame, and suddenly a squard of teleporting assassins shows up to try to kill you. It is yet again awesome.
C) Constant updates.
It seems every time I turn around they've added a new weapon, or frame, or a nice item. There's always something to do and I can't even keep up with how quickly things are coming out.
D) They listen to the community.
Digital Extremes actually made a new weapon type because someone in the community thought it would be cool to have a sword and shield. This goes with the constant updates, but they are always improving things, and interacting with the community.
I could keep going, but I think it's better if you just play the game. It's free and it's probably one of the best experiences you'll have in a free to play game. Just a suggestion though. If you like melee get excaliber as your starting frame. You'll be able to summon a lightsaber that shoots lasers, and if that doesn't make you want to play the game then nothing probably will.
