I say "NOT pay to win" three times for a reason. A lot of f2p games out there have a crazy "pay to win" mechanic to them, and it is a majior turn off to a lot of players that just want to get good at a game without having to use their hard earned stash-o-cash. Think of this game as more of a "pay to look good" game or a "pay to be lazy" game. I say this because EVERYTHING in the game (besides the chosen few things that have been closed off by the devs) is obtainable.
The reason I say that the market is for those who are lazy or impatient is because if you want it, you have to farm for it. You have to Some things can take one or two runs to get, while other things can take five to ten rounds to get what you need. And you have to build it. Building has a time on it, which can be anywhere from a few min to a couple days. You can use the real-to-game currency (called platinum, or plat for short) to "rush" your building, or you could just buy it in the market without all the farming. Real-to-game currency can alos be used to buy cosmetics to make you look fancier while you're shreding all the things. Or you can use it to trade other players for stuff. Players love the plat. They worship the stuff.
This game takes deication. It takes time. And a lot, I mean a LOT, of patience. Its easy to pick up and can be played with either mouse and keyboard or controller. It got a crazy weapon modding system that you NEED to understand if you want to be good, so I recomend at least 10-15 min videos on the modding systems. You canplay about 99% of the missions with friends or random people that drop in, and does require a decent amount of teamwork on plenty of missions. The devs are on top of this game all the time, and have released a good amount of new content at least once a month. I have found no bugs in the time that I have played this game, and so far love it. So go play it.
Now for the Con's (not gonna be much here 'cause im biased)
-Crazy graphics, so if your comp cant handle, you're screwed.
-Can lag at times if one person in squad doesn't have a good connection.
-Updates can take years if you don't stay on top of them. Ther have been plenty of time when I havent played for about 2 weeks, and have to spend about half an hour or more (depending on the update) downloading in the launcher before I could play.
-Farming. My GAWD the farming. You have to really WANT what you are farming for sometimes. But the joy you get after finally building that crazy op item that you spent days trying to get is priceless.
A few of my friends have had crashing problems when playing this game even when they have a great graphics card. I myself have not had these problems, so I can't really tell you weather or not that will affect your experience. Just thought I'd put that out there.
Now then if you got this far THANK YOU soo much for reading this post. You must like reading, 'caus a big block of text is usually a turn off to most people. I defiently recomend this game, so you should really pick it up. If you do play and want some help farming, getting through hard missions, or just some general advice, the in-game name's cjmRAZOR. Now then, enjoy the carnage and the action tenno.

MUST KNOW BEFORE YOU PURCHASE: YOU CANNOT SAVE IN THIS GAME. WHEN YOU DIE, YOU WILL HAVE TO START OVER, YOU LOSE YOUR ITEMS IF YOU CANT FIND YOUR BODY IN THE ALLOTED TIME. While the hype for beautiful scenery and the fantasy of living out some childhood dinosaur dream are appealing to some, this game falls short of providing a fulfilling experience for the money.  While providing a sense of survival with weather effects and quantifying torpor, stamina, water, and food essentially as a timer one has to constantly reset, the entire game's purpose is a time consuming, tedious, skill-less endeavor. It is a race against the clock for immediate tasks such as food or water, but its a long waiting game when it comes to progressing and purchasing "ingrams" or raising your stats. I'd almost say this game was deliberately designed to drain a persons time from them. When you start out, the game is difficlut. Particularly in an official server.  Progress is long and tedious.  When you die, you will lose everything unless you can by chance of god spawn near where you died and find our body.  I actually quit this game for a month because it was so frustrating.  The only reason I returned is becasue STEAM would not refund the game eventhough I was unsatisfied customer.  I gave it a second chance so I wouldnt have wasted $30 DOLLARS on an EARLY ACCESS game. I did the grind on the official servers, and later joined a tribe. I must admit, this is the only reason i still play ark today.  This is the only reason this game is fun.  When you get to play with other players and help eachother, or go exploring. The dinos are cool, but the game is full of glitches.  Intersecting geometry, some bad physics when dismounting dinos, when flying wyverns (cant fly them to save my life), there's no story, they could at least have a single player campaign as a tutorial where you could save your progress.  There really isnt even a point to this game. there is no reward, no end.  You get to summon these bosses if you "win" and collect the artifacts which litterally means more grind, more time out of your life to go waste even more of your life killing the boss to win a few decent items. This game will literally suck the life out of you. Its fun to play with your friends, if you have a good set up, the visuals are nice, the concept is great but has a long way to go. Finally, what in the dickens are they thinking charging $30 bucks for an early access game, then releasing a paid DLC for $20 when their first game isn't even complete.  Its starting to become clear these "Early Access" titles are just a scam to scale gradually the release of the game and charging more by releasing it in bits.  Kind of like chris roberts is doing with Star Citizen. Theyve raised 140 million in just backers,  who is going to be left to buy the game when it is actually realeased? Truth is, theyll milk it for as much as they can if they can get to 200 million because everyone that was ever going to buy the game has already "pledged."  I cant believe Ark has released a PAID DLC when their first release is not even working properly.  Its full of bugs and glitches.  I tried to get a refund from steam but because I had played it and just stopped for a month, they said i couldnt because I had the game for so long and played it too long, but if I could go back and avoided purchasing it I would have.

I feel by this point (after having spent far too many hours playing this game) I can offer a balanced opinion on Warframe. First of all I would like to say that I like the game and will no doubt play it for a while longer, however my tastes will not be the same as yours so take what I say with a grain of salt.
It is a very grind heavy game, if you do not have time to invest in gaming then it is unlikely that you'll get very far in warframe - I do not mean to discourage anyone but it is a simple fact that you'll struggle to reach TRUE end game (#FashionFrame). By this I mean to say that there will always be someone better than you in terms of equipment/mod setup.
It is a very unique game, I've heard warframe compared to Destiny but I think that is not a very favourable comparison for Destiny. Warframe is free and it has a huge amount of features, it is stunningly diverse in terms of abilities and finding the synergies between these is utterly rewarding. I don't think I could name more than a handlful of other games that are nearly as diverse and rewarding as Warframe when it comes to finding synergies.
It is NOT pay to win, lots of people complain that they feel pressured into buying platinum in order to progress but that simply is not true (from my experience at least). While platinum can certainly speed up your progression through the game, you are in no way forced to buy it. I have friends who have never spent any money on Warframe but still manage to have a relatively competitive and high end account, you just need to know how to negotiate and trade your in game items for platinum.
It is fun, that's probably the essence of why I love the game, it's a game where you can alternate between try-harding and chilling out in a heartbeat and I just love that freedom. The community is probably one of the best communities on Steam in terms of players helping players and simply put it is a great atmosphere to be in. Whether you get the game or not is your choice but I would ask you to think on this, is there any other game that you WANT to log on to EVERYDAY, that's Warframe for me.

Still is a damn good looker thanks to a combination of engine tech as well as a unique art design focus and implementation, even 3 years after its public start, helped along with constant updates to that department.
Continually expanded gameplay mechanics that award mastery as well as still remaining approachable. For example, the release of the new Parkour 2.0 movement system that revolutionized the mobility of players, making them true space ninjas over previous movement system mechanics that relied on a long-loved melee movement bug. Another example is the recent release of the Focus System tied with in-game story progression, adding to the ever-deepening lore of the game.
Arguably fair F2P microtransaction model, wherein a thriving player-based trade market for content-only-available items in-game are traded for premium currency, or outright buying said currency to trade for said items, or buy market items. This is one game that you can legitimately get everything for free given your dedication and some RNG.
Very active developers with consistent communication with the community, consistent game updates that expand the game quite a bit, and feedback given to them is actually noted and listened to.
================
Said consistent art design and focus can be a bit of a detriment when a lot of stuff is happening on-screen, leading to potential forms of information overload not to dissimilar to "helmetfire" at times. It isnt surprising when one is simply
with effects and flashes in this game, so be warned.
Constant game updates can lead to bad patches, and the developer is not a stranger to really bad band-aid fixes at really bad times, not to mention lack of technical capability when things go wrong. Fixed quickly enough, true, but...
If you're the kind who simply refuses to even give a buck to a F2P game, prepare to face the grind, and oh what grind you will face!
As active the developers are, they can seem to go off on tangents that the community (and even developers within their studio) see that could lead to major negatives if implemented into the game, as noted by their history for band-aid fixes that could negatively affect the game for months before they apply a real fix.

I'm not sure how they did it, but Warframe manages to scratch that "I want a game that’s grindy but I don't want to actually notice how much grind I have to do"
Instead of having a "Max character level", you have a mastery level which is representative of how many
weapons and warframes you've used.  Its simple but brilliant.  As long as they keep making new stuff (and the developers have been constantly cranking out quality stuff) then basically there's no level cap.  You just keep building and playing with new toys!
The developers are fantastic: super involved in the community, great sense of humor, high quality content. I could recommend this game based on how awesome the developers are. Seriously, this is the gold standard.
There's no getting around it though, it’s a free to play. There's gonna be some grinding.  But it’s a pretty enjoyable one, especially if you sort of take your time and really savor the environments and enemies and whatnot that Digital Extremes have made.
Enthusiastic recommendation from me, great stuff.
Edit: As was pointed out, I forgot to mention that you can trade for the premium currency in game for most of the different items in the game through the community.  Its definitely worth trying to get some because you'll want to expand your armory and warframe garage, but thankfully extra slots aren't too expensive.

Short version: Idea of the game is alright, but the devs are scumbags.
At time of review, this is an Early Access title, meaning that the game is still in development, but that players may purchase the game before it is completed. While this game is still incomplete, the devs decided to release a paid DLC for this game, which costs $20 on top of the price for the base title. In other words, Studio Wildcard literally has paid DLC for an unfinished game, which still has major optimization and balance issues.
The above may not sound so bad, but the worst part of it is that prior to the DLC's release, the creators claimed that certain content would be coming to the base game, namely a desert map and desert themed creatures. Suddenly, these claims disappeared from all immediately visible parts of the game's page, and then the paid DLC was released, which contained the aforementioned desert content.
If this was not sure evidence of some level of dirtiness in the dev team, they have also recently been caught attempting to rig the vote for one of this year's Steam Awards (Best Use of a Farm Animal) as seen here:
.
This company does not deserve your money. Please look elsewhere for better, and more ethically-produced games.

IMHO, Warframe is hands down THE best free-to-play game on the market. They've excelled in so many facets of their game it's kind of hard to believe more people aren't playing this and talking about it.
The gameplay is smooth, the shooting feels great, the melee feels great, the abilities are varied and useful. The graphics are solid, maybe not everyone's cup of tea, but they look great and the game is well optimized.  Just this year DE has released 4 big content patches easily equivalent to paid DLC in games such as Destiny, but it's all free.
The one thing Warframe falters on is introducing new players. It's a slog at first to collect resources for crafting and the tutorials don't really do the best job of explaining game mechanics and especially the tremendous depth of the mod system and customization.
The microtransaction model is easily one of the best out there. You don't have to pay for anything. The only thing gated behind money is some of the cosmetics, extra weapon and warframe slots, but even that you can sell rare mods and parts for to earn platinum (the in-game currency).
It doesn't cost you anything to try this game so download it, and if it interests you at all...invest some time because it just keeps getting better.

I'm not too sure I should be writing a review for this game as even 70+ hours in, I have barely scratched the surface as the game's wide variety of weaponry and warframes (characters) are still out of my reach. Warframe is a massive game full of missions on varying and randomly generated worlds against the unique enemy factions. In the game, there are numerous missions ranging from the simple kill everything extermination missions to the survival missions, to even rescue missions that require infiltration to save a hostage who you can then arm to help in combat until the mission ends. During these missions, you can obtain materials to build new weapons and characters to upgrade yourself to defeat the three unique enemy factions (Grineer who are militaristic clones with cybernetic augmentation and utilize jetpacks, flamethrowers, and heavy equipment to fight offensively. The Corpus, who are an economic oriented supercorporation that employs humanoid mercenaries and varying drones for either combat or support purposes. And the Infestation who are a mix between the Halo universe's flood and other traditonal alien zombies as they use their wide variety of units to overwhelm the players in huge masses). Due to how diverse the game is, there is an element for everyone with it's large arsenal, randomized missions, and interesting classes.
Positives
+ Relatively fair F2P model with a decent amount of grinding, however being that the layout and enemies are changed each time means missions are diverse enough that the time can be enjoyable
+Diverse roster of weapons and characters to fit any role as stealth, support, offensive, and defensive abilities and equipment are available.
+ Frequent updates adding new content to an already massive game
+ A decent and separate multiplayer mode that drops exclusive rewards for weapons that are used in the mode.
+Fun PVE experience with allies as most frames synergize well together.
Negatives
- Story quests are far and few besides the brand new Second Dream (At the time of writing this is the most recent major event) and some events can no longer be done and their decisions have already impacted the world.
- Earning new frames can take time as they have varying drop requirements and have a mobile-esque build time that can take up to three days if one chooses not to pay
- Being that the maps are randomly generated, the AI sometimes gets caught between cells and can do pretty stupid things, or worse, a player can get stuck at a bad combination and very rarely, missions may not function right. This is often not an issue as a /unstuck command can fix the situation and the game occasionally spawns in enemies so a mission can progress yet when it does happen, it's incredibly annoying.

Well, where to start? ARK is a game with the most potential of any early access game out there to date. But there are a few deal breaking things that made me quit this game all together. First off, The SERVER TRANSFER.. This has ruined the game completely, allowing huge Alpha tribes to go on a random server, teleport their dinos from a DIFFERENT server, and completely wipe a server that they've never put any time into. Now imagine being apart of a server that this happens to, you spend hundreds of hours building up your base and creating something you're so proud of, just for 10 guys to come on from another server and destroy all your hard work in a day. I would not recommend this game to anyone for this reason. Next up, we have the absolutely HORRIBLE game optimization. You could have a Titan X and still wouldnt get 60fps on this game, it is truly game breaking, you get bad frames, and the server lag is catostraffic. The dev team focuses so much on PUMPING out new game content, that they ignore the most fundamental part of their game.. GAME STABLILITY. It is basically none existent. So unless you are willing to put up with being online 24/7 to make sure people dont server transfer and wipe your server, and unless you're willing to put up with awful server lag and bad frames, (even on low settings it doesnt change a thing), then I would not recommend this game to anyone, until they remove the server transer function, and until they start focusing on optimizing their game and improving server stability.

Well, after 2 years and 1000 hours, I'd say this is worth trying :P
Basically, this is a game where you are kicking♥♥♥♥♥from start to finish and looking/feeling awesome while doing it, so expect something that's fun but not challenging.
The main problem is it can be grindy, so I'd recommend don't go for the completionist approach. If you are constantly leveling weapons and warframes just for the sake of it, then you'll probably find it to be very boring and grindy, instead just do whatever and play whenever you fancy and don't worry about collecting absolutely everything.
For new players (I'll try to keep it short):
It starts out awesome, and has a really good sense of progression for quite a long time. You'll find mods to augment your warframe and weapons with as you play, which are extremely generous with the bonuses they give you. Everything can be leveled, so you'll be getting exponentially more awesome the more you play (unless you're unlucky with RNG).
You'll probably decide quite early on which of the warframes sound the coolest, and you'll have something to work towards. It's not a quick process since you need to find and build all the parts (it can be a massive pain if you lack the resources), so it feels quite rewarding once you finally finish it. Each one is also unique, so whichever you choose, you'll get an entirely new way to play the game.
After exploring the solar system, you'll see alerts popping up in certain locations, which are events that anyone can hop into. You'll usually find some sort of reward, so it's good for a quick bit of cash, and occasionally it'll have a rare item or mod. There are sometimes huge events that last for a few days where anyone can participate, and these can sometimes shape the game world depending on the outcome.
The good:
Graphics are really nice
Gameplay is fun for people of all ages, and occasionally some parts are given a total overhaul
Massive updates and frequent hotfixes
Procedurally generated levels, so they're not all exactly the same
Build your own customised clan dojo if you have the resources
Anything non cosmetic can be earned in game (plus that's half the fun, buying them is boring)
The bad:
Quite repetative and can get grindy
The number of tilesets is quite limited, so you'll see a lot of very similar levels
Stealth is still almost pointless, if you can't go invisible there's no point even trying
Arrows and daggers do more damage than bullets and rockets
Sometimes RNG seems to spite you, which turns the game into a grind

Totally recommended.
It's among the few games with an actual fair trade beween RNG and reward (and no, you getting tired because you didn't even cared to learn the basics before screaming "paywall" and running away doesn't make this statement any less truthful), the amount of things you can't get  with other than money aren't significant at all aside from the Founder pack, which is exactly that: an incentive to people who practically gave money away to get some perks in-game when game's was in a REALLY early state of development.
Players with some brains can get platinum (the in-game significant currency that you regularly buy for real money; eg; LoL's RPs) by farming different things.
Of course, the game is not perfect and devs seem to focus more on stopping easy ways to farm and level up weapons and warframes than actually "tweaking" stuff for the good. Up to date, Mesa's Shooting Galery stills the weakest buff ability, and Peacemaker stills draining ridiculous amounts of energy for the little it does because it's consumpting cap is way too high so making it a duration + efficiency  affected is barely significative.
Saryn got an awesome mechanics rework that made her interesting to play with, but is still being an energy expensive Warframe and I can't believe their programmers greenlighted the stupidly unneficient way Spore work because it becomes an awesome resource hog and it hurts more your hardware than your enemies, regardless of what their youtube PR machine unanimously stated since the early ours after the rework (at least it's decen't now, it used to be terrible when they released the first instance of the rework), Toxic Lash is rarely used and I still don't know anyone saying it is good aside from people who uses full retard melee builds focusing solely on it.
Mag's Greedy Pull got an underserved nerf, it was like shooting someone with a shotgun in the face for calling you names. making it a personal utility would be enough, making it a requirement for stuff to be on line of sight AND not bypass walls reduced its usefulness like 1:100.
There is a story for every "farming friendly" Warframe out there that got nerfed. Digital Extremes do great things when they want (Raids, Spy 2.0, Rescue 2.0, Natha, Second Dream, Orokin moon, Saryn's new mechanics and synergy, sorties) but some other times they also do borderline stupid things that feel arbitrary at best (Mesas' and Saryn current energy consumption, Archwings are an uninteresting module whose resources spent on could have been invested on the actual game -what's next; Tenno Kart?-, some AoE from enemies just insta-kill u on higher levels, combos are more spectacular than useful -this is not a melee focused game, you can't even rely on it on higher levels-, their UI design is 80% focused on aesthetics and 20% on function, and more... ).
I haven't talked about graphics because it is pretty obvious that the game is way ahead of most (if not all) F2P currently in the market. Sound isn't spectacular aside from a few exceptions mostly quest-related things, but it accomplishes what it's meant for.
I think this game is a solid 7/10, it isn't just decent, it is good, at moments very good such moments are more and more frequent since I started playing, although, consistency isn't one its qualities. They could easily sell this game for $40 bucks if they reduced the grind and adding more story, so, I don't think trying it (or getting back into it) will hurt you.

Warframe is a third-person (over shoulder) shooter, with warframe (character) abilities and melee being just as relevant as the guns. The game has a lot of game modes that offer a variety of different types of gameplay, but for the most part the game is a hoard killing game. The progression in the game is based off repetitive gameplay and grinding, but it is mostly implemented in a enjoyable way. At least I find it enjoyable enough, that with the F2P model, I have no issue recommending for people to at least try the game out.
Positives:
- Large variety of very different weapons to play with
- Variety of enemy factions and unit types, requiring different stradegies to tackle efficiently
- Some progression feels very enjoyable
- A lot of customization with weapons and enemies that make choices important as you progress to end game content, or attempt to minimize grind with efficiency stradegies
- Co-op
- F2P model that feels right. Premium currency is tradeable. Premium currency is used to buy most asthetics, and to rush progress. End-game content ("prime" equipment and warframes) are not purchasable off the market, but from trading with players.
- Lore concepts are enjoyable
- Movement is one of the most enjoyable to play around with, out of any game I've ever played.
-Different mission types, such as spy missions, are great for changing the core way you play the game. This makes everything else more enjoyable.
Negatives
- Many weapons and equipment are just not viable for endgame, which is understandable in a progression game, but it is a problem with no weapon that has a similar feeling to replace it exists in the end. Sometimes feels forced to leave enjoyable options behind for the over powered weapons like the grenade launcher "Tonkor". Having more end-game weapon variety would be good.
- A lot of the difficulty increases comes with just upping the numbers on enemies, with limited skill based factors, or having enemies that just offer little counter-play. Though I'd say this is only a minor issue with the number of different enemies you have to deal with, but it's worth noting.
- The amount of RNG in some progression concepts is just very unenjoyable. Running the same mission 20+ times and not getting what you're looking for is very fustrating. Some things really should be revamped or have an extra system in place that can eventually garuntee what you're grinding for.
- Premium currency price feels steep, until you see that login rewards have a chance of being a discount of 20%, 50%, or 75%. Then it feel like you're getting ripped off any time you don't get at least 50% off. The RNG is even on premium currency, and it just feels very wrong. The prices and discounts should be reworked and remove the RNG attachement of login rewards.
The negatives are mostly only things you notice as you play the game for a large number of hours and mostly noticed from endgame missions. There is definitely more enjoyment in the game than gripes, but they can burn you out of the game fairly fast due to always being there.
In the end I just like killing enemies with different weapons, and this game is great for that.

I played this game on an AMD A10 pc and it lagged a bit and took ages to load world (i played sungle player) but it still was very, very fun.

You really can't go wrong trying a free game, even if you think you may not enjoy it. That's exactly what I did with Warframe, and I'm liking it so far.
Graphics look good, soundtrack is OK, voice acting is great (but doesn't match the subtitles sometimes), and animations are smooth. Gameplay is interesting, with a few annoyances.
Plenty to do with your friends, and there's a good amount of variety in the game modes, keeping it interesting.
The game has nice, large levels with plenty of hidden treasure to be found, and it encourages you to explore. The main issue I have with Warframe is that when you leave a room and come back, which happens quite a lot, most of the enemies that you just finished killing will respawn. This puts the player at a disadvantage (increases difficulty, I guess), but also becomes very tedious and extremely annoying. Sometimes you'll go through an area several times trying to find a cache (a well-hidden, but worthwhile treasure), and simply become very annoyed with the constant enemies.
Overall, I rate the game Seven out of Tenno.

I've had this game in my library for well over a year now, and I'll be honest, I gave up on it fairly quickly in the early stages. Now, a year and a whole ton of improvements, updates and bug fixes later, I am 100% hooked.
EDIT: After 6 months, I figured I'd update my review. After 6 months of playing, there are a few things i'd like to point out that desperately need fixing and/or attention from the developers -
#1 - The ability to go away for even just a week or two without losing everything you've spent days/hours obtaining. Unless you're willing to or have the ability to log in every few days to maintain everything you've built (feeding, repairs, just visiting to refresh the deterioration timer), then I'd advise you to not be heartbroken when you log in and all the things you've spent days worth of time acquiring are gone. And you might as well forget about breeding all together.
#2 - The constant pillaring. The pillars are everywhere and makes it near impossible to find land of your own to build any kind of substantial base on.
#3 - Dinosaurs will still randomly disappear, for no reason and Predators still spawn inside walls, rooms, bases, etc, and make meals of your more docile dinosaurs.
Also, jacking the price up from $30 to $60? I won't even dignify what a bad move that was. Come on, devs.
I'm sure there's more, but I'll just leave it this way for now.

Some of the resulting games are efficient soulless money harvesting machines, others are genuine but poorly executed attempts to have fun. Still others are genuine in spite of being refined and profit-oriented. Trying to make money isn't wrong, after all.
Coming from a lowly time where there were only a handful of frames and missions, faithful updates have developed it into a thriving hub of fun and gameplay options. Sure, you might spend five hours doing the same thing every now and then, but I imagine most are used to a bit of grinding in this day and age. As far as Free to play money making machines go, this one is a jolly and cheerful success for players and presumably also for the developers.

I have played 2200+ hours on this game. Purchased it on a whim when it was on sale in 2015, and then started actively playing in June of 2016. I've only played on official servers; both something I regret and don't regret at the same time. I see myself playing this game for a while - and as a person who plays only one game at a time, that's a big deal for me.
However.
While I do admire and respect a lot of what Wildcard has accomplished the game, they've fallen behind with consideration to the community. A while ago, transfers were enabled from server to server. The advent of this caused many servers to get raided by tribes on other servers, causing an uproar from the game's population. Again, transfers were reopened. Large tribes have ventured from server to server, wiping entire servers for the fun of it. From older, established servers to newer ones; where tribes have not had the same advantages for the same period of time in regards to developing bases. Wildcard has stood by and have done nothing to rectify the issue. Yes, it's PvP - but it's a bullying tactic and Wildcard has looked the other way.
I don't regret the time that I've spent playing; and I personally haven't gotten wiped. But the threat is always there - and the threat is presented by tribes I have no hope of defending against simply because they can lock down a server I'm on (by filling character slots with members from their own tribes) and prevent my tribemates from assisting - if they hope to try to defend at all.
With that said, I would encourage anyone who would like to play the game to play on private servers. DO NOT PLAY ON OFFICIAL.
Play the game at your own risk. ARK is time intensive. If you're interested in PvP, you need to have a group of folks you can trust and who won't drop the ball on you. If you're interested in the breeding aspect of the game... well, there goes your sleep. Building? Competition for resources. Taming? Well, those rates will vary and if you don't have kibble, you're in it for the long haul. Bring friends, solo's only truly manageable with modifications.
June 30th 2017 edit:
Having just reached a bit over 4k hours, I'll change this review from no longer recommending the game to recommending the game. As I mentioned previously, I do respect Wildcard for what they have accomplished with the game. The content is expansive and there is an "end game". Official PvP is a challenging venue - but if you aren't a member of the right tribe or playing on the right server, everything you have worked hard to accomplish will be wiped clear by other players on a regular basis. I would still caution any new player against playing on official PvP - the climate is extremely hostile and unwelcoming, and it would be better to join friends rather than try to strike out on your own with little to no knowledge of the game. Some PvP servers are friendly, but most are not.
Most of what I've said still stands true - breeding is time consuming. You need to study the competition very well when it comes to building - see where they do well, and see where they did wrong. In regards to the content, however - ARK stands out. There are many possibilities for the title - and I see a lot of opportunity for continued growth. ARK is the sort of game that combines a lot of popular elements (sandbox, open world) and encourages a healthy modding community.The game is well on its way to official release and Wildcard is working around the clock to insure that the quality of the game is what it should be - what any player may expect of a game that has been officially released.
While I still play other games from time to time, ARK is a favorite of mine - and has been for a number of months. I see myself playing it for a while and I'm looking forward to how the game's official release might impact the game's community and future.

There is no other purpose but a wild landgrab.  The game design doesn't account for this, so unless you get to a server very early, you have no good spot for a base.
So, if you're new, considering buying this game: don't.  You'll be wandering for hours trying to find a place to build a base,  and even if you do find one, you'll be battling egregious lag to build it and protect your investments.

Let me start this review by saying that I love being a space ninja. I love the idea of running around as a physics-defying gun-toting hyper-advanced assassin, and the ability to do that in Warframe is really and truly quite awesome.
The thing is, the game doesn't encourage you to do that. It introduces movement mechanics that are really fun to utilitize, and then gives you ZERO reason to utilize them. If you've played the game with others, you know what I'm talking about when I say you probably won't ever see anyone do a wall-slide or wall-jump in the middle of combat. They'll stick to simple maneuvers like sliding and bullet-jumping, and even then, it's probably safer to just stay behind cover and pop enemies in the head one by one.
Your strategy, no matter what weapons you choose to use, generally comes down to a few simple steps:
1) Use mods to get high max shield and high damage
2) Kill enemies as fast as you can while shields last
3) If shields fail, hide until they recharge
And none of this encourages using the kind of skills befitting of a ninja. It ends up being a dull slog through endless waves of enemies where all you do is shoot or slash them until they fall down, the same way, over and over and over again. The only factor that determines whether you succeed is whether you kill them all before your shields and health run dry.
It's simply bad design. The developers could be focusing on refining the core mechanics to make this a game that actually allows you feel like a space-ninja. A number of tweaks, such as the following...
- Make enemies less likely to hit while you're moving and performing acrobatics (right now they have absurd accuracy ALL THE TIME)
- Create levels designed to actually encourage use of advanced movement techniques (many current levels have weirdly shaped walls that make wall-sliding and such nigh impossible, or closed-in areas with very little space to use your full movement arsenal)
- Alter enemy AI so they lose sight of players, allowing players to flank (the current AI always knows where you are, even if you break line of sight completely)
... would make for a game that is much more interesting and fun to play at a very basic level.
Unfortunately, the developers seem more interested in adding more content than fixing some of the issues that are keeping this game from being truly enjoyable.
I like the idea of Warframe, but the game itself simply does not deliver on what it promises to be.

A friend said I should review Warframe. So here it is; >hrs on record<
That should be enough to state this game is worth playing, but if you need more than that I shall go on.
>Warframe is one of the few games that I have ever played that has been able to keep my attention for monthes on end. The graphics are beautiful and it has an interesting story to go with it.
>The community of the game is overwelmingly good, most players will be more than happy to help you learn the ropes and you aren't entirely seperated from players who have been around since the game dawned. Aside from that one troll who you run into every once and a while that has just discovered Loki's switch teleport or the jerkoffs who use the elevator before you can get in the community is great.
>The gameplay is fast and attention gripping. The grinding can seem a bit redundant at first but when you get used to it the feeling washes away in the shear joy you feel from every motion you make in the fast paced parkour system.
>IT DOESN'T HAND HOLD YOU FOR A MONTH. The game teaches you what you need to know within the first hour or so of gameplay and the rest is up to you to figure out. I found this especially attractive because I absolutely despise any game that has a tutorial window pop up every 5 minutes (like most games do now) and doesn't bombard you with you with so much that you can't figure out what's what. You learn as you go and it feels REWARDING. Warframe is like learning to become an artist, at first you doodle with your little mediocre weapons and you slowly develope into an elegant angel of death.
>Every weapon and warframe feel rewarding to and the customization is phenominal. The diversity and versatility of each frame creates the opportunity to play the game your way. You can make a healer a tank or a deffensive character an walking artilery cannon and the game maintains its entertainment no matter how high up you get.
>THE ANTICIPATION OF UPDATES WILL EAT YOU ALIVE. Every update so far has had me exicted and left me grinding to the point where I'll skip out on sleep just to get time in so I can unlock the new items or learn the next part of the lore. New frames weapons mechanics and so on at a realitively good rate keeps you intrigued enough to make you never want to log off.
>There are also in game secrets, such as secret items, secret rooms, parkour challenges, puzzles to solve and so much more intergrated into just regular missions. Some are more rewarding than others but they are all still extremely entertaining to solve and even better when you figure them out yourself.
In conclusion I absolutely love this game I can't wait to see where this game goes and continue to grow with it.
(P.S. whoever says this game is pay to win is an idiot, you can unlock everything except apperence items by just playing the game and you can sell in game items to other players to earn Platinum; the in game currency)
(P.S.S. This game makes Destiny look like walking garbage and it's free to play)

With just over 300+ Hours clocked in i feel i've analyzed this game just enough to make a review...
-Pros-
Great Visuals
This game for being free isn't demanding to run at all, the visuals are great and personally I dont see a huge difference between Medium and High settings so if your not getting enough fps just drop it down to Medium.
-Combat-
The combat system is great there are many different weapons you can fight with from rocket launchers to staves and to the hand held laser... There are too many weapons to even list, all these weapons have unique things that make them better for various player wether it be the damage, attack speed or critical chance. Plus, there are various mods mods that will add new combos from specific weapons...Ex. You can have a Stance for a single sword, dual swords, staves, sword and shield, nunchucks, and even sword and whip... yes I know lots of swords.
---Mods---
---There are many other mods that will add damage to your weapons and this will add a whole level to the game.
-Movement-
Ever since the parkour 2.0 update the movement in warframe has solid from wall "running", to bullet jumping across the room. There are even your own little movement combos you can create to get around faster. The movement also makes enimies lose accuracy so it adds a bit of realism to the game as well.
-Character (frames)-
There are so many frames to choose from I can't even count them you can have a solid support frame to stay in the back and heal and give energy to the teammates, maybe you like to go to the front lines and kill the crap out of enimies there are frames for that to, want a stealthy approach you guessed there are frames for that too, maybe you just wanna be balanced and provide support and help the front lines.. you guessed it there are frames for that too.
-Missions and Tile Sets-
The missions are all unique to each other none are very alike and the different tile sets are always nice because you can see more of the stunning visuals from this amazing game. The missions are all fun and unique as I said before you have different bosses, and different level enimies you can fight on different planets.
-Enimies-
There are a plentiful amount of enimies all taking damage from different things. Don't get me wrong all weapons and elemental types do damage to all enimies, but some do more to other to you mey always want to change your loadout a bit. There are different classes of enimies as well not just different reskinned enimies there are enough enimies to keep you coming back to find the next one.
-Currency System-
Warframe know not all people can afford platinum, knowing this they made it so that you can trade for platinum using rare mods or even other frames. There is also credits the common currency this is used to level up mods and create new weapons and items.
-Home-
Unlike other games when your done with a mission in warframe you dont just pick another one from the main menu you actually have a ship, interactable as well you can do many things in your ship from looking at the codex to personalising your warframe and companions.
-Daily Rewards-
If you wanna buy plat, but don't want to spend as much money or maybe you need to double your xp for a couple hours well daily rewards can do anything from give you materials to give you 80% discounts on platinum.
!-Updates-!
The dev's of Warframe are no joke they release new updates often they may not come with a lot of stuff, but every other month or so they will have a huge update adding new frames and weapons to the game making, this game playable for much longer than most games.
-Unknown (special)
--Wait Time--
Now this may seem like a bad thing to some people and a good thing to others personally I like the wait times they add a bit more to the game
-Pros Wait Time-
The Wait is not the best thing, but I like it i feel like it actually keeps me coming to the game to keep checking all the things I'm building or waiting for. It also adds a bit of realism to the game, If your a blacksmith and you want to build a new weapon you can't just finish it 1 hour you need to temper the steel shape it color it and various other tedious procceses. So I like the wait time personally.
-Cons Wait Time-
The wait time is also a bad thing for example it takes days for you to build a new frame and 12 hours for new weapons now the weapons build time isn't that bad you can start the build play for a couple hours go to bed and wake up the next morning and have it ready, but some of us don't like to wait 12 hours. Now the frames take a total of 3 days to build and man the time goes by very slow. Then before you even build the frame you need to build 3 other parts before it each taking 12 hours at least you can do this simultaneously. Now building the frame does take a while, but when you get it feels amazing to have that new frame and play with them. One last thing when you wanna build materials these can take anywhere from 1 hour to 24 hours now when I wanna build something with fieldron (material) I don't wanna wait 12-24 hours for me to get one and then have to that multiple times.
-Cons-
-Bugs & Glitches-
Warframe is an amazing game, but there are flaws in everygame and warframe is no acception. The amount of bugs in this game is imense, but they only happen so often. Ex. When you are running across the map and then randomly get stuck well great now I'm stuck and can't get out well this is a bug or glitch to get out of these you must do a command and once this command is done you will have to restart the game after the mission. Now I'm not saying that bugs happen every time you play, but every now and then you may encounter one. Ex. I was a playing a mission using one of my frames Valkyr who's 4th ability makes her use only melee, but she is invincible. I fell of the map while using this ability and i had it permantly using no energy it was fun yes, I could not exit the bug and I was stuck using pure melee for the rest of the game.
-Match Making-
Now they are working to fix this by actually letting friends and clan mates join games late before you could not do this. Still match making can put you in a lobby with rank 20's not level 20's. This will make the game impossible for you to get kills although it isn't a very big issue.
-Story-
The story behind the game is still a bit unclear to me although they are making one with the newest update U18 they actually added a bit of lore behind the game this is a small issue, but some people like a story behind their games.

+/- Weapons and frames are free, but the slots to be able to use them arent
The Bad:
- Not newbie friendly, several materials for starting weapons are locked into mid/late game planets
- Several mechanics are not told or hidden in hints on loading screens (which 50% of them are PvP hints)
- The way enemy and armor scaling works makes most weapons get useless, forcing you to mod them in specific ways
- Most mods are locked behind enemy drops. Each enemy has 3% chance to drop a random mod from it's drop table, if you add the rarity modifier on the mods, some mods have a 0.06% of dropping per enemy.
- Several mods for weapons and frames are mandatory, giving you almost no space for experimentation
- Due how weapon stats and mods interact, most weapons will only be used in one way to be effective (critical, status procs, pure elemental)
- Some stuff requires a LOT of grinding to acquire
- Some missions require certain frames to be done for long periods (Like Defense with Frost)
- PvP has no skill based matchmaking, be ready to get stomped by regulars over and over
- Matchmaking breaks ever so often
- Rivens, basically Diablo's random stat generation thrown into mods. There are at least 6 layers of RNG to get the mod you want.
- No proper trade/buy/sell mechanics or auction house, be ready to spam the trade chat and look for someone selling that one item you want in the middle of a torrent of other messages
- Devs work in mysterious ways. When they announce a new thing, it will:
1. Take months/years to be added to the game
2. Be scrapped after sometime, then players are told to deal with it
3. Be never talked again
4. Be scrapped, but replaced by another new thing not related to it
5. Be added, but something else is nerfed into the underground to 'balance' it
A free to play game that isn't pay to win

Where do I start? This game has, in my opinion, everything that a game needs. I guess I'll just make a list.
Pro's:
First of all, it has the social aspect, if you choose to tribe up with new people. I've met friends for life in this game that I wouldn't know how to be without anymore.
Second, It really is a game that never gets old. After playing for a long time, for most people and I, we need a break. But if we just wait a month or two, there are new things to explore, new dino's to tame, and new mods to enjoy.
Third, The PvP is actually amazing in this game, which is something that not a lot of survival games have. It is extremely fun fighting your arch-enemies as a tribe, seeing your friends on the ground fight with T-rexes against theirs, while there is a dance in the air of birds dodging bullets and trying to pick eachother up and throw them to a certain death.(Tip: ALWAYS carry parachutes :P)
4th, If the official servers get too much for you, as after 900 hours It was for me, there are servers with upped gather/tame rates that allow you too get everything A LOT faster, depending on the server you pick. there is a wide range from 5x to even a 100x gathering. Also some amazing building mods/mods to improve pvp.
The only downside would be that you can lose yourself in this game. I've lost friends because I was so into this game, as a tribe leader on an official server, that I had to make some tough deciscions. I'm not proud of it, but this game is very very realistic on that part. Leaders have to sometimes choose between bad descicions, and picking the worst one can end your tribe. It is a tough game, very hard to learn and to master. But I did it. A lot of people did it. And the journey is amazing.
Good luck out there, don't get eaten, and who knows, maybe I'll even raid YOU some time :P

Let me start this review by saying that I love being a space ninja. I love the idea of running around as a physics-defying gun-toting hyper-advanced assassin, and the ability to do that in Warframe is really and truly quite awesome.
The thing is, the game doesn't encourage you to do that. It introduces movement mechanics that are really fun to utilitize, and then gives you ZERO reason to utilize them. If you've played the game with others, you know what I'm talking about when I say you probably won't ever see anyone do a wall-slide or wall-jump in the middle of combat. They'll stick to simple maneuvers like sliding and bullet-jumping, and even then, it's probably safer to just stay behind cover and pop enemies in the head one by one.
Your strategy, no matter what weapons you choose to use, generally comes down to a few simple steps:
1) Use mods to get high max shield and high damage
2) Kill enemies as fast as you can while shields last
3) If shields fail, hide until they recharge
And none of this encourages using the kind of skills befitting of a ninja. It ends up being a dull slog through endless waves of enemies where all you do is shoot or slash them until they fall down, the same way, over and over and over again. The only factor that determines whether you succeed is whether you kill them all before your shields and health run dry.
It's simply bad design. The developers could be focusing on refining the core mechanics to make this a game that actually allows you feel like a space-ninja. A number of tweaks, such as the following...
- Make enemies less likely to hit while you're moving and performing acrobatics (right now they have absurd accuracy ALL THE TIME)
- Create levels designed to actually encourage use of advanced movement techniques (many current levels have weirdly shaped walls that make wall-sliding and such nigh impossible, or closed-in areas with very little space to use your full movement arsenal)
- Alter enemy AI so they lose sight of players, allowing players to flank (the current AI always knows where you are, even if you break line of sight completely)
... would make for a game that is much more interesting and fun to play at a very basic level.
Unfortunately, the developers seem more interested in adding more content than fixing some of the issues that are keeping this game from being truly enjoyable.
I like the idea of Warframe, but the game itself simply does not deliver on what it promises to be.

This is a game that succeeds in the free to play catagory. Its excellent Coop gameplay and varied choices of weapons and Warframes will keep you experimenting and doing new stuff for sometime. With sword fighting/melee and plenty of guns with ninja moves, you will be finding fun and crazy combos to dispatch your enemies. If your looking for an open world persay, then this is not it. You will be running missions and different events in a level like structure, similar to a super large Left 4 Dead in space with a vast amount of levels. I hear alot of people drawing the comparison to Destiny, but I have not played that.
Will you have to spend money? Eventually yes, but more importantly at some point you will WANT to! The login bonuses will eventually give you a certain percentage off Platinum, but you can get ALOT of things by grinding in game money, and thats not so tough once you know what your doing. The Devs are very active and over the years this game has improved greatly and is updated all the time. Like most MMO's and Coop affairs, its always better with friends, but you can do alot by yourself or with just two people. If you have a group of friends and are looking for a new Coop game to hang in, this is definetly a free to play worth taking a look at!

With just over 300+ Hours clocked in i feel i've analyzed this game just enough to make a review...
-Pros-
Great Visuals
This game for being free isn't demanding to run at all, the visuals are great and personally I dont see a huge difference between Medium and High settings so if your not getting enough fps just drop it down to Medium.
-Combat-
The combat system is great there are many different weapons you can fight with from rocket launchers to staves and to the hand held laser... There are too many weapons to even list, all these weapons have unique things that make them better for various player wether it be the damage, attack speed or critical chance. Plus, there are various mods mods that will add new combos from specific weapons...Ex. You can have a Stance for a single sword, dual swords, staves, sword and shield, nunchucks, and even sword and whip... yes I know lots of swords.
---Mods---
---There are many other mods that will add damage to your weapons and this will add a whole level to the game.
-Movement-
Ever since the parkour 2.0 update the movement in warframe has solid from wall "running", to bullet jumping across the room. There are even your own little movement combos you can create to get around faster. The movement also makes enimies lose accuracy so it adds a bit of realism to the game as well.
-Character (frames)-
There are so many frames to choose from I can't even count them you can have a solid support frame to stay in the back and heal and give energy to the teammates, maybe you like to go to the front lines and kill the crap out of enimies there are frames for that to, want a stealthy approach you guessed there are frames for that too, maybe you just wanna be balanced and provide support and help the front lines.. you guessed it there are frames for that too.
-Missions and Tile Sets-
The missions are all unique to each other none are very alike and the different tile sets are always nice because you can see more of the stunning visuals from this amazing game. The missions are all fun and unique as I said before you have different bosses, and different level enimies you can fight on different planets.
-Enimies-
There are a plentiful amount of enimies all taking damage from different things. Don't get me wrong all weapons and elemental types do damage to all enimies, but some do more to other to you mey always want to change your loadout a bit. There are different classes of enimies as well not just different reskinned enimies there are enough enimies to keep you coming back to find the next one.
-Currency System-
Warframe know not all people can afford platinum, knowing this they made it so that you can trade for platinum using rare mods or even other frames. There is also credits the common currency this is used to level up mods and create new weapons and items.
-Home-
Unlike other games when your done with a mission in warframe you dont just pick another one from the main menu you actually have a ship, interactable as well you can do many things in your ship from looking at the codex to personalising your warframe and companions.
-Daily Rewards-
If you wanna buy plat, but don't want to spend as much money or maybe you need to double your xp for a couple hours well daily rewards can do anything from give you materials to give you 80% discounts on platinum.
!-Updates-!
The dev's of Warframe are no joke they release new updates often they may not come with a lot of stuff, but every other month or so they will have a huge update adding new frames and weapons to the game making, this game playable for much longer than most games.
-Unknown (special)
--Wait Time--
Now this may seem like a bad thing to some people and a good thing to others personally I like the wait times they add a bit more to the game
-Pros Wait Time-
The Wait is not the best thing, but I like it i feel like it actually keeps me coming to the game to keep checking all the things I'm building or waiting for. It also adds a bit of realism to the game, If your a blacksmith and you want to build a new weapon you can't just finish it 1 hour you need to temper the steel shape it color it and various other tedious procceses. So I like the wait time personally.
-Cons Wait Time-
The wait time is also a bad thing for example it takes days for you to build a new frame and 12 hours for new weapons now the weapons build time isn't that bad you can start the build play for a couple hours go to bed and wake up the next morning and have it ready, but some of us don't like to wait 12 hours. Now the frames take a total of 3 days to build and man the time goes by very slow. Then before you even build the frame you need to build 3 other parts before it each taking 12 hours at least you can do this simultaneously. Now building the frame does take a while, but when you get it feels amazing to have that new frame and play with them. One last thing when you wanna build materials these can take anywhere from 1 hour to 24 hours now when I wanna build something with fieldron (material) I don't wanna wait 12-24 hours for me to get one and then have to that multiple times.
-Cons-
-Bugs & Glitches-
Warframe is an amazing game, but there are flaws in everygame and warframe is no acception. The amount of bugs in this game is imense, but they only happen so often. Ex. When you are running across the map and then randomly get stuck well great now I'm stuck and can't get out well this is a bug or glitch to get out of these you must do a command and once this command is done you will have to restart the game after the mission. Now I'm not saying that bugs happen every time you play, but every now and then you may encounter one. Ex. I was a playing a mission using one of my frames Valkyr who's 4th ability makes her use only melee, but she is invincible. I fell of the map while using this ability and i had it permantly using no energy it was fun yes, I could not exit the bug and I was stuck using pure melee for the rest of the game.
-Match Making-
Now they are working to fix this by actually letting friends and clan mates join games late before you could not do this. Still match making can put you in a lobby with rank 20's not level 20's. This will make the game impossible for you to get kills although it isn't a very big issue.
-Story-
The story behind the game is still a bit unclear to me although they are making one with the newest update U18 they actually added a bit of lore behind the game this is a small issue, but some people like a story behind their games.

- The good -
Let me start by saying that this is not a fast pace game if played as PVE. The game has no real agenda and i would compair it to minecraft with the exception of being able to dig into the ground. So far there are 3 different maps that you start out with nothing but your fist's and before you know it you will have tamed 10 dino's in only a few hours of game play time.
You will die A LOT! at the begining, and that doesnt matter who you are. everyone figures out what their limit's are and what all the different dinosaurs do. After all, what doesnt kill you makes you stronger.
If you'r a fan of a hunger games style PVP game i would recommend downloading ARK Survival of the Fittest, ARK even has an MLG once a month for teams aswell as single player PVP that i think is just awsome.
The game has been in "Early release" for as long as i can remember it being on steam for over a year now but it seems like they keep adding more features to the game about once a month and they activly try to balance out the game and listen to the community about bugs and recommendations.
- The bad -
The servers can't seem to handle very many people even through each server say's it can hold up to 75-100 players it get's laggy and dino's stop spawning at around 20-30 players on the server.
The whole "Pillering" thing in PVE is annoying because some people get out of control with that making it very difficult to build on a level area or for that matter placing your first camp fire so you don't starve...
I would not recommend playing the game on anything less than medium quality due to the fact that you are missing out on some very visualy dynamic scenes and it feels like an entirly different game between low and high detail.
- Overall -
I would recommend playing it if you like building things, Don't be thrown off by the fact that you're playing with"Dinosaurs", i was never a huge Dino Geek growing up but it never bothered me once in my 300+ hours.
- Recommendations for starting the game -

Warframe, Digital Extreme's most well known title to date, is a Free-2-Play MMOTPS
In Warframe, you take control of the Tenno, Masters of gun and blade, they are both silent and not so silent with ninja-like abilities, including wall running and wall grabbing
Warframe starts off very simple, but after the first quest, the game gives you alot of freedom to decide what to do next, the game is what i like to call, a "grindfest", in which you must repeat missions to grind materials and credits to build weapons, warframes, items, etc
Now I know F2P games have got a very bad reputation for being HEAVILY Pay-2-Win, but Warframe is not like that, everything can be obtained in the game through time and patience, and you could trade certain items to earn Platinum (Warframe's buyable currency) for free
As of this review, Specters of the Rail has dropped, so if you are curious about what Warframe has to offer, check out the community, they're really friendly and the devs actually listen to our concerns
in short: Warframe is a hard game to start off, but once you put time into it, you might enjoy it, who knows, it may become your obsession

2 years in and they already went this far.
Warframe is a co-op 3rd person shooter where we plays with a squad, up to 4 players in a mission at once.
The titular Warframes are your characters, each of them wields various abilities from vanishing from views to map wide explosions. They moves nimbly using their surroundings, they are essentialy space ninjas.
Warfashion is a game where you customizes the so called Warframes inside your very own spaceship. Collect them all and using various palettes provided by the game, color each of them to your liking. Of course, not only frames you can fashioned into pretty birds. Various guns and personal-stabbing-devices, flying drones and Kubrows-not-dogs (Catbrows will come in future), your ship, smaller ships for personal use, and even your very own (or shared) dojo can be beautified.
Wargrind is a role playing game where you as a space ninja, doing many hideous inexplicable things such as spying, sabotages, even murders, to collect rare component for the need of crafting rare items or sell them for False Profit.
Warfarming is a farming simulator where you go to various places in solar system collecting materials to craft every single thing craftable in the game for personal satisfaction and show it to other farmers. If you like Rune Factory and its battle heavy gameplay, you should give this game a try. Too bad there's only one love interest in this game, Space Mom.
Warface is a different game, there's the door.
Is it good? You bet.
Is it easy to get into? Tutorials do need more work, but the community generally pretty helpful.
Is it pay 2 win? Pay 2 convenience. Premium currency in this game can be obtained by buying with real currencies or from trading with other players. They are needed to enjoy the game fully, but it's not hard to get if you know what to do.
Is it still alive? 3rd most played free to play game on steam, 50K active players in steam alone not counting from consoles and standalone launcher.
Is it worth investing 1000+ hours? Well, it's not a crime.
Best frame? Zephyr <3

This game is amazing.
I'm coming up on 500 hours of gameplay and I'm still awestruck at the visuals. I've added bases at picturesque locations solely for the view. I've lived on mountaintops where I can see islands at the far end of the map and I've built fortresses on plateaus and I laugh at the Gigas that stare hungrily at me from below. I've traversed caves with swarms of beasts that can tear through your armor in a few hits, I've crawled among trees that are as tall as skyscrapers, and I've walked beaches that overlook the glimmering ocean as giant sharks try to leap out.
I recently started playing on the Center expansion map and it's even better. Cascading waterfalls falling from the heights of the map to the ocean below. Spires of rock pierce the sky. I cannot stress the visual value enough.
One of the few downsides is the crashes. Sometimes I'll pay for 10 hours and sometimes 10 minutes, but my fans will ramp up out of nowhere and the game will crash to my desktop. Hours of searching for a solution have been fruitless. This is often at critical points- I'll be flying or approaching a large carnivore or just freezing to death. I've lowered the settings and changed settings and nothing has helped.
The multiplayer is great. Many servers have increased gather and taming rates so the otherwise tedious grind gives way to actually enjoying the game and building incredible structures. I've fallen off of flying dinos and simply tamed another to get back to the first one. However, some players will cause newbies grief in PvP which ruins the fun- who wants to go back to stone tools after a total wipe?
But the game is beautiful, and it easily ranks as the top visual game I've seen, ever. Sadly, this ruins other games for me, but I'm excited about how much better things can go from here.

EARLY ACCESS REVIEW
So, I spent quite a few hours playing this game and although I pressed the recommend button, there are definitely things people need to know before buying this game. There should be a "meh" button, for games that you are conflicted about :P
PROS
- the world is amazing: a lot of work has been put into making the word aesthetically pleasing: fantastic graphics, very detailed, cool animations and sound effects
- a lot of things to do: from discovering and defeating/taming all the dinos available, to building bases, to exploring the land and the ocean, to hunting for resources and trying to stay alive while pretty much everything is trying to kill you. Yup you guessed it, loads of things to do!
- everyone can have fun: whether you like PVE or PVP, you prefer playing alone or with friends, you want a super hardcore, ultra difficult (borderline sadistic) environment or just a relaxed place where you can have fun, you can either join an already available server, host your own, or host your own game locally
CONS
- developer attitude: yes, I was one of those people who got extremely♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off when the developers released a DLC when the game is still not officially released. How you can have an expansion when the game is still in development is beyond me. Also, there are quite a few bugs and it takes forever for them to get resolved, which can be really frustrating. Finally, never believe the release dates that they announce for patches or what is going to be included. They might have aimed for that deadline in the beginning, but usually we get the stuff a lot later :P
- servers die very fast: the server list is endless, however my experience was that they get deserted very very fast, which is kind of a bummer
That being said, I enjoyed this game immensely. I did everything there is to do (and yes, I did buy that damn DLC) and had an amazing time. But now, I am kinda bored tbh... I definitely do not regret buying it and I might come back to it at some point, but for now, I hope this review was helpful and I hope that you'll enjoy the game!

This is the first part of a series of reviews I plan on doing. I’ll review pretty much every game I buy from now on, based on content, gameplay, graphics, replayability, and business practices . Keep in mind I don’t have the money to buy every game out there. Feedback appreciated.

So Star Wars Battlefront is perhaps one of the most beloved Star Wars game franchises out there. I have fond memories of the original, and the sequel, which in my opinion is the best one. I spent more hours on those games than I would care to count. But we’re not here to talk about the originals. We’re here to talk about EA’s Star Wars Battlefront.
I would like to Start off by saying that EA’s Star Wars Battlefront is not necessarily a bad game. It has everything your casual gamer needs -pretty, if not amazing graphics, controls that everyone is already used to, and (somewhat) enough content to keep them invested and coming back for a while. But notice I said “Casual.” If you are just looking for a simple game that’s easy to play and is very intuitive, then this game is probably great for you. If you just want to feel like Darth Vader or Luke Skywalker and look at the pretty environments like Endor, Hoth and Tatooine, then this game is probably great for you. But that is where it ends.
Content
First off, EA’s Star Wars Battlefront does have enough content to keep it from being completely repetitive. That being said, it pales in comparison to the original Battlefront games.  That argument is unfair however, because this game has nothing to do with the original games than the Star Wars title. It’s made and produced by different companies. Anyways, as I was saying, it does have just enough content to keep me from getting bored after a couple of hours (see replayability.) The different planets had plenty of little caves to explore, or Easter eggs that give me a little smirk every once in a while. There are 12 planets not including the Battle of Jakku DlC which adds 2 more. This turns out to be 3 maps per planet. This is where they get you though; some of those 12 maps are exclusive to the less popular gamemodes, so if you want to play them, you’ll have to pray you can find a game. There are 9 gamemodes in the base game, with an added map with the Battle of Jakku DLC. The most popular gamemodes from my experience are Walker Assault, Turning Point, Supremacy and Blast. I just wish it had more content. Only 4 planets? I was sure there would be more. 6 heroes? Of course, they’ve announced that there will be 4 paid DLC expansions which will include new heroes, maps, what have you. I’ll talk more about that in the business practices section. It doesn’t have very many blasters, but the weapons it does have are either mostly the same or grossly overpowered (I’m looking at you DL-44.) You can customize your characters with different heads, weapons and star cards. The customizing is very basic, and feels a little rushed. You can’t change the height, eye color, clothing, or size of your character. I bet people aren’t buying the game for customizing though.
Gameplay
EA’s Star Wars Battlefront, as I said in my synopsis, is simplistic, intuitive, and easy to learn. If you’ve played a first person shooter before, then you know how to play this game. While big companies like IGN or Gamespot run games like this at ultra high settings and maximized internet so they can get everything they need out of it for their reviews, I am perhaps one of the only game reviewers who plays♥♥♥♥♥♥settings on♥♥♥♥♥♥internet on a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ PC. I run this game on auto, which for me is mostly the lowest setting. My internet constantly cuts out. The point is, I may have gotten a lesser experience from this game because of my situation. However, despite all of this, I still had fun and came back for more. The gameplay basically consists of running around and getting killed. Running around and throwing grenades and getting killed. Shooting at someone until one of you gets killed. Running into a hero and getting sliced or electrocuted. Getting into an X-wing, A-wing, Snowspeeder, Tie fighter, or a Tie Interceptor and maybe getting a few shots off then either abruptly crashing into the ground or getting killed by an X-wing. Essentially, you shoot at another person until one of you dies. Or they snipe you from a mile away, which I find happening to me very often. Despite the very simple gameplay, it’s still fun to throw a thermal imploder, or fire a locked on missile, or jetpack onto a giant AT-AT walker and annoy the crap out of people. The game does not have a dedicated singleplayer, which wouldn’t affect me even if it did. I never play singleplayer campaigns in multiplayer games. It does, however, have missions, where you fight off waves of enemies on different maps either alone or with a friend. It’s pretty much exactly how you would imagine it. I don’t find my self playing missions very much, but I assume they are fun for people who like playing with themselves… err, playing by themselves. Battlefront lets players use what they call “Star Cards”, which are basically special powerups and boosts you can equip your character with to customize your play styles. The star cards you’ll mostly find are the Plasma Rifle, and the jump pack, which in my opinion are both a tad too powerful. Overall, the gameplay is simple yet can be fun if you don’t mind no lying prone and overpowered star cards.
Replayability
As previously stated, the gameplay is fun enough to bring me back. It has just enough content to keep me from getting bored very quickly. That being said, I only play the game for about an hour at a time, where I’ll go to play a different game, say Rainbow Six Siege for instance. After playing for several hours, it gets harder each time to convince myself to play more of it. This isn’t what a game should do. I should be skipping my homework to play this game. I should be looking forward to coming home and playing this game after a long day. This game just doesn’t do that for me. If all I need is a game that brings me back once in a while, then this is a great game. But I need more.
Business Practices
I guess I’ll start by admitting that months before this game came out, I was telling all my friends this game would be amazing. I argued with people in the YouTube comment section who said it would be terrible and EA would ruin it. I stood up for this game, I convinced myself it would be one of the best Star Wars games ever made. It deeply saddens me to admit that I was wrong. Before I was certain that EA cared too much about the fans to incorporate paid DLC or a season pass into their game. I was completely wrong about both. While the game is visually great, I am frankly appalled that they would do this to us, to me, a huge Star Wars fan. But you know what really pisses me off? The fact that they know that most people, myself included, will end up getting their DLC. I probably will end up paying over the $60 price tag for their extra content. Does this make me a hypocrite? Yes. I am ashamed of myself, but it is the truth. I need to see more of this game. In conclusion, this game is fun, and does have some replay value. It barely has enough content to entertain me. But the business practices alone horrify me.  On a scale of Attack of The Clones to Empire Strikes Back, I give this game a Revenge of the Sith (Slightly below average.)
