This is a pretty cool Space Ninja Hack n' Shoot n' Grind game.
It plays pretty much like GunZ did back in the day.
The Good:
+ Moviment is fast and fluid
+ Several characters and weapons to use
+ Lots of customization, both for fashion and for performance
+ Characters work a bit like MOBAs, having 4 skills and one passive
+ Fun combat and a lot of stuff to do
+ All weapons and characters can be unlocked for free
+ Premium currency can be traded between players and the market is very active
The Meh:
+/- Grinding for anything burns you out quite fast
+/- Anything free requires grinding, but most times its nothing big
+/- Several useless powers, weapons and skills
+/- Way too many time walls and daily limits
+/- Grind grind grind kill kill kill
+/- Requires you to play with matchmaking and join a clan to advance the game
+/- Late game doesnt rewards the effort
+/- Weapons and frames are free, but the slots to be able to use them arent
The Bad:
- Not newbie friendly, several materials for starting weapons are locked into mid/late game planets
- Several mechanics are not told or hidden in hints on loading screens (which 50% of them are PvP hints)
- The way enemy and armor scaling works makes most weapons get useless, forcing you to mod them in specific ways
- Most mods are locked behind enemy drops. Each enemy has 3% chance to drop a random mod from it's drop table, if you add the rarity modifier on the mods, some mods have a 0.06% of dropping per enemy.
- Several mods for weapons and frames are mandatory, giving you almost no space for experimentation
- Due how weapon stats and mods interact, most weapons will only be used in one way to be effective (critical, status procs, pure elemental)
- Some stuff requires a LOT of grinding to acquire
- Some missions require certain frames to be done for long periods (Like Defense with Frost)
- PvP has no skill based matchmaking, be ready to get stomped by regulars over and over
- Matchmaking breaks ever so often
- Rivens, basically Diablo's random stat generation thrown into mods. There are at least 6 layers of RNG to get the mod you want.
- No proper trade/buy/sell mechanics or auction house, be ready to spam the trade chat and look for someone selling that one item you want in the middle of a torrent of other messages
- Devs work in mysterious ways. When they announce a new thing, it will:
1. Take months/years to be added to the game
2. Be scrapped after sometime, then players are told to deal with it
3. Be never talked again
4. Be scrapped, but replaced by another new thing not related to it
5. Be added, but something else is nerfed into the underground to 'balance' it

2 years in and they already went this far.
Warframe is a co-op 3rd person shooter where we plays with a squad, up to 4 players in a mission at once.
The titular Warframes are your characters, each of them wields various abilities from vanishing from views to map wide explosions. They moves nimbly using their surroundings, they are essentialy space ninjas.
Warfashion is a game where you customizes the so called Warframes inside your very own spaceship. Collect them all and using various palettes provided by the game, color each of them to your liking. Of course, not only frames you can fashioned into pretty birds. Various guns and personal-stabbing-devices, flying drones and Kubrows-not-dogs (Catbrows will come in future), your ship, smaller ships for personal use, and even your very own (or shared) dojo can be beautified.
Wargrind is a role playing game where you as a space ninja, doing many hideous inexplicable things such as spying, sabotages, even murders, to collect rare component for the need of crafting rare items or sell them for False Profit.
Warfarming is a farming simulator where you go to various places in solar system collecting materials to craft every single thing craftable in the game for personal satisfaction and show it to other farmers. If you like Rune Factory and its battle heavy gameplay, you should give this game a try. Too bad there's only one love interest in this game, Space Mom.
Warface is a different game, there's the door.
Is it good? You bet.
Is it easy to get into? Tutorials do need more work, but the community generally pretty helpful.
Is it pay 2 win? Pay 2 convenience. Premium currency in this game can be obtained by buying with real currencies or from trading with other players. They are needed to enjoy the game fully, but it's not hard to get if you know what to do.
Is it still alive? 3rd most played free to play game on steam, 50K active players in steam alone not counting from consoles and standalone launcher.
Is it worth investing 1000+ hours? Well, it's not a crime.

This is the first part of a series of reviews I plan on doing. I’ll review pretty much every game I buy from now on, based on content, gameplay, graphics, replayability, and business practices . Keep in mind I don’t have the money to buy every game out there. Feedback appreciated.

So Star Wars Battlefront is perhaps one of the most beloved Star Wars game franchises out there. I have fond memories of the original, and the sequel, which in my opinion is the best one. I spent more hours on those games than I would care to count. But we’re not here to talk about the originals. We’re here to talk about EA’s Star Wars Battlefront.
I would like to Start off by saying that EA’s Star Wars Battlefront is not necessarily a bad game. It has everything your casual gamer needs -pretty, if not amazing graphics, controls that everyone is already used to, and (somewhat) enough content to keep them invested and coming back for a while. But notice I said “Casual.” If you are just looking for a simple game that’s easy to play and is very intuitive, then this game is probably great for you. If you just want to feel like Darth Vader or Luke Skywalker and look at the pretty environments like Endor, Hoth and Tatooine, then this game is probably great for you. But that is where it ends.
Content
First off, EA’s Star Wars Battlefront does have enough content to keep it from being completely repetitive. That being said, it pales in comparison to the original Battlefront games.  That argument is unfair however, because this game has nothing to do with the original games than the Star Wars title. It’s made and produced by different companies. Anyways, as I was saying, it does have just enough content to keep me from getting bored after a couple of hours (see replayability.) The different planets had plenty of little caves to explore, or Easter eggs that give me a little smirk every once in a while. There are 12 planets not including the Battle of Jakku DlC which adds 2 more. This turns out to be 3 maps per planet. This is where they get you though; some of those 12 maps are exclusive to the less popular gamemodes, so if you want to play them, you’ll have to pray you can find a game. There are 9 gamemodes in the base game, with an added map with the Battle of Jakku DLC. The most popular gamemodes from my experience are Walker Assault, Turning Point, Supremacy and Blast. I just wish it had more content. Only 4 planets? I was sure there would be more. 6 heroes? Of course, they’ve announced that there will be 4 paid DLC expansions which will include new heroes, maps, what have you. I’ll talk more about that in the business practices section. It doesn’t have very many blasters, but the weapons it does have are either mostly the same or grossly overpowered (I’m looking at you DL-44.) You can customize your characters with different heads, weapons and star cards. The customizing is very basic, and feels a little rushed. You can’t change the height, eye color, clothing, or size of your character. I bet people aren’t buying the game for customizing though.
Gameplay
EA’s Star Wars Battlefront, as I said in my synopsis, is simplistic, intuitive, and easy to learn. If you’ve played a first person shooter before, then you know how to play this game. While big companies like IGN or Gamespot run games like this at ultra high settings and maximized internet so they can get everything they need out of it for their reviews, I am perhaps one of the only game reviewers who plays♥♥♥♥♥♥settings on♥♥♥♥♥♥internet on a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ PC. I run this game on auto, which for me is mostly the lowest setting. My internet constantly cuts out. The point is, I may have gotten a lesser experience from this game because of my situation. However, despite all of this, I still had fun and came back for more. The gameplay basically consists of running around and getting killed. Running around and throwing grenades and getting killed. Shooting at someone until one of you gets killed. Running into a hero and getting sliced or electrocuted. Getting into an X-wing, A-wing, Snowspeeder, Tie fighter, or a Tie Interceptor and maybe getting a few shots off then either abruptly crashing into the ground or getting killed by an X-wing. Essentially, you shoot at another person until one of you dies. Or they snipe you from a mile away, which I find happening to me very often. Despite the very simple gameplay, it’s still fun to throw a thermal imploder, or fire a locked on missile, or jetpack onto a giant AT-AT walker and annoy the crap out of people. The game does not have a dedicated singleplayer, which wouldn’t affect me even if it did. I never play singleplayer campaigns in multiplayer games. It does, however, have missions, where you fight off waves of enemies on different maps either alone or with a friend. It’s pretty much exactly how you would imagine it. I don’t find my self playing missions very much, but I assume they are fun for people who like playing with themselves… err, playing by themselves. Battlefront lets players use what they call “Star Cards”, which are basically special powerups and boosts you can equip your character with to customize your play styles. The star cards you’ll mostly find are the Plasma Rifle, and the jump pack, which in my opinion are both a tad too powerful. Overall, the gameplay is simple yet can be fun if you don’t mind no lying prone and overpowered star cards.
Replayability
As previously stated, the gameplay is fun enough to bring me back. It has just enough content to keep me from getting bored very quickly. That being said, I only play the game for about an hour at a time, where I’ll go to play a different game, say Rainbow Six Siege for instance. After playing for several hours, it gets harder each time to convince myself to play more of it. This isn’t what a game should do. I should be skipping my homework to play this game. I should be looking forward to coming home and playing this game after a long day. This game just doesn’t do that for me. If all I need is a game that brings me back once in a while, then this is a great game. But I need more.
Business Practices
I guess I’ll start by admitting that months before this game came out, I was telling all my friends this game would be amazing. I argued with people in the YouTube comment section who said it would be terrible and EA would ruin it. I stood up for this game, I convinced myself it would be one of the best Star Wars games ever made. It deeply saddens me to admit that I was wrong. Before I was certain that EA cared too much about the fans to incorporate paid DLC or a season pass into their game. I was completely wrong about both. While the game is visually great, I am frankly appalled that they would do this to us, to me, a huge Star Wars fan. But you know what really pisses me off? The fact that they know that most people, myself included, will end up getting their DLC. I probably will end up paying over the $60 price tag for their extra content. Does this make me a hypocrite? Yes. I am ashamed of myself, but it is the truth. I need to see more of this game. In conclusion, this game is fun, and does have some replay value. It barely has enough content to entertain me. But the business practices alone horrify me.  On a scale of Attack of The Clones to Empire Strikes Back, I give this game a Revenge of the Sith (Slightly below average.)

You will get several hours of fun out of this game- however, you will get many more hours of frustration and tedious ♥♥♥♥♥♥y out of it than actual enjoyment.
tl;dr- unless you're going through a divorce, a lengthy prison sentence (in which they let you bring a gaming PC to your cell), or otherwise find yourself with an ungodly amount of time on your hands, I cannot recommend this to anyone. Also, it is only fun in certain situations. On private servers with increased rates of resource gathering and taming speed,  it can be fun. Otherwise, literally 99% or more of this game will be spent doing tedious things, and eventually you will wonder why you are spending 4 hour intervals of real world time swinging a virtual pickaxe at virtual rocks, or spending 16 real life hours taming a virtual dinosaur- and all of this work can be destroyed in seconds by someone raiding your base while you are offline. This game is only sometimes enjoyable in even the best conditions. It may take you dozens, maybe hundreds of hours to realize this, but eventually you will.
-----------------------------------
I have a lot of issues with this game. First of all, they released an expansion DLC before the game was even out of Early Access. This is insulting. Features the developers indicated would be in the base game were in DLC instead. Who makes paid DLC for a game that is still in Early Access? In all likelihood, this decision had something to do with the legal troubles facing the developers. You can google that on your own.
How will you spend your time in this game? Well, if you play on an official server, you'll spend most of your time staring at rocks and swinging your pickaxe at them.  The default resource gathering rate (what you'll find on official servers) is so low by default that I and many others find it unenjoyable and awful. Nobody has time for this (You CAN have a lot of fun on private servers that have an increased resource gathering rate. ) The same problem applies to taming animals. You can spend 2-16 hours taming something in this game. The game is designed with teamwork and organization into "tribes" in mind, but the amount of tedious, monotonous WORK in this game is absurd. At some point you will realize this game feels more like work than fun.
On custom servers this game can be quite fun, though. I've actually had some great times on it. Sadly though, I feel like the negatives outweigh the positives in this case. It is simply not possible to enjoy this game if you have any career, school, family, or relationship obligations. You may have fun for a while, but eventually all of your "belongings" in this game will be destroyed by a 6-12 year old while you are at work/school. Yes, you can play a PvE server, but that part of the game isn't exactly exciting most of the time. Dinosaurs routinely get stuck on rocks or the environment (Disclosure: AI was awful at least whenever I've played- perhaps they've updated the AI since. I don't intend to go back and find out.)
This game has/had so much potential, and may eventually be a great game. However, as of a couple months ago when I stopped playing, I cannot recommend it to anyone unless they are desperate to dispose of large chunks of time. This game is absurdly addictive to certain people, but in the end everyone I've met that plays this game has the same thing to say- it's a huge waste of time, and in the end you'll wonder why you didn't learn to fly a plane, write computer code, or take some classes instead of wasting HOURS AND HOURS of real world time taming a digital dinosaur.
PS- it runs like♥♥♥♥♥♥ It's about as unoptimized as ARMA 3. I have an i7 and gtx 970. Depending on your settings, expect 20-40 fps, or closer to 60 if you just turn the settings low enough to make it look like CS 1.6.

The Second Dream which really pulled all the biits and pieces of the story togethe that you will come across through play together. The second dream quest was AMAZING! + Great and helpfulcommunity

- If you are not a fan of grinding then walk away now. Grind XP Grind for mats. Grind for blue prints. GRIND GRIND GRIND your life away.
- The storyline to the game seems scattered. You will come across bits and pieces of the story as you play and it will all come together in their new quest line i mentioned before The second dream.

Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.

I started playing this game back when the Grineer spoke English and the tiles were completely broken. Over the years, this game has matured greatly--compared to other games that have existed for 3 years and have not aged well at all. In its original state, this game would not have been much to look at--but time, attention, and community support have caused Warframe to thrive and stand out as one of the great F2P games of our time.
Warframe is a great example of Free to Play done right. There is no pay wall or Pay to Win. You can spend 1000+ hours on the game without paying a single penny. One of the beautiful aspects about the game is that if you don't want to buy something with real money you pay in-game currency to buy the blueprints, and then you have to find the parts and have the resources to build them. Since the actual story is a bit lacking most of the time you will be hunting for parts to make your awesome Tenno warrior(s) (space ninjas) the best that they can be. Personally, I can find it to be a bit grindy at times and sometimes I feel a bit burned out from the game, but that's because I am someone who invests far more in story-driven games. Nonetheless, this is still a great game that deserves far more attention than it has. The community is thriving, the devs are constantly improving the game, and there is always something for you to be doing. It can be a great way to waste an evening with friends.
Pros:
+ Free to Play, no pay wall, and no Pay to Win
+ Unique Co-op gameplay
+ Literally thousands of hours worth of content for you to acquire
+ Continually being updated with new content and quick fixes to bugs, as well as decent Warframe balancing (still♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥about the Trinity rebalance a while back)
+ A whole fandom based on Vor
Cons:
- If you don't want to pay for your stuff you will have to grind for several hours to get it; don't get me wrong, it's well worth it, but grinding is a dealbreaker for some
- Some mechanics are poorly explained; this is especially frustrating when applying mods--but the wiki community helps
- Lotus gets on my nerves sometimes
- PvP is broken and sucks completely. It seriously makes Metroid Prime 2: Echoes multiplayer look good
- I won't say it isn't story-driven, but it definitely isn't the spotlight. For me, this is a con but for others who don't care just ignore this one
- A whole fandom based on Vor
Overall, this is a great game that is worth your time, money, and attention. It's great, but it can be made incredible if more of the community pitches in. I give it a riveting 2 thumbs up!

I understand the need for developers to make money. Really, I do. But I draw the line when your game isn't even out of early access and you've already started porting your game to consoles and charging $20 for a DLC map. In all honesty, ARK is a really cool game. The simple fact that I can play a survival-based game where I can ride a T-Rex whilst wielding an Assault Rifle or Rocket Launcher is just awesome. However, the game's graphical glitches, low-fps (even on low settings), and overall unoptimized state leaves me regretful of ever putting down the $30 for this game.
Again, I am okay with developers trying to make money on a game. But I have the belief that you finish the game you start making first before you begin creating new DLC maps and console ports. The developers just seem too unfocused. There is a lot of new content being put into the game at a decent rate, but none of the old problems I had over a year ago seem to be getting fixed. It almost seems like the devs believe putting more content into the game without fixing the old issues will make the game better, and although I'm okay with more content, I just wish more care would be put into the actual foundation of the game to help it run better.
I look forward to the idea of this game reaching its final state. However, at this rate, I'm unsure that it will ever make it to that goal. Not soon anyway. If you're on the fence about getting ARK, I suggest waiting for the full release, or at the very least, a big sale. There's just too many issues for me in this current release for the $30 price I paid for it. Sorry to those who love the game, but I wouldn't say anything if I didn't care.

I love this game.  I've played it to death it feels like and yet, even then, I've never really stopped playing.  I take breaks from it to avoid getting burned out on it.  However the variety of mission styles and the constant updates with new frames and weapons you can go after make it very fun.  I will admit that it is easier to have fun if you put some money into it to get some new gear but it isn't necessary for those that are adamant about not spending money.  For the most part pretty much everything is obtainable through farming.  However this is where the downside of RNG comes in.  Don't be surprised if you end up doing the same mission for hours and never get that drop you're hoping for.  That would be one of my only complaints on the game is the RNG factor for drops.  The wall running can be a pain at times as well.  However the community is very alive and the devs are constantly working on the game.  New patches and fixs are being released regularly to ensure that the game is fun and that bugs are removed.  The varying mission modes are fun by throwing in some way to make things interesting. As I approach 1000 in game hours (that's actually playing the game in missions, a stat recorded in game), I can finally, honestly recommend this game to people as a game worth playing. After U18, any doubt that the developers were heading in the wrong direction or worry that they weren't pioritizing the right features and content went out the window. They delivered the best major update that this game has ever seen, and probably ever will see.
But let's bactrack a bit.
I started playing this game just a few days before it launched on steam back in 2013. It was awesome; I was a space ninja. While there wasn't much to do and some of the game was very broken, the gameplay was fast paced and tons of fun. I could make my Warframe my own, and play any way that I wanted, whether that be stealthy, support, or just killing everything in the blink of an eye.
After a few months I bought into the $50 Founder pack. I was in love with the game, and while it still didn't have all it's ducks in a row it was getting better everyday. A few months later, I upgraded to the $100 founder pack. It was ludicrous really. The most money I had ever spent on video game, and the game was completely free.
The developers never stopped adding, never stopped reworking, never stopped raising the bar of quality. New weapons and frames added by the week, bosses revamped, entire game systems reworked. From melee, to missions, to movement, and everywhere in between. Everything could be improved, and it did.
But over the past 2.5 years the core issue of the game that held me back from being able to recommend it to people was that there was (as the Lotus might say) "no purpose". There was no direct story to be had, no real goal to work towards, just a bunch of grindng for the newest shiny thing to be released. The gameplay was something no other game could offer, but when the only thing to keep you coming back was your own desire for cool stuff to kill things with, the game was always missing that one part that would truly make it a complete experince.
And then Update 18 launched. The update that ended up being more than any of us expected. For years players speculated and theory crafted with the miniscule amounts of lore we had been given. We could all see the potential, but it was never really fulfilled until now. Being with the game for 2.5 years, wondering all this time who the Tenno really are, and finally learning the truth behind it all was an experience that only Warframe could offer me. Now there's a story to be told, a role to play in this shattered world we've been given. After 2.5 years you'd think it was an end, but no. This is only the beginning. Because the game is alive.
Sure, some of the things the developers do is utter bull crap, and we hate them for that, but at the end of the day the fact that they love their game shows. If you still haven't given Warframe a try, it's well worth at least that. What are you waiting for? It's completely free, afterall.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

So here's a game that had every reason to succeed and be great, but chose instead to simply be a mediocre time sink instead. The gameplay is solid, the graphics are great, combat is fluid and easy, crafting and grinding were bearable and even enjoyable. Here's where the problem lies though; there's no grand, or even small, incentive and nothing passed "press E to win" is ever explained properly.
At the start of the game you're introduced to a baddie who instantly gives you reason to play and a solid plot hook to latch onto with a multi-mission goal. It was a fantastic and promising start into a free mmo that needs to compete with my life for my attention and it was winning pretty well... Up until that quest was over, anyway.
After that quest the game dumps you into space with four different planets you can visit and three different enemy factions you can fight against, but it gives you zero explanation as to who any of them are or why you keep invading their territory to wreck their stuff. The missions you carry out have no overall effect on their hold on the planets, only serving to be the way that you collect materials to find your crafting projects.
This is a fatal flaw, in my opinion, as I'm not interested in a senseless slaughter/grind fest that lacks even a weak long term goal. I don't want to spend hours or even minutes killing the same ten enemy models when I don't even know what my own faction is. We don't play as humans, and if we do then it's never stated. There literally no personal investment that this game can offer unless you REALLY like being a mysterious humanoid space ninja, who works for a mysterious humanoid figure, whom you never meet in person, to kill swaths of other humanoids just so you can build yourself a new hat.
Tl;dr: Fun gameplay, but definitely not worth more than a week of time unless you really liked Ragnarok Online.

Thats just how it works.  You can set up defense and hope it holds while your away but I wouldnt expect that to work.  There have been tons of patches to address balance but the PVP aspect of the game is not my cup of tea, though if you live by the sword, you die by the sword in ARK PVP.
I played the game much more in a single player enviornment and I like that much more because I no longer have to worry about losing my home base or my animals starving to death (with servers, this is something you must consider unless you have a massive tribe willing to keep everything going while you take time off).  I play as I please and am pretty carefree about it.  It also makes doing some things much more difficult which I liked.
I do recommend the game but it has and still does have game bugs, which is expected, since its still in early access.  Also note, that the game requires a very strong computer which wasnt really an issue for me, however, people that do not read the recommended specs and purchase only to find they cant run the game, may have a bad experience and blame the developers so check your PC specs to see if you can run it BEFORE you buy.
Overall, an awesome game with good game play and, if your RIG can handle it, superb graphics.  I would recommend it!

Grind to get the materials to make good weapons and RNG to hopefully get the pieces you need for the Prime Warframes (I can't tell you how many months it took to get Vauban Prime, for example).
DE talks about trying to avoid releasing buggy updates. SotR was so buggy that you couldn't use the new Starmap (which was the main thing that was updated!), while The War Within?

And I haven't even gotten into the nerfs to good things, like Stealth and Affinity (Ha! Good luck trying to level up those new weapons when everything notices when you kill one guy halfway across the map). Or making it to where Nullifiers got a buff (oh hey, let's make it where the guy who's best at defending objectives has his Snow Globe popped when we get close and make it to where you need something that rapid fires to burst my bubble) and seemingly continued to get buffed.
I could go on, I could practically write a novella over all the problems DE is creating with Warframe, but I hope the point's been made. The players aren't killing Warframe; the devs themselves are killing it, through throwing in more and more broken systems and then failing to fully listen to the community when they point out its problems.
So, bye Warframe, and thanks for the memories.

On the verge of buying ARK but looking at reviews first? Good thing I'll give MY honest breakdown of the game for you. This review is biased as all hell, so don't look any further into this if you're easily triggered or dislike a lot of words.
ARK is one of those games you develop a love-hate relationship with.
If you're looking for a fun game to sink a
of time into, ARK might just be for you.
If you like taming sh*t, killing sh*t, building sh*t, crafting sh*t, eating the developers sh*t, ARK might just be for you.
This comes at a cost, though. Bugs and exploits? Look no further because ARK will satisfy all your needs! Dinos disappearing into thin air, dying to nothing, losing your entire inventory to the void, and much, much more!
If you don't play at least a somewhat modded server or at least a server with higher rates, look forward to the constant grind and eternal suffering. Nothing is fun about sitting around a dinosaur for 12 hours babysitting basically nothing. You press a button to make sure it doesn't wake up while it eats the food in its inventory. Vanilla ARK has its quirks and some people enjoy it, don't get me wrong - but this just never suited my needs; so I turned to modded servers.
As of this review I have 1.3k+ hours, and <400 were spent on vanilla ARK. Finding an unofficial server to fit your needs won't take much time as long as you check the "server advertisement" area. There's a big issue with mods and ARK though, and that is that they're not quite... compatible yet. Is that the right word to use here? The reason I mention this is because ARK will make you sit your♥♥♥♥♥through a 10-20 minute loading screen on heavily modded servers. Heavily modded meaning ~20+ mods, assuming they have at least a few of the larger ones in there (such as the dino overhauls, i.e Annunaki, ARK Comes Alive, Extinction). I always considered this as a sacrifice for a much more enjoyable and fun playthrough.
The game itself is rather unoptimized even for beefier PCs. I've had the exact same PC specs since I started this game, and my FPS throughout the patches have been spotty, some days I'm at a constant 60, other days jumping between 40-60. As of right now, even on my mid-grade PC I can run mostly highs and a few mediums
If you buy this game, Google "ARK launch options" and profit with the extra 20-30 FPS.
This game can be fun on your own, but if you're not playing with friends the experience is a lot less amazing. So pack a friend or two and bring them along for the hunt.
Now, here's a my quick overview of the pros and cons to ARK.

Ark: Survival Evolved. This game has so much to offer and at the same time this game is not yet polished and done. I have around 400 hours on record with this game. When I have free time I spend it playing ark. The game is very rich in graphics and offers alot of cool stuff to craft while you level up. This game is all about earning it and learning how to craft one thing to the next. I also appreciate the dynamics of how the dinos halp you evolve into a more civilized player helping you gather wood, stone and thatch. ect. If I had to recommend this game, I most certainly would but only if you have friends to play it with, this game is not as fun unless you and your buddies are playing. Eveny time you log in, its like your alway on a mission to get some type of resource without dying, like oil or crystal.
What to consider as possible cons:
The game is still unpolished and lacks proper building aspects like how the game forces water pipes to only go in one direction or sloped ceilings cant be supported by a pillar. The building can be very backwards at times and really makes it hard build what you planned to. Another possible con is the taming of dinos, it can take hours to tame on dino if its a high level or a high tier species. Lastly PVP servers are the worst, plan on getting robbed everytime you create a little thatch house.
Updates ruining the game:
Yes, the updates have recently been rough on the servers making them very laggy and sometime unplayable but I feel this will be addressed in the next few updates and certainly wont contiue after official release. I really love this game and PVE makes it even better allowing you to actually build something and keep it!

Pros:
friendly and transparent developer. They actually actively communicate in forum and social medias and took ideas from time to time from their fanbase
high cuztomization option. Whether it's for cosmetics or upgrades the amount of options are high. Color pick, helmet, body skin, armor, weapon skin, warframe has plenty for you to use.
easy to get platinum (warframe premium currency). This is one of warframe main pros, you can go pretty far without actually paying anything in this game provided you actively trading with people. There're a lot of ways to get platinum in warframe, from trading mods, trading riven mods, selling syndicate mods and weaponry, selling relics, etc.
bunch of pve content. The whole solar system is your playground
growing plot. The plot thickens with almost every iteration of major update with several mindblowing moment here and there, which is awesome if you love sci-fi.
Cons:
No auction system. Every trade must be done manually with other players in dojo or maroo's bazaar on earth. So if you don't like to actively communicate with people, this can be a bummer. It's also pretty hard to gauge warframe prices without 3rd party website like
Luckluster pvp content. The power level between pve and pvp content is far too big. In pve everyone is invincible mass murderer while in pvp everyone is hyperactive spider impala who dies from pretty much anything, heck you can even be killed from someone jumping too close to you (bullet jump has damage, although it's small it can still kill you). This frailness forced every pvp player to basically parkouring like crazy. Very, very frustating and not fun at all, hence the difficulty to get a full team or even any player at all to play with unless there's a pvp event. Even so, some players will just afk in pvp event (you still get small event point even though you lose the game). There's also Lunaro, a football+dodgeball sport like game which actually can be fun if you can get anyone to play with.

Mixed:
balance is out of the window regarding loadout choice.There're gimmicky, weird to use weapons with so-so damage (javlok, drakgoon) and powerhouses, simple to use, yet very damaging weapons (soma prime, tigris family weaponry) but regarding warframe focus on pve content equipment choice is based more on individual preferences.
very easy to get to endgame. Basicaly it's very easy to create a broken build that can steamroll  almost all content of the starchart. Is the game fun?  You betcha!
Does it have issues?  Of course!
Its unoptimized, is prone to crashing and random variety of bugs.  At times laggy, poor performance, etc.
Though I will add, I myself have made NO upgrades to my machine recently but I have seen a DRAMATIC improvement in performance from ARK the past month or so.  I am an avid fan of the Annunaki Genesis mod, among others, which is very large and when combined with other equally sized mods, spelled for a very VERY long load time, even into single player which took so long on average it was not uncommon to be timed out of servers due to it.  However lately, it doesn't seem to matter how many mods I load, or how large said mods are.  I'm in game within 5-7 minutes tops.  I'm loving it~
In conjunction with this, I have virtually no lag anymore, and no FPS drops.  Even during the game's periodic saving (which used to cause lag).
I honestly don't understand all the negative reviews of late.  This game is great!  So much so that I plan to purchase it on the Xbox One as well soon!
If you're not the type of person who can deal with bugs, performance issues, potential wipes, and other things that come with an Early Access game, then I'd advice waiting for final release.  However if that's not a bother to you, then I really do urge you buy the game!  Its beyond addicting!  "Just 5 more minutes~" will become an hour before you know it.
10/10 Great game.  Worth the money!

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

So here's a game that had every reason to succeed and be great, but chose instead to simply be a mediocre time sink instead. The gameplay is solid, the graphics are great, combat is fluid and easy, crafting and grinding were bearable and even enjoyable. Here's where the problem lies though; there's no grand, or even small, incentive and nothing passed "press E to win" is ever explained properly.
At the start of the game you're introduced to a baddie who instantly gives you reason to play and a solid plot hook to latch onto with a multi-mission goal. It was a fantastic and promising start into a free mmo that needs to compete with my life for my attention and it was winning pretty well... Up until that quest was over, anyway.
After that quest the game dumps you into space with four different planets you can visit and three different enemy factions you can fight against, but it gives you zero explanation as to who any of them are or why you keep invading their territory to wreck their stuff. The missions you carry out have no overall effect on their hold on the planets, only serving to be the way that you collect materials to find your crafting projects.
This is a fatal flaw, in my opinion, as I'm not interested in a senseless slaughter/grind fest that lacks even a weak long term goal. I don't want to spend hours or even minutes killing the same ten enemy models when I don't even know what my own faction is. We don't play as humans, and if we do then it's never stated. There literally no personal investment that this game can offer unless you REALLY like being a mysterious humanoid space ninja, who works for a mysterious humanoid figure, whom you never meet in person, to kill swaths of other humanoids just so you can build yourself a new hat.
Tl;dr: Fun gameplay, but definitely not worth more than a week of time unless you really liked Ragnarok Online.

I have been playing Warframe for over 200 hours since Beta/ release date. TL:DR Warframe is a fun and addicting game but loses its luster after a certain period of time due to lack limited gameplay. Warframe gets a 7/10.
Pros - 1) ( Spectacular ) Visually. From the robot-like ninja Tenno to the ornate Oroking Void design/ architecture to the vast biomes and empty desolate space, Warframe nails the Sci-Fi look. The environments are ( almost )completely immersive. 2) ( Unique ) Gameplay. Since you play as space ninjas, you move as such. Various parkour movement that works, flying in space with "jackpacks", congregating with other players to defeat bosses, collecting rare loot, hanging out with your clan mates in the clan's dojo, or even surviving hordes of malformed zombie-like creatures. It's a story/ lore influenced Third Person shooter with aspects of RTS and MMORPGs. 3) Community. By far Warframe has one of the best communities, ever. I'm a person that plays games such as CS:GO, League of legends, and Dota 2. I was amazed at how nice and helpful people are in this community. 4) Customization. In a lot of games, apart from weapon customization, there are not many things to change. In Warframe, you can customize everything from Warframe and weapons, to what specific color for each individual section upon your warframe/ weapon, VARIOUS ( hundreds ) mods and mod combinations for Warframes and weapons. What is a Mod? A Mod is an item that can be applied to your Warframe or weapon that will enhance its abilities in various ways. Wanna inflict a Poison DoT to enemies hit by your bullets? We got it. Wanna give a HP Regen to your allies? We got it. Wanna make your explosive projectiles split into multiple bullets for a multiple explosions and more damage? We got it! Wanna make your arrows pierce enemies allow collateral hits or even explode, we got it.
Cons - 1) It can be a bit pricey. Depending on the person you are, you will either be spending no money or a lot. One aspect it borrows from MMORPG games is the grind. Yes, believe it or not, this third person shooter will make you grind, a hell of a lot. You get a blueprint for a weapon, you grind the materials, and you craft the item which will usually take a few mins to a few days depending on item rarity. But of course, being a Free to Play game, microtransactions is DE's income. Don't wanna grind 4 hours of your life away to get materials for Prime weapon? No worries! give us 5$ and we will feed your pocrastination. Don't wanna wait 24 hours for it? Patience is a virtue? Nonsense, give us five more dollars and you can have it now! with a side of regret. Literally ( almost ) everything in this game has a time limit or has to be grinded for. One of the biggets downsides to this game. Out of the 224 hours i've played, I'd say 75% of it is grinding. 2) Replayability. I do not know if its true, but I heard rumors that Digital Extremes performs Witchcraft. 6 months is the life expectancy of Warframe players because they die for a few weeks/ months and then magically resurrected. Apart from necromancy, DE has the ability to control the minds of players and spend their money. It is truly an addicting game for a short period of time at which you realize after grinding the same mission killing the same chopped and reskined mobs on similar maps within the limited game modes that you realize you spent way too much money and you just lost a lot of your life.
Reasons to buy - Looks nice, plays nice
Reasons not to buy - Boring after a while, grind, grind, limited modes/ content, grind

First of all, let me just say that ARK is really, really fun to play especially if you have a group of friends to play it with you.  The devs release new dinos and world items on a regular basis so there's a lot to see and do.  There is also an active modding community which adds even more content to an already sizable game.
That said, the constant content updates and lack of optimization has made this game incredibly bloated.  I actually had to un-install it because it was consuming so much of my harddrive space.  At one point it had ballooned into 70+ GB and was **still** recieving more and more updates almost on a weekly basis.   There have been numerous complaints about the lack of optimization, but the devs seem more interested in releasing more and more dinosaurs to an already massively overpopulated map (which is, by the way, not very large so overpopulation and over-building is a very real issue on PVE-only servers).   And due to the lack of optimization, server lag is another major issue.
All in all, for a game that is still in early release (and has been for over 2 years) ARK is a great game with a lot of potential.  Unfortunately, due to the issues I stated above, I cannot recommend it at this point in time.

Personally i have 6GB RAM and a 2.7GH CPU and i can run this on Ultra with not even a spike in FPS.

I really would have liked this game. I love the Building and Survival genres. However, this game has many issues that need to be resolved before I could ever enjoy, or recommend it. I am especially displeased that after almost 2 years, none of these things have been addressed:
1. WARNING: This game is heavily stacked against the solo player:
a. The player spawn near high level dinosaurs all of the time. There is not any regulator in the programing in that regard like other games in this genre.
b. Those same high level dinosaurs can, and will, instantly spawn on top of the player. Again, unlike other games of this genre, this one does nothing to regulate distance or levels of spawning NPCs
I have played this thing over 95 hrs, several times and cannot survive solo, or teamed with my daughter, for more than 5 minutes. I think level 22 is the highest I have ever gotten, and that was on a private server. Join a tribe ASAP. You can go solo once you have leveled up quite a bit. All of the servers are pretty heavily used, so finding low level dinos is very rare. Even the private server is pretty heavily stacked against the solo player, but that is where I managed to survive the longest.
2. The player will suffer from hunger very quickly and it takes an insane amount of berries to fill him/her. Then, there is a time delay between eating and getting full which can cause insane problems.
3. There are bugs in the chase perameters of the dinos:
a. Sometimes, the dino will not stop chasing. I have died so many times starting out completely full of energy and running out while being chased.
b. I have had land based and air dinos kill me in deep water, where they are not supposed to be able to go. I have also had a Megoladon kill me in very shallow water.
4. I love the fact that the designers want this game to be as life like as possible, but I think the mapping system sucks. I could never figure it out. It does not have a marker showing you where you are. You have to look around and guesstimate. The problem I found, Everything looks the same, and the land masses are not clearly defined. I built several homes, but would never be able to find my way back to them.
5. I run a top of the line system with the best video cards, and I have trouble seeing other players around me unless we are right near each other. This is especially true on the public server. My system includes an AMD M3 5.2GHz gaming processor, 62 GB DDR3 3300 RAM, two NVIDIA 770GTX 2GB video cards interbussed. Just so you know, there is a difference in the graphics of this game between using Linux and Windows. I have tried it on both. It runs better on Linux, but the graphics are better through Windows, and had the same issue using both operating systems.
6.This game is VERY realistic, but like I said, it is heavily stacked against the solo player and seems to be built only for team play. If you are looking for something as good as and realistic as ARK, but is also geared for the solo player as well as team play, I suggest Out of Reach. It does not have dinos, but it does have elephants, rhinos, tigers, and many other African beasts and more. Plus, there are caves and other fun things, and a map that is very easy. Plus, the NPCs always spawn a certain distance from the player, and the chase will ALWAYS end at a certain range. The player always spawns on the beach, just like here, and true to nature, there are smaller animals near the spawn point (not many), and the bigger stuff is not far away either, so be careful.
For solo play, ARK gets two thumbs down. For team play, I will give it one thumb up.
Good luck and have fun. :)

Just want to add a bit about current pvp.
Basically the best way to describe the pvp in Ark is to compare it to a mobile 'turret defence' style game, or clash of clans kind of thing with a few exceptions.
First rather than build a base for yourself you build a base for you tribe and everyone in the tribe can contribute, the more people in tribe the better and faster you can build your base. The goal of course is so that when the other tribe chooses your base to attack it will repel the invaders while sustaining minimal damage.
Secondly when it comes to attacking, rather than have a limited time to complete the attack and limited resources, the invaders can bring to the battle as much as they want and spend as much time on the attack as they want, again the more people that participate the more damage they can do.
Now here is the kicker, unlike those defence games where after the attack ends you lose some resources and your base gets restored for the next attack, in Ark you lose everything and have to start over.
Basically, the biggest tribe always wins and the attacker always has the advantage, because a defender can't withdraw to get more bullets or repair damage, they can only wait for destruction,
Also because of the horrible pet ai in this game, almost everyone has to keep their dinos passive because if a dino runs off it will most likely become lost, dissappear into limbo, get killed by any stray wild dino, glitch out or whatever and the devs dont do anything about it.

I love this game, and I hate that I love it.
*Before reading on, I would like to point out that I play on privately run, and/or non-dedicated servers because I prefer not to PvP, therefore my review will exclude a large portion of PvP related information due to my lack of involvement with that aspect of the game.
Pros:
I adore the effort put into making this game immersive. There are so many facets of depth put into it and they're all fully customizable to give each player the unique experience that they're looking for.
From starvation, to climate, to breeding dinosaurs and crafting shelters to endure the elements, this is one of the most well planned survival based games I've played.
Each dino has a specific forte and utilization. I learn new things about each species every time I play.
Many methods of taming dinos and building bases are easier with multiple people, which encourages teamwork and communication.
This one's a gimme, but who doesn't love Dinosaurs? I mean come on.
New content is being released pretty regularly, as well as holiday events. This includes new weapons, new dinosaurs, new items, and new mechanics. (I just discovered that Tapejaras can cling to vertical surfaces and it's amazing)
Cons:
The game has its bugs, as most underfunded games do. There are a wide range of unfortunate glitches that the game would benefit from having fleshed out. None of these glitches have made the experience unbearable in my opinion. They have simply inconvenienced me. Problems include; Wild dinos getting stuck in/on objects, Dinos escaping pens/vanishing on wander mode, Dinos inexplicably dying, juvenile dinos starving in a matter of seconds, dinos refusing to eat a second time after beginning a tame and starving to death, dinos spawning in built structures, Grown crops visually glitching, and many others that I haven't encountered I'm sure.
Load times are rough when connecting to, or especially when booting up a server, and it doesn't help that the loading screen effect drops your FPS to 15 or less due to poor execution and rendering. (It's a similar fog/smoke effect to that of skyrims loading sequence)

Honestly, there is little I don't like about this game other than I wish Platinum (in-game currency) was a little cheaper.
Other than that, this game is easy enough to pick up and play, while at the same time, offers challenges to those with experience. The Mod system allows you to customize each warframe, weapon, and companion as you see fit. Warframe is a beauty to behold and the unique movement style of the Tenno (in-game space ninjas) leaves little to be desired.
Digital Extremes comes out with new content, buildable weapons, warframes and other such goodies as a decent pace, so you're rarily, if ever, idle. Just a great game all around.
The resource gathering may cause autism with extended exposure... But all in all great game.

I originally posted a jokey review back in 2015, but I figure I'm probably due for a proper one by now, since this game will probably be my most-played game on steam before much longer, surpassing TF2.
As a Founder (playing since Beta) I can say that after almost 780 hours (as of writing this review), while the game has started to get stale, I still very much think it is a fantastic game.
Is Warframe perfect? Far from it. Is Warframe *bad*? Most definitely not, by any stretch of the word. Warframe is a very good game that suffers from the usual free-to-play case of development hell, but that also results in new content (even if it's in small patches and teasers) coming out regularly, with large content patches every 6 months to a year. The devs have some amount of knowledge of what the community wants and are trying to constantly update the game to fit their own vision as well, meaning that there's commonly *something* new to try out. If you're just starting out there's a lot to do and see, a lot of warframes to get and mess around with, and a lot of challenges to overcome. Returning players won't have as much, but still at least a decent bit to see new every month.

I originally posted a jokey review back in 2015, but I figure I'm probably due for a proper one by now, since this game will probably be my most-played game on steam before much longer, surpassing TF2.
As a Founder (playing since Beta) I can say that after almost 780 hours (as of writing this review), while the game has started to get stale, I still very much think it is a fantastic game.
Is Warframe perfect? Far from it. Is Warframe *bad*? Most definitely not, by any stretch of the word. Warframe is a very good game that suffers from the usual free-to-play case of development hell, but that also results in new content (even if it's in small patches and teasers) coming out regularly, with large content patches every 6 months to a year. The devs have some amount of knowledge of what the community wants and are trying to constantly update the game to fit their own vision as well, meaning that there's commonly *something* new to try out. If you're just starting out there's a lot to do and see, a lot of warframes to get and mess around with, and a lot of challenges to overcome. Returning players won't have as much, but still at least a decent bit to see new every month.

That being said it's an early access game and as such suffers from network lag issues, poor graphics optimization, frequent crashes (especially w/ mods). I found this to be something I could deal with at first; however it's been around for some time now & the developers seem only interested in adding in-game content rather than to do some badly needed polishing on the game itself. Also adding a purchaseable DLC for an early access game which remains so unpolished is an incredibly sketchy move. As of currently I would not recommend purchasing this game as it feels its development hasn't been heading in the right direction for some time and there is no reason to believe that will be changing any time soon.
Despite that the game has enormous potential and can quickly become very addictive. If it were optimized and didn't suffer from its long-standing bugs it would no doubt be one of the most enjoyable games on the market. If new updates improved the stability of the game instead of making it worse I could deal with it. But I can't. It actually makes me sad to watch what's happening to it.

Been playing this game since it came out on steam almost three years ago, I have around 500 hours in it and my conclusion about this game. IT IS ONE OF THE BEST ACTION GAMES EVER MADE!!!
Here are the pros and cons
Pros
+ Free to play, but with pay to progress in it(buy stuff instead of farming it).
+ Awesome gameplay.
+ Continuously updated with new content and rebalancing of current gameplay with something better.
+ Very deep, but easily understood lore.
+ Great mechanics.
+ Awesome graphics.
+ Once you get the hang of it, it is easy to play.
+ So high diversity there is something for almost everyone in this game.
+ Massive replayability.
+ Can give you some of the best time with you and your friends.
+ One of the best communities out there.
+ The Mastery-rank system prevents pay to win.
+ This game rewards you with small prizes for playing daily.
Cons
- VERY HEAVY Grinding and farming. This can get frustrating sometimes.
- Steep learning curve for new players. But not as steep as some other games like Dota 2 or Starcraft.
- Some balancing issues. Mostly composed that alot of the new content is to difficult to aquire or not good enough to use. However the DE does listen to their community and rebalance things.
- Sometimes it can get a little repetative, but you can counter this mostly by using different gear and characters.
- The mastery-rank takes too much time to level up ones you get past level 5
Conclusion
One of the ABSOLUTE BEST GAMES I HAVE EVER PLAYED!!!!!
If you like action games and can fight the early learning curve you are going to have a GREAT time with this game.

Warframe is a 3rd person co-op shooter that's somewhat also hack n slash. At the time of this review, I've got slightly over 300 hours into the game and I've spent $0. My thoughts:
-It's free
-It's very diverse, with the amount of primaries, secondaries, melees, warframes, companies, and mods for all of those, as well as level design, planets, and mission types
-Everything can be done solo and co-op
-Art is great
-Updates, tons of updates
-Various events, like alerts
-Not just about running & gunning, stealth is completely possible, and rewarded
-Not pay to win, as every core aspect to the game can be earned without spending money, and even the cosmetic stuff as well.(It is, however, difficult, as you've got to trade with people. It takes time, lots of time, but it's an option.)
-Devs are active
-Grindy
-RNG reliant
-Lore could use some work(This is, however, being expanded upon continuously, through timed events, quests, and updates)
The big thing for me is the amount of diversity provided with the "class" system of warframes, and you can get all of the warframes and switch to them at any moment you're not in a mission, and the mods. To me, these, and the diversity in primary and secondary firearms and melee weapons is the biggest selling point to warframe. It's not a plain old run and gun shooter, it's got more diversity and depth to it than that. Yes, there's a lot of running and gunning, but it's more interesting because of this system. You also don't even need to run and gun, but can try to use stealth, and you'll be rewarded by not setting off any alarms. Oh, and you can craft just about everything.
The maps and level diversity are incredible. There're 14 different planets, all with unique environments. And all of them are locations in the solar system, and the mission names of all the planets are also named after real life locations. The design of the missions is great as well, and everything overall just looks wonderful. There're, going from the wiki, 16 different missions types for PVE, and for some, you don't just do them while on foot. Some missions have you using the archwing, a sort of addon to your warframe that allows you to travel through space and in the depths of the ocean.(Yes, it's free. Your first archwing is earned in a quest) There're also two extra sets of locations, not just the planets: The void and the orokin derelict. You need keys to get in those, which you acquire in game. And you get sweet loot from them too. Everything can be done solo and co-op, but co-op is recommended.
The problems this game has, though, are pretty obvious. It's pretty grindy and RNG reliant. Want to get a specific blueprint or crafting item? Have fun running through the same level over and over again til you get it. Needs resources to craft? Farming Simulator 2015. It can get pretty annoying to grind out resources and other things for crafting, but grinding is kind of relative to the person. Some people like grinds, some people don't think it's grindy, and some think grinding is awful and omnipresent. It's a personal thing. For me, I'm sometimes okay with it, it usually depends on what I need to get, how much of it I need, and where do find it. For many as well, the lack of lore is kind of disappointing. The current lore isn't completely built up yet, and there's lots of room for expansion and explanation. The lack of lore, however, is being fixed. With more updates, quests, and events, lore is getting built. It's not exactly coherent yet, but it's a work in progress, and I believe that once it's more coherent and tangible, it'll be good lore. There's lots of potential in this department.
Overall, I think the game is great. For the low low price of free, you get tons of content and diversity. You're a ninja in space. Literally. It's super fun to use all the mobility tricks, run around with the different warframes, and play through the different missions. It's even better with friends, so you can kickstart the co-op and start beating up bosses. Yes, the grind and RNG is present, and annoying, but if you're okay with that sorta thing, or fine with just not grinding for things, and just playing the game, it's amazing. 9/10 to DE, they've done a great job, and I hope to see it grow into something even beter.
Oh, and there're robo chickens with sticks. What's not to love about robo chickens with sticks?

ok i started this game a little after it came out and have been off and on since but might i just say how UTTERLY BADASS this game is. i have seen this game evolve from its early scary as♥♥♥♥♥♥♥beginings to what it is today. lets just start the actual details of this game.
#1 I absolutly love the idea. It's simple, fun, and the best mashup since robot dinosaurs. When i recomend this to my friends all i have to say is "space ninjas" and they are in.
#2 The gameplay... Oh my god the gameplay, when the devs say they will give you ninjas, THEY MEAN IT. whether your running through air vents or running on walls you get an amazing feeling of how each step you take is'nt some basic run that any genaric game can throw in but instead You feel like your really the one in control here.
#3  The Community, take your basic MMO with all those selfish ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s and loot gremlins, then make the exact opposite because everyone and their mother is willing to help you out with whatever the issue. If you think im exadurating I asked on the recruitment channel "hey is anyone willing to help me with a mission." ... i got (and i counted) 39 people who almost immedeatly responded asking what i needed help with. and after 2 years of playing i have yet to find a troll who I wasn't on good terms with within the course of one mission (about 5-10 min)
#4 the seperation of chat windows... many MMO's do this but usually it just ends up with a bunch of text thrown all over the place. Warframe seperates chat really well because if you put something in the wrong channel it will usually tell you to go to the right channel and delete your text. same goes if you like to CAPS SPAM.
#5 Everything is free, if your willing to earn it... As one of the devs said in an interveiw, there really arn't any "buy walls" leaving the game completely accessible to the poorer gamers (me) even better most of the best equipment isn't up for real currency sale. sure you can go to the trade chat and buy prime weapon parts but they're still gonna be like twice the price of any warframe you find.
#6 co-op is the absolute BEST... this game wasn't made with the intention of having pvp as the only way to play... in fact they didn't intend to have pvp at all (dueling rooms excluded). that was a much later thing when (i can only assume) people wanted to start killing eachother and begged the devs to make it so
Now to the problems
No game is perfect and Warframe is no Exeption
#1 Foundry times... remember how i told you about earning things, well this is how. First you have to get the material, which usually means grinding the same level on the same planet. I accually found a lot of fun in this but i'll get into that later. then you have to build your item from a blueprint you either bought from the in game currency market or you found on your travels. when you build the item it will take a good 6-72 hrs depending on what ur building (talking about weapons and warframes only. most keys take 1min to 6hrs). this can be a massive pain in the♥♥♥♥♥but it definatly beats that extra $5 you would have to shell out otherwise.
#2 the levels... Warframe has an ...interesting... level system. so you have to get kills and gain 'affinity' or xp to the common gamer. this 'affinity' goes to the weapons you have, which wouldnt be that bad if you had to level up your weapons a bunch of times just to get actual levels towards your profile. yah you pretty much gotta get 4-5 weapons to their maximum rank just to get to your next profile rank.
#3  the profile ranks... these are more or less useless after rank 8 because all they do for you is give you the ability to unlock the ability to get new weapons.. there is one other reason but i find it stupid and pointless so i'm leaving it out.
#4 missions... i can't really complain about these but i have had others get angry about it so i might as well add this. the missions themselves are fine you go in do your objective maybe loot around a bit and leave. that is fine, it's a formula that works just fine no problems here. what i have heard become a problem is the randomly generated maps. Warframe gives a randomly generated map using a multitude of miniature maps called "Tile Sets" these "Tile Sets" are then scattered and thrown together to make an area. once you play enough times on one planet or setting you begin to  memorize the tile sets and the map begins to look the same.
Even thogh there are issues the game is amazing and the issues i find fun acctually... the grinding can seem tedius at times but when your in a group of friends or fun people if feels like nothing at all. the leveling system can be annoying but it forces you to have fun trying new things. the profile ranks add to the trying of new things so you can unlock whatever it is that you want, and i've already said i have no problems with the tile sets because its just a mark of the place you are in. when you make a dojo with your clan you actually choose from tile sets but that doesn't make your dojo any less uniqe or fun to build. i would highly recomend getting this game if any of these reasons appeal to you.. and if you don't see anything you like, try it anyway, it's not like it costs money. welp that what i think anyways, i have racked up quite a number of hours and i'll be damned if i don't rack up more

One of the better survival sandbox games there are, if not the best.
Frustrating at times, this game offers a huge array of challenges to overcome in solo or group situations. This game will take up a huge chunk of your time should you choose to play it however, as dinosaur taming can take hours upon hours upon hours to do for some of the weakest ones.
The time sink alone is enough to deter a lot of people, and I myself have not even attempted to play on a vanilla server just for the fact that taming certain dino's can take days.
The environments are really well done but the worlds themselves are small. If given access to flying mounts you can traverse the entirety of any map in almost no time, but restrict it to land only mounts and it makes every trip into a journey to get anywhere.
Crafting is simple and easy to grasp and for the most part, player made weapons are a joke unless they are being used to tame. Melee weapons can do some pretty hefty damage, but you have to have flak armor and over 300 health to be able to take out a low level raptor. Guns can do a good amount of damage but run out of durability really fast and take a lot of resources to craft to be of any use and only increase your ability to kill low tier dino's.
The game itself updates pretty regularly and has a ton of things to do, but the endgame is relegated to killing raid bosses for useless trophies and breeding dinosaurs to more powerful breeds, of which there is a finite cap as to how strong your dinosaurs can ultimately be even through breeding.
Still, the game is great and worth the full price, although I'd wait to purchase any additional content until it comes on sale as there isn't a whole lot given for the price.

Aaargh, where to begin? Warframe looks great, it really does. I persisted with it on my first time around mainly because of that. But, coming back for a second time, I find the same problems I had to begin with: This is a parkour game. That is, it is about very elaborate ways of moving about the game-space, This means perfecting multi-key-strokes - down to the fraction of a second. If you are not willing/able to master the skills of hitting exactly the right key-combos, in exactly the right order, very very rapidly, you will not be able to move around in this game. And if you can't move around, any other skills you may have are irrelevant. The re-launch of the game involves even more elaborate manoeuvres. I gave up on the third one, because it's not enough knowing what to press, you need to know when, where and why. After about 20 attempts, I'd stopped caring.
I don't know if the game retains it's additional levleling-barrier: Originally. this meant that in order to level-up - and gain access to more content - you had to pass a combat test very much more difficult than any of the missions of your level. I tried this several times and always failed - albeit narrowly.
This is a game tailor-made to allow it's alpha/beta testers to lord it over new-comers. With the result that there is no reason at all for anyone else to bother with it. A shame, as I said, it looks great.

Now that I've spent a lot of time in this game I can fairly say that it's fun. It's a rare experience and there is a lot of new things to explore. I have been playing it for awhile and have seen several of the updates that added both good and bad things to the game. If it goes on sale I'd recommend it but that doesn't mean it's not worth $30+. For the time you can spend in it and the freedom you have there isn't a whole lot of other games that will look as good as ARK does.
With that being said, I don't recommend it because the community quite honestly sucks. Most servers have alpha tribes which essentially means they have been there since the beginning or they have nothing but time to play games in their life. Most alpha tribes will straight out brag about their time that they have spent playing it, as if spending over a thousand hours means anything right? Truth is, the reason why many people hit these numbers are not because they are building up a huge base and that they have constructed a really cool area in the game. You spend over a thousand hours playing the game when you are trying to build up to tame something new or to build something new and then alpha tribes just knock you back down to wood houses. Which wood is a very low level in this game. So assuming that you play on a PVP server, some dinos take upwards of 12hrs+ to tame unless you have kibble which tames much faster. The problem is that alpha tribes, most of them are aggressive and will attack you during or after you have tamed something. My friends and I would spend up to 5-6hrs taming something with berries because kibble is only possible if you find a nice alpha tribe, otherwise they'll kill your base before you make any.
So ARK isn't recommended because to truly enjoy it you have to spend hours and hours and deal with a toxic community on most servers. Now, PVE servers aren't that much better as people claim land with pillars, even if they have nothing else on the land but pillars because they want to control large areas. You can't destroy the pillars on PVE which brings us to why PVP is the only real option since it lets you destroy pillars. ARK simply isn't made for those of us who have jobs or don't have the time to spend on the game constantly. I had that opportunity but to build anything it would take hours to collect the resources. I can honestly say that at least 1/3 to half my hrs were spent idling away from the computer as I waited for caves to respawn or I was taming something and checking back every 5-10minutes or so. The game in my opinion, just simply isn't worth the time or the mostly toxic community. I also hosted my own server which sadly is the only place where I was able to build up and actually play the game beyond getting destroyed daily/weekly or surpressed by alpha tribe rules (example: can't tame larger dinos or some won't let you tame frogs or sabers for chitin/CP). The developers also support this kind of behaviour because they release harder dinos and higher tech which again only an alpha tribe has the freedom to get. So the developers constantly make it harder to maintain a lower base while always increasing an alpha tribe's power. It's an awful balance. As for official servers, they also suck as there is a lot of rubber banding which has nothing to do with my internet connection. Hosting your own dedicated server will eliminate most of this even on some servers that are highly populated, but official servers can't handle much more beyond 20 players without lag getting inreasingly worse. The game is also not optimized and it gets worse each time they add more content. I understand some game developers choose this approach but for ARK who released an expansion before release of the actual game, they should have optimized it.

I learned how to hide gear, dinos and a whole bunch of other things but again this game is unreasonable by the amount of time it takes to enjoy it at the moment.
