Warframe is a 3rd person co-op shooter that's somewhat also hack n slash. At the time of this review, I've got slightly over 300 hours into the game and I've spent $0. My thoughts:
-It's free
-It's very diverse, with the amount of primaries, secondaries, melees, warframes, companies, and mods for all of those, as well as level design, planets, and mission types
-Everything can be done solo and co-op
-Art is great
-Updates, tons of updates
-Various events, like alerts
-Not just about running & gunning, stealth is completely possible, and rewarded
-Not pay to win, as every core aspect to the game can be earned without spending money, and even the cosmetic stuff as well.(It is, however, difficult, as you've got to trade with people. It takes time, lots of time, but it's an option.)
-Devs are active
-Grindy
-RNG reliant
-Lore could use some work(This is, however, being expanded upon continuously, through timed events, quests, and updates)
The big thing for me is the amount of diversity provided with the "class" system of warframes, and you can get all of the warframes and switch to them at any moment you're not in a mission, and the mods. To me, these, and the diversity in primary and secondary firearms and melee weapons is the biggest selling point to warframe. It's not a plain old run and gun shooter, it's got more diversity and depth to it than that. Yes, there's a lot of running and gunning, but it's more interesting because of this system. You also don't even need to run and gun, but can try to use stealth, and you'll be rewarded by not setting off any alarms. Oh, and you can craft just about everything.
The maps and level diversity are incredible. There're 14 different planets, all with unique environments. And all of them are locations in the solar system, and the mission names of all the planets are also named after real life locations. The design of the missions is great as well, and everything overall just looks wonderful. There're, going from the wiki, 16 different missions types for PVE, and for some, you don't just do them while on foot. Some missions have you using the archwing, a sort of addon to your warframe that allows you to travel through space and in the depths of the ocean.(Yes, it's free. Your first archwing is earned in a quest) There're also two extra sets of locations, not just the planets: The void and the orokin derelict. You need keys to get in those, which you acquire in game. And you get sweet loot from them too. Everything can be done solo and co-op, but co-op is recommended.
The problems this game has, though, are pretty obvious. It's pretty grindy and RNG reliant. Want to get a specific blueprint or crafting item? Have fun running through the same level over and over again til you get it. Needs resources to craft? Farming Simulator 2015. It can get pretty annoying to grind out resources and other things for crafting, but grinding is kind of relative to the person. Some people like grinds, some people don't think it's grindy, and some think grinding is awful and omnipresent. It's a personal thing. For me, I'm sometimes okay with it, it usually depends on what I need to get, how much of it I need, and where do find it. For many as well, the lack of lore is kind of disappointing. The current lore isn't completely built up yet, and there's lots of room for expansion and explanation. The lack of lore, however, is being fixed. With more updates, quests, and events, lore is getting built. It's not exactly coherent yet, but it's a work in progress, and I believe that once it's more coherent and tangible, it'll be good lore. There's lots of potential in this department.
Overall, I think the game is great. For the low low price of free, you get tons of content and diversity. You're a ninja in space. Literally. It's super fun to use all the mobility tricks, run around with the different warframes, and play through the different missions. It's even better with friends, so you can kickstart the co-op and start beating up bosses. Yes, the grind and RNG is present, and annoying, but if you're okay with that sorta thing, or fine with just not grinding for things, and just playing the game, it's amazing. 9/10 to DE, they've done a great job, and I hope to see it grow into something even beter.
Oh, and there're robo chickens with sticks. What's not to love about robo chickens with sticks?

Gameplay: Warframe’s gameplay is simple, but very fast-paced. It mainly revolves around your type of Warframe taking the place of your “class.” Every Warframe is unique in their own way and has four abilities that suit their style. Excalibur, the ninja, has moves based on his sword, for instance 1 is a sword dash, 2 is a blind attack, 3 is an AoE blast and 4 is a supercharged sword for as long as you have energy to keep it running. Overall it is a speedy, close range killer.
The movement and parkhour system is of a major help in getting around in the game as it offers many ways to climb up a high area like the bullet jump and the wall jumping. Instead of walking up every individual floor of a theoretical parking garage, you can jump onto the wall, look up and hold spacebar and jump up the wall until you reach the top.
The accessibility in Warframe is perfect. Every single frame, weapon, archwing, etc. are all accessible by just playing the game rather than being locked behind a paywall. The only thing you’ll ever need to spend real life money on would be if you wanted to unlock more appearance customization.
The simplicity is also a downfall in my opinion as sometimes it feels repetitive. One example would be the melee combat, it feels like all you have to do is spam E until there’s no living enemies near you; and a lot of the game is repeating the same missions over and over again to grind for resources.
Gameplay: 8.2
Graphics: Warframe’s graphics are actually impressive, especially considering how old the game is. Most people say it looks like Destiny graphics-wise, which has some truth to it. The character models are some of the best I’ve seen in a game and the effects can be downright mesmerizing at times.
Graphics: 9
Sounds: The sounds in Warframe are about what you’d expect for a science fiction space shooter, usually all I can hear is gunshots and explosions but when things are calm the ambient sound is rather nice and feels fitting for the environment. So far I haven’t heard any sounds copied off of other games so I’d assume they’re all original. As for the music I never get to hear it really, as it’s always drowned out by everything else.
Sound: 7
Challenge: The challenge of this game is hard to really get an idea of how to explain it. It starts off with a good enough challenge to keep you truly interested in the game, but once you’ve reached all of the max level gear even the higher levels feel easy.
Challenge: 7
Fun: As for the fun factor, Warframe gives a lot of fast-paced action that isn’t locked behind a paywall so from there it is rather fun when you have a group of friends to play with. Trying to solo queue is a pain, and a lot of it feels like a grind to get the next blueprint or the next stash of plastids. The game could do with a randomizer in my opinion, or even just more missions that don’t give specific loot so people don’t play that same one over and over again.
Fun: 8
Overall: 8.4

Let me start off by saying that this game has truly hit the nail on the head of what a survival game should look like from my perspective. This game has beautiful scenery, a well delivered crafting system, and offers massive potential for growth into something much greater than it already is. That being said, there is one fatal flaw that I think may turn many away. It does not seem to be optimized yet at all on any platform, and has very bad stutter occasionally while playing. I have noticed it seems to get worse with the more objects you have placed on the map, but I would assume that is kind of a given. One smaller, yet still prominent flaw are a few spelling mistakes still scattered around the game. Some loading screens feature blatant typo's, as well as some of the in-game messages.
All things being said, I'd give it a 5/7, with wiggle room to move up to 6 or maybe 7 in the future
Bonus points because the devs work nonstop on releasing patches for this game, although they could be a little more directed to problem solving in the base game before even thinking about expansions. Just my two cents :) Definitely worth the buy IMO because it is one of those things that will only get better as time goes on.

after 2 years if not more of playing it, whats still my take? if your a fan of games that require heavy grinding, and love the repetition of the missions and how you grind and what you grind, and the exp farming and MR Grinding....weapon forging, and re forging, then this is for you. most certainly.

as ive said, quite simply, its "Labour intensive" now ofc at this point u will no doubt say in response "this games not for you" or "you lack the patience" or "the game offers alot if your willing to work for it, sounds to me like you just got lazy and gave up".
Well, your point is duely noted in that case, if only it was so simple. (also note my in game hours ;D )
I left the game recently, shortly after the Chains of harrow. i had been playing on and off for some time before then. my dislike of  the labour intensive grind and not least of all the monotinous reapitition of everything you do in the game in the end killed any will i had to play on. the game is always forcing you to grind for this, and get that. there is never any feeling of staying in one place, or freedom as such. because you always WILL need something. over 2 years it became more of a day job then a game thats getting you chill.
Farming has also become much more demanding in warframes current state to what it was when i started playing. they added more resorces and stuff that you had to get, for example, like kuva for your riven mods and rare resources like nitain extracts, which you can only obtain from alerts throughout the day. you where always forced to do a sortie each day for the rivens.
Then theres the relic farming thats needed before you actually start farming for prime parts, which are already by this point rare and grind intensive enough without the added fun of relics to be farmed for before hand. bck when i started playing you only needed to farm for the prime parts from the correct maps and rotations and tho still relying on merciful RNG you could get what u wanted aventually.
i found the relics only made this painful.(your probely thinking the same of my review by now)  iam not talking about hard grinding as such, the feeling of hoplessness as you try for your 20th attempt...no, iam talking about actual mental pain as you get the wrong relic u dont want after your 20th attempt with the charming knowledge that you then have to do it all over agian for a part. Every time a new prime comes to town. And waste Void traces every time you fail.
This is just covering a very unbelivably small part of this games "Preferenced" and "Opinionated" mechanics, which contributed and in the end ammounted too my leaving the game for the present. there are other problems that others in the reviews have stated. i would urge you to read them, and get a full picture of what your in for long term esspecially.

and Happy gamming whatever choice you make. and good luck.....may the RNGforce be with yall.

Been playing this game since it came out on steam almost three years ago, I have around 500 hours in it and my conclusion about this game. IT IS ONE OF THE BEST ACTION GAMES EVER MADE!!!
Here are the pros and cons
Pros
+ Free to play, but with pay to progress in it(buy stuff instead of farming it).
+ Awesome gameplay.
+ Continuously updated with new content and rebalancing of current gameplay with something better.
+ Very deep, but easily understood lore.
+ Great mechanics.
+ Awesome graphics.
+ Once you get the hang of it, it is easy to play.
+ So high diversity there is something for almost everyone in this game.
+ Massive replayability.
+ Can give you some of the best time with you and your friends.
+ One of the best communities out there.
+ The Mastery-rank system prevents pay to win.
+ This game rewards you with small prizes for playing daily.
Cons
- VERY HEAVY Grinding and farming. This can get frustrating sometimes.
- Steep learning curve for new players. But not as steep as some other games like Dota 2 or Starcraft.
- Some balancing issues. Mostly composed that alot of the new content is to difficult to aquire or not good enough to use. However the DE does listen to their community and rebalance things.
- Sometimes it can get a little repetative, but you can counter this mostly by using different gear and characters.
- The mastery-rank takes too much time to level up ones you get past level 5
Conclusion
One of the ABSOLUTE BEST GAMES I HAVE EVER PLAYED!!!!!
If you like action games and can fight the early learning curve you are going to have a GREAT time with this game.

This game is amazing.
DISCLAIMER: To start out i will say that there are PVE servers, but a very large portion of the game becomes either completely useless or completely unuseable when you opt fo a non-PVP server. So I will stricly be talking about playing on a official PVP server.
THE GOOD: I have by far had the most fun I've ever had in a video game here. If you can find a good server to live on, the experience is like no other. Suriving is no joke in this game, even at the end game you can still get wrecked by a low lvl dino if you don't come prepared. Battling, gathering, and stuggling to survive alongside some random people you met in the game is pure joy. I've made numerous friendships that I'm sure will last for many years to come.
THE BAD: This game is truely and brutally unforgiving. If you stop paying attention to a taming dino for just a minute, you could come back to watch hours worth of hard work during late nights to just stand up and walk away like it never even happened. This game is just a brutal when it come to battling with other tribes. If you are not the biggest, badest tribe on the server (aka the alpha tribe), then whoever is owns you and everything you've worked so hard for. This is why I mentioned earlier to find a good server. You must find a server where the alpha tribe doesn't take anything or ask for payments from its subjects and also doesn't attack unless genuinely threatened. If you find yourself on a server with an alpha that does any of that, you are♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥away your time.
Every game has its pitfalls and this game has some big ones, but at the same time those hardships are exactly what will drive you to learn to not be a noob and make lifelong friends along the way.

I've officially played this game for 1337 hours on steam at this moment. I think this was the best time to make the review.
Warframe isn't for everybody, at least not initially. It can take you a significant amount of time to really tap into the game, but I've always found it worth it. There can be a lot of grinding, but honestly only if you are  in a rush.
The game has changed immensely since I first started playing, but pretty much everything has been for the better. They've added recently true 3 dimensional space combat in addition to the multitude of other options for battle. I think the best way to play warframe is the to play what you have the most fun with. If you want to be a meta-kid, you can do that. Technically you can be a merchant, tank, support, caster, artillery, sniper, skirmisher. Between the warframes, the weapons, and the trading system all of that and more is possible.
I'll leave this at a simple truth. Warframe has the best free-to-play model I have ever seen. I hope more games follow suit.

Bought this game quite a while back. I saw a lot of potential in this game. It is seriously fun and there is so much to do whether it is trying to find food, build your "dream" house, collecting resources, slaying dinosours and even taming them. There are also plenty of mods to download to make gameplay far more interesting ranging from loot stack mods to even final fantasy swords (sick right?).
When i initially got it my pc could barely handle the game. I was running a gtx 560 ti. The game constantly crashed and so forth. So i stopped playing for a really long time. After about 6 months and buying a new gaming rig I tried getting back into after seeing countless updates being installed.
The game still constantly crashes saying my graphics drivers need to be updated even though I am running the latest driver. I even tried rolling back to an older more stable driver and it still gives me the same issue. I run the game with no mods in extreme low memory and still the same issues.
If you know how to get past this particular problem and have a decent gaming rig then i do recommend this game. As you see i have played Warframe for quite a long time.The first few hundered hours of Warframe are pretty much addictive when i started i would play for hours on end.Now the grind in the game is quite insane but there are some ways for players to lessen the grind but only in some ways.Resources and credits are quite easy to farm with certain squad loadouts but prime parts,certain mods can be a nightmare to get.The $ prices for guns are very expensive but blueprints for those weapons can be bought with the ingame currency and built using resources.There are a lot of character classes with different builds that will keep you trying new things for a long time.New characters drop from bosses which can be annoying since you get 1 part per boss run.Now all items have a building time from 1 min to 72 hours depending on the item.Weapons usually take either 12 or 24 hours,Warframes(characters)take 72 hours not counting each part that takes 12 hours to build.Endgame content is very low the only thing that comes close is raids that can last for a long time and drop only 1 reward not counting the resources and mods that can drop from enemies but those rewards for the most part are not useful at all and the ones that are have a very low drop chance which basically means you end up ignoring for the most part.The developers seem to be increasing the grind more to keep players playing until they can release a new mayor update with the recent example being a character that needs to researched from a clan dojo and one of the resources is alert only.But to be honest the gameplay is what makes Warframe as fun as it is,with the new parkour system you can move and shoot really fast and fire in mid-air.The lore of the game is quite cryptic but they have added ways for us to learn about the world through our own in-game achievements without reading codex entries.The world is quite intresting and very cool the design of the enemies are great though their Ai could use some work.The best thing is that 95% of the games content can be gotten ingame through either farming or trading certain items to earn Platinum which is the bought currency.The only thing that cant be acquired are special cosmetics that come with new Prime Warframe packs but they have made a statement that some of them will be farmable in game.The graphics are nice and it runs very smoothly on even lower end machines.The game unfortunately still has some bugs most of which arent very bad.All in all the game is blast but similiar to every game gets repetative the more you play it but for new players you have a load of content and fun that will keep you busy for quite a while and the game is constantly updated which helps aleviate the repetition a lot.New players dont be afraid to ask for advice because the game can be overwhelming for newbies.All in all a very good game with some flaws but i have a feeling ill still keep playing for a long time.

Warframe is a very cool, stylish, and fun space ninja game.
It has loads of fast paced action, plenty of unique playable "Warframes", tons of badass weapons, and even various companions.
While the missions can get repetitive, and there is alot of grind, the actual combat has so many possibilities that it keeps you wanting to try different things.
Like any (space) ninja game, it has a pretty good parkour system. I suggest you don't skip the tutorial, even if you are an old returning player.
This game is not perfect, it is a perpetual Work In Progress, but the developers care alot for the game and its community.
Beware though, the development cycle is often brash decisions caused by toxic outcry of entitled players, repeating until the dev team finally satisfies them.
The comunity is great for the most part, just.. not when it comes to the future of the game. People love the game so much that they want it to be their way.
All that said, I fully recomend this game. It has one of the best Free 2 Play models that I know of, with the only thing requiring purchases (of Platinum, a cash-bought in-game currency) are cosmetic-only items, and extra slots in your inventory. Everything else is farmable or earnable, and even the cosmetics and slots can be gotten fro free by trading items for Platinum.

At the time of writing this review I have merely only played about a lousy 5-10 hours, but the fact that this game has blown me away more than any other makes me very pumped to write this review for any lost souls out there who may be looking for the game of their life, and I am certain I have found mine. I know, I'm already furiously masturbating all over this hot piece of code called Warframe.
The gameplay is, at first, quite simple, but in a bigger picture it's actually really nice. You play as a Tenno, a space ninja of sorts. At the start of the game, you can choose between three different "Warframes" which basicly acts like classes in any other MMORPG. As you progress through the game, you can unlock blueprints to craft brand new classes, or, Warframes. Each and every Warframe are different from one another, ranging from their base stats to their unique set of skills. At the time, I belive there are over 30 different Warframes to unlock and play as.
There are two main things you will be doing in Warframe. Completing missions (either solo or with friends/random people) and grinding for components to craft your gear with. The missions in Warframe can vary from capture, defense, spying, escorting an NPC, kill a boss, or just simply reach the end of the map. It's all very fun and works well. The only downside with these missions is the NPC escort, because sometimes they tend to get stuck behind walls or they're just simply too stupid to find their way to you. This isn't really as big of problem I'm making it out to be, as when you've reached a long enough distance away from the NPC, they will teleport to you.
The enemies in Warframe are varied and a hell of a blast to slaughter through. In the beginning of the game, as in your first few hours, you'll be fighting the same robots for some time.
This game is NOT Pay2Win, as some would make it out to be. Yes, it's true that with "platinum" (the real money in-game currency) you can buy new weapons and Warframes with better stats than the base ones you start with, along with weird dog animal companion things... Yeah, I don't really know about that last one. Now this might sound very pay2win-ish, but trust me, the Pay2Win aspect in this game is mostly just for the lazy people out there. Everything that you can buy with real money in the Warframe Market apart from cosmetics can be crafted with regular in-game currency and materials. So, in the end, buying all that precious platinum is really just a way to speed things up, nothing else.
Of course, regular missions isn't the only part of the gameplay. You can play multiplayer gamemodes like Annihilation (free for all deathmatch), Team Annihilation (team deathmatch) and Cephalon Capture (4v4 capture the flag type of game). These three gamemodes are really fun to play, but you'll usually find yourself getting completely destroyed if you haven't upgraded your weapons and warframe first, haha. There are also challenges to these gamemodes which offer you extra experience upon completion which is a nice touch.
TL;DR: I'll just make a list of cons and pros.
Pros:

This game is fun. The universe is awesome and the graphics are cool as well.
Warframes, weapons, "pets".....also cool.
Free 2 Play? Yep. Unless you want to spend money on stuff to quickly get items.
Grinding? Yes but its better than paying for the item you want. Yes, I'm actually supporting the grind. Why? If you don't want to rush through the game and take in the scenery, the grind is worth it.
Bosses? Hard and sometimes fun. Other times.....annoying.
Some levels are fun, some are annoying.....when SOLO. When with a good team, fun and sometimes quick.
Community.......not sure but I'd give it an "A".
Hacking? None.
Lag? Yes but not very often.
Fun with friends? Yep.
9/10
Please note, the above, is based only on PVE.

I have been playing this for about two weeks and love it. It has a lot of RPG aspects like character stats as well as the open-world survival theme. You can build things as you level up and learn how. You can tame all kinds of dinosaurs, many of which may be ridden or flown after being tamed. They have their own stats, further enhancing the game in that your dino may not be the same clone as everybody elses'.
Graphically the game is breathtaking. I played it on an i7-5930K, 16GB RAM, and a 4GB GTX 980 Ti. It was movie-like. Wet shores, fluid water with reflections, sun-rays through the trees, real-time shadows on EVERYTHING, the works! Sometimes it is fun to simply stop and look around in the world.
Gameplay is highly addictive and entertaining. Taming a dinosaur, for example, does not happen instantly. Depending on the size of the dino it may take up to a week of in-game days to tame one, and that is AFTER you knock it unconscious with a non-lethal weapon. Oh and how you care for it (feed it) while it is down also determines its tamed starting stats and maximum level after being tamed.
On top of that there is the building system. Not only can you craft weapons and armor, but you can also craft all kinds of building materials and irrigation systems. You may build multi-level buildings, underwater buildings, even buidlings on boats! Building away from a source of water? No problem! You can build an irrigation system to bring water to your home or farm. That's right, you can grown your own plants for food and other resources as well!
So where does Ark fall short? Well, the only two things which I take issue with are the anti-cheat and the "official" servers. I don't cheat and I don't mind playing on official servers, but the anti-cheat is some off-the-wall system and the official servers can be plagued with players who do things merely to grief new or other players. These are the downsides to the great game.
The anti-cheat is called Battle-Eye, which I have never heard of prior to Ark. No big deal right? Well think again. The anti-cheat wants rootkit level access to my PC AND it wants to install a service AND it wants to be able to run code it downloads from time to time. Screw that! This is a Steam game, we have VAC here. I am not the biggest fan of VAC either, but I trust it a lot more than something which wants rootkit access (ring-0) to my system. No way in heck will I ever install something THAT invasive simply to prove I don't cheat at a game. I'll play without it or play something else.
The other bad thing is that there are servers where people with nothing better to do than grief others do things like building a single pillar every so often, on every tile in the game-world, which prevents new resources from growing and prevents new players from building their own shelters and such. The problem is that this is not breaking a game-mechanic. You are allowed to build anywhere somebody else has not built yet. You build things here, like in Minecraft. Combating this would be difficult pragmatically and would require a sever moderator to police their server to prevent it.
Oh wait! One more thing. The developers removed the ability to password-protect your server so you could list it but only friends could join. Instead they now depend on the Steam UI for private servers. If you choose to have your server "private", it simply doesn't add it to the global list of servers. To get in you need to invite a friend on Steam. However, this is Unreal Engine 4. If you know the hostname or IP address of the server, you can still connect. I will not go into how here, but basically you can no longer lock out your server, meaning somebody wanting to grief you CAN come into your "private" server while you sleep and demolish your work. Not cool.
Overall this game is excellent. Single-player and multiplayer are good, graphics are great, and the gameplay will keep you coming back for more. If you like Minecraft, The Forest, Turok, or anything in-between, pick it up and join us!
Update 2017-04-02:
This game was great when I first reviewed it, but things have been getting bad over the course of the last few major patches. First they introduce a "Tek Tier" of weapons and armor that are absurdly over-powered. Then they introduce dinos that do things like steal items from your inventory, that can knock a player out in a matter of seconds, that can knock you off your mount and stun you long enough to kill you, that can not only hit you and your entire group of dinos/friends, but also knock you out, and now the flying dinos have been made useless. Every flying dino is now absurdly slow, even slower than my character can run, they need to constantly land and wait to regenerate stamina, and they were reset to what they thought was a reasonable level. I personally had perfect tames that were 180 when tamed and up over 210 drop to 171 or below. Couple with that a UI that looks as though it belongs in UT3 and you break immersion.
Due to these additions and changes, several bad things have happened. Alpha tribes which dominate are essentially the only ones who can gather the needed materials to make the new tek gear, making the most powerful tribes more powerful. For those who play alone or co-op on PvE servers, flying dinos were your lifeline to materials and moving around safely. Now you cannot move or gather materials at all. Flying dinos had their health stripped, stamina all but removed, movement speed hard-set to walking speed and you cannot buff it, and they need to land every minute or two, usually resulting in death due to the low health.
Additional frustration for many comes from having dinos they did perfect tames on, bred, and had babies with even better stats now being destroyed and made useless. All of this due to complaints from players who only do PvP arguing about being unable to attack or do anything against flying dinos and their riders. In other words, the few who couldn't learn to play against a specific style of play.
I have changed my review because I had hundreds of hours as well as money for a dedicated server invested in this game and everything I worked so very hard for is gone. Dinos are ruined, on PvP the biggest tribes now don't even need dinos thanks to tek items, and single player/PvE are ruined. Oh, and teh UI is blue with blue text. Way to go! Nothing like eye-strain, which many players are now complaining about. I'd swear a different team did this patch.
I will update this review should changes occur to revert my hundreds of hours of work back into useable dinos, exactly the way I had them. No compromises, no BS. I am a PvE player. I don't grief and nobody who uses my server does. Should a patch to fix this not arrive, I will leave this review as-is as a warning to prospective buyers. At this point in time, do NOT buy this game.

Truly a model many, if not all F2P games should live by.
Where many F2P games seem to stumble upon extreme grinding or pay-to-progress/win at it's core, Warframe doesn't. Though gameplay might become somewhat repetitive later on, there's plenty of content and objectives to strife towards to keep it interesting.
At heart, the game is made as a cooperative game, where you and 3 others achieve the objective. Though there are plenty of different game-modes, most of the time it comes down to a hack-and-slash fest. This might become repetitive in the long run, there's still plenty of content, quests and game-modes to go by, as well as a lot of progression to keep it interesting. Pay-to-progress is there, but if you want to get the items you want without the need of spending money, it doesn't feel like an endless grindfest.
Of course, the game needs to stay afloat - and it cant do it for free. One can buy 'platinum' from the store, which can be spent on from aesthetics to weaponry and warframes (the 'armor suit' the player can use, each with it's own unique abilities). However, aside from the aesthetics, it can always be bought through in-game progress. Where the game really shines in this aspect is that it doesn't adhere to a huge level of grinding, though it's still common to 'farm' for particular resources in order to build the item you desire, but it never feels unfair.
Platinum, however, can also be traded amongst players. Some items can only be acquired through 'raiding' particular areas. People can salvage the items, then sell them. Prospective buyers can use platinum, as well as the ingame currency to buy the item from the other player. This ensures that Platinum retains its value, and players will still feel the urge to buy said currency with real-life cash. Apparently, this system's been working fine for the developers in creating revenue whilst players don't feel 'ripped off' or abused.
The game also has a PVP element. Whereas this usually creates the typical 'pay-to-win' approach, it doesn't. Depending on the armaments the player uses to enter a PVP arena, the player will receive a so-called 'conclave rank'. This conclave rank depends on the power and effectiveness on the items the player equips before entering the PVP arena. This way, well equipped players will be matched against other well equipped players, and new players will be placed against new players. It's definetly possible for a more experienced player to jump into the 'newbie arena' but will have to discard their most valued weapons in order to compete. For some reason - it works. Haven't had much trouble there, though i'll be honest that i haven't played much of the PVP element.
To top it all off, the game is almost continiously updated with new events, quests and updates, and i'll be honest: The game is brimming with content. I've also found the game's community to be surprisingly welcoming and helpful, which is really nice. The game is surprisingly deep as well, which requires some planning to which weapons you'll be using in which scenario to ensure maximum effectiveness.
Whereas many F2P games feel like a cheap cash-grab, Warframe really feels like it keeps players engaged (and thus, paying customers) through sheer amounts of content and high production value. It's a breath of fresh air in an otherwise deplorable market - and hopefully a standard for other F2P games to live by. Considering the fact that Warframe has a huge playerbase, i'm definetly sure the developers can say they succeeded well.
All in all, Warframe does a lot of things right. Its gameplay mechanics might become repetitive eventually, but long before you'll consider investing a serious amount of time in it - you'll find out whether it's to your liking or not.

There's very few games that consistantly lead me to return as they add cooler and cooler stuff, and I haven't met a dev team that is so active within their own community, either through dev streams ( which are fantastic and I wish more devs did them ) or prime times. The Warframe wiki is extremely informative, and I've found myself on that quite a lot as I've risen through the ranks as a player. Many, many players will point you in that direction.
Graphics are great for most any computer and the game provides lots of room to grow for the future to come. There isn't a specific set that's more overpowered than any other, and the game allows you plenty of options to customize your loadout to mess with your play style. Perfect.
Grinding is a female puppy, though. With a sheit ton of weapons and frames comes a lot of grinding. So much so that the dev team is having a difficult time fitting it all in on the current planetary map.
As for exclutivity and the factor of pay to win, nearly every single weapon, mod, and frame can be grinded out. The game also features a large base of platinum users that will buy certain parts or mods from you. So, with enough patience, you literally don't
to pay a single cent to play this game. At all. Certain events ( such as the Void Trader or alerts ) will assist you in boosting the value of your inventory, as well.
While we're on the subject of pay to win, I just realized there's steam DLC for it. Welp. Here's the deal, I looked at the $100 pack, which includes every bonus from the previous dlcs. In game, you currently may get the chance of anywhere from 20% to 75% off platinum perchases. You can get a $100 purchase of platinum and a handful of decent rare mods for
. Yeah. You read that right. You can't get that from the Steam Store. Those are decent mods, too. Going down the list, 150,000 credits is nothing. That won't last you a few hours. 20
mods usually mean a lot of common mods, which you'll get in your first 5 minutes of playing. Lightning Dash, Retribution, Mobilize, Rush, and Firewalker can easily be found / traded within your first 20 hours or so in the game. The 5 Exilus Adapters are worth about 150 platinum. the Resource, Resource drop, Affinity, and credit boosters (3 days) are only good if you play the absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥♥out of the game for the next few days. Those are all worth about 120 plat. In the end, you're paying 100 dollars for around 1,700 platinum and a bunch of RNG mods. That's not even worth (as I'm typing this up) the 50% off. Just wait for an in-game sale of 50-75% off and do it that way. Alright, next topic.
Jargon for this game is quite easy to learn. Basically, the only thing you need to know is that a catalyst is commonly referred to as a potato, due to its shape.
The learning curve is guided quite nicely. If there's a new major game feature, a tutorial will almost always accompany it. You start off with an MK1 Braton or an MK1 Paris and find new blueprints and parts or buy new blueprints from the market for ingame currency. Easy to pick up, hard to master. Each mod guides the weapon stats in its own way. Want a bow that does five digits of damage? You can do that. Want a sidearm that will always apply on-hit effects ( varying from a base effect of fire, ice, electricity, and toxin which, when combined with another, can also yield radiation, viral, blast, corrosive, gas, or magnetic ) you can do that all as well. More info on how it works
.
The community is normally always eager to help another Tenno out. They're friendly and as long as you stay away from global chat, quite nice. You'll often find someone willing to risk their life to come back and help you up when you're down.

Truly a model many, if not all F2P games should live by.
Where many F2P games seem to stumble upon extreme grinding or pay-to-progress/win at it's core, Warframe doesn't. Though gameplay might become somewhat repetitive later on, there's plenty of content and objectives to strife towards to keep it interesting.
At heart, the game is made as a cooperative game, where you and 3 others achieve the objective. Though there are plenty of different game-modes, most of the time it comes down to a hack-and-slash fest. This might become repetitive in the long run, there's still plenty of content, quests and game-modes to go by, as well as a lot of progression to keep it interesting. Pay-to-progress is there, but if you want to get the items you want without the need of spending money, it doesn't feel like an endless grindfest.
Of course, the game needs to stay afloat - and it cant do it for free. One can buy 'platinum' from the store, which can be spent on from aesthetics to weaponry and warframes (the 'armor suit' the player can use, each with it's own unique abilities). However, aside from the aesthetics, it can always be bought through in-game progress. Where the game really shines in this aspect is that it doesn't adhere to a huge level of grinding, though it's still common to 'farm' for particular resources in order to build the item you desire, but it never feels unfair.
Platinum, however, can also be traded amongst players. Some items can only be acquired through 'raiding' particular areas. People can salvage the items, then sell them. Prospective buyers can use platinum, as well as the ingame currency to buy the item from the other player. This ensures that Platinum retains its value, and players will still feel the urge to buy said currency with real-life cash. Apparently, this system's been working fine for the developers in creating revenue whilst players don't feel 'ripped off' or abused.
The game also has a PVP element. Whereas this usually creates the typical 'pay-to-win' approach, it doesn't. Depending on the armaments the player uses to enter a PVP arena, the player will receive a so-called 'conclave rank'. This conclave rank depends on the power and effectiveness on the items the player equips before entering the PVP arena. This way, well equipped players will be matched against other well equipped players, and new players will be placed against new players. It's definetly possible for a more experienced player to jump into the 'newbie arena' but will have to discard their most valued weapons in order to compete. For some reason - it works. Haven't had much trouble there, though i'll be honest that i haven't played much of the PVP element.
To top it all off, the game is almost continiously updated with new events, quests and updates, and i'll be honest: The game is brimming with content. I've also found the game's community to be surprisingly welcoming and helpful, which is really nice. The game is surprisingly deep as well, which requires some planning to which weapons you'll be using in which scenario to ensure maximum effectiveness.
Whereas many F2P games feel like a cheap cash-grab, Warframe really feels like it keeps players engaged (and thus, paying customers) through sheer amounts of content and high production value. It's a breath of fresh air in an otherwise deplorable market - and hopefully a standard for other F2P games to live by. Considering the fact that Warframe has a huge playerbase, i'm definetly sure the developers can say they succeeded well.
All in all, Warframe does a lot of things right. Its gameplay mechanics might become repetitive eventually, but long before you'll consider investing a serious amount of time in it - you'll find out whether it's to your liking or not.

There's very few games that consistantly lead me to return as they add cooler and cooler stuff, and I haven't met a dev team that is so active within their own community, either through dev streams ( which are fantastic and I wish more devs did them ) or prime times. The Warframe wiki is extremely informative, and I've found myself on that quite a lot as I've risen through the ranks as a player. Many, many players will point you in that direction.
Graphics are great for most any computer and the game provides lots of room to grow for the future to come. There isn't a specific set that's more overpowered than any other, and the game allows you plenty of options to customize your loadout to mess with your play style. Perfect.
Grinding is a female puppy, though. With a sheit ton of weapons and frames comes a lot of grinding. So much so that the dev team is having a difficult time fitting it all in on the current planetary map.
As for exclutivity and the factor of pay to win, nearly every single weapon, mod, and frame can be grinded out. The game also features a large base of platinum users that will buy certain parts or mods from you. So, with enough patience, you literally don't
to pay a single cent to play this game. At all. Certain events ( such as the Void Trader or alerts ) will assist you in boosting the value of your inventory, as well.
While we're on the subject of pay to win, I just realized there's steam DLC for it. Welp. Here's the deal, I looked at the $100 pack, which includes every bonus from the previous dlcs. In game, you currently may get the chance of anywhere from 20% to 75% off platinum perchases. You can get a $100 purchase of platinum and a handful of decent rare mods for
. Yeah. You read that right. You can't get that from the Steam Store. Those are decent mods, too. Going down the list, 150,000 credits is nothing. That won't last you a few hours. 20
mods usually mean a lot of common mods, which you'll get in your first 5 minutes of playing. Lightning Dash, Retribution, Mobilize, Rush, and Firewalker can easily be found / traded within your first 20 hours or so in the game. The 5 Exilus Adapters are worth about 150 platinum. the Resource, Resource drop, Affinity, and credit boosters (3 days) are only good if you play the absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥♥out of the game for the next few days. Those are all worth about 120 plat. In the end, you're paying 100 dollars for around 1,700 platinum and a bunch of RNG mods. That's not even worth (as I'm typing this up) the 50% off. Just wait for an in-game sale of 50-75% off and do it that way. Alright, next topic.
Jargon for this game is quite easy to learn. Basically, the only thing you need to know is that a catalyst is commonly referred to as a potato, due to its shape.
The learning curve is guided quite nicely. If there's a new major game feature, a tutorial will almost always accompany it. You start off with an MK1 Braton or an MK1 Paris and find new blueprints and parts or buy new blueprints from the market for ingame currency. Easy to pick up, hard to master. Each mod guides the weapon stats in its own way. Want a bow that does five digits of damage? You can do that. Want a sidearm that will always apply on-hit effects ( varying from a base effect of fire, ice, electricity, and toxin which, when combined with another, can also yield radiation, viral, blast, corrosive, gas, or magnetic ) you can do that all as well. More info on how it works
.
The community is normally always eager to help another Tenno out. They're friendly and as long as you stay away from global chat, quite nice. You'll often find someone willing to risk their life to come back and help you up when you're down.

I held out against Warframe for the longest time.  I like my shooters first-person.  But my gaming buddies would not stop praising it, so I finally said, "Fine!  If it'll make you STFU, I'll download it!"
I should have listened to them from the beginning.
Warframe takes place in the far-flung future.  You play as a Tenno, a literal space-ninja.  You fight with swords and axes and guns and all kinds of weaponry.  Each Tenno, of Warframe, has a different set of powers to master.  Some Warframes may not fit your playstyle, but there are plenty to choose from; I♥♥♥♥♥♥you not, there are currently TWENTY-FIVE DIFFERENT 'FRAMES to choose from, and the dev's add more on a regular basis.  Be warned, however, you start the game with one, but as you master the game you can defeat bosses that drop the components for other Warframes, and craft these in your Foundry.  Yes, the grinding component is VERY strong in this game, but I personally don't see it as the chore it's made out to be.
The learning curve may be a bit overwhelming at first for people brand-spanking new to this genre, like myself.  As long as you have friends who play it regularly, and are willing to help your n00b♥♥♥♥♥ you'll do just fine.
Play this game with friends when you're stuck, but consider going into missions solo as well.  Each mission is randomly generated, with a number of map 'tiles' acting as the mission proper.  Missions may have tiles that repeat, sometimes even multiple times.  This helps n00bs like myself grow familair with map structuring, and before long you'll know where all the super-secret goody-drops are located.
Another added bonus to this game is that it is completely free-to-play.  Yes, microtransactions exist, but they take a backseat to the gaming experience.  Everything, and I mean EVERYTHING, is available to non-paying players -- as long as they're willing to grind.  Microtransactions consist of purchasing fully-built Warframes, Warframe cosmetics, or fully-built weaponry.  No advantage is obtained if you buy a weapon rather than construct it; it's the exact same thing.  Team Fortress 2 may be free-to-play, but it's easy to tell the different between a F2P and someone who bought their virtual toys.  And there is quite a rift between these haves and have-nots.  In Warframe, there is no such rift -- not that I've noticed, anyway.
I never thought I would became as addicted to this game as I have.  This game pulled me away from Team Fortress 2 for a whole month, and I STILL come back to it regularly; no other game that I have currently installed can say that about itself.  And allow me to clarify: I like my FPS games.  I heart/less-than-three them.  For a game like Warframe to pull me away from a game like Team Fortress 2 -- that says a lot.

Summary:
It is a fun solo game for a while, but in my opinion, what appears to be a recent (and possibly severely buggy) full cross-server PvPvE transfer system is killing the official server game experience. Paid DLC dragons swoop in, in vast numbers, and destroy everything. If people thought Alphas controlling whole Non-DLC servers was bad, visualize one giant server where only part of the game is accessable to you. Survival of the Richest.
In addition, servers are not region locked, so expect to get wiped (or worse) by people that do not type in your language. The PvPvE is extremely divided by nation of origin, to the point that some servers are referred to as <insert nation> servers. The game client itself does not indicate this, so it is a trial and error system of finding a server where you will at least be tolerated.
---
A very detailed account of my actual experience:
I played on a fresh, private server with a bunch of friends for weeks (which was fun for a while). I loved the game, but the server went offline forever and all of my progress was lost. I decided to try official servers, which I assumed would have longer lifespans.
I settled on an official PvPvE server "held by an Alpha tribe for about a year."
Yes, huge swaths of terrain are claimed by instant death turret encrusted fortifcations.
Yes, the Alpha is brutally strict in wiping new players, indiviudals, tribes, and their own members from the server
Yes, I loved it  -
until the cross-server stuff started a war with flying projectile vomitting dragons I have no chance against.
The server's tribes had a tight knit community when I arrived. The only rules given were "Don't be a jerk." Except they don't tell you what that means. They don't tell you how to play. They let you, and expect you, to learn on your own.
For many that tried, this meant rage quitting as they were wiped for transgressions.
I have put in many hours in a short time, and lost many bases, but was allowed to continue playing. My biggest base, and only direct Alpha wipe? Due to the reckless actions of my only, chosen at random, tribemate/leader: the base, all dinos,  and the bird I was riding were rocketed to death (by the same person that enabled me to acquire the bird earlier that same day)
I laughed in global chat at the irony. My tribemate, on the other hand, spewed rage-fueled threats and insults at everyone, including the Alpha's leader. I was allowed to try again, this time on my own.
To be honest, up until recently, it had been a great experience. I was losing hours and days of effort at a time, but I was learning to be more respectful of others and more aware of the consequences of my own actions with increasing intensity. This is about the only game that has impacted my behavior and attitude toward others in a very positive way.
---
If I was having a life-impacting great experience, why do I not recommend it?
1) Its not for everyone. You must already posses a great deal of patience and some form of maturity.
2) The full cross-server transfers (though I have little knowledge of their workings) have started to crush my play experience entirely. The server is now constantly under attack by dragons I cannot even acquire (paid DLC on another server type that I do not want to learn or experience), and have no real hope of even scratching. The battle was supposedly between an Alpha on another server and the Alpha on our server, but the reality of it is: Most of our server is being attacked (often while offline) and it feels very much like pay to win possibly compounded by bugs and cheats.
3) They require an anti-cheat program to be installed for official play, but if you inspect the forums - it does not apper to be keeping up, or at least not fast enough to prevent calamity. That is indeed second hand knowledge, but it should be a consideration if you are interested in this game.
---
Admittedly, I have not tried the PvE server experience, and do not want to.

The long version of the review would be this:
Warframe is a co-op fantasy TPS which takes place in freaking space, Not convinced to play it yet? Well then let me go more in detail.
Warframes are called the suits you use to fight your enemies in the game, all of them has their own streangths and weaknesses, they all have one element or characteristic that their abilities are based around of (ex: volt has lightning, mirage has mirrors, oberon has radioactivity etc.)  Also once you unlock the arsenal you have access to their mods menu that allows you to upgrade them with a ton of different mods you find in your missions, also you can color your warframe as you like and add all sort of stuff to make their appearance look better and personalize them.
There are also Primary, secondary and a male weapon that you can equip, as well as being able to pick between a drone flying above your head called a sentinel or a dog following you around called a kubrow in your missions (The sentinel and kubrow aren’t just for decoration they can also help you out a lot on your missions)
But it wouldn’t be fair to end this review without telling you about the cons of warframe:
The game is highly real world cash oriented, and what I mean by that is you can buy almost everything there is in the game within 1 day if you have enough money whereas you would need to farm and farm for months to get the same result without real life cash. However I would not recommend that if you just start this game to buy all the stuff right away, in my opinion the farming is a part of the game and should be played to some extend or the game will be straight up boring.
Also in the beginning of the game when you don’t have that many good weapons and mods and try to move on to some of the higher tear missions, the damage you do feels very underwhelming, it takes some time to get your first good warframe and weapon with the right mods on them, but once you do you become op as hell. I would say to speed up the process a little bit you could join a clan and ask them to help you out with some missions
Occasionally there can be some bugs here and there but the development team usually fixes them within a few days do not worry about that too much
In the end warframe is a very fun and enjoyable game and it may be what you are looking for if you would like a new and unique experience that even some pay to play titles of the same gender cannot offer you.

I held out against Warframe for the longest time.  I like my shooters first-person.  But my gaming buddies would not stop praising it, so I finally said, "Fine!  If it'll make you STFU, I'll download it!"
I should have listened to them from the beginning.
Warframe takes place in the far-flung future.  You play as a Tenno, a literal space-ninja.  You fight with swords and axes and guns and all kinds of weaponry.  Each Tenno, of Warframe, has a different set of powers to master.  Some Warframes may not fit your playstyle, but there are plenty to choose from; I♥♥♥♥♥♥you not, there are currently TWENTY-FIVE DIFFERENT 'FRAMES to choose from, and the dev's add more on a regular basis.  Be warned, however, you start the game with one, but as you master the game you can defeat bosses that drop the components for other Warframes, and craft these in your Foundry.  Yes, the grinding component is VERY strong in this game, but I personally don't see it as the chore it's made out to be.
The learning curve may be a bit overwhelming at first for people brand-spanking new to this genre, like myself.  As long as you have friends who play it regularly, and are willing to help your n00b♥♥♥♥♥ you'll do just fine.
Play this game with friends when you're stuck, but consider going into missions solo as well.  Each mission is randomly generated, with a number of map 'tiles' acting as the mission proper.  Missions may have tiles that repeat, sometimes even multiple times.  This helps n00bs like myself grow familair with map structuring, and before long you'll know where all the super-secret goody-drops are located.
Another added bonus to this game is that it is completely free-to-play.  Yes, microtransactions exist, but they take a backseat to the gaming experience.  Everything, and I mean EVERYTHING, is available to non-paying players -- as long as they're willing to grind.  Microtransactions consist of purchasing fully-built Warframes, Warframe cosmetics, or fully-built weaponry.  No advantage is obtained if you buy a weapon rather than construct it; it's the exact same thing.  Team Fortress 2 may be free-to-play, but it's easy to tell the different between a F2P and someone who bought their virtual toys.  And there is quite a rift between these haves and have-nots.  In Warframe, there is no such rift -- not that I've noticed, anyway.
I never thought I would became as addicted to this game as I have.  This game pulled me away from Team Fortress 2 for a whole month, and I STILL come back to it regularly; no other game that I have currently installed can say that about itself.  And allow me to clarify: I like my FPS games.  I heart/less-than-three them.  For a game like Warframe to pull me away from a game like Team Fortress 2 -- that says a lot.

It's always a good chuckle when you're level 6 and your best weapon is a slingshot, and you get a little too close to a Carno. But it's even more of a chuckle when you're level 60, and eat the Carno with your level 250 Rex that you painted bright pink. And the chuckles turn to evil cackles when you're level 80 and one-shot the Carno with a rocket launcher, or a mountable machinegun turret on the back of a gigantic flying bird.
Excellent excellent excellent. Excellent survival game. Devs are active - with new updates coming out normally every 3 weeks to a month (bigger updates do take longer of course EDIT: Updates will now obviously be less frequent now the game is out of early access). While often challenging at the beginning, once you progress through the game it becomes an awesome experience.
Playing with friends is even better - the game is definitely playable solo, but when you have a tribe it's so much easier and more fun. People on servers can range from "Hi! How's it going?" to *eats you with a Giga* but that's going to happen in any online game. If you can, try to team up with people.
It's not 100% realistic (you're riding around on dinosaurs and with the addition of the Tek Tier (which basically adds halo armour and laser guns, but costs a lot of resources to craft), but it's still an awesome, fun, rewarding, at times VERY frustrating, but nevertheless amazing survival game.
A quick note about the Scorched Earth DLC - it is fun but can get boring after a while (as there are less dinos, it's a lot harder and it's just all desert). If it ever goes on sale, you may want to consider it if you want a change from regular ARK.
I would definitely 10/10 recommend this if you like dinosaurs, survival games or are reading this review. It's expensive, but if you can get it on sale then definitely add to cart. If you've gotten this far thanks for reading, and I hope you found this review helpful and that you enjoy ARK: Survival Evolved.

Warframe - Has excellent game play, looks awesome and loads of fun. Except that the devs/makers pull sneaky stunts to trick people into spending money. When I see a weapons selection that I can level up for, and save credits for my thought is that my ability to hold them in inventory would be equal to the spots shown. Warframe has a forge or crafting table that will make things if you save credits for blueprints, and find the needed parts to make things with, then it will forge things over time. Some take a minute most will take 12 hours. To speed up the process you can spend platinum pieces or money.
What I do not not like is when selecting a blueprint that it does not tell you that not only will this cost you $50,000 credits, take 12 hours to make, IT DOES show what you need in advance... BUT IT DOES NOT MENTION this will also require 1 or 2 or how many extra SLOTS in your inventory witch you do not have. IT WILL COST AN ADDITIONAL 12 PLATINUM to be able to inventory the item or items.
I would rather pay UPFRONT $50 to $60 dollars for a game and then have everything I need in game. Meaning, I level up for it, and find it, and earn it. Not where I am spending $5.00 , $10.00 along the way to make my inventory bigger. By the time I can forge all the weapons I might like, and other items... You would rack up a massive amount of money spent. The trick is you get some platinum and you play, and forget about the money you spent. Then it happens in time again, and again... NOT KNOWING THE COST UP FRONT IS SNEAKY SHADY AND UNDERHANDED IN MY OPINION ONLY.
I do not see why we can not have a CREDIT to Platinum way to build more Platinum, as well as ways to earn find and make more Platinum in game for all levels.
To really get the very best deals you need to look for are the ones with PRIME packages... You spend as little as $50,00 to $199.00 or so you do get a lot more digital stuff or virtual stuff sure, however you end up paying way more than say $50,00 to $60.00 for say like Fallout 4 and have all you need in a finished game... You at least know 100% your upfront costs. That is how RETAIL WORKS, and this is a form of RETAIL. I am thinking of contacting some consumer protection agencies to see of this sneaky policy might be changed. For now I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS GAME AS IT IS NOT HONEST ABOUT ALL THE POSSIBLE COSTS UPFRONT.
Sidenote: I do in fact understand that the money is used to keep the game being developed, I am not saying to make it all free. I am saying I NEED TO KNOW UPFRONT BEFORE I WASTE MATERIALS AND TIME WHAT SOMETHING WILL COST. I do not like these in game sneak payment schemes as they exploit the fact people often get shafted in the long run IF NOT TOLD UPFRONT <--- Notice the theme of my issue: NOT BEING TOLD UPFRONT.

I'm on the fence for this review. Ark is a great game and people can invest many hours into it. However there is a downfall to this game that the players need to be aware of and that would be the staffs choices and history with the players.
After two years they announced the offical release to leave EA and released a game still full of bugs and issues. This release was also announced with a brand new dlc shortly after. This made a large number of players beleive that they left EA status to release this dlc without the EA hate, which they got when they released Scorched earth.
Originally we were told for two years that we wouldnt be wiped. Later we found out that wiping all the servers was the plan all along until their testers advised aginst it. This was even told to media outlets that servers were going to be wiped and then imediatly the change was reversed. So you may be thinking, so what? Well In the end they wiped half of all the servers pc that included almost 75% of all the expanshion pack servers. We were told once that they wouldnt wipe servers if one player was active on them. Then they were saying to give us a month warning if they were to wipe. Then they said a week, and delayed that week down to 5 days and missed the eta for it..
Guess what? on that 5th day we got a patch that forced us to wait to transfer items, transfering 5,000 metal went from a 10min task to a 6-8 hour task. This further ruined the game as people couldnt evacuate anything from the closing servers in time. They kept this change too and are calling their anti-dupe method.
They also deleted all the old support tickets of all players, some had them open for months of missing charactors, they never replaced them, in the end they dropped support for everyone perminatly on the old servers and gave the players a copy/paste message saying they were sorry this happened.
Now the game is released, with bugs. They did not release enough servers for the specific regions, ratio was something like 40pvp per one pve. This led to overpopulation and people unable to play since day one of the offical release.
I however do NOT recomend getting the game based on the dev actions above, atleast not for the current price of $104 (dlc + game). Yes its a great game, but you need to take history into consideration too.

And with the constant support and addition of many new weapons and frames to play as + the primes and raids you can now do make it for a great good time.
The aesthetic is great, all factions are easy to tell apart and have their iconic features, the sound design and music in this game is spot on and the theme and execution of being this highly adaptable force of unstoppable power at high end/late game status that you work hard to achieve is just compelling!
Warframe is the only game so far that has made it so satisfying to step into a room, use an ability and instagib most of it because you're THAT powerful or shooting that grenade launcher you put so much love into and it does thousands of damage that makes it seem almost unfair!
Couple all of that with an incredible manuevering / parkour system where you can avoid shots and have ridiculously high mobility that straight up makes you feel like a super hero soaring across maps and quickly dashing around make for an incredible game.
The business model is non intrusive you can get EVERYTHING CRUCIAL in the game 101% free, the paid currency system is used mostly for cosmetics or paying to skip build times on items, or straight buying them from the store but that's highly not worth the value most of the time when you can pay less to just rush it once you have the ingredients and blueprint making it so if you want to pay to have things and you have a ton of money to burn, is viable, but if you're smart with savings you're rewarded with much more not only from the market in game but from trading as well!
Most of the flaws I can think of are some performance issues and some bugs at certain maps, but honestly unless you get really unlucky or you're actively looking for those you should be pretty fine.
Summing it up: Great combat/ Great movement system/ Great business model/ Great game types/Great updates.
It's a game I've played for a long time now, and I'll definitely keep playing for many more years to come!

This being essentially, ninjas in space, I would say it is a fun experience. Though after some time it feels repetitive, there is more then enough fun to be had, exploring the wide variety of planets and vast customization. Being able to change the color of your ship's inside, outside, your warframe and weapons, overall something I personally enjoy from a game.
I do have complaints about the game basically stating some obvious things. Balancing being the biggest. There being certain warframes which everyone uses because they're easily over-powered with the proper mod configuration and weapon combination. Such frames like Frost are a good example, Valkyr being another which comes to mind. Mind you! I do not mean to crap on them, seeing as they're really fun to play as, but it just seems like you know you're screwed in conclave when you see a Frost coming your way.
As for mods and what they're good for? Many things, though it seems sort useless after you get a good... ten or so warframe mods, out about 30+ knowing you'll only be using Vitality, Redirection, Flow, and Intensity to name just a few, everyone gets them, and after fully maxing them out, there is nothing more in regard for 'modplay', similarly to weapon mods and modifications for your companions, the Kubrow and Sentinel. It seems like after you've forma'd your favorite warframe and weapons about four times (The equivalant to 'prestiging' in games like C.O.D) you only farm for mods.
By that point it is just a hunt for what you don't have, like the rarer mods like Quick Thinking, or Rage which have a low droprate. Meaning you better have a friend who uses Nekros and doesn't mind the verbal obuse from the community, seeing as Nekros can increase the droprate of any enemy-dropped item by 100%, or deal with the plentiful amounts of idiots in the trading interface in the game, those who wish to ask unreasonable prices for a weapon part or mod you've wanted a long time. Such things like asking for four or five mods which you've spent over 900,000 credits in combination across all of them so they can just waste them on another mod, or use them... in the end trading doesn't seem too worth it, but it is the only way to get the exclusive in-game currency 'Platinum' without going out and buying it.
Overall, things could use fixing, but the farming is somewhat addictive, the co-op play when playing with someone you know, can be really fun; and other then getting used to the game's startup (Getting used to how things work) it is a long fun ride which will be having me and hopefully others coming back for the future.
(Chroma needs a prime, and immortal skin... Chroma's love, Chroma's life.) xD

After some consideration I've decided to write my review on Ark after playing the game for 600 hours I believe I can make a accurate review to help some of you guys out. Now first off I gotta adress the paid DLC that everyone seems to hate. Now I don't mind the fact they released paid DLC because firstly it's only a $30.00 game which is on sale all the time so the total amount of money you'll spend it you also buy the DLC is $50.00 which is still less than a full price game. Now I would be mad about a $50.00 price tag if I didn't get my hours worth out of this game but I've got 600 hours so far and I don't plan on quiting just yet. So the question is would you like the game if you're considering buying it? Well... Do you like Dinosaurs? Do you like PVP/PVE Survival games? if you do then this game is a great choice, now the game can be very grindy and I am aware of that but the game gives you all the tools you need to play on a server that has increased XP rates and taming rates, gathering and ect so for all of you who keep saying this game is too grindy... play on a private server!!! Now I do have some complaints I should warn you all about, This game still is technically early access so you are going to run into bugs here and there but I've yet to run into many game breaking bugs but they are out there and they will really annoy you sometimes but hey that's why it's still early access and the few issues I've had of dino's falling through the floor and stuff I just sent a ticket to the Devs and in a few days they were over on our server and helped us get the Dino that fell under the map, The Devs care about this game and their community and that matters in my opinion. Just beware, this game contains trolls and greifers, expect to protect you stuff or lose it and don't complain if you lost the Rex you spent all that time taming if you're not prepared to defend it, and even then there are PVE servers where players cannot ruin your day. Ark lets you play it the way you want to play it and that's what I love about Ark not to mention the cool dino's and amazing moments me and my friends have had. Well... Good luck out there Surviving!

This game just has way too many issues and inconsistencies.
Coming from Rust, it's surprising to see that most servers are very low pop. Most people seem to prefer single player or just a server for them and their friends. I thought this was weird, because I would have thought a big part of the game would have been raiding with Dinos. Seems like that's a no.
The first biggest issue is the overall UI. It's SO AWFUL! Everything about it is bad. There are some icons at the bottom right of the screen to tell you how your overall health is, but they seem to break often and don't work until you die (Maybe?) or rejoin the server.
The crafting UI is incredibly cluttered and theres no way to hide useless♥♥♥♥♥♥that you don't want to see anymore (Thatch stuff) or search for something quickly. There's also some minor annoyances like having to unequip items to repair them (Though not requiring a repair bench like in Rust is a really nice quality of life improvement).
The way you build houses is incredibly primitive. Unlike Rust, where the foundation will automatically reach down into the ground to a certain height, this game's foundation is very tiny. You need to build somewhere VERY flat or else you won't be able to build a house that's very big. You also need to individually craft each item, instead of doing it in the far superior way Rust does things, which includes upgrading current structures.
The last thing that is just dumb about house building is that in order to make sure you're not night raided every single night is to have a nice strong door. Well, too bad. You need to be level 20 for a door that isn't complete garbage. So if you buy this game and play on a PvP server, don't expect your stuff to last the night. I'm not against night raiding, but it's ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t that you need to be such a high level in order to combat it.
The last thing that's bad about this game is levels. Dinosaur levels, in particular. Levels seem to do nothing but increase dinosaur HP. That's fine, for the bigger dinosaurs, but not ♥♥♥♥ing dodos and small dinos like that that you'll need to be farming for hide. It just makes them harder to kill, but doesn't give any more loot. This is stupid because every time you hit them they seem to glitch forward 5 or so feet, and then they maybe do it again before you can hit them. Then maybe they just glitch on top of a rock. Once you kill them their limp bodies fly forward, sometimes being unharvistable because they're beside a rock.
The framerate sucks too.
Overall, this game still needs a LOT of work. Why it's the highest pop survival game is beyond me. Also, why in the ♥♥♥♥ is there DLC for this game already? And who are the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who bought that?

I look at all the negative reviews lately complaining and snicker to myself. If people really didn't like this game, they wouldn't have spent hundreds of hours (largely 500+) playing it. And for anyone playing less than.. let's say a hundred hours couldn't possibly have experienced what ARK has to offer. These are simply humorous posts, at best.
As far as bugs and balance go, the Wildcard team has done an excellent job addressing most issues (Even the controversial flyer one) with a level of clarity you don't typically see with other developers. They do a good job of quickly fixing problems as they come up. Now that a majority have been taken care of, I think it is personally reasonable for them to change their pricing since the game is largely to the state that they would like it to be on release.
The time investment is a double-handed sword... It keeps you involved and makes it interesting to do so, but in order to feel like you have accomplished anything, you HAVE to invest that time. Ironically, both of these make the value you get for the price of the game sway heavily in your favor.
As for the pricing, I doubt I would have much qualms about buying this game for 60$. I may not have played for as long as some of the top guys writing the laughably negative reviews, but you don't need to spend that much time to realize how addictingly fun this game is (especially with friends).
If you like open worlds, dinosaurs, or being able to murder your own friends in hilarious fashion... this game is perfect for you.

ARK Evolved came out at the right time, before, there wasn't many Survival games to go around with, choices were scarce. Minecraft dominated the survival geinre then came 7 days to Die and for a while i was waiting for a really challenging survival game and then BANG here it come, ARK Evolve a stunning grpahic Survival game and the best is: it's got DINOSAURS, not only you can craft, build stuff but you can also tame the dinos for your own use.
What a fantastic concept, dinos are everyone childhood's dream, who doesn't like dinos? Who has never been fascinated by them?
ARK is a beautifull game, the graphics are amazing and let's face it, you WILL NOT enjoy the game if you don't upgrade your PC hardware, it's a very demanding game if you want to enjoy it at it's best.
There is no plot, no storyline, nothing that tie you to an end, you get drop in a world full of dinos, some are flriendly but many are dangerous So it's all down to you how you will survive (or die) and evolve in order to conquer this pre-historic wold.
-PvP wasn't my thing, i tried many times and unless you are lucky enough to join a dominant Tribe, life and progress is non-existant as my buildings and constructions and tamed dinos wouldnt last 3 weeks.
-PvE on the other hand is more peacefull, where you can measure progress, with no griefs from others than your own mistakes and bad luck, it's a nice way to learn about the game and maybe getting the experience for PvP.
Overall, excellent survival game with beautifull graphics and plenty to do but ARK will definately test your PC hardware to it's limits.
