Updated (and also actual) review :
Warframe is apparently a very good free to play game if you wanted to experience so-called "ninja simulator in space" then this would be the game you're looking for. For the 3000+ hours I myself put into this game just like any other games that you guys wanted to play as long as possible, and I can say so myself before I put good things about this game into this review just so you can foresee what's coming next when you start playing this game.
First of all, the game is grindy and requires "time" in order to progress most of the part in this game. Believe me when I already put three thousands hours into this game. So if you don't have time to spend in this game as much as anyone else like any other MMOs then I sugguest that you should absolutely look on to the other games. (No seriously, just look for something else)
If the paragraph above did not persuade you as much then I can say so myself that you have found one of the game that are worth putting your time in as much as possible just to "git-good" in this game. Think of it as arena shooter mixed with RPG elements to make up for Warframe.
Movements :
Despite that this game does not run in source or quake engine, but if you're fond of arena shooter which are quite fast (or normally paced depends on your perspective on gaming) you should find yourself adapting to the movement system (parkour 2.0) within a short time span.
Gun/Melee-play :
Firearms in this game is what you can expect from generic shooters mixed up with some RPG elements (crits/status/projectile/hitscan/etc.) and
Melees is what you're looking at nowadays hack-and-slash with some (but not much) combo system which can be earned through mods.
There are many types of firearms and melee ranging from a pistol to a rocket launcher, from a dagger to a greatsword, you "technically" name it, it would be in the game for sure.
Overall it's good on both, but as of now if you joined in the lobby with certain MR level and higher you would see mostly a single type of weapon more than expected which is expected in this kind of game.
Hoping to see diversities? It is there, but faded out through the end-game to favor the meta.
Characters (Warframes) :
Warframe is in the range of MOBAs types of abilities. 4 skills with an exception of "no cooldown" cited by the devs so that Warframes could be Warframe as of is today. The newer frames (shortened writing of "Warframe(s)" and reworked one are more based to synergy so prepare to combo skills more often when you're going to play this game (alone or with friends).
The reason where loot and currency is not in the gameplay section is that I wanted to talk something about this to clear up some questions and how pros&cons at one of the core part of the game.
Loot :
It is an action rpg shooter. You kill enemies, and you expect it to drop items just like in any other RPG games. It actually keep you to keep playing this game to further find things that you don't have. But sometimes this game like to go far on some cases for example, a stance, remember I've said something about combo system earlier? Well, you can only use a real combo after you earned a stance, and sometimes the one that are actually good or newer ones that are added in the update barely drops at all. Also the primes (the better varaints of the original model) have 3 RNGs steps to be exact here's the scenario,
1) Get the relic of the primes you wanted to get, but
2) It doesn't always drop the one that you really need
3) After you obtain the relic you must fight with another RNG in order to get the loot
All of the steps above can be eased up to 4 times by having 3 more friends/players in your group, but as you know you're not your friends and they cannot be there at all times which is an obstacle for solo players (like myself). Don't (really) expect yourself to play alone to get really what you wanted otherwise you'll hit a very big grind wall.
The devs are expecting you to play this game casually (hell, even I am trying to shift myself into that section), but once in a while this breaks up and community complains for quite a bit that is also a harsh truth if you're willing to play this game.
Currency :
Just like any other F2P games, there's a premium currency to fuel their games. You can use this premium currency to : rush a crafted item,purchase an item/weapon/warframe,cosmetics,mods,etc.
You may look at this as a very bad intention to make people purchase more premium currency, but as an oversight of this game, most of the premium parts of this game are free with exception of some cosmetics which are only purchasable through premium currency. The constaint of "free" is hanged upon "time" where you wanted free premium items, but doesn't want to spend any money on it, this games provides that too only if you wait and play the game just like any other players would do so. It will come "eventually" which is quite a downer for some group of players.
Remember that grind wall that I've said earlier? It can also be removed with premium currency, or you can also casually play the game until you eventually get an item you needed.
Before I end this (actual) review I'd like to include the very short TL;DR version for the people out there who'd not like to read that paragraph for some reason :
Pros
+ Fast & Fun
+ Free to play
Cons
- Extreme Grinding
- Requires so much free time
P.S. : As most of the free to play games out there, yes there's a premium currency in this game too, and no, you do not require them (if most) at all in order to unlock some "premium" progress in this game. Most of the paid things in this game is mostly cosmetics, only do so if you want fashion for you and your friend's need.

If I could give this 2 thumbs down I would.
The dev team doesn't care what the customers want, they've made that very clear.  The game is not optimized at all, and is set to be considered finished in December.  I don't expect them to finish the game, at least not as a finished product.  The DLC they've added was supposed to be part of the main game, but instead of giving to us as an update they charge another 15 for it while still in Early Access.  The game is the funnest at early levels, there's even a mod called primitive+ but not alot of servers running it, or people playing it for that matter.  In fact, with that said, there's not alot of people playing Ark to begin with, most of the players seem to have given up.
Since I like restarting alot, I like extinction servers, which they have completely switched to the new Procedurally Generated (Randomized) map.  It sounds great!  Everything being randomized should be great!  It's not, at all.  90& of the maps it randomizes is choppy, ugly, and full of game crashing bugs.  In fact, the PGMaps don't even have all of the dinos in it, and you might even expect to find several Gigas running around which makes it completely unbalanced and horribly dangerous.  When I say game-crashing I mean expect to crash every 20 minutes, and if someone is riding a bronto the server might lag to the point you have 5fps.  The maps are much smaller than the standard ones.  As for the online playerbase, most of the servers that I've seen are nearly empty.  The extinction servers I liked so much, before the forced PGMaps, would run about 2-3 active players and maybe a dozen more not very active.  Now they're lucky to get 2-3 inactive players.
Pay to Win?  Since the game released the DLC only those buying it can play the desert maps and get the little dragon things.  Doesn't sound like a big deal.... until you can transfer them to other maps.  Yes, you can transfer DLC content from the DLC servers to the normal Ark servers!  Talk about completely breaking the balance of the game...  it's a huge step towards pay to win.
Also, when complaining to the devs about unexpected/unscheduled server whipes, glitches, bugs, etc their response is "thank you for your input" and "give it another try upon full release" - Jaeger.  Have a problem?  Response time is about 3 days.  When the PGMaps first came out about half the people couldn't connect to them, I think it was certain AMD processors.  It took them about 3 weeks to fix it, all the while keeping everyone in the dark about it and putting their new Halloween event in the hot-seat.

The game is fun with friends, building a fortified town with an army of dinos is quite enjoyable.
ARK can be incredibly frustrating at times though; the PVP in general is very buggy, none of the firearms are fun to shoot, dinosaurs have no physical indicators to show how injured they are, the movement feels ice-skatey, I could go on.
ARK is very poorly optimized, even on the highest settings the game doesn't look particularly impressive and yet runs with less FPS than GTA 5 being played on a playstation 2. If you want 60 FPS with anything less than a GTX 970 you're barking up the wrong tree, and I'm talking lowest settings here.
Another gripe I have is the levelling system, it's utterly pointless and serves only to slow progression in an effort to increase the time spent playing. Player levelling aside, dinosaur levelling is even more redundant. You could have a level 200 dodo and a level 1 dodo and they'd be equally easy to kill, what's more the bigger dinos with incredibly high levels are plopped in the same areas of the island where the lower levelled dinos so there's absolutely no sense of progression.
And let's get to the entire reason I'm writing this review: 'ARK: Survival Evolved', a pre-release early access game, has a DLC with a £15 price tag. To those of you who don't find this incredibly strange, Vanilla ARK is an incomplete game rife with bugs and feels generally just unfinished. Releasing paid DLC for an incomplete game is equivilant to making a car with no wheels and then selling people custom made spoilers.
And the saddest part of all of this is I have 105 hours logged on this game, will probably buy the DLC and plan on playing it a lot more throughout the winter holiday.

The core combat of Warframe is straightforward. This is a third-person action game in which you wield two primary weapons and a melee weapon against foes who are largely content to come right at you. You also gain suit powers that allow you to dash and slash through a bunch of enemies, or stun all foes within a certain radius, though these abilities can change drastically depending on what suit you equip. You could unleash fiery maelstroms, turn invisible, create a decoy, use teleportation to switch places with an enemy, or manipulate your foes to fight against their allies. Acquiring new suits, however, requires a significant investment of time or money

Release review:
One of ,if not the greatest survival game ever released. a must buy for anyone who enjoys survival, building or dinosaurs.
EA review:
Very fun survival game, dinosaurs make everything better. This can be seen by it being in the top 10 played games everyday.
it is a huge game with tons of mods and a massive community, theres so much to do it will take hundreds, if not thousands of hours to do it all.
PROs:
- big maps that take along time to cross even when flying.
- variety of maps with 4 officials and many modded.
- variety of dino's and mammals to tame, breed and keep you entertained.
- rideable dinos arnt hard to get even early on, dinos help with day to day gathering and killing.
- big crafting system for buildings, weapons, tools and high level cap (for players and dino's).
- very free building mode, can make a base almost anywhere. (underwater bases aswell)
- realistic in most aspects or as close to as a game should be.
- large variety of clutter, colors and visual effects so no 2 places look the same.
- many many mods and settings to edit your game as you choose.
- updates almost every week with either new content or fixes, mostly fixes as its end of EA.
Cons:
- bit buggy at times, gets better every patch.
- fps can be low on older systems but not unplayable (50+ on gtx960 on med/high).
- grindy if you dislike grinds nothing comes quick in ark except death.
- apparently bad public servers and PVP (i only play PVE private) run by alpha tribes.
- scaling can be bad, started naked with nothing and a Trex was right infront of me (doesnt happen often) a trex can die to a small bird if the level difference is high.
- long haul game, dont expect to finish this game quick even with a clan, this game requires months of work if you want to finish the content (achievements and big bosses).
- breeding system is difficult and long winded but needed for end game content.
- strong dinos can take a long time to tame (multiple hours) and could die before you get them.
- very easy to lose everything and have to start from scratch.
Dont listen to most of the bad reviews that complain about the servers, every game has bad servers at one point or another. happens once and everyone goes mad. same with the flyer nerf it isnt 'game breaking' and makes the game more fun and its definetly worth the asking price, almost 300 hours in at time of writing and nowhere near done everything.
Overall 9.5/10 great game.

the characteres one meets get repititive, say always the same stuff, and etc. nothing special there in terms of being an online game. not complaining here neither.
the trading system is crazy, you can't actually trade what you buy with real money (in-game platinum being moderately fair) but at the same time you can't buy with real money what you can trade but from other players, so if you don't get it from a drop or special store with in-game value, you have to buy it from other players, and some prices then to go all the way up to craziness.
The crafting system, oh good ol' warframe crafting system, the most bothersome thing in the galaxy, from 7 to 24 hours for a weapon, from 1 day to 9 days for warframe. jesus if it slow, and one can't speed it up but with platinum. but still, I can't complain. becuase in the end you can always make everything, worth it, for free.
The pet system, kubrows and sentinels. now that i have 374 hours in this game i decided its time for me to write a review,
started on my own, had a friend join, hes almost never online, but when i need him for an alpha rex, he's got my back
joined forces with another tribe a while ago, havent been able to get a giga yet but we got two quetzals and a large amount of rexes and spinos (selling the lower levels now tho)
anyways, lets get to the review.
the idea of the game itself, is great, and ARK:SE is easily superior to all the other (dinosaur) survival games out there
be prepared to face bugs, it rarely happens that you lose (a) dino(s) because of a bug, like a predator spawning inside your base while it wasnt supposed to, WildCard is most likely to give you those dino's back if you make a ticket about it
my tribemates lost a high lvl argentavis and they just spawned us one in of the same level
the only difference was that its experience requirements for level up got reset to that of a creature you tamed a minute ago x) if i recall correctly it is level 263 or something now, its insane (for me and my tribemates anyway)
even though sometimes a patch comes with something that causes me (and most likely others too) to crash every now and then, some patches give off this effect more than others, it can be annoying, but it doesnt happen 100% of the time
it is early access / alpha stage, so if you decide to buy this game (i recommend getting it on a sale) you need to be prepared to face bugs and accept the results coming from them, so dont whine when your freshly caught rex vanishes into thin air, just write a support ticket explaining anything you know about the bug
the Scorched Earth expansion pack looks very nice, i dont have it yet though, hoping for it to be 50% off sometime, otherwise im not really that interested in having to maintain a bunch of dinos on yet another server
you need a tribe!
at least 3 people i'd say
if you dont have time to play, for example you and your family are going to sweden for two weeks and you cant take your gaming pc with you, you are going to need tribemates to make sure your base doesnt get destroyed and your dinos dont get unclaimed, so dont play alone
other than the inactive friend i had noone else to play with, had a few "friendships" with nearby players but me joining them wouldnt profit them, so they wouldnt accept me either.
i have been able to play on a daily basis at the start, though after a while it turned into just getting online to spend like half an hour gathering enough meat and berries to keep my dinosaurs fed, and once that was finished i would already be tired of playing, i decided to ask a nearby tribe to merge, and we did, at first it was for me to be able to be online a lot less, but soon enough i found it a lot more enjoyable to play together rather than alone, and spent just as time as i used to on the game every day or once every two days, now even doing tames and expansions again rather than just dealing with the dinos being fed.
(long story short, join a tribe)
some people have this, some dont, there appears to be a memory leak that makes even 32gb ram computers lagg and/or crash, even if you play on "extremely low memory" mode, turning down a bunch of video settings ingame helps a lot with this though, you'll need to choose between quality or quantity (quantity being time spent on the game before you crash)
the concept of the game easily gets a 9,5/10
the game as a whole i am going to give a 6/10 for this moment
but i do see a lot of potention in this game, and if they end up fixing everything and finishing up all they intended to add to this, this could easily become a 10/10 game
your choice wether you want to wait for it to go out of its alpha testing phase or join the testing
and if you do want to wait, just put this game in the top 5 of your wishlist, so you dont forget about it :)

This is an amazing game, I highly recommend it to action / shooter (TPS) lovers.
The developer of this game (Digital Extremes) is a very dedicated team that develops this game with the help of the community, and for real. Prime time (Livestream with the Rebecca (community manager) and Megan (community coordinator) playing and showcasing updated content) every week, and Devstream (livestream with the game developers in which they talk about incoming updates and discuss topics proposed by the community) every 2 weeks.
Moreover, Warframe now supports Steam Workshop and players have already started to create amazing skins for the game.
As for the game itself,
+ good graphics
+ great agility and fluid movement
+ player-set pacing
+ great backstory and lore
+ no problems in matchmaking
+ no such thing as P2W
+ challenging endgame content
+ great customizability
+ lots of content updated very often
+ smooth learning curve
+ great community and developer
+ events
- farming / grinding can take a lot of time
- minor bugs and glitches, although it is frequently patched
I have over 1.2k hours in this game and I'm nowhere near quitting, I hope you'll join us!
UPDATE: 2.5k and counting..
P.S.: Don't buy the DLCs, the single worthy part is the platinum, which you can buy for a fraction of the price (Honor pack (18 euros - 300 pt) versus 370 pt - $5 (with 75% off coupon that you can get as daily reward) ;)

***THIS REVIEW IS ABOUT THE LAUNCHER, NOT THE GAME***
I honestly couldn't get into the game because of the terrible launcher.
Let me lay this out in the steps I took.
1: I downloaded the game, and spent a good part of a week downloading it due to my relatively slow internet connection, and lots of off hours.
2: I opened up the program to find out that instead of downloading the actual game, I only downloaded the base of it and still had to download the updates through the launcher.
3: I let the launcher utilize my full internet bandwidth for a ridiculous amount of time while it tries to download it's updates. Why they couldn't just channel their updates through steam, I'm not sure.
4: The launcher then replies telling me that it can't download it's updates. Note this is after nearly an hour of utilizing 100% of my bandwidth. There was nothing telling me how much it had downloaded, what it was downloading, nothing... I had to assume before this notice that it was updating itself because it refused to even tell me that.
5: I quit the launcher, and ignored it for about a week until one of my friends begged me to try again.
6: I startup the launcher again, and this time it actually tells me that it's downloading an update.
7: Launcher stops counting down on the update when the update reaches 3.1 MB left to download.
8: Launcher CONTINUES to download at top speed for another 15 minutes after that.
9: Launcher reports that the servers are offline, and it can't download the update, but yet at the same time it continues to download at top speeds this entire time...
10: I wait another 5 minutes for the launcher to try to reconnect to it's downloading servers, note that it's still downloading something this entire time.
11: I kill the launcher in disgust.
12: I open up the launcher again... it hides itself in the background, and continues downloading not presenting itself so that I can't kill it.
13: I have to use a special program to kill the launcher to stop it from downloading.
14: I once again try to open up the launcher, it once again hides itself in the background, and I once again have to kill it with a special program.
I am going to be blatently honest... I don't know the game, and I wanted to play it... it looks cool. This launcher however has this strange habit of downloading things without telling me what it's downloading, while even telling me that it can't download anything. For anyone who knows anything about computers, that raises millions of red flags.
Fix your launcher, make it more user friendly, fix it's bugs, message me on this comment, I'll try again, and I'll change the tone of this comment if your launcher behaves itself.
Until then, to everyone who reads this comment, understand that the launcher of this game is unreliable. It downloads without telling you what it's downloading. It's constantly locking up and refuses to respond to commands. It has a habit of hiding itself in the background while downloading. All these things make me not trust it.

after 1286.7 hours I figured it was time I contributed to the comment section for this game.  I will state a few things that are obvious for most, but people who have yet to play may be skeptical.  The game still need to be optimized more, when I first started playing this game on my 4-5 year old PC(with failing parts) I was playing on 1-20 fps, then I replaced the damaged PSU and jumped up to 30-40 fps with medium graphics.  I will try to best describe my first experience compared to a few from later on in my game play time.
(Old PC) 8GB RAM DDR3, an old i5, GTX 760 2GB, 750GB HDD 30-40fps(medium graphics)
(New PC) 16GB RAM DDR4, an i7 4.0ghz and a GTX 970 6GB and a 250GB SSD 30-40fps(Ultra graphics) and more if I lower the graphics a smidge for increased perfmormance
*Disclaimer* - I play on Unofficial servers as a personal preference from other open world sandbox and survival games, so my experiences does not reflect in official server game play.
I remember first spawning on the Island you hear the air, the dinos, the water.  You step back and take in the immersive and beautiful atmosphere, you gawk in wonder and amazement at the artwork.  Then I walked around trying to figure out what to do and were to begin.  I walk around and foraged some plants and was finding new kinds of berries and fiber.  I ran around the beach collecting rocks and was punching some drift wood trees littering the beach.  I remember watching some videos on the night time on the server to I constucted a 4x4 thatch house with a small fireplace and was satisfied with my work even though it was just a small shack.  I found out that dilos are dangerous and that dodo's are a good early source of meat and leather.  I built my way up to around level 10, I wanted a raptor because it is one of the nostalgic  dinosaurs like the TRex, Bronto, and Pteradon.  I managed to knock out a little raptor, my heart was racing but I never tamed anything before and was clueless on how to do so.  Hope fading for getting a new found friend as I noticed his torpor bar fading rapidly.  Then it happened, my first player on player contact since playing the game.  My screen shook and i ran sporaticaly for cover, poor choice, a huge TRex came blasting through the bushes and i thought i was toast.  Then I notice a player on his back and became nervouse but hopeful.  I am not nieve, I have played these type of games before and I know he could just off me at any moment.  To my surprise he doesnt he actually hops down and helps me out, even helps me tame my raptor and even made me a saddle :).  That was my first experience with this game and it really pulled me in.
Now yes I have taken breaks and some for longer than others like my most recent break.  I have worked solo, in tribes(big and small), but the one thing I like most of all is ramping up on a new server and surviving.  Running through the woods hear raptors in hot persuite and the only thing you got is cloth clothes and a sharp wooden stick.  Running, panting, dipping, juking, the raptor reaches you and bites you just as you jump from a ledge and splash into the water.  You look up the cliffside with a smirk because you just got away.............only to be eaten by a school of piranhas that just happened to notice your splash.
So would I recommend this game? most definatly.  I bought this game on a sale and its given me over 1.2k hours of entertainment.  The graphics are gorgeous, the gameplay is fun, and of course freaking dinos land air and sea what ever may fit your needs.   Want to go slow on a server with a small shack you can, want to go for soley PVP and work your way up to the rife and scope and then make a guilie suite and pick off player, you can.  Want to war bases on the back of large land air or sea dinos and raid a base in an epic battle, you can.  I have built structors that would amaze, tamed and raised dinos who got their names noticed on servers I have played on.  I have single handedly fought of raid groups with who were armed with 3 Quetz(huge bird) that were equiped with missle turrents and gatling turrents, as well as Argents(giant hawks) with nothing more than 1 Pteradon and gurrila tactics.  Never have I felt more alive than when I have played this game.  The only time I have felt my nerves peak as much is when your playing H1Z1 or Dayz(mod or stand-alone) and as you are looting you hear the door to the room your in open.
TLDR- Fun experiences both good and bad, amazing graphics, great to play with friends, and would strongly recommend this game and as many souls series players will state be prepared to die because its going to happen.  Happy surviving and good luck to all of you ;)

While occasionally lacking in polish, Warframe feels and plays great. The basis of the game is running around, somersaulting and filling grunts with bullets while earning some sweet loot. The core gameplay is solid - everything is smooth and meshes together well. Jumping around while lodging arrows and blades in skulls is fun enough even after thirty minutes in the same spot (which you probably will do at least once).
The primary gripe people have with this game is the grind. It is true that some items can take dozens of hours to get depending on luck. However, the gameplay is plenty fun enough to make up for it, and the bulk of the grind is just to try out everything. It should be no problem getting near the top in 150 hours or so - but getting everything else may take much longer.
The new player experience also needs some work - a lot of mechanics go unexplained, or explanations hidden deep within menus. A lot of information can only be found on the wiki, so be preapared to go there. But even before you know what to look up, you will have to figure out a lot of stuff on your own.
If you tried this more than a year ago, it's defninitely worth giving another try. The game is constantly updated, with major foundation changes every couple months. Since I started playing a year and a half ago, they revamped the melee system, trashed the menu screen for a personal ship, added an open-space gamemode, re-built the movement system, added storyline quests, added hubs, made 5 new tilesets, all while releasing 7 new characters and countless new weapons.

I have hundreds of hours in Warframe.
I cannot in good conscience recommend it to anyone.
Warframe features some of the best moment to moment game play around. You truly take the role of one of many space ninjas. Exciting movement, gliding through the air, hacking and blasting and casting. Its exciting.
But the entire game is built completely around RNG. Everything is a grind. Warframes are obtained one piece at a time, from bosses. You just grind until each part drops once (average of 5 - 6 times total for three parts) and THEN you STILL buy the Blueprint from the market for in game currency.
And so it goes. All the best stuff in the game is free. It just requires hour and hours of endless RNG grind. Which wouldnt be so bad, except the game features a very limited selection of mission types, and in the late game forces you to run certain types for certain rewards - or, well, chances at rewards - whether you enjoy that type or not.
All of which is a shame. For a game this fun, with game play this exciting, to lean solely on RNG and exploitative business practices is a disappointment.

Where should one begin when describing Ark? It is one of the most breath taking, stunning and visually beautiful first person survival games that is out there at this moment but that doesn't really fill up the bio. To say that it is just a regular "good graphics minecraft clone"  would be a real understatement as well.Ark is it's  own thing in many aspects.
The fact you are just dropped in and expected to figure out how to survive on your own is in itself frightening but also incredibly rewarding. There are no handholding in this game, and if it were a dino would probably use that as an excuse to rip your arm off.
The way the whole game works is amazing, you really have to work with the world and use it's own flaws to your advantage to be able to survive, and survival is a factor throughout this game. If it's not the dinosaurs threatening your life it's other players and the constant risk of getting raided and pillaged. I can say this however, it is not a game for the gamers who just want a story driven game that carries you along for a ride, if you want to fully enjoy Ark you have to put in the time and effort to learn and love it.
(-)
It is a bit rough around the edges sometime for instance the optimization and performance is quite lacking at times but it is still being worked on by the devs as we speak and they are pumping out updates more often than any other devs in any other game I have ever played so it's safe to say you will not feel forgotten at the playground in this game.
The grind times are a bit ridiculous at times but it is also understandable as it would otherwise be impossible to begin anew on a server or it would be too easy to climb the social food chain.
You are very often left at the mercy of the strongest tribes on the server and as we all know people on the internet have no mercy and no filters but that is something you really cant get away from with online games.
All in all this game is a solid 8/10 for me and I highly recommend it to people who are into the survival game genre.

The game offers a lot of wonderful basebuilding survival.
But it suffers one major fault, each and EVERY official online server is run by whats popularly known as an "Alpha-tribe", these alpha tribes has way to many easy options to effortlessly wipe every other tribe off the map.
Since launch this has only been made easier and easier, by adding DMD's (Dino's of Mass Destruction), like the Giganotosaurus, and various other choice weapons, like the dodorex etc.
These dino's are so powerful, and at the same time, nearly impossible for small tribes to get their hands on, that when first an alpha-tribe has manifested itself on a server, they wipe everyone else in the fear of getting overthrown, and so essentially play on their own online server - solo...
Normally i don't mind the scruffs and skirmishes of pvp, i normally thrive in such games, but with the amount of time required to tame, build and maintain a foothold on a server, the more important it gets to be able to at least make it hard, or undesireable for large alpha-tribes to wipe you out.
But as the game is now, and the direction it has gotten since day one, there is vastly more focus on bigger and stronger offensive weapons, that is just way too easily obtainable for the already big and established, in fact encourages them to just plainly kill everyone, makin all servers i have tried, ghost servers with scattered ruins the only evidence there was ever another tribe than the alpha-tribe.
For me to recommend the game, they would need to either start taking the game in another direction, or to make a new pvp-gamemode where wiping someone out comes with a cost, and not be free and easy as soon as you've got a Giganotosaurus.

While occasionally lacking in polish, Warframe feels and plays great. The basis of the game is running around, somersaulting and filling grunts with bullets while earning some sweet loot. The core gameplay is solid - everything is smooth and meshes together well. Jumping around while lodging arrows and blades in skulls is fun enough even after thirty minutes in the same spot (which you probably will do at least once).
The primary gripe people have with this game is the grind. It is true that some items can take dozens of hours to get depending on luck. However, the gameplay is plenty fun enough to make up for it, and the bulk of the grind is just to try out everything. It should be no problem getting near the top in 150 hours or so - but getting everything else may take much longer.
The new player experience also needs some work - a lot of mechanics go unexplained, or explanations hidden deep within menus. A lot of information can only be found on the wiki, so be preapared to go there. But even before you know what to look up, you will have to figure out a lot of stuff on your own.
If you tried this more than a year ago, it's defninitely worth giving another try. The game is constantly updated, with major foundation changes every couple months. Since I started playing a year and a half ago, they revamped the melee system, trashed the menu screen for a personal ship, added an open-space gamemode, re-built the movement system, added storyline quests, added hubs, made 5 new tilesets, all while releasing 7 new characters and countless new weapons.

After 480 hours in this game I think to myself "was that time well spent?" looking out the window I come up with my answer "YEAH IT WAS!" Warframe is an absolutly awesome game. It is a game about freakin space ninjas, whats not to like. It is an RPG, whats not to like. Its FREE, whats not to like. there is absolutly no reason for you not to try it out if you haven't already and if you have and you are burned out, get some friends, make a caln with a name that only you guys would understand, and do void missions and make millions of bucks (or credits).
I have spent a lot of time playing warframe. I made my account a little over a year ago in update 13. Since then, the game is almost un recognizable. The only things that are the same are the weapons, warframes, a couple of the bosses, and a couple of the tile sets. This is why I have been kept to one burn out in that time.
When I started playing warframe, my most played game on steam was star wars battlefront 2 and I had 24 hours on it. My friends got me into warframe right as summer break started and I spent almost the entire summer playing warframe (Half ot that time was probably spent farming nerodes for anyone who remembers farming survival on earth). I burned out aound update 14.5 and didn't get back into it until update 16.5. That might sound like a long time but it was only a couple of months. That is how fast the game changes.
The devs are always working to change the game for the better and you can see that in all of the content the devs post on twitch and youtube.
Warframe is like any other online gam, it is going to be hard for new players to fit in. Warframe is very grindy. I have heard people call it warfarm because the farm involved can get extremely intense. However if you can handle the farm, The result is very rewarding.
Another thing that turns people off warframe is that it is free. The steriotipical free game now is full of in game purchases . Warframe does have in game purchases but by no means do you need to buy anything. That being said, If you ask anyone who has been playing the game for a while, 999999/100000 of them will tell you they have bought some amount of platinum (what you buy). There is no reason to say that warframe is pay to win and that is why you don't play it. Everything can be obtained in game without platinum except cosmetics which don't really do anything but look different.
Overall, Warframe is a fantastic game. If you can put up with the grind and the ocassonal bugs (which are usually pretty hilarious) and you like RPGs, you should try this game out.

I have hundreds of hours in Warframe.
I cannot in good conscience recommend it to anyone.
Warframe features some of the best moment to moment game play around. You truly take the role of one of many space ninjas. Exciting movement, gliding through the air, hacking and blasting and casting. Its exciting.
But the entire game is built completely around RNG. Everything is a grind. Warframes are obtained one piece at a time, from bosses. You just grind until each part drops once (average of 5 - 6 times total for three parts) and THEN you STILL buy the Blueprint from the market for in game currency.
And so it goes. All the best stuff in the game is free. It just requires hour and hours of endless RNG grind. Which wouldnt be so bad, except the game features a very limited selection of mission types, and in the late game forces you to run certain types for certain rewards - or, well, chances at rewards - whether you enjoy that type or not.
All of which is a shame. For a game this fun, with game play this exciting, to lean solely on RNG and exploitative business practices is a disappointment.

I've spent a fair amount of time with Warframe and, I'm going to say it, I have been hooked. I initially wanted to start playing last year but I only had a low end laptop at the time. Having invested a bit of cash into a proper desktop, I can see that my patience wasn't wasted.
I've seen a number of reviews brand this game as a grind fest. Admittedly yes, there are times where you contemplate going after this one item that has a low drop rate but, for the most part, it doesn't feel like effort. It doesn't FEEL like a grind. There's so many different ways to play based on which warframe you're playing, which weapons and mods you have equipped, whether you want to play solo or in a group. Having this flexibility to play leaves so many possibilities.
And the lore, oh my god, the lore that has been produced so far has been incredible. And more is being released all the time with new quests and warframes. It keeps you questioning what really happened for things to get how they are and where things are headed.
Even when you don't feel like doing missions, you can hang out at your clan dojo, enjoy some of the mini games and things that they have there, or potter around the relays and see other people with their warframes. I think DE has created something great and I hope it lasts. I would definitely label this game as an enjoyable experience that keeps giving and surprising.

Alrighty... Like everyone points out, this game isn't exactly optimised. But I have the joy of owning a PC that regardless of it being around 10 years old, it will still run 'most' games, even if incredibly poorly. So with ARK, so long as I start at the lowest possible settings, I can slowly tweak them up to around mid-range with only a little bit of FPS drop. And since I am terrible at combat anyway, that doesn't bother me so much provided I can still flee at 1fps.
Anyhow, this game truly brings me to awe. When I play a game, I am in it for the immersion, and this game certainly meets those standards. As a solo player, the only creature I have tamed is a dodo and it lived for around five minutes. Every person I have ever come across usually shoves their spear down my throat. Every morning my water pipes have been torn down by some bored person or dino. Every base I've ever built has been raided by the time I log back on. But none of this matters because it really makes you feel cautious about your surroundings.
Instead of settling down, I decided to live the pirate life. Got myself a raft, hooked up a ballista turret, and started raining terror on random peoples walls for no reason what so ever. Watching people panic at the thought of being raided, and seeing them helplessly run around not knowing what to do sincwe you're in the middle of an ocean made me kinda happy. Then about an hour later I accidentally sailed into the range of an auto turret and lost my boat and cried. Soooo....
Overall this game is immensely fun if you're not taking things too seriously and don't expect your base to still be there when you sign back on the next day. Party play is the best way to survive (and the only way to truly experience the entire game), but solo play is definitely entertaining and it's fun to mess with people.

Oh good lord, what can I say about Warframe? Well I'm sure if you take a look at my play time which is 781.9 hours (at the time of this review), that alone should say it all. But I'm not gonna waste this review by leaving it at that so I will get into specifics.
YOUR A FRIGGIN SPACE NINJA! This is the concept of an imaginative five year old, but you know what? It's glorious when it is executed the way Warframe did. You can run, jump, wall run (actually it's more like wall hopping) and even bullet dive.
You get to choose from (currently and not including primes) 25 warframes with each of them having their own unique stats, abilities and play-styles. They can range from the frail but stealthy warframe to the big bruiser/tanky warframe. Each Warframe goes up to rank 30 and are upgraded with mods that add stats or passive properties to your warframe.
You get to wield all these cool weapons. You have your standard primary weapon which can be assault rifles, shotguns, sniper rifles, flamethrowers, bows, even rocket launchers. You have a secondary weapon which are pistols, throwing daggers, or arm mounted casters. Melee weapons which range from basic straight swords to giant hammers. Along with warframes, weapons have their own sets of mods too.
You also get companions that support you out on the field like the Sentinels (little floating droids) and the Kubrows (dogs) which do things from cloak you when enemies are near, to gathering loot that is laying on the ground for you. Your companions use mods as well
Warframes, weapons, and sentinels as well as a few other things can be either bought with real money or crafted in the foundry. The blueprints for frames and weapons can be bought with in-game credits. Once you have purchased the blueprint, it will appear in your foundry. Here it will display the required components needed to craft the item, the credit cost, and the time it will take to make the item. Once you have the items and the credits you can craft the item. Once you have started, there will be a timer that displays the amount of time it takes to make the item. You can rush the crafting process with real money. When it's done, you claim the item and a shiny new gun is now ready for use. Be aware that to make a warframe you need to build the components for it first (the helmet, the systems, and the chassis). After that you put them together using the warframe blueprint itself. Most warframe component blueprints are dropped from bosses. Some are dropped as rare drops and some are only found on alert missions.
Each warframe, weapon, and companion has a set number of mod space. The default amount at max level is 30 points. However you can economize your mod space by taking advantage of the polarity slots that halves the cost of a mod if the polarity of the slot matches the mod itself. You can add and change polaritises using an item called Forma that can be crafted from blueprints which are found in the special void stages or alert missions. You can also double the mod capacity by using Orokin Catalysts or Reactors (aka Potatos)
Every player has a ship where they do all of their shopping, crafting, customizing, and mission selecting. You start off with a Liset, but you can also craft the Mantis which change the effects of the air support item you can craft,
Form the ship, you choose your missions that are separated into planets. There are 14 planets to choose from with each one being populated by one of the three enemy types. On each planet there are nodes that have the missions themselves. This missions are up to four player co-op missions that can range from killing all the enemies in the area to collecting data packs from terminals through out the level to assasinating a boss. On top of missions in nodes, there are alert missions which give you rewards that other missions usually don't such as an increased ammount of credits, rare resources, rare mods, and even Orokin Catalysts and Reactors for your weapons and warframes. There are also invasion missions which allows you to participate in conflicts between the enemy factions. Each side will offer you a reward which you must choose from. Once you have finished these conflicts you will recieve your reward after the conflict is resolved. You may also get a message from some individuals who arent happy with your decision of choosing the other faction over their's. You might also be reminded that your actions have concequences by a certain individual. There is also currently two raid modes which consist of eight player co-op missions that are much different than the regular missions. The end rewards to the raids are special auras that can be applied to your cosmetic items that give you passive buffs when you wear them. There are also the void missions which can be accessed using tower keys that are awarded in some missions. Here you can get rare resources as well as components for Prime equipment which are like normal warframes and weapons but with better stats and cooler looks
The game is mostly co-op, but there is the Conclave for those who would rather get competitive with some PVP. The modes here range from Deathmatches to Capture the Flag (Capture the Cephalon). Each warframe and weapons have been optimized for PVP use.
Once you complete the mission, you are rewarded with credits (in-game currency) resources, mods for your warframe, and affinity (XP).
This is the usual routine for a typical Warframe player: Select warframe, select weapons, go on mission, complete mission, rinse and repeat. You might be thinking, that it sounds very tedious and repetative. You would be correct. However, Warframe has just enough varienty in missions and enough goals to shoot for that it makes it rather satisfying.
For the most part, the community of Warframe are rather supportive of each other. Being that the game is mostly co-op people are more inclined to help one another. Me and my group of friends actually made a clan dedicated to helping the new people. Things may turn sore when it comes to the two raid modes if people don't know what they are doing. But I did say "for the most part."
In the market, blueprints and some items can be purchased with the in-game credits. But most items are bought using Platinum which can be aquired by spending real money. With platinum, you can buy cosmetics, weapons if you don't want to go through the process of crafting them, boosters (affinity, credit, resource) and resources if you don't feel like farming for them. Platinum can also be used as currency for the player driven market. Players advertise in the trade chat what they are looking to sell or buy. Items consist of Prime equipment blueprints and components, special weapons, void keys, mods, and much more.
I'm not sure what it is about Warframe, but I'm more than willing to throw a couple bucks their way every once in a while. Most MMOs I refrain from spending money on, but I gladly spend disposable income here.

Oh good lord, what can I say about Warframe? Well I'm sure if you take a look at my play time which is 781.9 hours (at the time of this review), that alone should say it all. But I'm not gonna waste this review by leaving it at that so I will get into specifics.
YOUR A FRIGGIN SPACE NINJA! This is the concept of an imaginative five year old, but you know what? It's glorious when it is executed the way Warframe did. You can run, jump, wall run (actually it's more like wall hopping) and even bullet dive.
You get to choose from (currently and not including primes) 25 warframes with each of them having their own unique stats, abilities and play-styles. They can range from the frail but stealthy warframe to the big bruiser/tanky warframe. Each Warframe goes up to rank 30 and are upgraded with mods that add stats or passive properties to your warframe.
You get to wield all these cool weapons. You have your standard primary weapon which can be assault rifles, shotguns, sniper rifles, flamethrowers, bows, even rocket launchers. You have a secondary weapon which are pistols, throwing daggers, or arm mounted casters. Melee weapons which range from basic straight swords to giant hammers. Along with warframes, weapons have their own sets of mods too.
You also get companions that support you out on the field like the Sentinels (little floating droids) and the Kubrows (dogs) which do things from cloak you when enemies are near, to gathering loot that is laying on the ground for you. Your companions use mods as well
Warframes, weapons, and sentinels as well as a few other things can be either bought with real money or crafted in the foundry. The blueprints for frames and weapons can be bought with in-game credits. Once you have purchased the blueprint, it will appear in your foundry. Here it will display the required components needed to craft the item, the credit cost, and the time it will take to make the item. Once you have the items and the credits you can craft the item. Once you have started, there will be a timer that displays the amount of time it takes to make the item. You can rush the crafting process with real money. When it's done, you claim the item and a shiny new gun is now ready for use. Be aware that to make a warframe you need to build the components for it first (the helmet, the systems, and the chassis). After that you put them together using the warframe blueprint itself. Most warframe component blueprints are dropped from bosses. Some are dropped as rare drops and some are only found on alert missions.
Each warframe, weapon, and companion has a set number of mod space. The default amount at max level is 30 points. However you can economize your mod space by taking advantage of the polarity slots that halves the cost of a mod if the polarity of the slot matches the mod itself. You can add and change polaritises using an item called Forma that can be crafted from blueprints which are found in the special void stages or alert missions. You can also double the mod capacity by using Orokin Catalysts or Reactors (aka Potatos)
Every player has a ship where they do all of their shopping, crafting, customizing, and mission selecting. You start off with a Liset, but you can also craft the Mantis which change the effects of the air support item you can craft,
Form the ship, you choose your missions that are separated into planets. There are 14 planets to choose from with each one being populated by one of the three enemy types. On each planet there are nodes that have the missions themselves. This missions are up to four player co-op missions that can range from killing all the enemies in the area to collecting data packs from terminals through out the level to assasinating a boss. On top of missions in nodes, there are alert missions which give you rewards that other missions usually don't such as an increased ammount of credits, rare resources, rare mods, and even Orokin Catalysts and Reactors for your weapons and warframes. There are also invasion missions which allows you to participate in conflicts between the enemy factions. Each side will offer you a reward which you must choose from. Once you have finished these conflicts you will recieve your reward after the conflict is resolved. You may also get a message from some individuals who arent happy with your decision of choosing the other faction over their's. You might also be reminded that your actions have concequences by a certain individual. There is also currently two raid modes which consist of eight player co-op missions that are much different than the regular missions. The end rewards to the raids are special auras that can be applied to your cosmetic items that give you passive buffs when you wear them. There are also the void missions which can be accessed using tower keys that are awarded in some missions. Here you can get rare resources as well as components for Prime equipment which are like normal warframes and weapons but with better stats and cooler looks
The game is mostly co-op, but there is the Conclave for those who would rather get competitive with some PVP. The modes here range from Deathmatches to Capture the Flag (Capture the Cephalon). Each warframe and weapons have been optimized for PVP use.
Once you complete the mission, you are rewarded with credits (in-game currency) resources, mods for your warframe, and affinity (XP).
This is the usual routine for a typical Warframe player: Select warframe, select weapons, go on mission, complete mission, rinse and repeat. You might be thinking, that it sounds very tedious and repetative. You would be correct. However, Warframe has just enough varienty in missions and enough goals to shoot for that it makes it rather satisfying.
For the most part, the community of Warframe are rather supportive of each other. Being that the game is mostly co-op people are more inclined to help one another. Me and my group of friends actually made a clan dedicated to helping the new people. Things may turn sore when it comes to the two raid modes if people don't know what they are doing. But I did say "for the most part."
In the market, blueprints and some items can be purchased with the in-game credits. But most items are bought using Platinum which can be aquired by spending real money. With platinum, you can buy cosmetics, weapons if you don't want to go through the process of crafting them, boosters (affinity, credit, resource) and resources if you don't feel like farming for them. Platinum can also be used as currency for the player driven market. Players advertise in the trade chat what they are looking to sell or buy. Items consist of Prime equipment blueprints and components, special weapons, void keys, mods, and much more.
I'm not sure what it is about Warframe, but I'm more than willing to throw a couple bucks their way every once in a while. Most MMOs I refrain from spending money on, but I gladly spend disposable income here.
Warframe is an MMO that gets it right. I have been here since beta and it's only getting better and better. They are always adding new Warframes, new weapons, new quests and so on. Warframe is definitly a game that you should check out

The game offers frequent content updates. The developers usually listen to the community, although sometimes their intentions might not be aligned with the player's interests gameplay wise. There is still a lack of guidance built in game for new players, but the community should be very helpful in guiding new players. They are encouraged to look up information online. The combat is fast paced, with a variety of guns, melee weapons, and warframes to choose from, along with the mod system which allows deeper customization of each equipment's functionality. There are a variety of warframes the player can play as, each with their unique set of abilities, although some abilities may overlap with other warframes in regards to their role (damage, healing, crowd control, etc.).
Its F2P model is pretty lenient. You can trade in-game items for platinum (premium currency), which you could use to buy cash shop items. Items in the cash shop consist of cosmetics, inventory slots, dyes that are unlimited use, some consumables (XP boosters), or fully built weapons and armor (items in this game take resources and time to craft). While you could go ahead and use platinum to buy almost every equipment in the game, it would be a huge waste of money since a majority of this game's content is built around grinding for that gear that already quite easy to get. If you do plan to play it, you should focus your platinum in buying more inventory slots to collect more warframes and weapons. Platinum is also used as a currency to trade between players, for rare items.
The game has a lot of customization options available. Each piece of gear has four tint masks you can recolor along with an "energy color" option which controls the color of miscellaneous things like your warframe abilities, melee weapon trails, or gun muzzle flashes. You can also further customize your warframe by acquiring different helmets, or skins which can be from a simple retexture to a dramatic overhaul of the warframe model itself. Warframes are also able to equip syndanas (space capes), and armor pieces for even more customizability.

When I first started to play this game, I was told that it was too much of a grind unless you wanted to put all your hard earned money into it. After playing Warframe for a bit, I have discovered that what I was told is true...to a point. I would like to make one thing very clear, you will have to do a lot of grinding unless you want to pay money, but as the game is not PvP focused in the least, it also is not a pay to win game. After taking an (admitidly) small look around at all the things you can buy, I found that nothing you could buy with real money, is impossible to get for free. In my opinion, I found that being able to get anything for free, was not a far away dream filled with imossibly long time periods to get what you are looking for. So far (for me at least) I was getting all the resources and other stuff I needed to craft items and equipment just by playing casually and not looking for the resources. Another thing to point out is, get comfortable with the gear you have. This game is not about having thousands of weapons at your disposal to lay waste to things. Instead, you will take the time to level your equipment to max before moving on to something better. As I played longer, I did have to grind...a lot. Personally I like grinding so this was not an issue for me and i found it quite enjoyable. The community has been nice and supportive (in my region at least) and though they will not hesitate to point out rookie mistakes and the like, they have never been outright mean, and have only meant to help me improve through criticism. The tutorial does not teach much past basic controls, so I highly recommend checking out YouTube videos and reading the Warframe Wiki. If you are not a fan of grinding, I would not recommend, but if you can put up with it, or enjoy grinding, I highly recommend this game.

A wonderful game for those that have a lot of time on their hands. Even if you don't, you can still make full use of that time if you plan ahead. With that time, you take control of your warframe from over their shoulder, letting you actually
your customizations when you make them. [Hooray for third person!] From that warframe, you go against four different factions as a 'guardian of balance', led by the Lotus. And with a vast array of weapons to help you shoot, slash, blow up, crush, and knock away all of your opponents, you won't have a dull moment when in combat.
Speaking of combat, there are several game modes that require a multitude of tactics to keep you entertained. From rushing between defense points while being surrounded to being a sneaky ninja and steal all of their base's information. Even going after the head honchos to assassinate them. If that bores you, take to the skies with the archwing, or go deep into the heart of enemy territory in their raid missions. The choice is yours.
Yes. This is a microtransaction game. You will be tempted to get the in-game currency; platinum. Some like to outright buy the things instead of crafting them [which does take time]. However, if you don't mind waiting to build stuff while you are away from your computer or leveling other things, feel free to not empty your wallet. The only useful things to buy with platinum [you are actually given 75 to start with]. are item slows for weapons and warframe slots. Maybe an accessory you like or a color pack for customizations. But avoid getting things right off the bat to have them, it does ruin the gameplay.

Now that i have about 1467 hours in this game, its time to now give a full review
Pros:
F2P- You play this whole game without paying a single dime.
Community is great
Music, Sound Effects on point
Dev's answer to players through updates and forum posts
Helpful people
Graphics on this is amazing playing at 60 fps
You literally run this game on a potatoe.
Weapon variety (a bit) Some weapons you will be deeply attactched to than others.
Mods-able to upgrade your weapons and Frames in a variety of different ways
Frame choise- Going into a spy mission solo and want the stealthiest frame?
Raids- Are somewhat fun to play (See Cons)
Clan making and building
Customization
Very Fun with Friends
Now for the cons
Cons:
Pay to Rush- THIS IS COMPLETELY DIFFERENT THAN PAY TO WIN. For those who can't wait, this game isn't for you. 3 days for a new frame, Each part (Chassis, Helmet, Systems) takes all 12 hours. Weapons are only 8-12 hours. Clan weapons are usually 12-24 hours. Now you can use platium to skip the process of waiting, but it seems like a waste. 50 plat to skip a 3 day waiting period. 25 or less platium for 12 hours to 8 hours to rush. Or if you don't want to farm the resources, you can buy them straight off the market, But that is alot more pricey.
Cosmetics- Very expense but some are worth getting than others
Platium- Now this is very interesting. After completeing the tutorial, you are given 50 platium. This currency can be used to buy cosmetics, buy or sell mods, prime parts and rare weapons. Personally I don't worry too much about this. Rare skins usually cost around 150-170 platium. Some are worth getting in others. Depends all on preferance.
Trading- This is a big issue. People overpricing just to make some platium on  the side. (If no update on trading then i'll keep this here) But overpricing a mod or prime part just to make platium is just a big cut off from new players.
Raids- Now this one is my personal negative. I do not like the way raids are going at the moment. The first Trail we got was fun and exciting then the new Jordus Precept Raid was just a huge flop. In this raid, you gather the resources to make a device in order to proceed. Then you have to do the Raid AGAIN in order to build the darn thing. (only if you didn't gather enough from the first time around.) Then you build the darn equipment and you do it AGAIN. Making the players go back and forth and re-making keys seems to me to be a total flop.
Grind- This game has the biggest grind wall but is way better than most other games that are grind based. All hail RNG.
Overall, This game blew my mind when I played it and I would give it a 9/10 overall rating.

I burned out aound update 14.5 and didn't get back into it until update 16.5. That might sound like a long time but it was only a couple of months. That is how fast the game changes.
The devs are always working to change the game for the better and you can see that in all of the content the devs post on twitch and youtube.
Warframe is like any other online gam, it is going to be hard for new players to fit in. Warframe is very grindy. I have heard people call it warfarm because the farm involved can get extremely intense. However if you can handle the farm, The result is very rewarding.
Another thing that turns people off warframe is that it is free. The steriotipical free game now is full of in game purchases . Warframe does have in game purchases but by no means do you need to buy anything. That being said, If you ask anyone who has been playing the game for a while, 999999/100000 of them will tell you they have bought some amount of platinum (what you buy). There is no reason to say that warframe is pay to win and that is why you don't play it. Everything can be obtained in game without platinum except cosmetics which don't really do anything but look different.
Overall, Warframe is a fantastic game. If you can put up with the grind and the ocassonal bugs (which are usually pretty hilarious) and you like RPGs, you should try this game out.

I have hundreds of hours in Warframe.
I cannot in good conscience recommend it to anyone.
Warframe features some of the best moment to moment game play around. You truly take the role of one of many space ninjas. Exciting movement, gliding through the air, hacking and blasting and casting. Its exciting.
But the entire game is built completely around RNG. Everything is a grind. Warframes are obtained one piece at a time, from bosses. You just grind until each part drops once (average of 5 - 6 times total for three parts) and THEN you STILL buy the Blueprint from the market for in game currency.
And so it goes. All the best stuff in the game is free. It just requires hour and hours of endless RNG grind. Which wouldnt be so bad, except the game features a very limited selection of mission types, and in the late game forces you to run certain types for certain rewards - or, well, chances at rewards - whether you enjoy that type or not.
All of which is a shame. For a game this fun, with game play this exciting, to lean solely on RNG and exploitative business practices is a disappointment.

There's a reason this game is still the 5~10th most played game on Steam every day, 2 years after it opened its gates.
There are a lot of ways to enjoy Ark - and I feel like most negative reviews come from people who are playing it wrong. Let me elaborate - public servers provide an extremely different playing experience, compared to smaller private ones, or solo. Whether you thrive in a huge tribe living and dying at the endgame level, or prefer to have a quiet friendly experience, you have to find the right server or offline play settings according to your play style.
Underneath all of this, is an extremely deep game where you survive, grow and customize, build, fight, tame, gather, and explore. 165 hours in, I have barely scratched the surface of all the game has to offer, and I generally play single player (or with a friend). It's hard not to recommend what seems to be, overall, the best multiplayer survival game of the generation (sorry Rust).

This game has an amazing core to it, the progression of building up your character, your base and your pets is wonderful and compelling.  The potential for building communities on the PVP servers is huge.
However the apparent intent of the developers when it comes to PVP seems to be diametrically opposed to the progression side of the game.  When I started playing a few months ago you had a log telling you who destroyed your property, allowing for retaliation and for larger tribes to protect new players, that is gone and players are now free to grief to their heart's content in perfect anonymity. This drove a lot of new/low level players away because they could not progress when everything they had was stolen or destroyed every day.
To make matters much much worse unlimited cross-server transfer of characters/dinosaurs/items has now been implemented. The consequence of this that every PVP server is now open to invasion by every other server. There is no way to defend against this. There is no way to fight a tribe that can bring 60 players to a server with a population cap of 70, assuming you are even online when it happens.
The server I played on has gone, in the space of weeks, from being one of the most populace PVP servers to a ghost town, and of the tribes that were left most have now quit because since unrestricted transfers the server has been invaded by overwhelming forces every day.
If you want to play on a PVP server do not buy this game in its current state. There is simply no point. You wont even be able to level yourself up let alone progress to the point of being able to meaningfully take part in conflict on a local scale. Let alone within the trans-server meta.

I've spent a fair amount of time with Warframe and, I'm going to say it, I have been hooked. I initially wanted to start playing last year but I only had a low end laptop at the time. Having invested a bit of cash into a proper desktop, I can see that my patience wasn't wasted.
I've seen a number of reviews brand this game as a grind fest. Admittedly yes, there are times where you contemplate going after this one item that has a low drop rate but, for the most part, it doesn't feel like effort. It doesn't FEEL like a grind. There's so many different ways to play based on which warframe you're playing, which weapons and mods you have equipped, whether you want to play solo or in a group. Having this flexibility to play leaves so many possibilities.
And the lore, oh my god, the lore that has been produced so far has been incredible. And more is being released all the time with new quests and warframes. It keeps you questioning what really happened for things to get how they are and where things are headed.
Even when you don't feel like doing missions, you can hang out at your clan dojo, enjoy some of the mini games and things that they have there, or potter around the relays and see other people with their warframes. I think DE has created something great and I hope it lasts. I would definitely label this game as an enjoyable experience that keeps giving and surprising.

Let me get the good stuff out of the way: Warframe is by far the best third person shooter on the market. And it isn't even on the market. It's free. It's Diablo 3 with a fashion endgame, actually not garbage player trading and economy, and buttloads of character customization down to the color of the arrows you fire.
Alright?
Just play it if you like Diablo or other ARPGs. It's great, you're a literal god murderizing robots and meaties that stand in your way, and you're hella fashionable.
It's got some problems, though.
Warframe is a very incoherent experience. I mean, I know what Warframe is. It's a third-person shooter with a focus on character customization through loot drops. The core gameplay loop is solid, and feels good.
But then you have so many things that were started once upon a time but just never received any major updates and ended up being forgotten. Lunaro, Conclave, Archwings, and now Plains of Eidolon brings a bunch of new stuff that will never be looked back at.
Along with that, there's a distinct lack of real endgame, and the game boils down to "maximize your DPS with mods, and collect weapons to level up and never use again". There's very few bosses in the game, and with the exception of the Eidolon (which requires completion of The Second Dream, a very advanced questline, to even damage) none of them have complex mechanics past "dodge their knockdown attack".
At times, Warframe feels like a collection of odd half-finished minigames wrapped around a pretty great but ultimately very repetitive third-person looter shooter.
(But it's still better than The Division)

I have mixed feelings for this game's progress overall. The game is great and has a lot of potential. The graphics are great, and even though the gameplay can get a bit "grindy" it is still fun. Regular updates from the dev team are an encouragement that the game isn't going to dissapear into the "Forever Early Access Abyss".
In regards to updates though, this is also one of my greatest complaints: Devs releasing paid game branches and other total conversions instead of focusing on main branch updates and core. I would much prefer to see fewer "dino" updates and more "we optimized feature X to reduce cpu impact" or "we further optimized MP netcode to allow for more players to enjoy a game together without latency".
Multiplayer is fun and its always a rush trying to conduct a raid. Of course on most servers there are "super tribes" that basically control resources and prime locations. But that is part of the fight to survive. I enjoy running servers for the game and love seeing all the CRAZY THINGS people do.

I'll start by saying that only 1 of the 6 negative reviews that have loaded up for me today are valid. The other 5 literally state either "the game isn't finished", "stop adding content and optimize" or "greedy devs are greedy". None of these points are valid, even if the latter is arguably true. Even if the devs lied about the reasons behind the DLC (already nearly prepped and in need of money after a lawsuit) that has nothing to do with the review of the game. The other two points are from people who either have never played an Early Access game before or/and do not understand that ALL content is added before the game is optimized. This negative attitude has been so overwhelmingly mind blowing that I've been dragged into discussing it in this review, making me contradict myself - this kind of talk should be regulated to some moronic reddit thread, not a Steam review.
As for the game, this is one of several EA titles I own. This is by far the best and I would say outshines all of the other games in my library. The base premise of the game, open-world survival with dinosaurs, plays out as optimally as it could. The concepts behind the pet system and basebuilding are fantastic. I have heard several people state "the building sux" but I never hear of a comparitive game given in relation. For most mainstream gamers I would assume the closest thing to compare it to off the top of my head is Fallout 4. Except Fallout 4 building is terrible and atrocious...especially in comparison. In ARK most of the complaints come from random glitches where things don't snap together or the terrain is slightly to high/low and causes the entire base you started building to be null and require rebuilding. Valid complaints, but blown out of proportion. Yes, they suck. But the former is rare and the latter is honestly just bad luck or sometimes just poor planning. The crafting system is nothing overtly creative but still enjoyable and functional. The breeding system is ever evolving and seems to get better as it progresses.
It's not without it's issues while in Early Access though. The dinos/animals implemented at the beginning of the game (and even a bit later) are essentially useless now until they get around to rebalancing. The gathering/taming/etc rates on Official Servers are not worth playing unless you are single and/or your SO plays and/or you don't have a job. Unofficial servers help allievate those issues, but be prepared to spend time trying different servers out. While trying different servers you will likely be driven into ARK remission due to immense frustration from griefers or offline raiders. There WILL be one too many times you log on to your hard work being demolished while you were offline and helpless. There WILL be a time where you don't play ARK for months.
Through it all though, you WILL come back. Stronger and better than before.
ARK is Early Access. If you have played DayZ, Rust, Reign of Kings, etc. and enjoyed them then you will enjoy ARK. The thing about ARK though, is that it is good enough that I don't feel like it's Early Access. For Early Access I should be reporting bugs, trying to break new content and generally fulfilling the role of a playtester or someone who got an advanced copy of a game. I don't do any of that. I play ARK like it is a full game. I think that, to me, is what defines the success of ARK.
My final advice would be this: Are you thinking about buying the game? Do it. Don't worry about a sale (although...they are nice discounts...). Don't worry about accidentally falling into the old EA trap. Above all else, don't be turned away by the recent flood of poor reviews - 10 mins of research and you'll find 80% of them are completely irrelevant and are made by people with hundreds of hours of gameplay and simply amount to either "game's not finished" or "PAID DLC". Get it, love it.
ARK is love, ARK is life.

Let me get the good stuff out of the way: Warframe is by far the best third person shooter on the market. And it isn't even on the market. It's free. It's Diablo 3 with a fashion endgame, actually not garbage player trading and economy, and buttloads of character customization down to the color of the arrows you fire.
Alright?
Just play it if you like Diablo or other ARPGs. It's great, you're a literal god murderizing robots and meaties that stand in your way, and you're hella fashionable.
It's got some problems, though.
Warframe is a very incoherent experience. I mean, I know what Warframe is. It's a third-person shooter with a focus on character customization through loot drops. The core gameplay loop is solid, and feels good.
But then you have so many things that were started once upon a time but just never received any major updates and ended up being forgotten. Lunaro, Conclave, Archwings, and now Plains of Eidolon brings a bunch of new stuff that will never be looked back at.
Along with that, there's a distinct lack of real endgame, and the game boils down to "maximize your DPS with mods, and collect weapons to level up and never use again". There's very few bosses in the game, and with the exception of the Eidolon (which requires completion of The Second Dream, a very advanced questline, to even damage) none of them have complex mechanics past "dodge their knockdown attack".
At times, Warframe feels like a collection of odd half-finished minigames wrapped around a pretty great but ultimately very repetitive third-person looter shooter.
(But it's still better than The Division)
