Escribir un análisis profundo sobre este juego es muy complicado, así que intentaré resumir sus puntos fuertes y flojos (pero seguramente no lo consiga).
Este juego es una mezcla un poco extraña entre un Shooter y un Hack 'n Slash ya que, aunque la temática principal de Warframe sea el de un Shooter en tercera persona, contamos con un arsenal bastante agradable de armas tanto a distancia, cómo cuerpo a cuerpo, las cuales nos permiten oneshotear a los enemigos desde una distancia prudente o trocearlos cuerpo a cuerpo cual Berserker enfurecido. En este arsenal hay armas de muchos tipos (rifles, arcos, katanas...etc etc) de las cuales, hay muchas bastante originales sacadas de películas de Ciencia Ficción, cómo Elysium, pero no voy a profundizar aquí, hay para todos los gustos.
El recurso principal de nuestro daño serán las armas, pero los Warframe (una especie de ninjas mecanizados muy molones que serán nuestros personajes controlables) cuentan con un sistema de habilidades en plan LoL, cada uno tiene una pasiva y 4 habilidades, las cuales pueden ser pasivas también o de uso, así que cada Warframe es único, tú decides si quieres uno más de supporteo, tanky o de daño.
Warframe mantiene un componente muy alto de farmeo y grindeo, al estilo de otros RPG cómo Diablo, así que si no te gusta invertir muchísimas horas en farmear tu arma o warframe favoritos, repitiendo una misma misión infinitas veces, pasa a otro juego.
Sin embargo, Warframe posee un sistema de comercio muy bien elaborado. He leído en distintas críticas y análisis que Warframe es un Pay to Win, lo cual, no puede estar más lejos de la realidad. En Warframe prácticamente CASI TODO lo que se puede comprar por dinero real se puede conseguir invirtiendo sólamente tiempo en farmearlo, de ahí que sea tan de farmeo. Si te cansas de intentar sacar una parte del Warframe que tanto deseas tener, siempre puedes comprársela a alguien que la venda, por platino (que es la moneda "de pago" del juego) o si lo prefieres, puedes gastarte todos tus ahorros de navidad en comprarte directamente desde la tienda lo que quieras, pero créeme, eso no te hace superior a los demás, que te compres el set de Nekros Prime con sus dos armas hipermega chetas de turno no significa que seas superior a los demás, si no que tienes el dinero y las pocas ganas de invertir tiempo en conseguirlo jugando.
Algo que me gusta mucho de este juego es que la moneda "de pago", el platino, se puede comerciar con los jugadores (si tienes muchos objetos que ya no te hacen falta, los puedes vender en el canal de comercio a gente que los quiera, intercambiándolos por platino, para comprarte cosas que sólo se puedan conseguir con ésta moneda (cómo skins) y, cómo he mencionado antes, en este juego no tienes porqué gastarte un solo duro en jugarlo (solo el ancho de banda, claro, es online),... pero una cosa es cierta, y es que si te acabas viciando acabarás inviertiendo un mínimo en él, en este juego SÍ merece la pena completamente gastarte algo de pasta en él.
Puntos a destacar en la jugabilidad... el sistema de "parkour" que posee, la cantidad de piruetas y carrerillas, saltos por paredes cual ninja (que, básicamente es lo que eres, un♥♥♥♥♥♥ninja) que puedes realizar es increíble, muy dinámico, en pocas ocasiones permanecerás estático (ejem FROST DEFENSA, cof, cof).
Eso sí, al juego le cuesta arrancar, así que necesita paciencia, mucha paciencia. Nada más empezar a jugar te tocará asimilar muchas cosas, sobre controles, sobre aspectos de la jugabilidad... mucha información ya desde las primeras horas de juego, así que relax y ve por partes, no intentes aprenderte todo lo que hace cada objeto o sumergirte de lleno en los sindicatos desde la primera hora de juego, poco a poco.
Los gráficos son de lo mejor que he visto en mucho tiempo, demasiado bien optimizados para lo buenos que son... raramente te encontrarás con bajones de FPS.
Poco más que añadir, realmente no tengo apenas objeciones sobre este juego, quizás la banda sonora podría estar más currada, las melodías son muy repetitivas... y con la temática del juego podría tener melodías más épicas, la verdad.
¿Historia? Ah, ¿qué tiene historia? Cierto, léela en internet.
En fin, en resumen, si te mola el chinofarmeo y reventar hordas de bichos (?) con láseres y katanas mientras te recorres la galaxia, Warframe es un señor juegazo, merece demasiado la pena cómo para pasarlo por alto.

Warframe is a solid and unique kind of third-person-shooter that mixes high speed action with a number of features normally only present in MMO's. While the game does have a number of grind and time walls; the game play, social aspects, and very active development team will keep you interested more than long enough to forget that the walls were there to begin with as well as give the game a type of longevity that will keep you coming every update.
However while all F2P games these days do come with a hefty price tag to really get into it Warframe manages to keep the majority of it's prices to a convenience and comedic basis; the only exception to that is the amount of inventory you have. However the space you get to begin with is generous enough to give you the time to decide if it is a game for you. Warframe also has the added benefit of being able to trade other players for the paid currency in-game allowing for a truly free experience; if you're willing to work for it.
In the end as with most F2P titles Warframe is one that is defiantly worth looking into and will be hard pressed to disappoint if it does truly catch your interests.

Original Review -
Amongst negative reviews for DLC, Optimization, or other. I still say this game is worth it all. Im not going to write this review in order to battle other's viewpoints or problems they may have had with the game. I'm going to give you a review from someone who has played this game since it first became available on steam and has been able to put hundreds of hours all along the developement process.
Pros:
- Good map detail and environments (specific habitats, cave systems, climates, biomes, etc)
- Dino behavior is fitting and the Ai performs above all other similar games i have played
- Has good survival elements that help deepen the strategy of the game (food, water, equipment, character leveling)
- Encourages creativity with building mechanics, dino taming, defenses, tribe/alliance social aspects
- Good optimization (depends on the rig, i have had friends play this ranging with the usual toaster to gaming computer and they have all enjoyed the game and been able to play it)
- Active Devs, this is a big one, compared to other games in my library who are still an Early Access Game, they pale in comparison to the ongoing development of Ark. We get fixes and new content at a good rate. And the mod/workshop community is big as well.
Cons:
- Admins can make or break private servers (i have been able to find a good server with decent activity and awesome mod support) These kinds of servers are out there, you have to play the game enough to figure out what kind of Ark you want PVP, mixed, PVE, or whatever.
- Experimentation, in light of the last con stated. You'll need to play the game a bit to understand what is going on in order for the game to be enjoyable and adaptable. Vanilla setting are grueling so new players starting might want to check the settings of wherever they are joining in order to get a better idea of how the server plays.
- Paid DLC,
i can understand where the frustration comes here but here is what i have to say about this; The "NEWEST" dlc is the ONLY one that costs money. The company isnt forcing you to buy the newest map in order to play the game, there are hundreds of servers running the other two maps that are bigger, more diverse, and just as fun. So what if the game isnt finished, you arent forced to buy it! It was another way for me to show my appreciation and support by paying another $20 and get the extra content.
In conclusion, i recommend this game. It has been fun, its a game i come back to time and time again to play with friends and get my creative/challenge fix at the same time. Get the game, find a good server, promote mods/workshop activity, and enjoy the game. If you dont want the DLC dont get it, or wait until it comes on sale (which it does occasionally) The other two DLC will keep you way busy in the meantime, especially if there are add-ons involved.

ARK is a fantastic game with a lot to offer for survival game enthusiasts. While there are some preformance hops to meet to make this game run smoothly, it is visually stunning, and the scale of everything can be pretty daunting and imposing, which helps build a good atmosphere. Audio sounds amazing, though the audio settings sometimes run a little loud. Dinosaurs are big and stompy and destroy stuff, and surviving the first week is a huge undertaking before you hit your stride. Definitely a game to bring friends along in.
Pros
-Scale and visual effects are really nice
-Audio is impressive and intense
-Pick up every poop on the ground. Become the poop queen.
-Heavy survival theming
-Tame buttloads of deadly deadly dinos.
Cons
-Steep intro curve - its very difficult to catch a break early on, and you will probably die several times before you catch on
-Learning curve plateaus out once you tame out really strong and accessible dinos; the game progressively becomes easier the more you've done at success but...
-Sometimes BS dino AI or even turning radiuses can play against you. Its very easy to have a very strong dinosaur put into a very dangerous situation, which means you lose that dinosaur. Some may view this "you lose it, its gone" aspect as a pro.
Its a fun game, and worth a romp around if you can bring friends :)

Today was my last day for a while playing Warframe. I finally have to take a break. For the past two months I have played daily, and achieved a lot; it was what I chose to play in place of Guild Wars 2 while I waited for an expansion to come out. Tomorrow that expansion releases and I am planning to return to GW2, but i'm certainly not done playing Warframe.
In two months it's impossible for me to have experienced everything this game had to offer, but what I did get to experience was a wonderfully done third-person shooter with some of the most creative weapons I have ever seen. The game is incredibly pleasing to the eye, and difficulty progression is gradual enough that you actually feel like you have worked towards something when you realize you're sitting in a Tower 4 Survival mission by yourself, and you can play through it like any other mission you've done all day. I love games that push me towards completion, collecting everything, having every item, getting every achievement-- and Warframe is able to do that. It even encourages you to go back and remake some of your items or frames, just to have a slightly better version, and none of it felt like a grind. I never shut off Warframe in disgust, I never felt bored, and I never felt like it was a job. I made sure that I had built as many prime Warframes as possible before I go back to Guild Wars, because I know I want to have something to play with that's new and shiny when I do return to this game. You always want to make progress towards something.
There are very few gripes I have with this game, and those I do I have listed below, and are some things that need to be taken into consideration if you do want to play this game. First of all it is host based game. You rely on another persons internet to make your experience enjoyable and sometimes it's not. If you run into someone with terrible internet usually they do have the courtesy to drop out of the mission and let someone else host, or in a lot of cases know better than to host a mission in the first place. Once in a while you'll get someone who doesn't look at chat, or doesn't know better, or is just plain ignorant though, and they will ruin the mission for you. It's rare, but it happens. Secondly there is a trade system in Warframe, you can use it to buy and sell prime parts, mods, weapons, all manner of items, but at the same time there are some restrictions that I find somewhat dumb and unnecessary. At least one of two people must be in a clan to initiate a trade, because you must use a trading post to do so, this is a clan-specific building and would make a great addition to the Relays on every planet. Trade chat itself is also disappointing, but that's more the players you will find there, and is a problem in any game with P2P trading. Many people over-value their items and will insist on selling at a much higher price than what is acceptable. It makes trading hard, but again, it's not impossible.
As a final note I have to commend Digital Extremes on their dedication to fixing the game and adding new content. In my two months playing so far there have been no less than three hotfix patches per week, at least one of which includes new content. Two new frames have been introduced, and many more weapons than I can remember. Their microtransaction structure is well done, daily logins have a chance to provide discounts for Platinum purchases, which is the premium currency available in game. Not only can you buy Platinum at up to 75% off (which is a great deal), but you can trade for Platinum from other players. This means that absolutely nothing in Warframe is locked behind a paywall. It's not hard to farm Prime parts that are worth a decent amount of Platinum, and it could take you as little as a week to farm enough to be able to afford whatever the newest cash shop item is. It makes for a healthy trading economy and a happy player base, nobody is at a disadvantage.
So finally I'm going to give Warframe a conventional score out of 10. The drawbacks I listed are mostly quality of life changes that could be made, and I have encountered no real performance issues that prevented me from doing something in game. I give it an
; the overall UI could use some serious polish, and the trading system could stand some attention, but the gameplay is fun, the weapons and frames are unique, and everything is within your reach, even as a free to play player.

Warframe es uno de esos juegos que, al descubrirlo, consiguió mantenerme pegado al ordenador días enteros sin poder parar de jugarlo.
Escribir un análisis profundo sobre este juego es muy complicado, así que intentaré resumir sus puntos fuertes y flojos (pero seguramente no lo consiga).
Este juego es una mezcla un poco extraña entre un Shooter y un Hack 'n Slash ya que, aunque la temática principal de Warframe sea el de un Shooter en tercera persona, contamos con un arsenal bastante agradable de armas tanto a distancia, cómo cuerpo a cuerpo, las cuales nos permiten oneshotear a los enemigos desde una distancia prudente o trocearlos cuerpo a cuerpo cual Berserker enfurecido. En este arsenal hay armas de muchos tipos (rifles, arcos, katanas...etc etc) de las cuales, hay muchas bastante originales sacadas de películas de Ciencia Ficción, cómo Elysium, pero no voy a profundizar aquí, hay para todos los gustos.
El recurso principal de nuestro daño serán las armas, pero los Warframe (una especie de ninjas mecanizados muy molones que serán nuestros personajes controlables) cuentan con un sistema de habilidades en plan LoL, cada uno tiene una pasiva y 4 habilidades, las cuales pueden ser pasivas también o de uso, así que cada Warframe es único, tú decides si quieres uno más de supporteo, tanky o de daño.
Warframe mantiene un componente muy alto de farmeo y grindeo, al estilo de otros RPG cómo Diablo, así que si no te gusta invertir muchísimas horas en farmear tu arma o warframe favoritos, repitiendo una misma misión infinitas veces, pasa a otro juego.
Sin embargo, Warframe posee un sistema de comercio muy bien elaborado. He leído en distintas críticas y análisis que Warframe es un Pay to Win, lo cual, no puede estar más lejos de la realidad. En Warframe prácticamente CASI TODO lo que se puede comprar por dinero real se puede conseguir invirtiendo sólamente tiempo en farmearlo, de ahí que sea tan de farmeo. Si te cansas de intentar sacar una parte del Warframe que tanto deseas tener, siempre puedes comprársela a alguien que la venda, por platino (que es la moneda "de pago" del juego) o si lo prefieres, puedes gastarte todos tus ahorros de navidad en comprarte directamente desde la tienda lo que quieras, pero créeme, eso no te hace superior a los demás, que te compres el set de Nekros Prime con sus dos armas hipermega chetas de turno no significa que seas superior a los demás, si no que tienes el dinero y las pocas ganas de invertir tiempo en conseguirlo jugando.
Algo que me gusta mucho de este juego es que la moneda "de pago", el platino, se puede comerciar con los jugadores (si tienes muchos objetos que ya no te hacen falta, los puedes vender en el canal de comercio a gente que los quiera, intercambiándolos por platino, para comprarte cosas que sólo se puedan conseguir con ésta moneda (cómo skins) y, cómo he mencionado antes, en este juego no tienes porqué gastarte un solo duro en jugarlo (solo el ancho de banda, claro, es online),... pero una cosa es cierta, y es que si te acabas viciando acabarás inviertiendo un mínimo en él, en este juego SÍ merece la pena completamente gastarte algo de pasta en él.
Puntos a destacar en la jugabilidad... el sistema de "parkour" que posee, la cantidad de piruetas y carrerillas, saltos por paredes cual ninja (que, básicamente es lo que eres, un♥♥♥♥♥♥ninja) que puedes realizar es increíble, muy dinámico, en pocas ocasiones permanecerás estático (ejem FROST DEFENSA, cof, cof).
Eso sí, al juego le cuesta arrancar, así que necesita paciencia, mucha paciencia. Nada más empezar a jugar te tocará asimilar muchas cosas, sobre controles, sobre aspectos de la jugabilidad... mucha información ya desde las primeras horas de juego, así que relax y ve por partes, no intentes aprenderte todo lo que hace cada objeto o sumergirte de lleno en los sindicatos desde la primera hora de juego, poco a poco.
Los gráficos son de lo mejor que he visto en mucho tiempo, demasiado bien optimizados para lo buenos que son... raramente te encontrarás con bajones de FPS.
Poco más que añadir, realmente no tengo apenas objeciones sobre este juego, quizás la banda sonora podría estar más currada, las melodías son muy repetitivas... y con la temática del juego podría tener melodías más épicas, la verdad.
¿Historia? Ah, ¿qué tiene historia? Cierto, léela en internet.
En fin, en resumen, si te mola el chinofarmeo y reventar hordas de bichos (?) con láseres y katanas mientras te recorres la galaxia, Warframe es un señor juegazo, merece demasiado la pena cómo para pasarlo por alto.

Warframe is a solid and unique kind of third-person-shooter that mixes high speed action with a number of features normally only present in MMO's. While the game does have a number of grind and time walls; the game play, social aspects, and very active development team will keep you interested more than long enough to forget that the walls were there to begin with as well as give the game a type of longevity that will keep you coming every update.
However while all F2P games these days do come with a hefty price tag to really get into it Warframe manages to keep the majority of it's prices to a convenience and comedic basis; the only exception to that is the amount of inventory you have. However the space you get to begin with is generous enough to give you the time to decide if it is a game for you. Warframe also has the added benefit of being able to trade other players for the paid currency in-game allowing for a truly free experience; if you're willing to work for it.
In the end as with most F2P titles Warframe is one that is defiantly worth looking into and will be hard pressed to disappoint if it does truly catch your interests.

Warframe is a solid and unique kind of third-person-shooter that mixes high speed action with a number of features normally only present in MMO's. While the game does have a number of grind and time walls; the game play, social aspects, and very active development team will keep you interested more than long enough to forget that the walls were there to begin with as well as give the game a type of longevity that will keep you coming every update.
However while all F2P games these days do come with a hefty price tag to really get into it Warframe manages to keep the majority of it's prices to a convenience and comedic basis; the only exception to that is the amount of inventory you have. However the space you get to begin with is generous enough to give you the time to decide if it is a game for you. Warframe also has the added benefit of being able to trade other players for the paid currency in-game allowing for a truly free experience; if you're willing to work for it.
In the end as with most F2P titles Warframe is one that is defiantly worth looking into and will be hard pressed to disappoint if it does truly catch your interests.

It is a harvesting / building / construction / taming (Survival) game set in the most stunning scenery you ever saw in a game that will take your breath away again and again.

Ark Survival Evolved is game that will make you rethink the PvP Universe. Yes the game does have RPG only servers but that is not how the game was meant to be played. In this game, you can either strike out on your own and build a thriving farm or be a lone assassin taking from other players around you never being in one place to long. Best part of this game everything you can do as a loner you can do as a team.
This game also pays incredible attention to detail and few other games can come close to it's beauty play style or uniqueness. This is definitely a game that if bought at full price would still be well worth it.
Now for all you haters out there. There is some problems with the game, such as on some of the servers you can have extremely powerful tribes that dominate all resources and can be very difficult to raise yourself up without being forced to join one of the more powerful tribes. The taming of a more powerful creature can take hours upon hours, and the chance of another rogue player happening upon you is great, where they will not only try and kill you but they will attempt to kill the creature that you have spent the 4+ hours trying to tame.
But for all it's faults this game exceeded my expectations and continues to grow in both content and it's Biomes with the newest update of swamps and snow fields this game has just about everything a survival game should and then some.
Over all this game is well worth the price with support for this game constantly being developed and the creators listening to the ideas and woes of the community.

Today was my last day for a while playing Warframe. I finally have to take a break. For the past two months I have played daily, and achieved a lot; it was what I chose to play in place of Guild Wars 2 while I waited for an expansion to come out. Tomorrow that expansion releases and I am planning to return to GW2, but i'm certainly not done playing Warframe.
In two months it's impossible for me to have experienced everything this game had to offer, but what I did get to experience was a wonderfully done third-person shooter with some of the most creative weapons I have ever seen. The game is incredibly pleasing to the eye, and difficulty progression is gradual enough that you actually feel like you have worked towards something when you realize you're sitting in a Tower 4 Survival mission by yourself, and you can play through it like any other mission you've done all day. I love games that push me towards completion, collecting everything, having every item, getting every achievement-- and Warframe is able to do that. It even encourages you to go back and remake some of your items or frames, just to have a slightly better version, and none of it felt like a grind. I never shut off Warframe in disgust, I never felt bored, and I never felt like it was a job. I made sure that I had built as many prime Warframes as possible before I go back to Guild Wars, because I know I want to have something to play with that's new and shiny when I do return to this game. You always want to make progress towards something.
There are very few gripes I have with this game, and those I do I have listed below, and are some things that need to be taken into consideration if you do want to play this game. First of all it is host based game. You rely on another persons internet to make your experience enjoyable and sometimes it's not. If you run into someone with terrible internet usually they do have the courtesy to drop out of the mission and let someone else host, or in a lot of cases know better than to host a mission in the first place. Once in a while you'll get someone who doesn't look at chat, or doesn't know better, or is just plain ignorant though, and they will ruin the mission for you. It's rare, but it happens. Secondly there is a trade system in Warframe, you can use it to buy and sell prime parts, mods, weapons, all manner of items, but at the same time there are some restrictions that I find somewhat dumb and unnecessary. At least one of two people must be in a clan to initiate a trade, because you must use a trading post to do so, this is a clan-specific building and would make a great addition to the Relays on every planet. Trade chat itself is also disappointing, but that's more the players you will find there, and is a problem in any game with P2P trading. Many people over-value their items and will insist on selling at a much higher price than what is acceptable. It makes trading hard, but again, it's not impossible.
As a final note I have to commend Digital Extremes on their dedication to fixing the game and adding new content. In my two months playing so far there have been no less than three hotfix patches per week, at least one of which includes new content. Two new frames have been introduced, and many more weapons than I can remember. Their microtransaction structure is well done, daily logins have a chance to provide discounts for Platinum purchases, which is the premium currency available in game. Not only can you buy Platinum at up to 75% off (which is a great deal), but you can trade for Platinum from other players. This means that absolutely nothing in Warframe is locked behind a paywall. It's not hard to farm Prime parts that are worth a decent amount of Platinum, and it could take you as little as a week to farm enough to be able to afford whatever the newest cash shop item is. It makes for a healthy trading economy and a happy player base, nobody is at a disadvantage.
So finally I'm going to give Warframe a conventional score out of 10. The drawbacks I listed are mostly quality of life changes that could be made, and I have encountered no real performance issues that prevented me from doing something in game. I give it an
; the overall UI could use some serious polish, and the trading system could stand some attention, but the gameplay is fun, the weapons and frames are unique, and everything is within your reach, even as a free to play player.

Today was my last day for a while playing Warframe. I finally have to take a break. For the past two months I have played daily, and achieved a lot; it was what I chose to play in place of Guild Wars 2 while I waited for an expansion to come out. Tomorrow that expansion releases and I am planning to return to GW2, but i'm certainly not done playing Warframe.
In two months it's impossible for me to have experienced everything this game had to offer, but what I did get to experience was a wonderfully done third-person shooter with some of the most creative weapons I have ever seen. The game is incredibly pleasing to the eye, and difficulty progression is gradual enough that you actually feel like you have worked towards something when you realize you're sitting in a Tower 4 Survival mission by yourself, and you can play through it like any other mission you've done all day. I love games that push me towards completion, collecting everything, having every item, getting every achievement-- and Warframe is able to do that. It even encourages you to go back and remake some of your items or frames, just to have a slightly better version, and none of it felt like a grind. I never shut off Warframe in disgust, I never felt bored, and I never felt like it was a job. I made sure that I had built as many prime Warframes as possible before I go back to Guild Wars, because I know I want to have something to play with that's new and shiny when I do return to this game. You always want to make progress towards something.
There are very few gripes I have with this game, and those I do I have listed below, and are some things that need to be taken into consideration if you do want to play this game. First of all it is host based game. You rely on another persons internet to make your experience enjoyable and sometimes it's not. If you run into someone with terrible internet usually they do have the courtesy to drop out of the mission and let someone else host, or in a lot of cases know better than to host a mission in the first place. Once in a while you'll get someone who doesn't look at chat, or doesn't know better, or is just plain ignorant though, and they will ruin the mission for you. It's rare, but it happens. Secondly there is a trade system in Warframe, you can use it to buy and sell prime parts, mods, weapons, all manner of items, but at the same time there are some restrictions that I find somewhat dumb and unnecessary. At least one of two people must be in a clan to initiate a trade, because you must use a trading post to do so, this is a clan-specific building and would make a great addition to the Relays on every planet. Trade chat itself is also disappointing, but that's more the players you will find there, and is a problem in any game with P2P trading. Many people over-value their items and will insist on selling at a much higher price than what is acceptable. It makes trading hard, but again, it's not impossible.
As a final note I have to commend Digital Extremes on their dedication to fixing the game and adding new content. In my two months playing so far there have been no less than three hotfix patches per week, at least one of which includes new content. Two new frames have been introduced, and many more weapons than I can remember. Their microtransaction structure is well done, daily logins have a chance to provide discounts for Platinum purchases, which is the premium currency available in game. Not only can you buy Platinum at up to 75% off (which is a great deal), but you can trade for Platinum from other players. This means that absolutely nothing in Warframe is locked behind a paywall. It's not hard to farm Prime parts that are worth a decent amount of Platinum, and it could take you as little as a week to farm enough to be able to afford whatever the newest cash shop item is. It makes for a healthy trading economy and a happy player base, nobody is at a disadvantage.
So finally I'm going to give Warframe a conventional score out of 10. The drawbacks I listed are mostly quality of life changes that could be made, and I have encountered no real performance issues that prevented me from doing something in game. I give it an
; the overall UI could use some serious polish, and the trading system could stand some attention, but the gameplay is fun, the weapons and frames are unique, and everything is within your reach, even as a free to play player.

It is easy to love this game so much.
It perfectly created a cool system of cooperation between strangers, which is more than what most MMO games could offer.
Warframe does it perfectly. Sure, the farming aspect of it can get old given time. What game doesn't? But the thing with this one is that, even if you're a newb and you found a squad full of veterans, they'd most likely take care of you.
I'm not an OP'ed veteran, but I could hold my own. Still, I was the weakest of the bunch, and I got easily lynched and mobbed. My squad of strangers raced towards me as I started bleeding out. One vet launched himself into the air, and dropped just in front of me and started swinging his melee weapon, making wide swathes and cutting the mob into pieces, while another dropped on top of me and started reviving me.
Don't know how many times that happened to me, or how many times I did something like that for players noobier than me.
It really really makes you feel... good inside.
But this is a negative review. Why?
Because despite the fact I just stated, it is easy to hate this game because it is by far the worst in terms of updates. You can't play it until updates are done, and the best that MANY players get are unstable connections to the game's update servers.
Most of my hours "playing" it is actually me trying to update it.
It is posted in many forums. Just google it. We have stated many times that other games and programs that we play update and log-in with no problems, and yet somehow people manage to put the blame on us and/or our internet connections being lousy.
Uh, was it not stated clearly? I'll state it in all caps:  EVERY OTHER GAME WE HAVE, WHETHER STEAM OR NON-STEAM, UPDATES FAIRLY FAST AND STABLE. SO WHY CAN'T WARFRAME?
No solution exists, despite this problem being literally years old.
I still love the game though. Just won't be playing it anytime soon because of it's unresolved update issues.

Hmm...where to start? First off, all the missions are the same few modes. After a few hours, it just feels like you're playing the same content over and over with mininum rewards. There's different planets, but they all still have the aforementioned repetitive missions, but with some new enemies, slight reward changes, and story reasons for why you are doing the mission. On top of that, items take ridiculous amounts of time to make. For example, crafting a new Warframe takes 3 whole days, and you have to craft other items that take 12 hours each to make in order to be able to craft a Warframe. You can always skip the time, but with premium currency. Getting a new Warframe doesn't even feel rewarding, as you have to level all the way back up by playing through the repetitive missions. Completing missions doesn't feel rewarding whatsoever. It's just an infinite grind, and for what? To look cooler? To give the devs more money? The only things I enjoyed about this game were the ninja feelings it gave off and the combat, which quickly became stale. I would only recommend this if you get bored easily, since it'll definitely keep you occupied, or if you want to feel like a ninja for a couple of hours.
TL;DR: Repetitive cash grab that I only recommend playing if you're bored.

It's a very good game, albeit repetitive in ways.
The main hold is grinding up, levelling up warframes, weapons and minions, as well as clearing planets like mars, jupiter and venus and taking down the bosses who hold those planets.
The variety of items is just absurd, hundreds of weapons and armor combinations, several different types of missions, and even spacefaring wingsuits that you can use. It feels almost like Borderlands in that regard.
Story is kinda iffy, although there is a little depending on what quests you have open, there isnt really much to go off of, just go out and do your own thing.
Social aspects, matchmaking is really good, you can turn it off or make it friends only, and you can create clans and build dojos to satisfy your every need, it does well considering that it is a free game.
I'd recommend it, but you might get sucked into the endless grind to find more warframes and find the right weapons to build everything, be careful.

Today was my last day for a while playing Warframe. I finally have to take a break. For the past two months I have played daily, and achieved a lot; it was what I chose to play in place of Guild Wars 2 while I waited for an expansion to come out. Tomorrow that expansion releases and I am planning to return to GW2, but i'm certainly not done playing Warframe.
In two months it's impossible for me to have experienced everything this game had to offer, but what I did get to experience was a wonderfully done third-person shooter with some of the most creative weapons I have ever seen. The game is incredibly pleasing to the eye, and difficulty progression is gradual enough that you actually feel like you have worked towards something when you realize you're sitting in a Tower 4 Survival mission by yourself, and you can play through it like any other mission you've done all day. I love games that push me towards completion, collecting everything, having every item, getting every achievement-- and Warframe is able to do that. It even encourages you to go back and remake some of your items or frames, just to have a slightly better version, and none of it felt like a grind. I never shut off Warframe in disgust, I never felt bored, and I never felt like it was a job. I made sure that I had built as many prime Warframes as possible before I go back to Guild Wars, because I know I want to have something to play with that's new and shiny when I do return to this game. You always want to make progress towards something.
There are very few gripes I have with this game, and those I do I have listed below, and are some things that need to be taken into consideration if you do want to play this game. First of all it is host based game. You rely on another persons internet to make your experience enjoyable and sometimes it's not. If you run into someone with terrible internet usually they do have the courtesy to drop out of the mission and let someone else host, or in a lot of cases know better than to host a mission in the first place. Once in a while you'll get someone who doesn't look at chat, or doesn't know better, or is just plain ignorant though, and they will ruin the mission for you. It's rare, but it happens. Secondly there is a trade system in Warframe, you can use it to buy and sell prime parts, mods, weapons, all manner of items, but at the same time there are some restrictions that I find somewhat dumb and unnecessary. At least one of two people must be in a clan to initiate a trade, because you must use a trading post to do so, this is a clan-specific building and would make a great addition to the Relays on every planet. Trade chat itself is also disappointing, but that's more the players you will find there, and is a problem in any game with P2P trading. Many people over-value their items and will insist on selling at a much higher price than what is acceptable. It makes trading hard, but again, it's not impossible.
As a final note I have to commend Digital Extremes on their dedication to fixing the game and adding new content. In my two months playing so far there have been no less than three hotfix patches per week, at least one of which includes new content. Two new frames have been introduced, and many more weapons than I can remember. Their microtransaction structure is well done, daily logins have a chance to provide discounts for Platinum purchases, which is the premium currency available in game. Not only can you buy Platinum at up to 75% off (which is a great deal), but you can trade for Platinum from other players. This means that absolutely nothing in Warframe is locked behind a paywall. It's not hard to farm Prime parts that are worth a decent amount of Platinum, and it could take you as little as a week to farm enough to be able to afford whatever the newest cash shop item is. It makes for a healthy trading economy and a happy player base, nobody is at a disadvantage.
So finally I'm going to give Warframe a conventional score out of 10. The drawbacks I listed are mostly quality of life changes that could be made, and I have encountered no real performance issues that prevented me from doing something in game. I give it an
; the overall UI could use some serious polish, and the trading system could stand some attention, but the gameplay is fun, the weapons and frames are unique, and everything is within your reach, even as a free to play player.

Ark: Survival Evolved is a sandbox survival game developed and published by Studio Wildcard. Players are stranded on a lush tropical island inhabited by mammoth dinosaurs. Survive by scavenging resources to craft tools and build a home to withstand the elements. Pick seeds and plant them, collecting dinosaur excrement to fertilize your farm. Or build improvised weapons to hunt prehistoric beasts for their hides and meat. As you play you level up in RPG-fashion, earning points to increase your stats and unlocking new craftable items. Tame ancient reptiles with food to assist you as pack mules, or ride them to fly, swim, and run faster across the sprawling landscape. Every animal in Ark obeys a predatorial hierarchy and wanders a specific ecosystem; tamed Dodo birds won’t do much good against a pack of velociraptors. While dinosaurs pose a threat, it’s humans who will kill you without mercy or provocation. Join a tribe with other players and create a thriving community, sharing resources and working together to survive. Or, raid other tribes for loot, in fast-paced and brutal PvP.
Ark: Survival Evolved Key Features:
Tame wildlife - over 25 different kinds of dinosaurs to befriend and ride with more being added regularly.
Base building - simple tools make it easy to construct buildings so long as you have the required skills and resources.
Tribal PvP - join a tribe with other players to forge a community, or raid other tribe’s bases for rare resources and glory.
Huge open world - a gorgeous jungle landscape to explore and extensive underwater environments with hidden coves.
Dynamic weather system - endure the unforgiving heat, frigid cold, and monsoon rainstorms in an ever-changing environment.

Whilst I have been following DE's development of Dark Sector since 2008, I have only recently played WF. WF is a great third person shooter that combines the finesse of a ninja with the accuracy of a FPS game. The gameplay is great, and almost everything can be farmed with ease. Likewise, you have the option of purchasing Platinum with actual money, which can then be used to obtain cosmetics and gears. Having said that, this isn't your typical Pay2Win type of game; items and gears in WF are easily accessible if you are playing with a group of friends/ clan. The trade economy in WF is quite fair, and the community is awesome. Almost any random veteran gamer was kind enough to share tips and tricks, or even advise on gear progression. Most players are matured and understand that there is a lot info that hasn't been properly conveyed to a fresh WF gamer (a problem that I think is currently plaguing the MMO industry).
Here is where WF might deter new players entering the battlefield. The tutorial briefly touches on the game's basic mechanics, but fails to give an explanation about gear progression, syndicates, the importance of mastery rank, and how to open up new worlds/ areas in the game. The recruitment and trading interfaces might also be hard to maneuver if you are new to the game. WF is also not strong on storytelling. It puts the players in the shoes of a Tenno, but doesn't really explain the purpose of the Tenno properly. If you are looking for a compelling story, look elsewhere. Where WF really shines is in the gameplay mechanics. Each individual WF comes with 4 unique skills, which are unlocked with level progression. WF suits can be customised with mods, which will further enchance or reduce the WF abilities. If your looking for a good 3rd person shooter, look no further. WF is truly the MMO version of Mass Effect or Lost Planet.
TL;DR
Pros
====
- Great community
- Constant developer updates/ streams (via twitch)
- Great gameplay (wide variety of weapons and abilities)
- Gear and mats are easy to obtain (grindfactor: 7/10)
- Fun to play with friends or guildies
- Cool WF armor designs and skins
Cons
====
- Lack of coherent storytelling
- Some concepts in the game were not well explained

Does 1,700 hours say anything? No? Then I shall elaborate, broken down into a simple pros and cons list (don't expect it to be complete):
Pros:
+Pretty graphics (PhysX, PBR, lens flares, the works)
+Good combat engine
+Very large selection of weapons and Warframes
+High levels of customization with the equipment modding system
+Solid netcode (most of the time)
+Constant content updates
+Fair microtransaction system (no exclusive gear apart from cosmetics)
+Mastery system ensures that new players cannot buy overpowered gear with real money
+No subscription required
+Randomly-generated maps give variety to missions
Cons:
-Most Waframes and weapons can be bought with microtransactions, ruining progression
-Buggy physics engine, even with constant bugfixes
-No dedicated servers for matchmaking
-No option for first person mode (may be subjective)
-Classic F2P timers, wait 3 days for a Warframe to finish, etc.
-Uses up all, and I mean ALL, of your free time for the first 6 months
-Missions can get repetitive quickly, even with RNG'd maps
-Requires a sometimes-excessive amount of farming (I know, F2P, all that)
Thanks for reading my ramblings!

+Pretty graphics (PhysX, PBR, lens flares, the works)
+Good combat engine

+Mastery system ensures that new players cannot buy overpowered gear with real money
+No subscription required
+Randomly-generated maps give variety to missions
Cons:
-Most Waframes and weapons can be bought with microtransactions, ruining progression
-Buggy physics engine, even with constant bugfixes
-No dedicated servers for matchmaking
-No option for first person mode (may be subjective)
-Classic F2P timers, wait 3 days for a Warframe to finish, etc.
-Uses up all, and I mean ALL, of your free time for the first 6 months
-Missions can get repetitive quickly, even with RNG'd maps
-Requires a sometimes-excessive amount of farming (I know, F2P, all that)
Thanks for reading my ramblings!

ARK is a game all about survival, This game includes dinosaurs, customisable players and base building.
The main objective to the game is to retrieve the artefacts from 3 caves underground and transport them to the 3 obelisks around the map, once the artefacts have been transported to the obelisks you can summon the dragon of ARK and kill it, once you have defeated the dragon you will receive an achievement on steam, the game is full of community and official servers that you can join the play with your friends and battle it out with dinosaurs and other players. This game has its own building system that lets you collect resources and build thatch, wooden, stone or metal bases, you have to assemble the base yourself by using foundations and walls you made using the recourses needed for the desired build. You can also tame dinosaurs using tranquilliser darts or arrows in a bow, crossbow or a long neck rifle. Once you have knocked the dinosaur out you can tame it by giving it raw meat, Some dinosaurs require berries to tame. This game also includes a statistic system that allows you to have the choice of what you want your character to have. E.G; Health, Melee damage, food, water and movement speed. To craft stuff you have engrams and you can learn engrams by using engram points witch are obtained by gathering resources or taming dinosaurs. I think you should buy this game because it a really fun game to play and you can enjoy yourself and learn new dinosaurs that you never new existed.

This game used to have a very positive rating until they released an expansion while still in EA. The expansion takes you to a whole new map, introduces new (and old) creatures, new weapon, gear, items, caves, mechanics, etc. Well worth the asking price, considering the base game + expansion costs less than a triple A title, has content worth hundreds to thousands of hours (just look at the time played for most reviews, both positive and negative), no subscription fees, no microtransactions, and frequent content updates.
Just beware that if you are not running a mid to high end system you will need to run a few tweaks to play this game at an acceptable framerate. There are enough guides out there to help you with this (including steam community). The game is still in alpha and most optimizations will come once the content is in place. This is easily the most value I have gotten out of my money in any game, and still awaiting more.
If you're into taming dinos, riding tamed dinos, survival, open world exploration, crafting/building, PvE, PvP, single player offline, this game has it all.

This game is amazing for what it is. A mission based game where you grind for gear and experience. You can play with up to 4 players unless you are playing the ONE raid this game has to offer which you can have a max of 8 players. Missions are based on about 11  different objectives. Survival, Defence, Mobile Defence, Sabotage, Assassinate, Capture, Interception, Exterminate, Spy, Deception and Rescue. Several of these are very similar. It may seem like a lot of options, but after awhile you realize almost every mission is just to kill things and grind for drops. There is an ultimate goal of achieving a higher Mastery Rank which is achieved through leveling Warframes/Weapons etc which is an incentive to try every thing this game has to offer.
After awhile, the game becomes stale and repetative.
Boss's are NOT difficult and at the most have a a mechanic to stall you from finishing it quickly (invulnerability) or a simple order/way of killing them.
If you don't pay to play, Expect yourself to be playing a lot to enjoy the game and new things.  You might catch yourself having to farm A LOT but you gotta do what you have to do to make money to buy necesseties, QoL stuff, eye candy and upgrades.
Last thing I want to touch on is MOD-ING. One of, if not, the most important aspect of this game.
Although, Mod-ing right now is slightly stale because of some upgrades just always being more useful than others, it is still an awesome way of customizing your playstyle.
Example: You can make the ultimate sneaky ninja, a stronge and efficient skill user, a tank etc etc.
All this can be achieved with just slight tweaks to your mods.
Yes, it really is. With all the negative I lightly touched on, there is so much more positves about this game. Everyone can enjoy it and most of the time people are friendly. It's a unique game that can't really be compared to any other. This game is also free, yet is always being updated.
Every game has a few d-bags and this one isn't an exception.
What every game doesn't have is what Warframe offers

Frankly, there are a LOT of things, both good and bad, about Ark Survival.
I'll keep it very short and simple though, and save the more elaborate description for a youtube video.
Pros
1. TONS of stuff to do, be it building, taming/training dino's, mods, and so on. Literally there is TONS of content to explore.
2. The Experience. Yes, you can use console commands to spawn♥♥♥♥♥♥in, but frankly, the coolest thing I found about Ark was the "Experience". Learning about the Ark, and exploring it, and then sharing that experience with my friends. That alone was worth the cost of the game.
3. Developers. This may seem to be an odd one, but I see far too many games that frankly just don't listen to their "customers" and player base. A prime example of this is Warframe, or Star Conflict. Ark DOES listen to the player base, and they also are quite active in updating the game.
4. Always something new to test. Even if you explore everything in the Vanilla game, there are a TON of mods to tweak the game to do whatever you want, or to explore new content.
Con's
1. Poorly optimized. Yes, this is an old one, but to be fair, they've also programmed a LOT of launch options to try to fix it. Ultimately though, Ark has a LOT of powerful graphics and features, so of course its not going to work with everything. Still, buyer beware, you may have issues.
2. Connection problems. Sometimes you'll have a hard time connecting to a LAN game, or a server. just happens sometimes. For me, that's been quite rare though.
Overall, these are the major pro's and cons I can think of, and frankly, I consider the cost more then worth it. I know a lot of people are ♥♥♥♥♥ing about "The game isn't complete yet", but seriously, Warframe is STILL a Beta, and its been around for over 2 years now. I'd consider Ark a complete game as of right now, with them adding more content all the time.

Let me start by saying I have many hours into this game. This does not reflect my opinion of the game. There are many addicting qualities to this game. If you're in a tribe there's always things to do and your tribe always needs you and you feel like part of a team. It's an awesome feeling to make progress and watch your tribe grow. BUT the game has some gaping flaws that have only been exacerbated with the latest updates. Let me list the pros first:
+Graphics... The game is gorgeous to look at especially if you have a PC that can handle it.
+Team element... You build a special bond with your tribmeates as you pregress and grow your tribe. This is mainly due to how difficult it is to accomplish anything. Reaching milestones with tribemates is highly rewarding.
+Dinosaurs... There is a wide variety of dinosaurs and taming them is a blast.
+Server politics... This is the best part of the game but it's also sortof the worst. Vying for power in the ark is a tricky situation and it's fun to interact with other tribes and solve issues diplomatically.
Now let's get onto the cons of which there are numerous:
-Laggy... the more populated the server, the worse the lag. There are constant "Rubberband-ing" issues where your character will be flung back 5 seconds.
-Punishing... Everything worth doing in this game will take many MANY hours to accomplish. Slow taming dinosaurs can take 10 hours by itself not to mention the hours spent preparing for a tame. But you can lose these dinosaurs in mere seconds due to a slight misclick or even a rubberbanding issue. One of the most notorious issues for me is if you are riding a bird and you touch water it activates an ejector seat and flings you off. Now you are stuck in dangerous water and your bird will frantically fly around you or worse yet fly off into the sky never to be seen again.
-Balance... This is the biggest issue for me. There is no defender advantage. If you are a smallar budding tribe trying to establish yourself on a server good luck. The alpha tribes are typically drunk with power and wipe happy. And even if they are trying to maintain peace they rarely can. "Alpha" tribes are the tribes that have many players and devote many thousands of hours into the game making them bloated and unstoppable. Every server has them and they ruin the game. there is absolutely no way to defend against an attack from these tribes and you are entirely at their mercy. This was bad before the latest update.
-The latest update... Now you can transfer characters and dinos between servers. This may sound benign but let me explain what happened to our tribe. In an effort to drive people off a server to make room for their own people a tribe warped into our server and overnight mounted an attack on us. There was no warning and we were completely leveled to the ground. After all of the political discussions and diplomacy between tribes on the server none of it actually amounted to anything becuase some strangers warped in fully loaded and rolled on us.
-Physics... The physics in this game are simply broken. Falling is a nightmare and there is constant clipping on dinos and rocks and structures etc... makes the game nightmarish to play. Again these broken physics can cost you dearly.
Let me just say in conclusion playing this game is like being in a terrible relationship. You begin the game and there is a short honeymoon phase where you fall head over heels in love. Soon, though, you begin to realize that she is far from perfect. She is cold and harsh.. super possesive and demands that you spend all your time with her. She'll flip out and put you in the doghouse virtually without warning. The entire time you are with her you really hope that it will work out in the end but in your heart you KNOW that it will end in heartbreak and disaster. Then when it finally does end you are crushed and empty. Think of your last bad relationship. If I could get back all the time I put into it I know I would.

Overall I would recommend this game if you like a good survival game with dinos and Base Building.
I look forward to see where this game goes over the years.

There's a lot of good to this game, and I'll do it in a pro/con format:

*Every weapon is obtainable through crafting.
*You can play by yourself, with friends, or if you're feeling really dangerous, ONE friend.
*DE support is very helpful, and very responsive. The game is veeeeery community driven, and the players have changed the tide of the game.
Cons:
*The game can become FarmQuest 2077, as every weapon and Warframe does take some amount of rare resource. It is doable, though.
*Updates can be slow, and usually veteran players run out of content to do very quickly, causing players like me to take long breaks.
*Kickbot won't sing if you private message them.
All in all, I do recommend this progidal Free 2 Play game.

Well, yeah, you can install the game and play it but that's where it ends. I really doubt people have ever unlocked much of anything for free in this game. You get one character from the start, out of a choice of 3, and 2 weapons. That's it, 10 hours into it and I never found or unlocked anything, Basically, you'll have to pay for something. Now, for the gameplay it's allright but in the few years I've played this there has been no attempt to improve it. The sword mechanics are pretty bad, camera isn't anything to write home about, and the wallrunning is OK. Still, all these mechanics are made worse because the level design doesn't support any of it. The wall running is used in the tutorial and maybe once or twice in a level somewhere. There's a couple other bells and whistles that are nice but simply not enough. I guess theres some kinda story but the art design doesn't make me care about anything. Also, it's only partial controller support. I should have mentioned it earlier but it's listed on the store page. When they say partial, they mean almost none. Which is something that should exist for a third person game. It has potential but all the company seems to care about is selling DLC, but never advertising that it's DLC. Always implying that it's a free game, but it's sooo far from that. Everything is paywalled. Gameplay is NOT good enough to recommend paying for it either. Plenty of other multiplayer coop third person shooters. Sword gameplay is just basically standard melee combat. Like a beat em up, no MGS rising similarities to it at all. It's just a NO for me. Oh, and the community is absurdly devoted to the game. What's sad is the people who have put tons of time into the game don't perform any better than the newbie in combat, and generally will just run to the end of every mission ignoring everything, (probably because the mechanics aren't fun enough to bother using them, and they are just grinding the level system to be able to BUY a paywalled and levelwalled item or character). The end.

I will keep this short, no point in going what everyone else has already said, just simple highlights. Also no Pro/Cons, just words describing stuff:
# PRICING
* The pricing model is kinda fair, you get a log in reward, one of them is 75% discount for the ingame currency. This is THE ONLY TIME it is fairly priced, but it's a very often reward, no need to fret, and when it's 75% off it's honestly a good deal.
* Except for needing equipment slots (if you buy at 75% off it's like 25 cents) everything in the shop is fair: Anything non cosmetic drops, some cosmetics (helmets) also drop. Cosmetics are mostly really cheap.
* Except for the whale bait "Prime Access", everything is fairly priced, better than most games, and even the prime access is not so bad (everything it gives is also introduced as a drop in the game, except for a unique cosmetic).
* BEST PART: You can trade the real money currency, trading with players is hella clunky, but it works and is by far the cheapest way of getting anything and everything you need.
# Diablo Space Ninja Extravaganza
* This is a diablo-like game, you get loot drops, currency, enhancement stuff. The stats are fixed so it's IMHO infinity times better than diablo in this regard.
* The drops are a bit of a grind, but everything is fair or at least resonable.
# Upgrade mechanics
* In this game your power comes form two things: Equipment level (which at this point is near-irellevant beyond giving you extra "mod capacity", not a difficult grind at all.
* The real power comes from mods. They take a "meh" weapon and make it a weapon of mass destruction. However getting all the right mods is a grind (strong grind). However most are really cheap if you trade with other players (ingame currency or other rare mods).
* Some mods (great ones) are event exclusive so you either won't have them or cost an arm or a leg (they are not REALLY needed though).
# Game is wide but not deep
* The mechanics of the game are quite simplistic. The only real depth comes from weapon variaty and warframe abillities. That being said, game is not very deep, it is however unfathomly wide. 300 hours in and I still haven't touched a bunch of stuff (no derelict missions, haven't finished progression trough the map, no drako whatevers, no pet dog).
# Customizability
* If you play MMOs or diablo-likes for the "dress up" (admit it, that's what you REALLY like), then this game is for you. The customizability is off the charts.
# Replayability
* Yes, loads. Don't over do it, you can get burnt-out. I have friends with 1200 hours on record and they still play the game. Yes, it is replayable to no end.
# Gameplay
* Space NINJAS
* Space ... Ninjas
* Space Ninjas .... IN SPACE!
* Dogs. Space Dogs (sadly no space corgy #cowboyBebop)
# Conclusions
* Is it worth your time ?
* If you don't mind some grind and diablo-esque stuff (with space ninjas in space that have space dogs), yes!
* Is the pricing model ok ?
* I don't like prime access, but only on a conceptual level, it takes nothing from my enjoyment. The pricing model is amazing besides the small "unlock slots" stuff. It's dirt cheap but it forces you to buy some real money currency early on in the game. But again, this is one of the most fairly priced freemium games out there.
That is all.

I love this game, I've spent countless hours playing it (well, steam counted them). Though the game doesn't feel as optimized as it really could be. I'm going to recomend this game based on the fact that i keep coming back to it, but im going to be brutally honest in this review.
#1: playing without mods that fix many optimizations or gameplay issues feels like a waste of time.
official servers are hard, and im sure thats what the lead game dev intended, but its also sloppy and filled with holes. It seems that time and time again people will prefer to play on unofficial servers due to slightly higher rates (leveling, taming, eccedera) which doesn't really feel like cheating at all, it just makes the game bearable.
#2: official servers are terrible.
Although battleeye has relinquished much of the cheating found in official servers, it only works by scanning your computer for potential threats and leaves a lot of backdoors open for other threats, like DDOS and whatnot. Cheating is still a problem on many official servers. The next huge issue, being an opinion shared by most of the ARK gaming community, is that the base rates are ridiculously low. Without slightly altered rates for leveling, taming, and harvesting, say 5 times all of those, the game feels like a dying simulator. You pretty much get no where unless you're working with at least 5 other people, and even then its difficult. More times than not, you'll be killed and sent back to start from scratch by someone much stronger than you with a large tribe of 20 people or more. The last major point here, is admins for official servers seem non existant. Admins are available to help wth game breaking issues more often and most times, almost always on unofficial servers. Official servers however, if you got stuck in the ground or one of your tames decided to float endlessly, there would be nothing you can do about it.
#3: mods keep this game interesting.
It's no lie that this game can be a different experience each time you play it, it truly feels like you're playing in a wilderness. Then again, so does minecraft, and how many people over the age of 12 do you think play vanilla minecraft anymore? Simply put, it gets old, and there are only so many people who havent really gotten sick of the same routine over and over again. Updates seems to help alot, as there are many updates which integrate new game changing tools and creatures into the game, even whole new areas and DLC's to make a whole new different experience. But that isn't always enough, and many times these updates are rushed out and left unoptomized. Enter the world of ARK modding. Here people will create their own, unbroken versions of items and creatures from ARK updates that can be integrated into your game or unoffical server. New and exciting things aswell can be found to make for a completely new and different game. For example the Annunnaki Genesis mod, which is best played with servers running max levels of around 500 for players, adds all new bosses to the world to be killed and conquered, with all new items and gameplay mechanics. For posterity of this topic, the ARK now official "center" map was once a mod, and only became an official map due to how many people loved it and wanted more.
Conclusion:
The game is worth the money, but be prepared for the baggage that comes with the game. It's unfinished, unoptomized, but shows more potential than you would expect from this type of game, with the vast player base to boot. Most of all, don't be afraid to play on unoffical servers. Every one of them is different, with different mods and rates, and some fo them dont even have mods, some of them might aswell be the same as official servers with the only difference being an active admin who cares about your issues. Just make up your own mind by playing the game and just have fun with it.
last note: The lead director of ARK jeremy stieglitz, has a bit of a reputation for not being very nice to his fans. Well, more like he tells them off at almost every opportunity he can get. Maybe he's stressed, maybe he has other issues in his life, who knows. If you ever find yourself in a discord channel with him, like I have, during one of his "rants" or whatever, my advice would be to just keep your mouth shut or leave. It isn't a strange thing to eter his voice channel on discord and have the first sentence you hear from him be riddled with f***'s and unnecesary yelling. For lack of a better definition really, it feels like he just b**ches about whatever pisses him off for about an hour in front of an audience of say, 100 people, and anyone who speaks up and maybe, makes an opinion or asks about the game gets muted, and then brutally crucified verbally. It hasn't really happened to me, I didn't really speak up but, if anything, its almost funny to watch if you can deal with the fumigating anger irradiating off his crooked verbage.
Keep in mind also, a good majority of the bad reviews on this game are literally people complaining about how mean jeremy stieglitz is.. so take that into consideration when weighing the user reviews against whether or not you should actually buy the game.
MY PREVIOUS REVIEW:
I can't honestly recomend this game until Studio Wildcard gets their act together. Instead of releasing new content they should be focusing on fixing their older stuff thats littered with bugs and game breaking issues. File allocation is a mess, which makes loading times astronomical. It takes 30 minutes for most people to log into a server due to arks base game having over 15000 files, which is ridiculous. Thats without mods, maps, and everything else piled on top. Primitive + is an absolute disaster and doesn't even work. Half of the items are bugged and don't work at all, and server crashes are a common thing that happens about every 30 minutes when using prim +. On top of all the bugs and slowness of the game, that litterally requires you to have a solid state drive if you want to even load into the game at a decent pace *about 5 to 10 minutes*, Studio Wildcard has the gaul to release paid DLC on a game that might aswell be half broken.
This game has a lot of potential and i've enjoyed around 875+ hours playing on modded servers and the like, but its easy to see why people more and more are straying away from this game.
Studio Wildcard, get your priorities straight, or you're going to end up losing alot of your loyal players. If a game doesn't work, then you can't play it. If you can't play it, then theres no point in a paid DLC. Which mind you is litterally pay to win, as you can import dinos from scorched earth to other servers (including official).
If they could focus on fixing the game and making it playable for most people, then I would re-review this game completely. Until then consider me disapointed.

Cheating is still a problem on many official servers. The next huge issue, being an opinion shared by most of the ARK gaming community, is that the base rates are ridiculously low. Without slightly altered rates for leveling, taming, and harvesting, say 5 times all of those, the game feels like a dying simulator. You pretty much get no where unless you're working with at least 5 other people, and even then its difficult. More times than not, you'll be killed and sent back to start from scratch by someone much stronger than you with a large tribe of 20 people or more. The last major point here, is admins for official servers seem non existant. Admins are available to help wth game breaking issues more often and most times, almost always on unofficial servers. Official servers however, if you got stuck in the ground or one of your tames decided to float endlessly, there would be nothing you can do about it.
#3: mods keep this game interesting.
It's no lie that this game can be a different experience each time you play it, it truly feels like you're playing in a wilderness. Then again, so does minecraft, and how many people over the age of 12 do you think play vanilla minecraft anymore? Simply put, it gets old, and there are only so many people who havent really gotten sick of the same routine over and over again. Updates seems to help alot, as there are many updates which integrate new game changing tools and creatures into the game, even whole new areas and DLC's to make a whole new different experience. But that isn't always enough, and many times these updates are rushed out and left unoptomized. Enter the world of ARK modding. Here people will create their own, unbroken versions of items and creatures from ARK updates that can be integrated into your game or unoffical server. New and exciting things aswell can be found to make for a completely new and different game. For example the Annunnaki Genesis mod, which is best played with servers running max levels of around 500 for players, adds all new bosses to the world to be killed and conquered, with all new items and gameplay mechanics. For posterity of this topic, the ARK now official "center" map was once a mod, and only became an official map due to how many people loved it and wanted more.
Conclusion:
The game is worth the money, but be prepared for the baggage that comes with the game. It's unfinished, unoptomized, but shows more potential than you would expect from this type of game, with the vast player base to boot. Most of all, don't be afraid to play on unoffical servers. Every one of them is different, with different mods and rates, and some fo them dont even have mods, some of them might aswell be the same as official servers with the only difference being an active admin who cares about your issues. Just make up your own mind by playing the game and just have fun with it.
last note: The lead director of ARK jeremy stieglitz, has a bit of a reputation for not being very nice to his fans. Well, more like he tells them off at almost every opportunity he can get. Maybe he's stressed, maybe he has other issues in his life, who knows. If you ever find yourself in a discord channel with him, like I have, during one of his "rants" or whatever, my advice would be to just keep your mouth shut or leave. It isn't a strange thing to eter his voice channel on discord and have the first sentence you hear from him be riddled with f***'s and unnecesary yelling. For lack of a better definition really, it feels like he just b**ches about whatever pisses him off for about an hour in front of an audience of say, 100 people, and anyone who speaks up and maybe, makes an opinion or asks about the game gets muted, and then brutally crucified verbally. It hasn't really happened to me, I didn't really speak up but, if anything, its almost funny to watch if you can deal with the fumigating anger irradiating off his crooked verbage.

Well, as you can see i've played the living F**K out of this game. i have gone through every weapon, node, frame, quest, and piece of content this game has to offer. Let me tell you in a quick summary why you should play this game.
First off this is a free to play game unlike the others. 99% of the content in the game is fully unlockable without real money. money is used for a few, very exclusive aesthetic items and for convenience (if you dont want to farm, you can buy). that said, the currency you buy with real money is used in the game as the means of trading between players, meaning you can even acquire the currency used to unlock things quicker without spending real money just by selling things youve farmed to other players. there arent many other free to play games that can say that.
game description: third person shooter where your character has a set of 4 abilities unique to what character you're using. there are many different characters to choose from. you can be a rock golem that shoots bolders at your enemies, or a necromancer that summons killed enemies to fight for him. there is a character for everyones playstyle. the game really has done a great job building skillsets for anyone. want a stealth character, it's there. want a tank? here you go. want a caster with a bit of tankiness? sure. all characters can have their abilities augmented to cater more to ones playstyle with the use of mods. you can increase duration of skills, damage, or even how the skills interact with each other using mods, making each charcter even more unique. each character is also fully colorable, as is each weapon, companion, and even the ship you have on the loading screen.
This is a very arcade style third person shooter. if you're looking for competitive PvP, punishing gameplay, and high skillcaps this is not the game for you. the combat has some depth to it, but it wont take more than a few hours to master most of it. that doesnt mean the combat is dull or repetative, the game gives you hundreds of different ways to dispatch your enemies, but outside of style points, shooting them in the face works well for pretty much any situation. it's up to you if you'd prefer doing 3 backflips, grabbing onto a chandelier and then shooting lighting into water to stun your opponents, then dropping down and chopping them in half with your greatsword.
The graphical quality is nice, not top tier mind you, but it is a beautiful game that runs pretty well even on lower spec systems, showing nice amounts of optimization.
the art style is unique. you really wont find a game that looks like this anywhere else. it's bizzarrely lovely. the art style grows on you, even if your intial response was distaste. the developers get massive creativity points here.
There is content in this game to go through, and lots of it. there are dozens of tilesets, and most are randomized to some extent each time you play them, so they dont feel too familiar, even after dozens of runs. That said, the bulk of your time isn't going to be spent "beating" levels. all levels are very very difficult until you get some basic gear, at which point the game becomes pretty much a cakewalk. this is my biggest criticism of warframe, the difficulty scaling is horrible. for a new player, most maps seem almost impossible solo, for veterans,  those same levels are laughably easy.
The bulk of your time in this game is going to be spent grinding. make no mistake, this is a very very grindy game. if you want a shiny gold alternative to your favorite weapon, you're going to have to farm for it. that said, there is a robust trading market where you can acquire those items you cant/havent farmed. if the node you're trying to farm is too hard, there's always the really nice community in the recruiting tab to help you. which brings me to my next point.
the community in this game is fantastic. easily the best community ive ever seen in a video game. people are always willing to help you, give you information, or invite you to their clan.
Honestly, other than a lack of true endgame content for veterans, the only other major complaint i have with warframe is that for new players, there's so much information thrown at them all at once it becomes overwhelming. the learning curve for this game is actually pretty huge. just figuring out how to build your first weapon requires some work. I was totally overwhelmed a year and a half ago when i first started playing. theyve since added a dozen or so new features, and that only makes the problem worse for new players.
So to sum up:
Pros:
unique art style
good optimzation and graphical quality
fantastic community
developers care
addictive arcade style gameplay
tons of content to go through, 99% of which is fully acquireable without real money.
no pay walls
new content uploaded regularly/ bug fixes and game tweaked constantly
tons of customization
cons:
VERY grindy
steep learning curve
no endgame, very difficult early game
there's almost too much content at this point
