I have invested hundreds of hours into this game and I don't regret one single minute of it. My friends and I were playing for the most time on private guild servers, so I didn't interact with the community all that much, only when dealing with minor problems or gathering informations.
Since it was first released, this game has come further than most other Early Access titles. Though it is one of the least appreciated ones, due to a lack of communication and wildspread rumors.
You start with nothing but your bare fists and need to collect your surrounding materials in order to build tools, shelter and tame animals. What sounds very shallow is in fact a deep crafting system, an almost flawless building system and intelligent taming.
The progression is steady and fun. You can chose to take a risk and get to the next higher tier, or grind with your lower end tools to get to your goal. The only downside to this is, especially if you are a beginner, you may feel the urge to tame everything around you, crowding your base with unneeded dinos.
I have never encountered any problems related to sound and in fact, never needed to change the volume ingame. Not even while voice chatting.
The soundtrack is easy to hear while in the middle of screaming people and subtle enough to ignore, when cooking, crafting or gathering.
The performance is the main reason for most negative reviews.
ARK relies extremely on processing power, and thus, can not be played on most PCs without any lag. Though, this is not due to a lack of optimization or polishing. It is made for next gen machines and thus should be played with adequate hardware.
The system requirements to enjoy the game may be MUCH higher than the minumum requirements to start the game.
The game rarely ever crashes and the biggest problem is clipping and dinos getting stuck somewhere. But workarounds are typically easy to use, but sometimes frustrating and take a long time. I recommend frequent saves of the game and backing your save up, before trying something extreme.
One of the most active development teams for an Early Access title! Updates are being released almost two times a month, with roughly one major content update every other month. Community mods have even made it into the game officially. Wildcard has more than once hired community members for making awesome mods to improve the game even further.
The fact, that this DLC and the developers have gotten so much hate, because they sell a DLC is incredible. Many people don't seem to understand, what Early Access means and what it doesn't.
As an Early Access game, it means, the development team releases a game, that's still getting major reworks and content updates. It doesn't mean it is a typical Alpha game, that lacks content, runs unstable and can only be described as a tech demo.
ARK has content for hundreds of hours, tons of replay value and enough variety to keep playing while constantly discovering new things. Plus they release their game on consoles. What else is there to be said?
As of the DLC, it offers everything, you would ask for in a triple A title DLC. It offers new mechanics, a whole new feel to the game, the challenges of the new map are different and it feels finished. The DLC exclusive content can also be transferred to the old map without any problems.

I will keep this short, no point in going what everyone else has already said, just simple highlights. Also no Pro/Cons, just words describing stuff:
# PRICING
* The pricing model is kinda fair, you get a log in reward, one of them is 75% discount for the ingame currency. This is THE ONLY TIME it is fairly priced, but it's a very often reward, no need to fret, and when it's 75% off it's honestly a good deal.
* Except for needing equipment slots (if you buy at 75% off it's like 25 cents) everything in the shop is fair: Anything non cosmetic drops, some cosmetics (helmets) also drop. Cosmetics are mostly really cheap.
* Except for the whale bait "Prime Access", everything is fairly priced, better than most games, and even the prime access is not so bad (everything it gives is also introduced as a drop in the game, except for a unique cosmetic).
* BEST PART: You can trade the real money currency, trading with players is hella clunky, but it works and is by far the cheapest way of getting anything and everything you need.
# Diablo Space Ninja Extravaganza
* This is a diablo-like game, you get loot drops, currency, enhancement stuff. The stats are fixed so it's IMHO infinity times better than diablo in this regard.
* The drops are a bit of a grind, but everything is fair or at least resonable.
# Upgrade mechanics
* In this game your power comes form two things: Equipment level (which at this point is near-irellevant beyond giving you extra "mod capacity", not a difficult grind at all.
* The real power comes from mods. They take a "meh" weapon and make it a weapon of mass destruction. However getting all the right mods is a grind (strong grind). However most are really cheap if you trade with other players (ingame currency or other rare mods).
* Some mods (great ones) are event exclusive so you either won't have them or cost an arm or a leg (they are not REALLY needed though).
# Game is wide but not deep
* The mechanics of the game are quite simplistic. The only real depth comes from weapon variaty and warframe abillities. That being said, game is not very deep, it is however unfathomly wide. 300 hours in and I still haven't touched a bunch of stuff (no derelict missions, haven't finished progression trough the map, no drako whatevers, no pet dog).
# Customizability
* If you play MMOs or diablo-likes for the "dress up" (admit it, that's what you REALLY like), then this game is for you. The customizability is off the charts.
# Replayability
* Yes, loads. Don't over do it, you can get burnt-out. I have friends with 1200 hours on record and they still play the game. Yes, it is replayable to no end.
# Gameplay
* Space NINJAS
* Space ... Ninjas
* Space Ninjas .... IN SPACE!
* Dogs. Space Dogs (sadly no space corgy #cowboyBebop)
# Conclusions
* Is it worth your time ?
* If you don't mind some grind and diablo-esque stuff (with space ninjas in space that have space dogs), yes!
* Is the pricing model ok ?
* I don't like prime access, but only on a conceptual level, it takes nothing from my enjoyment. The pricing model is amazing besides the small "unlock slots" stuff. It's dirt cheap but it forces you to buy some real money currency early on in the game. But again, this is one of the most fairly priced freemium games out there.
That is all.

The thing that bothers me the most and only thing that bothers me, Warframe makes you pay for couple major things. You can argue Warframe doesn't "make you" pay them, but because of my personality of wanting to push it to the best stats available with fair progress speed, I find the game trying to make you either choose 1) farm for couple days, try to sell them for the next couple days for 2 ~ 4 inventory slot or 2) pay 5$ or 25~50$ when you get 50%+ sale (you don't see them often as you'd hope however, unlike GRP (one of Ghost Recon series game.) and buy whatever the hell you want, mostly inventory, bobble head, and Archwing stuff (cause screw farming those). other than those is not really worth it.
Don't sound like you don't have many things you'd have to buy, right? Before I get into this whole 'you gatta pay alot' business,
, AND selling since I find selling things take some time if you plan on selling them with reasonable price.
Now, do note, I like collecting things in game. Meaning, I don't sell weapons or anything I come across easily simply because my inventory is lacking. Also, I started to hoard even more after finding out DE decides to delete any weapons or frames when they believe it is out of date while not taking away existing said weapons and frames. That said, this game makes you bit hard to do keep all your previous weapons. In game real life money is called "platinum". You need 20 platinum to buy 1 Warframe inventory, 12 platinum for 2 weapon inventory (All weapons, does not separate primary, secondary, melee)
Theres 33 Warframes, and 221 weapons available if you start now (I did not count Founders exclusive Warframe and 2 weapons). It’s going to cost you alot just to get all the weapons and Warframes since… well it’s not like game is giving you 100 inventory space when you start out the game. And with that said, keeping all of your weapons with you will really halt your progress time to time.
If you are also like me who likes to be on top-average side in the stat wise, it also is sort of hard to do that.
There are limited time available mods (upgrades) for your weapons that were released in the events increasing your damage type by 120% which is very effective for your weapon, while other non-120% mod is very much useless. They hardly ever get released again and even if they do couple times a year, you have to literally farm them for 3days. If you want to buy them off of the players, they can easily cost you anywhere from 200~1000plat each. Not a great idea when there are many dmg type and weapon type (primary, secondary, melee).
So that's it. That's my opinion. You have TLDL on top. I just cant really suggest anyone to play this alone when they like to collect items and like being on the strong side in game without spending load of money, or just dont have time to spend extra hundreds of hours of farming and selling.

Well, as you can see i've played the living F**K out of this game. i have gone through every weapon, node, frame, quest, and piece of content this game has to offer. Let me tell you in a quick summary why you should play this game.
First off this is a free to play game unlike the others. 99% of the content in the game is fully unlockable without real money. money is used for a few, very exclusive aesthetic items and for convenience (if you dont want to farm, you can buy). that said, the currency you buy with real money is used in the game as the means of trading between players, meaning you can even acquire the currency used to unlock things quicker without spending real money just by selling things youve farmed to other players. there arent many other free to play games that can say that.
game description: third person shooter where your character has a set of 4 abilities unique to what character you're using. there are many different characters to choose from. you can be a rock golem that shoots bolders at your enemies, or a necromancer that summons killed enemies to fight for him. there is a character for everyones playstyle. the game really has done a great job building skillsets for anyone. want a stealth character, it's there. want a tank? here you go. want a caster with a bit of tankiness? sure. all characters can have their abilities augmented to cater more to ones playstyle with the use of mods. you can increase duration of skills, damage, or even how the skills interact with each other using mods, making each charcter even more unique. each character is also fully colorable, as is each weapon, companion, and even the ship you have on the loading screen.
This is a very arcade style third person shooter. if you're looking for competitive PvP, punishing gameplay, and high skillcaps this is not the game for you. the combat has some depth to it, but it wont take more than a few hours to master most of it. that doesnt mean the combat is dull or repetative, the game gives you hundreds of different ways to dispatch your enemies, but outside of style points, shooting them in the face works well for pretty much any situation. it's up to you if you'd prefer doing 3 backflips, grabbing onto a chandelier and then shooting lighting into water to stun your opponents, then dropping down and chopping them in half with your greatsword.
The graphical quality is nice, not top tier mind you, but it is a beautiful game that runs pretty well even on lower spec systems, showing nice amounts of optimization.
the art style is unique. you really wont find a game that looks like this anywhere else. it's bizzarrely lovely. the art style grows on you, even if your intial response was distaste. the developers get massive creativity points here.
There is content in this game to go through, and lots of it. there are dozens of tilesets, and most are randomized to some extent each time you play them, so they dont feel too familiar, even after dozens of runs. That said, the bulk of your time isn't going to be spent "beating" levels. all levels are very very difficult until you get some basic gear, at which point the game becomes pretty much a cakewalk. this is my biggest criticism of warframe, the difficulty scaling is horrible. for a new player, most maps seem almost impossible solo, for veterans,  those same levels are laughably easy.
The bulk of your time in this game is going to be spent grinding. make no mistake, this is a very very grindy game. if you want a shiny gold alternative to your favorite weapon, you're going to have to farm for it. that said, there is a robust trading market where you can acquire those items you cant/havent farmed. if the node you're trying to farm is too hard, there's always the really nice community in the recruiting tab to help you. which brings me to my next point.
the community in this game is fantastic. easily the best community ive ever seen in a video game. people are always willing to help you, give you information, or invite you to their clan.
Honestly, other than a lack of true endgame content for veterans, the only other major complaint i have with warframe is that for new players, there's so much information thrown at them all at once it becomes overwhelming. the learning curve for this game is actually pretty huge. just figuring out how to build your first weapon requires some work. I was totally overwhelmed a year and a half ago when i first started playing. theyve since added a dozen or so new features, and that only makes the problem worse for new players.
So to sum up:
Pros:
unique art style
good optimzation and graphical quality
fantastic community
developers care
addictive arcade style gameplay
tons of content to go through, 99% of which is fully acquireable without real money.
no pay walls
new content uploaded regularly/ bug fixes and game tweaked constantly
tons of customization
cons:
VERY grindy
steep learning curve
no endgame, very difficult early game
there's almost too much content at this point

This review only exists to clarify how "expensive" warframe is:
It's not f2p, or p2w. It is free-to-demo. At the risk of sounding arrogant, this is the undeniable truth of how the game works. Don't get me wrong. I think the game is awesome, but when you find yourself hitting your first paywall, understand that this is a free-to-demo game. Let me explain:
A fundamental aspect of this game requires real-to-in-game currency (platinum): Getting more warframes (aka characters). There are 50 of them. about 30% of them are variants of another,  but that's not the point. As of this review and you get to start off with 2 slots. TWO SLOTS. Weapon slot count is equally pathetic. More slots are only available by buying them with real money.
Did you farm your way up to end game without paying, and instead traded for plat from other players? Good for you. Just you though. Because at some point in time, someone had to buy that plat in order to progress through the game. If you did not pay real money, someone else did. This is fundamentally a paywall. You just circumvented it with obscenely hard work.
IMPORTANT NOTE FOR NEW PLAYERS ABOUT BUYING PLAT: You get daily rewards when you sign on. Sometimes you will get a discount on platinum puchase. They range from 20% to 75%. Wait until you get the 75% discount, and then buy the $200 or $100 platinum package for 1/4th of the price. Ark is rather interesting.
My first attempt was to play on public server 85, I struggled to get to grasps with the game at first and felt like all I was doing was dying, but the truth was that I was too much in a hurry to actually think about the game as a survival game.
You will die a lot ot start, the world is unforgiving and punishes those unprepared, like it should. On PVP you will be raided now and then depending on the servers playerbase and it's really important to establish a good relationship between yourself and the alpha tribe so that they might look after you. The game is interesting because it relies on social interactions, if you're the quiet type, don't be too suprised if you get flattened.
I got heavily raided in that server, and while I was initially salty, it was through my own aggressive expansion and gathering of the small tribes that made me a threat, from an alpha tribe perspective their main goal is to remain top dog, now they see a guy rallying support from the smaller tribes and forming alliences, what better a message to send them than to crush that tribe. It just makes sense, unless you have the power (and desire) to do so, learn your place i nthe peckling order.
I then moved over to another public server and became a part of the Alpha tribe, and the game was completly diffrent, for over 9 months we reigned supreme (only losing our huge bases after we quit for a few months) the servers history was rich, there were deceptions, wars, alliences and even inticate storylines attached to each faction crafted by their actions. We ruled with an iron fist and found that if players were aware of your specific rules they would abide to them. A really fascinating game.
Now there are a few minor issues.
-The game (thanks to it's constant development and thus improvement) has a couple of minor bugs.
-The updates usually always favour the strong (which isn't completly a bad thing, since the strong usually put in the most hours)
I would say this, with the dawn perodically generated maps this game will be amazing to play with friends.
If you like the thrill of PVP, esponage and politics then play the public servers, if you just want to build, then PVE is "ok" too.
Honestly, if you want to play a beautiful (and on ultra settings VERY beautiful) game, that's a cross between minecraft and DayZ, this is the ticket for you!

There are issues on balancing, dino types, and well, the concept that is tribes. Understandably, larger tribes will get more powerful, more quickly, then smaller tribes. However, once you have built up, you run the risk of inviting people who will dump/negate all of your work - which is mitigated to some extent with pins/tribe settings. But this leans the game towards several, medium-small tribes, which has it's own issues such as maintaining investments and building up with an alpha on the server.
As far as dinos, they are currently an insane time sink (forward loading the sink with kibble, or no), which can make losses incredibly devastating. These losses can range from bored alpha tribes, glitches, alpha dinos, or just general misfortune (such as getting shot down by an autoturret that's within a base getting rendered in). Not to mention that a tame can be killed (if you aren't careful/knowledgeable) hour(s) into a tame by wild spawns. The time sink has, in part, influenced the growth/propogation of unofficial servers - with custom rates, Ark can feel more like a casual video game than a second job.
Speaking of custom rates, the inherent balancing on official servers can be very... unpleasant. Building a 2x2x2 wood house can be rather time consuming on normal rates if done by hand - although done significantly faster if done by dino. However, that method has it's own risks as aforementioned. In essence, this makes can leave a bad taste in players mouths which causes them to stop playing (I had 5 new tribe members one week, and they all stopped playing within another). Furthermore, the gap between an established tribe and a new player is rather incredulous - it can lead to toxicity such as the established tribe abusing new players or upfront denial of play by way of foundation/pillar spamming. On the other hand, it can swing the other way with the established tribe being generous. However, the power difference is such that the average player has no hope of being competitive - with dinosaurs such as the giganotosaurus, quetzal, and mosasaur, a single tribe can easily overpower everything from the previous tier and below.
Overall, the experience can be pleasant if you find a good server with good rates, good fellow players to play with, and generally don't be a♥♥♥♥♥♥ However, the game favors aggression and toxicity (e.g. being raided while you are offline), so it can be very inciting and depressing. While I have found my time spent worth it, I feel it would have been better spent playing a different game - the game has time sinks designed into basic play to the point where I wouldn't be surprised if 3/4 of my logged hours were spent afk. In fact, I did use Ark as a sleep aid sometimes - since some activities are time gated, but very useful, it was a reliable source of boredom. But until they fundamentally change number balancing (eg rates,dino stats, etc) and game mechanics (passive tames, lack of interaction during a tame), it isn't worth it to invest time into this game. It's basically a salt factory like LoL, unoptimized enough where minecraft would be better, and generally as fun as watching paint dry at times.

Beginner's guide:  Warframe is simple as it gets!
1. What is a Warframe?
You are the Tenno, a space ninja, sporting a skin tight battlesuit called a Warframe.
This grants you four powers, a bit like in a moba.
These become available to you as you level up.
They are slotted on your alphanumeric 1,2,3, and 4, being your ultimate power.
You maneuver by WASD like in any FPS game.
You shoot with left mouse, zoom with right mouse.
Crouch with CTRL
Jump with SPACE
2. What are armaments?
You equip your warframe with a Primary, Secondary, and Melee weapon.
Primary are big guns, bows, rifles, cannons, gunblades, heavy stuff.
Secondary are pistols, shurikens, kunai, light stuff.
Primary and secondary have ammo, which you pick up as you go along.
Various types of ammo are colour-coded so learn which colour reloads what type of primary or secondary weapon. Not hard.
You switch between primary and secondary by pressing F.
You switch to melee by holding F or you can quick melee by tapping E.
Melee are anything. Swords axes staves bladeguns etc.
You attain your weapons by crafting them in your Liset.
3. What's the Liset?
It's your personal one-man spaceship. You see them fly in when you start a mission and pick you up when you end your mission. There are various amenities in the Liset that will be of service to you, including your forge and armory. The game will teach you these, just pay attention.
4. Loot?
You can loot EVERY ITEM, including Waframes.
PAY ATTENTION.
YOU CAN LOOT EVERYTHING.
INCLUDING WARFRAMES.
Or you can buy almost everything from the cash shop.
ALMOST.
USE THE WIKI.
4. What are MODs?
Mods are little cards you find as drops and you can insert them into your gear, pets, warframe or archwing.
You do this in your Liset, in the Armory.
You can level up these mods.
The game will teach you how.
They are a must, they make you stronger.
ALL OF THEM CAN BE LOOTED. USE THE WIKI.
5. What is Platinum?
It's the currency. You can sell your loot from the Void, or you can spend real money for Platinum.
The economy is perfectly free, and you can get anything if you are patient and smart about it.
6. How do I begin?
I'll give you one way to start the game, I'm not saying this is the best or the only way but it has its merit.
USE THE WIKI.
I recommend you pick Mag. There is little difference in which frame you pick as far as your ability to slaughter goes, but the Mag has several abilities which I find benefit your team even if you are a newbie and you have what to learn.
Think of the Mag as a semi-healer aoe support loot collector.
SKILL1 - PULL :: This skill makes you able to pull enemies and with the Greedy Pull MOD, loot to you. You used to be able to pull things through walls but now you have to have a clean line of sight. Boo hoo. Still a godly skill. Get Greedy Pull MOD asap!!
SKILL2 - SHIELD THING :: This skill makes you recharge your shields and deal the enemy's shield as damage to them. Works wonderfully on Corpus mobs. Aka box heads, aka robotmen aka Corpus mobs.
SKILL3 - BULLET MAGNET THING :: This skill creates a bubble around a target which will draw in all the gunfire. Very useful in heavy combat.
SKILL4 - OMFG I'M MAGNETO :: You lift and damage and drop and damage and damage and damage enemies. It hurts, so use it a lot.
Other mods to get: Look up the mag youtube video for the right build.
USE THE WIKI.
Once you are in, you get picked up for the story. It will teach you everything you need to know. Once you kick Vor's behind, you get to be on your way. To level up easily, complete every mission node on every planet. Team up with others for better results.

There are issues on balancing, dino types, and well, the concept that is tribes. Understandably, larger tribes will get more powerful, more quickly, then smaller tribes. However, once you have built up, you run the risk of inviting people who will dump/negate all of your work - which is mitigated to some extent with pins/tribe settings. But this leans the game towards several, medium-small tribes, which has it's own issues such as maintaining investments and building up with an alpha on the server.
As far as dinos, they are currently an insane time sink (forward loading the sink with kibble, or no), which can make losses incredibly devastating. These losses can range from bored alpha tribes, glitches, alpha dinos, or just general misfortune (such as getting shot down by an autoturret that's within a base getting rendered in). Not to mention that a tame can be killed (if you aren't careful/knowledgeable) hour(s) into a tame by wild spawns. The time sink has, in part, influenced the growth/propogation of unofficial servers - with custom rates, Ark can feel more like a casual video game than a second job.
Speaking of custom rates, the inherent balancing on official servers can be very... unpleasant. Building a 2x2x2 wood house can be rather time consuming on normal rates if done by hand - although done significantly faster if done by dino. However, that method has it's own risks as aforementioned. In essence, this makes can leave a bad taste in players mouths which causes them to stop playing (I had 5 new tribe members one week, and they all stopped playing within another). Furthermore, the gap between an established tribe and a new player is rather incredulous - it can lead to toxicity such as the established tribe abusing new players or upfront denial of play by way of foundation/pillar spamming. On the other hand, it can swing the other way with the established tribe being generous. However, the power difference is such that the average player has no hope of being competitive - with dinosaurs such as the giganotosaurus, quetzal, and mosasaur, a single tribe can easily overpower everything from the previous tier and below.
Overall, the experience can be pleasant if you find a good server with good rates, good fellow players to play with, and generally don't be a♥♥♥♥♥♥ However, the game favors aggression and toxicity (e.g. being raided while you are offline), so it can be very inciting and depressing. While I have found my time spent worth it, I feel it would have been better spent playing a different game - the game has time sinks designed into basic play to the point where I wouldn't be surprised if 3/4 of my logged hours were spent afk. In fact, I did use Ark as a sleep aid sometimes - since some activities are time gated, but very useful, it was a reliable source of boredom. But until they fundamentally change number balancing (eg rates,dino stats, etc) and game mechanics (passive tames, lack of interaction during a tame), it isn't worth it to invest time into this game. It's basically a salt factory like LoL, unoptimized enough where minecraft would be better, and generally as fun as watching paint dry at times.

This review only exists to clarify how "expensive" warframe is:
It's not f2p, or p2w. It is free-to-demo. At the risk of sounding arrogant, this is the undeniable truth of how the game works. Don't get me wrong. I think the game is awesome, but when you find yourself hitting your first paywall, understand that this is a free-to-demo game. Let me explain:
A fundamental aspect of this game requires real-to-in-game currency (platinum): Getting more warframes (aka characters). There are 50 of them. about 30% of them are variants of another,  but that's not the point. As of this review and you get to start off with 2 slots. TWO SLOTS. Weapon slot count is equally pathetic. More slots are only available by buying them with real money.
Did you farm your way up to end game without paying, and instead traded for plat from other players? Good for you. Just you though. Because at some point in time, someone had to buy that plat in order to progress through the game. If you did not pay real money, someone else did. This is fundamentally a paywall. You just circumvented it with obscenely hard work.
IMPORTANT NOTE FOR NEW PLAYERS ABOUT BUYING PLAT: You get daily rewards when you sign on. Sometimes you will get a discount on platinum puchase. They range from 20% to 75%. Wait until you get the 75% discount, and then buy the $200 or $100 platinum package for 1/4th of the price. That is plenty to give you that initial boost you need so you don't spend +50 hours more than you need to, crawling your way to end game.
Don't worry. After that, you won't need to buy a single bit of plat, unless you're lazy asf  or want to support the devs. You'll be able to trade for it to your heart's content.

I have taken a break from ARK for a while now. But found it needed to endless mention some things about it since I have done so much in it.
ARK is a wonderful timesink for someone competitive like me. I only played on PvP-Hardcore servers and met the worst and the best people. Surviving there alone is not an option for the long term so you are going to need people by your side. Those could be your friends, playing the game with, who have envisioned a similar goal like you. OR you could communicate in chat and make new friends.
I attempted the latter multiple times. A couple of times it became alliances. Some better than others and ofcourse some ending in horrible backstabs. One time I was accepted into a bigger tribe, they found me on a beach and I just talked with one of their guys for a while and they wanted me to be part of them. I have played with them for quite a while and had a lot of fun. It was one of many fun experiences in ARK for me.
I have also played with friends. My best experience with that being the alpha tribe on a server. We ruled the server and tried actually setting things up as if we were a governing organ. We communicated in english and had a couple of regulars who were also on the server and with whome with had good communications and a lot of fun. The backside of this I could refer to as "The Russian underworld". Most of the Official-EU-Hardcore-PvP servers are occupied by random europeans and a lot of russians. Who will always group up against said europeans. On the server on which we were the alpha tribe, most of our daily routine contained scouting out the map, looking for bases and seeing their growth. Overseeing the economics of your country one might say. How we still don't know, but the Russians showed exceptionally fast growing rates and exceptionally low attempts at communications in a language that would be understandable for us. Most of the time this resulted in us better being safe than sorry and taking care of the "infestation". Sadly this also resulted in the server dieing out, no matter how nice we were to english speaking people. They would always be choked out by some russians who then were put in the dirt by us.
It seemed like russians are the only one willing to invest time to become something, a sad but true fact.
So. I wasn't planning on making a review about graphics, game mechanics etc. That has been done plenty. It is in the end, in it's true essence, a multiplayer game. Multiplayer games are made by the people playing them. The game itself you could call a "sidenote". It's there, but it's just not the main part of the game, strange as it sounds.
When it comes to the multiplayer part of this game I can make 1 solid conclusion.
"It is not as good as it used to be"
When ARK was released (I bought the game 1 day after release) the servers were filled, everyone was learning the game together. Discussing this in chat and having a blast. Rivalries were created, the usual online game order was in place. People deciding to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, people trying to be nice, people who were neutral to all sides, people who were silent but deadly and ofcourse first time players who got either horrible murdered by ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s or helped out by the nice people.
What my current issue is what ARK is that all of those experiences are on PvP-Hardcore. Which in the end was the gamemode which died out faster than any other. People didn't want to be punished for dieing that much, the losing of levels was a step to far. Though understandable, I loved the punishment of hardcore. It inspired me to make better choices, same as the other people on the servers, you had to think before you acted or else all that you had worked for could go down the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
In conclusion, ARK is a wonderfull and beautiful game, but the multiplayer aspect in the more punishing servers has been reduced to next to none. There is no way to breach the language barrier between English speakers and Russian speakers besides constant ♥♥♥♥♥♥ google translations or learning the language yourself. For the multiplayer aspect was and still is a vital part of this game and since this has died out so much I have basically stopped playing. But if you wish to play on less punishing servers where you can build and make a fun little living for yourself where next to nothing can harm you and there is litterally not reason to even call it a "survival game" then this is the game for you.

This review only exists to clarify how "expensive" warframe is:
It's not f2p, or p2w. It is free-to-demo. At the risk of sounding arrogant, this is the undeniable truth of how the game works. Don't get me wrong. I think the game is awesome, but when you find yourself hitting your first paywall, understand that this is a free-to-demo game. Let me explain:
A fundamental aspect of this game requires real-to-in-game currency (platinum): Getting more warframes (aka characters). There are 50 of them. about 30% of them are variants of another,  but that's not the point. As of this review and you get to start off with 2 slots. TWO SLOTS. Weapon slot count is equally pathetic. More slots are only available by buying them with real money.
Did you farm your way up to end game without paying, and instead traded for plat from other players? Good for you. Just you though. Because at some point in time, someone had to buy that plat in order to progress through the game. If you did not pay real money, someone else did. This is fundamentally a paywall. You just circumvented it with obscenely hard work.
IMPORTANT NOTE FOR NEW PLAYERS ABOUT BUYING PLAT: You get daily rewards when you sign on. Sometimes you will get a discount on platinum puchase. They range from 20% to 75%. Wait until you get the 75% discount, and then buy the $200 or $100 platinum package for 1/4th of the price. That is plenty to give you that initial boost you need so you don't spend +50 hours more than you need to, crawling your way to end game.
Don't worry. After that, you won't need to buy a single bit of plat, unless you're lazy asf  or want to support the devs. You'll be able to trade for it to your heart's content.

OVERVIEW: Ark was tremendously fun at EA release in June 2016, when there was the promise that its systems would be further developed, and its gameplay refined. As of November 2016, this promise has been little realized even though the developer, Wildcard, has added a great amount of content to the game (mostly in the form of prehistoric fauna).  The more you invest on the official servers, the more vulnerable you become to the litany of poorly-designed gameplay changes that have been a hallmark of Ark's EA release.  Also, the use of paid-for ESP and aim-bot software is rampant, even though Ark uses BattleEye, an invasive anti-cheating program that runs in the background as you play.
*********
A GAME THAT COMPROMISES YOUR LIFESTYLE
I have played Ark for 1.5 years since its release in Early Access, and have accumulated thousands of hours playing on the same official PvP server.  It's super fun to play when you're scraping together sticks and stones to make a hut, but once you've invested your time into a defensible structure and a stable of animals, you realize that your investment will need to be maintained every day (hence the staggering number of hours some players have in the game).  While you sleep, or spend time with your family, your base will be raided, and it's common that your entire investment on the server—with the exception of your character level—will be wiped clean.  This is the jeopardy you put yourself in by playing this game.
BUYER BEWARE: There is not currently a defense strong enough to withstand a wipe carried out by determined players.  In fact, the developers added three out-of-scale animals (the giganotosaurus, the titanosaur, and the dodorex) to the game to facilitate this type of gameplay.  Ultimately, you will not be able to play without ​a ​nuclear threat looming over you, and you must use the ​out-of-scale dinosaurs against aggressors before they use them against you.  If the game took 30 min to an hour, this would be a fun​ decider of the​ late​-​game, but it takes months​ of real time​ to reach this level of armament​ in Ark​.
The fundamental flaw of Ark is that though it fosters many types of gameplay, they are not blended together by systems that balance the interests of a diverse audience.  Investment in strong infrastructure will be overcome by griefing.  Explorative gameplay (i.e. building Dinotopia) will be overcome by overwhelming PvP.  Even great PvPers will succumb to the plague of pay-for cheating software that swarms around this game.
After several contentious months during which players who owned the Scorched Earth DLC were able to attack base-game servers from expansion servers with little fear of reprisal, on 18 November 2016, the developers made it possible for players to transfer animals and munitions around the entire official PvP server network.  The PvP network has been non-stop warfare since that time.  Ark went from being a 4 hour daily commitment to a 24 hour commitment if you want to keep your stuff.  For a year and a half, my friends and I fought off every manner of griefer and possessive alpha tribe so that we could build an official server that was fun for new players, and that required relatively little maintenance.  Now, my entire server (30+ players) has fallen except for me, and I have been fighting round the clock against ESP hacks and aimbots to maintain what I built over a year and a half.
I feel cheated by a developer that has routinely ignored the best advice of its playerbase.  Don't put yourself in the same position.  Play a different game.
***********
Are you still here?  Good, I know the temptation is strong.  Take to heart these final words:
WHAT IS ARK?  I would say that Ark: Survival Evolved is a persistent-world shooter that requires large-scale resource management and long-term tactical posturing within the housing of a Cretaceous survival simulator.  But it doesn't take much work to overcome the survival aspects of the game, and soon enough, you'll be more worried about disconnecting than about being eaten by large carnivores or starving to death.
"BUT I LOVE DINOSAURS!"  If you're like me, and you're here for the prehistoric megafauna, know that it's less-nuanced than the cars and trucks in a racing game, and most of the animals look ridiculous compared to the life-recreations that we're used to seeing in paleontological references and museums.  This is not Walking with Dinosaurs, as will be apparent the first time you watch a tyrannosaurus rex L1 L1 L1 L1 a mammoth repeating the same attack animation.  The mortal combat that is a hallmark of dino documentaries is absent from this game.  Most of Ark's animal models are the equivalent of cheap plastic dinos that vaguely resemble any known genus or species.
"BUT I HEARD THE DEVELOPERS ARE VERY RESPONSIVE!"  It's true that developer Wildcard has pushed a ton of content Ark: Survival Evolved, but they did it without first building the infrastructure to make it all useful.  In fact, they have added new content that makes much of the old content redundant.  For instance, as of November 2016, you only really need to tame a giganotosaurus, a quetzalcoatlus, an ankylosaurus, and a mosasaur.  Everything else is just a step toward those goals. The poorest gameplay mechanics (creature AI, the creature-taming system, the building system, and the server-transferring system) have not been improved since launch in June 2015.  Instead, Wildcard has let the tail wag the dog: late-game PvP dominates development.
"STILL, IT LOOKS SO COOL!"  Yes, it does.  Don't be fooled by Ark as it's advertised: gameplay in Ark is mostly PvE with poor AI; most PvP is players vs bases while the defender is offline; and far from the trailers' rough-hewn stone cities of raptor stables and parasaur knights, most bases are ugly metal cubes bristling with turrets.
For a year and a half, I went against the PvP grain and built a city.  I made it impregnable, and with my allies, I drove out invaders who would threaten a peaceful way of life.  Now, I am beset on all sides by griefers and cheaters to whom Wildcard has given the keys of the entire official server network.  In the next few days, I will witness the ruination of everything I have built.  These are my final words to you, gamers: this game is not well made or expertly-helmed; don't get involved.

Classic survival game, think Rust but with dinosaurs. Was a great game. Then got plagued with horrible development choices and hackers. Offline is fun, but the slow grind gets stale soon. Not a bad choice if the price is $5-10 dollars and you have a few friends to hop into a private server with.

ARK is an amazing game with a fully customizable single player mode, an easy to use modding interface, bonus content including ever-expanding content straight from the developers themselves (additional DLC fees required), and incredible graphics (even on the lowest settings, if your computer isn't up to par) ARK stands above all other games.
It is the complete survival experience having to watch out for starvation and dehydration while taking character exhaustion into account as well. Your character spawns almost completely naked on a beach in a random location (with limited control of what section of the map you wish to travel to). You must literally start from the bottom and work your way up finding food and water all the while defending yourself against a growing variety of prehistoric beasts.
The only drawbacks I can think of are that the customizable settings can be frustrating for new users as the values are counterintuitive (eg: to increase your player's resistance you must enter a value below 1 instead of increasing from 1) and your character is extremely weak until mid-level gameplay without buffered settings or creative experience point use. Players will die several times as you learn to play.
Another small drawback is the ARK game files are huge I'm talking GBs of content also the graphics are fantastic, but this also means you will need a beefy computer for the higher settings.
I definitely recommend this game to every gamer on earth.
This is one of the very few games that $30 (or $15 when on sale) buys you hundreds of thousands of hours in gameplay. If you buy this game and enjoy it, you will undoubtedly get much more than your money's worth.
Personal review ARK gets 5 out of 5 stars from me.

If you like a large variation in the destructive capabilities that you can use to lay waste to the enemies around, with a friend or 3 to back you up, then you will absolutely LOVE this game. With the weapons in the game, you can pin enemies to the wall with arrows/bolts, BBQ them with flamethrowers, vaporize with massive lazer cannons, turn them into swiss cheese with shotguns, fry, corrode, electrify, freeze, poison, irradiate, and many other descriptions of pain from a variety of choices.... And that's just the weapons.
The suits that you as the Tenno wear (Warframes, duh), all have unique powers that complement themselves and others within the team. There is a warframe for what ever mood you happen to be in, from being the sneaky rogue type (I recommend the Loki frame for this), the charging Berserker (Valkyre or Rhino), or the more fragile, but more powerful Mage types (Nova comes to mind). Each Warframe has a theme that their powers are suited (get it?) around and this can effect the game play. One of the enemy types within the game is a robot. This means that warframes with more electric or cold based powers (Frost, Volt, or Chroma) could potentially be more useful in dealing damage to the robots.
Although a good portion of my time playing in the game has been in Solo mode, i would recommend that when you play it to play it with friends. If you happen to have none that want to run around the universe slaughtering things for credits and resources, then you can make some friends in the game by joining with Clans or through the Trading market. It is great being able to pull off insane amounts of damage against an enemy by coordinating with a team mate, or saving said team mate from near death if their timeing happens to be off.
I hope this Review helps those  looking to get into this game. It's free to play, so why not give it a shot. Just two warnings to new players: 1.) Its slow to start, getting better the longer you play and 2.)The longer you play, the more you'll want to play.

So, I've been playing this game for a while now and finnally thought I should review it. Lets get right into it shall we?
First off, lemme just say that this game, for being free, is really well optimized at least for my and my friend's rigs. The graphics overall as well are REALLY nice especially being a free game. I know that there are some other free games that have amazing graphics but this one (atleast for me) takes the cake. Now there have been some graphical glitches I've ran into but they're usually pretty minor. Speaking of glitches, this game MOST DEFINITLY has its fair share lemme tell ya. However, most of them usually get patched out the next hotfix so it's not that bad. There are also some hilarious ones so thats always a good laugh. As far as gameplay goes, this game wins it for me as well. The time and care that DE puts into each frame is amazing. Each frame is unique, has its own style and abilities. Even further from that the amount of weapons added into this mix makes it that much better. Then when you add in the mods, it makes the list of customization and amount of playstyles so much longer.
Now for the few cons:
Platinum. Need I say more? Well actually, I don't really have an issue with plat it's just expensive and I'm poor (from buying plat fml) Only reason I'm okay with it is because it supports the constant updates (and by constant I mean almost weekly).
Wait time. Theres a lot of it. Just get ready to wait for stuff you want. On average it takes most weapons 12-24 hours to make, warframe parts take 12 and the warframe takes a whopping 73 hours to craft. It's not bad persay but I still find it annoying even if it is to balence the game.
Other than this I cant really think of any other personal complaints I have with the game, really. Overall I would highly recommend this game to someone that likes PvE with some PvP games (sorta like Destiny I guess?) It's really a great game to sit down witha few friends and play the hell outta for an hour or two.

Back in its early days, I felt like Warframe was a dry experience. The first hour was pretty good but it lost its novelty as you played on. It felt like a grind. I believe the developers have improved upon that.
The story is a lot more engaging with cutscenes and progression. Also, the AI has been improved so you can now be stealthy rather than be caught a kilometer away while crouching. Lastly, the movement controls are a lot more fluid; running around looks a lot more natural (plus running and crouching doesn't give you that speed boost anymore).
In terms of meta-gameplay (ie. salvaging money, metals, items etc.) it's still pretty much the same. To progress in the story, you need to scavenge materials to meet blueprints which build items you can use. This makes it grindy which I dislike. If you can get past the stunning graphics of this game, you will see that it is a grind fest. Don't get me wrong, though; it's good fun!

REVIEW:
Looking for some fast-paced action? Or maybe you're thinking of going ninja-like and do stealth assasinations like a pro? Then Warframe is totally for you!
PROS:
- Fast-paced combat that requires some skill.
- Fast switch between combat and stealth.
- Nice and flashy graphics.
- Balance between MMO and FPS Shooter.
- Various playstyles.
- Diverse arsenal of weapons.
CONS:
- At some point, you'll grow tired of it. I can assure it.
- Is lacking in the selection of Warframes. You'll come across another player identical to you.
- Not 'MMO' enough. You can get builds for your Warframe. Different 'mods' and ranks for you weapons, but you're lacking the impact of, for example, an open world.
- The reuse of the maps gets boring throughout the game.
- Player interactions with other players is minimal or almost null, unless you always play in 'public matchmaking'.
- You'll eventually end up buying 'platinum' for some resources, weapons, or other Warframes. Even parts for the ship.
WOULD I RECOMMEND IT?
By the amount of cons I found, I wouldn't. But if you're looking for something to play solo or with friends, Warframe's a lot of fun.

If you're looking to buy this game or just recently purchased it, do NOT pick a live server with a ton of people on it! It may seem like a good idea, but the current OFFICIAL server hosts are utter garbage. The more people are on a server, the worse your experience is going to be. There will be massive lag spikes that last for what feels like an eternity, and when you're doing something crucial like fighting for your survival or trying to hand feed a newborn dino it is no good. I've lost awesome baby dinos and some of my own tames due to lag, and it's left a bad taste in my mouth. There are also several bugs in this game, and it feels like the developers hide behind the Early Access title to give them an excuse to not fix them in a decent fashion. Some of these bugs include but are not limited to: being stuck in boss arenas, losing characters during transfer due to lag [had this happen too!] with no way to get them back, tamed dinos getting stuck on non-player affected environments like crystals, rock formations and the like, the giant squids pulling tames and players under the map or being unkillable when a player/tame is grabbed, tames getting stuck under the map when nodes respawn or a supply drop comes down, dinos being killed when leaving boss arenas, and that's just a few I can think of! It can really leave a bad taste in your mouth and not want to play at all. Also time consuming, this game is very time consuming and will eat your life and soul away; things happen in real time, and you have to actively log in and run around your base to reset it or else people will destroy and take your stuff, you have to feed your dinos after so many days, and don't get me started on breeding! Babies take literal days to raise, and the first stage involves you shoving meat or berries into their inventory for several hours before having to make sure your feeding troughs are kept full every few hours [depending on what and how many you are raising; herbivores are much easier to raise]. Also the recent nerf to flight speed makes the wyverns I spent a good chunk of my time raising utterly garbage; they're slow as molasses now, almost painfully so, and the stamina drain makes fighting with them incredibly difficult. Then there's good ol' customer support; they take days to get back to you if you need their help, then you will get an automated response and then you get to wait another few days for an actual person to e-mail you back and tell you basically "Can't help, sorry! Against x policy to do y thing! Better luck next time!" or an even useless question and then waiting a day or so for their next reply.
All that salt and negativity aside, if you still want to play, this is a gorgeous game, and would be awesome and fun to play if there wasn't so much wrong with it. It's almost heartbreaking to see such a good game get treated like an afterthought by it's own makers.

If you like a large variation in the destructive capabilities that you can use to lay waste to the enemies around, with a friend or 3 to back you up, then you will absolutely LOVE this game. With the weapons in the game, you can pin enemies to the wall with arrows/bolts, BBQ them with flamethrowers, vaporize with massive lazer cannons, turn them into swiss cheese with shotguns, fry, corrode, electrify, freeze, poison, irradiate, and many other descriptions of pain from a variety of choices.... And that's just the weapons.
The suits that you as the Tenno wear (Warframes, duh), all have unique powers that complement themselves and others within the team. There is a warframe for what ever mood you happen to be in, from being the sneaky rogue type (I recommend the Loki frame for this), the charging Berserker (Valkyre or Rhino), or the more fragile, but more powerful Mage types (Nova comes to mind). Each Warframe has a theme that their powers are suited (get it?) around and this can effect the game play. One of the enemy types within the game is a robot. This means that warframes with more electric or cold based powers (Frost, Volt, or Chroma) could potentially be more useful in dealing damage to the robots.
Although a good portion of my time playing in the game has been in Solo mode, i would recommend that when you play it to play it with friends. If you happen to have none that want to run around the universe slaughtering things for credits and resources, then you can make some friends in the game by joining with Clans or through the Trading market. It is great being able to pull off insane amounts of damage against an enemy by coordinating with a team mate, or saving said team mate from near death if their timeing happens to be off.
I hope this Review helps those  looking to get into this game. It's free to play, so why not give it a shot. Just two warnings to new players: 1.) Its slow to start, getting better the longer you play and 2.)The longer you play, the more you'll want to play.

So, I've been playing this game for a while now and finnally thought I should review it. Lets get right into it shall we?
First off, lemme just say that this game, for being free, is really well optimized at least for my and my friend's rigs. The graphics overall as well are REALLY nice especially being a free game. I know that there are some other free games that have amazing graphics but this one (atleast for me) takes the cake. Now there have been some graphical glitches I've ran into but they're usually pretty minor. Speaking of glitches, this game MOST DEFINITLY has its fair share lemme tell ya. However, most of them usually get patched out the next hotfix so it's not that bad. There are also some hilarious ones so thats always a good laugh. As far as gameplay goes, this game wins it for me as well. The time and care that DE puts into each frame is amazing. Each frame is unique, has its own style and abilities. Even further from that the amount of weapons added into this mix makes it that much better. Then when you add in the mods, it makes the list of customization and amount of playstyles so much longer.
Now for the few cons:
Platinum. Need I say more? Well actually, I don't really have an issue with plat it's just expensive and I'm poor (from buying plat fml) Only reason I'm okay with it is because it supports the constant updates (and by constant I mean almost weekly).
Wait time. Theres a lot of it. Just get ready to wait for stuff you want. On average it takes most weapons 12-24 hours to make, warframe parts take 12 and the warframe takes a whopping 73 hours to craft. It's not bad persay but I still find it annoying even if it is to balence the game.
Other than this I cant really think of any other personal complaints I have with the game, really. Overall I would highly recommend this game to someone that likes PvE with some PvP games (sorta like Destiny I guess?) It's really a great game to sit down witha few friends and play the hell outta for an hour or two.

Ever since I purchased this game I have only grown to love it more and more. First of all there is constantly more content being added to make the experience of playing the game better every update. Though each new update introduces a few new bugs those are mostly dealt with and the game is back to being fun.
Now with the new DLC Aberration I would have to say it is moving to far away from the game I originally fell in love with as it adds so many I guess you could say "fantastical" creatures where I loved how most of the creatures in the game before had in some way actually existed on Earth in the past. Of course though I don't necessarily like the fact that the new creatures are extremely far from anything that has ever existed on Earth, based off of what I know about Studio Wildcard and the previous DLC and content added to the game i'm sure this DLC will be extremely fun anyways.
Then there is the matter of the one thing done to the game that I disagree with most: the flyer nerf. For those of you who don't know what the flyer nerf was it was part of an update that made it so you could no longer upgrade the speed stat on any flying mounts. Also it made most of the flyers base speed stat slower. But because of the amazing community surrounding this game and Ark's great mod support you can easily get the Classic Flyers mod and your flyers are back to normal.
All in all I think this game is amazing and all of the bad things are out weighed by the good things ten fold. I look forward to the future content to be added to this game and plan on playing much more than the 442 hours I have on the game at the time of writing this review. Ark: Survival Evolved is one of my top 3 favorite games of all time and a perfect 10/10 to me.

If you like a large variation in the destructive capabilities that you can use to lay waste to the enemies around, with a friend or 3 to back you up, then you will absolutely LOVE this game. With the weapons in the game, you can pin enemies to the wall with arrows/bolts, BBQ them with flamethrowers, vaporize with massive lazer cannons, turn them into swiss cheese with shotguns, fry, corrode, electrify, freeze, poison, irradiate, and many other descriptions of pain from a variety of choices.... And that's just the weapons.
The suits that you as the Tenno wear (Warframes, duh), all have unique powers that complement themselves and others within the team. There is a warframe for what ever mood you happen to be in, from being the sneaky rogue type (I recommend the Loki frame for this), the charging Berserker (Valkyre or Rhino), or the more fragile, but more powerful Mage types (Nova comes to mind). Each Warframe has a theme that their powers are suited (get it?) around and this can effect the game play. One of the enemy types within the game is a robot. This means that warframes with more electric or cold based powers (Frost, Volt, or Chroma) could potentially be more useful in dealing damage to the robots.
Although a good portion of my time playing in the game has been in Solo mode, i would recommend that when you play it to play it with friends. If you happen to have none that want to run around the universe slaughtering things for credits and resources, then you can make some friends in the game by joining with Clans or through the Trading market. It is great being able to pull off insane amounts of damage against an enemy by coordinating with a team mate, or saving said team mate from near death if their timeing happens to be off.
I hope this Review helps those  looking to get into this game. It's free to play, so why not give it a shot. Just two warnings to new players: 1.) Its slow to start, getting better the longer you play and 2.)The longer you play, the more you'll want to play.

So, I've been playing this game for a while now and finnally thought I should review it. Lets get right into it shall we?
First off, lemme just say that this game, for being free, is really well optimized at least for my and my friend's rigs. The graphics overall as well are REALLY nice especially being a free game. I know that there are some other free games that have amazing graphics but this one (atleast for me) takes the cake. Now there have been some graphical glitches I've ran into but they're usually pretty minor. Speaking of glitches, this game MOST DEFINITLY has its fair share lemme tell ya. However, most of them usually get patched out the next hotfix so it's not that bad. There are also some hilarious ones so thats always a good laugh. As far as gameplay goes, this game wins it for me as well. The time and care that DE puts into each frame is amazing. Each frame is unique, has its own style and abilities. Even further from that the amount of weapons added into this mix makes it that much better. Then when you add in the mods, it makes the list of customization and amount of playstyles so much longer.
Now for the few cons:
Platinum. Need I say more? Well actually, I don't really have an issue with plat it's just expensive and I'm poor (from buying plat fml) Only reason I'm okay with it is because it supports the constant updates (and by constant I mean almost weekly).
Wait time. Theres a lot of it. Just get ready to wait for stuff you want. On average it takes most weapons 12-24 hours to make, warframe parts take 12 and the warframe takes a whopping 73 hours to craft. It's not bad persay but I still find it annoying even if it is to balence the game.
Other than this I cant really think of any other personal complaints I have with the game, really. Overall I would highly recommend this game to someone that likes PvE with some PvP games (sorta like Destiny I guess?) It's really a great game to sit down witha few friends and play the hell outta for an hour or two.

FOR THOSE NEW TO ARK, OR WHO GAVE UP ON IT AND WANT TO KNOW IF IT'S WORTH RE-INSTALLING:
July 2017: Within the past few months ARK has begun to wind down on adding new content and has been making exceptional progress on bug fixing and optimizations. Gameplay is so much smoother now and simply feels better too. So many people over the past couple of years have been fed up that nothing was being done to fix the many game-breaking issues that caused them to leave and make negative reviews. Now that something is being done about it, I urge that players whom had quit long ago give ARK another try, as it is so much better than it used to be, and it might not crash your computer now
I'm so glad I put my money into ARK, because not only is it a great game, but the developers have been consistently working to make it better, and they've already fixed 90%+ of the various bugs and glitches in the game. Unlike so many other Early Access developers out there, Wildcard actually is dedicated and continues to improve on its game.
Many of the bug fixes included were loading times, broken mechanics, and game crashes. In both single player and multiplayer, the loading times took a minimum of 2-5 minutes, depending on how much time and building and taming you've already done. Just recently, the load times take less than 30 seconds, which is a vast improvement. For those of you who played this game years ago, the game seemed to crash every hour ro so, which sometimes required you to fully restart the computer, thus you would lose everything you were working on in the background and in-game. This has been fixed completely. I haven't had a crash in MONTHS, which means I can go back to 12 hour weekend sessions without rage-uninstalling again.
And yes, there have been various nerfs that were done over the past few months. The Infamous "Flyer Nerf" many players had gotten salty about was something that I believe was a necessary move. Not only does having a 5000% movement speed on a Ptero or Quetzal feel game-breaking, but it also makes ARK feel more like a Garry's Mod w/Dinos rather than a true survival sandbox. But if you feel like you need your flyer needs to travel faster than the speed of light, go ahead and get a mod or fix the ini settings so you can have your unrealistic, game-breaking speeds...
Also, there are a bunch of mods and projects out there right now that can spice up or completely change your experience in ARK that a lot of people love and support, so feel free to check those out as well.
All in all though, I recommend this game to anyone interested in dinosaurs, crafting, building, exploring, and becoming the Alpha Survivor/Tribe of the Island, or whichever map you end up playing on. Have fun out there!

Review Done back in November 2016:
There are several negative reviews for ARK about how unoptimized this game is; lagging and crashing being big issues for many players. But if you have a computer that's capable of running this game, you should ignore those that thumb-down ARK simply because they can't run it. To put it into perspective, my rig has an AMD FX-9590 CPU, 16GB RAM and a GTX 980 GPU. On Epic Graphics Settings, I can run ARK at 30 fps easily, which is good enough for me.
Now the reason I recommend ARK should be obvious, because like me, you were probably attracted to the whole "Taming Dinos, Building Things, and Causing Mass Amounts of Carnage," which Studio Wildcard definitely delivered on.
I have spent probably 400+ hours (I'm an offline mode scrub) building and taming, both in single player and multiplayer. I sometimes play 12-20 hour sessions with a few of my closest friends. and we have built a huge settlement on our private server. In the past 6 months, we have been able to build our own houses, a couple of granaries, several farms, pastures, and enclosures (for the dinosaurs of course) as well as a Harbor for our many boats, an armory, and several outposts throughout the map. That alone should speak volumes on just how easy it is to get hooked on this game, especially if you have friends to play with.
As for Scorched Earth, let it be know that it is a TRUE expansion. What I mean by a "True Expansion" is that it is not necessary to own it, but it adds a solid amount of flavor and replayability to the game -- something that major companies like Electronic Arts and Sega don't do - which provides another reason to consider supporting the development of ARK. Scorched Earth is worth a try if you want to die from heatstroke and dehydration, not to mention be obliterated by a bunch of new creatures that can be even more lethal than those in the base game.
And when the vanilla ARK gets boring after 100-200 hours or so, there are a lot of mods out there to spice things up. I recommend trying out Annunaki Genesis, as it offers an extremely high risk/reward dynamic as well as several features and mechanics that only amplifies the sheer awesomeness that is ARK: Survival Evolved.
In conclusion, if all of the above didn't entice you to buy this game, then at least you know where you stand. If you like what you read, I suggest buying ARK when it is on sale if you can, but if you can't wait, and you have the money, it's well worth the original pricetag without question.

Ok, I've played nearly 80 hours...
Warframe is and action third person shooter. The gameplay is fast paced with a lot of movements. Your Warframe is your suit you are using to fight. Each one has different stats and abilities. On top of that, you have a main weapon, a sidearm and a melee weapon. Each of those and your suit can be customized with mods you find during your missions. After a few hours of gameplay, you truly get some choices as how you want to build your character.
The game is played in missions which have a large variety of objectives. Defend spots, carry stuff, capture dude, extermination, kill boss, etc... They can be played with up to 4 players.
The progression in this game is amazing. There is a lot of mission of growing difficulty to play. There is tons of weapons to craft, try or collect plus the Warframes themselves. You never have enough mods.
You always have a goal, somehting to do. If you enjoy the gameplay, the game will never get boring.
However, it IS a free to play game and there will be paywalls. You can obviously buy new weapons and Warframes to progress faster but you can also handle crafting them. ( Warframes are very hard to craft but it still bearable. ) The worst is that you have a limited amount of weapons and warframes slots. If your are the collector kind like me ( or if you want more than 2 Warframes ), you'll have to pay.
But you know, I still did it to 80 hours without paying.

I highly reccommend this game to anyone who enjoys a grind system to get the weapon that you want. It is, without a doubt, the best, well balanced, cheapest, and most fun game in the F2P market. Is it not Pay 2 Win, it is, in my opinion, Pay 2 lose. Since this game is about the grind, and the joy when you get a weapon you have been grinding for, buying it just doesn't give you the feeling.
Pros:
Beautiful
Movement system has been reworked, it's fun and feels fast. Movement system is a highlight of the game.
It's not Pay 2 Win at all. The game starts you out with 20platinum, which is used for Catalysts and weapon/warframe slots.
The community is phenominal. I haven't met anyone in the game who isn't either silent, happy, or willing to help new players.
The weapon and mod system is pretty good, with certain mods being very difficult to get.
Mission Variety is decent, with a few types of them, such as Exterminate, Capture, Excavate, Survival, etc.
Weapons do get better with time, either by levelling them or "Formaing" them, giving them the ability to reduce the cost of certain mods.
Meh:
Certain event mods that are fantastic are no longer available. They are only through the trading system, and run pretty expensive on the market. You can grind to get the currency and buy them, but you can't directly grind for the event mods.
Snipers at this time are meh. They have their niche, but other weapons are either better at CC or DPS, but they are bursty. Bows are also pretty underused, but Bows also have some of the highest damage potential in the game, easily critting over 100k with buffs and mods.
In order to get more weapon slots, and Catalysts and the likes, you need to trade in game or pay money. But they are relatively cheap, but for a newer player it can be a problem.
Bad:
Tutorial isn't that helpful. You better have the Wiki up at all times for help, or ask questions that aren't on the wiki in region or a clan if you find one.
It's kind of buggy, with a few bugs popping up here and there, being somewhat crippling to play. Bosses occasionally get stuck in an invincibility phase, or never get into the phase. It's not hugely buggy, but you should know that it does pop up.
Servers occasionally go down without warning. Since when you end a mission early/abort it, you only get experience. But with a crash, you get nothing at all.
Overall, it's great. I am having a lot of fun, People are friendly, the game is reasonably balanced, and the developers are very active with the game.
(PS, just in case you try to do what I did, you CAN NOT trade the 50 starting platinum.)

There is a reason why reviews are mixed for this game.  It's early access, not optimized, and has frequent updates that sometimes leave the player starting from scratch again.  The developer's focus seems to be on new dinos more than the gameplay experience and the glitchy issues are a source of frustration for many gamers.
If you can get beyond that, and beyond the fact that even the paid version such as Scorched Earth, have technical problems (like your game crashes even with the most upgraded rig), you will have fun.  Just be prepared to slog through the upgrading, grind, grind, grind, and risk losing it all due to circumstances beyond your control.
On the positive side:
Once you level up a little bit and can get a shelter going, the game is addictive.  There are tons of distractions, dinos to tame, danger around every corner, and in PVP mode, players who will kill you without a thought.  Tribe up if you can.  There is safety in numbers.
All in all, when the developers get the game finished, it will become one of the classics.  For added fun, try Survival of The Fittest, or hang around on the original Island or Scorched Earth maps for the holiday updates. They are great fun.
Out of every early access game out there, Ark's been the one to stay consistently updated and fresh.

The vast majority of negative reviews for this game are just people whining about the DLC being released while the game is still in early access. While, yes, that's a little questionable, it has absolutely nothing to do with the gameplay. Literally the only thing you miss out on if you abstain from buying the DLC is a new map. That's it. They still patch the base game continuously and add content on a regular basis. You don't even miss out on the dinosaurs, because server hosts can freely add the new dinos to their maps if they want to.
And that right there is the main thing that makes this game great. While the official unmodded servers are a disaster and unplayable unless you're a no-lifer, the game is extremely mod-friendly, and you can customize your server (or single-player game) in pretty much any way that you want to create the experience that is most fun for you.
The boring part of every survival game I've played is the end-game. You always progress to a point where there is nothing left for you to do. That's not the case in ARK. You can always breed a better dino, or build a more ridiculous base, or even transfer your character to a new map and conquer it next.
I could probably say a lot more, but this review is mostly because 1) Steam wanted me to write a review of it, and 2) the game needs more positive reviews to counter the whiners spamming negative ones just because they are salty about something totally unrelated to the game itself. The fact of the matter is this is the best survival game on the market. A random DLC doesn't change that.

I haven't played much of this game.
Ok, I've played nearly 80 hours...
Warframe is and action third person shooter. The gameplay is fast paced with a lot of movements. Your Warframe is your suit you are using to fight. Each one has different stats and abilities. On top of that, you have a main weapon, a sidearm and a melee weapon. Each of those and your suit can be customized with mods you find during your missions. After a few hours of gameplay, you truly get some choices as how you want to build your character.
The game is played in missions which have a large variety of objectives. Defend spots, carry stuff, capture dude, extermination, kill boss, etc... They can be played with up to 4 players.
The progression in this game is amazing. There is a lot of mission of growing difficulty to play. There is tons of weapons to craft, try or collect plus the Warframes themselves. You never have enough mods.
You always have a goal, somehting to do. If you enjoy the gameplay, the game will never get boring.
However, it IS a free to play game and there will be paywalls. You can obviously buy new weapons and Warframes to progress faster but you can also handle crafting them. ( Warframes are very hard to craft but it still bearable. ) The worst is that you have a limited amount of weapons and warframes slots. If your are the collector kind like me ( or if you want more than 2 Warframes ), you'll have to pay.
But you know, I still did it to 80 hours without paying.

Warframe is one of those games I have a love/hate relationship with. There are several bad things about the game outweighed by the good.
Third person shooter Diablo-esque game where you're always grinding out something, power creep is the name of the game and even that terrible weapon you grew an attachment to for low level gameplay can be made rather good, and fun, through various means, including a grindy method that can be oh so frustrating, with a decent payoff in the end (I'm looking at YOU Kuva/Riven rerolls)
The cosmetic system is rather nice, if you dont like one thing about your warframe/character, you can change it. This can be through color pallets, skins for your body or helmet, customization is very intensive, and fashionframe is the true endgame.
If you get a few certain styles of melee weapon and get some fast attack speed and a certain mod set you can pretend to be a lawn mower (just be sure you have the tankiness to survive Lawnmower Simulator 2017.)
There is a LOT of variety, gun wise and melee wise, and the variety only increases every update. Soonish we'll have pump action shotguns, and recently we got the ability to use a glaive in one hand, and a pistol in the other.
The optimization. You can run this game very nicely on a toaster and it still look nice. Mad props to the dev team for this.
My only real issues with the game is that fresh content can be a bit buggy, but the devs are quick to fix in ways they can, and the community has a few issues but that has no actual impact on gameplay.
Overall I give this game a 10/10, DE legit seems to care about Warframe and its community.

I absolutely love this game.  I look forward to playing it each day.  I love that the Devs change the game to fit the season and to give us seasonal events. The biggest drawback of the game to me is that if you are a single tribe person (many of us are) is that it is nearly impossible to take a vacation and not lose your base or dino's.  I wish the Dev's would implement a switch that puts your entire base in stasis for at least 8 days so you can leave and not worry about coming back to a destroyed base and no dinos..     Other than that, love the game!!  Would recommentd.. side note:  for a noob.. the game is very frustrating in the beginning until you can establish a base .. we all went thru it... have patience .. there are many servers out there that have people that will help  you if they see you are willing to put in the work to survive!..
