Ark is a gorgeous game that has demanded many hours of my time to play. The basic mechanics of the game, the design of the environment as well as the animals are brilliantly put together for the awe of your playing. If the customer service and development team had a better connection with the community and their issues I would definetly recommend the game, but sadly this is not the case.
If you are wanting to enjoy this game, my suggestion is to play it as a single player game so you control the progression how you see fit or join a non official server. However, on Official servers the developement team has a "We will let this play out" attitude to most of their issues that are implemented by bad updates. Once an issue is introduced, the community take action to identify and report issues throughout the game and eventually they are looked into. The main issue is the lack of communication from the development team and when major issues arise that cost you literally hundreds of hours of work they do not have a system that is made easily known to users how to recooperate from that issue. Also, good luck if you reach out to them support issues or one of the social media outlets that they advertise.
One other peeve that I have is that this game has been in Early Access for a long time. While I understand the concept of EA and Alpha/Beta etc. this game should have been considered to be a fully released game the minute they started selling DLC. Instead, they lay on the fact that its an EA game with any or all mistakes they make with updates or poor execution of rollout of said updates. They are never, and I mean never, reliable on their time table for releases, server restarts or anything else. They often deliver promises of features in upcoming patches or events and rarely follow through with them. This past Halloween was a major point to this as they promised many things to occur that never made it into the game. When issues are represented that a holiday event has an issue, they do not try to correct it instead just let it "Play out" again as I stated earlier.
All in all the game has potential but the administrators, development team and the community management group lack in their ability to follow through with things. An even longer story short, save your money and many hours and put it toward a game you will enjoy and recommend to your friends!

As far as F2P games go, warframe has offered more hours of good gameplay than most games ive played in the last 10+yrs. At first the game might seem daunting and P2W, for some of the younger players, due to the time to craft and obtain items. Unlike most F2P games almot 95% of the content ingame is obtainable without spending a cent. With a little time and effort and some trades everything cn be crafted. The "Classes" which are called Warframes are versatile and each offers different stats, abilities, strengths and weaknesses, however with mods you can almost make any frame or weapon closer to how you wish to use or play it. The crafting is also pretty deep for a F2P, having to acquire the materials, and blueprints for each frame part or weapon. The material system is divided into planets with different mission types. each planet offering different resources. The devs in this game have been very generous an if you take the time to loot, play somewhat tactically the payoffs are great. While yes it is a bit grindy and will hurt the 15yrold COD fanboy run and gun croud. If your A player looking for a tactical/fast paced emersive shooter then this is the game for you. Warframe at first thought by many to be a cheap copy of Destiny, IMHO turned out to actually be the better of the two. More in depth better crafting/gameplay more diverse options for classes and customization. If you want a destiny type game with better gameplay mechanics, better crafting , better overall perfromance. Warframe is that option. It does seem a bit repetative due to similar mission types being each planet , each time its slightly a bit different and can be played in different ways to achieve the same goal. Making the game fun for some friends of varying skills/thought processes to get into together. All in all id give Warframe 9/10 only losing 1 point for some connectivity issues here and there.

The only F2P game I've had the privilege of playing where the developers have true integrity, a completely transparent and community-based development process, and where the game is truly without paywalls or pay-to-win content.
There is nothing, I repeat, nothing in this game that you cannot earn, and earn in a reasonable amount of time.
The in-game premium currency, Platinum, can be traded with other players, which means that there's an entire emergent economy of people trading parts and money which allows anyone to buy premium cosmetic items and shortcuts to better equipment or things like inventory slots without paying a single penny of real money, which is a huge bonus.
Combine that with a truly unique and enthralling scifi universe on par with series like Halo or WH40K, always improving gameplay mechanics and a seemingly endless torrent of new, free content and expansions, and you have an extremely addictive and enjoyable game.
I can't recommend this game enough, what do you have to lose? It's free!

Ever wanted to be a Space Ninja? Then this is the game for you. Rooms are the same but the order and number of each room is different every time. Now there are multiple tile sets it is pretty good and keeps things interesting.
The one caviat I do have with this game is that it takes a lot of effort to get going. This game is well known as Grindframe for a reason, you need to work for your items and run missions multiple times to get what you need. Then you wait X amount of hours while your items are built in the foundry. This can be rushed with premium currency and fortunately the business model is fair, at first I wasn't sure it was but after discovering there is a very active trading post where you can sell certain items for Platinum and in some cases a lot of it this makes that barrier go away.
I highly recommend this game if you have friends to play it with, soloing is very boring but get a bunch of friends together to run missions and make a clan and it becomes something really awesome.

Warframe can be described with the following 10-word phrase:
free-to-play, third-person, cooperative shooter about space ninjas.
I believe that the space ninjas alone would sell the game, but some people can't see the beauty of these interplanetary assassins, so allow me to elaborate.
You play as a tenno - a race of humanoid warriors that wear the titular warframe armor, which lets them move like ninjas and grants special powers - who is awoken from centuries of cryogenic sleep and tasked with defending the system from the opressive Grineer Empire's clone armies, the profit-crazy Corpus merchant cult, and a half virus, half nanobot, parasitic scourge called the Infestation.  The game's fast paced, run-around-y, shoot-'em-up-y gameplay makes it great for those aspiring to become ninjas themselves.  My only two gripes are connection issues that I have (though that may be my computer being a butt) and the absolute chore that grinding for resources is, but that's a symptom of it being free-to-play.  I CAN say that this is a free-to-play game done right: with a few exceptions in the cosmetics department, everything in this game can be obtained without spending real-world money (I HAVE spent money on it because the game is fekkin' amazing, but I never HAD to).  Overall, one of the best games I have ever played.

Since then we've moved to an unofficial vanilla server with slightly higher rates (2G, 2XP, 4T) and have been having a blast.
We're mostly socializing builders, sometimes even taking some contracting work for the alpha tribes making trading posts, entertainment buildings and the like in exchange for Cementing Paste and metal.
One of the things I like most about this game is the player driven economy. Players tame, breed and sell dinos to other tribes in exchange for things they need.
I personally have no problems with FPS, getting 50-60 FPS on my 980TI at all times at The Center on Epic preset (1080p resolution).
I really can't NOT recommend this game, it has given me so much fun and memories. I also met lots of friends.
One word about the negative reviews:
Most of them are because of the paid DLC that WildCard released, not because the game is not fun or engaging, most of the people posting bad reviews have a few hundred hours played and are STILL posting bad reviews.
In short, don't let the bad reviews discourage you, give the game a chance and you'll have the time of your life!

Personally, I think this is an outstanding game, and I would definetly recommend it to anyone who likes Third-Person Shotters or RPG's. The only thing that throws my opinion off about this game is the amount of microtransactions, since the game does sometimes push you to buy platinum.

The Good:
Action. Action. Action. The action in this game may be the best I've ever seen. Granted I'm not a huge gamer, but this is good stuff. It's amazingly fluid and dynamic, and has more options than you'll know what to do with. You can wall run up to your target and then perform a ninja-leap attack from said wall, use several pretty sick powers which vary depending on your Warframe, and pick from a slew of oxies, greatswords, dual swords, axes, hammers, rifles, snipers, pistols, glaives, bows, and kunai. I really can't say enough about this, but you get the point.
The Bad:
Hoo boy. Here we go. When you see the "Free To Play" tag, you probably think to yourself (if you've played a F2P before) "Yeah, but is it pay to win?". Yes. Yes it is. Is it ever. I think this may be one of the worse cases of "Freemium" out there. It's baad, M'kay? Here's why. This game is based around super cool suits of high tech armor that give you all kinds of butt-kicking powers. You choose one from three options at the beginning, and you can either buy or build others later. This building is based on buying blueprints for stuff with in game currency, rather than paying actual money for the completed item. Suffice to say building is a pain in the butt, due to astronomical waits and absurd materials and money requirements. Add to this the fact that you have a very limited inventory (two Warframes and about a dozen weapons total), which you can only upgrade with some real world greenbacks, and the fact that all of the best weapons and blueprints must be bought with real dough, and you'll find that the only way to really get ahead in this game is with a lot of real money, 'cause the in game dolla dolla bills y'all don't come cheap.
The Ugly:
This game would be much better if it were a little less... Grabby. The pay to win crap in here still bugs me, but in the end I still recommend it because it.s still super fun to play. give it a shot if you're in the mood for some killer fighting.

I have over 400 hours of game play on Ark Survival Evolved and it's DLC Ark Scorched Earth. The suprising part is I have not even tried PVP or any kind of multiplayer game play yet and I still find this game just as fun as when I started playing it.
Pros:
This game's settings are very beginner friendly because you can customize just about everything very easily.  Such as drop rates, spawning details, damage and resistance, food and water drain, taming speed, XP gain rate, and much more.  This can make the game enjoyable for a wide variety of player because you can control so many game changing details whether you want it slow and dificult or fast and easy.  There is a bit of a learning curve to the game play but not to much if you give the game a fair chance.  Anything you need to know you can find out on a very accurate and detailed wiki.
Cons:  It does require a good PC to run well.  It has its ocasional bugs but by FAR NOT the buggiest game I have played.  The devs often fail to release all the content in an update and have to set back the update arrival.  Or they have to leave some parts out for the next update.
Conclusion:  This game is worth playing and I strongly recommend this game to anyone who likes survival games, building, adventure, and prehistoric creatures.  The fact that the devs do not always get things done on time does not ruin the game it just means you have to be a little patient to get the goodies.  The bugs are not game breaking in my opinion anyways.  The game is a bit demanding on computer specs but if your computer can run it then its worth getting.

Wildly fun game, despite the technical problems that actually make the game frustrating at best, and infuriating at worst.
ARK does well in encompassing a feeling of "survival". After hours and days of playing, it's still easy to get lost, cold, hungry. Then you also need to worry about predatory dinosaurs/players that want you dead. The game can be aggressively difficult, especially in the beginning and if you don't have much time to devote to keeping up your defenses.
But it has some serious problems, and unless you're committed to put in time and "embrace the suck", you'll have a boat load of fun on the ARK.
The frustrating aspects are mostly from lack of optimisation. The game runs so very poorly at the minimum requirements that it's not worth playing. There are many mods/addons to the game, but they tend to be much worse (Primitive Plus takes 20 minutes to load, and once you're in, there's are bugs that keep you from major progression paths). The frustration is made worse for most by the addition of a paid DLC before official release and a solid bug free experience for paying customers. Yeah, just about everyone is mad about that, even though Scorched Earth is some grade A gaming.
The infuriating comes from bugs that really ruin the immersive experience. You put in the effort and the time (several hours) to get a tame, and then you go through the pain to make sure you can keep that highly prized commodity away from danger, only to have a glitch in the game kill it off or clip it through the terrain and into free fall to the void.
In my experience, and I have played mostly on official PVP servers, these are the only issues with the game, and if you can look past them as I do, you'll have a great time.

I absolutely love this game! The environments are beautiful, the dinos are awe inspiring and the action is heart-pounding. There is nothing like feeling the earth shake as you are being chased by a creature the size of a school bus. The sense of victory and accomplishment is real as you upgrade your items, tame dinos, make saddles, and take to the skies on the back of a pteranodon.
The negative reviews lately are by passionate players with hundreds of hours in-game. These people, despite the negative reviews obiously also love the game. They are upset because their specific feature request isn't being addressed, or more commonly because there is now a paid expansion being offered for an early access game. If the expansion is what is needed in order to keep the funds coming in to support the development of the game, I'm 100% for it, and I would think that someone with hundreds of hours in-game wouldn't mind chipping in $14.99 for a bit of additional content. Instead, they are upset that the developers would spend time on something other than the core game.
So this raises the question, Is ARK ready for prime-time? Do you get your money's worth on this Early Access title? I would say definitely yes! I have played many full-rease games with less content and more glitches. I honestly have never felt like I was simply test an in-progess product. And new content is being released all the time.
I should point out that I only rarely play ARK online. I prefer not to worry about what other players are doing and instead focus on my own experience.

As far as F2P games go, warframe has offered more hours of good gameplay than most games ive played in the last 10+yrs. At first the game might seem daunting and P2W, for some of the younger players, due to the time to craft and obtain items. Unlike most F2P games almot 95% of the content ingame is obtainable without spending a cent. With a little time and effort and some trades everything cn be crafted. The "Classes" which are called Warframes are versatile and each offers different stats, abilities, strengths and weaknesses, however with mods you can almost make any frame or weapon closer to how you wish to use or play it. The crafting is also pretty deep for a F2P, having to acquire the materials, and blueprints for each frame part or weapon. The material system is divided into planets with different mission types. each planet offering different resources. The devs in this game have been very generous an if you take the time to loot, play somewhat tactically the payoffs are great. While yes it is a bit grindy and will hurt the 15yrold COD fanboy run and gun croud. If your A player looking for a tactical/fast paced emersive shooter then this is the game for you. Warframe at first thought by many to be a cheap copy of Destiny, IMHO turned out to actually be the better of the two. More in depth better crafting/gameplay more diverse options for classes and customization. If you want a destiny type game with better gameplay mechanics, better crafting , better overall perfromance. Warframe is that option. It does seem a bit repetative due to similar mission types being each planet , each time its slightly a bit different and can be played in different ways to achieve the same goal. Making the game fun for some friends of varying skills/thought processes to get into together. All in all id give Warframe 9/10 only losing 1 point for some connectivity issues here and there.

I spent way too much money on this game.
I don't recommend it for any kind of completionist. Many items are exclusive to older members or extremely hard to obtain except for rare events which last less than 10 hours.
You are severely limited without spending a few dollars, and not just in cosmetics. You will not be able to own very many guns or characters (known as "warframes"). The standard for in-game currency is platinum, purchased with US$. You can trade item-for-item, though it is frequently frustrating.
That said, it can be run on mediocre-at-best computers, looks amazing at high graphics settings, has progression that seems almost infinite, and is very fun to actually play assuming you like parkour and third-person shooters. You can play stealth, support, tank, DPS, or any blend of those things that you want.

Edit: The review that follows was written during the early access phase of the game. It's certainly become better, and many bugs have been fixed. However, there remains much work to be done to fix the core game and tune the official server experience for players not part of mega-tribes.
TL/DR: Wildcard Sudios has terrible customer service, is realeasing a game with known game-breaking bugs. It's fun and looks nice though.
This is a un game. It looks nice (with a few minor allignment issues when building), and the map feels failry expansive. Hunting, gathering, building, and taming all feel fairly intuitive, with the exception of some cooking recipies not being apparent without resorting to looking things up on the wiki.
Building structures is half the fun for me, especially with gathering all the materials by hand and later by dino. The building system itself could stand to have some improvement in terms of constructable objects not being available in some building material tiers. Object placement/rotation could definitely use improvement, but it's not un-workable.
Multiple instance within the last twoo weeks of falling through the terrain have happened to both me and my tribe. Rafts still get stuck on either nothing, on terrain with poor collision, or harvestables that are a considerable distance away. The game is now within days of release, yet no response (let alone a fix) to reports about those bugs.
Wildcard's customer support is extremely lacking, to the point of being almost non-existent. I don't know if it's that they have insufficient staff or simply don't care, but people tend to have to wait _weeks_ for a response, let alone a solution.
They also do not respond well to notifications about people hacking the game. It could be that they think their the  anti-hacking program is all they need, but they don't seem to act when situations are brought to their attention, even with screenshot and video evidence.
Another strike against their community/customer support is that they announced that an extensive list of servers were getting deleted, many others were going to "Legacy" status, and did so within 5 days of the game's release. A far better solution, and onethat would be universally fair, would have been to wipe _all_ servers when the game goes live and announce the release a reasonable amount of time in advance.

Regretabbly I am having to change my review after continuing to play this game and gaining more experience with the development process.  After being out for 2 years and selling an expansion prior to the original game being finished....This game is still in Early Release!  So the Devs will randomly patch servers with catastrophic changes while providing little to no details on what  they are doing.  This causes players to loose hundreds (and in some peoples case thousands) of hours of work with a single update.  The amount of glitches (glitching through walls, glitching through dinos, getting stuck, falling through the map, etc.) that continue to occur while new content is pushed through is also a concern.  More attention needs to be paid to completing the game instead of continuing to add content while it is still in Eary Release.
Sadly at this point  I would advise users not to purchase this game until:
1. The game is finally officially released in a stable format.  (No more "Early Release")
2. The developers institute a better (more detailed) method for communicating upcoming patches and their impacts.
*Also, be warned the community on Official  & Open servers is extremely brutal.  Trolls will come through in numbers just to wipe out players on random servers.  Nearly the only way to have a good experience in this game is ot either be on a private server or in a Huge/Advanced tribe.  Other than that you will easily get trolled and wiped.*
________________________________________________________
Overall this is a great game, particularly for early access.  Graphics are supurb though due to the current game coding it requires high-end hardware to run them.  The Tribe system is rather good though still needs more advanaced governance features.  Truly I can't express enough how great the scenary is on epic graphic settings.  It truly is epic.  Also, the fact that they added a Community map "the Center" to the official game "free" DLC is also awesome.  I was a skeptic of their releasing an Expansion before the game was formally completed though after playing it for over a month my position has changed.  I believe the game is already good enough to be a standalone game in it's own right.  Likely one of the best early release games I have played.  In any case I strongly recommend this purchase as it is a game that you and your friends will enjoy for a long time.
Though please note the hardware requirements to run it on high settings are extreme.  and even then it will slowly utilize more system resources over time so this game wouldn't be the ideal choice if all you have is an old or low end gaming system.

So Ark has finally released from early access after 2 years what are my thoughts?
Firstly: Ark is a sci-fi prehistoric survival game where you start at caveman level tech with stone weapons and eventually obtain modern and future weaponary all the while you tame dinosaurs and other prehistoric or fantasy creatures.  While also engaging in ethier PVP or PVE type gameplay.
Second: Presentation wise the game looks gorgeous with exotic enviroments such as jungles, tundra, swamp, caves, and deserts. The creatures also look very well done.
Third: Performance wise the game can be hit or miss though it is much better now than it was before. I personally havent had much issues with it but I know people who have so take that what you will.
Final Verdict: Personally if you got some friends who have or want to play this game give it a try BUT wait for a sale as it is not worth $60 as much as it is $30 or $40 (I bought this when it first launched on Early access). As for the DLC and season pass thats just a matter of choice I liked the quality of Scorched Earth and how it made the game more challenging and I'm really excited for the Aberration DLC coming out in Oct 2017 but if those don't interest you dont buy them or wait for a sale if you really want them.
Sidenote:  Stick to unoffical servers as official servers are a mess with in PVP servers Mega tribes going to server to server wiping everyone and PVE consists of blocking off map sections with pillars to deny players any good base locations. Good unofficial servers will regulate pvp and pve to where it can be fun for all and not grief heavy.

Regretabbly I am having to change my review after continuing to play this game and gaining more experience with the development process.  After being out for 2 years and selling an expansion prior to the original game being finished....This game is still in Early Release!  So the Devs will randomly patch servers with catastrophic changes while providing little to no details on what  they are doing.  This causes players to loose hundreds (and in some peoples case thousands) of hours of work with a single update.  The amount of glitches (glitching through walls, glitching through dinos, getting stuck, falling through the map, etc.) that continue to occur while new content is pushed through is also a concern.  More attention needs to be paid to completing the game instead of continuing to add content while it is still in Eary Release.
Sadly at this point  I would advise users not to purchase this game until:
1. The game is finally officially released in a stable format.  (No more "Early Release")
2. The developers institute a better (more detailed) method for communicating upcoming patches and their impacts.
*Also, be warned the community on Official  & Open servers is extremely brutal.  Trolls will come through in numbers just to wipe out players on random servers.  Nearly the only way to have a good experience in this game is ot either be on a private server or in a Huge/Advanced tribe.  Other than that you will easily get trolled and wiped.*
________________________________________________________
Overall this is a great game, particularly for early access.  Graphics are supurb though due to the current game coding it requires high-end hardware to run them.  The Tribe system is rather good though still needs more advanaced governance features.  Truly I can't express enough how great the scenary is on epic graphic settings.  It truly is epic.  Also, the fact that they added a Community map "the Center" to the official game "free" DLC is also awesome.  I was a skeptic of their releasing an Expansion before the game was formally completed though after playing it for over a month my position has changed.  I believe the game is already good enough to be a standalone game in it's own right.  Likely one of the best early release games I have played.  In any case I strongly recommend this purchase as it is a game that you and your friends will enjoy for a long time.
Though please note the hardware requirements to run it on high settings are extreme.  and even then it will slowly utilize more system resources over time so this game wouldn't be the ideal choice if all you have is an old or low end gaming system.

So Ark has finally released from early access after 2 years what are my thoughts?
Firstly: Ark is a sci-fi prehistoric survival game where you start at caveman level tech with stone weapons and eventually obtain modern and future weaponary all the while you tame dinosaurs and other prehistoric or fantasy creatures.  While also engaging in ethier PVP or PVE type gameplay.
Second: Presentation wise the game looks gorgeous with exotic enviroments such as jungles, tundra, swamp, caves, and deserts. The creatures also look very well done.

Final Verdict: Personally if you got some friends who have or want to play this game give it a try BUT wait for a sale as it is not worth $60 as much as it is $30 or $40 (I bought this when it first launched on Early access). As for the DLC and season pass thats just a matter of choice I liked the quality of Scorched Earth and how it made the game more challenging and I'm really excited for the Aberration DLC coming out in Oct 2017 but if those don't interest you dont buy them or wait for a sale if you really want them.
Sidenote:  Stick to unoffical servers as official servers are a mess with in PVP servers Mega tribes going to server to server wiping everyone and PVE consists of blocking off map sections with pillars to deny players any good base locations. Good unofficial servers will regulate pvp and pve to where it can be fun for all and not grief heavy.

The short version of this review is that while I personally found the game fun to play, I can't really recommend it over the long term. I only realized that after putting 400+ hours and a total of $90 of microtransactions ($20 option * 6 times w/ 20% off coupons) into this game. My reasons are outlined below:
PROS:
-Fun either solo or multiplayer (but then again everything is fun with multiplayer)
-Updated reguarly with hotfixes and content
-Platinum (the virtual currency in this game) can be traded, meaning you don't have to spend a single cent if you're willing to farm rare stuff and trade them in exchange, but this requires much patience, espeically when you're new
-Various mission types
-Various random events (when you're part of a syndicate, for example) can be pretty tense when you're new
-Each Warframe has a different gameplay style
-Everything can be acquired via in-game credits with the exception of some cosmetic items
CONS:
-"Stealth" aspect of the game is substandard. Almost doesn't matter aside from Spy missions, stealth is not appreciated nor viable
-You are forced to buy inventory slots for weapons and new Warframes to experience more content, which requires Platinum
-Weapons and Warframes can only reach their full potential via special items (what the community calls "potatoes") which cannot be obtained normally. You can only buy them on demand with Platinum or wait for an alert mission that offers it as a reward, which happens very rarely. It's also a very rare daily login reward, but good luck with that. They're needed to expand mod capacity while the other special item (called "Forma") are required to half the cost of installing mods on your equipment, which is critical to being powerful, but fortunately the latter is fairly easy to obtain.
-The market makes absolutely no sense. Aside from the ridiculous Platinum cost of everything in general, an example is a rare resource called "Orokin cell". The market provides a permanent blueprint to craft them as an alternative to farming them on a mid-game world, but the cost is laughably ridiculous and much harder to do than just farming them.
-Platinum is way too expensive to purchase directly from the market, even with discounts. The discount coupons can be obtained as daily login rewards. Generally not advised to buy any amount of Platinum from the market without these, even if the savings is small. That is, if you must buy virtual currency.
-No votekick/ban function
-Archwing missions are boring and pointless
-RNG based rewards, essentially turns the game into a giant grindfest and a waste of time when you don't get what you want. This is 90% of the time.
-Gameplay gets very grindy and repetitive after a while, especially if your arsenal is limited. Also, It's all just about numbers going up, especially at end game. Not much strategy when you're one shotting everything with six or seven figures in Tower 4 void missions.
-Speaking of endgame content (or lack thereof), every mission pretty much becomes a laborous, linear chore when all you have left to do is farm resources, credits, or prime parts to feed mastery rank or whatever.
-Numerous game breaking glitches despite regular hotfixes
-Questionable physics. Parkour 2.0 has gotten me stuck in terrain more than once, even still today
-Lag can be crippling
-Balance issues. For example, leveling up equipment is really unbalanced (Draco anyone?)
-Too many experienced players asking for "taxis" to planets they don't even bother to unlock themselves
-Sometimes facepalm community that doesn't seem to get better. Refer to previous point. Also keyshare ditchers.
-Transmutation of mods is a complete waste of credits and time
-This game requires a ton of patience if you're not willing to spend a single cent. It's not pay2win, but it is very pay2advance. New players have it extremely rough.
-Crafting almost everything that matters in this game takes at least 12 hours in real time. They are mostly weapons. Forma take twice as long for every one. And you need lots of them. Warframes take six times longer. They can be rushed to immediate completion with Platinum, but nothing in this game is worth rushing.
-Mastery rank becomes mostly irrelevant after unlocking everything. The only reason to use bad weapons is to feed MR. These weapons are called "mastery fodder"
-Useless resources (Alloy Plates and faction resources like Detonite Injectors) that just pile up in your inventory and overly rare resources (Neurodes, Neural Sensors) that require hours of farming for a handful of them.
-Ordis (The mainframe and steward of your ship). Ceaselessly annoying and there's no way to mute him.
I have not tried PvP yet, but it exists. So again, even though I personally find the game fun and somewhat addicting, I can't really recommend it upon closer consideration. I do think it's worth a play since it's free. And I think it's one of the better free to play games out there. To this game's credit, it made me want to spend money on it, which I only exceptionally do with free to play games. And this is the first free to play game that made me want to spend as much as I did because I was having that much fun. The only reason I spent that much is because I was curious whether I really liked this or not, and I have a lot of Platinum to keep me going for a while as more updates and content roll out to determine that.

It's hard to recommend this game due to it being made for such a niche community, but I can wholeheartedly say this is THE BEST free to play game on steam. (yes, better than tf2)
First of all, WHAT THE HELL IS WARFRAME? Well, it's a third person sci fi shooter that relies heavily on grinding. Sound familiar? Well, think of it as a strange combo of Metal Gear and Monster Hunter. The combat, although not really stealth based, reminds me of Metal Gear Solid's combat. You can go guns ablazing, do cool melee combos, sneak up behind your enemies and take them out tactically, or just avoid them alltogether. This is what makes the combat fun, in that with so many different approaches to fighting, there comes millions of different strategies. Not onlythat, but each "warframe" has their own abilities that you can spec in using mods, which are devices you get during missions and from alerts that give you stat bonuses when you equip them.
Now, you're probably wondering "but wheres the Monster Hunter influence? Warframe sounds nothing like monster Hunter!!!". The way the progression system works is very similar to Monster Hunter. This game is NOT an MMO, due to the fact that you can experience everything yourself, if you so desire. How the item system works is each planet you can go to has a certain dropset for materials. You collect these materials by running the missions over and over again until an enemy drops however many of the things you need. Then, you use one of the currencies of this game, credits, to buy blueprints to create said items. (you get credits just for playing missions, so they're easy to farm) then, once you have everything, you create the item you want, and have to wait until its done. This can range from an hour to 3 days, depending on what you are building. Once thats done, it's yours! (considering you have the slots to keep it c: )
Now, as free to play games normally do, there is a premium currency in this game which allows you to bypass all that grinding and waiting, but it's also not to hard to get free. It's called platinum, (we'll call it plat, for convinience sake) and it is tradable with other players. People buy plat, and then trade it for blueprints they need to make "prime parts", which are all farmable in a place called the Void. You get the parts, you sell them for plat, and now you have plat to buy stuff.
There are many more systems that I'm not going to go into detail to explain, and instead I'm going to finish. Warframe is a hard to access game due to you having to constantly wait and grind to continually have fun with it, making it a huge timesink. But, the real fun is in the ride there, the grind you have to do to earn your item, and the amazing combat system that you play through to get your materials. Overall, I give Wareframe a 9/10. It's got it's quirks, but overall we have an amazing game with a solid foundation.

The only F2P game I've had the privilege of playing where the developers have true integrity, a completely transparent and community-based development process, and where the game is truly without paywalls or pay-to-win content.
There is nothing, I repeat, nothing in this game that you cannot earn, and earn in a reasonable amount of time.
The in-game premium currency, Platinum, can be traded with other players, which means that there's an entire emergent economy of people trading parts and money which allows anyone to buy premium cosmetic items and shortcuts to better equipment or things like inventory slots without paying a single penny of real money, which is a huge bonus.
Combine that with a truly unique and enthralling scifi universe on par with series like Halo or WH40K, always improving gameplay mechanics and a seemingly endless torrent of new, free content and expansions, and you have an extremely addictive and enjoyable game.
I can't recommend this game enough, what do you have to lose? It's free!

Ever wanted to be a Space Ninja? Then this is the game for you. Warframe is a Co-Op focussed 3rd person action game with tons of content very nice visuals and a buttery smooth framerate even on mid range rigs. The game is very satisfying thanks to the combat and movement systems, combine that with randomly generated levels so missions feel different every time to a degree. Rooms are the same but the order and number of each room is different every time. Now there are multiple tile sets it is pretty good and keeps things interesting.
The one caviat I do have with this game is that it takes a lot of effort to get going. This game is well known as Grindframe for a reason, you need to work for your items and run missions multiple times to get what you need. Then you wait X amount of hours while your items are built in the foundry. This can be rushed with premium currency and fortunately the business model is fair, at first I wasn't sure it was but after discovering there is a very active trading post where you can sell certain items for Platinum and in some cases a lot of it this makes that barrier go away.
I highly recommend this game if you have friends to play it with, soloing is very boring but get a bunch of friends together to run missions and make a clan and it becomes something really awesome.

Warframe can be described with the following 10-word phrase:
free-to-play, third-person, cooperative shooter about space ninjas.
I believe that the space ninjas alone would sell the game, but some people can't see the beauty of these interplanetary assassins, so allow me to elaborate.
You play as a tenno - a race of humanoid warriors that wear the titular warframe armor, which lets them move like ninjas and grants special powers - who is awoken from centuries of cryogenic sleep and tasked with defending the system from the opressive Grineer Empire's clone armies, the profit-crazy Corpus merchant cult, and a half virus, half nanobot, parasitic scourge called the Infestation.  The game's fast paced, run-around-y, shoot-'em-up-y gameplay makes it great for those aspiring to become ninjas themselves.  My only two gripes are connection issues that I have (though that may be my computer being a butt) and the absolute chore that grinding for resources is, but that's a symptom of it being free-to-play.  I CAN say that this is a free-to-play game done right: with a few exceptions in the cosmetics department, everything in this game can be obtained without spending real-world money (I HAVE spent money on it because the game is fekkin' amazing, but I never HAD to).  Overall, one of the best games I have ever played.
Fun and unique! Though, a "little" grindy. Sarcasm.

This game is pretty epic.  I started playing about a month ago and it's been my main game since then.  It's not just about the "space ninja" gimick but there are so many ways to play, equip and upgrade your warframe, weapons and pets that it makes the game extremely fun to play.  It's not just PVE and it is also not "pay to win".  Since the large majority of the game is PVE then if people can purchase things to better their PVE so be it - however they CANNOT purchase things for PVP with rl cash - it takes a lot of work to become good at pvp not only with upgrades/mods but also personal skill.  I would suggest this game to anyone who has a small group they play with and enjoys PVE as well as PVP.
Con:  The only con that I have to say about this game is the lack of PVP in PVE environments.  In my firm opinion there should be some sort of PVE mode that allows PVP at certain times - it would keep lazy players on their toes and stop people from being burnt out on pve games.
PS:  You can solo pretty much anything if you are good at this game so if you don't have friends you can always use matchmaking and join squads.

I do recommend this game, but only by a small margin, despite my over 1k hours on it.
It actually has quite a decent community for a F2P game, as long as you steer clear of the 'Region' chat tab. I've not experienced many rude people when trading, or when getting into a PUG, or asking someone to invite me for other missions.
There are plenty of weapon types. Even two automatic weapons could handle differently, whether it be recoil/accuracy, their projectiles having flight time, or pure fire rate and clip size. The melee combat is fairly well developed, and I don't see how they could add more depth without it becoming tedious.
Now, while the weapon variety is decent, there's still a problem with some of them. The Tonkor, for example, makes every other blast affiliated weapon obsolete. It has a high crit, decent blast base damage, and doesn't one-shot you when you're too close to an explosion. Rather, it won't even take away your shields if you have a reasonable amount. The only drawback is that the grenades it shoots cannot be manually detonated, like the Penta, but they still explode after a time anyways, and they're still easy to aim. Add that with the fact that you can use this weapon as soon as you hit Mastery Rank 5 (which doesn't even take two weeks), and now you have noobs running around with firepower that should be reserved for much higher Mastery Ranks. That's not good balance.
The Prime warframes are a cool idea, although a bit annoying. You get a frame you like (that isn't primed yet), then you put a reactor on it, which gives it more potential, and then a forma or three to give it even more specialization. Then when your favorite frame gets "primed", that frame you "potatoed" and "forma'd" is now obsolete, since it's always objectively better in various ways than the original. You can't transfer reactors/catalysts/forma to other frames/weapons. Now you have to accumulate forma and a potato to slap onto your shiny new primed frame variant.
Soon you'll realize that putting a potato or forma onto a non-primed frame is a waste of time and resources, and then when people demand you use that frame, your frame might not be as good as your squad would like, causing both you and them to get frustrated. But really, saving your potatoes for frames and weapons that actually matter is more important, because you need those weapons and frames to be any good. Really though, why should I be encouraged by other players to use my resources now on a frame that will be obsolete in a few updates? I shouldn't. They should let you transfer reactors at least.
I will say though, that the mod customization is pretty nice. Your weapons don't get better just from ranking up, you need to slap mods on them for there to be any difference. The higher the rank, the more mods you can slap on. With frames, you unlock abilities/rank up abilites, and small increments of health and shields as it ranks up. I'll be honest, this is a good mechanic. It lets you specialize directly, instead of hoping you get certain stats when you level up in most other RPGs.
Also, the game doesn't really require that you pay even a dime for it to be fun. You can get almost everything (aside from prime access stuff which is just fluff anyways) from selling prime parts/mods for plat that other suckers bought, then you can use that plat to get more frame/weapon slots or trade it for another part you need. Works well, but I'd like the ability to trade more things like the Stalker equipment, since he almost never even drops a blueprint of any of his weapons.
That leads me to probably my final topic: RNG. The Random Number Generator of this game hates you. It hates everyone. If you offer it prayers of sweat and salty tears, then maybe, just MAYBE it'll give you what you want. If you go to the void often, you'll get more forma blueprints than you'll ever want or need. Forma is used to alter mod polarity, or in short, further customize a weapon or frame. While that sounds helpful, you really don't need more than 3 or 4 forma per weapon or frame, any more is just a waste, unless it had no polarized slots to begin with. If you got too many junk prime parts, you could at least sell them for ducats, which come in handy at "end-game". But no. Forma will quickly become your most hated enemy, even worse than those heavy gunners and bombards that blow you to bits, and still worse than the nullifiers which are the bane of many frames. You will hate it.
Final Thoughts: Warfarm is pretty grindy. But you can have fun while doing it. Certain aspects need to be fleshed out (*cough*Archwing*cough*), other small things need to be removed (*cough*Drahk Master Disarming*cough*), but it's mostly good. Try it out at least, and beware the forma.

I noticed a lot of the negative reviews were from people that have been playing the game since it was released, often saying they dont like what it's become. So as a new player I can't really compare Warframe to what it once was, I can only compare it to what else is out there in the same genre. Ultimately, I'm talking about other online games. It can get a little bit repetitive its true, but I havent yet seen that as a bad thing, maybe in a few hundred hours more once I've stopped discovering new things and unlocking new things it might start to sink in. But in all honesty what online game doesnt have grinding or repititon. Honestly Warframe is the only online game I've played where I dont almost feel as if I'm entitled to some kind of wage playing it. For a free to play game it's absolutely incredible what it offers. STUNNING graphics, a decent enough story line and interesting lore, a variety of weapons and equipment to choose from. And most people probably think that it must be pay to win, that for a free game to be so...impressive, it must be too good to be true...well not exactly. Although there is a premium currency within the game, every weapon, warframe and equipment is accessible through playing. The premium currency, for a lot of players, is used to purchase a few extra warframe/weapon slots (in fact this is is what is recommended that new players do with their free platinum) or to skip construction times. A Warframe can be bought outright from the store, or you can spend time in the game collecting their blueprints and resources necessary to create it. Although this may sound somewhat tedious, its actually incredibly rewarding and I find it to be a very acheivment based game.
I give the game an 8.5/10, and best online/f2p game I've played

ARK: Survival Evolved is a perfect name. Overall, I would definitely recomend this game to people looking for a challenge. That said, this game is not to be taken lightly. Granted, I too have spent much of my time taming wild primitive beasts and building huts made of thatch and wood, but the game isn't as peaceful as you would hope. For the most part, the survival isn't really hard. Most of the time, food is obtainable, and as long as you stay near a water scource, that isn't much of a problem either. However, in ARK, survival isn't as simple as food, water, and shelter. I only had a few scarce deaths from those in the begining. No, the hardest part about this game, is the endless amounts of raptors, and T-rexes, and other variations of carnivorous beasts that are always on the hunt. As much as I have loved the beauty of nature, and the thrill of fighting lesser dinosaurs, I have had tenfold expriences of dinos spawning on me, and insta-killing me. Experience takes forever to get as well, granted, you can get it from doing just about anything, but because some simple things like a spear are locked until you reach a certain level, things can get a little boring. It becomes a race to the next level of when you can finally make a bed, or a fence, or even a wall. I know, this is a survival game, and the entire point of survival games is to be hard, but sometimes it feels a little unfair. If I went venturing into the forest unprepared and alone, getting eaten by an unfriendly resident would make sense. However, sometimes, I would try to build a temporary home near the ocean atop a hill in complete isolation, but then get destroyed randomly by a velociraptor that just so happened to convieniently spawn thirty yards away. Well, if anything, this game has certainly excelled at one thing, the dinosaurs are indeed TERRIFYING! This entire game makes you fear the unexplored. Granted, that's to be expected, as everything you encounter want's to invite you over to their dinner party, but you soon find out that you are indeed fairly low on the food chain. There have been plenty of times where I ran from a small creature, and ended up face to face with a much larger one, and ended up turning tail, and sprinting for my life. Hands down my favourite game. It relies heavily on teamwork, collaboration and assistance from your mates. Communicating with your tribe is so important, allowing you to schedule and delegate tasks to be done. The high-end visuals and animations makes this game incredibly realistic (despite the dinosaurs of course), and if there was any situation where you needed to survive on the smallest of things in the real world, you know that by progressing through the content with your friends, that you could rely on them.
There is always something to do, whether it be collecting materials to improve your shelter, taming new dinosaurs to conquer the land or merely discovery new engrams to become more powerful in your abilities.
Highly recommended to anyone who's on the fence. One thing I should mention though is that this game is not very well optimised. Even with an extremely high-end PC, there are points in time where you get random frame drops which can really make the game unplayable especially on medium-low end PCs.

Incredibly lengthy times to do anything followed by the endless amount of things that can interrupt some of these literal "timers" make for an overall painstaking and unfun experience.  Even with a 2x event going on with taming, harvesting and xp, it's still too damn long.  These games thrive on being lucky by being part of the alpha groups on any given server.  Most of these people have thousands of hours in the game which is not practical for a person who just wants to jump in and play or has an actual life.  These players that usually have the DLC have flying wyverns that are very fast and can breath fire.  You don't stand a chance.  A player told me it literally took them FOUR DAYS to train the wyvern.  I don't know if this was when the event was going on, but that is 96! hours of constant attention, by her or a tribemate.  I should mention that the DLC content is on seperate servers, but you can bring content to a normal server if you so choose.  It's really idiotic and unfair unless you pony up the cash.  Unless this game and games like this take a page from Subnautica, I can't even remotely begin to recommend it.  I rate games on their fun factor and unless you like dying and being reset to zero constantly, there is none.  The only fun I ever had was getting a trike and a high level raptor tamed (all the low levels die nearly instantly and aren't worth taming).  Which lasted all for ten minutes as a swarm of 5+ flying poisonous insects came from nowhere nearly ending my level 98 raptor's life.  Then the raptor was immediately killed a few minutes later after I told it to kill a parasaur (a non-violent herbivore) and it instead managed to aggro every creature in the area, sealing it's demise.  After having to sneak around an alpha raptor, t-rex, and players to tame this last raptor, and then logging in later to find all my equipment "borrowed" by a teammate, causing me to go outside in the middle of the night to get materials from scratch for the one hundredth time, then dying from a carno (basically a smaller t-rex) after I ran out of stamina, I officially gave up.
Lets not even get started on the paid DLC in Early Access topic, the inability to learn even most of the engrams (read: blueprints) yourself (you are basically required to be in a group), lackluster wannabe RPG mechanics, unintuitive menus, and TERRIBLY unoptimized settings.  If you don't have a gaming PC, don't even attempt to play this, it will not work.

Many people will complain about this game for the bugs, paid DLC, optimization, and rollbacks.  The game is great, it is super addicting.  It is also not for everyone.  If you want a major time dump, this is the game for you.  It is very rewarding and this is the only game to EVER make me want to pull all nighters 6 months in a row in the 21 years I have been gaming.
Bugs: Yes, they exist.  What multiplater game doesn't have any bugs?  Some suck, yes.  Some are annoying, yes.  And some make you lose 4 hours of taming.  But in all aspects, bugs are maybe worth 2-3% of actual gameplay.  I have 2400+ hours into Ark, and have experienced every bug known in this game.  I have had my fair share of dinos get stuck under the maps.  I have lost Ascendant gear to it falling through the floor, and I have had dinos die due to bugs.  It happens.  But by all means, none of it is gamebreaking.  Sure, after losing a lot of items due to a bug I will sometimes log off Ark because of frustration, but I'm not going to bash the Devs because they constantly are fixing bugs and exploits with every patch.
Paid DLC:  I do not quite understand why people are so upset about paid DLC. First off, its only 20$.  If you are complaining about 20$ for a video game, then I don't know why you are even playing games in the first place.  Second, you dont NEED to buy the DLC to experience Ark to the fullest.  Ark + Scorched Earth still costs less than a brand new game that comes out.
Optimization:  This game used to run a lot worse than it does now. My system was built for gaming, but I am going to be honest and say Ark does struggle at times.  There is a memory leak that causes my frames to sit at 15 fps (on Epic everything).  A simple restart of my pc fixes the issue.  The Devs are always releasing small optimizations to help the game run (and I am always logged on during these patches to see the difference it makes).  They have dramatically improved the way the game runs from when it first game out.  If you are still struggling with frames, there are some guides on Steam that takes about 5 minutes to do that can really improve your fps.
Rollbacks:  Yes they happen. And yes they suck.  I did lose some items and work in the recent rollback, but I understand why they did it.  They had to fix a major exploitive bug.  And the devs listened to the community and made rates 2x exp/gather/taming to compensate for the rollback.  And yes, I understand the people complaining about raising Wyverns.  It sucks.  But the Devs are working on the game still and this can be seen on the Patch Notes post on Steam.  They are constantly fixing things in this Early Access game.

The graphics aregreat the concept of being stranded (like a jurassic park game) on a dinosaur island having to survive, not just the dinos in your area, but the elements, the constant reminder that you will need to make food or drink water. The cons can be that the dinos dont seem to have a pathfinding system, they can wander in circles, straight lines, or be stuck walking into a wall for several hours. After playing in excess of 600 hours over the course of a year and wringing every cent's worth of gameplay I could out of the 30 bucks I paid I've finally decided to put my thoughts down. I love this game, I find open world survival sandboxes a hell of a lot of fun and I've met some incredible people through it. The animals are interesting and varied, the worlds are HUGE (until you tame a flyer and everything's 1-2 minutes flight away) and they're constantly adding new stuff.
But, it's a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥to run on my computer. It's no cheap laptop, I use it for 3D modelling and can run most games at decent settings. Ark constantly freezes it, takes forever to load, freezes if you alt-tab or do anything on the second moniter during loading, stutters terribly on any graphics settings, it's an absolute princess of a game that throws a tantrum every time you take your attention away from it. I usually end up restarting my computer out of despair after looking at a frozen screen for 5 minutes and trying every key combination I know.
tl;dr:
Great game, great online community, dinosaurs! Terrible optimization, tries to kill your computer at every opportunity, official server gathering/resource/taming rates are far too slow (friend and I spent 14 hours taming a Bronto before they added kibble to the game to speed it up).

After about 100 hours of gameplay, I can still seeing this my go-to co-op game for my spouse and I. We play MMO's and co-op shooters mostly but the ability to feel like we have been stranded on an island together with prehistoric creatures is not only exciting, but a dream come true!
Level up and evolve to be able to learn newer and more modern forms of defense and offensive items. We have tamed countless dinos, and built small establishments in multiple areas to ensure we have a place to if we get caught in a bind. Don't even get me started on the Giganotosaurus. We finally ran into one after about 80 hours of game play at the top of a peak and it killed one of my beloved Allosaurus and were forced to run for our lives.
The cons: I have gotten stuck multiple times building a wall where I would get stuck in the wall and have to demolish it in order to get unstuck. Our dinos also tend to get caught as well on boulders or trees so you have to keep an eye on them so you don't accidentally leave them behind. You may/may not have to tweak with server settings until you get comfortable with the controls and gameplay. The pre-existing settings were a bit too hard for us as first time players. We found ourselves spending more time trying to reach each other and re-acquiring items we lost in death. This was before we discovered the wonders of bed spawning! This did not deter us though!! Our very first time playing co-op together we just built a simple 2x2 thatch hut and upon completion found ourselves being devoured by a Rex!! Not ideal, but worth every second!
This game is beyond exciting and I highly recommend it to anybody who enjoys survival games. I do not PvP, so please DO NOT let the reviews discourage you from playing if you do not as well! You can play solo or with a few other people on a non-dedicated server if you do not enjoy PvPing. Good luck!!

Looking at the number of hours I have in this game you're probably wondering why I'm writing a negative review. Well I can assure you that I have gotten pretty far into this game, and have personally played with most of the features. because of that, I can make a fair judgement that the game, and it, as well as the developer, Studio Wildcard, is not good. If you don't feel like reading through all of the review, I've made headlines telling you why I don't recommend this game.
-----You might get several hours of enjoyment playing through the game, but after a while it will get boring, or even downright frustrating.-----
The game is not absolutely unplayable, it can be enjoyable, but it gets old. Starting a new game has it's moments, though it can be unforgiving. For example, the game lacks a tutorial, which can make it a little tricky for new players. Although like the lack of a tutorial breaking immersion and blocking the screen might be nice, the immersion will be broken when you have to look something up because a basic gameplay feature was designed with no logical base at all. The servers are full of players whose favorite passtime is slaugtering new players, and it takes a while to get to a point where you can fight against even the small creatures. Exploration is fun, for a while. Travelling through the map for the first time is fairly exciting, though once you've seen everything even the procedural maps start to get old. There are some interesting creatures running about, and finding something you haven't seen before is fun, but after a while the creatures get boring, too. The survival part of the game is great... at low levels. At high levels you have to get the same materials over and over again just to make some of the better equipment. I can't tell you how monotonous the game becomes once you get to the high levels. Speaking of high levels, the endgame is terrible. After the hundreds of hours of work it takes to even get to high levels there isn't anything to do, but use your power against low level players. Sure there are bosses, but there isn't really any reason to fight them. You have to make an expensive portal just to get to them, and the only real thing you get from them is a little flag saying you killed them. There are giants that can only be tamed and ridden by high level players, but they lose most of their health and abilities when tamed, so they are only good for killing players with weaker creatures, that's it.
-----The game isn't perfect, but the real problem is the developers.-----
Studio Wildcard has shown that their number one priority is to make money, not a good game. When I got this game there were less features, but the game was actually much more playable than it is now. It seems as though whenever they add something new, they also break something. Maybe they introduce a new bug, or maybe they just make the gameplay even less balanced. There are also old problems, such as bad collision, that have stuck with the game and will probably never get fixed. Performance-wise the game is just aweful. The game is constantly kept just on the line of unplayable, whether it be from poor or no optimization, or bugs making basic things just not work. The developers focus very hard on art, not gameplay. The videos and screenshots can show that the game looks (or at least could look) great, but they can't show that the game lacks depth. The developers have released several fan created mods as official add-on packs. I'm sure this was a great way for them to expand the game without actually doing any work. The sad thing is that the player made additions are actually better made than the base game. The final straw for me, however, was when the developers, instead of actually making the game better, released a paid dlc for their game while the game itself was still unfinished. After about 100 hours of gameplay, I can still seeing this my go-to co-op game for my spouse and I. We play MMO's and co-op shooters mostly but the ability to feel like we have been stranded on an island together with prehistoric creatures is not only exciting, but a dream come true!
Level up and evolve to be able to learn newer and more modern forms of defense and offensive items. We have tamed countless dinos, and built small establishments in multiple areas to ensure we have a place to if we get caught in a bind. Don't even get me started on the Giganotosaurus. We finally ran into one after about 80 hours of game play at the top of a peak and it killed one of my beloved Allosaurus and were forced to run for our lives.
The cons: I have gotten stuck multiple times building a wall where I would get stuck in the wall and have to demolish it in order to get unstuck. Our dinos also tend to get caught as well on boulders or trees so you have to keep an eye on them so you don't accidentally leave them behind. You may/may not have to tweak with server settings until you get comfortable with the controls and gameplay. The pre-existing settings were a bit too hard for us as first time players. We found ourselves spending more time trying to reach each other and re-acquiring items we lost in death. This was before we discovered the wonders of bed spawning! This did not deter us though!! Our very first time playing co-op together we just built a simple 2x2 thatch hut and upon completion found ourselves being devoured by a Rex!! Not ideal, but worth every second!
This game is beyond exciting and I highly recommend it to anybody who enjoys survival games. I do not PvP, so please DO NOT let the reviews discourage you from playing if you do not as well! You can play solo or with a few other people on a non-dedicated server if you do not enjoy PvPing. Good luck!!

Looking at the number of hours I have in this game you're probably wondering why I'm writing a negative review. Well I can assure you that I have gotten pretty far into this game, and have personally played with most of the features. because of that, I can make a fair judgement that the game, and it, as well as the developer, Studio Wildcard, is not good. If you don't feel like reading through all of the review, I've made headlines telling you why I don't recommend this game.
-----You might get several hours of enjoyment playing through the game, but after a while it will get boring, or even downright frustrating.-----
The game is not absolutely unplayable, it can be enjoyable, but it gets old. Starting a new game has it's moments, though it can be unforgiving. For example, the game lacks a tutorial, which can make it a little tricky for new players. Although like the lack of a tutorial breaking immersion and blocking the screen might be nice, the immersion will be broken when you have to look something up because a basic gameplay feature was designed with no logical base at all. The servers are full of players whose favorite passtime is slaugtering new players, and it takes a while to get to a point where you can fight against even the small creatures. Exploration is fun, for a while. Travelling through the map for the first time is fairly exciting, though once you've seen everything even the procedural maps start to get old. There are some interesting creatures running about, and finding something you haven't seen before is fun, but after a while the creatures get boring, too. The survival part of the game is great... at low levels. At high levels you have to get the same materials over and over again just to make some of the better equipment. I can't tell you how monotonous the game becomes once you get to the high levels. Speaking of high levels, the endgame is terrible. After the hundreds of hours of work it takes to even get to high levels there isn't anything to do, but use your power against low level players. Sure there are bosses, but there isn't really any reason to fight them. You have to make an expensive portal just to get to them, and the only real thing you get from them is a little flag saying you killed them. There are giants that can only be tamed and ridden by high level players, but they lose most of their health and abilities when tamed, so they are only good for killing players with weaker creatures, that's it.
-----The game isn't perfect, but the real problem is the developers.-----
Studio Wildcard has shown that their number one priority is to make money, not a good game. When I got this game there were less features, but the game was actually much more playable than it is now. It seems as though whenever they add something new, they also break something. Maybe they introduce a new bug, or maybe they just make the gameplay even less balanced. There are also old problems, such as bad collision, that have stuck with the game and will probably never get fixed. Performance-wise the game is just aweful. The game is constantly kept just on the line of unplayable, whether it be from poor or no optimization, or bugs making basic things just not work. The developers focus very hard on art, not gameplay. The videos and screenshots can show that the game looks (or at least could look) great, but they can't show that the game lacks depth. The developers have released several fan created mods as official add-on packs. I'm sure this was a great way for them to expand the game without actually doing any work. The sad thing is that the player made additions are actually better made than the base game. The final straw for me, however, was when the developers, instead of actually making the game better, released a paid dlc for their game while the game itself was still unfinished. I have now uninstalled the game, and it may be the only game in my library that I actually regret buying. I don't recommend it because I have a feeling that if you buy it, you too will, after a while, regret buying it.

Ark: Survival Evolved is an excellent dinosaur survival game that can keep you addicted for hundreds of hours. Ark is one of the best games I've played in the past few years, with a lot of promise for the future.
Ark is an open-ended game that lets you play it exactly how you'd like. Whether you enjoy battling, raiding, base-building, exploring, role playing, taming dinosaurs, breeding dinosaurs, you can focus your gameplay on one aspect without feeling like you're missing out on the rest of the game. The game's focus on dinosaurs make it a unique and innovative survival game.
Taming dinosaurs is one of the biggest parts of the game. It can be a lot of fun exploring the map for the perfect dinosaur you're seeking, and players will often help each other in pointing out locations of high level dinosaurs. For some dinosaurs, taming can be a really long, cumbersome process, but the results can be rewarding.
The dinosaur component of the game almost has a Pokemon "catch them all" type of feel, since you need eggs from specific dinosaurs to effectively tame other dinosaurs. Each dinosaur has a distinct value in the game; they are your weapons, they are your defenses, they are your transportation, and they are your gatherers. This makes it a lot of fun to try to build up your dinosaur army. Dinosaur saddles are only unlocked once you reach a certain level, making you strive for more experience points to unlock new dinosaurs (and items). Some higher level dinosaurs can take hours upon hours to tame if you're on an official server, but unofficial servers allow for multipliers to speed up gameplay if that's your preference. You begin to get attached to your dinosaurs, especially after spending so much time taming and leveling them up.
Taming requires a lot of time commitment and planning, and companion apps and websites are almost required for gameplay to look up recipes and calculate times and supplies required, otherwise you won't know if you're about to spend 30 minutes taming a dinosaur or 4 hours. (Disclaimer: I run the
and unofficial companion apps for Ark.)
The game does require some grinding, but specialized dinosaurs let you cut down grinding times, and gathering multipliers on unofficial servers can speed up the process for those looking to focus gameplay on other areas.
Ark has a great modding community and talented players have created stunning maps and add-on content to the game. It's great to see the game's developers recognizing and encouraging players to extend the game. They've even adapted maps and some mods to be part of the official game.
If you like base-building games, Ark is for you. On Player vs. Player (PVP), bases require a lot of strategy and thought to make sure that your defenses are well-placed and your valuable items (and dinosaurs!) are well protected. If you want a more free gameplay without having to worry about other players raiding you, Player vs. Environment (PVE) can be a lot of fun for those looking to just build awesome bases and villages.
On top of normal base-building, Ark has an innovating type of base-building where you can build mobile bases on the backs of dinosaurs, such as a Brontosaurus, or even flying or swimming dinosaurs for airships and boats. Gameplay mechanics like this feel completely ridiculous when you think into it, but really give Ark its unique style.  Who doesn't want to build a Quetzalcoatlus battleship?!
Ark is so much better if you're playing with a friend. My boyfriend and I would play hours upon hours for months, and we would have so much fun playing together. We would help each other build, do co-op mining or taming quests, and constantly log back in daily to check on our base. There are often other friendly players who are looking for tribemates if you don't have any friends who play.
In my opinion, one of my biggest problems with the game is balance issues -- specifically balance between players. Getting started in the game can be difficult, and "Alpha Tribes" (the strongest tribes on a server) with high-level dinosaurs can often be bullies and attack low level players without repercussion. In Ark, it's very easy to lose hours (and even months) worth of work in a couple hours by high level players. Because players of all skill level are on the same map, there's nothing from stopping higher level players from attacking lower level players.
When playing multiplayer, Ark requires you to constantly log back in. While this makes it very addicting, it can also become a bit stressful if you don't have much time to play but you happen to log in and find that you base was broken into, which means that you'll have to do repairs so that others can't easily enter. It can also be stressful if you're trying to start out alone, or with other new players, as it can take a lot of time to build a base that can withstand attacks of higher level players.
The challenge of PVP can be a lot of fun, however, it can be really frustrating when other players destroy hours of your work. With taming one dinosaur sometimes taking more than 4 to 6 hours on an official server, it can be heartbreaking to have one killed -- especially if it was just sitting innocently in your base. There are some somewhat agreed upon ethics in Ark, such as only killing a player's dinosaur if they're attacking you, however, not everyone will follow this rule and it's not uncommon to log in to find some or even many of your dinosaurs dead.
My hope is that there are some balance issues resolved in the future, because a lot of my friends have been really excited to play Ark, but dropped the game after having their dinosaurs and bases destroyed by higher level players when they haven't reached the point where they could even defend themselves.
Continuous updates keep you coming back to try out new dinosaurs and features. Studio Wildcard is constantly pushing out updates with new dinosaurs, items, and map changes. Players are very critical about the developers, complaining when they push back updates or making balance changes (pretty common for a lot of games), but I think the game's team should be commended for their transparency and the amount of communication they give regarding updates.  I'd rather developers be transparent and push back changes than a team that pushes out unfinished patches -- or doesn't even communicate with players.
Studio Wildcard is much more transparent than a lot of game developers I've seen. They constantly talks about upcoming patches as well as the game's far future, and they're great at getting players excited for upcoming changes with teasers and gorgeous promo videos for each patch. The team's true passion in the game really shows in their communication through Steam, Twitter, Reddit, and other channels.
With unique creatures, excellent multiplayer, flexible gameplay, and beautiful graphics, Ark: Survival Evolved is worth purchasing and will reignite your interest in dinosaurs from your childhood. The game has a bit of a learning curve and has some balance issues, but is so much fun for those who like adventure, survival, and base-building games. While the game requires relatively modern video hardware, the graphics are pretty realistic and gorgeous and the game can be enjoyed on lower graphics settings. The game's constant updates make it well worth playing and will make you keep coming back for updates.
