Warframe is a surprisingly addicting co-op third person shooter, and spiritual successor, if not sequel to Dark Sector, with a fair enough F2P business model and entertaining, satisfying, fast paced combat. It is still in active development, new content gets released at a reasonable rate, and hotfixes for issues come out blazingly fast.
In Warframe, you play as one of the legendary Tenno, a race of posthuman "space ninjas" dedicated to balancing and drawing out a war between the oppressive and xenophobic Grineer empire, and the Corpus, a collective of traders and engineers. You're sent to do various missions across the solar system, ensuring not one faction gains the upper hand. The story, unfortunately, is the game's greatest weakness. What's there is well written and has a host of great, memorable characters; for example, the exuberant Vay Hek, one of the most influential Grineer, who doesn't just chew the scenery whenever he appears; he DEVOURS it. Or the brilliant, yet cowardly Alad V, who has a vested interest in researching and experimenting on Tenno like you, but is a
diplomat.
In spite of this however, much of the story is not told very well through the game, a problem this game and Destiny share. While you get a decent enough amount of story through Inbox messages and through transmissions during the story missions (which are entitled Quests in your ship's navigation), and reading into it gives off an extreme Metal Gear Solid vibe, much of the story you'll need to know is only properly told in depth on the official wikia, and there are a few notable missions with a decent chunk of story that you just cannot do anymore (Tethra's Doom and Eyes of Blight are just examples, you can see them all on the wikia's Events page). The story doesn't have much of a linear narrative at all due to the mission structure, as well. While the quests make sense, you can kill the main villain of the Natah quest, Tyl Regor, before completing it. Things like this lead to a story that feels somewhat disjointed and patchwork.
The other game's main issue, while not nearly as bad, is the F2P model. Most of the things you can buy through the Market, you can create through the Foundry for free. However, doing so requires Monster Hunter levels of grinding. It's not as bad as a Korean MMO, but it does require some patience and dedication. Speaking of patience though, the model's biggest problem is it's timewalls. Creating things in the Foundry takes enough time to make mobile games blush, and the times can be inconsistent as well. Some weapons take 12 hours to make, others take 24. The worst offender by far are the Warframes, which require 3 parts to make, each having a 12 hour wait time, and even once you get all the parts, you have to wait THREE DAYS (exactly 72 hours) in order to actually combine the parts and get the Warframe. Thankfully, you can build more than one part in the Foundry.
There is also a good chunk of weapons and 'frames that you can only make if you're in a clan, which requires you to make a Clan Key (which also takes 12 hours :I) in order to access it's Dojo (basically a social hub for your clan) and acquire the blueprints. It is by far the worst part of Warframe, ignoring the problems with the story. The grind is good enough to pad out the gameplay, and yet, DE felt the need to do this for whatever reason. You can rush foundry crafting via Platinum, the game's premium currency, but you have to pay for that. No, it's nowhere near as bad as an outright paywall, but it's still annoying having to wait so long for a new toy. Finally, while you can still just craft everything you need instead of buying it (as such there is no real P2W), there are a few cosmetic items you unfortunately are locked into having to buy. The most egregious of which is the full Classic color palette. Without buying it, you get a paultry amount of colors, unable to color your items anything other than a shade of, for example, overly saturated green or vibrant♥♥♥♥♥♥yellow.
Other than these issues, the game is excellent in most other areas.
Visually, the game is incredible and impressively well-optimized for a small-ish independent developer, and Digital Extremes deserves all the credit in the world for them. I have cranked every option in the game up to the maximum, and rarely ever drop below 60 (only cases are sometimes in the Void due to the amount of enemies and reflective surfaces, and consistently in a Relay, due to the amount of players) on a fairly common mid-high end machine. The art style is fantastic, clearly taking inspiration from Japanese sci-fi and even a bit of Metroid Prime. Aside from a few questionable aspects (like the camera never holding still even when completely idle, or a few weapons being held incorrectly), the game is delicious eye candy.
In terms of audio, the music is...okay. It's not awful, but it's not memorable, either. It's standard cinematic fare, made with things like Damage, Evolve, Aeon, etc. without much melody or personality. There isn't really a single track in the game that stands out, or gets stuck in your head. The game could benefit from a Music 2.0. However, it shines in the SFX department. Many weapons have an incredibly satisfying feel to them. And, of course, the voice acting for the most part is fantastic.
Gameplay wise, it's incredibly fast paced, incredibly addicting and incredibly fun. There is a huge collection of primary, secondary and melee weapons, many of which having a fun gimmick to them. These include guns like the Opticor (Warframe's very own Spartan Laser), the Redeemer (a double-bladed longsword that doubles as an incredibly powerful shotgun), and the Amprex (a Quake-style Lightning Gun that chains to other nearby enemies). There are 13 different damage types, not including random critical hits (which interestingly enough, exist alongside headshots) and red crits (a critical hit that can only occur after your weapon's critical chance has reached 100% and above), 6 of them being made by combining 2 of the 4 base elements (Cold, Electric, Heat and Toxin).
Weapons and 'frames are upgraded via mods. Mods are random drops that give you stat buffs and sometimes special effects. You can fuse mods together to improve their stats, turning a 12%+ rate of fire buff eventually into a 72%+ buff. There are an estimated 605 mods too, so you have an incredible selection to choose from to make your gun perform exactly how you want it to. At first, the melee is a button mashing simulator, but you can increase your versatility by finding Stance mods, which alter your weapon's attacks and gives you the ability to perform combos with more than one button. There is, again, a pretty hefty selection of planets and missions to choose from, like a Domination-esque mission or a simple "kill everything" mission. You're able to do an impressive amount of parkour, being able to jump up and across walls, roll at incredible speeds through the air, and do an obligatory double jump. Getting the hang of the movement, and training your aim to compensate for your speed, is key to being successful at the combat in Warframe.
Finally, as a small side note, solo play is okay. You don't get any second wind mechanic (if you die in solo you'll be forced to use one of your 'frame's 4 revives, or abort the mission and keep your revive), but you won't be overly penalized for playing more "casual" difficulties.
Steam doesn't have a high enough character limit for in-depth reviews, so I'll end it with this. Warframe, in spite of it's problems, is an excellent F2P title that puts most others to shame. It includes fantastic gameplay, surprisingly memorable characters, AAA level visuals and an almost overwhelming amount of content, even having a PVP mode (which I have not tried and have no interest in right now, so I can't cover it).
And hey, it's free, so there's no harm in trying, right?

Okay, so this will be a long review, you ready? Got your popcorn? No? WELL TOO BAD IM STARTING ANYWAY.
So you start out with the Lotus, a lady who tells you to run and use your first ability, in my case, slash and dash, to kill your enemies. Around a minute later, You're given a choice. I believe its MK1 Bo staff or MK1 Skana. I chose skana personally. After killing more enemies, your given another choice. MK1 Kunai, or MK1 i forgot what it is, I chose kunai. Then your given your final choice for the mission, Primary weapon. I believe its MK1 Braton or MK1 Paris. paris being a bow and braton being a machine gun. I chose paris. So, in this game, you can rush through the entire level, do it however fast you want to, or you can stay, get loot, get mods, and really customize to your playstyle. Personally, i like stealth. So i eventually got the warframe Loki, whose abilities are, Decoy, Invisibility, Decoy explosion, and Radial disarm. There are many warframes, a new one being recently introduced, Atlas, who can read minds i believe. Now, to the point, this game is an absolute grindfest. Everone calls it P2W because of high platinuim *The premium currency* prices. Thats to put up a grindwall. They dont want you taking the easy way out.There are people with 3000+ Hours in this game that are barely halfway through getting a prime warframe. So, you may be thinking, "How duz me get muteeruels fur diss" Thats how you all sound obviously, but you can purchase blueprints in the market for credits, the money earned ingame. Platinuim is used to buy the component itself. Say you wanted a dual skana blueprint or something, you would need X amount of resources, that you get from each planet. Each planet gives its own resources, like earth, has rubedo, and mars, has something else. Anyway, onto the main factions in the game. The five main factions so far are the Grineer, the Corpus, the infected, the Orokin, and the Tenno, you are the tenno, You are the operator, ordis- sorry i got lost there. But you have this dude in your ship named ordis. Every so often he'll say funny things, like "Oh dear! The operator has come back with an archwing part! You must forge it immediately, Soon you'll be flying through the skies like a *Voice gets much deeper* WINGED DEATH MACHINE". Anyway  back to the factions, The orokin are the more advanced faction.They have these things called death cubes there, that shoot lasers that kill both them and you extremely fast, making it very useful. The grineer are the starters, Fairly easy. Nothing special about them. The corpus hold a lot of loot, and have tougher enemies. Like MOAs, for instance. These are robotic chicken like guys with machine guns. Onto the Infected, A failed lab experiment of the grineer, the infected are now insanely powerful, being leapers, chargers, and ancients. Ancients can grab you and pull you along with them, which is scary stuff. Onto the gamemodes, Ill only be listing 3 to save time, but theres the exterminate, where you kill everything on the ship, the survival, your air supply is cut off and you have to run around and get capsules to stay alive, whilst being shot, and defense, where you defend a certain item/artifact. Actually, theres 2 more I wanted to list, the crossfire, where you board a ship full of fighting grineer and corpus, and kill them all. I dont remember what the last one is called, but you take the side of a faction, like corpus, and they become teammates as you clear out infected or grineer. Thats all for now, updates WILL be coming, this game is still developing, fast, and insanely fun, this game is a Ninja grindfest with a lot to do.

Currently i play on a pretty much a toaster (its 6 years old - 16gig ddr3 ram, core i5 processor, amd gpu hd6900 series), its in dire need to have pretty much everything in it upgraded to run all the new fancy graphic games. Tbh on the server we had setup privately, we only started to have lag issues, and performance issues after we had 40+ dinos, a massive HQ along with the Giga tamed and guarding the house.  That being said, we had only 6 large bases like that on an entire map, and there were only maybe 15 people on the server total (there were a couple of randomers we allowed in to increase the population)
(note, i play on almost all lowest setting cus my gpu can't handle more atm and i dont have any major issues, last year i had it installed on my second ssd but that has since died so now it runs oin a hdd..and it is slower)
Here are some useful points for those who are actually curious about the game:
- if you want to run this on high specs and enjoy the game to its fullest potential, make sure you have a powerful pc which can handle it, only upgrading your gpu wont solve all issues - you will need better everything
- the game runs best if installed on an ssd, however you should have a second game dedicated ssd apart form one you would have your os installed on
- solo play can get tedious, you will; need to either make friends on the server or have few friends to play with you - that way it is way more fun
- you need stable internet connection, wifi wont cut most of the time
Pros:
- Surviving in this game and getting yourself setup is challenging
- Small group/ with friends gameplay is fun as well - also makes things little easier and safer ;)
- Recommend private or non-dedicated servers - also tends to be more stable overall if mod knows what they are at
- The server settings are highly adjustable for various play styles - increase of experience gain, taming speed and harvest decreased overall need to grind
- Game devs are still working steadily on the game (there have bee optimisation patches along the way which enabled me to actually run the game on my toaster - it didnt run at realease for example, and recently i have been able to turn up some settings from low to medium!!!)
- There is a lot to do in game, beautiful dynos, and hell, it can be hella relaxing to play it as well as gives you that rush when something is trying to eat you, or you get propelled through the air when you fail to tame a Giga and he wakes up...and theres no point to look for your stuff because you flew in possibly couple of pieces...
- Regular, new content; and as with all patches sometimes something can break but they are fast at fixing things when they release patches - guys its early access, be reasonable with demands
- I have seen what this game looks like on high spec rig, can't wait to upgrade mine; and no i wouldnt want this game to run on anything less - because that would take the pretty aspects of it away - lets move forward guys, not backwards in graphics, its 2016 for crist sake!
Cons:
- Loading times can be painful especially single player
- To get more enjoyment out of the game you need to look for a private server, but that doesnt guarantee there are nice people on it (griefing is typically an issue when you join as a randomer) However once you find one thats decent, all is good :)
- There are still dozens of small but annoying little bugs - getting stuck on doors/ doorways, terrain, etc.
- A lot of people complain about terrible performance on high end gpu's etc, i haven't a clue what that is about because i'm fine on my toaster...Granted, low and some medium settings all round, decresed grass etc and some settings are disabled, but hell, fps is fine, i dont lag, and i only crash when my gpu is choking. Buyt thats to be expected from something thats 6 years old and needs to get on with times and progress. I would quesation what they think is a high end gpu/ rig and whether their rig build is stable in the first place.
The cons, overall are negligent to me. and i highly recommend this game, if the little cons are not your cup of tea, i would highly recommned waiting for the full release and giving this game a shot.  This game can suit those into pvp and those who want to avoid that aspect as well. Personally i prefer pve, but on servers you can also set to have pvp just over the weekend and weekdays is just pve, which for me made all the difference and it was fair and peacefull overall.
As a final note, give this game a chance, and think of all those horrendous final releases with disgraceful issues that were out from EA for example - this is still an early release and it is still far more stable than anything else usually released at this level.

Hello (this is my first review ever, so no hate)
I played this game a lot, back when it was fresh out of  closed beta.
And it is one thing... time consuming. At first like in every other game you have nothing but your starter gear, you get familiar with the game (before it becomes overly complicated) and start grinding (or leveling at the beginning). It is more fun to play in a clan rather than alone, and so i joined a clan and indeed it was fun, we played alot togheter and farmed for the clan building and research. Farmed warframe parts, everything. I still didn't realized at that point that you grind for gear that you use to grind for other gear (kinda stupid but as long as a game entertains you that's not a big concern). I spent mony on that  game (around 200 bucks) bought myself warframe slots to store them, they felt like thropies. There is no pay to win (especially now that you trade with platinum). But someday you reach the point where you are faster then the updates. You leveled all your gear and forma'ed (making them even stronger then) everything seven times. Your dojo (clan building) is at max and you have every mod. Next Update Prime weapons and warframes appear, you farm one day and get the parts in 3 to 5 runs (exept Loki and maybe Rhino Prime). Sell the normal ones, lvl the Primes up forma them (and by lvling i mean you go to kiste/kappa/sedna mobile defense and destroy endless waves of enemies in a set amout of time and after one run you might be already lvl 24 (cap is 30)). New Update total overhaul, new mechanics and more bugs than you would have ever imagined. Half of the builds you made until that point are useless or nerfed to the ground (research weapon acrid where you have to spend a hand of formas on now weaker than the starter pistol, trinity blessing duration = god mod now usless 'cuz new mechanics) your efforts are now for short pointless. They fix it all up (not the builds, they stay nerfed) and that's not bad but the new mechanics where you shoot burning bullets and they have 'a chance' to inflame them kinda made me sad worked around that got decent builds up again. New frames arrive... total disappointment, a little bit new but as long as they or their attacks are not equal or better (crowd control, tank, buffs and dps) they are worthless or more of a side gag. They introduce some more mechanics pvp, alien dogs, more void lvls, some clan stuff and thats it, in less than a week you have everything, if not somewhere you can always find it for plat.
It's not bad, it's fun to play it has nice graphics but if you look in to the distance you are doing nothing than repeating (and it's really sad when nerfrage hits your stuff). You don't even have to do much stratagy on bosses only on endless defense and survival etc.)
If you really like repetitive gameplay/leveldesign/grinding that's the game for you.

Warframe is a surprisingly addicting co-op third person shooter, and spiritual successor, if not sequel to Dark Sector, with a fair enough F2P business model and entertaining, satisfying, fast paced combat. It is still in active development, new content gets released at a reasonable rate, and hotfixes for issues come out blazingly fast.
In Warframe, you play as one of the legendary Tenno, a race of posthuman "space ninjas" dedicated to balancing and drawing out a war between the oppressive and xenophobic Grineer empire, and the Corpus, a collective of traders and engineers. You're sent to do various missions across the solar system, ensuring not one faction gains the upper hand. The story, unfortunately, is the game's greatest weakness. What's there is well written and has a host of great, memorable characters; for example, the exuberant Vay Hek, one of the most influential Grineer, who doesn't just chew the scenery whenever he appears; he DEVOURS it. Or the brilliant, yet cowardly Alad V, who has a vested interest in researching and experimenting on Tenno like you, but is a
diplomat.
In spite of this however, much of the story is not told very well through the game, a problem this game and Destiny share. While you get a decent enough amount of story through Inbox messages and through transmissions during the story missions (which are entitled Quests in your ship's navigation), and reading into it gives off an extreme Metal Gear Solid vibe, much of the story you'll need to know is only properly told in depth on the official wikia, and there are a few notable missions with a decent chunk of story that you just cannot do anymore (Tethra's Doom and Eyes of Blight are just examples, you can see them all on the wikia's Events page). The story doesn't have much of a linear narrative at all due to the mission structure, as well. While the quests make sense, you can kill the main villain of the Natah quest, Tyl Regor, before completing it. Things like this lead to a story that feels somewhat disjointed and patchwork.
The other game's main issue, while not nearly as bad, is the F2P model. Most of the things you can buy through the Market, you can create through the Foundry for free. However, doing so requires Monster Hunter levels of grinding. It's not as bad as a Korean MMO, but it does require some patience and dedication. Speaking of patience though, the model's biggest problem is it's timewalls. Creating things in the Foundry takes enough time to make mobile games blush, and the times can be inconsistent as well. Some weapons take 12 hours to make, others take 24. The worst offender by far are the Warframes, which require 3 parts to make, each having a 12 hour wait time, and even once you get all the parts, you have to wait THREE DAYS (exactly 72 hours) in order to actually combine the parts and get the Warframe. Thankfully, you can build more than one part in the Foundry.
There is also a good chunk of weapons and 'frames that you can only make if you're in a clan, which requires you to make a Clan Key (which also takes 12 hours :I) in order to access it's Dojo (basically a social hub for your clan) and acquire the blueprints. It is by far the worst part of Warframe, ignoring the problems with the story. The grind is good enough to pad out the gameplay, and yet, DE felt the need to do this for whatever reason. You can rush foundry crafting via Platinum, the game's premium currency, but you have to pay for that. No, it's nowhere near as bad as an outright paywall, but it's still annoying having to wait so long for a new toy. Finally, while you can still just craft everything you need instead of buying it (as such there is no real P2W), there are a few cosmetic items you unfortunately are locked into having to buy. The most egregious of which is the full Classic color palette. Without buying it, you get a paultry amount of colors, unable to color your items anything other than a shade of, for example, overly saturated green or vibrant♥♥♥♥♥♥yellow.
Other than these issues, the game is excellent in most other areas.
Visually, the game is incredible and impressively well-optimized for a small-ish independent developer, and Digital Extremes deserves all the credit in the world for them. I have cranked every option in the game up to the maximum, and rarely ever drop below 60 (only cases are sometimes in the Void due to the amount of enemies and reflective surfaces, and consistently in a Relay, due to the amount of players) on a fairly common mid-high end machine. The art style is fantastic, clearly taking inspiration from Japanese sci-fi and even a bit of Metroid Prime. Aside from a few questionable aspects (like the camera never holding still even when completely idle, or a few weapons being held incorrectly), the game is delicious eye candy.
In terms of audio, the music is...okay. It's not awful, but it's not memorable, either. It's standard cinematic fare, made with things like Damage, Evolve, Aeon, etc. without much melody or personality. There isn't really a single track in the game that stands out, or gets stuck in your head. The game could benefit from a Music 2.0. However, it shines in the SFX department. Many weapons have an incredibly satisfying feel to them. And, of course, the voice acting for the most part is fantastic.
Gameplay wise, it's incredibly fast paced, incredibly addicting and incredibly fun. There is a huge collection of primary, secondary and melee weapons, many of which having a fun gimmick to them. These include guns like the Opticor (Warframe's very own Spartan Laser), the Redeemer (a double-bladed longsword that doubles as an incredibly powerful shotgun), and the Amprex (a Quake-style Lightning Gun that chains to other nearby enemies). There are 13 different damage types, not including random critical hits (which interestingly enough, exist alongside headshots) and red crits (a critical hit that can only occur after your weapon's critical chance has reached 100% and above), 6 of them being made by combining 2 of the 4 base elements (Cold, Electric, Heat and Toxin).
Weapons and 'frames are upgraded via mods. Mods are random drops that give you stat buffs and sometimes special effects. You can fuse mods together to improve their stats, turning a 12%+ rate of fire buff eventually into a 72%+ buff. There are an estimated 605 mods too, so you have an incredible selection to choose from to make your gun perform exactly how you want it to. At first, the melee is a button mashing simulator, but you can increase your versatility by finding Stance mods, which alter your weapon's attacks and gives you the ability to perform combos with more than one button. There is, again, a pretty hefty selection of planets and missions to choose from, like a Domination-esque mission or a simple "kill everything" mission. You're able to do an impressive amount of parkour, being able to jump up and across walls, roll at incredible speeds through the air, and do an obligatory double jump. Getting the hang of the movement, and training your aim to compensate for your speed, is key to being successful at the combat in Warframe.
Finally, as a small side note, solo play is okay. You don't get any second wind mechanic (if you die in solo you'll be forced to use one of your 'frame's 4 revives, or abort the mission and keep your revive), but you won't be overly penalized for playing more "casual" difficulties.
Steam doesn't have a high enough character limit for in-depth reviews, so I'll end it with this. Warframe, in spite of it's problems, is an excellent F2P title that puts most others to shame. It includes fantastic gameplay, surprisingly memorable characters, AAA level visuals and an almost overwhelming amount of content, even having a PVP mode (which I have not tried and have no interest in right now, so I can't cover it).
And hey, it's free, so there's no harm in trying, right?

This has become one of my favorite F2P games in the past few months I have been playing this on Xbox One. There is a great community, it has great gameplay, and unlike most F2P games, it's not pay to win. You can use cash to get early access to prime items or buy platinum, a secondary currency. However, with patience, you can get virtually anything you can buy with platinum or with prime access (excluding cosmetics, rushed builds, or extra inventory slots for Warframes, weapons or sentinels, but you can live without them). An alternative method for getting platinum is trading rare items to other players in exchange for platinum, meaning you don't even need to spend money on this game to get what you want. You even start off with about 50 platinum. This game has a number of features, including PvP combat in the Conclave, factions, the ability to fight in the vacuum of space with Archwings, and even underwater combat with Archwings thanks to the most recent update: Echoes of the Sentient. New content is always added with each major update, such as Warframes and PvP maps for the Conclave.

Recommended, because:
It's very fun and very player friendly, It contains parkour and a little bit fighting. However, I dislike it that it doesn't have custom missions, By custom missions I mean making custom missions for this game. It will be fun by selecting the maps and doing parkour with it.

There are a few system requirements that ARK doesn't tell you about before hand. Firstly you need infinate free time and willing to get involved in the game. Secondly you ideally need a crew of really good mates who also have infinate free time at their disposal. Thirdly, you need some sort of experimental future master-race machine that doesn't exist yet, as to be honest the game has never really worked very well in terms of performance. Turn the graphics up and it's a clunky mess, even on seriously OP computers. Turn the graphics down and it's a fairly functional pixelated chunky mess. Lots of things have been promised now long ago (DX12, further decent optimisation, etc) and not delivered upon, and for a game with so much promise that is frustrating.
I don't want to be completely negetive as I have had a good amount of fun in ARK. It's one of the most involving co-op experiences i've ever wound up getting sucked into. You and your clan will spend so much time building up infrastructure and a comprehensive garage full of dinos that when these things come under attack from other groups it can feel like a genuinely threatening experience. It has the ability to really get your heart racing. Unfortunately when you actually have to engage in combat, even when you're fully tooled up, the game is too clunky for the combat to be as rewarding an experience as it should be.
I often wonder whether this game is simply too ambitious for the unreal engine 4 technology it's been built on. There are a tonne of games running UE4 on Steam and other platforms, and for the most part they all look and run beautifully - perhaps the sheer scope of what happens on the huge 80 player maps in ARK is just a bit much for what the engine has been designed to deliver. If they are able to improve the way the game runs fairly dramatically at some point I will eat my hat so to speak and alter this review. The game feels like it could be so much more than it is with a bit of fine tuning, but the fine tuning never seems to come.

My Review:
Pros:
- Lots of customization
- Plenty of Warframes with unique abilities to choose from
- Lots of weapons that all seem unique in their own way
- A progression system that doesn't feel like such a slow grind
(As far as obtaining most materials, or leveling weapons and warframes)
- Helpful/Friendly community
- Fun movement mechanics
- Intense combat
- Space Ninjas
Cons:
- Doesn't really do a good job of directing you to obtainable goals/what you should be doing to progress in the game (You just kinda have to wing it and figure stuff out as you go)
- Having to wait long periods of time to craft something
- Platinum to dollar ratio is inflated
(You have to spend big to get anything good from the marketplace)
- Alert Missions not paying out what they say they would upon completion
(Which can be frustrating when you were getting something you really wanted/needed for completing it)
Overall, I enjoyed the game even with all of the negative things I noticed about it. As far as FTP goes, it's one of the best out there.
Plus, it's based in the Dark Sector universe. Which is freaking awesome.
(I know they've never officially confirmed it, but come on. Even if it's not based in the exact universe, there are so many nods towards their older game that it's rediculous.)
If you're looking for a free game to play, give it a try. It can be played without paying any money pretty easily. It just takes longer to do anything. Plus if you supplement this game with a little cash every once in a while, it's very enjoyable.

Let's start, this is an awesome game, that has to be said
However there are few points I must to raise, first the good ones.
It's a complete survival game with no "boring periods", you'll always have something new to do, some new dino to tame and some new building/thing to craft to continue the game progress.
It have a large amount of different dinos and gamestyles for you to follow, depending on your objective you'll have a different gamming experience basically
It's beautiful if you have a good computer, amazing graphics, even sometimes a little cartoon-style, it's really good to see.
Now the bad points
It's heavy as hell, you'll need a good machine to run this with no trouble on your fps and with a decent graphics, also, this game have a RIDICULOUS objective timming, forcing you to be hours or even more than a day or weeks, with no break time to do somethings such as tamming and breeding.
It also have MANY MANY....MAAAAANY bugs:
-buildings and items flying on the sky, even trees,
-when you die, there is a chance your loot will simply desapear or be eaten by something (which should not happen).
-when falling down from a flying dino, there is a chance you'll enter in the ground and have no further access to your loot.
-some features have been wrongly implemented, like some 'beacons', which is basically a loot falling from the sky, that in some cases, there is no way to access is because it have a fixed spawn point inside a rock
-your flying dinos sometimes simply fly over the sky and disapear (to tame a dino you'll waste a couple of hours, not to mention breeded ones)
-devs DO NOT ANSWER tickets, there is a terrible feedback service
-those dinos are dumb as ♥♥♥♥, I see simply games such as "Don't Starve" with enemies or allies walking over obstacles to reach your position, in ark, if you have a huge dino such as giganotossaurus and there is a small tree or a little dino in his front, like a dodo (literally is the size of his nail) it will be trapped and you'll need to walk him around manually or kill it (it happens to all dinos, flying, ground or water, no artificial intelligence was implemented, they'll follow you over a straight line, if there is something on the way, they'll be trapped)
-when you drop something it will be kicking on the ground, EVERYTIME.
-in rare cases, some agressive dinos may become invisible and you'll die for them.
-devs are constantly trying to make the game harder in stupid ways like: dinos can't be trapped anymore, you can no longer kill alphas by drowning them, dinos can't be used together to gather resources....and so on...with these things you'll end up with alpha rex/carno/raptors not drowning in the midle of the ocean, sinking and 'imune' to your damages as they are not on their habitat, you'll have huge carnivores running away from you because you 'faked' a trap over them by simply walking behind a rock, even if you climb a rock, the dino will be looking for you for a couple of seconds and then will run away in fear, it is stupid to lure something to tame on a better place as within some minutes or even seconds, it will be running in fear, by simply following you and not able to bite you (seems that according to the devs, it's against the game rules to make traps or use your intelligence and your environment to overcome some dino, of course, humans always won everything by fists and not by tools and thinking in better solutions, make so much sense..........right?!)
not to mention more complex bugs like, tribe alliances sometimes ends up with someone losing his tribe and everything he had because the game does not reconize him as his tribe anymore
and of course!....devs rather launch new dlcs instead of fix those bugs.
In resume, I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS GAME, but, if you think all those bugs and bad things mentioned above are not a problem, is a good game.

Warframe, how you surprised and impressed me ! Blistering fast and complex combat and exploration all rendered in eye-bleedingly awesome GFX.  And under the hood, a deep and challenging first person combat game with tons of customisable classes to enjoy in PVE and PVP modes.  Fluid in-match looting combined with an involving crafting system is how you level up your character through mechanical/technological/magical enhancements to turn your base bodily "Frame" into a warmachine fine-tuned to your liking.  Trade your cyborg organs and other crafting materials on the black market in-game, and link your character to your Steam account so you can sell off  any common surplus or especially valuable items on the Steam Economy.  And all this happening within the framework of an immersive and challenging universe with a growing body of lore.   Warframe impressed this cynical old gamer, reminds me of a game called "Too Human".   Best enjoyed co-op with a buddy, running PVE missions with just the two of you.

I have played Ark for over 1000 hours now, and I have (more or less) enjoyed every single one. Ark is one of the most unique games I have ever seen and the sheer enormity of content truly makes anything possible. You can do just about anything, from fighting on the back of a Tyrannosaur with plasma cannons mounted on it's head to building a medieval municipality that has it's own player-run economy.
There is so much potential in this game, and the way it can be adapted to suit every individual's playstyle makes it that much better. Due to the size of the game and the fact that Studio Wildcard has crammed so much content into a dynamic worldspace, the optimisation has it's limits. There will always be people complaining about bugs and glitches which have affected their games, but that is no reason to ignore just how much this game has to offer.
If you're not sure about whether to buy this game or not, wait until it goes on sale. The high sale price reflects the size of the game and it's limitless possibilites, and I don't think it is that unreasonable considering the amount of time you can spend playing this.

I played a lot of early-access-surival games. I consider them all to be borderline-scam: Lots of bugs, hackers, horrible balance of gameplay elements, vast lack of content. While most of these games can be enjoyed, playing them is still suffering and a lot of people hate them and stay away from them after being burned.
Ark is certainly different. First, Ark actually offers content. PvE in Ark is so rich that people play for months with only very occasional PvP breaking out even on the official servers with zero admin oversight.
A part of that is certainly that Ark actually offers a system to level up your character, assigning stats like health, damage etc and learning a tech tree of crafting recipes, but also the vast amount of dinosaurs to tame and the difficulty to get ressources.
Getting ressources is pretty easy, if you know where to find them and how to mine them. Safely getting there and back alive is a different story.
Thus, Ark is quite grindy - but doesn't really feel that way. I don't find myself doing the same thing for a long time in a row. You need wood you get wood in 2 Minutes. You get wood. You craft something. You need certain dinosaur eggs. You scout for 20 minutes to find one, tame it, and then stare at it yelling to make it lay eggs. It feels engaging.
Everything is server sided. 100%. And the netcode isn't good. If you open a door, try to walk thru, and then the server decides you didn't actually walk thru it properly, you teleport back. 20 times in a row. Glitching is hard to impossible i guess, but it makes a lot of things really tiresome.
Combat is borderline impossible. If the server has a bad day, you will randomly teleport around. Being hit, blocking, or hitting the enemy aren't things you have really control over or even notice. Sometimes you swing your weapon, apparently hit nothing but still something will die as a cause.
Same goes for inventories. Also 100% server sided. I guess Ark is quite hack proof (i have heard of hacks, but haven't seen hackers in 240 hours of gameplay) but it comes at a price, performance is really choppy.
Since these choices in engine design are very fundamental (engine devs who do not include this from the start will never do it) i doubt there will ever be vast improvements getting rid of these problems. They might become less obvious, but will always lure in the background.
There are also FPS drops to ~5 FPS which last anywhere from 5-30 seconds, even on powerful computers. The game will also eat up 16GB of ram and then crash due to the lack of ram - indicating problems with memory leakage. Occasionally the game will crash entirely, freezing your pc requiring a hard reset. I thought this was an issue with my pc hardware, until friends of mine had the exact same issue on different hardware.
On top of that, the game will download large amounts of data over steam without steam actually showing any data being downloaded. Patches come often, sometimes 4 patches a week with 1-2gb total size, so beware if your internet is low bandwith or actually volume limited.
Graphics look really good, the game can make use of even the fastest GPUs, but also runs well on really old and slow hardware if you switch off the fancy graphics. It isn't CPU heavy as well, even old AMD cpus can run it just fine.
PvP balance. Doesn't exist. Alpha tribes who establish themselves on the server, rule the server. You can annoy the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of them if you're a guerilla warfare expert, but they can crush you with ease any time you try to build up something.
Groups of people engage in server hopping: They hop on a server (with a fully skilled, leveled and geared up character with a high level dino) and then they raid the whole server. Every single base will be blown up, raided. And then they♥♥♥♥♥♥off and you'll never see them again, because they switch to another server. Alpha tribes with hundreds of defense turrets are quite save against that, but it takes months to build up to that point in Ark - and what you build up is easily crushed. If you succeed or not is quite random and depends on the actions of other players. Hiding is quite impossible, the map is too small for that and quickly traveled as a high level player.
Even worse, there is quite evil mechanics in the game: You can tranquilize a player with long range weapons, keep him unconcious with medicine, keep him fed, and handcuff him. People build dedicated, climatised prisons to keep people locked up indefinately - for fun.
The enviroment in Ark is also harsh, it certainly wants you dead. You starve quick. You die of thirst quick. You freeze to death quick. Dinosaurs eat you really ♥♥♥♥ing quick. Even once you have a base and think you're safe: Some large alpha beast will come and shred it. Got a metal base with defense turrets and think you're really save now? Titanosaur will spawn and stomp it to the ground like an anthill. Harsh.
Since the game has a lot of possibilities quite like a sandbox, a lot of weird♥♥♥♥♥♥can be done. Collision detection is rudementary, so you can put a long pole with C4 on a boat, drive it into someone elses other boat or base, and detonate the C4 which glitched inside the other base. Dinosaurs will glitch half way thru walls and can then attack whatever is on the other side.
The center point of an object can never pass thru a wall, but whatever sticks out long enough in any direction of an object (dino, player, boat) can easily.
This will also lead to you getting stuck in terrain, glitching under the map and ofc loosing items to that. My paranoia has me carrying a crossbow with grappling hook and a bird dinosaur following me in case i need a ride to get out of a ditch where ever i think the terrain builder did a sloppy job.
Currently the game heavily favors attackers over defenders. While building defense turrets is quite easy and they are strong - it is also easy to get around them with weird game mechanics. If you like to have a safe base - wrong game for you. If you like to go around raid people in ninja fashion with server hopping - great game for you i guess.
When your game crashes, or when you loose the connection to the server, you often end up dead. In a driving boat, you will drown. Flying over the ocean? You'll drown. Flying over a dangerous area? (which is most areas) - say goodbye to your♥♥♥♥♥♥ And don't think it happens rarely.
Ark has potential, but it also has a lot of problems that need to be worked on to make it a more enjoyable experience. I also didn't see any acknowledgement of the developers towards these problems, so i doubt they will be fixed at all.
tl;dr
The best early access survival♥♥♥♥♥♥game disappointment so far! Only recommended if you're a genre addict.

Warframe is a free-to-play, third-person, action shooter.
First off, I want to say that this game has one of the best monetization schemes I've ever seen in a F2P game -- where other games build their systems around getting players to spend money on stuff, and make letting players earn items by investing their time in the game be this difficult thing, Warframe feels like it was built with time investments as the primary expectation, and spending money second.
That is to say, a good 90% of the game's weapons, characters, and cosmetics can be earned and crafted without spending any money on the game, but spending money does allow one to gain access to them faster. The only things a player cannot earn are weapon and character slots, but these are reasonably priced.
Ostensibly, a player could even buy these slots without buying any of the game's premium currency because, at the moment, all trading can only be done for certain types of items (rare, high-end/late-game items and mods that cannot be bought from the premium store), and you cannot trade for credits, only premium currency. So one could earn a few of these items, sell them to other players, and use that premium currency to unlock more slots without spending a dime of their own money.
The game itself is fairly simple. There's a story, but it's in the background and really vague. You just go into missions, of which there are a variety of types and kill bad guys to get experience for you gear and character, materials to build new gear and characters, and mods to upgrade your gear and characters. You can play solo, but the game's scaling is generally geared towards multiple players. Matchmaking is easy and fluid (usually).
The way the game times the building of gear and characters combined with the rate at which you find the parts you need to build them means that once you get rolling, you can almost always have something new waiting to be leveled up, so there's a fairly constant sense of progression and growth, plus the fun of experimenting and figuring out the intricacies and tactical roles of each weapon and/or character.
There are a lot of bugs, some more significant than others, but the developer is constantly working to fix stuff. But their priorities are sometimes very different than their playerbase's.
All in all, I'd call it a 6/10 game. Nothing mind-blowingly awesome, but fun enough to sink time into, and an easy game to play when you want to kind of veg out, not worry about missing some critical plot point or something, if that makes any sense.

Taming dinosaurs takes upwards of 8 of continuous time. If you look away from the screen for more than 2 minutes, you will die. If you stop taming, you must start over. Pros:
+ Outstanding graphics
+ Crafting, sense of achievement

Con:

I'd definitely reccomend buying this game.

ARK is a great idea! a big island filled with dinosaurs, you try to figure out what to do next only using your survival instinct, building tribes and bases, taming and riding dinos. it all sounds perfect to any gamer regardless of what genre they like! But they executed the idea poorly.
Why did I give this game a negative review? because people who are reading this may be considering a purchase. And I'm going to tell you why you shouldn't buy it because the game will not give you a fun time as a new player.
So you liked the dino survival game idea and you purchased the game, you start playing it and the first thing is to choose a server, you might try the game offline for some time to grasp the concept or practice the basics, then you jump into a, let's say pvp server, you start chopping wood and stuff and try to craft your first items and food, then all of a sudden BAM you're dead, a high lvl player one shots you. You try again and again and again but you will be killed every time. So you tell yourself that maybe I should start with a pve server, so you join a pve server and start chopping again, you want to place your first foundation to build your home but you realize you can't because there is a pillar nearby built by another player! Ok no problem I will build my home somewhere else! You run and you run and you run and yoouuu ruuuuuun! Oh God it's like the whole map is occupied by pillars!! I can't even build a stupid 4x4 house! Then you think, ok this game is a multiplayer game, maybe I should join one of these tribes! You try to be friendly and ask nicely if someone is willing to invite you to their tribe, but no they don't want new players in their tribes, even if they do, they've built such a small base that you can't even bring a dodo to it. Then you say ok! I should bring my own friends to the game and start in a pvp server and lvl up really quick, but again bang bang bang, a pack of high lvl farmers killed you because you were farming in their spot! ... so ok guys let's go back to pve but this time pick a low population server so we can actually build a base for ourselves. Finally after wasting 20 hours trying to figure out where to even start! You realize that even as a 5 man tribe you need atleast 1 month of 6 hour/day grind to build an acceptable base (still not high-end), and it was impossible in a pvp server, you need to zerg it if you want to survive in a pvp server, like I don't know, maybe 20 people.
So my suggestion to the developers, if they are going to release this game and not just being a money-grabber machine that stays in early-access for 10 years, is to try to figure out a way to make it easier for new players to enjoy the game.
Right now, if you want to start the game solo, it's absolutely impossible to do anything in the game (except maybe masturbating in your hut on your private HOSTED server). To do this :
you can divide the leveling area and the high-end area of the map, this way any new player that enters a server will only see low lvl players like themselves, many mmo games out there use different areas for different game modes, for example you can make one big area a pvp zone and a tribe who takes a certain point of the map can be king of the island for the rest of the week and the winning tribe members can benefit from its bonuses. all sorts of pvp action can happen in that zone. You can see how beautiful pvp is in Elder Scrolls Online, cause players are constantly trying to capture an enemy keep or taking them back. these days all game companies are trying to put a big gap between high lvl players and new or low lvl players in their games, because getting killed by a high lvl player for no reason is just frustrating and nothing else.
Also you need to make the process of finding a tribe much more easier for new players, like come on! this game has been in development for years now and still the UI is the same♥♥♥♥♥♥ finding a tribe for a solo player is a nightmare. And even if they do, they will probably end up in a very weak tribe with no chance of surviving. Why should only 1 tribe in each server dominate? this will be also solved by dividing the map for different levels of tribes. The rewards for attacking and looting a tribe in the same area with the same level must be much higher, attacking a low lvl tribe or a low lvl player should yield nothing but shame :-P this way low lvl players can easily focus on building good defenses against other low lvl players instead of just rushing for high-end technologies, players who can join big tribes also have no problem, they will be carried by their tribe members.
So all in all, divide your players on the map by their levels, don't give your high level players a good reason to zerg low lvl players, getting killed by a high lvl player over and over is not enjoyable. So this way new players can join in and progress instead of getting frustrated and give you negative reviews because they couldn't even get past the wooden structures' blueprints.

Ark's a prime example of a misopportunity.  The game has a lot of potential don't get me wrong but it lacks direction.
Graphics:
Going by the trailers the game is visually stunning.  Reality: unless you've got a mammoth computer you're not going to get that, and even then it's not without it's issue.  Visually the trailers don't represent what you'll see from a graphical standpoint, unless you're using Ansel or something.
Some may say "It's still early access", but that doesn't fly anymore with the developers releasing paid DLC.  Sorry devs but if you've got time for DLC you've got time to optimize.
Gameplay:
The only time I really felt this was a survival game was on the first day I played and that's because I was still learning the mechanics of the game.  Ark has no tutorial.  Once you know to punch trees, farm dodos or jerboa for meat etc you're usually away laughing unless you continually run into a dinosaur that will just pull your childhood memories out through your ears.
Dinosaurs hit trees and cliffs and will constantly get stuck, which can be sometimes the only way you can tame.  Or, while they're fleeing from you they can go right off a cliff or run into dinosaurs that want use their bones to pick their teeth with.  Dinosaurs flee when they get in trouble but usually into ways that an animal wouldn't go.
The building mechanic is a hit and miss, it's can be a iffy - a lot of the time - to place items, can literally come down to the angle you're looking at.  People have made some beautiful buildings, and mods really enhance the flavour but this is usually done to fix things the developers won't or can't.
Online Play:
"Please, Sir, can I please play the game I paid to play?"  - a lot of servers are plagued by Alpha tribes who can literally control when and where you can play.  And if you don't do what they like... well, you get steam rolled, son.
Local play
There is no real single player in the usual sense: no campaign, quests or anything.  No NPC to augment a virtual tribe to tackle limitations.  Just you on the map unable to do boss content.
Bugs that shouldn't still be there
Don't even get me started on the amount of times I've gotten stuck in the floor of my building, or doorway or just plain fallen through stuff.  Or you're dead body just disappears before the despawn timer.  "But it's still early access"... "if you've got time for DLC you've got time to optimize.".
Personally, I'm taking a break from Ark.  Hopefully the developers will address issues, add more substantial content (as their early access notes suggest), maybe there'll be an actual single player (not just the local solo play we have now).  Who knows.  Be watching ya, Ark.

Alright, after reading all the negative and positive reviews, I've decided to add my own. First off, if you're wondering wether or not you'd be interested in this game, DON'T listen to all the negative reviews talking about the new paid DLC. It's unfair based on the state of the game (which is better than most games you can find that are fully realeased). Plus, you shouldn't worry about the DLC if you don't even have the game yet.
ARK is an early access game, meaning bugs are present. A lot of people are writing negative reviews because of a bug that annoyed them, which is unfair to the developers who are trying their best to keep the game functioning. Unlike other games where the developers aren't too active, or don't fix glitches often enough, the makers of ARK are constantly adding new dinosaurs while trying to fix glitches (such as the health bar glitch). As I said, bugs are present, but there are no major issues. Imo, ARK is an extremely fun game with rich content that can (and will if you let it) amuse you for hours.
Another thing I'm going to bring up before I get into the main stuff is my first experience with the game. No, I'm not one of those OG players, and haven't played for 1k+ hours like a lot of people I know. My introduction to ARK came from a YouTuber I watched (Vikkstar123). He and his friends were playing on a personal server, learning about the game together and getting to the endgame stuff. Although it was painful to watch for more experienced players, I was mezmorized by the idea of a dinosaur survival game as good-looking as this one. Eventually I did get the game, and was thankfully able to run it on my Mac (thanks for not being Windows only game like SOME games...). The only problem was I was using defalt settings. This means it would take forever to level things up, gather recources, and tame dinosaurs (the main point of the game imo). That would be my first recommendation-- turn up the taming, gathering, and xp rates. I eventually tamed my first dinosaur (which was a dinosaur I DEFINITELY shouldn't have gotten as my first), a Pachy, which I loved because it looked like a fossil Pokemon. Although when I did manage to tame it, it ended up dying within about five minutes of me having it to a couple of dinos. As this was my very first tame, I was heartbroken to have lost it so soon. I ended up putting off ARK for a while until I came back and gave it another go. Moral: turn rates up + tame dinos you're supposed to tame.
Now, back to what you want. Some things about the game you need to know if you're considering buying. You'll most likely end up spending time on servers, connecting with other users who love to play like you do. If you're into the idea of having PvP with dinosaurs and tribes (which does sound awesome), you should probably give that up. Unless you have almost no life, or 20-30 people to join your tribe, the idea of PvP should be out of your head. There will always be that alpha tribe who loves to level your base or kill your dinosaurs you worked for for fun. You'll be offline raided, online raided, or taunted. I'm not saying you shouldn't give it a go, I'm saying prepare to lose a lot of dinos and work along the way. However, for the more solo players, PvE servers can be amazing. I love PvE, especially on the server I play on (which has nice Admins). It's probably my favorite part of ARK other than the mods. The last type of server is official. This has the normal rates for everything, and if anything is lost to a glitch or bug, it will NOT be replaced. I honestly do NOT reccomend official to those who don't have hours on end to play this game. As I said with PvP, give it a try. You may like it better than I do.
The very last thing I'm talking about in length is the mods you can get. These are the player-created addons to the game which can make your experience more challenging, more fun, or just make some things a LOT easier. Some I'd reccomend are Structures Plus, where if you place something down you can pick it up again instead of having to destroy it, Recource Stacker, where you can hold a lot more of an object in a stack (meaning things like berries or meats will spoil less), and Annuaki Genesis, where there's TONS more to do including taming boss creatures, alphas, and posion/fire/earth/ice dinosaurs (not reccomended to beginers).
Looking back, I may have ranted a bit on this review, but I still hope it helps you. Here's a recap:
PROS:
- Great graphics
- Active and friendly Devs
- Rich content
- Lots and lots of dinosaurs that all have their own use
- Fantastic survival game
- Very customizable servers
- Massive tribes can enjoy the aspect of PvP
CONS:
- PvP is really not a choice for small tribes / solo players
- A lot of minor bugs that take a while to fix
- Too little focus on early game content (more on end game)
- Bad building system (mods like Structures Plus can fix this)
- No "creative" mode for Mods / Admins of servers (or even singleplayer)
- No stealth system (hiding from dinos)
- No dino pathing (they always seem to run into rocks or walls or get stuck in trees)
I do reccomend this game though. If you can get over the fact that once in a while you're gonna run into a bug or crash, then I highly urge you to buy the game. It's my all-time favorite and I hope it can maybe become one of yours :)

Okay, so this will be a long review, you ready? Got your popcorn? No? WELL TOO BAD IM STARTING ANYWAY.
So you start out with the Lotus, a lady who tells you to run and use your first ability, in my case, slash and dash, to kill your enemies. Around a minute later, You're given a choice. I believe its MK1 Bo staff or MK1 Skana. I chose skana personally. After killing more enemies, your given another choice. MK1 Kunai, or MK1 i forgot what it is, I chose kunai. Then your given your final choice for the mission, Primary weapon. I believe its MK1 Braton or MK1 Paris. paris being a bow and braton being a machine gun. I chose paris. So, in this game, you can rush through the entire level, do it however fast you want to, or you can stay, get loot, get mods, and really customize to your playstyle. Personally, i like stealth. So i eventually got the warframe Loki, whose abilities are, Decoy, Invisibility, Decoy explosion, and Radial disarm. There are many warframes, a new one being recently introduced, Atlas, who can read minds i believe. Now, to the point, this game is an absolute grindfest. Everone calls it P2W because of high platinuim *The premium currency* prices. Thats to put up a grindwall. They dont want you taking the easy way out.There are people with 3000+ Hours in this game that are barely halfway through getting a prime warframe. So, you may be thinking, "How duz me get muteeruels fur diss" Thats how you all sound obviously, but you can purchase blueprints in the market for credits, the money earned ingame. Platinuim is used to buy the component itself. Say you wanted a dual skana blueprint or something, you would need X amount of resources, that you get from each planet. Each planet gives its own resources, like earth, has rubedo, and mars, has something else. Anyway, onto the main factions in the game. The five main factions so far are the Grineer, the Corpus, the infected, the Orokin, and the Tenno, you are the tenno, You are the operator, ordis- sorry i got lost there. But you have this dude in your ship named ordis. Every so often he'll say funny things, like "Oh dear! The operator has come back with an archwing part! You must forge it immediately, Soon you'll be flying through the skies like a *Voice gets much deeper* WINGED DEATH MACHINE". Anyway  back to the factions, The orokin are the more advanced faction.They have these things called death cubes there, that shoot lasers that kill both them and you extremely fast, making it very useful. The grineer are the starters, Fairly easy. Nothing special about them. The corpus hold a lot of loot, and have tougher enemies. Like MOAs, for instance. These are robotic chicken like guys with machine guns. Onto the Infected, A failed lab experiment of the grineer, the infected are now insanely powerful, being leapers, chargers, and ancients. Ancients can grab you and pull you along with them, which is scary stuff. Onto the gamemodes, Ill only be listing 3 to save time, but theres the exterminate, where you kill everything on the ship, the survival, your air supply is cut off and you have to run around and get capsules to stay alive, whilst being shot, and defense, where you defend a certain item/artifact. Actually, theres 2 more I wanted to list, the crossfire, where you board a ship full of fighting grineer and corpus, and kill them all. I dont remember what the last one is called, but you take the side of a faction, like corpus, and they become teammates as you clear out infected or grineer. Thats all for now, updates WILL be coming, this game is still developing, fast, and insanely fun, this game is a Ninja grindfest with a lot to do.

This would be a great game if it didn't have so many bugs and N64 style problems. You can say "oh well, it's in Early Access" but let's face it, these days "Early Access" just means "we wont bother fixing bugs, and the game may never see an official release so we can continue ignoring the problems". There are bugs that have been in it since it's release date a year and a half ago. SImple ones like, you can't see your health sometimes. And they already have an expansion pack you can buy for a game that isn't technically released yet. So yeah, this isn't really beta anymore.
Bugs:
1. Can get killed right through walls. N64 style appendages going through walls/doors and damaging you. I just had a dino i spent about 19 hours gathering mats to tame get killed by an Allosaurus that stuck its head straight through the wall and ate him. So you will regularly be set back dozens of hours by this problem alone. Been a problem since release.
2. Can't see your own hp and no indication (screen turns red around the corners normally) of low hp. This happens randomly when you respawn. Been a problem since release.
3. Drowning above water sometimes. If you get exhausted while swimming, even with your head above the water, you will drown.
4. Losing all your stuff when joining a tribe. Occasionally, when you join a tribe, all of your stuff becomes the property of a completely random tribe. I had this happen with a base of mine before. Probably 150 house went into building it and once I joined a tribe, my entire base became owned by a completely random tribe on the server that was known for trolling people. I know about half a dozen other people who had this happen before.
5. Rubberbanding. Yup, even with good latency, you just get rubberbanded really hard occasionally. it's really odd seeing rubberbanding at 30 ms response. Been a problem since release.
6. Dinos getting stuck on walls. Anytime they run, they run in a straight line with no pathfinding algorithm. So they will run head first into trees, walls, rocks, etc and just get stuck. Been a problem since release.
7. Falling through the ground. I fell through the world once and lost all my stuff and a dino i spent numerous hours on. If you log out, your character will fall unconcious but not disappear. If you do this while on the second floor of a building, you may fall right through it. Also, if you make any kind of overhang on your house that is on columns and log out in it, people can loot your body right through the floor, kill you through the floor, and even drag your body through the floor and outside of your base. Been a problem since release.
8. Bad collision detection. You can be spearing an argentavis in its wings over and over and it just takes no damage at all. Yet some other attacks and dinos can hit things that are literally about ten yards away from their body. Been a problem since release.
Cheating in this game is also basically ignored. There was an entire tribe of people using aimbots and exploits on my server that wiped out all the biggest tribes after they had only been on the server for a few days. They remained for several months, no ban. Just trolling the server by blocking the spawns of all the basic resources trying to make the whole server unplayable. The most they ever do is occasionally wipe the servers due to massive duping. My Review:
Pros:
- Lots of customization
- Plenty of Warframes with unique abilities to choose from
- Lots of weapons that all seem unique in their own way
- A progression system that doesn't feel like such a slow grind
(As far as obtaining most materials, or leveling weapons and warframes)
- Helpful/Friendly community
- Fun movement mechanics
- Intense combat
- Space Ninjas
Cons:
- Doesn't really do a good job of directing you to obtainable goals/what you should be doing to progress in the game (You just kinda have to wing it and figure stuff out as you go)
- Having to wait long periods of time to craft something
- Platinum to dollar ratio is inflated
(You have to spend big to get anything good from the marketplace)
- Alert Missions not paying out what they say they would upon completion
(Which can be frustrating when you were getting something you really wanted/needed for completing it)
Overall, I enjoyed the game even with all of the negative things I noticed about it. As far as FTP goes, it's one of the best out there.
Plus, it's based in the Dark Sector universe. Which is freaking awesome.
(I know they've never officially confirmed it, but come on. Even if it's not based in the exact universe, there are so many nods towards their older game that it's rediculous.)
If you're looking for a free game to play, give it a try. It can be played without paying any money pretty easily. It just takes longer to do anything. Plus if you supplement this game with a little cash every once in a while, it's very enjoyable.

Warframe, how you surprised and impressed me ! Blistering fast and complex combat and exploration all rendered in eye-bleedingly awesome GFX.  And under the hood, a deep and challenging first person combat game with tons of customisable classes to enjoy in PVE and PVP modes.  Fluid in-match looting combined with an involving crafting system is how you level up your character through mechanical/technological/magical enhancements to turn your base bodily "Frame" into a warmachine fine-tuned to your liking.  Trade your cyborg organs and other crafting materials on the black market in-game, and link your character to your Steam account so you can sell off  any common surplus or especially valuable items on the Steam Economy.  And all this happening within the framework of an immersive and challenging universe with a growing body of lore.   Warframe impressed this cynical old gamer, reminds me of a game called "Too Human".   Best enjoyed co-op with a buddy, running PVE missions with just the two of you.

For a game that I have spent over 1.8k hours on, it was well worth it. This game however does not appeal to all audiences. It requires patience, effort and cooporation. If you are easily bored, have a low attension span and prefer to go right into the action I suggest moving on to FPS.
IMO I enjoyed Ark with friends (Irl and ones made ingame), there's just something about being in a tribe with loyal tribemates, working together, creating long lasting memories and over coming problems that arrise ingame. I remember when I started Ark, it was 1 week after release and I had an average fps of 10 on lowest graphics. I begged my friend to buy the game, he bought it and we messed around throwing poop at eachother and punching random dinos. Until we decided to join a tribe. We asked on chat if any clans were recruiting and one reply came saying we could join them. We built a mighty base (obviously got raided multiple times) and if it fell, we would rebuild again, with our spirits never falling. Only a few tribe mates remained after a few months however we stayed as a 4 man tribe, cracking jokes, having fun and progressing throughout different servers. Still today I play different types of games with these friends.
Now look where Ark is. I now run Ark at a steady 25-40 fps compared to 10 when released. Many many many new dinos, maps and items have been added, even a second Free to play game (Ark Survival of the Fittest). I recommend this game to the person who likes to work hard and enjoy the outcome, whether that be just finishing off a part of your metal base, taming a new dino or destroying a whole enemy tribe's base ;). In the end it comes down to what your into, if you don't have the patience to wait for a 5 hour tame then don't get this game. I think Ark though is best experienced with friends and tribemates as it a lot more enjoyable, fun and progressive.

For me the game started off great because of the gear system. This system allows frequent modding and testing. With a single set of mods you can improve every weapon and warframe in the game without having to reacquire the mods for each item, letting me experiment without hassle. The number of interesting weapons in the game also makes this experimenting seemingly endless. This one feature is the only positive aspect of the whole game I can come up with.
Lately (end of 2015) the development direction has accelerated down a path of greed. They have been implementing new research and material gathering methods that are atrocious. It is pretty obvious to the whole community that the game developers are just trying to coerce us into buying everything instead of playing for it by making the gameplay even less appealing than it was already. A masterpiece of a game made by amazingly talented people.
Warframe is a MMO-style game that can only be described as MLG Space Ninjas (MLGSN). I have had an immense amount of fun with it so far, and what tops it off is that it can only get better. With constant updates and patches that actually fix things, and with the developers actually listening to the community, you will not have to worry about Warframe becoming  another DayZ.
The reviews on this game are mostly positive, but I feel strongly that the negative reviews may be forgetting a few things. For instance, the game is only repetitive if you make it so. The game in fact encourages you to try everything out, to use new combonations of gear, mods, and weapons to achieve success. The second thing our negative reviewers leave out is that many people forget to have fun while playing this game, and would rather grind in the void than actually take the time to explore many of the planets and to enjoy the beautiful music, environments, and diverse enemy types.
Quite honestly, the only qualms I have with the game is simply stuff they have yet to add (More Archwing missions pretty please :3)  I know the developers will continue listening to feedback and will make this game a haven for all gamers to come... Eventually. Keep up the good work gents ^-^

For a game that I have spent over 1.8k hours on, it was well worth it. This game however does not appeal to all audiences. It requires patience, effort and cooporation. If you are easily bored, have a low attension span and prefer to go right into the action I suggest moving on to FPS.
IMO I enjoyed Ark with friends (Irl and ones made ingame), there's just something about being in a tribe with loyal tribemates, working together, creating long lasting memories and over coming problems that arrise ingame. I remember when I started Ark, it was 1 week after release and I had an average fps of 10 on lowest graphics. I begged my friend to buy the game, he bought it and we messed around throwing poop at eachother and punching random dinos. Until we decided to join a tribe. We asked on chat if any clans were recruiting and one reply came saying we could join them. We built a mighty base (obviously got raided multiple times) and if it fell, we would rebuild again, with our spirits never falling. Only a few tribe mates remained after a few months however we stayed as a 4 man tribe, cracking jokes, having fun and progressing throughout different servers. Still today I play different types of games with these friends.
Now look where Ark is. I now run Ark at a steady 25-40 fps compared to 10 when released. Many many many new dinos, maps and items have been added, even a second Free to play game (Ark Survival of the Fittest). I recommend this game to the person who likes to work hard and enjoy the outcome, whether that be just finishing off a part of your metal base, taming a new dino or destroying a whole enemy tribe's base ;). In the end it comes down to what your into, if you don't have the patience to wait for a 5 hour tame then don't get this game. I think Ark though is best experienced with friends and tribemates as it a lot more enjoyable, fun and progressive.

In the end I really enjoy this game and can't wait for the further updates it will be recieving in the next few weeks.

Because this game is in Early Access, this review is likely to change over time.
ARK: Survival Evolved is an Open World Survival game where you play as a lone individual, male or female, stranded on a mysterious sanctuary known as an Ark.
There are three known Arks: The Island, The Center, and the Scorched Earth.
The Island is a lush tropical paradise overflowing with life of all shapes and sizes.
The Center is a beautiful and mysterious land with floating rocks and treacherous caverns.
The Scorched Earth is a harsh desert where mythical monsters lurk beneath the sands.
As a resident of the Ark, you must explore, fight, and craft your way to the top of the food chain while avoiding and/or commanding the many creatures to become the ultimate survivor.
Although not implemented, the game features a story that will have "Matrix-like revelations".
Community-made mods add diverse opportunities to the gameplay.
There are two types of servers, Player vs. Environment (PvE) and Player vs. Player (PvP).
If you or any of your tamed creatures die, you can recover the items if you are fast enough.
There is a wide variety of animals that you can tame, breed, and hunt.
There is a limitless array of servers, both Official and Unofficial, that you can play.
Create or join a tribe to gather resources, form alliances, and wage war with other tribes.
Build whatever you like from primitive armaments to futuristic war machines.
Build wherever you like from the deepest oceans to the tallest mountains.
Work up the courage to face the Ultimate Life Forms and prove you are the ruler of the Ark.
Customize your character and any tamed creatures to your heart's content.
Play on a local server to mimic singleplayer that pauses time when you leave.
Enter the Survival of the Fittest tournament to win special prizes.
It is extremely easy to die in this game if you are not careful.
Choose your friends carefully when on a PvP server, trust is not a guarantee.
Only server admins can upload mods. (you will download the mod upon joining the server)
Some servers employ Hardcore Mode, which means you lose
if you die.
Thieves and Hackers are expected on both PvP and PvE so be wary of those you meet.
Always make sure you're safe before logging out since all multiplayer servers run in real-time.
While I recommend this game to anyone who wants a challenge or loves prehistoric creatures, it's not for me unless the developers can improve the game's mechanics for single-player use.
I'm not trying to be harsh on the game, survival isn't easy after all, never is and never will be.
However, this game's design makes it so players have to spend countless hours with friends just to keep their stuff from being stolen by raiders or eaten by wild animals.
Fortunately, I'm willing to keep an eye on it in the future since it is still in Early Access.
