Warframe is an cooperative online game in a state of Galactic Ruin. In its story, you play as the Tenno, a group of beings who survived being thrown into the Void and came back with mysterious powers. You are led by the mysterious Lotus, who awakens the Tenno to aid her in removing the threat of the militaristic clone-breeding Grineer Empire, the technologic cult known as the Corpus, and the mysterious Infestation from the Origin System.
The game features several planets, asteroids, and other playable locations such as all of the planets we presently know of as well as Ceres, Eris, and more. The maps are randomly generated in a series of tiles that are strung together, although the style of the tile depends largely on the map tyle and sometimes even the game mode.
Warframe by itself allows you to take action with several Warframes with unique powers useful for solo gameplay or teamplay, as  well as offering you an armada of weaponry at your control, from several shotguns, bows, pistols, swords, daggers, and most anything you can think of.
(If this review seems sloppy, I did a great job at writing it before, and even hit the character limit with explanations on how the game is, but Steam decided not to post the review when I clicked 'Post Review.')
The pros of the game that I can think of are:
- Digital Extremes (DE) are some of the most passionate developers, willing to stay late into the night to work on major game updates, or even come in on their days off to make sure something gets out on time if not slightly late. They hold bi-weekly development livestreams (Devstreams) on Twitch showcasing upcoming content and bug fixes, while holding weekly livestreams called 'Prime Time' where members of the Community Team play the game with other players in Warframe, while also looking at Fan Art submissions and enlisting some community-driven projects and challenges.
- The game is constantly evolving. Major updates come every few months, new weapons are added commonly, new Warframes are added every now and then, and reworks to older content are added to advance the feel of Warframe. Parkour 2.0 was recently added, which changed the way a player plays the game normally.
- There is an armada of weapons and Warframes at your control, allowing you to play the game effectively in any style you want: as a Support, as DPS, as a Tank (although there is no "true tank" Warframe), as a lone ranger, etc.
- There is a lot of mythology and history pressed into Warframe. Many of the Warframes are based on mythological, cultural, or historical elements (such as Mesa, based on a Western Cowboy, or Chroma, based on Greek depictions of Dragons). This adds a nice personal feel to the Warframes you play as.
- There are no pay walls or Pay-to-Win mechanics in Warframe. Everything in the game that isn't there for aesthetics (such as cosmetic syandanas or skins) or convenience (such as weapon/Warframe slots to increase the amount you can have stored for use) are obtainable in-game. There is no Warframe or Weapon that is only available through real money, except for Excalibur Prime, Lato Prime, and Skana Prime, which were bundled together as part of the Founder's Program in the early days of Open Beta.
- In-game real-money currency (Platinum) can be obtained through trading with other players as well in exchange for other items that can be traded, such as mods, Prime parts, Arcanes, etc.
However, while all of this sounds appealing, Warframe is what I would call a textbook example of Stockholm's Syndrome, in that the more you play it, the more you find yourself attached to it, regardless of its many, many flaws.
To note on its flaws:
- I want to tackle the idea of "RNG" first, as this is largely what ruined Warframe. Warframe is all about RNG in almost all of its aspects. There could be a 3% chance of something spawning in any given mission, or a 2% chance that you will obtain a weapon. All Warframes obtained from the Void or Bosses are RNG-based, and you will likely come across a few or a few dozen of one part of a Warframe before you have all of the parts.
- Grinding. Along with RNG, Warframe is also known as "Warfarm" as you need to farm to get most everything, which unfortunately is a quick way to make players burn out and not appreciate the effort put into the game. For example, a recently-reworked boss (Tyl Regor) was very fun my first time around. Hell, it was probably my favorite boss and I was so happy that he was the only boss to feel like a real boss in the game. However, he drops a new Warframe, and not in the traditional 3-parts that a Warframe requires. The Warframe he drops requires EIGHT parts. So, after my twentieth or thirtieth time fighting Tyl Regor, I eventually grew to hate the boss, hate the tile, and worked my hardest to blow through the mission as fast as possible without enjoying it.
- Void Farming. Advanced versions of Warframes and Weapons are called "Prime" versions. If you want one of these advanced versions, you need to travel into the end-game realm called the Void and play specific mission types in there to obtain parts you can use to make the Prime weapon. However, if you're a Veteran player, you'll know that the Void is unforgiving. If you want a newly-released Warframe, expect to spend anywhere from 20 - 40 hours or longer in total attempting to get just 1/4 of the parts you need to craft that Warframe. Keep in mind that these 20 - 40+ hours attempting to get one Prime part is within one mission type. You will be playing the same exact mission over again and again and again and again and there is no guarantee you will ever get the part you're looking for. There is no system within the game that cycles out Prime parts that you already have received. Expect to get the same Prime part that you don't need about six times in certain mission types.
- The community of Warframe is how you would expect from a free-to-play Online Game, but I feel that Warframe's community is worth noting for being some of the biggest entitled power-players I have ever had the misfortune of coming across. Normally power play is acceptable, but I find that in Warframe, power players (those who want to use the strongest gear to kill as many things as possible) and meta gamers (being those who require certain Warframes and/or weapons in groups to do things as effective as can be) become a huge hindrance. Playing the game, I don't like bringing the most powerful gear. I like actually having fun with the game by trying to aim down at an enemy. However, it becomes annoying when someone with a really powerful gun comes along out of nowhere and eliminates everything on the tile, or even just to kill the enemies that I was having no problem taking down.
- Enemy AI in the game becomes difficult in the worst of ways. They do not become smarter, using advanced tactics. They merely have a larger health/shield/armor pool while dealing more damage. This does not force players to change their strategy more than it just encourages power play. Playing Warframe is no challenge and is far from rocket science. Tip 1: Run and Gun. Tip 2: See Tip 1.
I have over 1500 hours logged on Warframe. I have played since soon after the game's largest (and arguably best) event, the Gradivus Dillemma, ended. It's been nearly two years since I started.
If you are looking for a quick game to play to bide your time while you attempt to look for something else to play or just to kill some time, go ahead and give Warframe a try.
If you are looking for a game to make your home that you can play daily and feel great playing it, I would encourage you to look elsewhere.
I cannot wholeheartedly recommend Warframe.

Ok. I have enough hours on record to give a review.  I feel like I have come to understand the issues that surround this game.  The problem comes from a simple fact of what this game set out to be is not what it eventually evolved into.  To summarize, Ark: Survival Evolved is pitched as a survival game but in actuality, it is an RTS.
An RTS where a single unit requires hours of investment and bigger units sometimes require days.  But to further elaborate, unless you have joined a server that has only just come up, it is an RTS where you join in after the opponents have already lost and a single army has won the map.  The server isn't big enough for everyone.
But the size of the maps are huge, how is it not big enough for everyone?  The answer is flyers.  Mid game, the thrill of survival is lost as soon as your first flyer is secured.  Early game, you wouldn't think of lugging your convoy too far due to a need for food, shelter, and the dangers of an ever imposing wilderness.  After a flyer is secured, you have to go out of your way to be in any real danger.  The thrill of flying over the landscape is exciting and fun but it actually detracts from the excitement of being in any real danger on the maps themselves.  But this is an addition that is too late to address now that it has been done.
With all of that being said, the game itself is addictive.  Fighting for your right to exist on the map is full of military and political conflict.  The dinos and environment are visually astounding with the right hardware.  The development team, even though they are bad about false promises, actually never fail to deliver regular updates of some kind and are truly as passionate about the game as are the players.
The only caveat is that, being in early access, The game is BADLY unbalanced and in favor of established tribes, but I believe the developers are on the right track to bring the best dino based survival experience to all of us, even if many people will get their toys taken away before we get there.

I don't generally play free-to-play games, but Warframe has the best model I've seen for premium content. Ultimately, you're paying for convenience, and some minor aesthetic bonuses. Other than that, every warframe (character) and weapon can be obtained through free grinding.
The setting is gloriously illustrated through the snippets of audio/text flavor and codex entries. While I've played the game off and on for about three years, there has always been a regular release of content, regular and timely bug and hot fixes.
Gameplay is varied, though extended play can make things feel samey, especially when you're grinding for a particular drop. Some warframes and weapons aren't as effective as others, but there is generally strong builds for every play style.
To have suitable variety to your gaming experience you'll probably be spending ~$40 for additional character and weapon slots.
Multiplayer aspects are generally a positive experience, trolling and harassment are relatively non-existant (I've seen none in my play time). However, some missions and drop hunting requires some coordination, but the devs included LFG type chat channels to help offset the non-guild players. Trade is a bit restrctive with an arbitrary tax of grindable currency, however, it is possible to trade for premium currency, which I think grants big props.
Overall, I think this game is worth any MMO player's attention.

You wake up on a tropical beach, the sun is shining and you have some wierd tech implemented into your arm. Oh and you are practically naked.
That's the first thing most people experience when they plays ARK for the first time. It makes you feel safe, relaxed. Tiny Dodo's strut around on the beach, fearless of the new, naked, lifeform. Everything is peachy!
Behind you the edge of a green and lush jungle peeks your interest and you set off to explore. But for each step you take that relaxed feelings seeps away as the warm sunlight cant reach you anymore. You can't hear the waves hitting the shore anymore. Instead you hear a cacophony of animal noises, insects and birds. Every shadow, every movement puts your senses on edge. Warframe is a free to play TPS / hack 'n slash co-op game with stealth and parkour elements. In it the player becomes one of the Tenno, space ninjas awakened from a long slumber, who control powerful suits known as Warframes which provide different abilities and allow them to tackle on dangerous jobs from Lotus.
The graphics are just incredible. Each location has its own design style, the environments are shiny and rich in details, while the special effects are just plain beautiful. The only downside might be the fact that the last one can be a little bit too distracting at times and hard to see through during a fight.
In the sound department, the music is appriopriate to the situation (speeds up when in a fight, for example) and whatever plays in the background is usually the theme of the faction you're fighting against (though it can get overriden by the boss' theme if someone like that appears). A few of the tracks deserve a mention for being just plain incredible, such as Drums of War, Becoming the Hunted, Cold and Gold, We Are Not Alone, Reap What You Sow and
. The sound effects aren't anything special, but they are diverse enough to not get boring or tiring. The voice acting is also really good, even if a bit scarce.
The gameplay consists of you and up to three other players deploying on a mission and completing a specific objective (like killing all enemies or capturing important targets) while moving through randomly-generated rooms. You get to use between three weapons - primary, secondary and melee (which can be of many different types, like bows, shotguns, rifles, sniper rifles, pistols, shurikens, kunais, swords, axes, hammers, polearms, scythes, glaives, knuckles, gunblades.. yeah, this game has
of weapons) - as well as an assortment of movement options, including, but not limited to sprinting, sliding, wall-running etc. You can also attack enemies while performing any of those maneuvers, giving you a large degree of freedom as to how and when to move in and strike.
As far as stealth elements go, you can obviously use cover to keep yourself out of sight of enemies. You can also use silent weapons like bows and shurikens to take them out from a distance, or sneak up behind them and perform an insta-kill stealth execution. Some abilities can also make you invisible or silence everything within a certain radius. The mechanics are very solid and it's fun slicing stuff down.
There is also the Archwing and its own missions, where you move in no-gravity using the eponymous mechanical wings, shooting down foes akin to a space shooter. While it isn't as diverse as the standard gamemode, it is a good change of pace from time to time. Not to mention, even more awesome.
The amount of equipment, types of environments, and missions you can encounter is staggering. The diversity is what keeps it from getting too stale.
Another good thing is that the multiplayer functions pretty well - even with high ping, you will notice an obvious delay, but it won't impact your experience or general gameplay as much as in some other games.
Story-wise, the game isn't really all that rich, but it is solid nonetheless. There is a lot of lore in transcripts and descriptions of some weapons and Warframes, and the quests also provide an interesting narrative as far as the identity of Lotus and the Tenno themselves goes, as well as what happened in the past and what the player characters did before they were put to cryosleep. I'm not going to be spoiling anything, as you should discover it yourself, particularly when it comes to the newest Second Dream quest.
I think this is it for the pros, so let's start counting out the cons. The game is still, quite obviously, a glorified grind to get better stuff. Fortunately, most of the time it's somewhat fun to play.
Speaking about multiplayer, if the host's computer lags horribly due to all the stuff going on in the game, you can expect your gameplay to be similarly laggy, with everything "flash stepping" all over the place.
Another bad thing is the fact that enemies are pretty stupid sometimes. They tend to take cover at not exactly the best spots, or forget that you just sped right past them and still sit there waiting in cover, just being covered from the wrong direction. Harder missions only strengthen the enemies' stats together with spawning elites more often, and sometimes new types of enemies.
Also another thing is that the game requires a LOT of grinding to even get moderately powerful. At the beginning you're going to struggle to complete the missions that aren't the absolute simplest of all, since you don't have much resources to manufacture new stuff, and the starting equipment is very weak. And even if you do get strong weapons, they're not going to be powerful enough without a good assortment of high-rank mods for them to customize their damage output. Of course, if you have a friend who's been playing the game for quite some time and is willing to help you out in getting started, this becomes a bit less of an issue.
The amount of slots you get for equipment is also very limited. While it isn't so bad with weapon and sentinel slots, you get only two Warframe slots for starters, kind of limiting your options as to how many roles you can fill in a team. You really need more slots to be able to do something besides one or two things.
The last thing is the fact that the game is pretty glitchy. Objects can spawn at wrong places due to random generator just messing up, or you can land outside the map and fall into the Void to a collision detection glitch or a lag spike. And this isn't an uncommon occurence.
Overall, this is a grindy and harsh at the beginning, but very fun game once you get far enough. You should check it out if you don't mind a sluggish beginning, especially if you've got more experienced friends who can help you get running.

You wake up on a tropical beach, the sun is shining and you have some wierd tech implemented into your arm. Oh and you are practically naked.
That's the first thing most people experience when they plays ARK for the first time. It makes you feel safe, relaxed. Tiny Dodo's strut around on the beach, fearless of the new, naked, lifeform. Everything is peachy!
Behind you the edge of a green and lush jungle peeks your interest and you set off to explore. But for each step you take that relaxed feelings seeps away as the warm sunlight cant reach you anymore. You can't hear the waves hitting the shore anymore. Instead you hear a cacophony of animal noises, insects and birds. Every shadow, every movement puts your senses on edge. The atmosphere is really thick, you can almost taste it.
Suddenly you hear a rapid thumping sound. A rapid thumping sound that is getting closer and closer. All of your instincts tell you to run. You run, hoping that your steps will take you back to the beach. Then you hear a high pitched screech, you turn around and see a flurry of teeth and claws.
You wake up on a tropical beach, the sun is shining and you have some wierd tech implemented into your arm. Oh and you are practically naked.
ARK is a survival game set on an island with various biomes and filled with Dinosaurs and other prehistoric animals. Your mission is to survive through crafting tools, weapons, shelter. You can tame almost all of the wildlife and most can be tamed, mounted and help with different tasks.
Play with friends, form tribes and wage war againgst other tribes. Charge you enemies on lightning quick Raptors, crush your foes with a mighty Brontosaurus or swoop down from the skyes.
If you arn't into PvP there are PvE Boss encounters to be found. Try your luck againgst some mighty fearsome creatures!
As of writing this ARK is still in Early Access. The game is being updated regulary but already have ALOT of content that will keep you occupied for many many hours.

Ah, Warframe. Where do I begin? I started playing Warframe a few days after the launch of Update 9 (that's back when Nova first came out), and since then the game has basically changed in every way. From Parkour to Damage, we've seen it all (except stealth, but I'll get to that later. I'll give a short version of my review and a long version. Short first.
_________________________________
Intro:
Warframe is a unique 3rd Person Shooter that combines elements of your average third person shooter with a twist: Character abilities and a "mod" mechanic, allowing you to essentially play whatever Warframe you want, however you want. Deep combat and customization (not physical customization).
THE GOOD:
- The unique "mod" mechanic makes for very deep and thought provoking gameplay and combat, and with the right mindset you can build Warframes to utilise certain abilities, weapons, or gameplay styles.
- Fun combat! Who cares about depth when it isn't fun?
- A Warframe for just about everyone!
- Good Customer Support
THE BAD:
- Only 2-3 weapons per category are viable for use in the end-game, as well as certain Warframe's abilities being rendered useless at the infinitely scaling enemy health bar.
- Good weapons tend to get put in then quickly destroyed via nerfs, and in wanting to allow weapon diversity, it reduces viable weapons to the 2-3 mentioned.
- Most Weapons and Warframes are hidden behind several layers of RNG, causing some Warframes to be nigh unattainable unless you trade for them via real world money's worth of an in-game currency
Overall: This game has many issues. MANY, many issues. It's fun at the end of the day, but albeit, very frustrating at times. I'd say give it a play.
Intro:
Warframe is a unique 3rd Person Shooter that combines elements of your average third person shooter with a twist: Character abilities and a "mod" mechanic, allowing you to essentially play whatever Warframe you want, however you want. Deep combat and customization (not physical customization).
That basically sums up the good. The game is very fun, despite all of its flaws. Which I will point out.
[NOTE: These issues could be resolved in the coming weeks, months, or years. Research for yourself unless you're seeing this before Update 18+]
THE BAD:
Warframe's end-game roster is very limited, and despite efforts to make other weapons worth using to increase diversity, most of what they do is nerf. Not just any nerf, but destroy. Weapons, anyway. Warframe balancing is awesome (although how Mesa has not been nerfed yet is beyond me). In trying to increase the roster, they have managed to wittle down what's worth using in total to about
. All of which are locked down behind many walls of RNG. Every time a weapon worthy of use in the Meta is released, it is quickly shoved back into the "NO META FOR YOU" box, effectively removing perfectly good weapons, weapons you spend real money on and lots of time on, might I add, and making them utterly useless. Beware, fellow Tenno.
And don't even get me started on stealth. It's nonexistant. Empty. A shell of something amazing. Cake without yeast. It's that kind of mess. Same goes for Archwing. And Sharkwing. Same deal.
The majority of the elements feel half-a**ed, and thrown in for the sake of a reminder to finish them later, else they'd quickly forget the idea in the first place. Not that that's not what's happening right now, that is.
Mods: You've heard the good. Here's the bad. Some mods are nearly impossible to get, and harder to rank. It takes an incredible amount of work to do. Not only that, but they constantly "fix" locations that will allow us to gear ourselves at some point in this lifetime by being the most efficient with Fusion Cores, XP, and resources (slight hyperbole;
). Not to mention those hard-to-get mods are the best ones. The ones absolutely necessary for the end-game. You will not be successful without them. Period.
They never nerf weapons well, as nerfs always destroy weapons, and buffs are needed for many things but are rarely ever seen. Again, buffs are seen on Warframes just as much as nerfs. Warframes are balanced, weapons are not.
My biggest issue with this game is their tendency to take perfectly viable weapons and mods (ones not on the 11 roster of viable weapons), and beat them to a pulp and throw them away, spitting in the face of anyone who put work into it. You can always make more money... but you can never get more time... days and days of work, all for naught at the press of a few keys by the devs. Be careful in what you craft. Wait a LONG time before you craft it. Make sure it won't get nerfed, and you won't get burned. Like I have many times.
This game is worth playing, but it has many core issues that need to be fixed to keep people coming back. It's no coincidence more veteran players are leaving with each day, and they're losing players just as much as gaining new ones. It's this mentality of f*cking over experienced players and rewarding noobs, and nerfing to oblivion that will ultimately ruin this game if it isn't addressed. Play it while it's here.

I've got 1800+ hours into the game and have run my own server for a year now. I thought I would hate this game when I was pressured into buying it from a friend. My boyfriend and I pretty much only game traditional MMO style and have never cared for survival games. That being said... the first hour I was hooked. The basis of the game is great and it has so much potential for more.
That being said... they have stated multiple times that they are trying to get as much content in as possible before the run the main optimization so that they do not have to repeat it a bunch. If you want a highly polished game and on time ETAs this is probably not the game for you. (Just pretend there is no ETA and you won't be mad when they definitely miss it.)
Make sure your computer can handle the game in its current state and find yourself a good unofficial server. Those are the best two pieces of advice I can give you. I started on officials and if I'd had to remain on officials between the time suck of vanilla and the toxic official communities I never would have stuck with the game this long. This game really depends on who you play it with. Find your style and find a server that matches that style and this will be a fantastic game for you.
There are a wide variety of dinos for you to tame, and breeding is fun as long as breed and baby timers are turned up. Exploration and building is here too for those that enjoy that. PVP is plentiful on pvp servers and raiding in the game is quite fun. If you're more into PVE like I am, there is plenty to do for you as well.
Overall I would say this game is worth the buy. The only way I wouldn't recommend it to you is if you're impatient and wan't a finished, polished game. They are still working on things and are not the best at communicating when things will come out. As long as you know and can forgive this, I think you'll get a lot of enjoyment out of the game.

I really, REALLY wanted to give ARK a better review, so I will!
The Fixes:
--Collision has been dramatically improved (the hopping-out-of-water issue is not nearly as common now), even though there are still conflicts with how dinos (especially unridden dinosaurs) navigate.
--Dino Population is no longer nearly such a problem. The developers have added an option for server hosts to change the spawn frequency of dinosaurs, which is noble goal, but seems to have had the side effect of removing all terrestrial predators from the game if you tweak that option down. I hope this will be patched soon.
The Cons:
--Scaleability remains an issue. No, this isn't the ability of dinosaurs to have scales. It IS the balance of progression as human players or their dinosaurs level up: there is next to none. The only thing that seems to really matter in combat is maneuverability, and that is based on the size, turning speed, and hitbox of the dinosaur, which cannot be changed. A human being, no matter how well-equipped, will never be able to face down the larger dinosaurs alone. (Which makes sense - you are just a solitary, squishy little hooman.) However, neither will your dinosaurs, upon whom you lavish DAYS of attention and careful nurturing, only to have them swarmed by level 2 fish and eaten alive. Whereas a real dinosaur could simply STEP OVER THE FISH and make it to shore alive, a combination of AI and collision makes navigating with non-ridden dinos a grief-inducing chore.
The Good Things:
--Graphics: The graphics ARE a VERY shiny use of the Unreal 4 engine. There are optimization issues, but eventually - I hope - they will be addressed. ARK is definitely one of the more graphically-advanced games available, and many of the screenshots I take are pure photo-ops.
--Taming Dinosaurs! Admittedly the reason I bought the game, because who doesn't love riding around on giant saurians? "Dinotopia" lives! 'Nuff said.
--Attention from the Developers: Too many times, there have been games where the developers supported it for a month after launch, and then washed their hands of it. Not so in ARK. The developers are patching the game like heck in preparation for the full release in August, 2017, and I am pleased to say that they are finally addressing issues that have caused longstanding pain for me and other players. Here's hoping they can finish it all in time.
In summary, ARK has an incredible amount of potential, and is on the road to fully living up to that potential as a AAA-quality title. While obviously intended as an MMO, with dozens of people on a single server, the issues that plagued a single-player experience are being fixed or addressed by giving more options to the player/server host. I am happy to give ARK my full, positive recommendation, and would say it's definitely worth the price it was originally listed at, $30 USD. I'm still iffy about the sudden doubling of the price, like a lot of people.

I know a lot of people are upset over paid DLC already but i'm not sure what the point in getting up in arms about it is about.  It hasn't affected the development progress of Ark, only expanded it.  I have 66 hours in the game so far and I've BARELY touched the surface of what I can do.
I should also point out it's price point IMO for how enjoyable it's been so far and how many hours put in and still not bored, it's money WELL spent.  Considering other "indie" games I won't mention at full AAA prices that completely flop, this is an under priced title, with a lot of stuff to offer.  I paid less than the price of 1 AAA title for two copies of a game I still enjoy.  Many negative reviews are unfortunate since they simply disagree with a developer move and review the game based on a business decision rather than the game itself.
I've built 3 bases....well 2, the third even though it has Dino doors I use as a storage place for wood mid way through the two other bases.  One base is in a safe area south of the map, and the other is north east which a little more life.  Planning to build another north west of the island in the snowy mountains but I want to be a little more prepared since it's full of t-rex's.
Point is, almost 70 hours in, I've bought two copies, one for me the other for the wife and we feel like we're only just getting started.  For me, it is one of those games that you really shouldn't start playing without having some time on your hands because time goes by like nothing.  In the last two days, I've some how put in 31.2 hours and gone to bed at 2am feeling like crap the next morning but I'll do it again simply because I'm enjoying the game.
I do have some suggestions for the developers I'd like  to see.  I'd have to write them down as I'm playing since they tend to come to mind while doing something in game.  I'll edit the review as I remember them.
1. One for sure I'd love to see is when chopping at things, other animals and dino's should be curious about the noise and you shouldn't always feel safe no matter how loud.  I want you to think twice about going out at night and making a lot of noise.
2. This one I can't say won't be fixed since it's still early access, but I'd like to worry less about my dino's following me and getting stuck.  They need to be able to follow me better without getting stuck between two trees, but again, early access so it's just me thinking out loud.
3.  Since viewing a hand held map and marking a position isn't unrealistic, i'd like to see the ability to mark spots on our map.  Maybe you can already and I haven't figured out how?  If not this is a must.
More to come, but I highly recommend it personally.  I own too many games, many are top favorites, but Ark is easily #1 IMO.  I think it's worth your time and money to try out.  Don't go in thinking you'll get an idea in the 2 hour refund window Steam offers.  You won't even touch the surface.  It requires a lot of your time.
For reference at the time of this review, I play off an early 2016 Alienware with a GTX 980m at almost full Epic settings with 60ish FPS at 1080 for anyone wondering.  My wife uses my old ROG gaming laptop with a GTX 660m and can play on medium at 720p with a few things like view distance turned down to smooth it out.  Even at those settings her game still looks fantastic, not a good but still very enjoyable.  I also use the xbox one elite controller which i find feels good with this game along with some mouse input in my inventory.
Hopefully knocked out a few details.  Enjoy the game.

I really, REALLY wanted to give ARK a better review, so I will!
The Fixes:
--Collision has been dramatically improved (the hopping-out-of-water issue is not nearly as common now), even though there are still conflicts with how dinos (especially unridden dinosaurs) navigate.
--Dino Population is no longer nearly such a problem. The developers have added an option for server hosts to change the spawn frequency of dinosaurs, which is noble goal, but seems to have had the side effect of removing all terrestrial predators from the game if you tweak that option down. I hope this will be patched soon.
The Cons:
--Scaleability remains an issue. No, this isn't the ability of dinosaurs to have scales. It IS the balance of progression as human players or their dinosaurs level up: there is next to none. The only thing that seems to really matter in combat is maneuverability, and that is based on the size, turning speed, and hitbox of the dinosaur, which cannot be changed. A human being, no matter how well-equipped, will never be able to face down the larger dinosaurs alone. (Which makes sense - you are just a solitary, squishy little hooman.) However, neither will your dinosaurs, upon whom you lavish DAYS of attention and careful nurturing, only to have them swarmed by level 2 fish and eaten alive. Whereas a real dinosaur could simply STEP OVER THE FISH and make it to shore alive, a combination of AI and collision makes navigating with non-ridden dinos a grief-inducing chore.
The Good Things:
--Graphics: The graphics ARE a VERY shiny use of the Unreal 4 engine. There are optimization issues, but eventually - I hope - they will be addressed. ARK is definitely one of the more graphically-advanced games available, and many of the screenshots I take are pure photo-ops.
--Taming Dinosaurs! Admittedly the reason I bought the game, because who doesn't love riding around on giant saurians? "Dinotopia" lives! 'Nuff said.
--Attention from the Developers: Too many times, there have been games where the developers supported it for a month after launch, and then washed their hands of it. Not so in ARK. The developers are patching the game like heck in preparation for the full release in August, 2017, and I am pleased to say that they are finally addressing issues that have caused longstanding pain for me and other players. Here's hoping they can finish it all in time.
In summary, ARK has an incredible amount of potential, and is on the road to fully living up to that potential as a AAA-quality title. While obviously intended as an MMO, with dozens of people on a single server, the issues that plagued a single-player experience are being fixed or addressed by giving more options to the player/server host. I am happy to give ARK my full, positive recommendation, and would say it's definitely worth the price it was originally listed at, $30 USD. I'm still iffy about the sudden doubling of the price, like a lot of people.

I tried Warframe a year ago, and was not very impressed. The game was incredibly dense and hard to get into, the movement was awkward and the combat was floaty and felt all wrong. What interested me was the design and the world if Waframe, and the game failed to live up to it's awesome visuals.
I decided to try it again recently, and that may have been one of the best gaming desicions I made in 2015.
Warframe has transformed from an ugly duckling to a swan. In my opinion, this game is now one of the very best free to play titles available on steam.
Everything has improved immensely. The game is much easier to get into, though it is still dense and packed with features. The combat is responsive, fast paced and exciting, and rewards good aim and skillful use of abilities. And the movement system, which was part of what turned me off the game the last time I tried it, is now one of it's most attractive features.
And Warframes biggest selling point for me personally is still it's amazing visuals. This is a gorgous game, and it's futuristic visual style is unique and exciting.
You should know what you are getting into with Warframe though.
This game is all about the grind. You grind for Warframes, you grind for weapons, and you grind for crafgting materials and credits. That would be a big turnoff normally, but in Warframes case it just doesn't matter because the gameplay is so enjoyable. Blueprints, parts and materials drop frequently enough that you always feel like you are making progress, and thanks to the amazing movement system each mission is a breeze to speedrun through should you choose to.
This is a multiplayer title with strong mmo elements, but thankfully the drop-in style of play is simple and effective. Simply selecting a mission will drop you into a group of players right away, with little wait time. Most players seem to be friendly, and the Warframe community has in my experience been nice and helpful. YMMV. I quickly met people who were more than willing to help me get started, and many of them ended up on my friends list.
Getting into Warframe can seem daunting at first, simply because there is so much content. There are planets to unlock, warframe and weapon blueprints to find and craft, lots of crafting components to collect and many, many missions and game modes to get familiar with. Starting out as a fresh player with very little knowledge of exactly what I was getting into despite having tried an earlier version of the game felt a little confusing, simply because of the breadth of options available to me. Getting my bearings and finding some sort of direction took an hour or two, and I must admit I consulted Reddit and the wiki for information. The greatest resource, though, were the very helpful players of the game. After a couple of hours, I got into it and found some goals to work towards, and since then the game has been an impressive and fun experience.
If you are wondering whether this game is for you, just try it. It's free, it's fast paced and fun, and it looks amazing.
I recommend Warframe to anyone who enjoys fast shooters, mmos and collecting stuff!

Well. I have been playing Ark since June of 2015. It has come a long way. There are issues with the game but it is getting better with just about every update.  There are things that as a player I wish were fixed faster but I am not a developer and I trust that Wildcard has their heart in the right place. I have over 4400 hours played.  In that time I have seen many of the issues fixed as well as the new ones begin but as far as content and enjoyment, the game has immersion factor that keeps me thinking about it all the time. You can roll solo or tribe up and go pvp or be a laid back pve'r and build yourself a dino farming operation and get into breeding dinos to get genes from dinos together to make superior creatures that you have raised from babies and cherish their growth. There is always something to do. Sometimes it's work but you get what you give and when you get together with a great group of people it really takes you into a whole new dimension in gameplay. What you can do is up to you. Problems aside...and one day many issues that people harp on will be gone, this game is outstanding. With a good rig it looks amazing. No matter what map you play the game is hard to start but it gets better every time you die as long as you learn from your mistakes. I see why people are so negative but they just don't want to like it. It truly is a game worth way more than what I paid for. Like I said before, I believe in the people at Wildcard and I know they want a great game and of course make money but they don't act like money hungry jerks. The do read what we say to them, they do respond, the do work hard and late to make it better each opportunity they have. So do yourself a favor and don't listen to the negative. Play Ark for what it is and remember that if something is wrong they will, maybe not as fast as you want, fix it. It's a great game and you will lose your dino, it will get killed, you will die by accident, or something could spawn in your base but if you learn and research or ask around on your server you will get better. You will get better dinos, better quality items, and all leading to a much more improved gaming experience. So Good Luck and Stay Alive!

Ark is a fairly fun game, I had the greatest 100 hours until the last 27 where I just found myself doing nothing but flying dinosaurs over and over. However, that type of thing happens to me with ever sandbox I've played and it's just a matter of time, but I normally am able to play for longer than 100 hours before this happens.
The real problem comes where you see the "early access game" before buying it. Now don't get me wrong, early access games can be great but you have to realize this game already has DLC. That's right, DLC. The devs were so determined not to take this game out of early access that they decided to create DLC to get more money than to actually make a finalized product. It's almost like the devs are sticking a middle figer up our♥♥♥♥♥to get more money, and honestly Ark did not need it. It's a very fun game for the first 100 hours I played it and I would not mind going back to it, but the fact that I already bought the game for $30 (more than enough for the game's devs to make a finalized product) and now I have to pay another $20 just to get 1 new map. It isn't like the map is truly anything special, I mean I don't have it but from what I have seen, It would be better just to get a map from someone in the workshop.
All in all, did I enjoy this game? Yes, very much so, the gameplay is great and just as long as you like sandbox games you will have a great time.
Would I recommend this to friends? No, The fact that DLC is already out in an early access game and it costs $20 only means that later along the line, when this game reaches a true launch date there is going to be way more dlc and the people that are attracted to non-early access games will have to pay like $80 for a game that is truly still only worth 30.

I have always loved dinossaurs, since i was little, and Ark: Survival Evolved just hits me very deeply when i play.
At first I was reluctant to buy the game and the reason is simple, I got to know about the game through mainstream events and speeches. "If everyone likes it, then i am not going to like it." That was my unique and original thought in that occasion.
But in the end, I bought it. I stopped caring about those mainstream events, but rather on my myself and in what i wanted.
"I wanted to play with dinossaurs."

It isn't for me to say that it is worth it or not. You are the one who is going to pay for it, you are the one who is going to play.
That isn't for me, nor anyone else, to decide, nor at the very least manipulate anyone, including you, to either buy or don't buying the game. (This is the second time that I further support your own personal decision).

Play with friends, or alone. PVE or PVP it is your choice.
The game has its major flaws, like any other game. Soon or later you will understand it. But it is rather how you see and how you manifest it that will reflect your behaviour. You can take the majority of the reviews, included mine as an example.
For me, Ark: Survival Evolved is a rollercoaster of experiences, that no other game has ever offered me before. I can only recommend a game like this, not for my own personal perception but has evidence for my own play time.
I guess that makes me an Ark Nerd.

At the time of writing this review I have almost 1200 hrs played on PC and 650 hrs on Xbone. This review is based on my view of the current state of the game. If changes are made to the game I will more than happily edit my review to reflect that. Also this review does speak of the features added with Scorched Earth DLC but being that those features directly effect the core game they are relevant in this review.
First off I love Ark. So much to do and learn. The interactions with other players, who to trust or not to trust. (Protip: Don't trust anybody.) The challenge and learning curve are great.
I have only played on PVP servers. I've played on both Island and Center maps. Currently I play mainly on a Island\Primitive server. My tribemates and myself have clawed our way through trolls, rivals, and even "friends/allies" to get to where we are currently, the undisputed magnanimous alpha tribe of the server. We get along with most everyone on the server currently. We don't get involved in skirmishes between other tribes but we will hunt trolls or defend smaller tribes we are involved in trading with.
There is a certain demographic of players known in the community as being destructive to servers. I will not name this group but will simply refer to them as the "Scourge" (Term used based on definition. NOT a tribe name!) Lots of time this "Scourge" inculdes streamers who generate views by causing havoc and distruction on servers. They then can recruit their viewers into the game to bolster their manpower immediately. Once a server has been ruined they move on to the next. I have dealt with this "Scourge" several times and have witnessed their tactics first hand. That said, when this "Scourge" first showed up on my current server we wasted no time hunting them down in attempt to keep them in check. This requires a ton of effort. This "Scourge" is relentless, they are good at what they do, and most importantly they have numbers. I will also mention that I witnessed several members of this "Scourge" use exploits, glitches, and or cheats to gain access to our heavily guarded and defended main building on one occasion. Luckily we were online at the time and they were reported. Nevertheless most of our server rallied behind us and we were able to suppress this "Scourge" and place a relatively large number of them into a prison.
I took a break for about 2 months to go on vacation and play the new WoW xpac with some friends. I still checked in with my tribemate occasionally. They told me it was a constant chore keeping the "Scourge" in check but they were able to do so. As the newness of the WoW xpac has already started to wear off for me I decided this morning to log back into my beloved Ark, see my tribemates, and checkout the new stuff that had been added in my absence.
Up until this point in my story my review would remain positive. Sure the "Scourge" is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥and I wish the developers would do something about it. It is a pvp game however and with a lot of effort we were able to come out on top. Also in regard to Scorched Earth DLC costing extra, I do not agree with this. Although it isn't enough to make me give a negative review. I just don't think that a game that is still in early release should have paid released for it. Finish and release the base game that I paid for. Once the base game is complete I would happily pay for DLC for this game. I haven't purchased the DLC yet but I'm sure I will if my main concerns are addressed.
Finally to my main point for a negative review. When I log in this morning and talk to my tribemates about all the new stuff added in my absence I am informed that things have heated up and the "Scourge" threat is greater than ever. Its not enough that the server banded together and battled back the "Scourge". Now we have to contend with the "Scourge" building a massive army on a scorched earth server and then marching them through a one way gate onto our server and wiping us out in the off hours. How is that not broken? How is it even a thing that they can march their dino army through a portal and attack us with absolutely no risk of us marching our army of dinos back through to attack them? My tribemates informed me that they have tried to stop them but it seems like every tactic they come up with is patched by the Devs. Block off pillars? Ok, now they can come in through drops. Block off spawns? Nope, now they spawn on the structures. Give me a break.
My tribemates recently found one of the "Scourge" streamers channels that is in the group we have been warring with. They have been watching, trying to learn what they can do to combat the winter that is coming. My tribemate gave me the link to the stream. I brought it up right as the guy was logging in. Right there on his favorites list was our NA server. There were about 5 or 6 other servers on the list but they were various EU servers. My tribmates had been watching for a while. The particular EU server they were currently invading was in its off hours. Just a handful of people online at the time. The "Scourge" had been preparing. They marched onto the server with no less than 7 Rock Elementals and insane amounts of resources. The "Scourge" flooded the server quickly filling all available player slots preventing any players native to the server from logging on to defend their bases and dinos. In almost no time they had a base of operations put up, smithys and crafting structures down. That server was doomed. Regardless of preparation or skill there is no winning that fight. The "Scourge" will swoop in, destroy everything on the server, and a few hours later when there a no more bases to destroy, dinos to kill, or views to be had they will move on. I've witnessed it with my own eyes.
I've seen several negative reviews based on the fact that Scorched Earth is a paid DLC. I've seen a lot of those reviews flamed because the commenter says you shouldn't review the base game based on the review. In this case the DLC has a HUGE impact on the base game. Paid DLC or not the current state of the game sucks. I really want to play again but I'm not going to put time into a game when all my work is just going to be wiped out in a single night  when there no way to defend against it. I as well as others have posted my concerns on the official game forums in the past with no response from the Devs. This is how I make my voice heard. Fix this game so I can change my review to positive play this game on a level playing field again.

The lack of freedom to play the game because every peice of loot or reward is compartmentalized into a specific  mission, faction, mode, and tileset.  Anything popular is nerfed "because everyone is doing it" and "because balance" (yet "balance" never happens), then whatever made it popular is reintroduced behind a new Pay or Grind Wall.  Anybody who exposes this is drummed out of the forums.  Digital Extreme's excuses, twistedly regurgitating what players say to cover what it does.
On 02/08/2013 DE stated that Warframe is about 4 Tenno Devastate Massive Armies (skip to 2:54)

In 2015, after months of wrecking the spawn code, DE decided that a reduction to 30 enemy on the field at once is more than enough enemy on the field at once.  In other words, DE was sooo over that Massive Army stuff.
DE's not too crazy about the 4 Tenno Devastate part either, but, it knows that "OP" sells.  So DE nerfs, releases "OP", nerfs, releases "OP", nerfs ........ never stops jerking the player base around.  There's a history of power creep too, all the while "balance blah blah blah...", nerf, power creep, nerf, power creep, nerf ....
The Warframe Meta:
It's possible to have every piece of player content in this game without spending money thanks to trade, by following this simple Meta:
1)  Join a good clan that will carry you around.
2)  Camp camp camp.
3)  Grind grind grind.
4)  Trade trade trade.  Trade your syndicate mods and weapons, trade Void Trader exclusives. trade rewards and loot.  Trade it all to new players who don't know better, or completionists.  Do it before it gets nerfed, or wait until it's taken out of the loot/reward tables then sell it to completionists for a lot more.
Recommendation:  I do not recommend this game to people who like to own something when they spend money for something.  There is too much turmoil in it's development for that.  However, if you don't mind the flux and find the camp, grind, trade "free to play"(or not) meta appealing, then you might be happy with Warframe.  It's your choice.  Have fun, if you will, or can.
My experience has been fraught with opposition and disappointment, even though I spent ~$185 on Warframe, so I'll have to avoid such games in the future.

At the time of writing this review I have almost 1200 hrs played on PC and 650 hrs on Xbone. This review is based on my view of the current state of the game. If changes are made to the game I will more than happily edit my review to reflect that. Also this review does speak of the features added with Scorched Earth DLC but being that those features directly effect the core game they are relevant in this review.
First off I love Ark. So much to do and learn. The interactions with other players, who to trust or not to trust. (Protip: Don't trust anybody.) The challenge and learning curve are great.
I have only played on PVP servers. I've played on both Island and Center maps. Currently I play mainly on a Island\Primitive server. My tribemates and myself have clawed our way through trolls, rivals, and even "friends/allies" to get to where we are currently, the undisputed magnanimous alpha tribe of the server. We get along with most everyone on the server currently. We don't get involved in skirmishes between other tribes but we will hunt trolls or defend smaller tribes we are involved in trading with.
There is a certain demographic of players known in the community as being destructive to servers. I will not name this group but will simply refer to them as the "Scourge" (Term used based on definition. NOT a tribe name!) Lots of time this "Scourge" inculdes streamers who generate views by causing havoc and distruction on servers. They then can recruit their viewers into the game to bolster their manpower immediately. Once a server has been ruined they move on to the next. I have dealt with this "Scourge" several times and have witnessed their tactics first hand. That said, when this "Scourge" first showed up on my current server we wasted no time hunting them down in attempt to keep them in check. This requires a ton of effort. This "Scourge" is relentless, they are good at what they do, and most importantly they have numbers. I will also mention that I witnessed several members of this "Scourge" use exploits, glitches, and or cheats to gain access to our heavily guarded and defended main building on one occasion. Luckily we were online at the time and they were reported. Nevertheless most of our server rallied behind us and we were able to suppress this "Scourge" and place a relatively large number of them into a prison.
I took a break for about 2 months to go on vacation and play the new WoW xpac with some friends. I still checked in with my tribemate occasionally. They told me it was a constant chore keeping the "Scourge" in check but they were able to do so. As the newness of the WoW xpac has already started to wear off for me I decided this morning to log back into my beloved Ark, see my tribemates, and checkout the new stuff that had been added in my absence.
Up until this point in my story my review would remain positive. Sure the "Scourge" is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥and I wish the developers would do something about it. It is a pvp game however and with a lot of effort we were able to come out on top. Also in regard to Scorched Earth DLC costing extra, I do not agree with this. Although it isn't enough to make me give a negative review. I just don't think that a game that is still in early release should have paid released for it. Finish and release the base game that I paid for. Once the base game is complete I would happily pay for DLC for this game. I haven't purchased the DLC yet but I'm sure I will if my main concerns are addressed.
Finally to my main point for a negative review. When I log in this morning and talk to my tribemates about all the new stuff added in my absence I am informed that things have heated up and the "Scourge" threat is greater than ever. Its not enough that the server banded together and battled back the "Scourge". Now we have to contend with the "Scourge" building a massive army on a scorched earth server and then marching them through a one way gate onto our server and wiping us out in the off hours. How is that not broken? How is it even a thing that they can march their dino army through a portal and attack us with absolutely no risk of us marching our army of dinos back through to attack them? My tribemates informed me that they have tried to stop them but it seems like every tactic they come up with is patched by the Devs. Block off pillars? Ok, now they can come in through drops. Block off spawns? Nope, now they spawn on the structures. Give me a break.
My tribemates recently found one of the "Scourge" streamers channels that is in the group we have been warring with. They have been watching, trying to learn what they can do to combat the winter that is coming. My tribemate gave me the link to the stream. I brought it up right as the guy was logging in. Right there on his favorites list was our NA server. There were about 5 or 6 other servers on the list but they were various EU servers. My tribmates had been watching for a while. The particular EU server they were currently invading was in its off hours. Just a handful of people online at the time. The "Scourge" had been preparing. They marched onto the server with no less than 7 Rock Elementals and insane amounts of resources. The "Scourge" flooded the server quickly filling all available player slots preventing any players native to the server from logging on to defend their bases and dinos. In almost no time they had a base of operations put up, smithys and crafting structures down. That server was doomed. Regardless of preparation or skill there is no winning that fight. The "Scourge" will swoop in, destroy everything on the server, and a few hours later when there a no more bases to destroy, dinos to kill, or views to be had they will move on. I've witnessed it with my own eyes.
I've seen several negative reviews based on the fact that Scorched Earth is a paid DLC. I've seen a lot of those reviews flamed because the commenter says you shouldn't review the base game based on the review. In this case the DLC has a HUGE impact on the base game. Paid DLC or not the current state of the game sucks. I really want to play again but I'm not going to put time into a game when all my work is just going to be wiped out in a single night  when there no way to defend against it. I as well as others have posted my concerns on the official game forums in the past with no response from the Devs. This is how I make my voice heard. Fix this game so I can change my review to positive play this game on a level playing field again.

First off, this is a great game as long as you know what you are looking for and how to play it. In my experience the best way to play this game is to get some friends together, rent or make a dedicated server and play like mad. Mess with mods, try different maps, make the game how you want it to be. There are also a ton of modifiers that can easily be changed to make the game as grindy or quick as you want. Single player is fun as well but adding friends just makes it better.
Unless you are looking to troll people, PVP or listen to people whine…DO NOT PLAY ON OFFICIAL SERVERS. There are plenty of free unofficial servers that you can try out and maybe make some friends. There are some bugs, but not many game-breaking ones that I have experienced. Sometimes you lose your bag. Sometimes it crashes on loading. I personally don’t think the bugs in this game are that big of a deal. Especially with the control that you have over spawning items in etc. Everything is replaceable.
I am not a fan of paid DLC in early access but I can at least see some possible reasoning behind it. We all know about the lawsuit and that they probably needed money after the settlement blah blah blah. The biggest thing I am upset about with the DLC release is how the devs have responded to their customers/investors. They should have been up front about the development of the DLC from the beginning and should be apologetic for not being upfront. However, I do know that the DLC was part of their plan long BEFORE the settlement. Just read this article from September 2015.
They clearly state that development of expansion content would begin “soon” after this article. The dev also says that it will be ready a few months after launch. The scheduled release of the Ark was scheduled to be in June 2016 and the DLC launched in September 2016. I am not an expert but I think that could be classified as a “few months”. I also know that at least 3 other studios are working on this game. Maybe the DLC was on time and the main game wasn’t? I am not going to pretend to know that one or all of those studios were working on the DLC…just saying it’s a possibility. Regardless, the devs should have clearly, openly, repeatedly said that this was their plan and not left it in the hands of a single interview.
I tend to judge games on how many “fun hours” I can get out of a game for the amount of money I have to spend. Based on that, I have to recommend this game. If you like these types of games and stay away from the official servers, I have a hard time believing that you won’t get your money’s worth.
On that note, people with 500+ hours that don’t recommend the game: I challenge you to take a look at your game library and find your games that you only dumped 30 bucks into and see if they match your Ark hours. Some games will, I have no doubt, but those are gonna be few and far between. If you think 30 bucks for 500+ hours of fun isn’t worth the money, I question your standards or your mental capacity. If you played the game for 500+ hours and you didn’t like it, you are being equally idiotic by playing something that long and not having fun. If you lost everything because some DLC dragon came and burnt it all up, there is always a price to pay for playing on official servers or "free" unofficial ones, no matter what game it is.
A newcomer can easily get their money’s worth from current content, officially released or not.

My Experience:
So I've played this game since it came out and ever since it has had more warframes, weapons, upgrades, maps, and gamemodes. The only thing that Warframe is infamous for is the intense grinding. Now I admit, even I was tired of the grind after a while which is why I might not have as many hours as others people who played Warframe when it came out. The first time I played it I was amazed by the fact that there can be a free to play game this wonderfully made. As I played the game, I'd occasionally get bored but not to the point where it was excruciatingly boring, but there were times. The only thing that kept me going were the quick and huge updates with new fun Warframes that had different weapons stats etc. I was finally exhausted with the game when update 15 came out with the introduction of Rhino Prime (Not 100% sure)? It was too boring to look at I had quit. Several months later I see so many things have been added. The biggest change of all was the archwing addition. I was blown away at the fact that they would make something like that. In additon, the game was running sweet 60 fps with my gtx 660,(an ok graphics card). Ever since then I've been playing Warframe again casually with my friends. You just need to give Warframe some of your time (and money for slots lol).

I think the gameplay is something that most people could appreciate but for some perspective on the grind, I have 30 something hours played and I have only just gathered the parts to make another warframe and then I will have to wait 72 hours for it to craft or something like that.

1st Review - October 2016
What can I say? This game has taken so many turns as I progress through it that it would be difficult to relate it to any other game. Mostly, it is because the game is quite unique due to the depth of it. Base building, modding, loneliness, early game struggles, major setbacks, and huge victories can all be found in this game. Don't forget all of the crazy creatures you get to interact with as well! Starting a small graveyard around level 50 is recommended, you're going to need it for those epic dino losses. I have played on Xbox One, PC, official and my own servers. Currently, I host a dedicated Scorched Earth Server, and I couldn't be happier. That is, of course, unless I receive more friends that would like to come play on my server! Wink Wink.
Revised Review - July 2017
Alright let's be clear. Thought this game would stay thick and get thicker. Believed that this game had the opportunity to excel where others had not.
- Paid DLC
- Charging people full price for "Retail Parity" or whatever they are barfing out of their PR department nowadays.
- Admitting to the public that they can't even go 72 hours without making drastic changes to the ultimate futures of all players who play on official servers. - Let's not forget that the team has admitted that they do not have any "major" mechanical changes to the core of the game. What does that mean? Two more DLC's and the team moves on to another project. Look it up, it's there.
- Etc. Etc.
The point is that there is no point that I can make that others have not. What I CAN offer you is insight. Played on Xbox since day one, built a gaming PC inspired by potential performance gains.  The game runs great, just check my Steam screenshots to see some of the HUGE structures and literal cities I have created.
Ultimate Verdict: Ark Team = The Opposite of Thick
What is the opposite of thick you may ask? Decide for yourself. Enjoy.

Liked: Has (or maybe had by the time you read this), a mix of game play: guns, melee, mobility, nukes and other large radius powerful abilities.  The Art Department is great.
Disliked:  The development over the past 2+ years where my fun was repeatedly nerfed and the game cannibalized to expand the Pay or Grind Wall.  The lack of freedom to play the game because every peice of loot or reward is compartmentalized into a specific  mission, faction, mode, and tileset.  Anything popular is nerfed "because everyone is doing it" and "because balance" (yet "balance" never happens), then whatever made it popular is reintroduced behind a new Pay or Grind Wall.  Anybody who exposes this is drummed out of the forums.  Digital Extreme's excuses, twistedly regurgitating what players say to cover what it does.
On 02/08/2013 DE stated that Warframe is about 4 Tenno Devastate Massive Armies (skip to 2:54)

In 2015, after months of wrecking the spawn code, DE decided that a reduction to 30 enemy on the field at once is more than enough enemy on the field at once.  In other words, DE was sooo over that Massive Army stuff.
DE's not too crazy about the 4 Tenno Devastate part either, but, it knows that "OP" sells.  So DE nerfs, releases "OP", nerfs, releases "OP", nerfs ........ never stops jerking the player base around.  There's a history of power creep too, all the while "balance blah blah blah...", nerf, power creep, nerf, power creep, nerf ....
The Warframe Meta:
It's possible to have every piece of player content in this game without spending money thanks to trade, by following this simple Meta:
1)  Join a good clan that will carry you around.
2)  Camp camp camp.
3)  Grind grind grind.
4)  Trade trade trade.  Trade your syndicate mods and weapons, trade Void Trader exclusives. trade rewards and loot.  Trade it all to new players who don't know better, or completionists.  Do it before it gets nerfed, or wait until it's taken out of the loot/reward tables then sell it to completionists for a lot more.
Recommendation:  I do not recommend this game to people who like to own something when they spend money for something.  There is too much turmoil in it's development for that.  However, if you don't mind the flux and find the camp, grind, trade "free to play"(or not) meta appealing, then you might be happy with Warframe.  It's your choice.  Have fun, if you will, or can.
My experience has been fraught with opposition and disappointment, even though I spent ~$185 on Warframe, so I'll have to avoid such games in the future.

Needs a TONNE of optimisation at the moment, which it will hopefully get before full launch.
Initially I too complained about the stupidity of paid DLC on an early access game, but given the developers' justification of it, I can personally see reason for it (I would have thought they could still have very much done this with a free DLC, though... maybe not, but I can't see why. Never mind).
My biggest complaint though, is that it is horrendously unbalanced for singleplayer. Yes you have many, many options to customise the game to your liking, giving you the ability to balance it yourself, but that just seems like a needless faff. I just kind of hoped that perhaps certain things were made easier to cater for there being one player, but they aren't. Also, if you, like me, disagree with the crafting costs of many items (especially in the setting of SP), then you have to open a certain game file, and write code to adjust the recipes. Then when you go into the game, if that item needed to be crafted using a Smithy, for example, you'd need to break that Smithy (can't just pick it up oh no. That would be too simple), rebuild it (or spawn another in because F-U) and place it down again, instead of the crafting costs updating automatically like they should. So, to summarise, there is no crafting cost slider option, you have to write code, and then you have to faff around and jump through flaming hoops every single time you load the game back up just to be able to craft items using your preferred crafting costs.
Other than that, this is a really good game. Plenty to do, plenty of danger and it has the stretch goals of beating the bosses if that's what you want to do. Y'know, if you get bored of building bases and adding to your family of killer dinosaur pets. Also you can ride dinosaurs. I mean come on. What other game lets you do that?

I have put in about a doller per every hour I've played in this game, according to the ingame time counter, and steam's own money spent counter.
My love of this game will never go away, but my tolerance of the actions of Digital Extremes (the developers of Warframe) has slowly been declining over the last 2-3 years. Compared to the developers of most other F2P games, they're still pretty good. However, they used to be entirely honest, community oriented, and in-touch with their game. Over the past year and a half, they've delayed a major update by half a year and allowed other content to be held back as a result, they've conducted a major nerf wave on several of the classes in the game (the warframes) with the promise of rebalancing later (hasn't happened), they've taken legal action against a player of the game after sensitive information was leaked and content was manipulated by another party entirely, they've broken drop tables and allowed subpar rewards to be available in high tier missions where they don't belong, and a handful of other things.
I'm leaving a negative review at the moment because of the legal action they took against the community member here in the last week. In addition, they've been very stubborn and defensive. Unless this is resolved in such a way that it makes up for the damage done, my review is remaining negative.

I don't like the Steam review system because I'm honestly 50/50 on whether or not I'd recommend the game. The gameplay is fun, but really only with friends do to the massive amount of grinding/resource gathering required on the official servers. This is remedied on private servers though. My main negative issue with the game now, however, is with the DLC. If they want to release DLC for a game that is still in early access, it shouldn't still be in early access in my opinion. Currently, however, you are allowed to transfer stuff over from the dlc server to the old server, which is a massive pain. I'm currently dealing with random people who have no time on the server I'm on coming in and wiping all of the players with tames from some random Scorched Earth server. Where is the counterplay in that. How are you supposed to defend against something you don't even know is coming. Not only that, they added another creature that can destroy stone structures. A hour long tame is able to destroy stone structures and can't be damaged by automatic base defense such as turrets. Wildcard keeps adding ways to destroy bases but doesn't add any ways to defend them. If you're going to play on this game, ignore the official servers, just play on private servers. Or else you'll lose 350 hours of work by something you can't control unless you plan on spending weeks worth of time gathering materials.

The more money they have the more they can put into the game at the end of the day, regardless of early access or not. I think that they've added enough content to prove that they are committed to making it the game it can be. The released the DLC to also test the multi-relm mechanic, which I think is only only going to increase it's worth and if they wouldn't have done it now, they would have later. All in all a great game.
